544060|2026-06.headline: RBZ Jewellers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 60% YoY to INR121 crores, with EBITDA up 39% to INR18 crores at a 14.9% margin.
544060|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations was INR121 crores, up 60% YoY, in line with prior guidance, led by retail at INR78 crores (+70% YoY). EBITDA rose 39% to INR18 crores (14.9% margin) and PAT rose 28% to INR9 crores (7.5% margin). Management attributed margin pressure to muted gold price inventory gains, lease amortisation of INR76 lakhs, lease liabilities of INR115 lakhs, and pre-opening costs for the Surat store. The call focused on the store rollout (four stores this fiscal), a shift toward a gold metal loan (GML) based hedging model, and a long-term target of 75:25 retail to B2B mix.</overview>

segments.name: Retail (Harit Zaveri Jewellers)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR78 crores, up 70% YoY. Ahmedabad store grew from INR24 crores turnover in FY21 to INR408 crores in FY26. Share of retail in B2B/B2C mix targeted at 50:50 in one to two years and 75:25 long term.

segments.name: Wholesale (B2B)
segments.commentary: Revenue reported as 42 (unit not clear, likely INR crores), up 47% YoY. Management says order book is strong for the coming quarter and B2B volumes grew.

segments.name: Job work
segments.commentary: Revenue approximately INR1.2 crores. Job work is 54% of mix per management, and management is seeking customer gold advances to reduce working capital.

guidance_outlook: Surat store (large format, ~10,000 sq ft) to open around late September 2026, ahead of Navratri (11 October); capex about INR10 crores; 52-60 staff hired.
Rajkot large-format store to open before October/early Q3; Maninagar and Gandhinagar mid-format stores in Q3 (possibly November).
Management expects Q2 performance in line with earlier projections, supported by IIJS order book; July and August order books described as full.
Capex break-even targeted within about one year per store; large-format inventory deployment INR125-150 crores, small-format around INR50 crores.
Debt-to-equity expected below 1:1 (about 0.8 debt to 1 equity) by fiscal year end; medium-term target 1.5-2:1 via GML.
Sanctioned debt of about INR300 crores, not yet fully utilised.
Inventory valued at about INR400 crores; market value about 18% above book.
Employee costs expected to keep rising as store and senior hiring continues; marketing spend to rise.
capex_capacity: Total factory capacity 1.8-2 tonnes a year; current consumption about 900-1,000 kg, around 50% utilisation.
Seasonal utilisation reaches 70-85%, sometimes near 90%, in peak months (July-September).
Surat store capex about INR10 crores; large-format inventory INR125-150 crores; small-format about INR50 crores (plus or minus 10-15%).
Plan to roll out about seven stores in total; four are in this fiscal year, and a few more have leases signed, some in Gujarat.
Retail inventory around 350 kg per an analyst question, not confirmed by management.
demand_pricing: IIJS show described as strong, with good buyer growth and order book; corporate design appreciation noted.
18-karat share of corporate sales: 0% before December, targeted at least 20% by year end.
Management says gold in USD fell about 30% from peak; INR gold has been flat, leaving negligible inventory gain in Q1.
Management says it does not expect 18-karat occasion wear demand to rise across India; 22-karat remains dominant.
Retail Q1 volume about 49 kg versus B2B about 125 kg; own production about 15-20% of retail volume.

qa_highlights.question: Expected timeline, investment and break-even for new stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Surat in Q2, Rajkot early Q3, Maninagar and Gandhinagar in Q3. Large-format capex break-even within a year or less.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term retail vs wholesale mix and debt-equity target?
qa_highlights.answer: B2B:B2C targeted at 50:50 in one to two years and 75:25 long term. Debt-equity below 1:1 by year end, rising to 1.5-2:1 via GML at about 3-3.5% cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline year on year?
qa_highlights.answer: Negligible inventory gain as gold rate was flat, INR76 lakh lease amortisation, INR115 lakh lease liabilities, and pre-opening staff and marketing costs for Surat. Management estimated the total impact at about INR9 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How will the GML hedging work and what share of inventory will be hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Gradual move toward hedging, with about 50% in year two and 75% in year three. Retail cash flows will repay GML sub-limits. Bank negotiations are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the company shifted to GML from cash credit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites a 30% USD gold correction, rising custom duty and a stronger balance sheet, with better ratings and banking relationships. GML is a natural hedge and is cheaper than the roughly 9% cost of the current borrowings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the franchise route planned and what is the long-term business split?
qa_highlights.answer: Franchising is premature. Current brand investment is meant to make the brand franchisable later. B2B will remain, and B2C profit share is expected to rise over three to four years.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from pre-opening costs, lease accounting and muted gold price gains; quarterly EBITDA margin trend as stores open.
Store ramp-up in Surat and Rajkot against the one-year capex break-even target.
Gold price volatility on about INR400 crore inventory; hedging transition depends on bank GML sub-limits still under negotiation.
Rising debt as borrowings grow; target D/E of 1.5-2:1 depends on GML availability and rating upgrade.
Job work share (54%) and working capital cycle; customers must provide gold advances.
Shift toward 18-karat jewellery; management says its contribution is still small.
544060|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on retail expansion and demand visibility, but evasive on store-level revenue forecasts, segment EBITDA (withheld for competitive reasons), and the franchise timeline. Management openly acknowledged the margin dip and pre-opening costs.
key_quotes: So we are going to transform into a retail side.
We are utilizing factory at around 50% of capacity.
Right now we are not sharing it because of competitive reasons.

505978|2026-06.headline: Triton Valves Q1 FY27 group consolidated sales rose 38.5% YoY to ₹186.5 crore; EBITDA ₹12.4 crore, with ₹4.75 crore one-time tax credit lifting PAT to ~₹9.75 crore.
505978|2026-06.overview: Management reported group consolidated sales of about ₹186.5 crore, up roughly 17.5% QoQ and 38.5% YoY, with about 20% volume growth and the rest value growth. EBITDA was about ₹12.4 crore versus ₹11.3 crore QoQ and ₹8.8 crore YoY (the slide labelled the YoY figure incorrectly). Gross margin contracted about 145 bps QoQ and 181 bps YoY, which management attributed to commodity pass-through with copper and brass prices near historic highs and the Iran/war disruption. Management also flagged that climate control shrank, metals was hit by delayed Middle East raw material supply, and the merger tax credit flattered PAT.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Sales ₹103 crore, up from ₹78 crore YoY and ₹86 crore QoQ; growth led by tubeless (~25% volume YoY), TPMS (~75-80% YoY) and EV components (~103% YoY). Tube valves ex-motorcycle segment grew ~20%. Tubeless, TPMS and EV lines running above 85-90% utilisation.

segments.name: Metals (Triton Valves Future Tech, brass mill)
segments.commentary: Sales ~₹79 crore, up from ~₹50-52 crore YoY and ₹68 crore QoQ; capacity utilisation ~65-70% post expansion, implying ~30% headroom. Current ROCE above 16%, with management targeting 20%+ and possibly 25%. Scrap sales now netted off under Ind AS, reducing reported standalone top line without affecting EBITDA.

segments.name: Climate control
segments.commentary: Sales ~₹3.9 crore, down YoY and QoQ. Management cited Chinese dumping, copper costs and a weak AC season; it is lobbying for QCO and minimum import price. Q2 expected to be quiet, with recovery from Oct-Nov.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of a 'reasonably good' Q2 if the second half of the quarter holds, and says FY27 will be much better than FY26.
Annualised Q1 group EBITDA ~₹50 crore vs ~₹40 crore in FY26; PBT, EBITDA and revenue expected to run slightly above annualised Q1 levels.
Group ROCE expected to rise from ~12.5% to 13-14% this year and ~15% by mid-next year; new investments targeted at 20-25% internal ROCE.
Ambition of a ₹1,000 crore revenue target by about FY30; management says it has a plan that does not depend on climate control recovery.
EV component vertical targeted at ~₹100 crore over the next few quarters, with climate control also scaling to ~₹100 crore if trade remediation happens.
Double-digit EBITDA margin is not expected until commodity prices stabilise; management said it would take a long time.
Tax credit of ~₹4.75 crore already availed, plus a further ~₹0.3-0.4 crore claimed, subject to assessment; no advance tax outflow expected for ~14-15 months.
capex_capacity: FY27 group capex planned at ~₹15 crore: ~₹10 crore for automotive (tubeless, TPMS, EV components) and ~₹5 crore for metals (special alloy foundry, extrusion and drawing equipment).
About 50-60% of the ₹15 crore is expected to be commercialised in FY27, with the balance in FY28.
Automotive tubeless, TPMS and EV lines are at 85-90%+ utilisation; management said capacity will run out during the year without investment.
Metals utilisation ~65-70% post expansion, leaving ~30% volume headroom.
Climate control has spare capacity; management said it only needs orders.
demand_pricing: Automotive growth described as ~80% vehicle production growth and ~20% share gain; passenger car and two-wheeler production grew ~12-15% YoY in Q1 (per management).
Management expects automotive growth to moderate in Q3-Q4 but remain positive; new programmes cited with AUMOVIO, SENSATA and Bosch (LOIs from AUMOVIO and SENSATA in TPMS).

Metals: Q1 started slowly from Middle East raw material disruption; ~₹10 crore of metals sales were not delivered on time due to Hormuz issues. Demand strong into Q2; management expects Q3 seasonal traction in metals and climate control.
Prices pass through to automotive and climate control customers every three months. Brass selling price to external customers now above ₹1,000/kg vs ~₹500-550/kg last July-August.
Management expects metals to reach 60%+ of group revenue over 2-3 years; special alloys (naval brass, marine grades) being developed as import substitutes.
Climate control faces Chinese dumping; management is refusing to cut margins to win volume.

544028|2026-06.headline: Tata Technologies Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4.3% QoQ in constant currency to $175.4M (25.2% YoY), with management reiterating double-digit FY27 organic growth.
544028|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 revenue was $175.4M, up 4.3% QoQ and 25.2% YoY in constant currency, with Services at $136.6M (approximately 78% of revenue). Operating EBITDA was about $28M, a 16.1% margin, up 10 bps QoQ, while PBT fell to INR 252 crores from INR 283 crores because Q4 included a one-time Labour Code provision reversal. Management highlighted the $100M Tenneco engagement and a Japanese OEM full-vehicle program, and reiterated double-digit FY27 organic growth with growth expected to be much greater in H2 than H1. Near-term margin expansion may moderate due to upfront ramp-up investments and a Germany wage increase in Q2.</overview>

segments.name: Technology Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue $38.8M, +4.2% QoQ cc and +27.9% YoY cc. Education grew 9.1% QoQ while product business declined 2.6% (seasonality); margin fell 250 bps on mix toward education.

segments.name: Automotive non-anchor
segments.commentary: Revenue $43.9M, +6.7% QoQ and +56.3% YoY. Non-anchor is about 49% of services revenue and about 36% of total automotive, per CFO.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: Revenue about $10.2M, +6.4% QoQ and +38.1% YoY. Management sees a path to a $100M target in the next two to three years.

segments.name: IHM
segments.commentary: Revenue about $15M; no growth rate was disclosed on the call.

segments.name: Europe (geography)
segments.commentary: Revenue about $67.9M, +10.1% QoQ, supported by Es-Tec integration; Germany saw an uptick, but some customers are under restructuring.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: strong double-digit organic revenue growth, with services as the primary growth engine; management reiterated this on the call.
Growth is expected to be much greater in H2 than H1 FY27, with the ramp-up of closed deals as the main driver; quarterly phasing depends on team mobilisation and customer readiness.
Management said it would not focus on a specific margin milestone; it expects QoQ margin expansion to continue in Q2 despite the annual wage increase in Q2.
Tenneco ($100M, 5-year deal) begins execution in Q2, scales toward calendar year-end, and will require incremental headcount and cost.
Management said Germany wage increases in Q2 will be absorbed, which may moderate the pace of margin expansion near term.
capex_capacity: Several large strategic engagements and full-vehicle programs entered mobilisation in Q1, requiring upfront investment in talent, ramp-up, transition and delivery readiness ahead of steady-state revenue.
BMW TechWorks crossed 2,000 engineers; it is a JV and not consolidated into revenue.
Headcount optimised to 12,579 with a balanced FTE vs outsourced mix; hiring is selective and focused on strategic skill areas.
Development cycles of 18 to 24 months for full vehicles, versus 36 to 48 months at many Western OEMs, per management.
demand_pricing: Tenneco: $100M multiyear transformation engagement spanning engineering, digital, AI-enabled processes and operational modernisation; described as mostly new business with a small renewal element.
A North American industrial equipment manufacturer engagement covering systems, software and embedded software, using AI-enabled methodologies.
A leading global OEM Range Extender Vehicle program; a leading off-highway manufacturer selected Tata Technologies as preferred partner.
A Japanese OEM full-vehicle development program, which management described as a first-time relationship in this space and a path into Japan.
Management said deal momentum continued into Q2 and that additional large deals have closed beyond those disclosed; no customer names or sizes were given.
Management said tariffs and EV tapering had held back demand over the past ~18 months, and that clarity is now returning and investment is resuming.
On AI pricing, management said AI is a force multiplier on productivity and that it sees the work volume as expanding, not shrinking.

544028|2026-09.headline: Tata Technologies Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.2% YoY in constant currency to US$178M; operating EBITDA margin held at 16.1% despite salary increments.
544028|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed constant-currency revenue growth of 22.2% YoY to US$178M, with services up 26.2% YoY (22.1% excluding ES-Tec). Total revenue in INR rose 2.1% QoQ to INR 1,699 crore, held back by a Technology Solutions decline tied to a revenue-recognition change and education timing. Operating EBITDA margin was 16.1%, flat QoQ, absorbing a ~100bp salary-increment headwind, and PAT was INR 171 crore. Management reiterated strong double-digit FY27 growth and said margins should expand in H2, while ES-Tec (Germany) remains soft.

guidance_outlook: Reiterated strong double-digit consolidated revenue growth for FY27.
Expects sequential margin improvement in H2 FY27; management said margins expand in Q3 despite typically soft Q3.
Management reaffirmed 18% and 20% as the North Star margin range; no date given for reaching 18%.
Expects some additional softness at ES-Tec in Q3, with conditions to stabilise in 2027.

Expects new large programmes, including the US$138M deal, to contribute more meaningfully in H2 FY27 and inform order book for next year and the year after.
Expects to win a couple of further large deals before calendar year-end and continuing into Q4.

Competition: European ESPs in China, Europe and North America; Indian ESPs mainly in India-targeted vehicle programmes.
Management expects structural outsourcing by OEMs as Chinese OEMs set new benchmarks in speed and cost.

543212|2026-06.headline: Borosil Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR253.6 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 14.6% from 17.8% on a ~INR10 crore West Asia cost hit.
543212|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue from operations grew 9% YoY to INR253.6 crore, with Glassware up 16.8% and Non-glassware up 4.2%, both stated as volume-led. Operating EBITDA fell to INR35.9 crore from INR40.2 crore as fuel and packaging inflation from the West Asia conflict hit margins; management said price increases of 5-7% were taken but realisations lag into Q2 onwards. PBT dropped to INR17.4 crore from INR23.5 crore (last year included a INR7.2 crore one-time stamp duty reversal), and PAT fell to INR12.8 crore from INR17.4 crore. Management reiterated an FY27 EBITDA margin of about 18% excluding other income, and a steady-state ambition of 18% without the conflict impact.</overview>

segments.name: Larah Opalware
segments.commentary: Sales INR83.6 crore, up 9.8% YoY from INR76.2 crore, stated as volume-led with hardly any price contribution. Management guides roughly 9% growth going forward.

segments.name: Glassware (borosilicate microwavables, serveware, tumblers, lunch boxes, storage)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR65.6 crore, up 16.8% YoY from INR56.2 crore; management said growth was entirely volume-led with price pass-through lagging. Utilisation about 90%.

segments.name: Non-glassware (small appliances, bottles and flasks, cookware, kitchen essentials)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR98.1 crore, up 4.2% from INR94.2 crore. Hydra (vacuum flasks) remained hit by BIS compliance requirements, offset by domestic appliances and stainless steel cookware.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 18%, excluding other income; management framed 14-15% historically and ~18% as the steady-state level without West Asia impact.
FY27 capex estimated at about INR125 crore, with an overall range of INR125-150 crore including solar and opal furnace rebuild maintenance capex.
FY27 consolidated depreciation expected at about INR92 crore.
Solar Phase 3 savings estimated at INR27-28 crore at EBITDA level in FY27; management declined to say how much would be retained after pass-through.
Price realisation from the 5-7% increases expected to flow in from Q2 FY27 onwards.
Long-term ROCE aspiration of 20-24% (later referenced as 20-22%) on the business; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Stylenest India (subsidiary) Hydra plant in Rajasthan: 2 double-wall lines commenced commercial production on 30 June 2026; third line expected in Q2 FY27.

Bharuch, Gujarat glassware plant: capex INR42 crore, sanctioned in Q4 FY26 to make jugs, jars and bottles currently sourced (~INR100 crore sales) from BSL Bharuch; commissioning by end Q3 FY27.

Jaipur borosilicate pressware blast furnace expansion from 25 to 32 tons per day plus a third forming line; capex INR50 crore; commissioning by end Q4 FY28. Current furnace utilisation about 90%; furnace rebuild due Jan 2028.
Opalware utilisation described as full; Glassware about 90%.
demand_pricing: Price increases of 5-7% by category taken across multiple categories (management says some above that); execution started mid-May and realisation lags into Q2.

Chinese dumping in borosilicate glassware persists despite rupee depreciation and higher freight; anti-dumping investigation pending with authorities, timing uncertain and not included in guidance.
Whiteware (Opalware sub-category) about 10% of Opalware sales vs under 5% last year; management said margins are well below the regular range, so it will not push that mix up.

Omnichannel presence across 24,000+ retail outlets, e-commerce, quick commerce and B2B/export; first two exclusive Borosil brand stores opened in Pune and Gurugram, Jaipur next, capex INR40-50 lakh per store, no store-count target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Glassware's 16.7% growth was price vs volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was entirely volume-led; price pass-through is lagging and was only a couple of crore in Q1 against about INR12 crore West Asia impact. Price hikes range 5-7% by category.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 margin and capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About 18% EBITDA margin for FY27 excluding other income; capex about INR125 crore, with a range up to INR150 crore including solar and furnace maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Has Chinese dumping eased given rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management says dumping continues with no visible difference despite rupee weakness and higher freight. Anti-dumping investigation is ongoing, and no benefit is assumed in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 growth inflated by channel inventory stocking ahead of price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management rejected that view, saying price impact arrives only in Q2 and there was no forced sale or retailer stocking. Inventory build is typical ahead of Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in ~18% margin given historical 14-16%?

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to 20-24% ROCE and why is ROCE around 11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed low ROCE to heavy capex over three to four years, plus inventory built for BIS challenges. It described 20-24% as a medium-term aspiration; it did not provide a bridge or timeline.

544424|2026-06.headline: Globe Civil Q1 FY27 revenue (total income) rose 37.26% YoY to INR929.23 million; PAT up 40.42% to INR7.09 crore.
544424|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income for Q1 FY27 was INR929.23 million versus INR676.98 million a year earlier, up 37.26% YoY. EBITDA rose 33.03% to INR15.80 crore with a stated margin of 17.01%, and PAT rose 40.42% to INR7.09 crore (net margin 7.63%). Management attributed growth to projects won after the IPO (Central University Bathinda, Haryana Cricket Association stadium, Kanpur) and said working capital was elevated by pre-final/final bills and early material procurement. Management guided to 10-15% growth in FY27 on the existing order book, with order book targeted to reach INR1,200-1,500 crore.

segments.name: Institutional / education
segments.commentary: Management called education its main focus, citing IITs, IITs/IIMs/NITs as major revenue sources; recent bids include Central University Tamil Nadu and IIM Visakhapatnam. IIT Delhi and an INR100 crore IIT order were mentioned.

segments.name: Sports infrastructure
segments.commentary: Two small sports projects of about INR50 crore each done, and a ~INR200 crore stadium (Jhajjar) under execution, with management aiming to build eligibility for bigger sports projects. Stadium revenue to date was about INR30-35 crore, and completion is targeted in about 15 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 10-15% from the existing order book, excluding any new project wins.
Expected FY27 execution of about INR300-350 crore from the ~INR700 crore order book, with the largest revenue in the last quarter.
EBITDA margin expected to be maintained at around 17% (similar margins), and management said margins are sustainable for the next one to two years.
Target to add at least INR500 crore of new orders within 3-12 months, taking the order book to about INR1,200-1,300 crore; next milestone INR1,500 crore by year-end.
Management says it wants order book at least 3x annual turnover.
capex_capacity: Management said it can handle 10-15 projects simultaneously; 11-12 projects are currently running.
Single-project eligibility is INR500-650 crore in normal projects; larger projects possible via joint ventures.
Existing setup could support revenue of INR500-600 crore without a major increase in fixed cost.

Mobilisation advance (up to ~10% of contract value against bank guarantee) available but not availed on Bathinda or the recent IIT project.
demand_pricing: About four to five tenders (~INR800 crore) were pending opening; bids placed at two to three per month, including Bihar, Tamil Nadu, Visakhapatnam and Nagpur.
Selective bidding favoured central government and funded projects; competition cited as 5-6 bidders versus 10-15 on NHAI tenders.
Management described competition as healthy with decent margins, not heavy under-bidding.
Top 5 projects contribute about 70% of turnover; one private client (DPS) and one cricket stadium are the main private projects, the rest are government.
Repeat clients include CPWD (about 20 years), NBCC (fifth or sixth project) and DPS (three projects in total).

qa_highlights.question: What drove Q1 revenue growth and what share of revenue came from which projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Post-IPO wins (Central University Bathinda, Haryana Cricket Association, Kanpur) drove growth; Bathinda structure work and NBCC project contributed most. A new project typically takes 6-8 months to reach full revenue flow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the order book and what pipeline exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Current order book about INR700 crore; four tenders (~INR800 crore) awaiting opening; target at least INR500 crore new orders in 3-12 months, taking book to INR1,200-1,300 crore; next milestone INR1,500 crore by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables and inventory rise, and what is being done on cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose on Q4 final and pre-final bills (Aligarh NBCC billing expected to close by 15 September; Telecommunications India Limited by 30 September). Inventory rose on material bought in Feb-Mar 2026 ahead of price increases. Routine government and DPS bills take 30-40 days to realise.

qa_highlights.question: Why were some projects delayed and what is the stadium contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Stadium start was delayed by statutory approvals; it started scaling from March. Stadium revenue to date is about INR30-35 crore. Management said approvals for government projects now sit within EPC scope, making them faster.

qa_highlights.question: Will the current margins be sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident the current margins (about 17% EBITDA) are sustainable for the next one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR700 crore order book will be executed in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects INR300-350 crore of execution in FY27, based on current monthly run-rate of INR30-40 crore.

risks_watch: Receivable days elevated: final bills pending on NBCC Aligarh and Telecommunications India Limited; collection timing is key to cash flow.
Inventory and working capital rose faster than revenue; watch whether it normalises as orders scale.
Order inflow needed to reach INR1,200-1,500 crore target; four tenders (~INR800 crore) pending with no guaranteed wins.
Project start delays from statutory approvals (Bathinda, cricket stadium) can push revenue recognition out by 6-8 months.
Heavy reliance on government clients and top 5 projects (~70% of turnover).
544424|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on execution and margins, but guidance is conditional on new order wins. Management was candid about delays, receivable timing and the number of pending tenders. Several answers were vague or repetitive on order targets and FY27 growth.
key_quotes: We always believe that we should have at least 3 the turnover -- 3x order book of the turnover.
Yes. We're confident that this margin are sustainable for the next couple of years.

505196|2026-06.headline: TIL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 86% YoY to INR117.1 crore, with EBITDA margin at 6.2% (vs 1.5%) and PAT at negative INR5.5 crore.
505196|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR117.1 crore included Tulip Compression (TCPL) only from 8 May to 30 June 2026, so the quarter is a partial-period read. Standalone revenue grew 25% YoY to INR78.6 crore, with EBITDA up to INR3.4 crore (4.3% margin vs 1.5%), but standalone PAT was negative INR7.2 crore. Management flagged that blended margins will stay volatile for the next six to eight quarters because of product mix and supply-chain localisation, and gave no near-term margin guidance. The company delivered nine ReachStackers and reported a current order book of INR211 crore against a pipeline of about INR373 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.1 crore (1.5%) in Q1 FY26; 9.6% in Q4 FY26 per analyst
+223% YoY vs INR1.1 crore; margin up from 1.5%

segments.commentary: Revenue INR78.6 crore (+25% YoY), EBITDA margin 4.3%. Management said FY26 turnover was about 50% defence. Nine ReachStackers delivered in the quarter.

segments.commentary: Consolidated from 8 May 2026 (part period). Order book INR328 crore, pipeline INR117 crore. FY26 revenue about INR278 crore per management. Management's medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin view is 14-15%.

segments.name: Aftermarket / services
segments.commentary: FY26 aftermarket about INR56 crore. Management's long-term aim is 40-45% of revenue; parts margins 25-35%, service margins slightly better.

Five-to-seven-year ambition to roughly triple turnover; no significant capex needed up to about INR700-750 crore turnover, beyond bridging capex of INR5-10 crore.

Pick and carry crane (CarryKing 515) launch targeted Q4 FY27 with 520 configuration to follow.
demand_pricing: ReachStacker market share 38-40% after a comeback; CONCOR order described as one-time, first such order since 2014-15.

qa_highlights.question: ReachStacker market share, competitors and whether the Q1 order is CONCOR.

qa_highlights.question: Can the current order book deliver more than INR200 crore this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm the figure. It said the order book is exhausted over about nine months and new orders will add to it, and expects a significant jump in turnover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall from Q4 to Q1, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product mix and localisation drive volatility; Q4 had Air Force cranes and ReachStackers. No harmonised margin for six to eight quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Tulip's business, revenue, margin, and plans to raise stake.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 14-15% medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin, equity infusion up to INR50 crore, and a 74% stake target over a few years. Export to Nigeria has just begun.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debtor days.
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors rose at end-FY26 due to a large IAF missile crane order in late March. Target is 60-75 days; TIL is now an MSME, which should speed customer payments.

qa_highlights.question: Chinese competition and pricing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TIL competes on reliability, durability, and aftermarket uptime commitments, not on credit terms.

Tulip integration and TCPL full-quarter contribution in Q2 FY27.

543957|2026-06.headline: Redtape Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 19.4% YoY to INR47 crore on 3.7% revenue growth to INR480 crore, with no price hikes and e-commerce deliberately de-prioritised.
543957|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 3.7% YoY to INR480 crore, with gross margin at 47.5% and EBITDA margin at 20.4%. PAT rose 19.4% to INR47 crore, the company's highest-ever Q1 profit in absolute terms. Management held MRPs flat and absorbed minimum wage and input cost inflation through sourcing, supply chain and retail efficiencies. E-commerce declined as management refused to match marketplace deep discounting, and online share of revenue fell to 22% from 30%. Management described the e-commerce dip as a one-off, but gave no quantified guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited >200 bps improvement; management attributed it to retail margins, operating leverage and supply chain
down from around INR28 crore in Q1 FY26, due to lower e-commerce platform rebates

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: 56% of Q1 turnover; management says footwear carries Q1 and Q2 while apparel peaks in Q3 and Q4. Open footwear ASPs improved sequentially.

segments.name: Apparel
segments.commentary: 39% of Q1 turnover; seasonally stronger in Q3 and Q4. Category-wise YoY growth not disclosed.

segments.commentary: 5% of Q1 turnover. Sunglasses are in about 80% of stores; hard luggage in only 10-15% of stores as the category has shifted online.

segments.commentary: Declined YoY because management declined incremental marketplace discounting. Online share fell to 22% from 30%. Management aspires to return to 30%.

segments.commentary: Softer early in the quarter, improved as the quarter progressed. Management credits store-led model and better product/category mix for margin gains.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: UAE franchise stores were hit early in the quarter and recovered in the last month. UK master distributor Style Label Manchester appointed; transactions started. No export revenue guidance given.

guidance_outlook: Store additions: 33 opened in Q1 FY27; aspiration of about 150 (150-plus) by FY27 end, versus an earlier 200-250 aspiration. Management says it will 'remain close to that number'.
EBITDA margin to be kept stable at around 20% for the year; management also expressed aspiration to increase margins.
Revenue growth: management hopes to continue the growth rate of the last 3-4 years; no quantified FY27 guidance.
E-commerce share expected to recover towards 30% of revenue; management called the Q1 dip a one-off.
Inventory target to reduce from 173 days to 150 days. Inventory build-up expected in Q2 ahead of festive season.
No MRP increases planned; management aims to offset cost inflation through efficiencies.
capex_capacity: New stores: 33 opened in Q1 FY27, with an aspiration of about 150 for FY27. Ramp-up takes 45-50 days for a 1,000 sq ft store and about 75 days for a 3,000-4,000 sq ft store.
New store formats are mostly 800-1,500 sq ft, as expansion into South, East and West India is more store-count intensive.
Store in Forum Mall, Kolkata opened; malls to be used where they are stronger than high streets, particularly in South and West India.
Inventory at 173 days; Q2 build-up expected, then reduction in Q3 and Q4.
No acquisitions in the pipeline at present; management is open to opportunities in footwear and apparel.
demand_pricing: Demand was soft early in Q1 due to macro headwinds and cautious consumer spending, then improved through the quarter.

Marketplaces pushed higher discounting; Redtape declined to match beyond levels it considered appropriate for the brand. Management said there is no fixed discount ceiling and that it decides event by event (for example BBD).

ASPs rose sequentially across footwear and apparel from product and category mix, not broad-based price hikes. MRPs were held flat despite minimum wage and input cost inflation linked to the ongoing war.
Management declined to quantify inflation, calling it 'a regular business'.
Non-BIS inventory remains; the industry has an extension of one year, with management expecting a further extension.
A September 2025 income tax search is ongoing; management says no material claim or risk has been identified so far.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the e-commerce weakness, and what is the discount level beyond which Redtape will not participate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline was a deliberate choice, not a structural weakness. It declined to set a fixed discount threshold, saying it depends on event size and margin impact, and that it expects e-commerce to recover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inflation burden and will price hikes follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said minimum wage and war-related costs were absorbed, MRPs were not raised, and it would not quantify the inflation as it is a regular business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the lower other income?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vivek Agnihotri said lower e-commerce platform rebates cut other income to around INR8-9 crore from about INR28 crore in the prior-year quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement above 200 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said retail margins were stronger, with operating leverage and an optimised supply chain. No category-level margin split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Does Q1 margin mean moderation is likely for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is to keep margins intact and aspire to improve them, while noting that it will not sacrifice margins for top-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the income tax search from September 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the process is ongoing and could take 2-3 years, with no material claim or risk identified to date.

544525|2026-06.headline: GK Energy Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 71.1% YoY to INR 505 crore, with PAT up 61.6% to INR 59.7 crore.
544525|2026-06.overview: GK Energy reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue, with standalone revenue of INR 505 crore (up 71.1% YoY), EBITDA of INR 86.1 crore (margin 17.05%, up 47.7%) and PAT of INR 59.7 crore (up 61.6%). Order book stood at INR 541 crore as of June/early August 2026, including orders received after June. Installations more than doubled to 24,118 systems, and 109 MW of renewable capacity was commissioned, taking the cumulative base to over 164,500 systems and 726 MW. Management reiterated FY27 revenue doubling and PAT in double digits, with the PM-KUSUM 2.0 tender expected in Q3 as the key dependency.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company reach about INR 3,000 crore revenue in the remaining three quarters?

522101|2026-06.headline: Kilburn Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to about INR117 crores with 20.1% EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance of INR700 crores kept, H2-weighted.

EBITDA rose to ₹10.89 crore at a 16.2% margin, up 640 bps YoY, driven by operating leverage, shop-floor efficiency, price increases and exits from low-margin business. Q1 PAT was normalised versus Q4, which had a one-off deferred tax gain (Q4 PAT ₹5.88 crore). Management reiterated a 20% EBITDA margin target, a capex plan of ₹30 crore for FY27 and a long-term sales CAGR aim of at least 20%.

506401|2026-06.headline: Deepak Nitrite Q1 FY27: record consolidated EBITDA of INR 554 crore (21% margin) and PAT of INR 345 crore, up 207% YoY.
506401|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 35% YoY and 22% QoQ to INR 2,592 crore, with EBITDA up 159% YoY to INR 554 crore and margin at 21% versus 11% a year ago. Phenolics delivered record EBIT of INR 418 crore at a 24% margin, while Advanced Intermediates EBIT was INR 67 crore at an 8% margin. Management said April was disrupted by a maintenance shutdown, propylene shortages and gas curtailment, so the phenol run rate of about 1 lakh tonnes applies to parts of the quarter rather than the full period. Debt funding for the INR 11,500 crore propylene-polycarbonate project has been closed, and the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.27x.

segments.name: Phenolics
segments.commentary: Record revenue of INR 1,775 crore and EBIT of INR 418 crore (24% margin), supported by stronger realisations, sustained demand and high utilisation. Management said the business is almost entirely domestic.

segments.name: Advanced Intermediates (AI)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR 804 crore and EBIT of INR 67 crore (8% margin), helped by better realisations, higher operating rates and product mix. AI export mix is about 40-50%; raw material costs stayed high for some products.

guidance_outlook: MIBK and MIBC to be commissioned with acetophenone in August 2026; the remaining projects (multipurpose agrochemical intermediates facility, etc.) are due in Q2 FY27, with commercial volumes from January.
Management aims to reach 4 lakh tonnes of phenol in the existing Deepak Phenolics asset in the short to medium term, with about INR 70-odd crore of debottlenecking capex.
Polycarbonate commissioning targeted for H2 FY28-29 and BPA a couple of months later; propylene from the PDH project is expected to support phenol volumes.

Capex: about INR 1,200 crore spent to date, another INR 1,000-1,600 crore in FY27 (figures varied in the call), and about INR 3,000 crore in FY28. Peak debt estimated at INR 8,000-8,500 crore including working capital, with D/E below 1.
capex_capacity: Ammonia-to-amines integration chain (nitric acid plant, nitration and reduction) completed and stabilised; the company says it now runs 8 products simultaneously.

Phenol capacity is about 3.5 lakh tonnes, and management says it is debottlenecking toward 4 lakh tonnes through advanced process controls. Run rate reached about 1 lakh tonnes per quarter in parts of Q1, but was not sustained through the full quarter.
MIBC pre-commissioning runs reportedly exceeded design capacity; management said it can ramp above 100% once demand comes in.
Debt for the INR 11,500 crore propylene-polycarbonate project is closed, funded 60:40 debt to equity, with the 25% equity already contributed.
demand_pricing: Management said phenol demand in India is roughly balanced with no new global capacity, and some supply is short. Imports were duty-free for most of Q1 until the government reimposed the duty.
Raw material costs were high in April, but procurement secured feedstock for continuous operations. Management said feedstock costs are competitive domestically and globally.
Freight and insurance costs rose. The company responded with CIF to FOB shifts, larger parcels, and a product reformulation for a Middle East customer that changed its hazard class.
Consolidated export mix is about 20%. AI is roughly 50-50 domestic to export; Phenolics is almost entirely domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Did phenol run rate reach 1 lakh tonnes per quarter, and how is propylene covered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1 lakh tonnes was a run rate reached in significant periods, not the full quarter, because of raw material sourcing and a short maintenance shutdown. Debottlenecking is aimed at the 4 lakh tonne mark in the short to medium term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Phenolics spread in Q1 and outlook for Q2-Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose spreads and said Deepak buys feedstock below international index levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the phenol capacity now exceed earlier maturity assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main change was confidence. Advanced process controls, costing about INR 80-100 crore cumulatively, enabled higher throughput, with INR 70-odd crore more planned for debottlenecking.

qa_highlights.question: Is the phenol supply-demand balance sound?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no new capacity, China is largely self-sufficient, demand is balanced and India is short of supply.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak debt and capex plan for the INR 11,500 crore project?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,200 crore has been spent. Peak borrowing is about INR 6,800 crore plus working capital, for total peak debt of INR 8,000-8,500 crore. Management said D/E will stay below 1x.

qa_highlights.question: Could you quantify incremental revenue and EBITDA margin from the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, but said the margin profile of new products is in line with or above the AI average.

risks_watch: Phenol throughput depends on propylene and feedstock availability; April showed how a shutdown and raw material shortage can cut volumes.
Ramp-up timing for the Q2 AI projects and the MIBC run rate; management said the alkylation and multipurpose plants slipped because of manpower and gas shortages.
Polycarbonate and BPA commissioning (H2 FY28-29) and the debt drawdown schedule.
Freight and insurance costs and the reimposed phenol import duty could change domestic realisations.
Management declined to give Phenolics spreads, AI product-level margins, and the MIBK/acetone ratio, so these remain unverified.
506401|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on the phenol and integration outlook, but guarded on spreads, margins and specific product economics, which management repeatedly declined to quantify. Timelines for the polycarbonate project and the AI ramp-up were described as on track but were given loosely.

532156|2026-06.headline: Vaibhav Global Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.7% to INR917 crore and EBITDA rose 37% to INR102 crore, but constant-currency revenue was broadly flat.
532156|2026-06.overview:
Reported revenue grew 12.7% YoY to INR917 crore, EBITDA rose 37% to INR102 crore (margin 11% vs 9.2%), and PAT rose 50% to INR56 crore. Management said reported growth was helped by favourable FX and a U.S. tariff refund of about INR38 crore, of which INR25 crore sits in other operating revenue and flows fully to gross profit and EBITDA. Excluding the refund, B2C growth in USD was largely flat, with the U.S. up 4% and U.K. flat in local currency and Germany up 6%. FY27 guidance of 9-11% revenue growth and 50-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion was reiterated.</overview>

538635|2026-06.headline: Snowman guides 10-15% top-line growth for FY27 despite war-driven volume dip; Gateway ICD volumes stagnant, DFC-JNPT link now complete.

Snowman pricing rose 5-7% on average across warehousing customers, and management guided 10-15% top-line growth across all segments. Rail EBITDA was pressured by lower double-stacking (39% vs 40-42% earlier), higher underframe and empty running, and wage and fuel inflation, with relief expected from Q2. 536974|2026-06.headline: Captain Polyplast Q1 FY27 total income rose 16.3% YoY to Rs 81.66 crore, with EBITDA margin up 99 bps to 12.07%.
536974|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of Rs 81.66 crore (+16.3% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 9.86 crore (+26.7%) and net profit of Rs 4.66 crore with diluted EPS of Rs 0.78. Management said the quarter was hit by geopolitical-driven raw material inflation but revenue growth and margin both improved. Solar EPC order wins of 1,500 pumps in the first four months were highlighted, with 800 already executed and 700 pending. Ahmedabad plant (70,000 sq ft) commenced production, and the company was listed on NSE in July 2026.

segments.name: Micro-irrigation
segments.commentary: Backbone of operations; sales network across 16 states with about 750 dealers. Management targets around Rs 600 crore of micro-irrigation business on existing capacity. Shifting mix toward commercial, non-subsidy and allied products.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Two verticals: solar water pumping (PM-KUSUM, currently only Maharashtra; empanelled in Maharashtra and Gujarat) and rooftop. Management did not quantify segment revenue or growth; said solar revenue was H2-weighted last year. Targets solar EPC contribution of 50% over next 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Blended EBITDA margin expected to improve about 10-15 bps every quarter as Ahmedabad ramps up; volume growth cited as main margin driver.
Micro-irrigation margin uplift of 1-1.5% expected once Ahmedabad is fully operational, over the next 2-3 years.
Raw material (LLDP/HDPE) prices up about 30-35% versus Jan/Feb levels after a ~50% spike at end-March; price revisions expected to be largely complete by end of Q2, with full benefit from Q3.
Central government price revision mechanism expected by end-September.
Expects working capital to improve by year end as micro-irrigation receivables are collected in H2.
capex_capacity: Ahmedabad facility (70,000 sq ft, Gujarat) commenced production; will in-house valves, connectors and accessories (about 10% of micro-irrigation system value); full replacement of outsourced components expected to take at least 2-3 years.
Existing micro-irrigation capacity across Rajkot, Kurnool and Ahmedabad can support around Rs 600 crore of business; management sees no manufacturing bottleneck.
Solar EPC is service-only; no in-house manufacturing, so growth constrained by execution rather than capacity.
Dedicated solar execution team already set up; limited incremental manpower needed in states with existing micro-irrigation teams.
demand_pricing: Solar pump orders: 500 pumps from MSEDCL in Q1 and 1,000 more in July 2026; 800 of 1,500 executed, 700 pending, expected to be completed by end of August 2026.
Solar rooftop: 60-70% of rooftop business sourced from existing micro-irrigation dealers; solar pumps largely via dedicated solar dealers.
Replacement demand in mature states (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu) currently about 10-20% of micro-irrigation demand.
Export growth said to be in line with domestic growth from a very low base; future growth to come from new customers. Africa and Latin America named as focus markets.
Other states' solar tenders expected to be floated around September; awaiting tender release.

qa_highlights.question: Dealer network and scope for expansion in under-penetrated markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 750 dealers across 16 states; no need for more dealers in existing states. Expansion focus in Northern/Eastern states (Jharkhand, West Bengal, Bihar, UP).

qa_highlights.question: Current status of 1,500 solar pump order execution?
qa_highlights.answer: 800 completed, 700 pending, expected to be completed by end of the current month.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of polymer prices and price pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material prices rose about 50% at end-March and are now up 30-35% vs Jan/Feb. Free-pricing markets have passed on increases; Gujarat revised subsidy prices; other southern states expected in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Solar pump growth outlook and share in business?
qa_highlights.answer: Expects solar EPC to reach 50% of overall business in 3 years; expansion planned to Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Karnataka and Haryana this year.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital cycle for micro-irrigation vs solar pumps?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-irrigation payment cycle 5-6 months (8-10 months in Andhra Pradesh); solar pump receivable cycle 3-4 months. Majority of working capital sits in receivables, not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmedabad facility margin benefit and ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-irrigation margin benefit of 1-1.5% when fully operational; blended margin uplift of 10-15 bps each quarter during ramp-up. Initial focus on cost efficiency, standalone sales later.

qa_highlights.question: Export growth drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Export growth similar to domestic, but from a very low base; meaningful growth requires new customers.

risks_watch: Raw material (polymer) cost inflation and pace of state price revisions, especially Tamil Nadu, Andhra and other southern states.
Working capital intensity rising in Q1-Q2; receivable cycles of 5-10 months for micro-irrigation.
Dependence on state tenders for solar pump expansion beyond Maharashtra and Gujarat; tenders expected around September.
Competitive pricing pressure in solar pumps, per management.
Execution bottleneck in solar pump installation as order book scales; export still a small base.
536974|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on volumes, order wins and margin trajectory, but cautious on near-term cash flow and tender timing. Several answers were vague on quantification (solar segment revenue, growth comparisons), and the line had multiple audio drops.
key_quotes: So for the solar rooftop business, I can say that majority of our rooftop business is coming from the existing dealer network.
So definitely from Q3, we can see the full impact of that price revision.

541403|2026-06.headline: Dollar Industries Q1 FY27: operating EBITDA up 11.4% to INR 48 crore at 11.8% margin, on price hikes and no discounting, while volume fell 1.6%.
541403|2026-06.overview: Operating income rose 1.4% YoY to INR 405 crore, with gross margin up 192 bps to 37.4% after a 4-5% calibrated price increase taken in April. Management chose not to match market discounting, so revenue growth was limited and volume declined 1.6% YoY, mainly from Dollar Man. PAT rose 22.1% to INR 26 crore and net debt fell to INR 192 crore from INR 277 crore at March 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 11-13% and operating EBITDA margin of 11.5-12.5%.

financial_highlights.value: INR 192 crore (Net debt/equity 0.20x; net debt/operating EBITDA 1.01x)

segments.name: Dollar Always (economic)
segments.commentary: 44% of revenue; volume flat YoY; ASP up from INR 47 to INR 49 after price hike.

segments.name: Dollar Man (incl. Big Boss)
segments.commentary: 38% of revenue; volume down around 3-3.5% YoY, the main driver of the overall volume decline; ASP up from INR 82 to INR 85.

segments.name: Dollar Woman (Missy)
segments.commentary: About 8% of revenue; volume up 1.5-2% YoY; ASP up from INR 100 to INR 104.

segments.name: Dollar Protect (rainwear)
segments.commentary: 5.6% of revenue; value growth 49% and volume growth 68% YoY.

segments.name: Force NXT (premium)
segments.commentary: About 4% of revenue in Q1; volume up 7% YoY but value declined on lower ASP as innerwear mix rose; overall ASP about INR 220. FY26 base INR 85-90 crore (4.5% of sales).

segments.name: Socks
segments.commentary: About 2% of sales; volume down around 7% YoY.

segments.name: Quick commerce channel
segments.commentary: 5% of revenue (vs 3.1% in Q1 FY26); value growth 59.4%, volume growth 15.1% YoY.

segments.name: E-commerce channel
segments.commentary: About 4.5% of sales per management; total e-commerce including quick commerce about 10%.

segments.name: South region
segments.commentary: Value growth 22.9%, volume growth 7.3% YoY; 8.9% of revenue vs 7.2% in Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: INR 19 crore revenue across 15 countries; value growth 16.2%, volume growth 15.5% YoY; 4.9% of revenue vs 4.2%.

segments.name: G.O.A.T (JV, D2C)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue INR 16.44 crore (+21% YoY), PAT INR 2.27 crore (13.8% margin); FY26 revenue about INR 50 crore, FY27 target INR 75 crore (management also cited 25-30% growth).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 11-13% (in one answer, a 'target of 12-13%' was cited for the ad-cost math; the internal target was described as 11-12%).
FY27 operating EBITDA margin guided at 11.5-12.5%.
Management expects the industry pricing and discounting to stabilise over the next one to two quarters.
Ad spend capped at INR 100 crore annually; ad cost expected to fall to about 5% of sales from 5.5% last year, a ~0.5% margin benefit if growth target is met.
Cash conversion cycle to fall 6-7 days vs March 2026 in FY27 and by 15-18 days over three years; target 130-135 days in three to four years.
Debt target: total debt to zero by FY28; INR 86 crore repaid in Q1 alone. No major capex commitments near term.
Lakshya Phase-2 under way to raise active retailers from about 80,000 towards 90,000 in FY27; no new states entered for now.
Force NXT expected to grow 20-25% YoY over the next 2-3 years; G.O.A.T JV targeted at INR 75 crore in FY27.
capex_capacity: No major capital expenditure commitment in the near term; capital allocation focus is free cash flow and debt reduction.
Project Lakshya: 327 distributors across 14 states as of June 2026, contributing 31% of business in Q1 FY27 (about 20-22% of distributors enrolled).
Enrolled retailers about 1,73,561 vs about 80,000 active; Phase-2 targets reactivating about 1 lakh inactive retailers.
No new states are being enrolled in Lakshya because each rollout disrupts the state for 5-6 months; UP and other large states remain unenrolled for now.
Force NXT D2C website being built, with agencies in talks; innerwear (bamboo and modal) and activewear launched under the brand.
demand_pricing: Price hikes of 4-5% taken in April 2026 across all brands; management says no further hike is planned as yarn and cotton prices have stabilised.
Volume decline attributed to customer scepticism after the price hike and intense competitor deep discounting; management chose not to match discounts.
Management says low-cost inventory contributed only a small part of the margin gain, since input prices began rising from late February.
Lakshya distributors' ROI is 17-24%; receivable days are better in Lakshya states than in non-Lakshya states.
Management noted the industry-wide price discipline is improving; Q1 volume decline was the main concern raised by analysts.

544202|2026-06.headline: Stanley Lifestyles Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR 9,935 lakhs (from 10,861 lakhs) and PAT was just INR 65 lakhs, on delayed handovers and B2B shipment disruption.
544202|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined about 8.5% YoY to INR 9,935 lakhs in Q1 FY27, driven by slower retail conversions as residential handovers slipped 12 to 18 months and by B2B billing that stalled due to West Asia freight disruption. Management said gross margin was maintained and EBITDA was INR 1,722 lakhs (17.3% margin), with PAT of INR 65 lakhs. The company opened 3 Bangalore stores and closed 4 (3 Bangalore, 1 Mumbai), entered Sri Lanka via a JV, opened a Jaipur store, and announced a store-format overhaul (Stanley Superlative Living) plus a proposed amalgamation of subsidiaries. An internal audit flagged a fraud by the company secretary, under investigation.

financial_highlights.change: Down from INR 10,861 lakhs in Q1 FY26 (about -8.5% YoY)

financial_highlights.value: Maintained (no figure given on Ind AS basis)

financial_highlights.metric: Pre-Ind AS gross margin (average, all formats)
Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin (average, all formats)

financial_highlights.value: About INR 90 lakhs per month (about 2.25% of annual revenue)
financial_highlights.change: Expected to stay roughly flat as company adds people
Up from INR 62 crores as on March 2026

segments.name: Retail (COCO and franchise)
segments.commentary: Customer inquiries and footfall are encouraging but conversions are slower as buyers (80-85% new premium/luxury home buyers) await possession. Network: 47 COCO stores, of which 35 are store-level EBITDA positive per management. FOFO franchisees are on a cash-and-carry model with no credit given.

segments.name: B2B / export
segments.commentary: Products are produced and held, but invoicing did not happen in Q1 due to freight and logistics disruption from the Middle East conflict; management called the B2B visibility the highest ever. US tariffs have stalled export talks, and the company is pinning hopes on BIS certification enforcement for imports from 14 August 2026.

segments.name: Sofas & More / Stanley Boutique / Stanley Level Next
segments.commentary: Average annual revenue per store: Sofas & More INR 4.5 to 6 crores; Stanley Boutique INR 4 to 6 crores; Stanley Level Next INR 10 to 14 crores (some stores up to INR 20 crores). Boutiques to be converted into Sofas & More over 2 to 3 years in the six metros.

guidance_outlook: Brand architecture change (3 brands into one Stanley and one Sofas & More) expected to complete in about 3 to 4 quarters; conversion of Boutiques to Sofas & More is gradual, taking 2 to 3 years.
Target of 15% to 20% YoY same-store growth for mature stores; Q1 SSSG was slightly negative due to format changes.
Store-level EBITDA break-even expected 6 to 12 months after opening; ROI (capital with interest) expected in 24 to 36 months.
Management says manufacturing can scale to about 2x current revenue by recalibrating the factory with a few added machines.
No explicit margin guidance given; corporate costs expected to stay roughly flat as the company adds people for the new formats.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity utilisation about 68% to 70%; over 1,000 skilled artisans said to be fully utilised.
Sofas & More capex about INR 2 crores per store (5,000 to 6,000 sq ft). Large single-city flagship stores (Stanley Superlative Living) capex up to INR 20 crores.
Hyderabad Jubilee Hills (Road No. 45) Superlative store said to be 2 to 3 weeks from opening; large-format plans for Mumbai, Bangalore and Delhi, with one city one mega store in four cities.
Q1 openings: 3 Bangalore stores (2 Varthur, 1 Mysore Road). Closures: 4 (3 Bangalore, 1 Mumbai); management said 2 of the Bangalore closures had already been relocated.
New stores: Stanley Boutique Colombo, Sri Lanka (July 2026, JV with Singer Sri Lanka PLC) and Sofas & More Jaipur (first Rajasthan store).
demand_pricing: Demand demand: customer inquiries and footfall encouraging, but conversions slowed as residential handovers were delayed 12 to 18 months in several projects; West Asia supply chain issues constrained construction material availability.
Stanley Superlative Living targets buyers with budgets of INR 3 to 5 crores and above, aiming for average ticket size up to about 10x current levels with full home design, build and install.
Management said 6 COCO cities (Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Delhi, Chennai and one other) account for about 80% of India's luxury housing, per company claim.
Sofas & More: about 95% of customers are direct buyers without designers or specifiers; Stanley relies more on specifiers and design-led purchases.
Export exposure is small; management said the business is mainly domestic and US tariffs have stalled talks with large US buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation about INR 15 crores per quarter (above INR 50 crores a year)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Sudhir Iyer attributed it to Ind AS accounting; IGAAP depreciation would be lower, and the charge is front-loaded in the earlier years of asset lives. He did not give asset-class detail.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company report pre-Ind AS margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said only Ind AS numbers will be published, but pre-Ind AS figures are available offline. Management then gave pre-Ind AS averages: gross margin 56% to 60%, EBITDA margin 11% to 13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the order book and B2B billing?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book stood at INR 68 crores on 30 June 2026, up from INR 62 crores at March 2026. Products are produced but cannot be invoiced until logistics clear.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Stanley Superlative Living format?
qa_highlights.answer: A large-format store in mature markets, replacing smaller Stanley stores. Management said Hyderabad is the proof of concept; the format consolidates Boutique and Level Next. Sofas & More becomes the value-premium brand.

qa_highlights.question: How many COCO stores are store-level EBITDA positive?
qa_highlights.answer: 35 of 42 mature COCO stores are EBITDA positive, after cash rent (the answer refers to 42 stores out of 47 total). Break-even takes 6 to 12 months and ROI 24 to 36 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are same-store sales growth and mature store revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 mature-store SSSG was slightly negative due to format changes; target is 15% to 20% YoY. Average annual revenue: Sofas & More about INR 5 crores, Boutique INR 4 to 5 crores, Level Next about INR 10 crores plus.

513472|2026-06.headline: Simplex Castings Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 35% YoY to ₹60.95 crore and PAT rose about 45% to ₹6.86 crore, with near-term order book at ~₹150 crore.
513472|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations was ₹60.95 crore, up about 35% YoY from ₹45.21 crore and up 11% QoQ from ₹54.76 crore. EBITDA rose about 25% YoY to ₹11.52 crore, with margin of 18.89%, and PAT rose about 45% YoY to ₹6.86 crore (PAT margin 11.25% vs 10.48%). Management said the near-term order book has expanded to roughly ₹150 crore+ from a historical ₹80–100 crore range. Management guided to ~₹300 crore FY27 revenue and ~₹500 crore by FY28, and flagged working capital reduction as a FY27 transition priority.</overview>

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Not yet contributing; management targets more than ₹100 crore next year from railway business, including casted bogies (~200 per month capacity conditional on wagon orders) and fabricated locomotive bogies at Tedesara expected at ₹60–70 crore turnover.

segments.name: Power sector fabrication
segments.commentary: No power/BHL orders in last year; management targets ~₹100 crore from power sector next year via orders secured through RXIL with BHL and L&T.

segments.name: Shipbuilding (Mazgaon Dock)
segments.commentary: First order of 5 sets about ₹4.5 crore; 3 sets already cast and first offered for inspection. A further pipeline order is about ₹8 crore.

segments.name: Steel and metallurgical
segments.commentary: Steel is the core market; management says ~₹300 crore of FY27 revenue will be fed by steel sector. Non-ferrous is about 20% of order book.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Target 5–10% of business in FY27 (with shipbuilding, 10–15%), working first with one ordnance factory (Khamaria, Jabalpur); not expected to grow 20–30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance ~₹300 crore; management says ₹60 crore done in Q1 and balance ~₹150 crore order book to be executed in FY27, plus pipeline orders by March.

Revenue target of ~₹500 crore by FY28; management says the current fundraise is sufficient to reach this, and expansion beyond existing two units (~₹300–350 crore capacity) will come via organic or inorganic routes.
Capacity utilisation currently 50–60%, targeted at least 80% by end of FY28.
Working capital: FY27 described as transition year; target operating cycle of 60–70 days by FY28 from about 100–120 days today.
Fabrication capacity expansion of 1,500 tons per month (~18,000 tons annual) versus ~6,000 tons currently being done, implying an addition of 6,000–8,000 tons.
EPC business to be restarted selectively: order sizes ₹100–150 crore, ~2-year execution, minimum margin 15–20%, targeting about ₹100 crore annual revenue, funded from bank limits and accruals.
capex_capacity: Capex in progress at Tedesara (Rajnandgaon) unit, expected to complete in FY27; CWIP about ₹30 crore incl. working capital.
Fabrication expansion: 1,500 tons per month capacity addition, roughly 18,000 tons per year, for power and fabricated bogies.
Foundry is debottlenecking only: one CNC machine at ₹4–5 crore plus conveyors and cranes; machine moulding plant only on drawing board.
Capacity utilisation 50–60% currently; targeted 80% by end FY28.
Future capacity beyond current two units is not yet committed; management says investments will be funded from internal accruals, not new borrowings.
demand_pricing: Order book near-term ~₹150 crore+; management intends to keep it at ₹100–150 crore to limit liquidated damages (typically capped at 5%, some up to 10%).

Working capital: product mix shift at Unit 1 toward fast-moving, shorter-cycle products; Unit 3 to follow. Railway bogie cycle 30–45 days; RXIL and Invoice Mart discounting payments in ~30–35 days after dispatch at ~5–5.5% discount rate.
Steel demand supported by ArcelorMittal expansions (two in Odisha, one in Andhra Pradesh); management says steel boom expected to last 4–5 years.
Non-ferrous and metallurgical (Balco, Vedanta, Hindustan Zinc, Nalco, Aditya Birla) about 20% of order book.
Competition from Shyam Metalics and Rungta also expanding; management says Simplex is one of few large players in Bhilai.

qa_highlights.question: Current capacity utilisation and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Running at roughly 50–60%; targeting at least 80% by end of next financial year, with gradual increase starting this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is ₹300 crore FY27 revenue guidance on track?
qa_highlights.answer: ₹60 crore done in Q1, with ~₹150 crore order book to execute in FY27 and pipeline orders to come by March; management said ₹300 crore is in line.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital fall from 60–90 days (or 100–120 days) to target levels, and what is the margin cost of invoice discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Shift to railway bogies (30–45 day cycle, payment upfront from wagon builders) and RXIL/Invoice Mart (30–35 days post dispatch). Discounting costs about 5–5.5%. Management said ₹300 crore revenue would need only about ₹50 crore working capital at 60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins fall as railway and power fabrication (tender-based) grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management conceded railway and power fabrication will be at similar margins to today, not higher; margin uplift will come from selecting more complex, niche products.

qa_highlights.question: Is the fundraise sufficient to reach ₹500 crore, and any further borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current fundraise is sufficient for the ₹500 crore projection; further expansion will be funded only from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: Green hydrogen DRI project status?
qa_highlights.answer: Project closed. Grant of ~₹160 crore was subject to GST (~₹30–35 crore) because of IP and asset-sharing conditions; the reissued tender required an operating DRI plant, so Simplex did not bid.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term opportunities beyond ₹500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to detail; areas mentioned include machine tool castings, defence and possible technology JVs or acquisitions; management reiterated no concrete plans yet.

542812|2026-06.headline: GFL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24% YoY to INR 1,588 crore and PAT more than doubled QoQ to INR 219 crore on R32-led fluorochemicals growth.
542812|2026-06.overview: Chemical segment revenue grew 23% YoY to INR 1,574 crore with EBITDA up 29% to INR 458 crore and segment PAT up 33% to INR 261 crore. Fluorochemicals was the standout, with revenue up 52% YoY and 44% QoQ on R32 sales, and existing R32 capacity is already at peak utilisation. Battery materials remain pre-revenue to small (INR 20-30 crore per quarter cited by an analyst), with a ramp promised from Q4 FY27 and a significant step-up in FY28. The Oman battery project has been put on hold and its capex is being moved to India, and the approved sovereign funding for Oman will not transfer.

financial_highlights.change: +24% YoY; +39% QoQ; margin 27% vs 22% in Q4 FY26
+19% YoY; PAT margin 14% vs 7% in Q4 FY26
+29% YoY; +30% QoQ; margin 29% vs 26% in Q4 FY26
-43 days vs 192 days in Q4 FY26

segments.name: Fluoropolymers
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 15% YoY and 8% QoQ, driven by mix shift to higher-value grades and new-age applications (semiconductors, data centres, green hydrogen, batteries). Management guides 15-20% (later 17-20%) annual growth.

segments.name: Fluorochemicals (R32 and refrigerants)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 52% YoY and 44% QoQ, mainly R32. Existing R32 capacity is fully utilised; a R32 expansion (about 20,000 t total capacity cited by an analyst) is due in Q2 FY27. R134A is on track for commissioning in FY27.

segments.name: Bulk chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11% YoY and 1% QoQ, primarily on better realisations; described as steady.

segments.name: Battery materials
segments.commentary: LiPF6 has nearly completed qualification and is in its growth phase; PVDF qualification is close; LFP and cathode active material revenue expected toward end-FY27. Current revenue is small, with dispatches on CIF terms recognised in the next quarter.

guidance_outlook: R32 capacity expansion to be commissioned in Q2 FY27; management expects full utilisation of the incremental R32 capacity in calendar 2027.
R134A capacity to be commissioned in FY27 (management said it is targeting earlier than year-end); capacity size not yet disclosed.
Battery materials: management says it is on track for a 3-digit INR crore quarterly revenue in Q4 FY27, with significant ramp-up in FY28 and full potential from FY28 onwards.
Gross block of INR 836 crore expected to rise to about INR 1,200 crore by end-FY27 as CWIP is capitalised.
FY27 capex plan held at about INR 2,300 crore in EV/battery and about INR 800 crore in chemicals; total announced plan of INR 6,000 crore over the next two years.
AHF (anhydrous hydrofluoric acid) capacity to come in phases, first set by end-FY27 or Q3, mainly for captive use.
capex_capacity: R32 capacity expansion due Q2 FY27; existing R32 capacity at peak utilisation.
R134A brownfield project at an existing refrigerant site, to be commissioned in FY27; TCE feedstock to be imported, not backward integrated.

Oman battery materials project (about USD 216 million capex) put on hold; capex being redirected to India. Sovereign funding of about INR 1,200 crore approved for Oman will not be available for India.
Land for battery expansion available at the existing Dahej B (Jolva) site; a second Dahej site is being added for FY27-end/FY28.
Fluoropolymer debottlenecking is done continuously, roughly every second quarter; new-age fluoropolymer capex sized in the previous quarter at about INR 250 crore.
demand_pricing: Fluoropolymer price increases were marginal and pass-through of input cost increases (methanol, sulfur, oil-linked inputs since March 2026); management said formula-based contracts protect margins.
R32 is sold globally: about 40-50% under long-term contracts, remainder spot or contract-to-contract. Domestic and export pricing described as 'very close'.
Management said 3M's exit is past and it has taken the impact; AGC's announced UK facility shutdown has begun generating customer enquiries, with traction expected in a quarter or two.
Domestic BESS demand projected at 220-250 GWh by 2030 (versus earlier global ~1,800 GWh view).

qa_highlights.question: Have Chinese peers' fluoropolymer price increases been passed on by GFL, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Kapil Malhotra said only a marginal increase was taken to recover input costs; growth is mainly from higher-value grades where competition with Chinese players is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth visible for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said it is absolutely visible; new fluoropolymer capacity is nearly fully utilised and further capacity will be added for semiconductor and battery applications, without disclosing specifics.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Oman funding shortfall require a fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said fundraising is ongoing and project-by-project; he does not see funding as a constraint for India capacity.

qa_highlights.question: How is fluoropolymer growth split between volume, price and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split it precisely, saying growth is primarily mix (higher grades) plus volume from new fluoropolymers, not price.

qa_highlights.question: Will R32 capacity be fully utilised in calendar 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said full utilisation is expected as capacity is commissioned, based on contracts and market understanding.

risks_watch: Oman project shift to India: loss of about INR 1,200 crore sovereign funding for that project and need for new funding of about INR 4,000 crore for battery chemicals.

R32 and R134A quota allocation under the formula (baseline and production over 2024-26) is not yet clear; management declined to say which new players will receive quota. An analyst also raised a question on consumption quota that management could not answer and will follow up on.
Battery materials revenue remains small; ramp is contingent on customer qualification (about 1.5 years stabilisation cited) and CIF-term revenue timing.
Standalone-to-consolidated revenue gap widening sequentially, which management attributed to CIF consignments booked in Germany and US subsidiaries.
Raw material cost volatility (sulfur, fluorspar, methanol) with only formula-based or marginal pass-through in fluoropolymers.

544081|2026-06.headline: Jyoti CNC Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 37% to INR509 crore, but consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 23.4% on Huron revenue deferral.
544081|2026-06.overview:
Standalone revenue grew 37% YoY to INR509 crore with adjusted EBITDA margin of 28.4% and PAT of INR88 crore (17.2% margin). Consolidated revenue was INR508.5 crore (+24% YoY), but Huron revenue was deferred because the company moved from percentage-of-completion to recognising revenue only on dispatch, citing end-user certificate and export licence delays. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA was INR119 crore (23.4%) after a INR10 crore unrealised forex loss; reported EBITDA was INR109 crore (21.4%). Management guided to 25-30% top-line growth and about 25% EBITDA margin for FY27, with the 10,000-machine expansion due by end-September.</overview>
