segments.name: Standalone (Jyoti India)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR509 crore (+37% YoY), adjusted EBITDA margin 28.4%, PAT INR88 crore. Management says standalone margin was about 27.5% after Huron effect. Demand from general engineering, automotive, EMS, defence and precision engineering.

segments.name: Huron (Germany, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Produced about EUR6.5 million of machines in Q1 but billed about EUR3 million; roughly INR35 crore of revenue deferred versus Q1 FY26 (about INR70 crore). Management says costs are fully booked, so the gap hits margin. Recognition moved from percentage-of-completion to dispatch-based.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 25-30%; EBITDA margin guided around 25%, which management says it is committed to.
Huron FY27 revenue expected at INR300-325 crore, with Huron EBITDA margin of 8-10%; management says Huron will be PAT positive this year.
Standalone FY27 capex about INR200-225 crore against a total expansion target of about INR450 crore for the new capacity; management said capex will not touch INR300 crore.
Debt to stay at about March 2026 levels; management targets net debt not above 2x EBITDA. OCF for FY27 expected at about 50% of EBITDA.
Order book expected to reach INR2,500-3,000 crore by year-end; FY27 machine volume expected above 8,000 units.
capex_capacity: New 10,000-machine-per-year facility targeted to commence operations by end-September 2026; machine shop, sheet metal and paint shop buildings ready or near completion, with foundry about one month late (October).
Current capacity 6,000 machines per year; 5,550 machines built in FY26; Q1 FY27 utilisation 86%.
Management cites a targeted INR450 crore capex for the new capacity and says it is on track.
CNC controller: HMI ready; commercialisation expected in about two years; PLI application filed with capital subsidy about 25% central plus matching state support (about 50% total).
Raw material and inventory built up over the past nine months to support the ramp-up; management expects working capital and inventory to improve after the new facility is operational.
demand_pricing: Order book INR4,848 crore; mix: aerospace and defence 38%, general engineering 20%, automotive 19%, EMS 13%, die and mould 4%.
Q1 revenue mix: aerospace and defence 37%, automotive 35%, general engineering 17%, EMS 6%, other 5%.
Blended realisation about INR34.56 lakh per machine in Q1 FY27 vs INR34.41 lakh in Q1 FY26; management expects the range to hold.
Management says the Rajkot unit booked more than 250 machines in July and that the company crossed 1,000 machines in one month in the domestic market.

India imports about 60-62% of machine tool demand, mainly from Japan, Europe and South Korea. New NX double-column machine targets railway, commercial vehicles, infra, power and heavy engineering, with 6m model launched and 8m and 10m in development.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Huron's accounting change and what drove the revenue gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says end-user certificates (EUC) and export licences now take longer, and auditors apply a conservative dispatch-based approach. Revenue will return to POCM once EUC is received; the company says it can book POCM if EUC arrives within 3 months of order. Around 7-8 machines across multiple orders are pending, and management expects clearance in one batch.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an impairment risk if the Huron investigation drags on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no impairment risk ("Not at all").

qa_highlights.question: Will the Huron revenue shortfall reverse in the coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 dispatches to improve, but says large machines have long lead times, so the bulk should come in Q3 and Q4. Management said the company should be judged on an annual basis, not quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex and debt plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone capex of INR200-225 crore for FY27 against a INR450 crore expansion total. Debt is expected to stay flat versus March; management targets net debt not above 2x EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost rise and why was it not capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs were booked to P&L because the new capacity has already been put to use (building and components), so capitalisation was not applied.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected FY27 Huron margin and does it reach PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Huron FY27 revenue expected at INR300-325 crore with EBITDA margin of 8-10%; management said Huron is PAT positive this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sequential margin decline explained by Huron alone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes; it pointed to the same standalone business at about 27.5% margin in Q1.

500330|2026-06.headline: Raymond Q1 FY27 consolidated total income rose 13% to INR628 crores, with EBITDA up 14% to INR100 crores at a 15.9% margin.
500330|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income reached INR628 crores (up 13% YoY) and EBITDA reached INR100 crores (up 14% YoY) at a 15.9% margin, versus 15.7% a year earlier. Aerospace (JKMGAL) revenue grew 40% to INR123 crores, but its EBITDA margin fell to 21.2% from 23.7% because R&D for new programmes was expensed in the quarter. Precision Technology and Auto Components (JKMPTL) revenue grew 11% to INR444 crores, with EBITDA up 46% to INR61 crores and margin expanding to 13.8% from 10.6%, driven by export ramp-up and operating leverage. Management reiterated a 25% organic growth commitment for aerospace and plans for an aftermarket business launching in Q2 FY27 and a greenfield facility in Andhra Pradesh targeting commercial production in late 2027.

financial_highlights.change: +13% YoY (vs INR555 crores in Q1 FY26)
+14% YoY (vs INR87 crores in Q1 FY26)
Company stated it remains net debt-free

segments.name: Aerospace & Defence (JKMGAL)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR123 crores (+40% YoY) and EBITDA INR26 crores at 21.2% margin, down from 23.7%, due to expensed R&D for new programmes. Order book of INR5,960 crores over 10 years and RFQ pipeline of INR1,632 crores; mass production of precision defence components has commenced.

segments.name: Precision Technology & Auto Components (JKMPTL)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR444 crores (+11% YoY), led by export ramp-up, with EBITDA INR61 crores at 13.8% margin (vs 10.6%). Automotive aftermarket product line scheduled for launch in Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Aerospace: committed 25% organic growth for the year; management said it is slightly ahead of that in Q1.
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to follow the current trend, per management's answer on FY27 margins (analyst had cited a 12-13% range).
Aerospace mature EBITDA margin target around 25%; precision manufacturing around 12-13% in the near and medium term.
Andhra Pradesh greenfield facility (Gudipalli, near Bangalore Airport) targeted for commercial production in late 2027; up to 6 months of approvals, so meaningful revenue from FY28.
Existing aerospace facility now expected to exceed the earlier INR600 crore revenue estimate, per the Parivartan improvement programme.
Asset turns on new business: aerospace about 1.8-2.2x, automotive about 2-2.5x; ROCE expected to be broadly maintained.
Aftermarket business for automotive components and white-label products to roll out in Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: INR1,000 crore five-year capex plan: INR510 crores for aerospace and INR430 crores for auto; management says it is progressing on schedule.
Greenfield Andhra Pradesh facility (Gudipalli, near Bangalore Airport) groundwork on track; commercial production targeted for late 2027.
Setting up an advanced training and production facility near the greenfield site ahead of schedule for pre-launch readiness.
Plans to add special processes such as heat treatment at the Andhra facility to increase vertical integration.
Current aerospace order book relates only to the existing facility; new capacity is over a year away.
demand_pricing: Aerospace demand described as well ahead of supply; management said supply chain constraints (titanium, alloys) eased in Q1 but cited a large backlog.
Export revival for auto components helped by the India-UK CETA (in force 15 July 2026) and the rollback of US tariffs; Tier 1 buyers rebuilding inventory.
Aerospace customer concentration: over 25 global customers, with top 3 at about 40-45% of the business. Management aims to widen this to 8-10 high-value customers.
Input costs rising: logistics, carbide and HSS tooling, and minimum wage increases. Some costs are being passed to customers; management expects some quarterly pressure.
Management said it had N4 self-certification and that engine-critical parts are the core; it is not yet in N1 (rotating parts).

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise equity for inorganic deals after the warrant issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it keeps evaluating inorganic opportunities across aerospace, auto components and defence; the warrants give flexibility, and it will update only when deals are close.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company exposed to aerospace casting and forging supply bottlenecks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not exposed as much because critical-part programmes have not yet transferred; the constraint is seen as an execution advantage.

qa_highlights.question: Will consolidated EBITDA margins stay around 12-13% in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the same trend as shown in Q1 at consolidated level, with margins better than last year.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the 10-year aerospace order book versus the earlier 5-year figure?
qa_highlights.answer: The change was made to give longer visibility; the 5-year breakup summed to about INR2,765 crores versus INR2,350 crores last quarter, which an analyst computed as about 17% QoQ growth, and management confirmed this. The INR5,960 crore book covers only the existing facility.

qa_highlights.question: How much can the existing facility produce, and what is the timeline for the new facility revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing facility is expected to exceed the earlier INR600 crore estimate under the Parivartan programme. New facility revenue starts in FY28 after up to 6 months of approvals.

qa_highlights.question: What are asset turns and long-term margin targets by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Aerospace new business asset turns of 1.8-2.2x and auto 2-2.5x. Long-term EBITDA margin targets are about 25% for aerospace and 12-13% for precision manufacturing.

risks_watch: Aerospace margin (21.2%, down 2.5 pp YoY) depends on R&D write-offs and product maturity; management expects stabilisation as programmes move to steady state.
Rising input costs (tooling, logistics, wages) may compress margins for a quarter before pass-through or efficiency offsets.
Customer concentration: top 3 aerospace customers at about 40-45%.
Greenfield ramp depends on customer approvals (up to 6 months); late 2027 start with FY28 revenue impact.
Inorganic deals are not yet identified, and the warrant issue means possible dilution if deals close.
Medical certification obtained, but no business plan yet; defence strategy under development after hiring a former BEL executive.

532749|2026-06.headline: Allcargo Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.2% YoY to INR546 crores and PAT turned to a INR14 crore profit from a Q1 FY26 loss.
532749|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR546 crores, up 11.2% YoY and 6.2% QoQ, with gross profit of INR163 crores (+11.6% YoY) and EBITDA of INR71 crores (+39.2% YoY). Express volumes grew 6.7% YoY to 312,000 tonnes and realisation per tonne rose 6.4%, with management attributing much of the yield gain to natural escalation from service-quality improvement and only about 20% to diesel pass-through. Consultative Logistics revenue grew 6.1% YoY on a stable 7.5 million sq ft of warehouse space under management. Management reiterated a 3-year plan targeting Express EBITDA margin of 10% and a company-level EBITDA margin of about 13% this year.

financial_highlights.change: Within 28%-29% range over Q4 and Q1 per CFO
Includes about INR8 crores one-off from lease closure; normal run-rate about INR5 crores

segments.name: Express Logistics
segments.commentary: Volumes up 6.7% YoY to 312,000 tonnes; realisation per tonne up 6.4%; revenue up 13.5% YoY. Gross margin 26.3% and EBITDA margin about 6.2%, against a 10% three-year target.

segments.name: Consultative Logistics
segments.commentary: Warehouse space under management stable at 7.5 million sq ft; revenue up 6.1% YoY and 6.3% QoQ. Revenue per sq ft up 3%; EBITDA margin about 29.56%; customer retention 98%.

guidance_outlook: Company-level EBITDA margin expected around 13% for FY27, implying about 1 percentage point annual improvement over three years (confirmed by CFO).
Express EBITDA margin trajectory: 7.5% targeted this year and 10% in the three-year plan; management said it is 'inching up' from 6.2%.
Pre-Ind AS operating PBT margin guided to 5%-6% this year and to improve thereafter.
Growth ambition: grow 1 percentage point above logistics industry growth; industry estimated at low double digits (1.2x-1.5x GDP of 6%-7%).
Price realisation actions expected to continue into Q2 FY27, with diesel pass-through impact seen fully from Q2.
Consultative Logistics revenue to grow slightly faster than Express, per management.
Capex: INR10-15 crores for Express infrastructure improvements; about INR20 crores additional capex for Consultative Logistics this year.
capex_capacity: Express: constant infrastructure improvements of INR10-15 crores; hubs described as well capitalised.
Consultative Logistics: about INR20 crores additional capex this year, tied to new business and warehouse additions.
Warehouse space under management at 7.5 million sq ft in Q1 FY27 (about 8 million sq ft earlier in the year per Q&A); two large warehouses were consolidated to reduce white space.
Express fleet and network: about 95% road and 5% air; capacity utilisation and lane planning cited as cost levers.
demand_pricing: Express realisation up 6.4% YoY; management attributes most (about 80%) to natural escalation from service-level improvement and about 20% to diesel pass-through, with DPH mechanism passed through since June.
Labour cost inflation from minimum wage hikes is passed through in CL and Express contracts; annual GPI exercise applied.
Express KEA share about 60%-63% of revenue, retail about 20%, strategic balance; reclassification prevents direct comparison with earlier 80:20 split.
E-commerce and quick commerce: CL runs sort and fulfilment centres for majors; Express does not do last-mile for e-commerce.
Industry view: Express industry growth low double digits; shift from unorganised to organised players cited as a driver.
Q1 FY27 macro indicators cited: June e-way bills about 137 million (+14.5% YoY), GST collections near INR2 lakh crores (+14%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Express EBITDA margin and what are the levers to expand it?
qa_highlights.answer: Express EBITDA margin about 6.2% vs CL at 29.56%, giving the blended 13%. Yield enhancement is the main lever; cost and operating efficiency add further. Three-year target is 10%, with 7.5% targeted this year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the 24-month priorities and capital allocation policy after the demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth 1 percentage point above industry, with margin improvement across gross, EBITDA and PAT. Express is well capitalised (INR10-15 crores capex); CL needs about INR20 crores this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Express gross margin base change versus earlier disclosures?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY26 figures reflected pre-merger Allcargo Gati numbers. Post the merger effective 1 November, prior quarters were recast to include CL aggregation, so the margin trajectory is around 30% from Q3 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the realisation increase is diesel versus natural escalation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split the 6.3%-6.4% number precisely; roughly 80% natural escalation and 20% diesel pass-through. Diesel pass-through effective June, with full impact in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why has CL warehouse space declined over the last three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes are not impacted; two large warehouses were actioned to reduce white space, lowering cost without affecting revenue capability.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company focus more on CL given its margin and EBITDA contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both businesses get focus; CL revenue growth will be slightly faster than Express while balancing profitability of both.

risks_watch: Diesel and labour cost inflation: pass-through lags may compress margins in Q2 before full recovery.
Express EBITDA margin at about 6.2% remains far below the 10% three-year target; progress must be tracked quarterly.
Q1 PAT of INR14 crores includes about INR8 crores of one-off lease-closure income; underlying profit is lower.
CL warehouse area under management fell from about 8.4 million sq ft three quarters ago to 7.5 million sq ft; monitor volume impact.
Pre-Ind AS operating PBT margin of about 2.7% (per analyst) needs to reach 5%-6% this year.
Segment disclosure: analysts requested air/surface split and pre- vs post-Ind AS EBITDA bridge; not provided on the call. KEA classification changed, so historic comparisons are limited.
532749|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on volume, pricing and CL retention, with a clear 3-year margin plan. Evasive on the KEA/strategic reclassification and on the exact diesel versus natural-escalation split, and it did not provide a segment EBITDA bridge.

532493|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue was modest at INR182 crore, while a INR2,205 crore HAL Uttam Radar order lifted the total order book to about INR4,300 crore.
532493|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 as modest on revenue and profitability, blaming customer approval delays and last-stage technical issues that it expects to normalise in coming quarters. Q1 order inflow was INR185 crore, in line with guidance. The July receipt of the INR2,205 crore HAL Uttam Radar subsystem order (about INR1,870 crore ex-GST) roughly doubled the order book. Management reiterated FY27 revenue of about INR1,350 crore (guided as more than 15-20% growth) and flagged a planned demerger of the Space and Weather divisions from April 1, 2027.

financial_highlights.change: Described as modest; no YoY figure given in call

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone order book at quarter end
Consolidated order book at quarter end
financial_highlights.change: Includes about INR244 crore of service orders

financial_highlights.metric: Order book after July HAL Uttam Radar win (as stated)
financial_highlights.change: Uttam order roughly doubled the book

segments.name: Defence (Uttam Radar, HAL)
segments.commentary: Largest order in company history: about INR2,205 crore from HAL for critical subsystems for Uttam Radar, with a 5-year execution window. Phase 1 of 12 numbers due by September 2027, about 14 months from order date.

segments.name: Space, Metrology and Hydrology
segments.commentary: About 34% of the standalone order book. Management guided INR120-150 crore of FY27 revenue from space. Space and Weather is to be demerged as a separate listed entity, with first-year standalone revenue guided at INR300-plus crore and at least 18-20% PBT margin.

segments.name: Joint venture (Astra Rafael Comsys)
segments.commentary: Order book INR836 crore; FY27 booking target INR360 crore. Management expects INR500-750 crore of further ARC orders over the forecast period.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target about INR1,350 crore, plus or minus INR25 crore; growth stated as more than 15%, with 15-20% given in Q&A.
FY28 revenue about INR1,600 crore, plus or minus INR50 crore, with growth of 15-18%.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR1,600 crore, excluding the Uttam order; management said it may be improved over the next few quarters.
Over 5 years, management expects at least 6-7x FY26 revenue. It sees order intake of INR8,000-9,000 crore over 3-4 years, excluding chip sales, counter-UAV, EM wall, exports and BrahMos NG.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be similar to FY26, with a positive delta increase; no long-term margin guidance given.
Management said it expects the Q3 and Q4 working capital position to be broadly similar to FY26, and it has no plan to dilute equity for working capital.
capex_capacity: Uttam Radar: Phase 1 of 12 numbers due by September 2027; roughly 25+ numbers per year thereafter; management said total quantity could be executed by FY31.
Own satellite to be launched within the first 6 months after the Space and Weather entity lists; part of a planned satellite constellation.
Management said production lines and teams are fully ready for large-scale execution; investment in automated process engineering and infrastructure is ongoing.
Migration to SAP/HANA completed; standalone accounting for the space business has run from the start of the year.
Two complete radars of own IP and one drone-mounted electronic intelligence product are targeted for around Diwali 2026.
demand_pricing: AMCA AAAU: company is L1 and BEL is L2 for the active antenna array unit development, with a contract expected in about a month. Management did not disclose the quantum; the AMCA radar DcPP RFP has 3 shortlisted consortium partners.

Tejas Mk1A EW: AATRU subsystem already qualified; the EW suite is in final qualification, after which production orders follow. Management expects about INR500-600 crore of additional orders from these programmes.
Su-30 upgrades (Virupaksha, Angad): Tier 1 radar and Tier 2 EW role; management expects about INR3,000 crore of orders over the forecast period.
QRSAM: expects INR700-800 crore of orders for the first 3 regiments; part of the existing INR4,300 crore book is expected before year-end.
Shatrughat and Samaghat (P-75I): management expects INR100-120 crore of production orders from BEL for the two programmes combined.
BrahMos: supplies gimbal-based RF seeker components and telemetry products; a new-generation (NG) seeker is in development. Upside from NG is not in the order inflow projections.
Exports: a couple of BTS orders executed and prototypes given for qualification; MMIC component leads from US and Europe, with sizable orders possibly taking about 2 more years.

qa_highlights.question: Which top-line growth target is correct: 10-15% (press release) or 15-20% (presentation)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the correct target is in excess of 15%, i.e. 15-20% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the year-end order book target?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding Uttam, management reiterated order booking of about INR1,600 crore for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is EW (Tejas, Su-30) and LCH content in the order inflow projections?
qa_highlights.answer: Angad and some LCH subsystems are included in the 4-year projections. Tejas Mk1A is additional, around INR500-600 crore. Management said none of the EM wall or counter-UAV revenue is in its numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to positive cash at the end of FY26, which kept overdraft utilisation in Q1 minimal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Uttam execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall execution is about 5 years, with total completion before FY32 and possibly by FY31; Phase 1 of 12 numbers is due by September 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What margin guidance is available for new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to margins, citing product mix and lifecycle economics. It expects margins to be as healthy as the current business, or nearly so.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 6-7x five-year revenue target based on the defence business only?
qa_highlights.answer: The order visibility excludes space, apart from the existing book. Management said the 6-7x is against the combined FY26 base of INR1,057 crore, since the demerger has not yet happened.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 revenue decline and was there deferred revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited inspection and specification-proof delays, development-cycle issues and supply-chain issues that pushed some programmes out of Q1. It expects Q3 and Q4 to be stronger and said quarterly numbers are internal estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital moderate further in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant change versus FY26 is expected; Q1 and early Q2 are seasonally better and pressure rises in Q3 and Q4. Management ruled out equity dilution for working capital.

544921|2026-06.headline: Arcil Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 107% to INR143 crores on INR1,066 crores recoveries (up 151%), with acquisitions seasonally light at INR353 crores.
544921|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a recovery-led quarter: total recoveries rose 151% to INR1,066 crores and standalone PAT more than doubled to INR143 crores, driven by a large corporate resolution. Acquisitions were INR353 crores (Arcil share INR143 crores), about INR150 crores lower than Q1 FY26, consistent with the seasonal pattern where most acquisitions occur in Q4. AUM was INR19,574 crores (up 16% YoY) and borrowings fell sequentially to INR1,100 crores, with management expecting to draw down more in the coming quarters. Consolidated PAT was INR59 crores versus standalone INR143 crores, and management urged investors to assess the company on a standalone and full-year basis.

financial_highlights.change: +151% vs INR425 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Write-back of security receipts, fees and expenses written off earlier

financial_highlights.change: +107% YoY; PAT margin about 52% of total income
From INR1,200 crores in March 2026; debt-equity 0.34x
About INR150 crores lower than Q1 FY26
Relates to receivables expected to be realised near term
Per analyst question; not stated by management

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: About 68% of AUM and a corporate book of about INR13,000 crores; recoveries are chunky and event-driven, which drove the Q1 spike.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: About 24% of AUM; over 3.29 million retail borrowers on the platform, with steady granular repayments. Retail and SME rose from about 21% to 31% of AUM since March 2024.

segments.name: SME
segments.commentary: About 8% of AUM; management treats SME as an independent business it wants to grow.

segments.name: Collection as a service
segments.commentary: Still at infrastructure-build and proof-of-concept stage with own assets and a few NBFCs; no revenue or pipeline numbers given.

guidance_outlook: No numerical AUM or acquisition guidance; management expects AUM to rise while acquisitions are matched by equal resolutions, with resolutions of about 20-25% of opening AUM each year.
Management expects acquisitions to rise through Q2 and Q3, with pipelines described as strong, and to draw down more borrowings and marginally increase leverage.
Write-backs of previously written-off assets are expected to decline over time; maximum write-offs over the next three years are cumulatively under INR100 crores.
Management expects its fee income momentum to be maintained, though it said the Q1 write-back was not a full-year trend.
capex_capacity: Borrowings were reduced to INR1,100 crores in Q1 to fund acquisitions later in the year; cash and bank balances INR252 crores, which management says gives ample capacity to fund acquisitions.

Own investment in AUM was about INR4,200 crores (about 22% of AUM) as of June; the FY26 average investment ratio was about 33% (INR2,000 crores on INR6,000 crores acquired), and Q1 FY27 is running at about 40%.
Mandatory minimum SR investment is 15%; co-investor deals allow as low as 2.5%.
Last-mile funding of up to 25% of acquired loan value is available to support turnarounds.
demand_pricing: Industry stress (banks and NBFCs, including SMA, NPA and written-off) is about INR23 lakh crores per management, growing about INR1 lakh crore a year; ARCs participate in roughly 10%.
Special mention accounts were about 30% of new ARC acquisitions in FY25, up from about 14% in FY24 (CRISIL data cited by management).
Acquisition cost held at 26-27% of dues every year; Arcil's AUM is about 14% of the INR1.4 lakh crore dues under management.
Arcil's share of industry AUM rose from 11% to 15% over two years; share of new acquisitions was 17% in FY26 on about INR6,000 crores acquired.
Management attributed improved industry recovery rates (cited as moving from about 35% to about 85%) to a stronger economy and real estate recovery.

543714|2026-06.headline: Landmark Cars Q1 FY27 pro forma revenue grew over 22% YoY to a record Q1, with PAT nearly doubling; EBITDA margin about 5.8%.
543714|2026-06.overview: Management reported its best-ever Q1 on pro forma revenue from operations, up over 22% YoY in a seasonally soft quarter, with PAT nearly doubling. Management attributed roughly 19 percentage points of growth to volume and about 3 points to OEM price hikes. Management said it will judge the business on EBITDA, PAT and cash profit rather than gross profit, given the mix shift toward newer brands with different margin structures. Q&A covered EV aftersales economics, the ChargeZone charging partnership, workshop capacity (expressed in bays rather than outlet count), rental costs and cost efficiency. Management gave no numeric quantification for the ChargeZone revenue share or for FY28 profit targets.

financial_highlights.change: +22% YoY (approx. 19 pts volume, ~3 pts price per management ballpark)
roughly similar to last two years, per CFO

financial_highlights.value: almost INR60 crore in Q1 FY27
INR27 crore for the quarter; rental cost roughly INR25 crore; Ind AS lease impact about INR2 crore
about 0.95x last year as stated by CFO

financial_highlights.metric: Share of EVs in vehicles sold by value

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR79 lakh in Q1 FY27
financial_highlights.change: up from INR73 lakh in Q4 FY26

segments.name: New vehicle sales
segments.commentary: New vehicle sales margin trend cited by analyst at 1.7% in FY25, 2.0% in FY26 and 2.3% now; management said price hikes give a one-time benefit and demand above supply reduces freebies. Management expects a normalised ~1.5% EBITDA margin on pro forma new car sales in Q2-Q4 FY27 when asked.

segments.name: Aftersales
segments.commentary: Management said aftersales is growing at about 14-15% historically; EV aftersales revenue per vehicle is higher, with EV margins (ex-warranty) similar to the ~15% currently cited, and not expected to be lower. Share of aftersales from high-growth brands is 19% vs 38% of new car sales from those brands, per analyst.

segments.name: Outlets
segments.commentary: Total outlets about 141 (77 showrooms and 64 workshops per analyst's question). Management stopped classifying outlets as new a couple of quarters ago.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a more normalised and consistent demand trajectory through the later part of FY27, with no repeat of the GST-related disruption seen in Q2 FY26.
Management expects cost (employee and other expenses) as a percentage of revenue to fall further as revenue grows; no quantified target given, with a detailed number promised later.
Capex guided at around INR50 crore for the year; Q1 spend below proportionate share, with no commitment for the rest of the year.
Borrowing costs described as stable; surplus cash to be used to repay working capital loans.
Management said it is in talks with OEMs and possible takeover opportunities but will proceed on its own terms; no timeline given.
Asked about FY28 reaching FY23 peak profit levels, management declined to commit, citing macro uncertainty.
capex_capacity: Mumbai (Jogeshwari) workshop of about 50,000 sq ft inaugurated to serve Mercedes-Benz, BYD and Jeep; BYD and Jeep part due to be completed in the next few months.
New Mahindra workshop in Hyderabad to start operations soon; existing Hyderabad Mahindra capacity already exhausted, per management.
BYD outlets in Pune became operational in July 2026; two new BYD outlets opened about 7-10 days before the call.
MG network to reach 17 outlets with an LOI received for an additional Ahmedabad showroom.
Management said workshop capacity will be added in bays rather than workshop count, and smaller workshops will be consolidated into larger sites.
demand_pricing: Management said OEM price hikes (Mercedes-Benz and others) raise absolute gross profit per car, not percentage margin, since Landmark receives a percentage of the hike.
Price contributed roughly 3% of the 22-23% top-line growth; the remainder (about 19%) was volume, per management ballpark.
Mercedes-Benz sold 9,786 units in H1 CY2026, up 9% YoY; Mercedes-Benz plans over 40 new global models from 2027.
MG: new SUV launching in August expected to boost volumes; new Majestor deliveries began last quarter.

Mahindra: strong momentum with more launches to come; BYD: supply to improve through the rest of the year, hybrids later this FY; Kia: Syros EV orders healthy, new Sorento in September; Honda: City facelift, ZRV and Alpha 0 EV later this year.
Management argued that competition such as Audi's share push expands the luxury market (about 50,000 units) rather than cannibalises it.
Premium and mass segments grew faster than luxury in recent months per Aryaman Thakker.

qa_highlights.question: Will OEM price hikes improve Mercedes gross margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Thakker said price hikes raise absolute margin per car but not the percentage margin, as Landmark receives a percentage of the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Could Audi's share push pressure Mercedes sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new entrants expand the luxury market; the segment has hovered near 50,000 units and luxury penetration fell last year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ChargeZone partnership add revenue, and at what economics?
qa_highlights.answer: ChargeZone runs about 16,000 charging points; Landmark onboards EV customers and earns a recurring revenue share with wallet credits for customers. Commercials were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 margin normalisation and Mercedes QoQ revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2-Q4 to be normalised, with an EBITDA margin around 1.5% on pro forma new car sales; Q1 is seasonally the weakest quarter and Mercedes grew strongly YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV aftersales margin versus ICE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EV margins are similar to the ~15% currently seen and are not expected to be lower; warranty costs (such as batteries) were excluded from the analysis.

qa_highlights.question: Will rental costs and cash conversion change?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said lease amortisation was about INR19 crore, with lease plus interest about INR27 crore; full-year rental cost expected around INR100-110 crore including Ind AS adjustments. EBITDA-to-CFO conversion was about 0.95x last year and expected to be similar.

532796|2026-06.headline: Lumax Auto Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% y-o-y to INR 1,364 crore, with EBITDA up 51% at a 15.1% margin and PAT up 83% to INR 99 crore.
532796|2026-06.overview:
Revenue of INR 1,364 crore grew 33% y-o-y, with EBITDA of INR 205 crore (up 51%, margin 15.1%, up 190 bps) and PAT of INR 99 crore (up 83%). Management said the margin would hold for the rest of the year, and guidance was kept unchanged: 15% EBITDA margin for FY27 and about 20% revenue CAGR. Growth was helped by a low base and industry production up 22% y-o-y, but management expects growth to slow in Q3 and Q4 after the post-GST-rationalisation base effect. The order book stands at INR 1,600 crore, with about 24% expected in FY27, 56% in FY28 and 20% in FY29.</overview>
