segments.name: Advanced Plastics (incl. IAC, ~60% share of division)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 47% y-o-y from INR 525 crore to INR 769 crore; order book INR 787 crore. Division is more than half of group revenue; margin band 16-20%.

segments.name: Mechatronics
segments.commentary: Revenue rose ~56% y-o-y from INR 54 crore to INR 84 crore; order book close to INR 500 crore. Management expects ~INR 400 crore FY27 revenue and ~INR 1,000 crore by FY31; currently 6-7% of group.

segments.name: Structure and Control Systems
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 21% y-o-y from INR 180 crore to INR 220 crore; order book INR 130 crore.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 6% y-o-y from INR 98 crore to INR 104 crore, hit by non-lighting products and pricing; management still guides for double-digit growth for the rest of the year.

segments.name: Alternate Fuels (Greenfuel)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 17% y-o-y from INR 95 crore to INR 111 crore; order book INR 200 crore. Q1 EBITDA margin was ~23%, including ~3% one-off tooling revenue; underlying ~20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance is unchanged: about 20% revenue CAGR (FY25-FY31 vision) and EBITDA margin of about 15% for FY27; management expects Q1 margins of 15.1% to be sustained for the rest of the year.

FY27 capex guided at about INR 300 crore, including Mechatronics greenfield and new IAC plants; Q1 capex was INR 23 crore. About 10-12% of capex may be debt-funded at JV or subsidiary level; the rest from internal accruals.

Targets: FY28 EBITDA about INR 1,000 crore, implying 15.5-16% margin (including other income); longer term, move toward 20% EBITDA margin over 5-7 years, with 17-17.5% cited as a satisfactory interim outcome.
Mechatronics JVs to operate at 14-15% EBITDA over the next 12-24 months; Greenfuel margin range 19-20%.
Aftermarket: management expects growth of 15% or more versus 10-12% under the earlier strategy.
Minority interest expected at 11-13% of PAT. Inorganic growth not planned for the current year, but strategic fits are being evaluated.
capex_capacity: New IAC plant at Chakan for Mahindra & Mahindra demand, with some product-line optimisation across facilities.
Mega Mechatronics plant at Manesar, Haryana, expected to commission by Q3 FY27; consolidates Lumax Yokowo, Lumax Alps Alpine, Lumax Ituran and Lumax FAE.
Greenfuel to set up a new facility in Nashik to serve Mahindra (passenger vehicle CNG delivery system).
FY27 capex guidance of INR 300 crore; order book of INR 1,600 crore to be served on this spend for FY28 and FY29 needs. Capex may be revised for FY28 if order book grows.
SHIFT centre in Bangalore for software-defined vehicles and ADAS development.
demand_pricing: Industry: production up 22% y-o-y in Q1 FY27 (PV +17% to 14.5 lakh, CV +15% to ~3 lakh, 2W +23% to 72.5 lakh, 3W +39% to 3.5 lakh); management expects slower growth in Q3-Q4 because of the high FY26 base.
Plastics prices rose ~30-40%; 80-90% of the increase is passed through to OEMs within the same quarter under back-to-back arrangements, with spillover to the next quarter for a few OEMs.
Electronics components rose by more than 30-50% in some cases; the low Mechatronics share limits the margin impact.
Maruti Suzuki revenue grew 48% y-o-y in Q1; Bajaj Auto revenue grew ~64% y-o-y, attributed to wallet-share gains and new models.
Aftermarket growth was held back by pricing: competitors absorbed input-cost increases while Lumax passed them on in non-lighting categories.
Order book: ~one-third sits with IAC, mostly Mahindra. Order book across verticals: Advanced Plastics first, then Mechatronics, Alternate Fuels and Structures and Control Systems.

539807|2026-06.headline: Gross revenue rose 109% YoY to INR 2,680 crore and PAT rose 45% to INR 85 crore, while net revenue fell 3% to INR 147 crore.
539807|2026-06.overview: AvenuesAI (formerly Infibeam Avenues) reported Q1 FY27 gross revenue of INR 2,680 crore (+109% YoY) and PAT of INR 85 crore (+45% YoY), with EBITDA excluding other income of INR 100 crore (+41% YoY). Net revenue was INR 147 crore, down 3% YoY, and management said take rates have compressed slightly. Management guided FY27 consolidated gross revenue to INR 11,000–13,000 crore (about 35%+ growth) and EPS to INR 8.75–9.50 on the post-split face value of INR 10. The company also announced the merger of its AI subsidiary Neuromind and Phronetic AI into the parent, and a face value change from INR 1 to INR 10.

financial_highlights.change: -3% YoY (about -1% QoQ per analyst question, not confirmed by management)
vs 47% in Q1 FY26 (as cited by analyst and confirmed by CFO)

segments.name: Payments (CCAvenue, BillAvenue, ResAvenue)
segments.commentary: Core merchant acquiring; transaction volume INR 1,479 billion (+74% YoY) across utilities, government, retail, B2B and hospitality. Management says UPI is about 22% of transactions and online acquiring market share is 8-10%.

segments.name: Consumer (Rediff, RediffPay, RediffOne)
segments.commentary: RediffPay is moving out of CUG into production this month. FY27 guidance assumes no meaningful contribution from RediffPay. RediffOne is being positioned as an enterprise operating platform.

segments.name: Intelligence (Phronetic AI / Neuromind)
segments.commentary: PayCentral, described as an agentic payment platform built on Google's Agent Payments Protocol, is in early days. Neuromind is to be merged into AvenuesAI; on-prem SLM products are in early phases with impact expected 9-18 months out.

segments.name: Credit (asset-light distribution)
segments.commentary: Proposed investment of up to 2.5% in RatnaFin Capital (NBFC) and up to 7% in Online PSB Loans. Lending risk is said to remain with regulated partners; no revenue contribution quantified.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated gross revenue guided at INR 11,000–13,000 crore, about 35% growth and above.
FY27 EPS guided at INR 8.75–9.50, on the post-corporate-action face value of INR 10.
Management says the cost base is front-loaded for AI, international expansion and financial services, and it is not building for a short-term margin spike.
EBITDA margin 'guardrail' of about 15% set by management, described as a floor rather than a target.
Management wants investors to focus on net revenue, not gross revenue, as the better indicator of progress.
Meaningful e-commerce platform/AI rewards results are expected to show up in Q3–Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: Management ruled out large data-centre investments (hundreds of MW); it may invest selectively in smaller data-centre capacity.
Focus is on application-layer SLMs and transaction intelligence scores built on the company's transaction graph data.
Licences received: in-principle approval from Central Bank of UAE for Retail Payment Services (Cat III), and RBI authorisation to set up a prepaid payment instrument system in India.
Management said it has US expansion aspirations this year.
demand_pricing: Take rates compressed slightly, which management cited as the main reason net revenue fell 3% YoY.
Management said UPI MDR for businesses is expected on large merchants and high-value transactions, but the Act is still awaiting Rajya Sabha, presidential assent and gazette notification.
Shiprocket Checkout integration gives same-day settlement, international payments, no-cost EMI and payment links to B2C and SME merchants.
Credit distribution through RatnaFin and OPL is expected to bring merchant financing, checkout financing and working capital products to the CCAvenue ecosystem.
Management says Apple Pay and Samsung Pay are enabled on the platform; it operates on the acquiring side.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Neuromind merger and face value change on the Rediff DRHP timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the corporate action has no bearing on the Rediff filing, which it called a separate event. It said the process is at an early stage and some updates are on the SEBI website.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant onboarding traction on PayCentral and whether MDR is an opportunity or a threat given a 8-10% share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PayCentral is early, with the Indian protocol working well and international growth faster. It said MDR is positive but not finalised, and the company sees no consolidation threat on the acquiring side.

qa_highlights.question: Why EBITDA rose while net revenue fell, and should investors focus on net or gross revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investors should focus on net revenue, and the EBITDA increase came from lower expenses. The CFO said EBITDA rose 41% YoY and margin moved from 47% to 68%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 EPS guidance flat when PAT margin is about 57%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will protect core earnings and reinvest incremental accruals into AI, transaction intelligence and new revenue streams. It said the 2027–2029 ambition is a strong earnings base plus a large AI-led business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI infrastructure plan and the expected returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management ruled out large data-centre capex. It is focused on transaction intelligence scores, financial behaviour graphs and SLM application layers, which it said LLMs cannot replicate because they lack the data.

qa_highlights.question: Top-5 client concentration and diversification?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the strategy is to go horizontal with a larger merchant base, and that international focus is on larger clients. It did not give a top-5 revenue share.

risks_watch: Net revenue fell 3% YoY, so gross growth is not translating to net revenue; watch take-rate trend.
FY27 EPS guidance (INR 8.75–9.50) is flat in a year where revenue is guided up about 35%; management is reinvesting incremental accruals.
MDR monetisation timing and pricing are uncertain pending the Act's final notification; competitive response from large incumbents is a risk.
Middle East exposure (UAE, Saudi) may be affected by the regional conflict, per management.
Rediff DRHP timing and the merger of AI subsidiaries; promoter stake increase has not been committed to a timeline.
Credit distribution (RatnaFin, OPL) depends on closing; no revenue contribution has been quantified.

532927|2026-06.headline: eClerx Q1FY27 operating revenue rose 15.2% YoY to USD 125.9M with 2.8% QoQ growth, its 12th straight sequential increase; EBITDA margin 23%.
532927|2026-06.overview: Q1FY27 operating revenue was USD 125.9M (up 15.2% YoY, 2.8% QoQ) and INR 11,524M (up 23% YoY), the 12th consecutive quarter of sequential growth. Operating EBITDA was INR 2,652M at 23% margin, down 260 bps QoQ mainly on wage increments, and PAT was INR 1,643M (14% margin). New deal wins were USD 41M (up 25% YoY). BFSI was roughly flat QoQ and Media/Retail/Fashion remained soft, while Analytics and Automation crossed a USD 100M annual run rate. Management reiterated a 24-28% full-year EBITDA margin range and top-quartile growth for FY27, and said it expects another sequential increase in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: -260 bps QoQ (wages 210 bps, computers/network 40 bps, S&D offset -60 bps); -96 bps YoY
Lower on reduced investable surplus; total revenue INR 11,702M, +24% YoY
OCF/EBITDA 38%, seasonally low due to FY26 variable pay payout in Q1
Billed headcount up on higher utilization

segments.name: Analytics and Automation / Technology & Analytics
segments.commentary: Grew 7% QoQ, ahead of company average, and crossed a USD 100M annual run rate. Management cites AI demand in Hi-tech and BFSI, with data preparation and exploratory data analysis as early entry points.

segments.name: BFSI (Financial Services)
segments.commentary: Revenue down 0.1% QoQ after -2.8% in Q4 and -3% to -3.5% in the prior quarter. Management expects growth from H2FY27; early wins include a Fayetteville contact-centre deal and mortgage servicing work in the US.

segments.name: CMT (Communication, Media & Telecom)
segments.commentary: QoQ growth slowed to 1.3% from 7% in Q4, which management called a quarterly aberration unrelated to US regulation. International centres Cairo, Manila and Fayetteville grew.

segments.name: Hi-tech and M&D / Retail
segments.commentary: Hi-tech outlook described as positive; Hi-tech and M&D saw a growth turnaround. Retail and M&D described as soft due to Middle East-related supply chain pressure. Fashion & Luxury flat QoQ and +2% YoY.

segments.name: Emerging business (F&A-led)
segments.commentary: Strong growth for the fourth consecutive quarter; expanding F&A support to APAC for one client and moving from SMB into mid-market.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expected within 24-28%; management advised the midpoint (~26%) as more realistic, since FY26 closed at 27%.
Top-quartile revenue growth among listed peers reaffirmed for FY27; management believes Q1 was also top-quartile.
Expects sequential revenue growth in Q2FY27, with quarter-on-quarter variation acknowledged.
Margins expected to improve QoQ from Q2 onward if revenue grows, since Q1 carried the annual increments.
CMT/Fashion & Luxury: full-year CLX growth guided at about 0% to 2%; Q2 seasonally soft.
Capex for FY27 guided at INR 130-150 crore; three-year capex to be set in next year's budget.
FY27 ACV aspiration to exceed the ~USD 170M achieved in FY26.
Investor Day planned later in the quarter.
BFSI growth turn expected from H2FY27.
capex_capacity: Adding about 1,600 seats across Mumbai, Pune, Chandigarh, Mohali and Coimbatore, becoming operational in a staggered manner over the next three to four months.
Seat count dipped slightly in Q1 as some production seats were refitted; the new capacity also drives higher Ind AS depreciation and interest.
Coimbatore operations started in Q1, supporting delivery and talent access.
Spend on computers, servers and network infrastructure rose; management expects communication and networking costs not to fall as a share of revenue near term because equipment is more expensive.
Cairo and Lima set up 12-15 months ago; Manila headcount doubled over 15 months. Lower gross-margin locations are growing faster, which dilutes margin.
demand_pricing: Roll-off guided at 15-20% of revenue over a four-quarter period, expected to hold for FY27 though quarterly volatile.
Deal sizes in AI are relatively small; management described AI revenue as icing on the cake, not yet a material share.
Pricing pressure from competitors acknowledged but described as nothing extraordinary; total cost of ownership is the main buying criterion.
Top-5 client softness attributed to a lower refresh cycle in US FCC due to a less onerous regulatory environment, not to client-specific weakness.
Non-top-10 clients are a stated priority to reduce concentration; quarterly volatility noted.
Inbound interest up after analyst recognition; management says deal sizes are increasing.
QA 360 pilot with a large CMT client goes live in Q2, auditing about 0.5M interactions per month.

qa_highlights.question: Is BFSI lagging a concern, and when will it catch up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BFSI was flat QoQ and expects momentum and benefits from H2FY27 based on pipeline and conversions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI and technology investment reflected in headcount, and when will it pay off?
qa_highlights.answer: Investments include an AI COE, pilots and product enhancements. Tech & Analytics growth of about 7% is cited as the proxy; ROI is judged by growth, conversions and margins within 24-28%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did headcount decline, and is growth at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Total headcount fell but billed headcount rose on higher utilization. Management reiterated sequential growth and top-quartile FY27 growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a US regulatory impact on CMT, and what is happening with top-5 clients?
qa_highlights.answer: No regulatory change in either direction. CMT slowdown called a quarterly aberration; top-5 softness linked to lower FCC refresh cycles as US financial regulation has eased.

qa_highlights.question: What drove margin changes and FX impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding FX, QoQ margin impact would have been 330 bps, mostly increments. FX contributed about 50 bps QoQ. Management expects margins to rise from here.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and revenue guidance for the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex INR 130-150 crore. Three-year capex will be set in next year's budget. Top-quartile growth guidance unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold as the company grows toward USD 1B?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to stay within 24-28% if tech, analytics and AI reach 30-40% of revenue, despite competitive pressure.

533033|2026-06.headline: ISGEC Q1 FY27 standalone total income up 51% to INR 1,585 crore, but PBT up only 10% to INR 123 crore; FY27 standalone revenue guided up 10-12%.
533033|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income rose 51% YoY to INR 1,585 crore and EBIT grew 15% to INR 157 crore, with PBT up 10% to INR 123 crore as Q1 FY26 had high forex-driven other income. Manufacturing EBIT margin was 12% and projects EBIT margin 5.25%. Consolidated PBT was INR 53 crore, held back by an INR 83 crore loss at the Philippines ethanol plant, which ran at about 65-70% utilisation. Management kept FY27 standalone revenue growth guidance at 10-12% and said it is conservative, citing carry-forward of order execution into FY28.

financial_highlights.change: about 45% higher vs INR 1,374 crore in Q1 FY26
includes INR 37 crore depreciation, INR 20 crore interest, INR 10 crore forex
vs INR 381 crore at 31 Mar 2026 and INR 408 crore at 30 Jun 2025
down INR 170 crore QoQ from INR 476 crore; INR 832 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Industrial Projects (standalone)
segments.commentary: Income up on improved execution per schedule; management expects roughly INR 1,000 crore per quarter in Q2 FY27 and projects EBIT margin of 5-6% for FY27. Export orders booked in Africa and Latin America.

segments.name: Manufacturing (standalone)
segments.commentary: Income lifted by dispatch of a roughly INR 130 crore US order that had been on hold; EBIT margin 12%, guided 12-13%. Steady-state consolidated manufacturing revenue guided at INR 750 crore plus per quarter.

segments.name: Isgec Hitachi Zosen
segments.commentary: Orders in hand INR 889 crore. FY26 revenue about INR 670 crore; management expects about 10% growth in revenue and profit in FY27.

segments.name: Saraswati Sugar Mills
segments.commentary: Revenue down due to lower cane availability last season (untimely rain); cane availability improvement steps under way for next season.

segments.name: Philippines ethanol (CBPI)
segments.commentary: Q1 loss INR 83 crore at about 65-70% utilisation; crushed about 84,000 tonnes of cane, sold over 8 million litres of ethanol. Management targets about 90% utilisation by December and a much lower loss in Q2.

segments.name: Eagle Press and Isgec Titan Metal
segments.commentary: Eagle Press about INR 150 crore a year; Isgec Titan Metal expected at about INR 150 crore in FY27 vs INR 102 crore in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth guided at 10-12%; management says the figure is conservative with a bias to realism.
Manufacturing EBIT margin guided at 12-13% for FY27; projects EBIT margin guided to improve slightly within 5-6%.
Isgec Hitachi Zosen revenue and profit guided about 10% higher than FY26.
Manufacturing capacity expansion (approved INR 502 crore) to add up to about INR 1,200 crore annual revenue when fully complete; main benefit from FY28-29.

Bhartauli machine-building phase 1 (INR 73 crore) to complete in early September 2026, with about INR 225 crore annual revenue potential; billing expected only from Q1 FY28 as work-in-progress builds first.
Dahej skids and modules facility expected to complete around 31 May 2027.
Philippines ethanol depreciation expected about INR 95 crore in FY27 (WDV method); interest about INR 19-20 crore per quarter.
capex_capacity: Bhartauli (Haryana) presses plant: phase 1 INR 70-73 crore completing first week of September 2026; phase 2 (INR 218 crore) completion expected around end-CY2027 or Q1 CY2028.
Dahej (Gujarat) SEZ skids and modules facility expected to complete around 31 May 2027.
Casting factory expansions, tubing and piping shops at Rattangarh and standard mechanical press factory at Bawal are running largely on schedule, with some facilities completing in FY27.
Board-approved manufacturing capex INR 502 crore; separate corporate office building under construction in projects business.
Q1 capex about INR 47 crore, funded from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand strong across almost all product lines; export inquiry base described as healthy.
Export orders booked in Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia; more than INR 750 crore of export orders booked in Q1.
Standalone orders of about INR 1,200 crore booked in July to date (Q2 FY27).
Management says INR 95/USD rupee improves competitiveness versus other bidders; export logistics costs, freight rates and transit times have risen due to the geopolitical situation.

Commodity prices (steel, copper, aluminium, nickel) stabilised but slightly above pre-war levels; war-related material cost increases have a small adverse effect on profitability, absorbed through contingencies.
Project mix shifting to shorter-duration (max 33-36 months, target 2-2.5 years) technology-intensive orders; avoiding long contract/site-erection-heavy orders.
Sugar machinery export orders up, particularly sugar refineries; management declined to detail the large export orders.

543253|2026-06.headline: Mrs. Bectors Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR548.7 crores with EBITDA margin at 13.1%, targeting 14% by Q4.
543253|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16% YoY to INR548.7 crores and 12.9% QoQ, with exports reported as high-double-digit growth. EBITDA rose 23.8% to INR72.1 crores, margin up 80 bps YoY to 13.1%, and PAT rose 25.5% to INR38.8 crores. Management said price increases and Project IMPACT largely offset input cost inflation in Q1, but expects Q2 to be the most challenging quarter for commodity and packaging costs. Full-year guidance is mid-teens revenue growth and a 14% EBITDA margin by Q4, with about 16% targeted by FY30.

segments.name: Biscuits (Cremica)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR325 crores, up 15.7% YoY; domestic biscuit sales grew high-single digits on both price and volume. Management said biscuit EBITDA margin is slightly below company average.

segments.name: Bakery (English Oven, Naturbaked, QSR)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR215 crores, up 17.5% YoY; Naturbaked crossed a monthly revenue run rate of INR1 crore. Bakery EBITDA margin is above company average; B2B/QSR returned to good double-digit growth.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Grew at high-double-digit rate; volume-led. Export contribution is about 35% of revenue; US contribution is about 23-25% per management, and US is back on growth after tariff-related slowdown.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Grew 58% YoY per management; Kolkata bakery unit (commissioned Q4 FY26) now serving East markets.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 revenue growth targeted at mid-teens (about 17-19% cited in Q&A context); biscuits low-teens, bakery low-teens, exports close to mid-teens.
EBITDA margin target of 14% in Q4 FY27; Q2 expected to see the sharpest commodity and packaging impact, Q3 fully covered by pricing and cost actions.
Project IMPACT expected to deliver about 0.4-0.5% cost benefit this year.
Medium term: EBITDA closer to 16% (15-16%) by FY30 with revenue target of INR4,000 crores.
Consumer price increases of about 2-2.5% taken during Q1, with the balance of the impact in Q2; Q1 inflation impact about 1.5%.
capex_capacity: Capex this year covering existing and in-progress projects could reach about INR3,400-3,500 crores at current prices, per management; excludes Bangalore.
Bangalore plant: shortlisted location; this year's new investment approx INR200 crores beyond last year's spillover; machine orders still being finalised.
Khopoli (Maharashtra) plant commissioned March 2026, stabilising; Kolkata unit commissioned Q4 FY26 (about INR20 crores).
MP plant opened mainly for exports (closer to port) with fiscal incentive; now starting central-market distribution.
Capex funding: about 60% from internal accruals and 40% borrowings this year.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand healthy across retail and institutional; consumption better than feared at last call.
Competition intense in biscuits, especially Upper North India; company stepped up trade promotion and marketing spend.
Plan to add 40,000 billed outlets above INR200/outlet (about 12-13% increase in billed outlets).
Export orders are month-to-month, not a long order book; management said no restocking benefit in Q1.
Inflation impact about 1-2% over last year; contract manufacturing about 1-1.5% of revenue.
Domestic general trade split roughly 50% Upper North and 50% Rest of India; English Oven revenue about 80% North India, with upcountry and NCR now roughly equal.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic biscuit growth and mix of price vs volume?
qa_highlights.answer: High-single-digit growth, with both pricing and volume contributing.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for FY27 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 is the toughest quarter for commodity costs; Q3 fully covered by pricing and cost actions; 14% EBITDA targeted by Q4 and about 16% by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Is export growth driven by restocking or one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no restocking; growth is from new SKUs (e.g., peanut butter cracker at Walmart) and projects that resumed after US tariff slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly freight and fuel (plant fuel consumption) plus higher marketing and trade promotion spend.

qa_highlights.question: Excise/export incentives status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government incentives have not yet materialised; importers pay destination duties. New Zealand FTA and UK are emerging markets.

qa_highlights.question: Capex run rate beyond current cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity supports about INR3,500 crores revenue at current prices, plus Bangalore; more capacity to be added as business grows; funding 60% internal.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 margin pressure from commodity, packaging and freight costs; management expects only partial recovery in Q2.
Escalation of West Asia conflict, vessel availability and freight costs affecting exports.
Intense competition in Upper North biscuits; sustained elevated marketing and trade spend may weigh on margins.
Execution of Bangalore and wider capacity expansion, and funding mix (40% borrowings in FY27).
Management did not disclose domestic biscuit segment margin; delivery of 14% Q4 target depends on pricing pass-through and Project IMPACT.
Reiterated revenue expectations (mid-teens growth) vs Q1 high-teens growth; seasonality cited.
543253|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on Q1 execution and margin trajectory, but cautious on Q2 cost pressure and the West Asia situation. Management was evasive on segment-level margin for domestic biscuits and on export duty/incentive details.
key_quotes: Importantly, the growth was accompanied by margin expansion.
So quarter 2 could be a quarter where we will be able to cover most of it, not entirely, but quarter 3, again, we will be fully covered.
Naturbaked has crossed a monthly revenue rate of INR1 crore.
So over a period of next 3 to 4 years, say, by 2030 financial year, we want to hit EBITDA closer to 16%.

543954|2026-06.headline: Allcargo Terminals Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose to INR47 crore (vs INR35 crore YoY) on 7.2% TEU growth to 1,76,499 TEUs.
543954|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR214 crore, up from INR187 crore a year earlier and INR208 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA excluding other income was INR47 crore, with management citing yield management, technology-led efficiencies and higher transhipment share. PAT fell to INR6 crore from INR9 crore, hit by tax on dividend from JV companies and a prior-year tax item. Management also announced a leadership change, with Pranav Choudhary replacing Suresh Kumar as MD from September 1, 2026.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR187 crore Q1 FY26; vs INR208 crore Q4 FY26
vs INR35 crore Q1 FY26; vs INR44 crore Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR2,898 (corrected from INR2,690 stated on call)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR9 crore Q1 FY26 and Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: c. INR13,000 (vs c. INR11,000-11,500 a year earlier)
Up QoQ/YoY; includes ~INR1 crore ESOP impact for the quarter

segments.name: Container handling (CFS, EXIM)
segments.commentary: Volumes 1,76,499 TEUs, up 7.2% YoY; imports are 75-80% of CFS volumes. Annual handling capacity rose ~20% in FY26 to ~1.03 million TEUs (~10.1 lakh TEU per management).

segments.name: LCL business for Allcargo Group
segments.commentary: Close to 10-12% of revenue from handling LCL containers for Allcargo Logistics at JNPA, Mundra and Chennai; margins said to be similar to third-party business.

segments.name: Nepal JV
segments.commentary: Operates one ICD and three ICPs with a Nepal partner; contributes about 2-3% of overall revenue and profitability.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA per TEU expected to stay around INR2,400 going forward (CFO); management later guided to INR2,400-2,500 range.
3-year plan (Plan 2030) targets EBITDA per TEU of INR2,750 including Farukhnagar, and capacity of 13 lakh TEUs / ~1 million TEU operator.
Tax rate expected at 25% going forward under the concessional regime.
No dividend at present; management says it will move to regular dividends once projects are funded and cash flows are covered, timing not given.
Management expects ICDs to add a natural profitability uplift in ~1.5 years; without it, profitability expected to hover around current levels given competition.
capex_capacity: Plan 2030 capex estimate ~INR400 crore covering Farukhnagar, Speedy JNPA expansion, Mundra and Chennai; ~INR100 crore expected to be spent in FY27.

Funding: INR120 crore equity raised recently (INR25 crore called, ~INR90 crore yet to be called); ~INR50 crore internal accruals; ~INR70 crore annual business cash flow; debt of INR100-150 crore with banks already tied up.

Speedy JNPA: ~60,000 TEU addition after 10-year renewal; tender done, work to start post-monsoon, completion by Jan-Feb 2027; ~INR20 crore capex in FY27. JNPA facility upgrade of INR40 crore co-funded 50:50 with JNPA.

Farukhnagar PFT: completion targeted Feb-Mar 2027 (standalone PFT initially, domestic focus); ICD portion by Oct-Dec 2027. Management says PFT volumes will be 20-25% domestic and 75-80% EXIM once ICD is operational.

Chennai (Kattupalli cluster): site identification in advanced negotiations; firm timeline expected next quarter. Mundra: land acquired; decision on extension with landlord or a larger facility to be taken during the year (current licence to 2030-31).
Capacity utilisation at ~80-85% (vs 60-65% three years ago); Chennai and one Mundra facility fully utilised. Capacity rising from 8.3 lakh to 13 lakh TEUs by 2030 vision.
Smart yard management system piloted at JNPT, the largest facility; myCFS app automates ~70% of the 14-15 step import workflow, with export work being added.
demand_pricing: Average realisation up to ~INR13,000 per TEU from ~INR11,000-11,500 a year earlier, driven by yield management, better selling practices and a recent rate increase.
Management attributes the EBITDA per TEU improvement roughly 50:50 to yield management and operational efficiencies (RST modernisation, yard management systems).
Higher transhipment share and favourable cargo mix (ODC, reefer, container size) cited as margin drivers.
Pan-India scale has reduced transport, equipment and security costs; input cost increases (fuel, transporter contracts) absorbed through rate changes.
Management says the market is very competitive and further yield gains beyond current levels are limited.
Rail and DFC: Mundra's rail coefficient is high; JNPA rail share has room to improve. Allcargo Terminals holds ~7.5% in HORCL and expects preferential DFCC access in ~1-1.5 years.

541195|2026-06.headline: MIDHANI Q1 FY27 turnover rose 40.46% to Rs 239.49 crore, but LPG and raw-material costs compressed EBITDA margin to about 20%.
541195|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 turnover was Rs 239.49 crore (up 40.46% YoY) and value of production Rs 260.36 crore (up 7.9%). PBT rose 25.89% to Rs 23.92 crore and PAT rose 27.42% to Rs 16.31 crore. EBITDA was Rs 46.6 crore (up 12.89%), with margin about 20% versus roughly 23% expected, pressured by LPG price spikes and adverse raw-material price variance of about Rs 13-14 crore. Order book stood at about Rs 2,329 crore as of 1 July 2026, now won entirely through competitive bidding.

financial_highlights.value: About Rs 2,329 crore as of 1 July 2026

segments.name: Order book mix
segments.commentary: Defense about 66%, space (ISRO) about 21%, energy about 9%, others about 4%.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Current-year export sales Rs 33 crore to date with open export order book of about Rs 25 crore; target about 10% of turnover (about Rs 100-120 crore).

segments.name: Titanium
segments.commentary: Melted about 750 tonnes last year after new melting facility; titanium orders worth about Rs 600 crore cited. Management says titanium and super alloys carry higher margins than special steel.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 margins expected to be hit somewhat; management expects normalisation from Q3 FY27, with EBITDA margin returning toward 20-21%.
FY27 growth expected to exceed FY26 growth, though management said sustaining Q1's 40% growth through the year is not practicable.
FY27 normal capex about Rs 50-60 crore, mostly maintenance; Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex over 2-3 years, with returns from year 4 and proposal still awaiting Board and ministry approval.
Metal bank: procurement under way for one customer; further clarity expected by end of Q2 FY27, with implementation targeted next quarter.
Aluminium JV plant at Nellore (with NALCO) being closed; a separate wide-plate rolling of customer-supplied 7000-series aluminium billets has been done as first commercial order.
Export expectation: at least 15-20% increase on the 10% export base over the next 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex proposed for replacing ageing equipment; sent to ministry for evaluation, management declined to give timeline.
Isothermal forging completed in 6,000-tonne press for nickel-based super alloy for fighter aircraft engine; orders for four super alloy grades and three titanium grades to be executed this year.
New titanium melting facility commissioned last year; about 750 tonnes melted last year, with expected growth.
Spring plant in campus started; sample order received from BEML. Preliminary BAFA licence obtained for metal powder equipment, expected on campus by next year.
Bulletproof jacket (ABHED, from DRDO/IIT Delhi) fabricated; testing expected to complete this quarter, with test certificates by next quarter.
demand_pricing: Raw-material prices of nickel, molybdenum, tungsten rose sharply; cobalt also higher. Adverse price variance of about Rs 13 crore (or Rs 14 crore per later remark) in Q1.
LPG price nearly doubled due to Middle East conflict; furnaces are LPG-fired, affecting Q1 and possibly Q2.
Freight cost mostly booked at fixed terms; management said it sometimes absorbs freight increases on fixed-price contracts.
No nomination-based orders now; all orders won through competitive bidding.
Titanium sourced by import from Eastern Europe (former Russian Federation); management reports no import constraints currently.
Scrap usage in melt typically 50-60% for normal aerospace grades; virgin material mandated for human spaceflight and critical engine parts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin compress in Q1 and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Madhubala Kalluri cited raw-material prices and LPG prices, which nearly doubled. She said Q2 may be hit, with normalisation expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin return to 20-21% from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD S.V.S. Narayana Murty said yes, and that the Q1 shortfall was due to the raw-material and LPG issues.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 1,000 crore capex yielding EBITDA, and what is FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex takes 2-3 years, with returns from year 4. FY27 capex will be about Rs 50-60 crore, mostly maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the aluminium plant still on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Nellore aluminium JV plant is being closed, pending ministry approval. The separate wide-plate rolling of customer-supplied aluminium billets is an alternative route.

qa_highlights.question: Will the S400 certification generate meaningful revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is testing-only revenue, conservatively estimated at about 10% of export base, with clarity in a couple of quarters.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin recovery to 20-21% in Q3 depends on LPG and raw-material prices easing; Q2 margin likely lower.
Fixed-price defence contracts leave the company exposed to raw-material and freight cost increases.
Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex is not yet Board- or ministry-approved; no timeline given.
Metal bank benefits are customer-owned and not on company balance sheet; implementation and utilisation are still to be confirmed.
Scrap inventory policy and sales of titanium scrap; management says scrap is a strategic asset rather than surplus.
541195|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and certifications, but cautious and somewhat evasive on margins, capex timelines and the scale of new orders. Management repeatedly attributed Q1 margin pressure to temporary LPG and raw-material factors and declined to quantify the Rs 1,000 crore capex return or the S400 revenue.
key_quotes: Q2 may be little bit hit will be there, but Q3 we have hope that we will be coming to normal state.
Only because of these little raw material and LPG issues only that was little lower bottom line.
So, we reduced our scrap inventory by Rs. 75 crores.
We are not going ahead with that plant.

532993|2026-06.headline: Sejal Glass Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR117.95 crore, up 52.88% YoY; management guides FY27 revenue growth of minimum 25%, up to 40%.
532993|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 52.88% YoY to INR117.95 crore, with India up 67.03% to INR36.43 crore and UAE up 47.31% to INR81.52 crore. Consolidated EBITDA grew over 44% YoY to INR18 crore and PAT grew over 63% YoY to INR7.22 crore. Management cited a one-time-like INR1 crore people-cost hit from appraisals and a Taloja labour union agreement, plus UAE logistics and fuel-related cost increases, as drags on Q1 margin. Guidance was framed as a 25% minimum and up to 40% revenue growth for FY27, with EBITDA margin up about 1% and PAT margin of 9-10% targeted, mainly from Q3-Q4.

financial_highlights.value: ~INR52 crore total, of which term loan ~INR38 crore and working capital ~INR14 crore

segments.name: India (Silvassa, Taloja, Erode)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR36.43 crore, up 67.03% YoY; India exports about 6% of sales, domestic 94%. Silvassa utilisation ~77%, Taloja ~55%, Erode ~15%.

segments.name: UAE
segments.commentary: Revenue INR81.52 crore, up 47.31% YoY; utilisation ~71% on tempering base line, with 95% of UAE output sold locally and in GCC, Africa emerging. Order book about AED70-72 million.

segments.name: Railway / fire-safety / bulletproof verticals
segments.commentary: Railway was under 1% of Q1 revenue; fire-rated glass production to start Q3 FY27. Management targets 10% of revenue from these verticals next year, including railway.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at minimum 25%, with upside to around 40% if geopolitical situation stabilises and order inflows continue.
FY27 EBITDA margin to improve by about 1% over upcoming quarters; PAT margin target of around 9% (CFO) to 9-10% (promoter) for FY27, mainly in Q3 and Q4.
Q2 FY27 revenue expected at INR140-145 crore (15-20% QoQ growth from Q1 INR118 crore).
FY28 revenue growth expected at least 25% YoY (early-stage guidance).
UAE monthly revenue on track to AED31 million in Q1 and AED35 million in Q2 per prior commentary; July at AED11.87 million.
Management indicated 25-40% annual growth range over the next 3-4 years.
Expected UAE revenue mix shift to around 60:40 (UAE:India) this year and 50:50 next year.
capex_capacity: UAE third tempering line (capex incl. fire-rated tech total ~AED15 million) installed; commercial production expected Q3 FY27 end, third line utilisation 15-20% initially. UAE total tempering capacity to ~24 lakh sq m per annum.
UAE plant utilisation ~71% now, target 85%; existing two lines expected to reach ~75%.
Silvassa targeted at 85-90% by year end; Taloja 75% in coming quarters; Erode 25-30% in coming quarters.
India capex is maintenance-type, below INR1 crore per item.
Funding: UAE capex from internal accruals plus proposed ~AED7 million long-term bank loan, roughly 50:50 debt-equity.

Management indicated capacity additions across UAE third line and Taloja/Erode could add about INR75 crore revenue capacity on top of ~INR600 crore from existing capacity (analyst-stated, confirmed by promoter).
demand_pricing: UAE order book about AED70-72 million (~INR175 crore), up from ~AED50 million; incremental inflow AED22-27 million; execution from June-July over next two quarters.
India order inflow above INR50 crore from developers including Godrej, L&T, Prestige and Raheja, to be executed over about 6 months.
Customer execution is gated by end-customer site readiness and design approvals, delaying size release; management says July UAE revenue already crossed AED11.87 million.
Bad debts below 0.5% over last three years; top 15 clients currently >70% of India business, ~200 repeat clients.
Management says no listed architectural glass peer in India; Asahi India Glass is mainly automotive and Borosil is solar.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 margin guidance and what is the closing order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated EBITDA up about 1% and PAT around 9%; order book referenced as India >INR50 crore and UAE ~AED70 million. Promoter said 25% is minimum growth, up to 40% upside, after an earlier TV comment of 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Current and peak capacity utilisation by plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Silvassa ~77%, Taloja ~55%, Erode ~15%, UAE ~71%. Targets: Silvassa 85-90% by year end, Taloja 75%, Erode 25-30%, UAE 85%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there capex planned and how much capacity will it add?
qa_highlights.answer: India capex under INR1 crore per item for maintenance. UAE third tempering line and fire-rated tech total ~AED15 million; commercial production Q3 end; total tempering capacity ~24 lakh sq m per annum.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the Q1 margin squeeze?
qa_highlights.answer: Appraisal and yearly increments plus a Taloja labour union agreement added about INR1 crore people cost; UAE logistics hit by June war disruption; raw material costs up about 1% due to diesel and energy surcharge.

qa_highlights.question: Why has UAE monthly sales stayed near AED10-10.5 million despite a AED60-70 million order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Tailor-made orders are released in size only when end customers are ready, so production timing lags order inflow. July UAE revenue reached AED11.87 million.

qa_highlights.question: How is the UAE capex funded and what are FY28 expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Funded from internal accruals plus a proposed ~AED7 million long-term bank loan. FY28 revenue growth expected at least 25%, too early for margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Railway and new vertical contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Railway under 1% of Q1 revenue; target 10% of revenue from railway, fire-safety and related verticals next year. Approved vendor for Kapurthala, Raebareli and Chennai railway facilities.

511196|2026-06.headline: Can Fin Homes Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 29% YoY to INR 2,609 crores, but rundown of INR 1,857 crores absorbed the AUM gain.
511196|2026-06.overview:
Disbursements of INR 2,609 crores beat the INR 2,500 crore internal plan and grew 29% YoY across all six zones. Book rundown rose to INR 1,857 crores (from INR 1,730 crores in Q4), mainly from part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crores after the annual-to-quarterly reset, so net AUM growth was about 10.8% YoY. Yield held at 9.81% and cost of borrowing fell to 6.98%, lifting spread to 2.83% and NIM to 3.81%. Management reaffirmed 14% AUM growth and a 10 bps credit cost for FY27, while ROA slipped to 2.39% on higher opex and an IT project rollout is underway across 250 branches.</overview>

511196|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 disbursements fell to INR2,375 crore as Project Tejas IT migration hit branches; FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore held.
511196|2026-09.overview:
Can Fin Homes completed the full go-live of Project Tejas (IT transformation) across all branches, with the final ~93 old branches and new branches moving live from 1 October 2026. Disbursements for the quarter were INR2,375 crore, net of about INR29 crore of NHB-mandated cancellation netting, and management attributed the shortfall to one-time migration and process changes plus a Telangana Section 22 verification issue. Management held FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore and AUM growth of 13-14%, and guided FY28 disbursement of INR16,000 crore with 15%+ AUM growth. Prepayments eased to INR1,795 crore from INR1,857 crore in Q1, and the company passed on a 10 bps housing rate hike effective 8 October 2026.</overview>

segments.name: Branches live on new system (Project Tejas)
segments.commentary: Rollout in phases: 11 branches in July (5 old, 6 new), 89 in August (75 old, 14 new), 77 old in September and 98 in October (93 old plus 5 new). Disbursements at branches during their go-live month dropped about 70-75%, recovering to 80-90% of prior run-rate the following month.

segments.name: Branches not yet migrated (93-branch cohort)
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursement was INR435 crore in Q1 and rose to INR454, INR458, INR424 and INR481 crore in the months of July-September per management's slide 20 data (management's figures; not independently verified).

segments.name: Sales team channel
segments.commentary: Sales team headcount about 90 now, targeted at 150 by year-end and 250 in FY28; management expects INR1,500-1,600 crore from sales in FY27 versus INR560 crore in H1.

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: Disbursement has stabilised at INR230-250 crore per period, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement guidance held at INR13,000 crore (20%+ growth over INR10,500 crore in FY26); Q3 target about INR3,500 crore with the shortfall to be recovered in Q4.
FY27 AUM growth guidance of 13-14%, closer to 14%; management said the 15% AUM growth figure for FY28 is a resultant of disbursement and rundown.
FY28 disbursement internal target INR16,000 crore (about 22% growth), implying 15%+ AUM growth, closer to 15.5%.

Spread and NIM guidance of 2.75% and 3.75% maintained; management said it will pass through rate hikes, with about 12-13 bps of liability cost increase on the full book from the 25 bps repo hike and 10 bps passed on so far.
FY27 credit cost guidance of 10 bps maintained; gross NPA expected to fall in H2.
Plans to draw NHB refinance earlier, from Q3 if sanctions are higher, to benefit from lower rates; exploring an additional refinance limit.
capex_capacity: Project Tejas fully live: LOS and LMS live across all branches as of 1 October 2026; modules including risk, ALM, borrowings (by September 2025 onward) and deposits/DMS (January) implemented per management.
25 of 28 branches planned for FY27 are already operational with staff; these are expected to contribute in Q3 and Q4.
Branch expansion: about 12 branches added in UP in the last year, per management.
About 129 staff who were deployed on the IT project are being redeployed to branches and departments, with some support retained for 1-2 months.
demand_pricing: Management said underlying demand is robust with no change, and attributed the Q2 shortfall to process changes (about 8-10 additional OTPs per borrower and co-borrower), a 5-day post-month data handover lag, and a new Telangana Section 22 sub-registrar verification requirement.
Housing loan rate raised by 10 bps effective 8 October 2026 (new customers from 12 October); about 87% of floating book is on quarterly reset, about 12-13% on annual reset.
Management expects a 25 bps repo hike to translate into about 12-13 bps on the book, with plans to pass on about 15 bps next time.

Prepayment rate was about 15.5-16% historically and about 17-17.5% recently; management said a 100 bps rise could narrow the rate gap by around 60 bps, reducing prepayment and rundown by about INR400 crore.
Higher-ticket (INR30 lakh+) loans have grown, and the company is also looking at AHF-linked INR15-25 lakh loans as NHB AHF share rises.
PMAY 2.0 uptake described as slow relative to CLSS-1, with limited presence in the high-need states (Odisha, Bengal, Bihar, UP).
Management said the sales team contributed INR560 crore in H1 FY27 and targets about 20% of disbursement from sales in FY28.

540401|2026-06.headline: Maximus Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 52% YoY to INR59.91 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.64% from 9.81% on Middle East war input costs.
540401|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue from operations was INR59.91 crores versus INR39.52 crores a year earlier, with EBITDA up about 18% to INR4.58 crores. Margin compression, attributed to higher input and freight costs from the ongoing Middle East war, and higher finance costs (INR1.53 crores vs INR0.92 crores) left PAT at INR2.05 crores versus INR2.33 crores a year ago. Management highlighted the proposed associate acquisition of Quebec Petroleum (40% stake), a Kenya grease plant planned for Q3 FY27, and a Tanzania warehousing expansion. Management guided to crossing about INR200 crores revenue in FY27 on a conservative basis.</overview>
