segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Highest EBITDA margin among the three verticals (manufacturing, toll blending, trading) in Q1 FY27 and historically. Operations in UAE and Kenya.

segments.name: Toll blending
segments.commentary: Management says it is being pursued aggressively; in talks with an East African MNC for toll blending.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Lowest-margin vertical per management. Long-term target split: manufacturing plus toll blending 75-80%, trading 20-25%.

segments.name: Specialty lubricants
segments.commentary: Contribute around 40% of topline, per CFO.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to cross about INR200 crores on a conservative basis, with healthy EBITDA margins (stated even under the ongoing war scenario).
Margins expected to hold at current levels or improve over the next couple of quarters if supply disruption persists, through product mix diversification.
Kenya grease manufacturing facility planned for commissioning in Q3 FY27.
Tanzania expansion: initially warehousing and distribution, moving to manufacturing once scale is reached.
Recently launched modernisation programme: automated batch blending, additional storage and warehousing, improved filling lines, and capacity expansion at UAE and Kenya plants.
Capacity considered sufficient for next 2-3 years on single-shift basis; additional storage capex needed for full utilisation.
capex_capacity: Combined manufacturing capacity of about 50,000 KL across UAE and Kenya plants.
Capacity utilisation at about 45% across both units.
Kenya grease plant to cater to East African market, which has few grease manufacturers; also to support toll blending.
Proposed acquisition of an additional manufacturing unit as an associate; process underway, details to be shared later.
Quebec Petroleum: associate investment with initial 40% stake, aimed at entering the Indian domestic market.
demand_pricing: Management says demand for lubricants is supported by industrialisation, infrastructure, vehicle ownership and mining, power and construction; customers are shifting toward premium and specialty products.
Cited Middle East and Africa lubricant market growing from about USD 9.1 billion (2024) to USD 12.4 billion (2034).
Company serves more than 400 customers across 25+ countries and 50+ industries.
Top 10 customers account for roughly 70-75% of revenue, including distributors; company sells mainly through distributors, not B2C.
Product prices and landed costs (freight, insurance) rose due to the Middle East war; company passed on a partial cost increase, which also raised receivables.
Base oil and white oil prices are positively correlated with crude, with a lagged and non-identical impact on lubricant prices.
In Kenya, incumbents Shell and Total have not changed payment terms despite new entrants.

qa_highlights.question: How sensitive are margins to base oil and crude price movements?
qa_highlights.answer: Not directly coupled but positively correlated; raw materials (base oils and white oils) move in the same direction with a lag and not in the same proportion.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation of the 50,000 KL capacity, and targets over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45% utilised; capacity is sufficient for 2-3 years on a single shift, but full utilisation would need additional storage capex.

qa_highlights.question: Which vertical has the highest EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing, both in Q1 FY27 and historically; toll blending is being pursued more aggressively.

qa_highlights.question: Share of premium and specialty versus conventional revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialty lubricants contribute around 40% of topline.

qa_highlights.question: Why have receivables risen faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher topline (about 50% growth), higher product prices and landed costs from the war, and partial pass-through of cost increases to selling prices.

qa_highlights.question: What if supply disruption lasts more than six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has onboarded new customers and broadened product baskets; margins may dip further but aim to hold or improve through diversification; still expects over INR200 crores revenue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will Quebec Petroleum contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Associate with 40% stake; its profits will be included in consolidated financials; focus is India domestic market, while Maximus covers Middle East, East and North Africa.

qa_highlights.question: Target revenue split between trading and toll blending over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing plus toll blending 75-80%, trading 20-25%; split between manufacturing and toll blending not disclosed as they overlap in co-branding.

qa_highlights.question: Concentration of revenue and B2B versus B2C mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Top 10 customers about 70-75% of revenue (distributors included); no own retail outlets; major revenue comes via distribution channels.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin down about 217 bps YoY to 7.64% due to input and freight costs from the Middle East war.
Working capital: receivables rising faster than revenue; financial cost up about 65% YoY to INR1.53 crores.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers about 70-75% of revenue.
Quebec Petroleum associate acquisition and additional manufacturing unit acquisition: terms and financials not yet disclosed.
Competitive response in Kenya from incumbents such as Shell and Total; payment terms unchanged so far.
Management did not split revenue between manufacturing and toll blending; the reported Q1 PAT decline despite revenue growth needs monitoring.

544138|2026-06.headline: JG Chemicals posted record Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR315.7 crores (+44.8% YoY) and EBITDA margin of 11.5%, with PAT at INR26.1 crores.
544138|2026-06.overview: Management reported all-time quarterly highs for revenue, EBITDA and PAT in Q1 FY27, with revenue up 10.3% sequentially. Utilisation is in the early 80s (of achievable capacity) and volume growth was in double digits across categories. Management attributed margin gains to operating leverage, higher-priced and specialised orders, cost-reduction initiatives and a small inventory gain that it declined to quantify. The Dahej (Gujarat) greenfield plant is now guided for commissioning around November 2026 (Q3 FY27), later than the earlier first-half target, and guidance was reset to 50-60% utilisation in FY28 and about 14-15% EBITDA margin.

financial_highlights.change: Management said mid-teens for current quarter in a later answer
Rising every quarter/year per management; prior-period figures not given

segments.name: Zinc oxide / rubber and tire (core)
segments.commentary: Tire and rubber remain the largest pillar; company supplies every Indian major tire maker and 9 of the top 10 global tire companies. Tire approvals take about 5 years.

segments.name: Non-rubber (pharma, ceramics, specialty chemicals, agri, cosmetics, electronics)
segments.commentary: Около 18% of revenue this quarter. Ceramics is being seeded for about a year; approval cycle in ceramics estimated at 1-3 months versus about 5 years in tire.

segments.name: Zinc sulphate
segments.commentary: Less than 5-6% of FY26 sales. Southern India is the core market; Western India expansion planned using by-product raw material from Dahej.

segments.name: Recycled rubber (JG TUR) and new products (LabPure zinc oxide, JG-ZRA)
segments.commentary: JG TUR pilot trials well received; commercial launch hoped within about 12 months, capex and revenue not yet disclosed. LabPure and JG-ZRA introduced this quarter as niche, higher-margin grades.

guidance_outlook: Dahej (Gujarat) greenfield Phase 1 of about 15,000-17,000 tpa zinc oxide: commissioning around November 2026 (Q3 FY27); revenue potential INR300-400 crores; EBITDA margin 11-12%; total greenfield capacity about 40,000 tpa.
Dahej utilisation guidance: 50-60% in FY28 (first full year), about 70-80% in FY29; Phase 2 expansion to start around then.
Consolidated EBITDA margin: management now targets about 14-15% (previously 13-14%), with a 14% reference point stated later; current-year margins expected to stay near current level.
Naidupeta brownfield expansion (about 5,000 tpa debottlenecking) expected to commission in Q3 FY27; Naidupeta capex figure to be provided offline.
Management expects higher sales in Q2 FY27 and similar margin profile to continue into the current quarter.
Export share of sales 10-15% today, about 15% expected in FY28-29.
Target payback 3-4 years and ROCE in mid-20s on new capex, per management.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity at West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh facilities close to 70,000 tpa; combined capacity to exceed 115,000 tpa after Dahej phases are on stream.
Dahej greenfield (Gujarat): about INR100 crores investment, civil work advanced, equipment installation underway; commissioning around November 2026.
Naidupeta brownfield: about 5,000 tpa added, expected Q3 FY27. Capex amount not disclosed; to be shared offline.
Q1 FY27 capex and remaining FY27 capex not disclosed on call; management said it would follow up offline.
Naidupeta solar Phase 1 operational; R&D centre at Naidupeta inaugurated.
Proposed UAE subsidiary (BDJ Materials and Metal Trading FZCO) to source raw materials and handle global distribution; not yet incorporated.
demand_pricing: ATMA data cited: Q1 FY27 vehicle volume growth of up to 26.6% for passenger vehicles, 16.5% two-wheelers, 16.5% commercial vehicles and over 11% three-wheelers.
Tire industry capex of about INR25,000 crores announced; about 25% of Indian tire output exported.
Management expects zinc-linked realisations to stay higher ('new normal') as commodity prices have risen; says company is neutral to zinc price levels.

Raw material: zinc dross supply disrupted by geopolitical conflict, but company maintained uninterrupted supply; management said crisis favoured established suppliers and shifted some customers toward JGC.
Around 90% of new sales expected to be direct to customers rather than through distributors.
Dahej customer mix guided at about 60% tire and 40% other segments.

qa_highlights.question: How much of EBITDA came from inventory gains and how much is reversible?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said margin came from operating leverage, higher-priced and specialised orders, and only a small inventory gain; amount not quantified. Margins of 10-12% are structural, with upside from value-added products.

qa_highlights.question: Will Dahej commission early or late in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said around November 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will realisations sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said higher realisations are the new normal given higher commodity prices, and he sees no near-term reversal.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the FY28 Dahej utilisation guidance lowered from 65-70% to 50-60%, and the margin guidance raised from 13-14% to 14-15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cut is conservatism because the plant start moved from H1 to Q3 FY27; it still sees close to 60%. The margin rise reflects new products and higher-realisation product launches.

qa_highlights.question: What are the payback and ROCE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Payback of 3-4 years targeted, implying about 20-25% annual returns; ROCE expected in the mid-20s.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth outlook and split between zinc oxide and zinc sulphate?
qa_highlights.answer: Mid-teens volume growth in the current quarter. The 15,000-17,000 tpa Dahej Phase 1 is all zinc oxide. Zinc sulphate is less than 5-6% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new products (LabPure, ZRA) carry higher margins and what is their market size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said these are niche, higher-margin products for non-tire customers, slow to ramp; no market size or margin figures given.

532698|2026-06.headline: Nitin Spinners Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR875 crore (+10.3% YoY) and EBITDA margin rose to 17.78%, with PAT up 83.6% to INR75.3 crore.
532698|2026-06.overview: Revenue of INR875 crore was the company's highest ever quarter for a second straight quarter, up 10.3% YoY and 1.8% QoQ, driven mainly by yarn realisations. EBITDA before other income was INR155.6 crore (+39.85% YoY), with margin at 17.78% versus 14.02% a year earlier and 15.17% in the prior quarter. Management attributed the margin gain mostly to yarn price realisation outpacing cotton cost, with smaller contributions from power cost savings and efficiency. Management guided that the new capacities (fabric +35 million metres, spinning +74,000 spindles) will add INR200-300 crore revenue in the near term, though the commissioning timeline has since been reset.

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: Running at 98% utilisation. Yarn spread (yarn price less cotton) reported at about INR130/kg currently versus about INR110 in the prior quarter. Management said yarn price increases outpaced cotton, and a fall in outside yarn sales was due to higher in-house fabric consumption and stock in transit.

segments.name: Woven fabric
segments.commentary: Utilisation above 92%. Fabric margins have not expanded like yarn; pass-through is only of actual cotton increases. Fabric revenue was about INR700 crore plus in FY26 and is about 20-21% of revenue, targeted at about 30% after expansion.

segments.name: Knitted fabric
segments.commentary: Utilisation at about 55-60%, below the pre-US-tariff norm of 60-65%, because of US tariff uncertainty; the US had been a major market for knit fabric.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to stay in the company's 16-20% band; management said it aims for the upper end but gave no firm guidance on reaching it. Management said it expects current margins to be maintained, and declined to comment on improvement.

Renewable power capacity expected operational by end Q3 FY27; management estimates about INR50 crore annual EBITDA benefit, with about INR1.2-1.5 crore already in Q1 and an analyst assumption of about INR12.5 crore per quarter from Q4.
Blended power cost expected around INR5.50/unit once solar covers about 60% of requirements.

New capacity: weaving starts in about two months, processing in about 1.5 months later (around Diwali), spinning on stream by about December; utilisation to ramp to 31 March 2027, with fabric 100% ramp taking a quarter or two into FY28.

Expansion adds about INR1,000-1,100 crore of turnover at full run-rate, of which about INR500 crore is fabric (FY28 fabric revenue targeted at INR1,200 crore) and yarn about 40% for external sale; management said incremental fabric revenue is 'not factoring in' the price volatility.
Management said no new capex is planned until after FY28 beyond the announced expansion.
capex_capacity: Fabric capacity expansion of 35 million metres (weaving plus finishing; solid and yarn-dyed fabrics; no printing capacity added).
Spinning expansion of 74,000 spindles; about 22,000 metric tons of new yarn capacity, of which 16,000-18,000 MT goes into fabric and some to yarn dyeing.
Capex of about INR1,100 crore; Rajasthan textile scheme incentives apply, with capital subsidy booked in other income.
Renewable power expansion on schedule for end Q3 FY27.
Spinning utilisation 98%; woven fabric utilisation over 92%; knit fabric 55-60%.
demand_pricing: Cotton prices rose about 8-10% in Q1 on lower global output and West Asia-related logistics issues; India removed cotton import duty.
Indian cotton had been priced above the Cotlook index in 2023-24 (about +5-7%); it now trades at about -1 to -2% versus Cotlook, a delta of about 7-8 points.
Indian yarn exports to China rose to about 110-115 million kg in CY26 from 90-100 million kg in 2025; management sees China's import demand continuing.
Management said spinning capacity exits in the last 1-2 years and the post-US-tariff demand slump have rebalanced supply.

Volumes: management said yarn outside sales fell because of in-house consumption by fabric units and about some stock held at quarter-end due to vessel shortages; these were said to have dispatched in July.
Price pass-through: yarn price increases exceeded cotton increases (management cited about 120-125% pass-through on a 100% cotton increase); fabric pass-through is only 1:1 on cotton.
India crop: about 318-320 lakh bales for 2025-26, versus 326-327 lakh bales in 2024-25; 2026-27 acreage about 0.5-1% lower; rainfall over the next month is the key factor.

qa_highlights.question: What are the yarn spreads in Q1 and Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads were about INR110 in the last quarter of FY26 and are now about INR130, and management said this is sustained at current conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Are current margins of 17-18% sustainable for the next one to two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to maintain the current level, with cost savings helping, but declined to comment on any further improvement or on a decline.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 EBITDA expansion is from power savings, realisation, and inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Power savings contributed about 0.5% of EBITDA and a similar amount from solar; the gross margin rise to about 40% came mainly from yarn realisation. Inventory gains were described as very small, and the working capital cycle is broadly unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What share of new capacity revenue goes to fabric, and how fast will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: About 600-plus crore of the expansion's turnover is fabric, with yarn ramp-up complete by 31 March 2027 and fabric taking a quarter or two more into FY28; fabric revenue is expected at INR1,200 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company consider a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, as it is in a growth phase funding capex through internal accruals and loans, so a buyback would not be prudent now.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company planning garmenting or home textiles as the next growth leg?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said garmenting is only an idea with nothing firmed up, and home textiles and garmenting are both seen as equally good opportunities, with Europe the key opening for home textiles after the US slump.

544367|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue INR256.4 crore with reported PAT INR46.7 crore; gross margin rose to 47.2% and order book stood at INR1,945 crore.
544367|2026-06.overview: Revenue was INR256.4 crore and reported EBITDA INR64.7 crore (25.2% margin). Excluding a INR7.82 crore non-cash Ind AS 29 hyperinflation loss on Turkish operations, management cited adjusted EBITDA of INR72.5 crore (28.3%) and PAT of INR54.5 crore. The order book closed at INR1,945 crore, about 1.9x last year's revenue. Sangli machinery installation is under way with trial production targeted this month, but customer audits mean meaningful volume is guided for Q3-Q4. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 20% and standalone EBITDA of around 20% or high teens, and flagged likely temporary margin moderation in Q3 from new capacity fixed costs and aluminium pass-through.

financial_highlights.change: Year-on-year growth not stated for group; Quality Power standalone rose from INR37 crore to INR69 crore per management
Increased; to rise as Sangli and Endoks capacity is capitalised

financial_highlights.value: INR1,945 crore (Endoks INR801 crore, Mehru INR585 crore, Quality Power standalone INR553 crore)

segments.name: Quality Power standalone
segments.commentary: Order book INR553 crore; standalone revenue INR69 crore per management, up from INR37 crore. Management expects standalone EBITDA of around 20% and flagged Q3 margin moderation from Sangli fixed costs and aluminium cost lag.

segments.name: Mehru
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR83 crore, up from about INR60 crore. Q1 EBITDA about 18% versus internal target of 22-23%, hit by copper and oil price spikes in April; revised guidance to around 18%. Order book INR585 crore; capacity near 100% utilisation.

segments.name: Endoks (Turkey, power electronics / BESS)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR107 crore revenue; Turkish revenue dipped slightly due to Eid holidays. Order book INR801 crore. Power conversion system facility civil works complete, operations expected Q3 FY27. Pipeline about USD60 million BESS PCS orders, with USD40 million more expected in 12 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20%; management declined to raise it before Q3, saying revision may come then.
Margin guidance: model around 20% or high-teens EBITDA; coil products stable guidance about 20%, with most recent orders booked above 25%.
Q3 FY27 standalone margin moderation expected from new Sangli fixed costs and aluminium cost pass-through; margins expected to normalise as utilisation rises over the next 15 months.
Sangli coil facility: trial production targeted this month; commercial revenue to trickle in from Q3, meaningful from Q4. Peak revenue potential about INR1,500-1,800 crore.
HVDC magnet wire facility: full production targeted by Q4 FY27 after three to five months of stabilisation.

WS Insulators acquisition: consolidation expected from Q4 FY27 after SEZ approvals; EV about INR315 crore. Insulator order target of about INR200 crore over next nine months; standalone potential INR250-300 crore without capex, INR450-500 crore with capex.
Management indicated FY28 growth guidance of 50%, pending order book and delivery timelines.
Order book slated for completion in about 15 months.
Interim dividend of INR0.25 per share declared.
capex_capacity: Sangli new facility: machinery installation in progress; last-mile issues around sequencing, utilities and statutory approvals; building completion certificate pending. Approvals and about 60 global customer audits expected to take about six months; initial ISO/OHSAS audits about one month.
HVDC CTC magnet wire facility at Sangli: machinery installation commencing; full production targeted Q4 FY27.

Endoks PCS facility: civil complete; interiors and power electronics fit-out in progress; facility estimated at about USD70-80 million revenue capacity for about USD2 million capex plus about USD1 million further spend.
Winwin Speciality (Vizag, SEZ): about 40 acres of land; planned INR50 crore capex for capacity; about 120 people on site.
Possible second facility decision (Turkey or Vizag for European and export markets) in 6-7 months.
Fundraise of less than INR500 crore planned, including Winwin acquisition funding, INR50 crore capex and US sales entry; roadshows from 20 August and raise targeted before AGM.
demand_pricing: Demand strong across businesses; energy storage at Endoks has inquiry levels ahead of expectations. Data-centre bids of about USD100 million seen, but 12-month delivery periods limit participation for now.
Two large HVDC programmes expected: one partly awarded (expected Q3-Q4) and Barmer tender close to award. About half a dozen STATCOM projects in talks across US, Europe and Australia.
Management said order acceptance is not the constraint; capacity ramp is. Factories sit on close to two years of order book at current capacity.
Every executable order in the book was booked above the margin guidance communicated to the market; pricing discipline maintained.
Group procurement consolidation (CPO appointed) expected to lower aluminium casting and other input costs; about INR3 crore of volume discounts benefited Q1.
Chinese HVDC bidders: management views the four Chinese entities allowed to bid as non-operational with limited near-term threat; local content norms unchanged at 60-70%.

532457|2026-06.headline: Gulshan Polyols Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR646 crore (+8% YoY) and EBITDA rose 135% to INR91 crore, a 14.2% margin.
532457|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of about INR646 crore was the highest quarterly turnover in company history, up 8% YoY. EBITDA of INR91 crore grew 135% YoY, with margin at 14.2% versus 6.5% a year earlier, and PAT of INR54 crore rose about 307% YoY. Ethanol was the main driver with an 18% segment EBITDA margin, while grain processing improved from weak levels and mineral chemicals stayed steady. Management called Q1 exceptional on favourable raw material prices and high DDGS prices, and kept FY27 guidance unchanged while signalling a conservative stance.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue INR426 crore and EBITDA INR81 crore (18% margin); largest contributor to revenue and profit. Installed capacity about 26 crore litres per annum; order book about 19 crore litres.

segments.name: Grain processing (starch, sorbitol, derivatives)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR170 crore and EBITDA INR8 crore in Q1. FY27 guidance is revenue about INR800 crore at about 5% EBITDA margin; no capacity expansion this year.

segments.name: Mineral chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR24 crore and EBITDA INR5 crore (23% margin). Described as stable; no significant capacity expansion planned.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of about INR2,600 crore, unchanged.
Ethanol revenue about INR1,700-1,800 crore on supplies of about 22 crore litres (Q&A cited 21-22 crore litres generating about INR1,800 crore).
Grain processing revenue about INR800 crore; mineral processing about INR100 crore.
Consolidated EBITDA margin about 10-11% and PAT margin about 5-6%; management said it expects to end the year above these margins but is guiding conservatively.
Ethanol debottlenecking to lift utilisation to 100-110% of existing capacity by FY28, with capacity up about 15-20%.
On-site plant at Trident expected to be operational by end of FY27, adding some revenue.
capex_capacity: Majority of recent capex is complete; FY27 focus is on utilisation and cash flow, with only ethanol debottlenecking planned.
Major expansion into specialty and import-substitute chemicals, grain-based derivatives, expected from FY28; products still under evaluation and not yet named.
Starch capacity to be ramped to 100% utilisation by end of FY27; no starch expansion this year.
Capital subsidy of INR5 crore received from Madhya Pradesh in Q2, adjusted against plant and machinery capex.
Ethanol plants at Assam and Madhya Pradesh; four plants in total grinding about 3,000 tonnes of grain per day.
demand_pricing: Government support for ethanol: E20 achieved; E30 targeted by 2030. Management said higher blending beyond 20% may slip 6-12 months because of protests, but E20 will not be rolled back.
Ethanol feedstock mix: about 40% FCI rice, about 50% maize, about 10% broken rice/DDGS.

Maize prices currently INR23-25/kg across plants (Assam 23, Muzaffarnagar 23, Gujarat 24, MP 25); Q1 raw-material costs were favourable and Q2 is seasonally pressured until the Kharif harvest in October-November.
Maize DDGS priced at about INR20-22; stable for about two quarters. DDGS contributes about INR10 per litre of ethanol cost.
Grain processing: domestic starch and derivative prices improved as exports began from Gujarat; sorbitol exported to more than 40 countries. Management expects a sharp YoY improvement in the segment.
Inventory cap of 30-45 days of grain because of storage and working-capital limits, so raw-material volatility is only partly hedged.
Talks on opening ethanol exports to neighbouring countries (Japan, Indonesia mentioned in press); not yet started.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong Q1 ethanol margin a one-off, given FY guidance of about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was exceptional on favourable raw material prices and record DDGS prices. Q2 is seasonally weak, and H2 (Q3-Q4) is usually stronger; guidance is conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Will E30 timelines slip given protests?
qa_highlights.answer: E20 will not be rolled back. E30 is set for 2030, and blending beyond 20% may be delayed by 6-12 months. Steady-state ethanol demand is not expected to be affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ethanol order book and how confident is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: About 19 crore litres already received, with about 2 crore litres more expected. Management is confident of 21-22 crore litres for FY27, generating about INR1,800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw-material price volatility managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Stocking is capped at 30-45 days of grain. Management will stock up during the April and October harvests, and the full-year margin is expected to average out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term ethanol growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity to rise 15-20% through debottlenecking, targeting 100-110% utilisation of existing capacity by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the grain processing underperformance and what is the recovery outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recovery has started with a big YoY margin improvement. Starch capacity is to reach 100% by year-end, with FY27 grain processing EBITDA margin about 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export exposure and hedging approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about INR18 crore, or 5-6% of quarterly turnover. The company does not hedge FX and relies on a natural hedge from equivalent imports.

qa_highlights.question: Were any government subsidies recognised in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Grants and incentives are accounted for on a receipt basis, and nothing was received in Q1. INR5 crore MP capital subsidy was received in Q2 and adjusted against capex.

risks_watch: Q2 seasonal pressure on maize and grain costs before the Kharif harvest; margins may fall short of Q1 levels.
Possible 6-12 month delay to blending beyond E20 because of protests, which could slow incremental ethanol allocations.
Grain processing (starch) remains low-margin, around 5% EBITDA guided, with a recovery still to be proven.
Specialty chemical expansion from FY28 has no named products or capex figure yet.
Ethanol export opening is still at talk stage; timing is uncertain.
Reliance on OMC purchase orders for the 2 crore litre balance not yet received.

544550|2026-06.headline: Pace Digitek Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 51.3% YoY to Rs.555 crore; FY27 guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated on Rs.10,803 crore executable order book.
544550|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs.555 crore (up 51.3% YoY) but down sharply from Rs.1,097 crore in Q4 FY26, which management attributed to milestone-based recognition and a high Q4 base. EBITDA was Rs.86.1 crore (15.5% margin vs 14.9% in Q4) and PAT was Rs.63 crore (11.3% margin vs Rs.55 crore in Q1 FY26). Order inflow in the quarter was about Rs.1,677 crore, with two energy EPC wins (NLC, DVC, ~Rs.1,412 crore) and a BSNL OFC project (~Rs.265 crore). Management said the 5 GWh BESS line is operational, with a further 5 GWh line due to be commissioned by December 2026, and reiterated the FY27 revenue guidance.</overview>

segments.name: Energy (BESS, renewable EPC, BOO)
segments.commentary: Contributed 79.5% of Q1 revenue and is the main growth driver; energy executable order book Rs.8,453 crore, split Rs.4,074 crore BOO and Rs.4,367 crore EPC. Management expects energy to be about 65-70% of the order book by year end.

segments.name: Telecom & ICT (BharatNet, Railway Kavach, BSNL OFC)
segments.commentary: Contributed 20.5% of Q1 revenue; executable order book Rs.2,350 crore. Kavach about 30% complete; BSNL OFC (~Rs.265 crore) to execute over about 2.5 years. Management said telecom has better margins but lower volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated; management said it sees no concern in achieving it, with most revenue expected from the existing order book.
H1 FY27 targeted at 40-45% of full-year revenue vs 35% in H1 FY26.
Q2 container supply planned at 210 units; management expects about 125+ containers per month in the next calendar year.
FY27 PAT margin guidance of 10.5-11% for BESS, with the lithium-ion cell cost increase said to be factored in.
Cash flow from operations expected to turn positive by March 2027; inventory and receivables expected to stabilise between December and March.
Energy-to-telecom order book mix expected to move to about 65:35 or 70:30 by year end.
capex_capacity: BESS capacity is 5 GWh operational (two 2.5 GWh lines); a third 5 GWh line is due for installation in October 2026, targeting 10 GWh by early December 2026 as India's largest operational BESS facility.
Total capex of about Rs.300 crore for the 5 GWh expansion phase, the container fabrication unit, and related setup, mainly land cost, funded from the earlier private placement.
In-house container manufacturing started with trials this month; batch production from next month. Over 300 containers supplied to date.

BOO projects: 975 MWh commissioned to date (MSEDCL standalone BESS, about Rs.900 crore recognised in P&L); four BOO projects expected to add about Rs.750 crore annual revenue once all are commissioned.
Pune R&D centre inaugurated about three weeks ago; cell manufacturing planning under way. Applying for 4 GWh under the government cell PLI scheme (10 GWh total scheme).
demand_pricing: Bidding for about 27 GWh of tenders; NTPC Renewable Energy and NTPC Green tenders noted, with NTPC Green tenders drawing only 7-8 bidders versus 32-51 in earlier state tenders.
Management said bidding aggression has eased after a 4 GWh Maharashtra project was cancelled and a Punjab tender saw a single bid at higher prices.
Management said cell cost is about 60% of total BESS cost, unchanged; recent tenders include price variation clauses while older tenders do not. Stock was built in March to lower Q1 cell costs.

C&I BESS (below 5 MWh) received product approval from large Indian customers; first trial order of about 25 units, with management referring to potential for thousands per year. Management guided C&I EBITDA margin about 4-5 points above grid-scale product margin of 13-15%.
Container unit value about Rs.4-4.5 crore; about 70 containers per month currently.
Early exports: small container supply to a Saudi company in Q1 and an MoU signed in Saudi Arabia.
MEGMEET tie-up for AI data-centre power solutions in India; demo equipment planned; management said a concrete revenue plan could come in about one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Telecom & ICT order inflow break-up and execution timeline for the Rs.2,350 crore telecom book?
qa_highlights.answer: Of Rs.1,677 crore inflow, NLC and DVC EPC wins were about Rs.1,412 crore and BSNL OFC about Rs.265 crore. EPC projects run about one year; OFC about 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance not higher given the energy order book visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: BOO solar-plus-BESS capex is capitalised as a fixed asset and not recognised as revenue, so physical execution will exceed reported revenue. Revenue recognition comes from EPC and standalone BESS in BOO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash flow and working-capital profile by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Telecom net working capital is about 5 months (~150 days); energy is expected at 90-100 days. Management expects operating cash flow to turn positive by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue path needed from Q2 onwards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the remaining Rs.2,700 crore should come from the existing order book, with Q1 seasonally low due to government funding and approval cycles.

qa_highlights.question: How will rising lithium-ion cell prices affect EPC and BOO margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 10.5-11% margin already includes anticipated cell price increases; price variation clauses in new tenders and stock built in March mitigate impact.

532891|2026-06.headline: Puravankara Q1 FY27 presales rose 28% YoY to INR1,439 crores and PAT turned positive at INR25 crores; FY27 presales guidance of INR11,200 crores reiterated.
532891|2026-06.overview: Presales grew 28% YoY to INR1,439 crores on 9% higher volume (1.36 million sq ft) and 18% higher realisation (INR10,589/sq ft). Collections rose 40% to INR1,199 crores and 745 homes (0.94 million sq ft) were handed over. Total income rose 63% YoY to INR877 crores, EBITDA margin expanded to 25% from 15%, and PAT was INR25 crores versus a loss of INR69 crores a year earlier. Management kept FY27 presales guidance and the INR700 crores debt-reduction target, while adding four Bengaluru land opportunities (GDV ~INR5,200 crores) and signing a sale of Purva Zentech to ICICI Prudential AMC at ~INR625 crores EV.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR69 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Reduced by INR74 crores in the quarter

segments.name: South
segments.commentary: Contributed INR1,046 crores of presales in Q1 FY27 per management. Projects cited include Northern Light and Provident Equinox.

segments.name: West & Commercial
segments.commentary: Contributed INR393 crores of presales in Q1 FY27, including ~INR200 crores from Purva Estrella (per Rajat Rastogi's estimate). Aerocity received OC for 1.3 million sq ft; Miami has RERA and is on sale.

533470|2026-06.headline: Rushil Decor Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 27.8% YoY to INR 2,920 mn, but EBITDA margin was 7.9% and PAT only INR 20 mn amid input cost and freight pressure.
533470|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 27.8% YoY, driven by normalised Andhra Pradesh MDF operations and a 65.3% jump in laminate revenue. Gross margin was 39% and EBITDA INR 182 mn (7.9% margin), but profitability was hit by elevated resin/chemical costs, higher freight and West Asia shipping disruption. Management said prices are now sustainable with no further hikes beyond the taken ones, and debt is on a schedule to be cleared around FY29 with no major capex beyond maintenance.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,456 mn (+17.2% YoY), EBITDA INR 123 mn (8.4%). India revenue INR 1,447 mn (+32.9%), India volume 52,162 CBM (+16.1%), realisation INR 27,736/CBM (+14.4%). Capacity utilisation 66% after the April maintenance shutdown; exports subdued at ~255 CBM.

segments.name: Laminate (total)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 736 mn (+65.3%): India INR 251 mn (+60.6%), export INR 485 mn (+67.9%). Volume ~8.8 lakh sheets (+27.9%), blended realisation INR 836/sheet (+29.3%). EBITDA INR 52 mn (7%).

segments.name: Jumbo laminate
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 110 mn (+25% YoY), volume ~1.13 lakh sheets (+20.4%), EBITDA INR 23 mn (20.6%). Management puts utilisation at 29% on a 1 mm-equivalent basis against 28 lakh sheets capacity.

segments.name: PVC / MDF retail
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 96 mn (+13.1% YoY), volume +6.9%, EBITDA INR 8 mn (7.9% margin).

guidance_outlook: Jumbo laminate utilisation aspiration: ~50-55% in FY27 and 70-75% next year; ~60% utilisation would give ~INR 75 cr revenue, 90% ~INR 140 cr (Phase 1 + Phase 2).

Management expects Jumbo margins to be maintained through the year; existing laminate normal margin cited at 9-10%, combined laminate margin expected above 10% once Jumbo ramps, subject to chemical and war uncertainty.
Consolidated EBITDA margin target of 10-12%; management said realistically 1-2 quarters more to reach it.
MDF utilisation for FY27 expected to exceed FY26's ~75%; internal targets of 50% volume and 60% value from value-added products.
Debt including working capital ~INR 260 cr; scheduled repayment ~INR 55 cr per year, expected to be debt-free around Q2 FY29; only INR 5-10 cr operational capex planned in FY27.
Current MDF exports running at ~3,200 CBM in July vs 4,000-5,000 CBM per month last year; no revenue guidance given for FY27.
capex_capacity: Jumbo laminate capacity 28 lakh sheets (1 mm basis); capex ~INR 90 cr; management cites asset turn ~1.4-1.5x at full potential.
Jumbo utilisation 29% currently, aspiration 55-60% in FY27 (per call; reconcile with 50-55% stated later), 70-75% next year.
MDF capacity utilisation 66% in Q1 FY27 vs 83% in Q4 FY26 (April planned shutdown); FY26 full year ~75%.
Laminate plant had a single-boiler constraint after Jumbo capacity was added in one plant, reducing output in Q1.
No major capex beyond maintenance; operational capex INR 5-10 cr in FY27.
Entered two new export markets (Honduras, Greece); added 15 distributors and 46 retailers/dealers in Q1.
demand_pricing: MDF industry growing at ~20% CAGR; management says ~800 CBM/day of new capacity can be absorbed, but new capacity (organised and unorganised) is adding competition in domestic market.
MDF price hike of ~15% taken and sustained with no discounts; no further hikes after that. Laminate ~10% hike (taken in Q4 FY26) covering inflation; no further hikes.
Resin prices up ~35-40% vs pre-war; wood prices flat; resin easing in July described as 'very marginal'.
MDF OEM share 35-40% of domestic volume; OEM and retail prices currently the same; no fixed-price long-term OEM contracts.
Export MDF held back by container shortage and high freight; orders in hand but customers must approve higher freight before shipment.
Thailand and Vietnam are supplying the West Asia/export demand; 8-10 overseas factories have BIS licences, but no significant imports into India yet.
Laminate domestic volume growth 15-20%; export growth from new Far East customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MDF OEM vs retail split and how did it move in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: OEM is 35-40% of domestic volume, rest via distribution and retail; the mix in Q1 was the same as Q4 per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jumbo laminate utilisation and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 29% on a 1 mm-equivalent basis; capex was ~INR 90 cr for 28 lakh sheets; full-potential revenue ~INR 140 cr at 90% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MDF volume stay flat YoY and why were exports low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the planned April shutdown, elevated chemical prices causing buyers to hold back, and West Asia disruption; exports were ~255 CBM due to container shortage and high freight.

qa_highlights.question: Will further price hikes be taken to offset input inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no hikes beyond 15% (MDF) and 10% (laminate); market will not accept more, so no guidance on further hikes.

qa_highlights.question: When will the consolidated EBITDA margin reach 10-12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Aspiration is this quarter, but realistically 1-2 quarters more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to full potential revenue (~INR 1,100 cr)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no FY27 revenue guidance; said laminate normal turnover ~INR 200 cr could reach INR 250 cr and Jumbo will take time, with no guidance given for the total.

544459|2026-06.headline: Shanti Gold Q1 FY27 revenue rose 144.69% YoY to INR716.38 crores, with PAT of INR50.48 crores, though management flagged about 2-2.5 points of EBITDA margin from one-off inventory gains.
544459|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 144.69% YoY to INR716.38 crores and PAT rose 46.94% to INR50.48 crores, with PAT margin at 7.05%. EBITDA was INR71.45 crores at a 9.97% margin, which management said includes roughly 2-2.5 percentage points of unrealised inventory gain from the FIFO-to-WAC change. Management guided to 7.5-8% EBITDA margin going forward, reiterated FY27 guidance of 50-60% value growth and 30-40% volume growth (about INR3,500 crores revenue), and said the Marol (Mumbai) plant commenced operations in June 2026. A INR100 crore rights issue was approved to fund working capital and growth.

financial_highlights.change: +144.69% YoY vs INR292.78 crores in Q1 FY26
+39% YoY vs INR51.41 crores in Q1 FY26
Management plans to take it up to below 1x

segments.name: Studded jewellery
segments.commentary: Management said about 70% of jewellery sold is studded; in a separate answer it said 75% of revenue is designer jewellery and 25% plain gold, and about 75% is cast-studded. The figures given during the call are inconsistent and need clarification.

segments.name: Plain gold jewellery
segments.commentary: Management cited about 30% of jewellery sold as plain gold, or 25% of revenue, in different answers.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were 4% of Q1 revenue. A Dubai office is awaiting RBI approval; management described it as the base for international expansion, currently serving three to four countries.

guidance_outlook: FY27 value growth guidance of 50-60% YoY, equal to a revenue target of about INR3,500 crores; management said it could revise upward if Q3 demand is strong.
FY27 volume growth guidance of 30-40% YoY. Management called a repeat of the roughly 61-62% Q1 volume growth 'wishful thinking'.
Sustainable EBITDA margin of 7.5-8% for FY27 after removing the 2-2.5 point inventory gain; management said margin could move toward 10% over three to four years as new facilities scale.
Jaipur facility to start around mid-November or December 2026, with capex of about INR47 crores.
Management expects working capital needs to rise and plans a debt/equity mix that stays below 1x, funded by debt plus the INR100 crore rights issue.
capex_capacity: Marol (Mumbai) manufacturing facility began operations in June 2026, with a new 4,000 kg-capacity line that is ramping up; management said it is a different jewellery line from the existing plant.
Existing Mumbai plant capacity is about 2,700 kg and is running at about 75% utilisation.
Jaipur facility capex is about INR47 crores; first phase is 50,000 sq ft on a 3-acre site, expected to add about 1,200 kg. Operations are targeted for mid-November to December 2026.
Rights issue of 46,43,471 equity shares of INR10 face value, aggregating up to INR100 crores; the issue opened on the day of the call. Post-issue share count is about 7.67 crore shares.
demand_pricing: Volume growth was about 61-62% YoY in Q1, driven by new designs, new customers and new markets. Management said gold was in a narrow INR142-150 band in FY27 and that May-June were subdued.
Gold prices rallied again in the weeks before the call following the IIJS exhibition; management said its long-term view on gold is very bullish.
Management said the exchange-programme trend in retail does not affect its demand.
Management said North India was recently entered and most northern clients are new; it said North and South margins are broadly similar.
Management said demand is strong after exhibitions, with orders in hand for export and domestic markets.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin trajectory and gold price views?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to about 4% PAT margin and 7.5-8% EBITDA margin. It said gold was in a narrow band, with a strong long-term view on gold.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the revenue growth is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume grew about 61% YoY in Q1, and FY27 volume guidance is 30-40% against value guidance of 50-60%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other expenses up 132% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reflects indirect expenses to support growth, not hedging losses, and that it is comparable to the scale of growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity utilisation and the Jaipur capex?
qa_highlights.answer: The Mumbai plant is at about 75% utilisation. Jaipur capex is about INR47 crores, with operations expected around mid-November to December.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for negative operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds ready stock rather than producing order-to-order, so cash is tied up in inventory. Cash flow would turn positive only on an order-to-order model.

qa_highlights.question: Will the rights issue be used to add borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rights issue proceeds will go into gold inventory and working capital, and it will keep existing borrowings without taking new ones at this stage. It also said it expects to add both debt and equity over time.

risks_watch: Roughly 2-2.5 points of Q1 EBITDA margin came from a one-time inventory gain after the FIFO-to-WAC change. Underlying margin is 7.5-8%, so Q2 margin will show the true run-rate.

Working capital intensity is rising with 50-60% value growth guidance, a stock-heavy model and a debt/equity target below 1x from 0.50x. Management said cash flow from operations has been negative for several years.
Management said it uses gold metal loans only selectively; hedging policy and the share of GML-backed inventory were not clearly quantified.
Jaipur commissioning timeline (mid-Nov to Dec 2026) and Marol ramp-up are critical to the FY27 volume target.
Export share is small at 4% and the Dubai office is still awaiting RBI approval.
Management's answers on product mix (studded versus plain share) were inconsistent across the call.
544459|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and growth-focused on volumes and capacity, but cautious on margins and the sustainability of the Q1 profit. Management was vague on several numerical details (product mix, North/South split, gold hedging) and deferred some answers to year-end.
key_quotes: So roughly 2% to 2.5% was the inventory gain.
So the long-term, our vision towards the gold is very, very bullish.
The reason for being negative cash flow is like, we utilize all the funds and we keep the stock readily.

542597|2026-06.headline: MSTC Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose ~22% YoY to Rs 94.25 crore, with PAT up 31% to Rs 58.12 crore on a 69% EBITDA margin.
542597|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose about 22% YoY to Rs 94.25 crore, led by e-commerce revenue of Rs 89.49 crore (vs Rs 70.03 crore). The trading and marketing (110% BG model) segment was exited and revenue from it fell to zero, so segmental reporting stopped from this quarter. PAT rose 31% to Rs 58.12 crore, and the Mahindra JV (MMRPL) posted its first positive PBT in about four years. Management described the quarter as the highest Q1 e-commerce revenue and PBT/PAT since listing, with new verticals (EPR, TReDS, travel) still awaiting regulatory or government go-aheads.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 70.03 crore YoY; highest Q1 e-commerce revenue

segments.name: E-commerce (only reporting segment from Q1 FY27)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 89.49 crore vs Rs 70.03 crore. Scrap sales make up about 50-55% of e-commerce revenue; minerals/coal blocks and other platform, software and AMC services make up the rest.

segments.name: Trading and marketing (110% BG model)
segments.commentary: Exited in FY26; dues recovered and revenue fell to zero this quarter. Segmental reporting discontinued.

segments.name: Mahindra JV (MMRPL)
segments.commentary: Posted a positive PBT for the first time in about four years, a token amount (share ~Rs 10 lakh), driven by higher ELV feedstock inflows under EPR norms.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to sustain double-digit growth on average, with lumpy quarters expected; no specific quarterly growth guidance given.
Margins expected to average near current levels, but may come under pressure at higher volumes, per the CFO; the 60%+ margin is not guaranteed.
TReDS platform: internal target to operationalise within FY27, contingent on RBI approval; transaction fee is the primary revenue source; no revenue quantum projected.
EPR e-trading portal is ready and integrated; awaiting government notification. Initially 5 sectors, expanding to about 15.
Travel portal: B2B live for government/PSU use; B2C launch awaits IATA empanelment. Revenue expected to be selection-fee based and slow to build.
Dividend: policy guided by DIPAM minimum of the higher of 4% of net worth or 30% of PAT; FY26 dividend already declared and subject to AGM approval.
Management declined to quantify EPR revenue potential (analyst's ~Rs 400 crore estimate for 2030-31 was called premature).
capex_capacity: Asset-light model: new verticals are being added selectively, stabilised, then scaled.
Travel portal and TReDS built on existing infrastructure; management says cost to establish was low.
Coal and mineral exchange feasibility under study; no timeline or capex quantified.
Corporate office opened in New Delhi; pan-India operations expanded.
demand_pricing: Scrap is cyclical with steel sector pricing and volumes; management expects mineral-block sales to be sustainable but cannot say whether 20-25% growth will continue.

544619|2026-06.headline: Sudeep Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR158.3 crore, with EBITDA margin at 34.7% despite an LPG-driven specialty slowdown.
544619|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 27% YoY to INR158.3 crore and EBITDA rose 25% to INR54.9 crore, with margin at 34.7%. PAT increased to INR40.6 crore (PAT margin 25.6%). Pharma, food and nutrition (PFN) grew 31% (management also cited 30% in Q&A), mainly on volume from phosphates. Specialty ingredients grew 19% after LPG shortages in April and first half of May cut utilisation, and NSS (European subsidiary) was weak due to energy costs at a major infant formula customer in Ireland. Management said specialty and PFN momentum should continue into Q2, with price pass-through on phosphates mainly landing in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: +27% YoY from INR124.9 crore in Q1 FY26
vs INR31.3 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Pharma, food and nutrition (PFN)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 31% YoY, 69% of total; growth mainly volume-driven on phosphates with largest customer, with about 3% from currency. Bisglycinate (Absorbis) Q1 sales already exceed full FY26 sales.

segments.name: Specialty ingredients
segments.commentary: Revenue up 19% YoY, 31% of total; utilisation below 50% for half the quarter due to LPG shortage, supplies restored at higher cost. Segment margin 26% including NSS; mid-30s excluding NSS.

segments.name: NSS (European subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Challenging quarter; major infant formula customer in Ireland scaled down and delayed buying. Management expects FY27 flattish to single-digit growth; target similar margins to core specialty by FY28. Five customer approvals and 12 active projects since new business head joined in June.

segments.commentary: Phase 1 commissioning targeted April 2027; major long-lead equipment deliveries due October 2026. 21 customers at lab validation, 16 at pilot scale, 7 at pre-commercial/commercial validation; 8 customers now qualified. Two MOUs signed with South Korean cathode makers in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Specialty ingredients expected to return to historical growth trajectory from Q2 FY27; core specialty expected to bounce back in Q2.
Price increases on phosphates (phosphoric acid up ~50% in the quarter) expected to largely offset input cost impact in Q2.
EBITDA margin target of 37-38% sustained; management said pre-investment margins were 37-38% and current level is ~35%.
Greenfield Nandesari facility: FDA approval expected in Q1 FY27 quarter; supplies to start in Q3 FY27. Expects FY28 growth in PFN to be sustainable.
Two significant binding off-take agreements for SAM expected later in calendar 2026; scale-up from 100 to 200 KTPA to be timed after signing, with current target between CY2030 and CY2031.
Working capital: long-term sustainable cycle closer to 150 days; near-term target around 170 days excluding battery business.
Greenfield utilisation expected around one-third in FY28, with hockey-stick ramp in year three; optimum utilisation 70-75%.

Specialty facilities ran at under 50% utilisation for half the quarter; LPG supply secured at higher cost, operations normalised by quarter end.
Asset turns at scale for battery and greenfield expected at about 2.7x to 3x; asset turns at 200 KTPA may exceed that.
Phase 2 HPMC/PVP excipients not expected to be commercialised this financial year.
demand_pricing: Phosphate demand exceeds current manufacturing capacity, giving visibility for the rest of FY27.
Phosphoric acid price up ~50% in the quarter due to logistics costs and sulfur price spike; pass-through mostly reflected in Q2.
Bisglycinate: two large North American customers approved; company behind schedule on deliveries; management expects it to be a top 2-3 PFN product within 2-3 years.
Europe was a key growth contributor for core specialty; NSS weighed by energy costs.
Management said NSS and specialty are not competing with the exited German distributor in existing categories.

qa_highlights.question: How much of PFN's 30% growth came from price vs volume, and what is bisglycinate visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth mainly volume-driven (about 3% from currency); price increases to show up in Q2. Bisglycinate sales are behind schedule on delivery to two US customers; significant growth expected in the next 2-3 years rather than this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is PFN growth sustainable, and what does the greenfield add?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity can add only a couple of percent more; greenfield commissioning in Q3 gives the next leg of growth. Management expects PFN growth to be sustainable at scale in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did specialty margin fall to 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sub-50% utilisation for half the quarter and overhead inefficiency; NSS dragged margin. Core specialty without NSS was in the mid-30s.

qa_highlights.question: Scale-up plans for battery materials and land availability?
qa_highlights.answer: 100 to 200 KTPA scale-up will be timed after binding off-takes; Dahej site can support 200 KTPA; beyond that a new location is required.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of NSS customer issues and the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Largest infant formula customer scaled down Irish operations due to energy crisis; FY27 flattish to single-digit growth. Plan: new sales head expanding outside Ireland and supplying mostly from India; margins similar to core specialty possible in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and steady-state utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built up for raw materials and battery business; long-term working capital cycle closer to 150 days. Optimum utilisation 70-75%.

qa_highlights.question: Europe distribution and phosphoric acid sourcing for battery business?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales team built to replace the exited German distributor; no overlap in existing products. No phosphoric acid sourced from China for SAM (FEOC compliance); about 3 other countries plus India supply.

500003|2026-06.headline: Aegis Logistics Q1 FY27 PAT rose 212% YoY to INR545 crore and normalized EBITDA 184% to INR727 crore, driven by a record LPG distribution quarter.
500003|2026-06.overview:
Management reported record Q1 FY27 results, with PAT of INR545 crore (up 212% YoY) and normalized EBITDA of INR727 crore (up 184%). The Gas division posted its highest-ever EBITDA of INR591 crore (up 296% YoY), with distribution volumes of 2.77 lakh MT (up 91% YoY, up 19% QoQ). Liquids EBITDA rose 28% to INR136 crore on INR178 crore revenue. Management announced several port and capacity milestones, including commissioning of a 36,000 MT ammonia terminal at Pipavav and a Board-approved 52,000 MT LPG tank at JNPA.</overview>

qa_highlights.question: How should EBITDA per ton be viewed near term and structurally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR7,000+ per MT is sustainable. It expects the margin not to fall back to INR4,000, citing procurement gains from VLGC shipping as volumes rise.

qa_highlights.answer: 25% is the benchmark for logistics; anything above depends on the enablers. Distribution growth is expected to be higher, closer to 50%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not take inventory or price positions and will distribute on a monthly basis, rather than act as a trader.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash across subsidiaries fund the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: AVTL is self-funded through equity, and ITOCHU is planned to rise to 25% over three years. Standalone cash is around INR2,700 crore, and consolidated liquidity exceeds INR5,940 crore. Management will hold cash until it finds opportunities.

503101|2026-06.headline: Marathon Nextgen Q1 FY27 total income hit INR 217 crores, a multi-quarter high, with PAT of INR 52 crores and INR 900 crores of new redevelopment GDV added.
503101|2026-06.overview:
Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR 217 crores (multi-quarter high), EBITDA of INR 66 crores and PAT of INR 52 crores. Sales on the existing portfolio were 38,000 sq ft with booking value of INR 86 crores and collections of INR 118 crores (MNRL's 40% share of Monte South); including the merged portfolio, sales were 46,000 sq ft, booking value INR 108 crores and collections INR 146 crores. Two redevelopment projects (Versova and Sewri, INR 450 crores GDV each) were added, and the company says it is debt-free with about INR 200 crores of acquisition capital after a INR 900 crore QIP. The merger with group entities is awaiting NCLT shareholder and creditor meetings in early September 2026.</overview>

Operating EBITDA CAGR of about 40%-45% and PAT CAGR of about 35%-40% over FY25-FY28.
EBITDA margin expected to stabilise at about 12%-13% and PAT margin at about 5%-6% by FY28.
No specific FY27 revenue guidance given; management declined to quantify a quarterly run rate or Q2 trends.
ROCE expected to improve progressively as Bokaro commissions from Q2 FY27 and ramps up.
capex_capacity: Bokaro colour-coated line: hot trials ongoing; to be capitalised in Q2 FY27.
Cold rolling and Galvalume lines to be commissioned in subsequent quarters; full ramp across about 6 quarters through FY28.
Bokaro capital drawdown already in capital employed; plant not yet generating returns.
Certifications (ISO 9001, 14001, 45001, 17025, IATF 16949) not yet applied for; to be pursued after commissioning and stabilisation.
demand_pricing: Management says steel consumption growing 10%+ vs GDP of about 7-7.2%, supported by government infrastructure and private capex.
Colour-coated products demand growing 7%+; antidumping duties, QCOs, PLI and import substitution cited as supportive.

Fuel and power cost spike from Middle East conflict hit margins; industry-wide, so management sees a level playing field. Talks under way with customers to add gas price indexation to price variation mechanisms.
ZAM adoption encouraged by MNRE order for rooftop solar; company does not yet have ZAM customers and plans to offer Galvalume, galvanised and ZAM together.
Bokaro output of about 0.5 million tons vs India flat-product market of about 80-85 million tons; management calls it an entry-level position.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company give a Q2 or FY27 revenue run-rate and state how much revenue Bokaro will generate and when it reaches INR500 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide on FY27 or Q2 numbers. It said ramp-up will take at least 3-4 quarters for the 1,50,000-ton line, and the FY28 guidance is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Did the company collect the delayed receivables from a key customer in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said collections typically arrive in the first 1-2 weeks of a quarter, and all pending amounts were received at the start of Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a competitive moat in ZAM given the technical entry barriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 14 years of galvanising process experience and a planned full range of Galvalume, galvanised and ZAM. It acknowledged the company has no ZAM customers yet, so stickiness must be built over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand-supply outlook for colour-coated and galvanised products in the East, given new industry capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects steel demand growth to persist for 3-5 years, cited Eastern region catch-up and roofing/cladding, PEB and pre-galvanised structural demand, and said quality (not capacity) is the main differentiator.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company capitalised the colour-coated line and what is the industry landscape?
qa_highlights.answer: Capitalisation is expected in Q2 FY27 once hot trials finish. Management said colour-coated demand is growing 7%+ and that quality will matter more than capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the improved pipes and tubes and rolling mill utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Rolling mill improvement was demand and customer driven. Pipes and tubes utilisation rose from about 34% in FY26 to 40% annualised in Q1 FY27, which management expects to reach 65-70% by about FY29.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin pressure from fuel and power costs; gas price indexation in customer contracts is still under negotiation and not yet agreed.
Bokaro ramp-up execution (3-4 quarters per line) and capitalisation timing in Q2 FY27 will drive ROCE, which is currently 9.5%.
Pipes and tubes utilisation at about 40% leaves large unused capacity; delivery to the 65-70% target by about FY29 is unproven.
Rising colour-coated capacity in the East and quality concerns among domestic suppliers could pressure pricing.
Net debt of INR468.9 crores (0.57x D/E) with Bokaro debt still being drawn; leverage should be monitored.
Limited disclosure: management declined to give FY27 or Q2 numbers and did not give a timeline for certifications or export plans.
542669|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term targets and demand, but guarded on near-term numbers. Management repeatedly refused to give FY27 or Q2 figures and said Bokaro certification and export plans were too early. On margins, it attributed the EBITDA compression to fuel costs and said these had since eased.

543415|2026-06.headline: Anand Rathi Wealth Q1 FY27 underlying PAT rose 24% YoY to INR116 crore, with AUM up 21% to INR1,06,300 crore.
543415|2026-06.overview:
Management reported its 19th consecutive quarter of profit growth, with underlying consolidated revenue (excluding fair value gains, ESOP and related tax) up 18% YoY to INR336 crore and PAT up 24% to INR116 crore, a 34.4% margin. Reported revenue and PAT including fair value gains were INR430 crore and INR163 crore, with INR96 crore of the other income being mark-to-market gain on the Anand Rathi Global Finance (ARGFL) holding. Net flows were INR2,743 crore in the quarter, and client attrition was 0.09% of AUM with zero RM attrition. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR1,415 crore revenue and INR460 crore PAT, with Q1 delivering 24% and 25% of these respectively. The call also covered a Board approval to apply for an AMC licence, a UK subsidiary, and a GIFT City licence in progress.</overview>

segments.name: Flagship wealth management (ARWL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,06,300 crore, 13,941 client families after net addition of 1,600+ in last 12 months; client AUM attrition 0.09% in Q1 and zero RM attrition. AUM per RM described as rising, with 33 clients per RM.

segments.name: Digital wealth (B2B2C subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR2,526 crore, up 23% YoY; clients up 16% to 7,320.

segments.name: OFA (SaaS platform subsidiary)
segments.commentary: 6,890 subscribers and platform assets of INR1.66 lakh crore as of 30 June 2026.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: Net equity MF sales of INR1,900 crore in Q1. Management cites FY26 market share of net flows at 2.3% (presented as 2.47%), up from 0.18% in FY19-20; distributor yield about 1.09% post-GST, with 1-3 bps possible pressure from TER changes.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,415 crore and PAT guidance of INR460 crore reiterated; Q1 achieved 24% and 25% respectively.
Management modelled AUM growth of 20-25% p.a. over next 3 years: 10-12% from mark-to-market plus net sales of INR1,100-1,200 crore per month (about 1% of AUM per month).
Long-term target of about 4% share of AMFI Category II assets (around INR6 lakh crore in ~8-10 years), requiring 22-23% asset growth.
Board approved applying for an AMC licence; GIFT City licence in process (second stage underway).
capex_capacity: Board approved AMC licence application; first stage of licensing done, second stage in process per management.
UK subsidiary operations started in Q1; management said it would be built brick-by-brick, not scaled quickly.
Management cites capacity for about 6,500 new client families with existing RMs (33 clients per RM against capacity of ~50), plus 490 trained RMs and 100 more RMs about 60% ready.
Fund of funds in UK with 11 schemes listed there for UK participants.
demand_pricing: Net flows of INR2,743 crore in Q1 despite volatile markets; equity MF net sales INR1,900 crore.

Platinum families (INR50 crore+ bucket) about 230 vs 211 earlier; target 450-500 in two years. Upgrade rate from sub-INR5 crore to INR50 crore cohort guided at roughly 10-20% per quarter (management estimate).
Model portfolio of 14 mutual fund schemes beat Nifty by about 6% in Q1 (Nifty about 7%, portfolio about 7% after costs per management; figures as stated).

Structured products: management says ARGFL products dominate the mix; third-party share kept low for credit risk. Q1 MLD primary issuance INR2,187 crore (INR1,875 crore to group companies, INR312 crore third party), up from INR1,704 crore; secondary INR968 crore vs INR755 crore.
Client retention on three RM departures to a competitor: about 90% of INR758 crore assets retained as of June end (INR658.5 crore), excluding market movement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 update on Platinum families and how fast will the INR5-50 crore bucket upgrade?
qa_highlights.answer: Platinum families are about 230 vs 211 earlier, from 40-45 at launch about 2.5 years ago; upgrade rate estimated at 10-20% a quarter; management expects four-digit client counts in a few years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cap on AUM per RM?
qa_highlights.answer: No cap; management says AUM per RM should keep rising while client attrition stays low (0.09%), and some RMs have reached INR500-1,500 crore. The figure was INR100 crore at listing.

qa_highlights.question: How is asset allocation managed in volatile markets and why not recommend gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the highest portfolio beta is 0.6-0.65 and it sells products it buys; it does not recommend gold given household gold holdings of about 28% of savings. Overall mix is about INR55,000 crore equity and INR4,500 crore debt plus structured products.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the other income of INR110 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: INR96 crore is mark-to-market gain on ARGFL holding, revalued semi-annually by a third-party investment banker; the rest is interest on surplus cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is there yield pressure from TER changes in mutual funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pass-through is limited to 1-3 bps of its roughly 1.09% post-GST yield, and scale gives bargaining power; it has no plans to recommend stocks, PMS or long-only AIFs currently.

qa_highlights.question: Will ARWL enter investment banking or other capital market businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it will pursue only an AMC licence and no investment banking, focusing on intergenerational wealth rather than transaction-driven capital management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term AUM growth plan and how is it sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 20-25% AUM growth from embedded client returns, capacity in existing RMs, new RMs and penetration, citing 90-95% confidence; the 4% Category II target implies 22-23% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the RBI bank guarantee circular on derivatives volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management views the circular as positive, expecting reduced high-frequency trading volumes, and sees negligible or positive impact on ARWL.

540710|2026-06.headline: Capacite Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 7% to INR629 crore, but EBITDA fell 3% to INR99 crore after a INR10 crore commodity provision.

PAT fell to INR40 crore (6.2% margin) from INR47 crore, impacted by an additional INR10 crore provision for non-ferrous commodity price escalation not yet covered by government indices. Order book stood at INR13,535 crore, with FY27 inflow guidance of INR4,500-5,000 crore and INR1,071 crore booked so far.

qa_highlights.question: Capex increase from INR165 crore to INR193 crore?

qa_highlights.question: Gross debt rise to INR522 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase due to about INR150 crore of receipts shifted by 10 days, collected in the current month; management says annual gross and net debt will decline.

544058|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 5% YoY to about INR125 crore while gross margin was 61.6-62%. EBITDA declined from about INR31 crore to INR27 crore as advertising, brand building and retail transformation spend rose; PAT was INR2.3 crore (1.8% margin). Management said demand moderated from mid-May and remains measured, and that Mufti 2.0 benefits will take multiple quarters to show in numbers. The company opened 5 stores and closed 7, ending at 427 stores.

financial_highlights.change: down from about INR31 crore YoY

qa_highlights.answer: Management sees positive signals from renovated and new stores but said it is too early to project, and it will not give projections.

qa_highlights.question: Does premiumisation work in Tier 2 and 3 cities where about 59% of stores are?
qa_highlights.answer: Premiumisation is store-specific and calibrated to each local market and competitor set; it is not limited to Tier 1 cities.

qa_highlights.question: Is current marketing mainly for existing customers or for new ones?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: retention of existing customers and acquisition of new footfall.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue growth outpace the roughly INR5 crore YoY increase in marketing spend, and can growth recover within 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not confirm revenue growth above ad spend within a year; it said it is unable to extrapolate growth numbers for the next couple of years, while expecting to return to growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will inventory days hold steady or fall?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects some reduction; the CEO said inventory is cyclical and the company has had no write-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Can gross margin be cut to fund growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GP and pricing are reviewed every season and it will stay in the mid-premium segment, without committing to a margin cut.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression: EBITDA fell from about INR31 crore to INR27 crore YoY while marketing rose; watch whether revenue growth follows the marketing spend.

Competition from both Indian and foreign apparel brands, with some competitors spending above 15% of revenue on advertising.

Same-store revenue target of mid-single-digit growth against a flat store-count trend and a recent 3-year growth slowdown.

key_quotes: For the next 2-odd years, it's going to be very difficult for us to say what exactly the numbers will pan out.

Management said it expects about 20% CAGR, with potential to grow beyond 20% in coming years.
Ambernath depreciation is about Rs 14-15 crore; full-year overall depreciation is seen at Rs 35-40 crore.
capex_capacity: Patalganga land: all clearances received; Phase-1 capex about Rs 200 crore for API and utility blocks, with formulation blocks later in Phase-2; boundary wall construction has started.
Management expects about 40% completion around 2.5 years from acquisition, per MIDC requirements.
Block F at Lote: construction not yet started, expected to start in the next couple of quarters.
Ambernath: two anesthetic liquid inhalation products launched; EU GMP audit scheduled for second half of November 2026; CEP expected October-November 2026.
Contrast media (Iohexol) launch delayed about two quarters; now expected in H2 FY27 as R&D fine-tunes the technology.
Two ADHD product launches in the pipeline; SAP go-live expected in four to five months.
demand_pricing: Demand described as strong in Q1, but water shortage at Lote MIDC (Koyna river supply) cut production for about 15-20 days, deferring about Rs 35 crore of sales.
Company works on purchase-order basis and says it can pass on solvent, power and raw-material price increases to customers.
Solar tariff: Rs 4.5-5 crore retrospective charge, sub judice; management says the ToD-related and other increases will be passed through to customers.
Cardiovascular product: commercial-level volumes reached, but management said a larger contribution would take 9-12 months as customers complete qualification.
ATS-8 product: management reiterated 250 metric tonnes target over two years, not in the current year.

CMO/CDMO: term sheet close on a large anesthetic CDMO contract, expected to be announced next quarter; quality already approved; DSM vitamin ramp at near-peak volumes with a dedicated facility running.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Patalganga construction delayed, given Lote is full and greenfield pharma takes three to four years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said boundary-wall work has started and ground is broken. API blocks and utilities come first, as Lote is nearly capacity-exhausted; formulation blocks come in Phase-2. Ambernath is the formulation scale-up site.

qa_highlights.question: What is the customs/export issue and is there a provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a two-day lapse let an export authorisation expire before the shipping bill was raised. A new CBN export authorisation has been received, the matter is sub judice, and no provision has been made. Management said the consignment is small and limited to one shipment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost outlook for Q2 water and power, and is guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the water issue is resolved, the solar charge is largely retrospective, and price increases will be passed on. It reiterated FY27 guidance of close to Rs 1,000 crore revenue and 32-35% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambernath alone adds about Rs 14-15 crore; full-year depreciation is expected at about Rs 35-40 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How big is inventory and how will it unwind?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing inventory is about Rs 230-240 crore, built up for the planned shutdown. It will be liquidated over the next three to four quarters now that the shutdown is cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: Is there potential for growth above 20%, and what is the H2 ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 FY27 ramp-up will be much stronger than the current run rate, and growth beyond 20% is possible given CMO/CDMO, new products and capacity additions, subject to regulatory approvals.

543689|2026-06.headline: Uniparts Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR347 crore and EBITDA 55% to INR90 crore, with management guiding FY27 growth a few points above FY26's 21%.
543689|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR347 crore (+27% YoY), with EBITDA of INR90 crore (+55% YoY, +10% QoQ) and PAT of INR57 crore (+64% YoY, +11% QoQ). Management said the quarter was in line with its quarterly guidance and above its annual guidance. Construction equipment is now 45% of revenue and drove growth, while large ag is at its cyclical trough and growth there comes from new wins. Aftermarket was flat YoY in absolute terms but fell to about 12% of revenue as OEM business grew faster. Net cash is about INR190 crore and the company is debt-free, with about half a dozen acquisition targets under review.</overview>
