segments.name: Construction equipment
segments.commentary: Now 45% of total revenue and the main growth driver in Q1 FY27; momentum that began in 2H CY2025 has continued, supported by US and European infrastructure spend.

segments.name: Large agricultural equipment
segments.commentary: Conditions subdued; management expects about a 15-16% decline in CY2026 after about 30% in CY2025. Growth is from new wins, particularly in Europe, not market recovery.

segments.name: Small agricultural equipment
segments.commentary: India performing well on government subsidies and mid-to-high HP adoption, with strong new wins. Western small ag still soft but volumes have started recovering after three years of decline.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: About 12% of Q1 FY27 revenue (vs 15% in FY26 and 20% in FY25), flat YoY in absolute terms; tariff-driven price volatility deferred channel purchases.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth to be a couple of percentage points above FY26's 21% growth, per management; Q2 FY27 expected to be in line with Q1.
Management expects FY27 EBITDA margin comfortably above 20%; long-run cycle margin guidance remains about 20% (peak to trough).
Second half expected to be better than first half, linked to the ag recovery.
Mexico facility: first customer deliveries from the warehouse expected in Q3 FY27; FY27 Mexico revenue in mid-single-digit USD million.
Warehouse sales expected to stay in a 52-56% range over the next 12-18 months.
Material cost range of 34-37% of revenue is considered sustainable; fabrication vertical expected to become meaningful in 18-24 months.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex of INR12 crore; organic capex (fresh equipment plus repairs and maintenance) guided at 2.5-3.5% of revenue.
Fabrication facility for small and medium-sized fabrication set up about 2.5 years ago; now in deep discussions with OEMs to supply fabrications.
Restoration of the Ludhiana finishing shop is on schedule; customer supply uninterrupted.
Mexico operations on track; Phase 2 may add manufacturing in Mexico.
demand_pricing: Channel mix: warehouse sales about 56% of Q1 FY27 revenue (vs 50-52% in Q1 FY26); locally made and locally sold about 22% (vs about 25%); the balance is direct exports.
Margin hierarchy by channel: locally made and sold is lowest; direct exports are the base (about 20% margin); warehouse sales are highest.
Product margins stated as broadly similar across three-point linkage, precision machined parts and fabrication; material consumption differs by product mix.
New business order book over INR225 crore on a trailing 12-month basis; new wins split roughly equally between Europe and US, with the majority of wins in ag and construction.
Above-70 HP three-point linkage is a single-digit market share with a major European OEM win in FY26; below-70 HP is dominant share globally.

qa_highlights.question: Will the construction share of revenue structurally rise and can it be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said construction is 45% of revenue; drivers (new wins, industry recovery, wallet expansion) are multi-quarter. Mix will rebalance as ag recovers.

qa_highlights.question: Is construction higher margin than tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Product margins are fairly similar; differences come from channel. Warehouse sales are highest margin, direct exports about 20% base, and locally made/sold lowest.

qa_highlights.question: What is the update on acquisitions and their revenue timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About a dozen targets evaluated since IPO in hydraulics, fabrication and PTO; about half a dozen currently under close review. Targets must be ROCE/ROE accretive within 18-30 months, manageable, and not deeply distressed.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the 33.3% material cost and the gross margin level?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly product mix (three-point linkage, precision machined parts, fabrication have different material consumption), plus channel mix; inventory gain only about INR1 crore. Material cost range 34-37% is typical.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the aftermarket?
qa_highlights.answer: Flat in absolute terms YoY; demand deferred by tariffs and inflation. Management expects normalisation over the next 12 months as tariffs have come down.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to gain share in large ag?
qa_highlights.answer: Share is lower due to OEM validation and testing cycles; FY26 wins are now flowing into P&L, and deep discussions are ongoing on several opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2.5-3.5% capex guidance inclusive of acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It covers organic capex (fresh equipment and R&M). Acquisitions would use the INR190 crore cash and could involve debt; the balance sheet is strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 and H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 expected to be in line with Q1 and robust; H2 expected to be better than H1, tied to the ag recovery.

risks_watch: Large ag remains at cyclical trough in CY2026 (about 15-16% decline expected); recovery is only expected through CY2027.
Western small ag recovery is early and consumer buying for big-ticket items remains deferred due to economic uncertainty.
Aftermarket softness: tariffs and West Asia-driven inflation; management expects normalisation over the next 12 months.
Input cost and supply chain pressure from the West Asia situation.
Margin sensitivity to warehouse sales mix, currency movements and industry recovery pace.
Acquisition execution: no deal yet despite about a dozen targets evaluated since IPO; timing and value accretion uncertain.
Mexico warehouse ramp: first deliveries expected Q3 FY27.

541929|2026-06.headline: Synergy Green Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹75.71 crore and 7% PBDIT margin were weak; management reiterates ₹500 crore FY27 revenue and 300 bps margin uplift.
541929|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 total income was ₹75.71 crore with absolute PBDIT of ₹5.3 crore at a 7% margin, as dispatches slipped on customer lifting, prototype approval delays and shipping constraints. Production rose about 10% YoY and the new 45,000 tpa capacity reached 66% utilisation in Q1, with July utilisation at 85% (about 3,200 tons). Raw material, consumable and energy inflation (linked to the West Asia conflict and an MSEDCL solar banking change) cut margins, which management expects to partly recover from Q2 via one-quarter-lagged indexation. Management maintained FY27 guidance of ~₹500 crore revenue (33% growth) and ~300 bps PBDIT margin expansion.</overview>

segments.name: Wind foundry (SG iron, grey iron, steel castings, 3-30 MT)
segments.commentary: Capacity expanded from 30,000 to 45,000 tpa; FY26 utilisation was 93% on old capacity. Q1 utilisation 66% on new capacity, July at 85%, with 80-90% targeted within 2-3 months.

segments.name: Machining (in-house)
segments.commentary: Machining capacity 20,000 tpa; product development 50% complete and utilisation reached 50% in July. Target 40-50% in-house machining, reducing outsourcing costs.

segments.name: Non-wind (power, mining, L&T, BHEL, Terex)
segments.commentary: BHEL PO received in Q1 (8-9 months development); L&T development underway. Terex order book strong on yen appreciation (~20% vs INR). Non-wind and gearboxes ~30% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance ~₹500 crore (33% growth), reiterated despite weak Q1.
FY27 full-year PBDIT margin to improve ~300 bps YoY, driven by volumes, export concentration in H2 and machining contribution.
Q2 expected to see indexation recoveries on raw material (~200 bps) and partial consumables recovery; new customer revenues from Q2.
Utilisation target of 80% on full 45,000 tpa capacity for FY27; 80-90% within 2-3 months from July.
Executable order book positioned at ₹500 crore for FY27; ₹600 crore achievable next year with higher capacity.
Land for 100,000 tpa project targeted by December or March; next project start by Q3 of next year; fundraising ideally Q1/Q2 2028.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 45,000 tpa (expanded from 30,000 tpa); in-house machining 20,000 tpa; 10 MW captive solar.
Plan for 100,000 tpa capacity; land acquisition targeted by December or March; greenfield capex takes 15-18 months to commission.
Additional 5 MW wind PPA via open access to offset power cost inflation; solar + PPA to cover 50-60% of power needs.
Vestas 4 MW platform: tooling started mid-May; samples expected Q4 FY27, full production Q1 FY28. Nordex NX N 5 MW prototypes cleared in Q1.
Inventory held at 8-10 weeks; target to keep shop order book below 8 weeks.
demand_pricing: Q1 dispatches lower due to delayed customer material lifting and prototype approvals with a key customer; export rollouts hit by ship availability amid West Asia conflict. Unsold production went into inventory.
Furan Resin (third-largest cost item) rose ~60%; PNG/LNG prices up 60-70%; pig iron and CRC inflation from shortages and imported scrap logistics.
Realisations expected to rise from ₹138-140/kg to ₹145+ levels in coming quarters; management said no change in realisation in Q1.
Vestas ~40-45% of business historically, expected to fall toward ~30% as new OEMs (Nordex, Adani) are added; Nordex growing; Adani 3.3 MW in serial production.
Indian suppliers estimated 5-10% cheaper than China on landed cost for wind products after yen appreciation; US market favours non-Chinese suppliers.
Management views wind demand stronger than solar; night-time wind tariffs 25% higher than solar daytime, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Could the ₹500 crore FY27 target slip into next year given slow offtake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 production was strong but did not convert to sales; Q2 execution is at a much higher flow rate, and product approval has come from 50% of customers.

qa_highlights.question: Did realisations spike given 66% utilisation implies ~7,400 MT?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said produced material was not all sold, creating inventory, and realisation is unchanged, with revenue recognition pending.

qa_highlights.question: Is other income of ₹4.4 crore from power sales?
qa_highlights.answer: No; likely FX-related or export incentives. Management has not sold power; solar lapsed units were lost under the MSEDCL policy change.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the ₹600-700 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Renamed the executable order book; ₹500 crore set for FY27 given hurdles, with ₹600 crore possible next year on higher capacity.

qa_highlights.question: When will the next capex and fundraising happen?
qa_highlights.answer: Two or three good quarters needed first; land by December or March; project start by Q3 next year; fundraising ideally Q1/Q2 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Will Vestas concentration stay the same at ~₹600 crore revenue in two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Vestas wants more allocation but capacity is going to new OEMs (Nordex, Adani) each allocating ₹100-150 crore; wind is ~₹400 crore of revenue, non-wind and gearboxes ~30%.

qa_highlights.question: Is offshore wind or Adani 5 MW participation viable?
qa_highlights.answer: Adani 5 MW parts often exceed 30 MT, so imported from China; Adani 5.2 MW bearing (6-7 ton casting) supplied. Offshore volumes not expected for 5-10 years; company focuses on 3-4 MW onshore.

544487|2026-06.headline: Patel Retail Q1 FY27 total income rose 69.35% YoY to INR310.24 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to about 6.3% on raw material intensity.
544487|2026-06.overview: Total income reached INR310.24 crores, up 69.35% YoY from INR183.19 crores, while EBITDA grew 23.92% to INR19.68 crores and PAT rose 37.43% to INR9.52 crores (EPS INR2.85). Management attributed the margin compression (about 133 bps decline cited, and a 233 bps figure also mentioned) to a higher raw-material-intensity mix in manufacturing, export and commodity-linked business amid volatile raw material prices and odd order timing. The company added stores at Rasayani and Babgaon in Q1 and opened its 53rd store at Uran (Raigad) after quarter-end, and expanded Indian Chaska into Madhya Pradesh. Management guided to positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 and 8 to 10 new stores in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +69.35% YoY vs INR183.19 crores in Q1 FY26
decline of 133 bps as stated (233 bps also cited in same answer)

financial_highlights.value: around INR101 crores (as referenced by analyst)

financial_highlights.metric: Private label contribution to retail sales

segments.name: Retail (Patel R-Mart)
segments.commentary: 53 stores after Uran opening; average monthly sales per store put at INR80 lakh to INR1 crore, mature-store sales about INR20,000 per sq ft; ticket size INR500 to INR1,000; wastage below 0.1%. Payback about 24 months.

segments.name: Manufacturing / food processing
segments.commentary: Utilisation currently 50% to 55%, targeted at around 80% to 82% by FY27-FY28; automation expected to cut labour cost and improve quality consistency. Private label share of domestic sales cited at 45%, export sales at 37%.

segments.name: Exports and B2B
segments.commentary: Management stated about 40% of revenue from exports and rest from manufacturing and retail; export contribution to bottom line cited as 35% to 40%. These figures were not reconciled in the call.

segments.name: Indian Chaska (brand)
segments.commentary: Expanded to Madhya Pradesh in August 2026, taking presence to eight states and one union territory; MP averaging INR10 lakh to INR12 lakh per month; whole spices category to be added this quarter.

segments.name: Online / quick commerce
segments.commentary: App has more than 50,000 downloads but online sales were around INR50 lakh in Q1; private label not yet listed on Blinkit or Zepto, with per-SKU terms being finalised; pilot quick commerce running from first stores.

segments.name: Apparel and fashion (general merchandise)
segments.commentary: 8% to 9% of revenue; inventory holding period 15 to 20 days.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to move back toward 8% to 9% over coming quarters, with margin in Q1 not treated as steady state.
Positive operating cash flow expected by H1 FY27; conversion of current assets built up in FY26 into cash targeted.
8 to 10 new stores targeted by FY27, each expected to generate about INR1 crore per month in revenue.
Capacity utilisation targeted at around 80% to 82% by end-FY27 to FY28.
Expansion into Western suburbs and Pune/PCMC over the next five years, cluster-based; more gaps still being identified.
capex_capacity: Current processing utilisation 50% to 55%; medium-term target 80% to 82%.
New store payback about 24 months to recover capex and inventory rotation; store size and investment about 5,000 to 6,000 per sq ft as stated.
Automation being introduced at processing facilities, aimed at labour cost reduction and unified quality.
Store additions in Q1 at Rasayani and Babgaon; Uran (53rd store) opened after quarter-end.
Pune/PCMC store economics said to be broadly similar to existing network; 2 to 3 pockets identified.
demand_pricing: Management attributed Q1 margin decline to higher raw material intensity in export and commodity-linked business and volatile raw material prices.
Mature-store sales about INR20,000 per sq ft (retail); average monthly sales per store INR80 lakh to INR1 crore.
Online remains touch-and-feel in Tier-2/3/4 locations; society-focused activation and 30-60 minute delivery trials underway.
Private label planned as combo packs (e.g., rice, dal, salt) to make per-SKU listing and ad costs sustainable on quick commerce.
Plans to launch 2 to 3 more Indian Chaska categories (e.g., protein-related) from next quarter, targeting categories with INR2,000 to 3,000 crore market size.

qa_highlights.question: What must improve to move EBITDA margin from about 6.3% back to 8% to 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 decline was due to higher raw material intensity in manufacturing, export and commodity-linked mix and volatile raw material prices; it expects improvement in coming quarters and not treating Q1 as steady state.

qa_highlights.question: Positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 still on track, and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 balance sheet and cash flow not yet published; expects much better operating cash flow by H1, converting FY26 current-asset build into cash.

qa_highlights.question: How many new stores in FY27 and revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: 8 to 10 stores by FY27, expected to contribute around INR1 crore per month in revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation 50% to 55%; targeted around 80% to 82% in the medium term, by end-FY27 to FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Share of own brands across channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Own brands about 17.5% of overall revenue; private label 17.55% of retail sales, 37% of export sales and 45% of domestic sales as stated by the CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Performance of recently opened stores vs older stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new stores are operationally breakeven since day one, with some growing strongly; payback target about 24 months.

risks_watch: Margin recovery to 8% to 9% depends on raw material cost stability; Q1 EBITDA margin about 6.3%.
Operating cash flow guidance for H1 FY27 unverified; balance sheet and cash flow not yet published; inventory and receivables elevated after FY26 build.
Online and quick commerce traction remains small (about INR50 lakh in Q1) and competition from platform in-house brands noted by analysts.
Internal inconsistencies in disclosed figures (133 bps vs 233 bps margin decline; export share 40% vs 35% to 40% export contribution to bottom line) need clarification.
Store maturity: some stores still not up to mark per management; 8 to 10 new stores in FY27 execution.
544487|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on growth and store ramp-up but cautious and somewhat non-specific on margin and cash flow timing; several answers deferred figures (e.g., online targets, five-year scale) and the call had audio breaks during key answers.

524164|2026-06.headline: IOL Chemicals Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR756 crore and PAT 90% to INR64.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.6%.
524164|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR756 crore against INR551 crore a year earlier, up 37%. EBITDA rose 60.7% to INR111 crore, lifting margin to 14.6% from 12.4%, and PAT grew 89.9% to INR64.5 crore. Management attributed the gains to higher capacity utilisation, product mix, export realisations and operational efficiencies, and said there was no material inventory gain in the quarter. FY27 guidance was retained at 15-20% revenue growth, 14-15% EBITDA margin and 25-30% exports, with management saying revenue could exceed the INR2,600-2,700 crore range but not upgrading guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs 36% in Q1 FY26; non-ibu revenue up 67% YoY
Management did not split volume vs price

segments.name: Pharmaceuticals (API)
segments.commentary: Non-ibuprofen products were 43% of pharma revenue, up 67% YoY; growth described as broad-based across the portfolio. Most assets run at 80-95% utilisation, with paracetamol lower at about 55% of enhanced 10,800 MTPA capacity.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Management said the chemical segment margin trended up in the quarter, helped by higher ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride capacity, better realisations and higher exports. Triacetin plant (6,000 MTPA) started production only in May 2026, with steady-state revenue potential of about INR120 crore a year.

guidance_outlook: FY27: revenue growth of 15-20% (management said around 20% in Q&A), EBITDA margin 14-15%, exports about 25-30% of revenue.
Management said the INR2,600-2,700 crore full-year revenue guidance remains unchanged, may be crossed in the current scenario, but will not be upgraded.
FY28 (indicative, conditional on current scenario): revenue growth 15-20% and EBITDA margin 15-17%.
Near term: non-ibuprofen to reach about 50% of pharma revenue, with roughly 50% ibuprofen; by FY29, non-ibu expected at 50-55% of API segment with margins similar to ibuprofen.
Capex of about INR200 crore a year; about 60% expansion and new products, 40% infrastructure and efficiency. Next major project on the 101-acre land is not expected in FY27.
Regulatory: two to three more quarters expected for Triacetin approvals.
capex_capacity: Paracetamol capacity tripled from 3,600 MTPA to 10,800 MTPA; operating at about 55%, targeted near 70% by end FY27.
Triacetin plant of 6,000 MTPA commenced production in May 2026; capacity to ramp as market penetration grows. Inputs are acetic acid and glycerol.
Capacity of ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride increased during the period.
Capex of around INR200 crore per year, with INR100-200 crore spent annually over the last four to five years.
R&D spend of INR26 crore in FY26; analytical equipment bought (XRD, LCMS, GCMS).
101-acre land parcel held for future expansion; statutory permissions in process; no project expected to commission in FY27.
demand_pricing: Healthy demand across paracetamol, pantoprazole, metformin, fenofibrate, clopidogrel and levetiracetam. Management said price increases were passed on to customers.

Ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride prices rose sharply in March 2026 after the US-Iran conflict; since then prices have been stable to slightly easing, and management expects the raw-material-to-ethyl-acetate spread to hold.
Energy and logistics costs rose in the quarter; management said most of the increase was passed on.
Sequential gross margin fell as input costs rose before finished-product prices fully caught up. Some prices were pre-agreed with large customers.
Exports: some export customers have agreed quantities, so the export share can move quarter to quarter.

Regulatory: CEP approval for all products; US FDA approval for five products, with two to three more pending ANDA approval by formulators; NMPA China approval for clopidogrel; ibuprofen previously approved in China.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for paracetamol given weak demand in past years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity was tripled to 10,800 MTPA, utilisation is about 55%, and it expects about 70% by year-end. Demand is growing, with domestic traction and exports.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 profit came from one-time inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no material inventory gain this quarter; a 10-15 day benefit existed at the end of Q4 FY26. The improvement was attributed to utilisation, mix, efficiencies and export realisations.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA outperformance came from operating leverage versus mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin gain mainly to internal efficiencies and higher utilisation, with no major product mix change apart from greater export penetration.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a split of pharma growth between volume and price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a numerical split. It said the majority came from higher volumes, with higher export realisations also contributing, and most assets at 80-95% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth muted in prior quarters and how long will demand last?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher volumes, better pricing on established products and new products, and cost pass-through. It said there is reasonable order-book visibility for the coming quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Triacetin revenue potential and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Production started only after May 2026, so about one month was in Q1. Steady-state revenue potential is about INR120 crore a year from the 6,000 MTPA plant. Management declined to compare its margin with ethyl acetate.

risks_watch: Raw material and energy price volatility (linked to the US-Iran conflict); margin sensitivity to lag in passing through costs.
Export share (28.5% in Q1) may fall back toward the 25-30% guidance band if customer agreed quantities shift.
Paracetamol utilisation at about 55% against the target of 70% by year-end.
Pending US FDA approvals for two to three ANDA-linked products and Triacetin regulatory approvals expected in two to three quarters.
FY28 margin outlook is explicitly conditional on the current scenario; management said it may not hold if conditions change within six months.
Lack of disclosure on the volume versus price split and on the regulated versus non-regulated export mix.
524164|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the diversification story, but guarded on forward numbers: management held guidance, declined to upgrade it, and said FY28 targets depend on current conditions. It was evasive on the pharma volume/price split, the R&D pipeline, CMO opportunities and the regulated-market export mix.

544133|2026-06.headline: Exicom Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 57% YoY to INR237 crore with EBITDA margin at 8.8%; consolidated EBITDA loss narrowed to INR22 crore.
544133|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 57% YoY to INR236.8 crore, with Critical Power up 80% to INR176 crore and EV up 15% to INR61 crore. Standalone EBITDA more than doubled to INR20.9 crore (8.8% margin), helped by operating leverage and richer mix. Consolidated revenue rose 61% to INR331.1 crore, but consolidated EBITDA was a loss of INR21.9 crore (down from INR38.6 crore loss), as Tritium margins normalised after drawing down low-cost acquired inventory. Management guided to consolidated EBITDA breakeven within two quarters and Tritium breakeven by Q4 FY27, while working capital rose on parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad plant operations and higher receivables.

segments.name: Critical Power (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR176-177 crore, up 73-80% YoY and down ~11% QoQ; BharatNet is among the largest contributors, with a 60% share in that project per management. Export sales about INR15 crore (~8% of Critical Power).

segments.name: EV Charging (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR61 crore, up 15% YoY but down QoQ from Q4 DC-charger pull-forward; consolidated EV grew 50%. FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of total.

segments.name: Tritium (consolidated, US DC fast charging)
segments.commentary: Revenue about USD10-10.5 million in Q1, second consecutive quarter above USD10 million; bookings about USD20.8-21 million, roughly double the usual ~USD10 million per quarter.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA breakeven expected within the next two quarters (management could not specify Q2 or Q3).
Tritium EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27, with 3x revenue growth versus last year targeted.
Standalone Critical Power exports targeted to rise from ~8% to ~15% of Critical Power sales within FY27.
AC charger monthly run rate expected to rise ~50% over the next three months.
Parallel-run fixed costs (~INR8.7 crore in Q1) expected to phase out as Gurgaon transition completes over coming quarters.
Tritium large strategic contracts (USD20-30 million for CY27 from Fortune 100 trials, USD20 million GRID-FLEX from hyperscaler) contingent on trial success.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad plant commissioned in Q4 FY26 and fully in production in Q1 FY27; management says it gives 3x production capability versus Gurgaon.
Standalone depreciation rose ~67% YoY, and management said standalone D&A increase was INR10-12 crore.
Management said DC charger utilisation is ~65% (90-100% for DC power system lines), AC charger ~100%, and PCBA and battery lines ~100%.
Ordered an additional AC charger line; management said the Hyderabad plant was built for ~2x AC capacity.
Tritium US factory capacity is about USD100 million a year versus ~USD10 million current quarterly revenue run rate (about one-quarter utilised).
demand_pricing: Critical Power order book ~INR1,000 crore; consolidated order book INR1,400 crore-plus as of 30 June 2026.
Large DC power system order of INR85 crore from a leading Indian telco; supply agreement with a large tower company for power systems and batteries.
BharatNet: INR700 crore open orders plus ~INR800 crore of service orders over 10 years; BSNL Phase 2 expected ~2,000 sites at INR90-100 crore.
BESS (commercial and industrial, mostly under 0.5 MWh): ~15 MWh orders worth ~INR20 crore in hand and ~34 MWh (INR45 crore) in advanced pipeline.
EV charger order book about INR200 crore for AC/DC chargers in India plus ~USD2 million export orders; 10 new export countries won; 15 new network operators added in Q1.
Margins on some large orders were hit by forex and commodity price increases, partly offset by volumes.
Supply disruptions in semiconductors, plastics and copper were cited as the main constraint, not capacity.

532700|2026-06.headline: Domestic revenue fell 1.9% YoY to INR111 crore in Q1 FY27, while EBITDA rose 42% to INR8.8 crore on cost cuts and Digital grew 43.3%.
532700|2026-06.overview: Management attributed the soft quarter to the West Asia conflict, which caused event cancellations, curtailed artist travel and lower advertiser demand across media. Digital (Gaana) revenue rose 43.3% YoY to INR31.1 crore and its losses narrowed, with management targeting breakeven as soon as possible. Cost rationalisation drove the EBITDA and PAT improvement, with non-digital EBITDA up 7.4% and PAT up 85%. Management gave no numerical guidance and said the Events business is H2-weighted.

financial_highlights.change: +43.3% YoY; 30.2% of total revenue vs 23% last year
vs INR17.9 crore last year (~19% growth)
vs INR9.8 crore last year (~15% lower)

segments.name: Radio (FCT advertising)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR62.2 crore, about 56% of total revenue. Inventory utilisation fell about 8% while rates rose about 4%. Volume market share was about 27-28%.

segments.name: Digital (Gaana)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR31.1 crore (+43.3%), with Gaana at INR21.4 crore (+19%). Losses fell to INR8.3 crore from INR9.8 crore. Around 70% of subscribers are on profitable price points.

segments.name: Non-FCT / Events
segments.commentary: Non-FCT revenue INR17.5 crore, hit by event cancellations and artist travel disruption. Management says Events is about 35:65 H1:H2 and that Q1 and Q2 are seasonally subdued.

guidance_outlook: Management gave no formal profitability guidance for FY27.
Traditional media (Radio, TV, Print) expected to stay subdued through FY27.
Events expected to grow and to be strong from Q2 onward; some international artist concerts moved from Q1 into Q2.
Cost-model restructuring (station networking, AI, new broadcast tools) expected to benefit all quarters of FY27, with no quantum given.
Gaana targeted for breakeven as soon as possible; a quarter-level slip is possible if customer acquisition costs rise.
Gaana monthly pricing is about 10% below competition; annual pricing retains headroom; price raised to INR799.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning figures were discussed on the call.
demand_pricing: Radio advertiser demand remained soft in Q1 FY27 owing to macro and geopolitical uncertainty; management said the pressure extends across TV, print and outdoor.
Radio rates improved about 4% despite inventory utilisation falling about 8%.
Gaana subscription pricing moved to INR799; the company says it is the only pure-subscription service in India, versus free and premium tiers at competitors.
Management says the industry is moving toward subscription, citing Universal Music's 72-hour exclusivity for premium subscribers and Spotify's free-tier restrictions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the radio advertising weakness only due to West Asia, and will the company diversify beyond media?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the weakness is an industry-wide shift away from traditional advertising plus geopolitical impact. It said the three verticals are Radio, Digital and Events, and that the company will stay in media while experimenting with AI.

qa_highlights.question: Will Events cancellations be recovered, and what is the seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Some events moved into Q2, including international artist concerts. Events is roughly 35:65 H1:H2 and Q1 and Q2 are normally subdued.

qa_highlights.question: What cost savings can be expected and what is the profitability outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify savings and cited networking of stations, AI and new broadcast tools. It declined to give profitability guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What are Gaana's subscriber profitability and path to breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of subscribers are at profitable margins. Management aims for breakeven as soon as possible, with the lower-value subscriber base being churned out.

qa_highlights.question: Would a buyback be considered with INR390 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a Board discussion and that the feedback would be taken.

qa_highlights.question: Has industry subscriber growth moderated, and how is pricing positioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said annual pricing has headroom, monthly pricing is about 10% below competition, and the industry is moving toward subscription. It did not give subscriber growth data.

risks_watch: Radio advertising remains soft; management expects traditional media to stay subdued through FY27.
Gaana still loss-making at INR8.3 crore in the quarter; breakeven timing is open, and CAC increases could delay it.
Event cancellations and artist travel disruption from the West Asia conflict, with Q2 recovery dependent on the timing of international concerts.
Buyback request from shareholders is pending a Board decision; no commitment made.
Cost-saving quantum not disclosed, so the EBITDA trajectory beyond Q1 is unclear.
532700|2026-06.management_tone: Confident about Digital and Events and about the subscription model, but cautious and non-committal on Radio demand, cost savings and profitability. Management declined to quantify savings, guide on profitability or commit to a buyback.
key_quotes: Encouraging to note that despite prevailing macro headwinds, the non -digital business improved profitability, delivering EBITDA growth of 7.4% and PAT growth of 85% during the quarter.

So the entire industry and all streaming players believe that for music industry to grow, it is the only way it's going to be through subscription, which we have been doing for the last 2 years, we believe, on subscription economy only.
Generally, Ronak, we don't provide any guidance on this.

544144|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~44% YoY to INR1,890 crore and reported EBITDA rose ~87% to INR71.5 crore (3.8% margin), with reported PBT turning positive at INR1.9 crore.
544144|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations grew about 44% YoY to INR1,890 crore, with new vehicle volumes up about 81% reported and about 91% like-to-like. Reported EBITDA rose about 87% to INR71.5 crore, margin 3.8% vs 2.9%, helped by a one-off ~INR5 crore lease-modification gain in other income. Organic revenue grew 33% YoY, indicating the existing network contributed alongside the FY26 acquisitions (RKS Maruti, Globe CV BharatBenz, Audi/Olympus). Management said the acquired businesses are now EBITDA-positive in aggregate (~INR9.4 crore) but still loss-making below EBITDA due to depreciation and finance costs; reported PAT was INR1.4 crore vs a loss of INR8.8 crore a year ago.</overview>

segments.name: Passenger Vehicles (ex-luxury)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR836 crore (+73% YoY reported, +54% excluding luxury per call); new vehicles 10,475 units (+83%); service volumes 1,90,801 (-5%) while service income INR169 crore (+11%). Organic PV revenue +49%. PV EBITDA margin ~4% per management, with Maruti ~15.5-16% and JLR ~17-18% at segment level.

segments.name: Luxury (JLR and Audi)
segments.commentary: Reported revenue +42%; new vehicles +39%; service volumes +87%. Organic luxury revenue +21%, service volumes +9%. JLR EBITDA INR10.5 crore vs INR8.2 crore a year ago; Audi EBITDA ~nil, with margin dip attributed to Audi.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles
segments.commentary: Revenue INR564 crore (+33% reported, +35% per call; organic +21%); new vehicles 3,495 units (+41%); service volumes 52,647 (+15%), service income INR107 crore (+47%). Sequentially volumes moderated vs Q4. Management cites CV EBITDA ~3.6-3.75%.

segments.name: EV (Ather two-wheelers and e-VITARA)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR55 crore (+122% YoY; reported EV revenue +113%); new vehicles 3,330 units (+153%); service volumes 13,232 (+60%), service income ~INR3 crore. EBITDA ~INR2 crore; margin ~3.4%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects acquired businesses to be PAT-positive from Q2 FY27 onwards; RKS and Olympus targeted for PAT profitability by end of Q3, with Olympus possibly one more quarter.
RKS service volumes expected on track by Q4 FY27.
PV service volume growth expected at ~6-7% from Q2 (not the 15% previously guided), with ASP continuing to rise; Maruti service volumes expected to reach double digit from Q2.
Blended EBITDA margin: management hopes to reach ~4% and says ~4.3-4.4% by year end; 5% unlikely this year unless mix changes.
FY27 revenue targeted at INR8,200-8,300 crore vs ~INR6,400 crore in FY26 (~20-25% growth).
H2 PV growth so far running ~80-90% YoY in most months, expected to moderate on high base; Q3 flagged as key with Audi launch.
Capex limited to replacement and ongoing projects; no acquisition or expansion planned; surplus cash to be used first for debt reduction.
capex_capacity: Q1 network additions: new Maruti Suzuki service centre at Koyilandy (Kerala), two Tata CV outlets at Perumbavoor and Kazhakuttam, and a JLR sales and service facility in Nagpur.
New vehicle inventory ~32 days vs ~50 days a year ago; absolute inventory up only ~14% YoY despite higher revenue; sequential build ahead of festive season and OEM launches.
Audi inventory elevated, expected to fall to ~20-25 days in August-September.
Ather inventory ~5 days, JLR supply somewhat constrained.
Keralam revenue share fell below 50% for the first time (49%), state mix: Tamil Nadu 22%, Karnataka 12%, Telangana 8%, Maharashtra 5%, Punjab 4%, Andhra Pradesh 0.3%.
demand_pricing: Pre-festive inquiries up ~20% YoY over recent days, ~17-18% over the last month; bookings up ~22% YoY.
Keralam inauspicious period ends 16 August; retail expected to pick up from 17 August (Onam-Chingam).
CV demand weak in construction: tipper segment low to negative growth; SCV and cargo holding.
Maruti price increases modest (INR5,000-7,000 for most models; INR10,000-15,000 for some), with no major impact on demand or margin.
Entry-level cars recovered: Alto K10 and WagonR strong; S-Presso slowing; Arena returned to growth.
Spare parts short supply in the market, causing vehicles to stay in workshops.
Running repairs up ~8.8% in July; free service turned to growth in Q1.
Commercial ticket size ~INR16-17 lakh is pulling blended margin down.

531213|2026-06.headline: Manappuram Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 45% QoQ to INR585 crore, with consolidated AUM up 9% QoQ to INR69,635 crore.

526247|2026-06.headline: Premier Explosives Q1 FY27 revenue fell 28% YoY to INR102.6 crore, EBIT margin 4.7%, order book INR1,393 crore (94% defence).
526247|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations declined 28% YoY to INR102.6 crore as dispatches and project execution slipped, mainly on export deliveries held up by maritime disruption and imported countermeasure components. EBIT fell 80% YoY to INR4.8 crore (4.7% margin) and PAT fell 80% to INR3 crore (3% margin), with raw material costs squeezing margins. Management said the export licence backlog is largely cleared and expects the delayed execution to complete in Q2 and Q3. Order book stands at INR1,393 crore, and FY27 revenue target is retained at about INR600 crore. Apollo Micro Systems' acquisition of promoter stake was discussed, with synergy details deferred to next quarter.</overview>

segments.name: Defence and Space
segments.commentary: Revenue declined about 35% YoY per analyst question; management attributed delays to export licences and component imports, not customer acceptance. Defence is 94% of the order book.

segments.name: Industrial explosives / bulk
segments.commentary: About 6% of order book. Singareni execution of about INR25-30 crore remains for FY27; margins described as very thin, with some contracts negative. Coal India work withdrawn.

segments.name: Services (O&M)
segments.commentary: INR42 crore of order book (3%), no separate commentary on quarterly performance.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target retained at about INR600 crore (analyst-reported INR600-700 crore earlier); management said Q1 revenue of about INR103 crore leaves 9 months to deliver INR500-600 crore.
EBITDA margin target of 15-20% for the year, reiterated; management said the gap in Q1 would be made up in coming quarters.
FY27 order inflow expected at INR200-300 crore; management said run rate of INR1,000 crore-plus per year over the next two years.
Export execution targeted at INR150-200 crore in Q2 FY27, with prior-quarter export backlogs expected to clear in the quarter.
Order of INR430 crore (Oct 2025) to be fully executed in FY27 per management, versus earlier guidance of about two-thirds; Q1 execution was about INR21 crore.
Other expenses run-rate of INR9-10 crore per quarter cited as sustainable.
Katepally RDX/HMX water trials expected in September 2026 (about one month); mixing plant dummy trials expected by end September after imported mixer components are airlifted.
capex_capacity: Katepally: RDX and HMX plant integration and erection almost complete; water trials expected September 2026, lasting about one month before production.
Katepally mixing plant: 2.5 tonne planetary mixer installed; imported components delayed by shipping, now being airlifted; dummy trials targeted end-September 2026.
Andhra Pradesh expansion: land pricing unresolved; company has asked the state government to revise price. Management said Apollo would continue the expansion, with a decision after presentation.
Flares produced in own plant; production has started on the July 2023 flares order, with backlog of about INR75 crore to complete in 4-5 months. Chaff payload depends on imports, now executed.
Drones: company builds payloads and partners with drone makers as a partner, not a standalone supplier.
demand_pricing: Export licences: several received in the past week, with some in pipeline; material moving out of factories. Export of INR150-200 crore targeted in Q2.

INR350 crore international defence order (April 2026): export licence still in process; management said licence processing takes at least 3-4 months after importing-country import licence; some dispatches expected in the last quarter of the year.
Bulk explosives: pricing tied to raw material costs; more than 40 players in the segment; management declined to predict FY28.
RDX/HMX: international demand good, but licences difficult; management said war-driven demand has lifted prices for now.
Alternate raw material for mines/loitering munitions under DRDO, ARDE and HEMRL testing; management expects about 6 more months.
Naval opportunity linked to Apollo association; potential to be clearer by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall from INR20 crore to INR11 crore, and is INR11 crore sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said earlier quarters had expected credit loss provisions and forex losses that did not recur; a sustainable run rate of about INR9-10 crore per quarter was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin improve from the 35% level, and what is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will improve as the product mix and dispatches improve; it reiterated the 15-20% EBITDA target and did not quantify a gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the roughly INR400 crore of export licences, and what export revenue is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Several licences received in the past week, with material moving; INR150-200 crore of export is targeted in Q2, and prior-quarter export backlogs expected to clear this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR430 crore October 2025 order on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 execution was about INR21 crore, the order will be fully executed in FY27 (not two-thirds), and capacity is available with chaff imports already executed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Defence revenue fall 35%, and was it procurement or acceptance delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall to export licence and component import delays, and said customer procurement and acceptance were not a cause; completion expected in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook if raw material prices normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material prices are not normalising yet; contracts already signed must be executed first, then prices will be raised. The 15-20% EBITDA target is for this financial year.

risks_watch: Q1 EBITDA margin fell to about 6% (per analyst calculation) from about 15% in the prior year, with raw material cost and under-absorption cited; recovery to 15-20% depends on contracts and price pass-through.
FY27 revenue of INR600 crore needs INR500-600 crore in 9 months after INR103 crore in Q1; Chaff imports remain dependent on conditions abroad.
Export licence timing (3-4 months processing plus importing-country licence) could delay the INR350 crore April 2026 order.
Katepally commissioning relies on water trials in September and imported mixer parts; any slippage pushes production later.
Andhra Pradesh expansion land pricing unresolved; Apollo's stance on expansion not yet confirmed.
Pending LD (liquidated damages) reversal of about INR30 crore on the July 2023 flares order, expected by October-November 2026.
Unclear Apollo synergy details; management said more to come next quarter.

532504|2026-06.headline: Navin Fluorine Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 44% YoY to INR1,044-1,045 crore, with EBITDA up 73% and PAT up 108% to INR243 crore.
532504|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue grew 44% YoY to about INR1,045 crore, with operating EBITDA of INR357 crore (34.2% margin, up 566 bps YoY) and PAT of INR243 crore. All three verticals (HPP, specialty chemicals, CDMO) grew strongly, and the company became net debt free during the quarter. Management announced a new INR90 crore advanced materials adoption capex and a Phase 2 CDMO cGMP capex of INR125 crore. Management guided to a 32-33% EBITDA margin range going forward (plus/minus 1%), while flagging gross margin pressure from higher raw material costs.</overview>

segments.name: HPP (HFCs/fluorochemicals)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR540 crore, up 33% YoY on healthy volume growth and improved realisations; management describes HFC pricing as constructive given demand-supply dynamics.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (agchem)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR325 crore, up 48% YoY. Management plans campaign orders for 4-5 agchem molecules this year; LatAm agchem pricing pressure persists, and EBITDA is not expected to return to the old ~30% level.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR180 crore, up 82% YoY. Pipeline of 30-40 molecules, about 10 late stage; 3-4 molecules expected to get FDA readouts in the next 8-12 months. Management targets about $100 million for FY27.

segments.name: Advanced materials (incubating within HPP)
segments.commentary: Not separately reported. Chemours liquid cooling project targeted for completion by end Q2 FY27; Chemours reportedly sold about $1 million of two-phase cooling liquid in the quarter (per analyst). DRDO TDF partnership announced.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected in the 32-33% range (plus/minus 1%) on a normalised basis over the next one to two years, supported by HFC, debottlenecking and Chemours capacity.
CDMO FY27 target of about $100 million reiterated; FY29 asset turn of 3x on INR288 crore cGMP4 capex stated as the near-term view.
Gross margin dipped about 100 bps QoQ from Q4 FY26 on raw material costs; management said price pass-through will lag.
Advanced materials adoption capex (INR90 crore) to be done in two phases, first phase around mid-Q4 FY27 for commercial-scale qualification; not included in any return projections.
Growth visibility beyond FY28 depends on the current capex cycle (cGMP Phase 1, adoption capacity, Chemours).
capex_capacity: New advanced materials adoption capex of INR90 crore, internally funded, to be set up at Surat; creates two core platforms and augments analytical equipment.
CDMO cGMP4 Phase 2 capex of INR125 crore (part of INR288 crore approved Feb 2024), operationalisation expected Q4 FY27; Phase 1 operational in Q3 FY26. Dedicated to European CDMO partner.

HFC capacity addition of up to 15,000 MT of R32 on track for Q3 FY27; company currently has about 9,000-10,000 MT and total would be about 25,000 MT. Revenue band of INR600-825 crore cited from original capex approval.
MPP debottlenecking at Dahej on track for completion by Q3 FY27; management cited 2x asset turn.
AHF capacity of 60,000 MT between Surat and Dahej seen as adequate for the next 4-5 years; AHF commissioned in the subsidiary NFASL.
Renewable project of INR15.73 crore (14.9 MW hybrid) expected to supply more than 60% of energy needs once operational.
demand_pricing: R32: management expects a 35-45% contracted share of capacity over five years; a couple of contracts signed and more at a late stage.
R32 long-term demand said to double over a decade while quota-driven supply shrinks by half; Indian oversupply expected for about five years with exports to global market.
Specialty chemicals: volume recovering, but pricing pressure persists in LatAm; 13-14 new molecules launched last year and 5 new molecules being participated in, of which 3 are patented.
HFO supply to Honeywell: asset commercialised July 2022; original seven-year term with a three-year extension at Honeywell's option, so runway beyond FY29.
Management stated that raw material cost inflation is rising amid global war tensions and supply chain risk.

qa_highlights.question: Advanced materials: end-use applications, and growth beyond FY28 given current capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is to make advanced materials a material business unit by end of decade, modelled on today's CDMO. Focus on data centers, electronics, semiconductors, defence; the adoption capex is phased, with first phase complete around mid-Q4 FY27 to start commercial-scale qualification.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR90 crore adoption capex a pilot or commercial scale, and what is the payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said five products are already lab-approved and this capex takes them to commercial-scale qualification; not a pilot. No asset turn is assumed in numbers for the INR90 crore.

qa_highlights.question: R32 pricing and India capacity additions versus quota start in Jan 2028?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give pricing; said it will stay the lowest-cost R32 producer through its integrated HF chain and renewable power. Expects India oversupply for about five years and exports.

qa_highlights.question: Why did subsidiary (NFASL) margin fall about 12 pp QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Campaign mix differs quarter to quarter, and AHF transfers from Dahej to Surat are at arm's-length, so value shows up at Navin Fluorine (NFIL) level; group margin remains solid.

qa_highlights.question: CDMO: is the new capacity dedicated, and is the MSA for an extra molecule with the same customer?
qa_highlights.answer: New capacity dedicated to European CDMO partner; an MSA for an extra molecule in the same supply chain takes Navin to API minus 1. Also working on an early-phase molecule with the same customer.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $100 million CDMO target for FY27 still on track, and is INR900 crore cGMP capex math right?
qa_highlights.answer: $100 million target reiterated as on track. Management confirmed the 3x asset turn on INR288 crore by FY29, and that Phase 1 and Phase 2 combined are about INR900 crore is not exactly right; the INR288 crore figure is the approved base (3x = about INR900 crore revenue).

qa_highlights.question: HFC contracts, AHF utilisation, and the reason for the margin mix change YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: A couple of R32 contracts signed, with more near conclusion; balanced approach kept. Margin mix explained by HF price highs in Q1 FY26 and rising RM costs now; gross margin down about 100 bps QoQ, offset by fixed-cost productivity.

500408|2026-06.headline: Tata Elxsi Q1 FY27 revenue crossed INR1,021.1 crore (+6.5% YoY constant currency), but EBITDA margin fell to 21.2% on one-offs and onsite-ramp costs.
500408|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR1,021.1 crore, up 6.5% YoY and 1.3% QoQ in constant currency, led by media and communication (+11.5% YoY CC) and transportation (+6.7% YoY CC). EBITDA was INR216 crore (+15.7% YoY) at a 21.2% margin, while EBIT margin fell 330 bps QoQ and rose 80 bps YoY. Management attributed the sequential margin drop to about 150 bps of one-off/short-term costs, about 220-230 bps of investments in people, go-to-market and US onsite/subcontractor ramp-ups, partly offset by about 40-50 bps of currency gains. Healthcare was flat QoQ in CC (-0.3%) due to delayed deal awards.

financial_highlights.change: +6.5% YoY in constant currency; +1.3% QoQ in constant currency
Increase attributed to customer Chapter 11 receivable provisions and upfronted annual costs

segments.name: Media and Communication
segments.commentary: Grew 4.7% QoQ in natural currency and 2.9% QoQ in CC; 22.2% YoY natural and 11.5% YoY CC, driven by ramp-up of earlier-announced engagements and large operator/broadcaster programs.

segments.name: Transportation (SDS >55% share)
segments.commentary: Grew 6.7% YoY in CC and 13.3% YoY in natural currency; 78% of automotive revenue from OEM customers. Germany/Continental Europe softness and slower ramp-ups offset by US, APAC and aerospace/off-road adjacencies.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Exited near flat at -0.3% QoQ in CC; less than 10% of revenue. Deal awards delayed; management still expects growth within this fiscal year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth aspiration unchanged (high-single-digit per prior commentary), contingent on healthcare recovering.
Management expects growth in media and communication and transportation over the next two to three quarters.

Onsite-offshore cost pressures expected to ease over the next two to three quarters; about 150 bps of one-off costs expected to largely go away in Q2, with some transitioning over the next couple of quarters.
Q2 margin expected to be a balance between wage-hike impact (company-wide revision effective Q2) and one-offs falling away; sequential margin ramp expected toward Q4.
Management aims to deliver a profitable Q2 while removing one-timers; wage hike quantum to be disclosed at end of Q2.
Adjacency revenue quantification to be disclosed by end of FY27.
capex_capacity: Onsite-offshore mix shifted about 0.9-1 percentage point in one quarter to roughly 74/26 versus a 75/25 target; management said the business model is unchanged and work will move back offshore over subsequent quarters.
Investments in specialized talent, AI tools, AI infrastructure and cloud continuing; sales headcount added in US and Europe with advisors for large deal pursuits.
Forward teams and third-party specialist contractors deployed for US transitions because of visa delays; company has applied for visas for its own staff to replace contractors over time.
Platforms scaled: Neuron (Sky Europe zero-touch network operations, 30-70% efficiency gains cited), ViTel, AnaTel, DevStudio, TETHER.
demand_pricing: Media and communication: large consolidation deals from customers undergoing M&A; company was incumbent/prime vendor in two transactions and gained share from competitors.
Automotive: US, APAC (Japan, India) deal traction and large bids; Continental Europe on wait-and-watch.
Geography: Europe is slightly more than 40% of transportation revenue, US about 25-30%, remainder APAC.
Hiring: fresher intake moderated (about 100-150 engineers added last quarter); laterals only for specific needs; focus on bench utilisation.
Visa costs (e.g., H-1B fee changes) absorbed and bundled into hourly rates through annual COLA negotiations; not passed through to customers.

qa_highlights.question: How is margin trajectory expected to evolve; are the onsite and subcontractor costs one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Nalin Rana said about 150 bps of one-offs (transition, retention, a customer-specific cost, upfronted annual costs) should largely go away; about 220-230 bps of investments are stickier and should improve over time as subcontractors are replaced by own staff or moved offshore.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q1 other-expense increases mainly forex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said forex was not a big item; main drivers were a provision for receivables from a customer in Chapter 11 and upfronted annual costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 growth aspiration still high-single-digit given transportation issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Manoj Raghavan said the aspiration is unchanged, contingent on healthcare picking up.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q2 wage hike going to dilute margins, and will H2 ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Nalin Rana said Q2 will carry wage-hike impact largely offset by one-offs rolling off; margins are expected to ramp sequentially toward Q4 once wage hikes are baked in.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers asking for subcontractors, and is the onsite shift structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers are not asking for contractors; the need is driven by H-1B constraints during transitions. Management said the offshore model (about 75/25 target) is intact and onsite will decline over subsequent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the media and communication pick-up industry-wide or company-specific?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wins came from consolidation deals where Tata Elxsi was incumbent; M&A activity is creating share gains, and a top customer's restructuring is seen as potentially positive.

risks_watch: Continental Europe automotive softness and slower ramp-ups in Germany.
Healthcare deal closures delayed; segment still flat QoQ.
Margin recovery depends on Q2 wage-hike size (to be disclosed end of Q2) offsetting one-offs.
US visa constraints forcing contractor use and onsite cost; H-1B fee changes not recoverable from customers.
Customer Chapter 11 receivable provisions and restructuring of a top media customer.
AI-led pressure on engineering R&D budgets (management says budget reallocation, not deflation) and pricing; adjacency revenue not yet quantified.
500408|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on media and communication and the US/APAC automotive pipeline, but cautious on Europe automotive and healthcare; margin answers were detailed yet deferred the wage-hike quantum to end-Q2.

500408|2026-09.headline: Tata Elxsi Q2 FY27 operating revenue INR 1,055.7 crore, up 2.3% in constant currency; EBITDA margin 21.9%, up 70 bps QoQ.
500408|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 1,055.7 crore, growing 2.3% in constant currency, with all three verticals up sequentially (transportation +2% QoQ, media and communication +3.4%, healthcare and life sciences +3.5%). EBITDA was INR 231.4 crore, up 7.1% QoQ and 19.7% YoY, with margin at 21.9%. Management attributed about 60-70 bps of the margin gain to currency and 10-20 bps to operating leverage and fading one-offs, which absorbed an annual wage revision. Europe automotive remained soft and the transportation outlook depends on it; management expects H2 to exceed H1 across businesses except the Europe-dependent part of transportation.

financial_highlights.change: +2.3% constant currency (QoQ growth per management's framing)
Up from previous quarter; peak pre-COVID ~81-82%

segments.name: Transportation
segments.commentary: Grew 2% QoQ in constant currency, driven by auto OEMs in US and India; Japan flattish, rest of Asia flat, Europe soft. Aerospace and defence adjacency is growing from a small base and is not yet quantified.

segments.name: Media and Communication
segments.commentary: Grew 3.4% QoQ in constant currency on ramp-ups of closed deals and AI-led wins, including a GenAI virtual assistant engagement with a global technology leader.

segments.name: Healthcare and Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Grew 3.5% QoQ in constant currency after bottoming last quarter; win with a global renal care leader for next-gen home dialysis systems.

guidance_outlook: Company does not provide guidance as a policy; no guidance revision.
Management expects H2 FY27 revenue to exceed H1 (and therefore be higher YoY in H2), with growth in US, India and Asia; transportation H2 depends on Europe.
Margins expected to improve gradually via operational leverage, utilisation gains and pyramid correction over the next 2-3 quarters; no margin number given.
Wage revision is complete for the year; no material employee cost movement expected in rest of FY27 beyond selective investment.
Q3 is a short quarter with fewer working days; customer-specific furlough decisions awaited.
capex_capacity: Utilisation about 78%, up QoQ; management sees headroom versus pre-COVID peak of about 81-82%.
Pyramid rebalancing planned over next half-year, moving engagements to junior staff and using a bench trained at lower levels.
Deal ramp-ups typically take 2-3 quarters to reach full run-rate; aerospace programmes need at least 2-3 quarters to ramp.
Onsite-offshore revenue mix steady at roughly 25:75.
demand_pricing: Automotive: new multi-year deal from a leading automotive OEM for a cloud-based telematics and connected vehicle ecosystem, not yet ramped up.
Europe: large automotive deals in the final shortlist but unsigned; decision-making delayed by OEM situation; no ramp-downs on signed Europe deals, but some project run-offs.
Aerospace: collaboration with Sarla Aviation on Shunya eVTOL; global aerospace supplier engagement for test rig and validation; growth not disclosed due to small base.
AI demand: enterprises still earmarking AI budgets that partly compete with ER&D discretionary spend, but buying is becoming more ROI-focused.
Leakage: improved YoY, as multi-year large deals protect the base and supplier-side automotive revenue losses have largely shifted to OEMs.
Talent: strong demand for ER&D talent from GCCs; retention focus. Senior-level pay largely variable.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is growth and what drove margin expansion despite wage hikes; how much one-off reversal is left?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-70 bps of margin gain came from currency, 10-20 bps from operational leverage and one-offs fading; wage hikes were offset. Operational leverage expected to continue, with a slightly upward margin trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: Did the quarter pan out as planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Media and communication and healthcare were in line with confidence from closed deals; automotive was the uncertain piece, but US and India deal wins helped deliver growth.

qa_highlights.question: Are signed deals sufficient for growth or are new wins needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Both are needed: ramp-ups take 2-3 quarters and project run-offs require replacement wins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the steady-state margin improve with new deals?
qa_highlights.answer: New deals are innovation and product engineering, with margins described as reasonably flat; margin gains would come from pyramid rebalancing and utilisation across the organisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is there guidance revision for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No; company does not provide guidance as a policy.

qa_highlights.question: Concentration and health of group customers (Tata Motors, JLR)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said JLR is facing its own challenges and is being watched; much of automotive growth comes from outside group customers. Revenue concentration not disclosed.

risks_watch: Europe automotive: large deals unsigned and decision delays persist; timing uncertain.
JLR business performance and layoffs; impact on group-customer spend visible across H2.
Q3 furloughs and short working days could pressure revenue.
Healthcare concentration: only just stabilised, with diversification still early.
Wage cost structure: employee cost per head rising ahead of revenue; margin recovery relies on utilisation and pyramid correction.
Aerospace and BESS/manufacturing growth not disclosed; small base makes it hard to track.
500408|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on US, India and non-automotive verticals and on H2 being better than H1, but cautious and noncommittal on Europe automotive timing and on margin numbers, which were withheld.
key_quotes: And I think that is the confidence that we carry beyond anything else.
So this is a work in progress, but yes, we will have to progressively move towards, over the next, I would say, 2 to 3 quarters, we will see that gradual improvement in our margins, right?
As a policy, and in general, we don't provide guidance at all.

542857|2026-06.headline: Greenpanel Q1 FY27 combined revenue rose 8.5% to INR350 crore and EBITDA turned positive at INR32.5 crore, but exports fell to zero and OEM volumes degrew 14%.
542857|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 8.5% YoY to INR350 crore on a combined basis, with MDF operating EBITDA margin at 10.3% versus 4.4% a year earlier. Price hikes of around 15% taken in April were largely rolled back by peers through May to July, so realisations are now close to pre-hike levels. Exports fell to zero and OEM sales degrew 14%, while domestic MDF volumes grew 12% YoY and retail MDF grew about 20%. Management declined to give margin or utilisation guidance, citing daily chemical cost and discount volatility.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated operating EBITDA (ex-euro ECB currency impact)

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR12.4 crore in Q1 FY26
from INR353 crore at start of quarter

financial_highlights.value: INR2.5 crore overall, INR1.8 crore on ECB

segments.name: MDF (retail)
segments.commentary: Retail MDF grew about 20% YoY and domestic MDF volumes grew 12% YoY, the fourth consecutive quarter of domestic volume growth. Retail is about 75-80% of the mix.

segments.name: MDF (OEM)
segments.commentary: OEM sales degrew 14% YoY after management chose not to supply at discounted prices during the chemical shortage; OEM is about 20-25% of mix.

segments.name: MDF (exports)
segments.commentary: Exports fell to zero in Q1 as freight rose from about $400-500 to $5,500-6,000 per container; Middle East made up about 80-85% of past exports and remains effectively shut, with July and August exports negligible.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Volumes +10.4% YoY and revenue +5% YoY; around 5% price hike taken in Q1, with only a small part passed on as schemes. Management said QoQ plywood margin fell from 7.5% to 2.7% on product mix and higher fixed costs.

guidance_outlook: No quantitative margin or capacity utilisation guidance given; management cited chemical cost and discount volatility.
Management aims to ramp domestic volumes over the remaining nine months to improve full-year market share versus peers.
Management said the objective is to maintain Q1 margins, with possible lag in passing on any future price hikes.
Management expects pricing and demand pressure to persist through FY27, with improvement hoped for in FY28.
Management said double-digit MDF margins are not a very tough ask if volumes and utilisation rise; current utilisation is about 50-60%.
No MDF growth capex needed for 18-24 months beyond maintenance; plywood capacity to rise 30-40% via minimal debottlenecking investment.
capex_capacity: MDF utilisation is around 50-60% (cited as about 51% in Q&A); management intends to enhance utilisation this year, subject to market volumes and exports.
Action has a new line coming in South India and another continuous press is coming up in Madhya Pradesh.
Plywood: plan to fully utilise current capacity, then add machinery in existing facility at minimal investment to lift output 30-40%.
Maintenance shutdown: 5-7 day line shutdown taken this quarter due to lack of orders; management prefers splitting maintenance into short shutdowns rather than a 15-day stop.
Working capital up 4 days QoQ on higher finished goods and timber inventory for seasonality, but still 5 days leaner YoY.
demand_pricing: Peers rolled back the approximately 15% April price hike in phases through May, June and July; management said almost all of the hike is now rolled back, with 1-2% retained in some segments and markets.
Management said the company now prices OEMs at par with peers rather than at a premium to Century, to regain OEM volumes.
Channel partners are holding inventory on a hand-to-mouth basis, with destocking in Q1 and expected to persist given volatile prices.

Management estimates industry growth at mid-teens in the prior quarter; Arun Baid noted Greenpanel had the lowest industry growth in India this quarter and Century has out-volumed Greenpanel for two quarters.
Chemical costs are about 4-5% above pre-war levels and rising again; timber costs are stable, and mixed wood is being used in place of eucalyptus.
Q1 cost savings from timber and efficiencies were about 6-7% combined, and low-cost inventory from last fiscal helped gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company diversify export markets given the drop in exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is exploring other markets, but freight volatility and foreign manufacturing make it hard to compete; alternative markets cannot replace lost Middle East volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7.4% ASP increase due to channel mix shift to retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly. A large part came from removing OEM discounts, so OEM sales came through at near retail prices, shifting mix toward retail price levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company not the price maker as market leader?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it avoids undercutting and does not lead on rollbacks, but takes the lead on hikes; averaging out export pricing into the domestic market would have triggered further price cuts.

qa_highlights.question: Why has market share been lost and what is the game plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 OEM sales were intentionally held back during chemical shortage; the company now plans to price at par with peers and focus on volume and utilisation, with the aim of regaining share from Q2 FY27 on a smaller base.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be sustained if raw material costs fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to maintain Q1 margins; if chemical costs rise again, the industry may take another price hike, with some lag.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth capex planned over the next 18-24 months?
qa_highlights.answer: No MDF capex beyond maintenance; a small plywood debottlenecking investment to add 30-40% output.

risks_watch: Export recovery depends on Middle East normalisation and freight rates, currently $5,500-6,000 per container versus $400-500 before.
Chemical cost volatility and competitor discounting could force further price rollbacks or hikes; the Q1 margin gain may not persist.
Market share loss versus Century and rising capacity from Action (South India) and a new Madhya Pradesh line could keep pricing under pressure through FY27.
Channel destocking and hand-to-mouth buying may keep Q2 volumes below run-rate.
Forex loss of INR2.5 crore on the euro ECB, and plywood margin decline to 2.7% QoQ.
542857|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious on near-term guidance, citing daily chemical and discount volatility, but confident on the structural case for margin recovery through volume and utilisation. Management was defensive when pressed on market share loss and on why it did not act as price leader.

540774|2026-06.headline: IFGL Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA fell 17% YoY to INR31 crore on raw material and LPG cost spikes, while consolidated PAT rose 58% to INR17 crore.
540774|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 8% YoY to INR297 crore, with domestic up 7% and exports up 9%, but gross margin fell to 43% from 47% on higher raw material prices. Standalone EBITDA dropped 17% YoY to INR31 crore as input costs and LPG availability constraints outpaced price increases, which management says will pass through with a lag. Consolidated total income rose 13% YoY to INR515 crore and consolidated EBITDA rose 2% to INR40 crore, with PAT up 58% to INR17 crore. The Europe segment was weak because British Steel's low output cut offtake at Sheffield Refractories, while US operations grew double digits with improving margins.

financial_highlights.change: Management says base has grown; target double-digit for year-end

segments.name: Standalone India
segments.commentary: Revenue INR297 crore (+8% YoY); EBITDA INR31 crore (-17% YoY) hit by raw material costs and LPG/fuel price surge. Price increases were implemented but are only partly offsetting costs.

segments.name: Europe (Monocon UK + Sheffield Refractories)
segments.commentary: Management attributed the weak quarter mainly to Sheffield Refractories' low sales due to British Steel's blast furnace problems, with losses rising to about INR7 crore from INR3 crore QoQ (per analyst). Monocon UK losses reportedly fell QoQ and it is approaching breakeven.

segments.name: US subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Revenue grew double digits YoY with improved margins from cost optimization; management described margins as more than double-digit and robust.

segments.name: Monocon and Sheffield Refractories (overall)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue grew double digits YoY despite headwinds; Monocon has opened offices in Australia and Saudi Arabia and is entering iron and steel and foundry refractories.

segments.name: Hofmann Ceramic
segments.commentary: Order book held at similar levels YoY; management targets reducing losses and breakeven by end FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects price increases to flow through progressively over coming quarters, but says they are temporary and offset only input cost rises, with no additional margin expected from them.
Consolidated EBITDA margin target is double digit, dependent on geopolitics and overseas demand; earlier 12% margin reference was not reaffirmed explicitly.
British Steel expected to restart blast furnace and normalize offtake in Q2 FY27; Sheffield Refractories expected back to normal.
Speciality Steel (ex-Liberty Rotherham) melt shops are expected to restart around November-December 2026 per market sources.
Management says staff cost is at about 10% of revenue and is not expected to go beyond this level.
Management believes the worst is behind on profitability, but cautioned that conditions can change quickly.
capex_capacity: Sheffield Refractories Phase 1 plastic ramming mass production has started at IFGL Vizag facility; marketing trials underway, with full customer trials and accreditation still needed.
Adding mag carbon brick and casting flux new lines could add INR150-200 crore of revenue at peak capacity for these two products.

Chinese JV: government appropriate authority approval sought; authorities advised changing location and reapplying, so the project is on hold. Investment so far is only in land (Gujarat), with some spend.

R&D facility in Odisha: management said spend is around INR20 crore, disputing an analyst's INR100-150 crore figure. R&D is developing foundry materials, thin slab caster tundish SEN for the US, and recycled material use.
demand_pricing: India steel demand forecast to grow 7.4% in 2026 and 9.2% in 2027 (management citation).
US steel production up 6% YoY; US business revenue up double digits, with new product introductions (thin slab caster tundish SEN) made in the US.
UK: British Steel now in public ownership; British Steel produced at very low levels in Q1 due to blast furnace problems.
Ocean freight spikes due to geopolitical situation hit UK and China operations.
Price increases were negotiated per contract and are temporary, tied to input costs from geopolitical tension.
Management said there was no market share loss in domestic business; the base has grown, which lowered the percentage growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove overseas subsidiary growth and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Manoj Rakhecha said the Americas drove top-line growth with robust margins. Management expects momentum to continue across subsidiaries and aims to turn loss-making units (UK, Europe, America, Germany) back to profit. Company-wise margins were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall 17% if there was no competitive pricing pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said raw material and LPG/fuel costs rose sharply due to geopolitics, and price increases from customers were not enough to offset them.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Europe EBITDA turn negative (-8%) after nearing breakeven in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe comprises Monocon UK and Sheffield Refractories. Sheffield's sales were low because British Steel's output was minimal; Monocon UK is near breakeven. Q2 expected to normalize; no orders lost, just timing.

qa_highlights.question: Will staff costs stay near 10% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Agarwal said standalone staff cost of INR28.7 crore is up from INR24 crore in Q4 but level with Q1 FY26; management aims to contain it. Consolidated employee cost rose partly due to a provision reversal last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is 12% consolidated EBITDA margin still the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is aiming for double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin, dependent on geopolitics and overseas demand, and expects to return to that level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Chinese JV and R&D investment?
qa_highlights.answer: The Chinese JV is on hold pending government approval; the company must change location and reapply. Only land in Gujarat has been bought so far. R&D spend is about INR20 crore per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst behind for profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Manoj Rakhecha agreed with that view for today but cautioned that conditions can change quickly; he cited early green shoots in European steel.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak revenue capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: No overall peak revenue figure given; the two new lines (mag carbon brick and casting flux) could add INR150-200 crore at peak.

544111|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% to Rs.172 crore and EBITDA 8% to Rs.52 crore, while PAT fell 14% to about Rs.12 crore on finance costs and a tax-regime shift.
544111|2026-06.overview:
Management reported operating revenue of Rs.167 crore (+8% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs.47 crore (+3%, margin 28.12%) for Q1 FY27, with consolidated revenue of Rs.172 crore (+10%) and EBITDA of Rs.52 crore (+8%). Occupancy held at 92%, but ADR growth was only about 2% amid West Asia disruption, weak international air traffic and flat domestic air traffic. PAT declined about 14% to close to Rs.12 crore, reflecting about Rs.2.5 crore higher finance charges from Zillion acquisition financing and a Rs.2.2 crore deferred tax provision on the move to the new tax regime. Management guided to a stronger ADR trend from Q2 onward, with the BRICS Summit, weddings and exhibitions cited as drivers.</overview>
