segments.name: Food and Beverage
segments.commentary: F&B contributed about 43% of total revenue in Q1; Flurys stood at 111 outlets (cafes, kiosks, tea rooms) after adding one at Inorbit Mall Vizag, with first standalone North India cafe opened in Gurugram in August.

segments.name: Hotels (owned and managed)
segments.commentary: Portfolio stated as 42 hotels with 2,677 keys (one slide reference in call says 2,667). Ran Baas Patiala ARR about Rs.33,000 and Lotus Palace Chettinad about Rs.13,000, both still stabilising.

segments.name: EM Bypass Kolkata mixed-use project
segments.commentary: 33 of 69 service apartments sold at average about Rs.20,633 per sq ft; expected cash inflow Rs.70-80 crore this year, of which Rs.21 crore received.

guidance_outlook: ADR growth guided to high single digits for the coming season, supported by BRICS Summit in Delhi, about 40 wedding dates Nov-March, Aero Show Bengaluru and Bharat Mobility Expo.
Pipeline of 12 hotels with 472 keys in FY27, taking portfolio to 3,149 keys by end-FY27 from 2,677 keys.
Flurys target of 29 additional outlets in FY27, taking count to about 140; target of 400 outlets by 2030.
Long-term ambition of more than 6,000 keys by FY2030; management also cited 87 hotels and 6,719 keys over four years.
Other income guided at about Rs.3.5-4 crore per quarter; further cash inflow of about Rs.50 crore expected from EM Bypass by year-end.
Effective tax rate guided to fall to about 30-35% in Q2-Q4 FY27 under the new regime (from about 40% in Q1).
capex_capacity: EM Bypass Kolkata: 218 hotel rooms plus 69 service apartments, completion targeted early 2030; second Kolkata hotel referenced for opening in 2030.
The Park Juhu (78 rooms, converted from service apartments): design complete, launch targeted October 2027; long-term financing tied up for Zillion acquisition.
Vizag 100-room hotel: on site, launch expected in August 2026, completion early 2030.
Malabar House, Fort Kochi (17 keys, about half an acre): acquisition in progress, completion expected October-November 2026; acquisition cost about Rs.64 crore.
Pune FSI raised from 2.5 lakh to 6.7 lakh sq ft; plan of 2.5 lakh sq ft for hotel and 4 lakh+ sq ft for residential.

Capex for Pune (200 rooms), Navi Mumbai (250), Vizag (100), EM Bypass (220) and Jaipur (150) over 4-5 years: about Rs.1,140 crore at Rs.1.2 crore per room, plus Zillion acquisition about Rs.210 crore, Juhu renovation about Rs.80 crore and Kochi about Rs.64 crore (total about Rs.350 crore additional, cited with EM Bypass funding offset). Operating capex Rs.40 crore per year plus Flurys Rs.40 crore per year. Net capex about Rs.1,500 crore, to be funded from EBITDA of Rs.240-250 crore per year. About Rs.200-250 crore of capex expected within FY27.
Completed SAP S/4HANA implementation for Finance during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Occupancy 92%, described as India's leading occupancy; RevPAR leadership in upper upscale maintained.

Management said All-India ADR growth was 6% in the quarter, versus about 2% for the company as stated in analyst question; domestic passenger traffic flat and international inbound air traffic down about 10%.
City-level domestic passenger declines cited: Mumbai -3.5%, Hyderabad over -12%, Chennai -13%.
Juhu ARR about Rs.18,000-20,000; management expects Bombay ARR growth of 10-15%.
Management expects ADR to improve from Q2 onward; said Q2-Q4 should be distinctly better than Q1.
Pricing on EM Bypass service apartments: average about Rs.20,633 per sq ft; Juhu acquisition at about Rs.40,000 per sq ft versus market levels cited near Rs.1 lakh per sq ft.

543336|2026-06.headline: Chemplast Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA loss of INR115 crores on INR1,125 crores revenue; net loss INR176 crores on VCM high-cost inventory.
543336|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue rose to INR1,125 crores from INR1,100 crores a year earlier, but input cost spikes from the Middle East disruption drove an EBITDA loss of INR115 crores and a net loss of INR176 crores. Management attributed the loss mainly to high-priced VCM inventory booked around March-April, which it says will be consumed by July-August. Specialty chemicals (CMCD) volumes grew 21% YoY and the segment is described as recovering, while Suspension PVC and caustic/chloromethane remained under price pressure. Management expects spreads near $160/t from September onward, with the Karaikal PVC plant offline after a 17 July fire.</overview>

segments.name: Suspension PVC
segments.commentary: Revenue INR569 crores vs INR608 crores YoY; prices fell in April after duty exemption let Chinese imports surge, and demand softened seasonally. Management guides spread to ~$160/t (India, replacement basis) from September.

segments.name: Paste PVC
segments.commentary: Realisations about $200/t above Suspension PVC per management; Cuddalore 7,000 t debottlenecking on track for October 2026 commissioning.

segments.name: Specialty / CMCD
segments.commentary: Volumes up 21% YoY on revenue of INR427 crores; 14 molecules commercial out of ~50 in pipeline; INR1,000 crore revenue target reiterated as on track. MPB-3 Phase 3 and pilot Phase 3 commissioned; utilisation ex-new assets ~60-70%.

segments.name: Refrigerant gas (R32)
segments.commentary: Commercial production started May 2026 from swing plant; full 14,000 t capacity expected online by end of FY27 per management, with ramp-up in Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Value-added chemicals (caustic, chloromethane, H2O2)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR129 crores vs INR138 crores; lower output due to planned caustic membrane changeover; caustic pricing under pressure from weak demand and excess supply.

guidance_outlook: Management expects VCM high-cost inventory to be consumed by July and part of August, with normal-price VCM from September and better Q3 performance.
Targeted spread of ~$160/t between PVC and VCM; management says ~$120-130/t needed for EBITDA neutral and a further ~$20-30/t for PBT positive.
Management declined to give a numerical guidance but said 'reasonable performance' expected from Q3 FY27.
Onerous contract net provisions of ~INR90 crores (CCVL) and ~INR30 crores (Chemplast) expected to be reversed in Q2 FY27.
R32 full capacity expected online by end of FY27; management says margin contribution is healthy but too early to forecast sustainability.
Debottlenecking of 7,000 t at Cuddalore Paste PVC due October 2026.
capex_capacity: Karaikal PVC plant manually shut after a fire on 17 July 2026; no injuries or spillage reported; restoration timeline not disclosed on the call.
Cuddalore Paste PVC 7,000 t debottlenecking on track for October 2026.
CMCD: MPB-3 Phase 3 and pilot Phase 3 commissioned in Q1 FY27; CMCD capacity expanded from ~1,100 t to ~5,400 t per analyst question (not contested).
R32: 14,000 t capacity targeted online by end of FY27; swing plant commercial production from May 2026.
Caustic soda capacity 120,000 t, operating range 100-120k t given electrolyser ageing.
demand_pricing: Paste PVC demand recovered to 70-80% downstream operating rates in June as Middle East situation eased; Europe and Asia supplies turned aggressive from mid-June.
Suspension PVC prices fell in April; customs duty on PVC resin exempted 2 April-30 June 2026 and reinstated 16 July 2026; minimum import price (MIP) imposed for six months.
Anti-dumping recommendation on EU and Japan Paste PVC imports lapsed; Madras High Court ordered provisional assessment and importer bonds for retrospective ADD recovery.
Agchem market subdued with generic competition from China; management says demand on commercialised molecules remains healthy but some ramp-ups delayed by a quarter.
Caustic soda and chloromethane prices under pressure from weak regional demand and excess supply; hydrogen peroxide volumes up sequentially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VCM sourcing situation and would the company partially shut the plant given negative economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Replacement VCM ~$700/t delivered vs PVC ~$900+/t, a $150-160 spread; management is evaluating alternate VCM sources and expects VCM prices to soften further.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 PVC-VCM spread and what spread is needed for EBITDA and PBT breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 spread was negative (VCM ~$1,000+/t landed vs realisation ~$700-750/t). EBITDA neutral needs ~$120-130/t; PBT positive needs another $20-30/t.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company locked into fixed-price PVC contracts with floating raw material costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts are formula/market-linked on both PVC and VCM; the Q1 loss came from VCM parcels booked at March peak prices when PVC prices later fell.

qa_highlights.question: How concentrated is CMCD revenue across the 14 commercial molecules and is the INR1,000 crore target agchem-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is mostly agchem and spread across multiple customers and innovators; management declined to give product or customer concentration. The INR1,000 crore target is reflective of agchem molecules already commercialised; pharma and other specialty projects are not included.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CMCD utilisation and ROCE trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding the newly commissioned MPB-3 Phase 3, utilisation is ~60-70%; management expects returns to reach industry levels this year as costs optimise.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to service debt with ~INR235 crores annual interest and negative FCF from growth capex?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said conserved cash and current accruals will cover debt servicing; liquidity is sufficient and no equity dilution flagged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the spread for Paste vs Suspension PVC?
qa_highlights.answer: Paste realisations are ~$200/t above Suspension PVC per management.

543283|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 43.4% YoY to INR426 crores, with same-store sales growth of 28.7% and pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA margin of 8.1%.
543283|2026-06.overview:
United Foodbrands (Barbeque Nation) reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR426 crores, up 43.4% YoY, with consolidated SSSG of 28.7% on top of 14.4% in Q4 FY26. Growth was volume-led (dine-in transactions up 63.5%) with no price increase taken. Pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 8.1% from about 5.5% in Q4 and roughly 350 bps higher YoY, helped by a 130 bps sequential gross margin recovery in Barbeque Nation India. International gross margin fell on Middle East-linked food inflation, and net debt rose marginally to INR106 crores.</overview>

segments.name: Barbeque Nation India
segments.commentary: Same-store sales growth 33.5%, revenue growth 43.4%, dine-in transactions up 68.6%; gross margin up ~130 bps QoQ. Captive digital ecosystem drives 65% of dine-in transactions (from ~61% in Q4); MAUs ~1.4 million, up ~60% YoY.

segments.name: Barbeque Nation International
segments.commentary: Revenue growth 46.6%, SSSG 8.5%, dine-in volume growth 45.2%, gross profit up 40.3%. Restaurant operating margin 18.7%, but gross margin down ~3 pp on Middle East-linked inflation; added 1 UAE restaurant.

segments.name: Premium casual dining (Premium CDR)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth ~36%, SSSG 13.6%, dine-in volume growth ~40%. Mature restaurants deliver restaurant operating margin of upwards of 20%; added 1 and closed 1 restaurant, network unchanged. Q4 FY26 cohort expected to lift segment margin.

guidance_outlook: SSSG expected to moderate through FY27 as comparables tighten, with Q3 and Q4 FY27 lapping the strongest quarter of FY26; management called this a base effect, not weaker demand.

Margin levers for FY27: gross margin recovery in India, mature portfolio ROM expansion, new-store cohort maturation and back-end cost leverage; management did not give a pre-Ind AS double-digit EBITDA margin timeline.
Target of 300 restaurants by FY27 (about 40 additions this year vs ~35 last year); 15 restaurants under construction to operationalise in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
FY27 capex guided at ~INR140 crores (INR120 crores for new outlets, INR20 crores maintenance and ancillary), per the prior guidance reiterated on the call.
Management sees Barbeque Nation India capable of ~600 restaurants at current scale, up from an earlier view of 400-450, given the Big Buffet format in Tier 2/3 markets.
Momentum said to be continuing into July; revenue crossed INR400 crores for the first time, and the quarter ended at about INR425 crores.
capex_capacity: Restaurant count closed Q1 FY27 at 266 after 5 additions; target of 300 by FY27 maintained.
15 restaurants under construction, expected to open in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
Barbeque Nation India store format reduced to ~3,500 sq ft from 4,500 sq ft; newer format's revenue per restaurant said to be among the highest.
Expansion funded largely from internal accruals; borrowings to be kept at prudent levels.
demand_pricing: Growth described as entirely volume-led; no price increase taken in Q1 despite inflation. Average per-cover spend declined due to value initiatives from Q2 FY26 and has now stabilised at Q4 FY26 levels.
Average revenue per mature restaurant is around INR7 crores; management has not given a target for the next step.
Repeat business is ~45-47% of the base, with the new-vs-repeat mix shifting slightly toward new guests. Average bill is ~4.3 pax, and repeat tracking relies on one mobile number per bill.

Delivery growth of 62% was supported by value SKUs across Barbeque Nation, BBQ and Dum Safar brands and by higher marketing spend. Delivery share of mix rose ~2 pp YoY and carries commission and packaging costs of about 30%.
Management described the mature cost base as 'normalised' after recent hires in culinary, marketing and digital; each INR1 per-cover improvement adds about INR1.5 crores of annual cost impact.

500147|2026-06.headline: John Cockerill India Q2 CY26 standalone revenue up 82% YoY to ~INR149 crore; consolidated INR299 crore (+18% YoY), order book ~INR4,500 crore.
500147|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 82% YoY to about INR149 crore and consolidated revenue reached about INR299 crore, up 18% YoY, but both fell sequentially as Q1 benefited from closing older projects. Management attributed weaker Q2 margins to upfront costs on newly started projects, organisation-building spend and one-time consolidation costs after the China, Germany and Belgium entities were brought under the listed company. Order wins of about INR1,200 crore in the quarter lifted the consolidated order book to about INR4,500 crore (standalone about INR2,200 crore). Management expects revenue and margins to build in H2 as new projects ramp, though it gave no quantified guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Expected marginally lower in next two quarters

segments.name: Standalone (India)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR149 crore, up 82% YoY; top customers Tata Steel and JSW. Order book ~INR2,200 crore.

segments.name: Consolidated group
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR299 crore, up 18% YoY; ArcelorMittal to be added to top customers after consolidation. Order book ~INR4,500 crore. Top five customers ~80% of revenue.

segments.name: Value-added services
segments.commentary: Service revenue in Q2 about one-third of Q1; management says lower because project progress was slower, not lack of orders, and services margins remain strong.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated INR8,000 crore top-line as the CY30 north-star, to come from organic growth (JVD, Volteron) and external acquisitions; several acquisitions under evaluation, no timeline given.
Management said consolidated revenue in H2 should improve significantly; did not expect to reach the ~INR2,000 crore CY25 pro-forma figure but 'should not be very far' if US is included.
Execution of new orders to ramp in Q3 and Q4 as engineering and procurement progress; impact on H2.
Employee cost expected to rise as manpower is added on the execution side; other expenses to be marginally lower than Q2 level in the next two quarters.
One-time transaction, forex and notional interest costs expected to stop from H2 after the parent agreed to a share-based payment instead of cash.
Further order wins expected before year-end across Asia, Europe, US and India; a JVD contract in Asia is in advanced discussion, targeted this year.
capex_capacity: Taloja Rolls Coating facility put into operation in June 2026; testing and trial orders underway, production initiation now.
Advanced Coating facility at Taloja, India, inaugurated (value-added services).
Shanghai office opened in China; workshop for assembly of special machines planned to open in Q3 CY26.
Execution timeline on contracts is typically two to three years; management now uses three years as the working assumption for the current book.
Headcount expansion on execution side planned, with employee cost rising.
demand_pricing: Order inflow ~INR1,200 crore in Q2, driven by demand for advanced processing, electrical steel, downstream quality and plant modernisation.
Management cited EU tariff-quota regime (18.3 million tons, 15% duty beyond quota) as supportive for hot-rolling, cold-rolling and processing-line investments.
India per capita steel consumption ~93 kg vs global ~230 kg; India steel production expected at 161.7 million tons this year.

JVD (Jet Vapor Deposition) pitched as a zinc-coating alternative to hot-dip galvanizing; customer savings cited at least INR1,000 per unit, up to 20x that, mainly for automotive and AHSS grades; first contract delayed by customer investment-approval process.
Potential cold-rolling order in the range of EUR50-100 million expected this year.
Competitors named: SMS and Danieli (Tier-1 OEMs), also Primetals; all have downstream portfolios.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR8,000 crore CY30 top-line target still valid, and how will it be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, as a north-star; two streams: organic (JVD, Volteron) and external acquisitions, which are under investigation. Volteron IP sits with John Cockerill SA, not the listed entity, and is not yet commercial.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the CY25 pro-forma revenue (~INR2,000 crore) far above reported (~INR960 crore), and can the US entity bridge the gap?
qa_highlights.answer: INR2,000 crore was a guideline; US is not a large contributor. Revenue depends on order progress. Management expects significant H2 improvement and said the gap should not be very far if US is included.

qa_highlights.question: Why did John Cockerill SA reduce holding from ~75% to ~70.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to group priorities; SA remains a large shareholder and will get convertible preferential shares that would take it back to 72%+.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost structure outlook (employee cost ~INR68 crore, other expenses ~INR70 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost to rise with execution hiring; other expenses marginally below current level in next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone and consolidated order book, service revenue, and top-customer concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated ~INR4,500 crore, standalone ~INR2,200 crore. Service revenue ~one-third of Q1. Top five ~80% of revenue; standalone top are Tata Steel and JSW.

qa_highlights.question: Quantum of one-time consolidation costs in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify; said it would come back to the analyst. Costs covered transaction, forex, notional interest, legal, audit and due diligence across Belgium, Germany and China.

risks_watch: Margin pressure in Q2 from upfront costs on new projects; recovery depends on H2 execution ramp.
Revenue lumpiness: sequential decline in Q2 from Q1 project close-outs.
Consolidation and ongoing parent-company cost sharing (R&D, technical development) may persist beyond one-time items.
JVD first commercial contract repeatedly delayed by customer investment validation; Volteron not yet commercial and needs pilot validation.
Gap between INR8,000 crore CY30 target and current run-rate; acquisition plans have no detail or timeline.
Revenue guidance of ~INR2,000 crore CY25 pro-forma was not met; management did not reaffirm a specific figure.
Customer concentration: top five ~80% of revenue.

Evasive on several specifics: the consolidation-cost quantum, regional revenue split, and the reason for delays in the JVD contract and Taloja facility.

544244|2026-06.headline: Gala Precision Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue ~INR75 crore (+20% YoY), EBITDA margin 16.51%, PAT margin 11.44%; FY27 EBITDA margin guided 17-19%.
544244|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was about INR75 crore, up 20% YoY, with EBITDA of about INR12 crore (+28% YoY, 16.51% margin) and net profit of about INR8 crore (+29% YoY, 11.44% margin). Management said order booking rose about 40% YoY and first-quarter revenue is typically 20-22% of the full year. A roughly INR3 crore dispatch slipped out of the quarter due to a customer payment delay, which management said cost about 5 percentage points of growth. Management reiterated 20-25% FY27 revenue growth and a 17-19% EBITDA margin range, and said FY27 working capital would stay at similar levels (around 180 days) pending a KPMG study. The call also covered a Chennai ramp-up, a planned Wada land purchase, and a reduction in forex hedging cover from 70% to 40% of export collections.

financial_highlights.change: vs ~INR80-85 crore same period last year

segments.name: Disc Springs (DSS)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 54% of Q1 FY27 revenue, sales +31% YoY, growth attributed mainly to the Wada plant. Disc springs are a niche category with customer buying of INR5-10 crore each.

segments.name: SFS
segments.commentary: Contributed 29% of revenue, INR223 million. Management cited growing customer adoption and new business wins; the SFS cost spread versus European peers was described as 10-15% (up to 18%) on exports and 2-3% in India.

segments.name: CSS
segments.commentary: Contributed 17% of revenue, INR125 million, citing steady demand across industrial and mobility applications.

segments.name: Fasteners (Chennai)
segments.commentary: New Chennai plant (4,600 MT installed capacity, high-tensile bolts) is ramping; Phase 1 utilisation about 70-80% in Q1. Wind-turbine fastener contribution is about 25-26% of Q1 sales as stated, with the offshore-wind product targeted at 10% of FY27 fastener sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 17-19%; management said it is confident and that this range holds for FY28 as well.
FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-25% YoY; management said it is on track or exceeding this.
Effective tax rate expected at around 20% or less, helped by deductions and a solar open-access project due for commissioning in Q3.
Working capital expected at similar levels (around 180 days) for now; KPMG study report expected by end-August 2026, with targets to be set in Q3.
Chennai Phase 1 utilisation targeted at 80-90% in Q2 and ~70% for Phase 1-2 combined by Q4; Chennai EBITDA expected to be comparable with Wada around Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
New Wada land (10-11 acre) capex of about INR40-45 crore, mostly in FY28, subject to completing the purchase (2-3 months).
capex_capacity: Chennai plant: new fastener facility with 4,600 MT installed capacity; Phase 1 utilisation ~70-80% in Q1 FY27; Phase 2 mezzanine (~10,000 sq ft) construction to finish in Q2 and more machines by Q3, required in Q4.
Chennai monthly run rate: manufacturing INR4-5 crore per month; June production ~INR4.5 crore but dispatches lower due to an item on hold.
Hot-dip galvanising (HDG) plant commissioned at Chennai, brought in-house to improve margin and delivery.
MoU signed for ~10.15 acre of land at Wada, adjacent to existing plant; ~50,000 sq ft shed planned mainly for fasteners and partly disc springs; legal due diligence underway.
Solar open-access project initiated, expected commissioning in Q3 FY27.
demand_pricing: Order booking up ~40% YoY, per management.
Pricing stable; management says it offers 10-20% savings to customers while holding margins, and passes through raw-material increases with a lag.
Fasteners cited as the main growth driver. Customer wallet sizes: fasteners INR50-500 crore vs disc springs INR5-10 crore.
New products (bolts, smart fasteners for offshore wind, wedge lock washers) are ~30-35% of order book, per management.
Company said it is taking share from European producers; some multi-year accounts grew share of business from 5-10% to 50-75%.
Forex: forward cover on export collections reduced from 70% to 40% due to euro volatility and war-related uncertainty; ~4% of 12-month exposure already covered.
Product mix: ~85% customised products; ~15% sold to fastener distributors at company level. Disc spring and Gallock 75-80% to OEMs; SFS >95% direct to OEMs.
Management said a single ~INR3 crore+ dispatch was held because of a customer payment delay; ex-this, growth would have been ~25%.
Management cited TAM of USD100 billion for fasteners, with Gala addressing ~USD2.5 billion including bolts and nuts.
Seatbelt retractor spring: customer approved Gala as source after July visit; small-batch supply to start, slow ramp due to safety-critical nature.

544821|2026-06.headline: Kusumgar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 102% YoY to INR247.2 crore and EBITDA margin hit 31%, but management gives no formal guidance.
544821|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR247.2 crore, up about 102% YoY but down about 21% QoQ from INR312.8 crore in Q4 FY26, which management attributed to an export push pulled into Q4 after US tariff uncertainty eased. EBITDA was INR75.9 crore at about 31% margin, up roughly 900bps YoY from 22% and down from 41% in Q4. PAT was INR42.6 crore (about 17% margin) versus INR6.6 crore a year ago. This was the company's first earnings call after its July 15, 2026 listing, and management declined to give formal forward guidance, citing unpredictable approval timing, government tenders and tariff exposure.

~+900bps YoY vs 22% in Q1 FY26; down from 41% in Q4 FY26
vs INR6.6 crore (5% margin) in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Aerospace and defense solutions
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue was significantly driven by spillover ready parachute contracts that were partly shipped in Q4 FY26; management said this quarter is broadly reflective of an average quarter and that Q1 is typically the weakest for some segments.

Operating cash flow expected to be positive in FY27, per management's answer to a direct question.

demand_pricing: Management said Q4 FY26 was an anomaly: export volumes were pulled forward after US tariff uncertainty resolved, and 10% to 15% of revenue comes from the US.

India defense: described as incumbent supplier for a large set of products; global defense business described as challenger with inroads still being qualified.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise revenue breakup across the four segments?

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 revenue came from spillover parachute orders versus new orders; why did Q4 spike?

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook given EBITDA swung from 19% to 37% to 31%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 EBITDA margin similar to FY25 and FY26 on a percentage basis; future swings should be a few percentage points, not as dramatic as the recent shift.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 55% to 60%. No large core capex planned; maintenance capex of 5% to 10% of gross block; new-area capex not yet defined.

qa_highlights.question: Executable order book as of June 30?
qa_highlights.answer: Declined to disclose; orders are split between formal POs, LOIs and projections. Management said it may provide better visibility in a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.answer: Management did not circulate the June debtor figure; said Q4 receivables were artificially high and business has normalised. Said operating cash flow will be positive in FY27.

544821|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the long-term story and margin resilience, but cautious and at times evasive on near-term numbers: management refused guidance, order book, segment split and debtor figures, citing structural unpredictability and its newly listed status.
key_quotes: So, if you look at '25 and '26, I think there would be reasonable guides for, I mean, we should expect very similar numbers in '27 for EBITDA as a percentage.
So, we are working on single segment, so that's why the segmental report is not applicable to us.

544315|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR853 million from INR1,024 million, with EBITDA at negative INR149 million and a net loss of INR176 million.
544315|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations declined YoY as Middle East conflict supply-chain disruptions hit S&P and trading execution for most of the quarter. Management attributed roughly INR50-55 crore of revenue impact to the quarter and expects execution to normalise by end-Q2 FY27. Order book rose to INR699 crore, mainly on S&P orders, and management guides to an order intake of about INR1,000 crore for FY27. Strategic moves included a small stake in WaHa with India and UAE rights, a first European ZLD order, and continued traction for the H-Xtreme heat exchanger.</overview>

segments.commentary: Revenue lost of about INR15 crore in the quarter due to the disruption.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: About INR42-43 crore of orders were delayed or down in the quarter.

segments.name: Roserve (Water as a Service)
segments.commentary: Management said it is performing well with marquee projects in execution and aims to build recurring, annuity-style revenue; no figures given.

guidance_outlook: Execution expected to normalise by end-Q2 FY27; management said Q2 should show growth but remains subject to developments over the next six weeks.
Order book of INR699 crore; management said 80-85% conversion in FY27 would yield growth for the year.
FY27 order intake target of about INR1,000 crore, with large domestic and international orders expected to convert over the next three to four months.
EBITDA margin historically 14-16%; temporary margin pressure from talent and execution investment, expected to stabilise once growth crosses about INR850 crore.
Medium-term guidance of 20-25% growth with EBITDA margin of 12-16% over the next two to three years (management's stated range).
capex_capacity: First project delivered with new REM membranes in partnership with NALA Membranes, targeting textile and paper effluent.

Semiconductor entry via a US partner with a Micron collaboration; initial focus on membrane replacement, then project segment.

Revenue for Q1 fell YoY and the company posted a net loss versus a profit a year earlier.
WaHa opportunity has no revenue or size disclosed yet; stake is under 2%.
Order intake target of about INR1,000 crore requires converting large domestic and international pipeline in the next three to four months.
Management said margin and growth guidance will depend on the outcome of large-project execution and market developments.
key_quotes: Our revenue performance during the quarter was impacted by supply chain disruptions due to the conflict in the Middle East for the better part of the quarter.

535755|2026-06.headline: ABFRL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% to INR2,026 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 8.2% and reported loss widened to INR249 crores.
535755|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 11% Y-o-Y to INR2,026 crores, with established businesses growing high-single digits at stable margins and newer businesses growing about 30%. EBITDA was INR167 crores (8.2% margin), with the Y-o-Y decline attributed mainly to lower treasury income and investment in new businesses; excluding treasury income, management says EBITDA rose. Reported loss widened to INR249 crores from INR234 crores, driven by higher Ind AS depreciation and finance costs from new stores. Wedding-related demand was hit by Adhik Maas, and TCNS like-to-like growth slowed to about 2%, which management called disappointing.

financial_highlights.change: Y-o-Y decline, mainly lower treasury income; ex-treasury EBITDA up Y-o-Y per management
vs INR234 crores loss in Q1 FY26
down from roughly INR1,150-1,200 crores at start of year
more than 45 stores added in quarter

segments.name: Pantaloons (incl. OWND)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,204 crores (+10%); Pantaloons standalone grew 7% with 4% LTL, OWND grew 55% and contributed about 2-2.5 points of segment growth. Segment margin 15.9% is down as OWND (in investment phase) dilutes profit; Pantaloons brand margin is similar to last year, around 18% per management.

segments.name: Ethnic (designer-led, TCNS, Tasva, Jaypore)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR454 crores (+4%), 5% LTL. Designer-led brands grew high-single digits and are profitable; TCNS retail grew 10% with low-single-digit LTL and non-retail channels declined; Tasva grew 35% with double-digit LTL and 90 stores, but is still loss-making.

segments.name: Luxury (The Collective, Mono-Brand, Galeries Lafayette)
segments.commentary: Double-digit Y-o-Y growth; network of 51 stores after 3 additions. Management says The Collective profitability is in mid-teens this quarter. Galeries Lafayette is still loss-making; The Collective plus Galeries Lafayette expected to break even at combined level in H2 FY27.

segments.name: TMRW (new brands)
segments.commentary: Primary sales +11%, secondary sales +16% Y-o-Y; cash losses narrowed and Y-o-Y EBITDA losses narrowed. Over 140 stores including Wrogn after 20+ additions in the quarter. 2 of 6 brands are profitable at brand level.

segments.name: Newer businesses overall
segments.commentary: Grew around 30% Y-o-Y, supported by retail footprint expansion, with continued investment.

guidance_outlook: Management expects TMRW to grow 20%+ for FY27 and to see losses narrow on an annual basis; TMRW brand-level cash profitability targeted in 12-18 months and overall profitability in FY29-FY30.
Ethnic portfolio expected to grow 20%+ for FY27, with H2 significantly higher than H1; TCNS expected to return to early double-digit growth.
Standalone cash expected to be about INR500 crores by year-end; annual cash funding requirement INR500-550 crores for next 2 years; company expected to be FCF positive by FY29-FY30.
Capex plus working capital for FY27 about INR450 crores, of which capex about INR300+ crores.
Store additions: about 20 new Pantaloons/OWND stores in FY27 (mostly H2, with 20-22 planned in H1 per Q&A), 35-40 TCNS stores, 25-30 Tasva stores, 75+ TMRW stores.
Inflation of around 4%+ in input costs; most pressure expected in Q2 and Q3; about half of the price increase passed on in Pantaloons, with gross margin impact expected in H2.
capex_capacity: Store network 1,286 at quarter end; more than 45 added in Q1 across portfolio, with 10 added in Pantaloons segment (1 Pantaloons, 9 OWND).
Capex about INR300+ crores in FY27, for new stores and renovation of Pantaloons and other stores.
Around 150 Pantaloons stores renovated, contributing more than half of revenue.
TMRW to add 75+ stores in FY27; Galeries Lafayette next store planned in Delhi in 2-3 years, after Mumbai stabilises.
demand_pricing: Demand described as steady but not strong; May was better, June softer ahead of market-wide EOSS. Adhik Maas hit peak wedding season and occasion wear purchases; designer wear order book declined amid global disruptions.
Pantaloons LTL was about 4% in Q1 versus 14% in Q4 FY26 (which included an EOSS timing shift); management targets high-single-digit LTL for the full year.
Inflation around 4%+ in both Pantaloons and OWND; half of the cost increase passed on, rest absorbed. Management does not expect higher discounting in H2.
TCNS LTL slowed to about 2% from 7-8% in the prior two quarters, partly due to liquidation of old inventory; management targets high-single-digit to early double-digit LTL.
Tasva LTL in mid-teens over recent quarters; Tasva needs revenue of INR400-500 crores (about double current) to become profitable.

524372|2026-06.headline: Orchid Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 15% YoY to INR304 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR25 crore, on a merged Dhanuka basis.
524372|2026-06.overview: Orchid Pharma reported Q1 FY27 on a combined basis after the Dhanuka Laboratories merger (effective 10 July 2026, appointed date 1 April 2024), with FY25 and FY26 restated. Revenue from operations rose to INR304 crore from INR263 crore, and gross margin improved about 3 percentage points to 33%. EBITDA rose to INR25 crore from INR10 crore a year earlier. Management described the quarter as mediocre and said recovery would be gradual, with cephalosporin pricing still under pressure from overcapacity. Project milestones for 7-ACA (March 2027) and cefiderocol (commissioning December 2026) were reiterated.

financial_highlights.change: up ~15% from INR263 crore in Q1 FY26
up ~3 percentage points from ~30% in Q1 FY26
up from INR10 crore in Q1 FY26
down from INR1,398 crore in FY25
down ~4 percentage points from ~36% in FY25
EBITDA loss ~INR50 lakh, much better than prior quarter
earlier quarterly run-rate cited as INR20-25 crore

segments.name: Cephalosporin API / core business
segments.commentary: FY26 volumes and pricing fell 15-20% by product in a difficult cephalosporin year. Cefixime faces the most margin pressure, mainly in rest-of-world markets. 7-ACA pricing has been stable for about a year.

segments.name: Exblifep (Cefepime-Enmetazobactam)
segments.commentary: Europe volumes grew about 300% QoQ in Q3 FY26, about 170-175% in Q4 FY26 and about 50% in Q1 FY27. The Russia licence has an estimated 10-year value of about USD178 million, not current revenue. South Africa registration is done and GCC coverage is in place, but Middle East rollout is delayed by regional conflict.

segments.name: AMS (Antimicrobial Stewardship)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR5 crore in Q1 FY27 from Orblicef and other brands. Quarterly EBITDA loss narrowed to about INR50 lakh.

segments.name: NP-NC (Dhanuka Laboratories)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR21 crore in Q1 FY27, against an earlier quarterly run-rate of INR20-25 crore. Management said it would not reach 25% of revenue in 3-4 years.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give FY27 YoY revenue growth guidance; it said it hopes for better QoQ sales in H2, when regulated demand is seasonally stronger.
Merger synergies are expected to show initial benefits from FY28.

Cefiderocol: facility commissioning targeted for December 2026, then validation and initial batches in January-March 2027. Indian approval expected 6-9 months after that, subject to a DCGI trial waiver, so around Q3 FY28.
7-ACA (Jammu): first commercial batch targeted by March 2027. Ramp-up to 80-100% utilisation within the first year, with long-term split of 80% captive and 20% third-party sales.

US formulations strategy: guidance still 2030, with annual updates only. Generic ANDA filings from the cefiderocol facility take a few years; some new molecules may be filed by end of next year, with nothing commercial before 2028.
capex_capacity: 7-ACA project capex about INR750 crore, with commissioning and first commercial batch targeted by March 2027.
Cefiderocol project capex about USD20-25 million; facility commissioning by December 2026.
Management said FY27 capex is not significantly large beyond completing the 7-ACA and cefiderocol projects.
Equipment originally sourced from China was rerouted through Italy, adding execution complexity without changing timelines.

Jammu site chosen for low power costs, abundant water and cheap steam from agricultural waste, plus GST benefit. PLI incentive expected for 2 years, with extension to be sought after the plant starts.
demand_pricing: Management said the industry still has overcapacity and cutthroat competition in non-regulated markets.

7-ACA weighted average price about USD60/kg per management, stable over 10-12 years. 7-ACA supply is concentrated among 3-4 Chinese producers (Sinopharm Weiqida, Zhuhai United, Yili Pharmaceutical, Livzon named).
Cefixime is under the most margin stress, driven by rest-of-world volumes.
Management expects regulated-market demand to improve over the next 2-3 quarters, with H2 seasonally stronger.
Ceftriaxone non-sterile supply from the new 7-ACA-linked capacity is planned for other Indian sterile manufacturers, which currently import from China.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins recover in H2 FY27 or only in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-regulated competition will persist and is hard to predict. It hopes regulated demand improves over the next two to three quarters, and called Q1 mediocre.

qa_highlights.question: What are the 7-ACA ramp-up and captive vs third-party split?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up to 80-100% by the end of year one, starting slowly. Long-term guidance is 80% in-house and 20% third-party. All output goes in-house until customer GMP approvals are obtained.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is budgeted for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant new capex beyond completing 7-ACA (INR750 crore) and cefiderocol (USD20-25 million).

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth reach about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not be prudent to give an annual growth number at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Exblifep partner pipeline and FY27 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Advanced talks for South America, Mexico, Philippines, Thailand, Morocco and Australia. Management does not guide yearly numbers; the USD1-2 billion is lifetime potential. Management hopes for three or four more agreements by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk of Chinese 7-ACA price cuts once the plant is running?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Chinese producers have stable pricing and no cartel-like Pen G situation, so it sees little room for drastic cuts. It also acknowledged that Chinese pricing is unpredictable and that the company is working on yield and tighter concentration as its plan A.

544838|2026-06.headline: XtraNet Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to ~Rs 51 crore, but EBITDA rose 89% to ~Rs 10 crore (20.59% margin) on services mix.
544838|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 11% YoY to about Rs 51 crore in Q1 FY27, while operating EBITDA rose 89% to about Rs 10 crore, with margin up 855 bps to 20.59%. PAT was about Rs 6 crore (+77% YoY), a PAT margin of 11.88% (+444 bps). Management attributed the margin expansion to a higher services share, which was about 65-68% of revenue versus about 46% in Q1 FY26. Order book stood at about Rs 373 crore across 55 projects as of June 30, 2026, after fresh orders of about Rs 60 crore in the quarter.

segments.name: Data center infrastructure and IT operations
segments.commentary: Largest segment at about 48% of Q1 FY27 revenue; management targets about 50% of revenue long term and 35-40% annual growth in this segment.

segments.name: Enterprise applications
segments.commentary: Contributed about 26% of Q1 FY27 revenue; ERP design, configuration and implementation across finance, HR, procurement and billing modules.

segments.name: Proprietary platforms (Synergy, XtraTrust)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 14% of Q1 FY27 revenue; XtraTrust is a MeitY-approved certifying authority with about 850,000 subscribers onboarded.

segments.name: Digital services
segments.commentary: Contributed about 12% of Q1 FY27 revenue, covering banking support, cloud analytics, AI, IoT and blockchain.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of Rs 500+ crore versus FY26 revenue of about Rs 365 crore, implying about 35-40% growth.
Management expects 55-60% of the current order book to be executed in FY27 (the CFO said 55%).
Medium-term target of 35-40% revenue CAGR over the next three years.
Target long-run mix: data center about 50-55%, enterprise applications about 20-25%, proprietary platforms and digital services about 30%+ of service margin.
Services target of at least 60% of revenue, with a 50-75 bps EBITDA margin improvement in FY27.
Effective tax rate of about 25% assumed for the next two years.
capex_capacity: Active bid pipeline of about Rs 1,200 crore; 40-45% is at an advanced stage, and management expects about 30% of the pipeline to convert within the next quarter.
Data center and DR pipeline of more than Rs 600 crore (50-60% of total pipeline), covering DC modernization, new DR setups, NOC and SOC.
Management is expanding data center capacity at XtraTrust to onboard more subscribers, targeted within the next quarter.
Company has built more than 50 data center and command/NOC/SOC setups to date.
Hardware inventory was built ahead of the price rise, so existing government projects are protected from price escalation.
demand_pricing: Government and PSU customers were about 47% of FY26 revenue; in the order book, 45% is government and 55% non-government.
Order book split: about 45% direct and 55% indirect orders.
Around 50% of the order book is recurring (annuity) revenue over 4-5 years; about 40% of the submitted bids are recurring.
Digital trust market: about 11 licensed CAs in India; XtraTrust competes mainly with eMudhra, with 10,000+ channel partners.
Hardware costs have risen about 3-4x over the past year; management reports no cancellations so far, but is monitoring supply.
Product deployment EBITDA margin is about 6-8%, versus about 20-22% for services end-to-end, per the CFO.
Management now applies year-on-year price escalation clauses in new bids, linked to USD variation and OEM supply costs.

qa_highlights.question: What growth trajectory is expected for data center revenue over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 35-40% annual growth in the segment, keeping it at about 50% of revenue, driven by DC modernization, new DR setups, NOC and cyber SOC.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin guidance and its drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is Rs 500+ crore versus FY26 Rs 365 crore (about 35% growth), supported by the Rs 375 crore order book (55-60% executable in FY27) and new bids.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company compete in digital trust and PKI against peers such as eMudhra?
qa_highlights.answer: XtraTrust has about 850,000 subscribers on recurring models, 10,000+ partners, 30-minute issuance, and an in-house PKI engine; eMudhra is the main competitor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle for data center projects?
qa_highlights.answer: End-to-end cycle of 12-15 months; government billing realises in about 120-150 days, and O&M/services billing in 45-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between services and products, and the margin difference?
qa_highlights.answer: Services were about 60% of FY26 revenue, now 65-68% in Q1; product EBITDA margin is about 6-8% versus 20-22% for services.

qa_highlights.question: How do CAPEX and OPEX models and recognition work?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 50-60% of a project is CAPEX billed over 6-18 months; the rest is billed over 4-7 years as O&M. Revenue is recognised on billing with straight-line annuities and no step-ups.

qa_highlights.question: Is hardware price inflation passed through to clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a direct pass-through; prices are locked with OEMs per project after order, and price escalation clauses are now used in new bids and repeat orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the typical bid-to-order conversion timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Government and PSU orders take about 60-90 days from proposal to order; large enterprise, aviation and BFSI take 30-60 days.

risks_watch: Hardware cost increase of about 3-4x; management says product availability is becoming a challenge, and future orders may face pricing pressure.
Margin dilution during CAPEX-heavy phases of large projects (12-14 months), since product margins are lower.
Management's guidance (Rs 500+ crore FY27) implies a sharp step-up from Q1 run-rate (~Rs 51 crore, +11% YoY), and the call did not clarify Q2-Q4 phasing.
Dependence on government and PSU clients (about 45-47% of revenue) with 60-150 day billing cycles affects working capital.
Inconsistent figures in the call: order book cited as Rs 373 crore and Rs 375 crore; the 55% vs 65% executable share and the 40-45% vs 50% recurring share also vary.
Monitor Q2 FY27 conversion of the Rs 1,200 crore pipeline and the data center capacity expansion at XtraTrust.

544744|2026-06.headline: Powerica Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26.7% YoY to INR780 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 13.6% on commodity inflation; DC order book hit INR900 crore (INR1,100 crore by Aug 7).
544744|2026-06.overview:
Revenue grew 26.7% YoY to INR780 crore, with EBITDA of INR106 crore (13.6% margin) and PAT of INR64 crore (8.3% margin). Management said elevated commodity and energy prices, a lag in passing costs to customers, and an adverse revenue mix compressed genset margins, with recovery expected from Q2-Q3 after two-phase price hikes. Order book as of July 31, 2026 was INR1,700 crore, of which data center orders were INR900 crore. Wind IPP portfolio visibility rose to about 638 MW after new awards, and FY27 double-digit revenue growth guidance was reiterated.</overview>

segments.name: DG sets (Cummins-powered)
segments.commentary: Order book of INR1,700 crore as of July 31, 2026, with data center orders at INR900 crore; genset EBITDA margin fell to 5.6% in Q1 on commodity costs and mix. Capacity utilisation 75-80% on one shift.

segments.name: Wind / IPP and EPC-BOP
segments.commentary: Wind is 18.6% of revenue, growing 28.8% YoY at a 48.6% EBITDA margin, helped by 51.3 MW added in Feb 2026. Owned IPP capacity is 330 MW, with a roadmap to about 638 MW.

segments.name: MSLG (defence/large projects)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell on slower order booking because international inquiries were put on hold by the geopolitical situation. Won a INR41 crore tender to be executed in 12-15 months and has a large PSU order executable by Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Allied business
segments.commentary: Contributed 9% of revenue; management attributed the slowdown to milestone-based project revenue recognition and defence product approval cycles of 1-3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 double-digit revenue growth guidance reiterated.
Genset margins expected to stay subdued in Q1 and part of Q2 and improve from Q3 onward, per management; no formal margin guidance given for the DG business this year.
Order book up 15-19% YoY as of July 31, 2026, depending on product mix.
Data center order book expected to execute over 12-18 months; management expects data center at 20%+ of revenue on an annualised basis.
Wind pipeline: 50 MW to go live in Q4 FY27, 150 MW in FY28, and 100 MW the year after.
Management expects 250-300 MW of EPC/BOP execution per year, at about INR400 crore of top line.
capex_capacity: DG set capacity: one shift in operation, utilisation 75-80%; management says capacity is sufficient for current demand and can be expanded if needed.
IPP portfolio: 330 MW operating, targeting about 638 MW (management corrected 633.55 MW). 50 MW added this FY, 150 MW in FY28, 100 MW later.
New wind projects: 100 MW GUVNL PPA signed and under construction; 50 MW GUVNL LOA awaited, with PPA expected Nov-Dec 2026; 100 MW SECI LOA received, PPA pending SECI call.
Two wholly-owned subsidiaries, Windfusion Renewable and Whisper Wind Renewable, set up for transmission connectivity; 49% stake acquired in Fuji-Kailash Energy.
Net cash of about INR193 crore is earmarked for the 300 MW under construction and pipeline wind projects.
demand_pricing: Data center order book rose from INR400-500 crore to INR900 crore as of July 31, 2026, and INR1,100 crore as of Aug 7, including a single order of over INR200 crore.

Price hikes taken in two phases: a small increase mid-Q1 and the balance at start of Q2. Quantum not disclosed; management cited a 10-15% range as not accurate. Old orders executed at pre-hike prices, new orders quoted at new prices.
Management expects one or two quarters for price pass-through, citing CPCB IV+ precedent of ~33% price increase over 9 months.
Manufacturing is the largest end market by share, followed by real estate; rentals and commercial are among the faster-growing segments.
Management said competition in data centers is rising, but it cites execution reputation; no market share data available.

qa_highlights.question: Order inflow and order book comparison vs March 2025/2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book as of July 31, 2026 is up 15-19% YoY versus the same quarter last year, depending on product mix.

qa_highlights.question: Genset margin outlook and whether the order book is fixed-price?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are impacted by the West Asia crisis for Q1 and part of Q2, improving from Q3. Older orders have fixed prices, with some price hikes obtained; new orders carry new prices.

qa_highlights.question: Data center BOP share and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: BOP execution is about 30% of data center project value. Margins vary order to order by volume, delivery timeline, engine requirement and customisation; no fixed margin given.

qa_highlights.question: DG capacity utilisation and expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 75-80% on one shift; current capacity is sufficient, with expansion planned if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Wind PPA timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: 100 MW GUVNL PPA signed and under construction. The 50 MW GUVNL PPA is expected by Nov-Dec 2026 after LOA and about 90 days. The 100 MW SECI PPA is pending SECI's call.

qa_highlights.question: Wind EBITDA margins by project type?
qa_highlights.answer: New projects earn 82-83% EBITDA per management, old 330 MW projects 62-63%, EPC 10-11%. Analysts noted these figures as stated by management.

risks_watch: Genset margin (5.6% in Q1) recovery depends on whether price hikes stick over one or two quarters amid high commodity and energy prices.
Old data center orders were priced before the hikes, so margin may stay below the new-order level until they execute.
MSLG order inflow slowed because international inquiries were paused by the geopolitical situation; the pipeline is not yet quantified.
Wind PPAs for the 50 MW GUVNL and 100 MW SECI projects are still pending, and commissioning depends on them.
Competition in data centers is rising, and management said it lost two direct data center projects to Cummins in the past (per analyst).

544617|2026-06.headline: Excelsoft Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44.05% YoY to INR802.63 million, while EBITDA margin fell to 16.24% from 18.02%.
544617|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 44.05% YoY to INR802.63 million, led by the education technology services (ETS) business, which grew 177% YoY. EBITDA rose 29.78% to INR130.31 million, but margin contracted about 178 bps to 16.24% due to nearshore build-out, international sales hiring, one-time recruitment and AI training costs. PAT rose 57.13% to INR92.28 million, helped by lower interest cost. Management guided FY27 revenue of INR350-360 crore and year-end EBITDA margin of 24-25%.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR7.8 million last year (per Q&A)
Management expects to normalise to last year's level or slightly lower by year-end

segments.name: Education technology services (ETS)

530555|2026-06.headline: Paramount Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17.4% YoY to INR 529.4 crore; operating margin (ex other income) expanded 320 bps YoY to 6.6%.
530555|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations grew 17.4% YoY to INR 529.4 crore but fell 7.7% QoQ, which management attributed to the seasonal Q4-to-Q1 pattern. Operating profit excluding other income rose 129.2% YoY to INR 34.7 crore, with margin up 320 bps YoY and 136 bps QoQ to 6.6%. The US export recovery after the IEEPA tariff invalidation drove exports to INR 155 crore (29%+ of revenue, up about 77% QoQ), while domestic revenue reached INR 374 crore. Order book rose to INR 615 crore from INR 583 crore, and a fresh equity raise of about INR 122 crore lifted net worth to INR 894 crore.</overview>

544402|2026-06.headline: Jash Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 17% YoY to Rs156 crore and PAT turned positive at about Rs5 crore; FY27 target Rs875 crore reiterated.

Management said shipments to Qatar, Singapore and other Middle East customers were held back (about Rs15 crore in total), so the quarter was below what management expected. Consolidated order book stands at Rs932 crore (India Rs293 crore, outside India Rs639 crore). Management reiterated FY27 revenue of Rs875 crore and PAT of about Rs100-105 crore, and said Rs1,500 crore revenue is targeted by 2031.

US tariff: 15.6% currently (10% special tariff plus 5.6%); management is budgeting for 25% and says it will not price for 100%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 margin gain is from tariff refund versus manufacturing benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a combination; the Rs5.6 crore tariff refund was booked in consumption. Dharmendra Jain also said the revenue reversal for deferred March recognition (Rs27-28 crore) was offset in June, leaving about Rs10 crore positive.

qa_highlights.question: Rodney Hunt margin profile and path to 10% PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 40% of revenue is from old orders and 60% from new orders; expected PAT margin is 8-9%; 10% may be reached by FY28 if things go well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Russia-sanctions/tariff risk and bidding in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bidding continues but aggressive order-chasing has slowed; it will review after the next US visit, and a US Senate bill was cited as a risk.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Saudi and US plant timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi: approvals received, land application submitted, plant ready by December 2027 and operational by March 2028. US: land acquired, contractor to be finalised; both targeted in operation by March 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs875 crore FY27 target expected to be exceeded and what is executable?

qa_highlights.question: Why did Jash Process Equipment (WesTech) underperform?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costing systems differed from what was expected at acquisition and marketing was not aggressive; a two-to-three-quarter transition is needed to set a clear direction.
