segments.commentary: Revenue up 30% YoY, about 6% of total revenue. Launched 345 SKUs (portfolio 1,312 vs 1,264 at FY26 end); distributors expanded to 155. Management targets about 10% of revenue over time.

segments.name: Tooling
segments.commentary: Utilisation 84%; 30 mold orders received in quarter, pipeline of 124 molds. Plans 20% higher output than the 148 molds developed in FY26. Being moved to Meraki Precision Tool Engineering Limited from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Moderated in Q1 on seasonal demand after 38% growth in FY26; about 30% of quarter revenue from exports. Under 1% of revenue; medium-term aspiration about 10%.

segments.name: Battery (Avinya)
segments.commentary: Revenue about 4x YoY on a low base, but Q1 contribution weak amid raw material cost increases, pricing pressure and shorter customer delivery timelines. Management expects improvement from Q2 but calls it a continuing concern.

guidance_outlook: Sales expected to rise sequentially each quarter; Q2 to date reportedly shows continued strong YoY growth.
EBITDA margin expected to improve gradually in Q2–Q3 as raw material price settlements with customers conclude by end-Q2/early Q3.
Target of about 12–13% sustainable margin for automotive ancillaries on OEM business (management view, versus about 19% cited by analyst as current).
Targeted to be net debt free within 3 years.
Aftermarket expected to keep growing around 30%; new distribution warehouse in West India planned this quarter.
Tooling output to increase 20% in FY27 versus 148 molds in FY26.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex focused on EPDM capability: one new line operational in Q2 FY27 and two further lines planned in FY27.
Tooling toolroom expansion and land acquisition in west area near Sambhaji Nagar planned in FY27.
Hutchinson-linked technology investment in machines and equipment for new product development (no JV; amount not given).
Industrial product business needs no major capex (low-value tooling made in-house).
Capacity utilisation at 73% in Q1; tooling at 84%.
demand_pricing: Industry posted record Q1 sales: passenger vehicles +25% YoY to 1.27 million units; two-wheelers +20.3%; commercial vehicles +18.3%; three-wheelers +29.7%; vehicle exports record Q1.
Raw material cost up about 4%; about 2% passed to customers so far, with the remaining about 50% of the increase still under negotiation.

Technology partnership with Hutchinson (sealing systems) signed; initial focus on glass run channel products for Indian market. Management expects clarity on revenue by end-2026; no revenue figure given. Named competitors: SFC, Anand Nishikawa, Toyota Bussei.
Mahindra: Tier 1 sealing products SOP scheduled for Q3 FY27; Tier 2 injection moulding tooling and sunroof sealing in development.
Management said pre-COVID margins are very difficult to regain given changed raw material prices and competitive pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue is expected from the Hutchinson partnership over the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical estimate; products are being co-developed for all customers with focus on India, and clarity on timing expected by end-2026. Focus product is glass run channel.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating margin plan and when will margins improve?
qa_highlights.answer: About 4% raw material inflation with about 2% passed through; the rest expected to be settled by end-Q2 or early Q3. Internal margin targets exist but were not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the JV exit proceeds be used?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR100 crores received; INR8 crores for tax; 25% of the remainder for working capital; the rest for strategic capex in EPDM, tooling expansion and western land.

qa_highlights.question: When does the battery business reach breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 contribution was weak; management hopes for improvement from Q2 but acknowledged it remains a concern without giving a breakeven figure.

qa_highlights.question: Will the growth momentum continue through the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 to date shows strong growth and expects sequential sales increases; not a one-off from low base or deferred orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin level and why has top-line growth been muted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 12–13% sustainable margin for OEM ancillaries; attributed past slow growth to actions taken over 2–3 years and to electrical content gains not reaching the company's sealing and moulded parts portfolio.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation: about 50% of the 4% cost increase still unrecovered from customers; settlement timing (end-Q2/early Q3) is a key watch item.
Battery segment losses continuing; Q1 contribution described as weak.
Industrial Products sales moderation in Q1; seasonality versus trend.
Geopolitical developments, commodity price volatility and global supply chain dynamics flagged by management.
Hutchinson partnership revenue remains unquantified; timing clarity only by end-2026.
Debt: net debt-free target within 3 years; finance cost trajectory not quantified.
Restructuring execution: tooling hive-off by Q3 FY27 and Avinya merger by Q4 FY27.

540136|2026-06.headline: HPL Electric Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35% YoY to ₹515 cr, but EBITDA margin fell to 12.26% on raw-material inflation, with metering margins roughly halved.
540136|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations grew 35% YoY to ₹515 cr, the highest-ever Q1, while EIA grew 9% to ₹63 cr and PAT rose to ₹19 cr. Consumer & Industrial (C&I) hit a record ₹278 cr (+55% YoY, ~54% of revenue) and Metering & Systems grew ~17% to ₹234 cr. EBITDA margin moderated to 12.26% as metals, industrial plastics and semiconductors inflated after February 2026 due to West Asia geopolitical disruption, and depreciation from recent capacity investments weighed on PAT. Management guided that pricing and mix actions are under way, with margin recovery expected over one to three quarters if input costs ease.</overview>
<parameter name="financial_highlights">[{"metric": "Revenue from operations", "value": "₹515 cr", "change": "+35% YoY"}, {"metric": "EIA (EBITDA as stated)", "value": "₹63 cr", "change": "+9% YoY"}, {"metric": "EBITDA margin", "value": "12.26%", "change": "moderated YoY; exact prior-year figure not stated"}, {"metric": "PAT", "value": "₹19 cr", "change": "increased YoY; rate not stated"}, {"metric": "Consumer & Industrial revenue", "value": "₹278 cr", "change": "+55% YoY; ~54% of revenue"}, {"metric": "Wire & cable revenue", "value": "₹146 cr", "change": "+79% YoY"}, {"metric": "Metering & Systems revenue", "value": "₹234 cr", "change": "+17% YoY"}, {"metric": "Gross margin (per analyst citing deck)", "value": "~30%", "change": "down from ~38% last year; not confirmed by management"}]

segments.name: Consumer & Industrial (C&I)
segments.commentary: Record ₹278 cr revenue, +55% YoY, ~54% of Q1 revenue. Wire & cable ₹146 cr (+79%) already above 40% of FY26 full-year wire & cable revenue; lighting +78%; industrial switchgear ₹56 cr (+19%).

segments.name: Metering & Systems (smart metering)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹234 cr, ~+17% YoY. Order book ~₹3,200 cr as of 7 Aug 2026, with metering & systems over 96% of orders. Metering margin fell roughly 50% in Q1 per management, driven by industrial plastics and metals.

guidance_outlook: Management expects C&I and smart metering to both deliver revenue growth; C&I visibility of 12-18 months described as strong, with high double-digit growth expected.

Current margin levels described as a conservative baseline; recovery could take an extra quarter, with C&I margins possibly back to target by Q3 FY27 if copper and other input prices stay at current levels.
If the Middle East situation eases and crude falls, management said margins of 16-17% could be restored, and it aims to grow margins further.
Smart metering visibility of 2-3 years cited; pace depends on AMISP execution. About 7 crore meters installed nationally to date.

Capex expected to be mainly maintenance (tools, dies) for metering; new projects may need capex but are expected to carry separate revenue streams. Analyst suggested ₹50-100 cr for the next year or two; management did not confirm.
capex_capacity: Metering capacity is in place after recent investments; future metering capex is mainly maintenance (tools and dies).
Automation: recently commissioned a new MCB machine that replaces 44 workers, producing ~18,000 MCBs a day, with 7-8 such machines installed across factories. Stated ROI is 3-4 years.
Seven factories, three tool rooms and over 100 injection moulding machines; electronics manufacturing described as large and internally integrated.
Backward integration in metering: relays and some critical components are not yet made in-house; management said work is in progress under a Chinese-partner MoU but gave no timeline.
Water meters launched; gas metering considered as a future category, with no commitment.
demand_pricing: Smart metering: ~7 crore meters installed nationally per latest official figure, against a first-phase target of 25 crore. Management said the Adani group's acquisition of Intellis Smart is positive, as HPL is an approved vendor for both companies.

Smart meter pricing: contracts are fixed-price; semiconductor lead times up to 52 weeks. Management expects to pass on some price increases on new tenders, but acknowledged competitive pressure from AMISPs.
C&I pricing: wire & cable has had a couple of price increases, passed on quickly; lighting saw its first price increase in ~7-8 years; switchgear pass-through is slower.
Distribution: 900+ authorised dealers and 85,000+ retailers; 'one consumer one family' scheme incentivises cross-selling.
Data centre cables: HPL does not have the full range yet; it plans to launch products with international certifications around May-June 2027.
Exports: a Middle East utility recently approved HPL's meter; DEKRA-certified MCB and lab support sales in ~55 countries.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margins fell from ~38% to ~30%. What steps are being taken to restore margins, and is hedging used?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall mainly to input costs rising from February due to West Asia conflict. Long-term contracts, alternate materials and design changes, and price pass-through are being used; semiconductors are bought at order time, while metals and plastics cannot be hedged. Metering margins fell about 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Will smart meter price increases pass through on new tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is asking AMISPs for price increases on new orders, but competition limits this. Pricing power depends on being a trusted, quality-focused supplier.

qa_highlights.question: Is the wire & cable growth sustainable, and what is being done in channel expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Copper tonnage is up 1.5-2x from a year ago, with growth across solar, industrial, real estate and retail. Management is spending on BTS marketing, a third-party last-mile sales team and dealer/retailer expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How is the AMISP consolidation (Adani/Intellis) affecting order flow, and is there an industry tender slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the Intellis acquisition positive as HPL is approved by both. Orders are placed on 3-4 month requirements, not multi-year locks. Management said ~25 crore meters' first phase is largely tendered and enough orders exist for the next 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin baseline for new orders, and when do C&I margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Current Q1 margins are a conservative baseline; new metering orders have supply lead times of several months, so price relief comes with a lag. C&I margins could recover by Q3 FY27 if input prices hold.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex rise, and what new products are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Metering capex is mainly maintenance. New projects would carry separate revenue streams, and details will come later. Analyst's ₹50-100 cr estimate was not confirmed.

506687|2026-06.headline: Transpek Q1 FY27 revenue fell 6.5% YoY to INR155.1 crore and EBITDA fell 32.4% to INR24.1 crore, with a 15.6% margin.
506687|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR155.1 crore, down 6.5% YoY, with EBITDA of INR24.1 crore (down 32.4% YoY) and a 15.6% margin, and PAT of INR8.9 crore. Management attributed the decline to aggressive pricing, oversupply and subdued export demand. The company remains net debt-free. Management said it is moving to a more aggressive growth stance, with an Odisha greenfield site (INR250 crore over 5-6 years, subject to board approval) and a multi-purpose pilot plant at Ekalbara. The DuPont contract, now assigned to Arclin, continues on unchanged terms, with renewal talks expected between Q4 CY26 and Q1 CY27.

segments.name: Polymers (end-user application)
segments.commentary: Largest end-user segment at 48.7% of Q1 revenue; down from 60-65% a few years ago to roughly 45-50% over time as the portfolio diversified.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: 22.5% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: 10.11% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: 18.7% of Q1 revenue; management cited rising contribution from organic peroxides, dyes and surfactants during the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at least 15% over FY26 (about 15-20% stated), with acid chloride sales to rise from about INR4 crore to about INR15 crore this year.
Target to double business size in 5 years; management said the strategy is finalised.
EBITDA margin guided at 15-20% going forward, with product-wise margins varying.

New products: one product expected to add about INR50 crore annual revenue, with commercialisation near year-end FY27 and revenue from next year; a second product expected to add about INR50 crore annually; several others could add INR50-100 crore each.
Odisha greenfield project: board decision targeted within 25-30 days; construction could start by end-November 2026 if approved; commercial production 1.5-2 years after start; payback 4-5 years.
Multi-purpose pilot plant at Ekalbara: 6-7 months to build, around February 2027.
Management said the company expects to run all four sites at full permitted capacity this quarter.
capex_capacity: Odisha greenfield capex of about INR250 crore over 5-6 years in multiple phases, pending board approval and feasibility study; DuPont-linked capex in the past was about INR110 crore.
Multi-purpose pilot plant (four streams, multi-step chemistry, fluorination, distillation) being built at Ekalbara; about 6-7 months to complete.
Effective capacity utilisation of about 70-75% (best case 80-82%) because capacity is product-specific and permits are 20-30% below the sum of stream capacities.
Expansion blocked at Ekalbara (about 10 years of approvals pending) and Dahej (about 1.5 years for permissions). Of three job-work sites, two are in the same Ekalbara area.
Management said about INR200 crore of capex over the last 5-6 years was largely replacement and captive thionyl chloride capacity, not growth capex.
demand_pricing: Pricing pressure from Indian and global competitors; price erosion in some products. Open-market acid chloride pricing is competitive, while Arclin pricing is formula-based cost-plus.

Arclin (ex-DuPont) contract assigned in full with the same terms. Management said Arclin's order volumes are rising this quarter, and the contract is a pass-through for raw materials; rupee depreciation is passed on to the customer.
Management said it is in talks with about 2 customers on sizeable contracts, but decisions are being delayed.
Electronics-grade trimethylbenzoyl chloride (TMBC/246 TMBC, for photoinitiators) is being developed for one large customer; purification work is ongoing.
Management said there were no product discontinuations, though some product demand fell sharply in certain quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Growth has lagged the 10-12% CAGR previously guided (FY19 revenue INR595 crore vs FY26 INR621 crore, EBITDA INR117 crore vs INR80 crore); would the company consider a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said estimates are not guaranteed due to cycles, guided at least 15% revenue growth for FY27, and said the board sees buybacks as lower-return than reinvesting in growth.

qa_highlights.question: What happens if the Arclin/DuPont contract is not renewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no reason for non-renewal (nine-year supplier, no rejected kilos, no missed deliveries) but is preparing for a worst case; a non-renewal would be a significant blow to volume and margins, with recovery taking time.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the INR300 crore Silox investment not being monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stake is illiquid under the shareholder agreement; the partner has been offered the stake but has not bought it, and no near-term resolution is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US tariff advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no special tariff; Transpek pays the normal 18% rate, and customers receive duty drawbacks.

qa_highlights.question: Why expand capacity when utilisation is only 70-75%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said permissions at Ekalbara are blocked, product-specific streams require a mix, and Odisha is needed for new products.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex now being committed ahead of demand, and what revenue do the new products add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is investing partly ahead of demand. It said two products could add about INR50 crore each annually, and that the INR150-200 crore guided earlier had not yet materialised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected IRR or payback on the INR250 crore Odisha project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payback would be 4-5 years.

risks_watch: Arclin/DuPont renewal (talks expected Q4 CY26 to Q1 CY27); the contract is a large share of volume and margins.
Margin pressure from competition and from volatile raw material prices (management cited a jump from about $2,600/t to $4,000/t within 10 days).
Odisha board approval and permit timing; the 2 to 1.5 year execution timeline is long.
New product commercialisation has slipped in the past (a battery electrolyte product was stopped after a technology change).
Silox stake (about INR300 crore) remains illiquid with no near-term monetisation.
Management said the West Asia conflict and logistics are a risk to global demand.
506687|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and the balance sheet, but cautious on near-term demand and pricing. Management was evasive on Silox monetisation, contract volumes and product-level margin disclosure, and gave specific but unverified timelines for new products and Odisha.
key_quotes: Transpek has been a consistent 9-year supplier now. Without not a single kilo even rejected by the customer in terms of quality.
Margins, of course, we have to target, and we are targeting 15% to 20% overall margins.
We are looking at almost INR 250 Crores over 5-6 years.
Payback would be 4 to 5 years.

543223|2026-06.headline: Max India Q1 FY27 consol revenue rose 66% YoY to INR68.6 crore, but EBITDA loss widened to INR25 crore; AGEasy breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27.
543223|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR68.6 crore versus INR41.3 crore a year ago, though it fell sequentially on lumpy DM fee income. The EBITDA loss was INR25 crore, against INR23.2 crore a year ago and INR6.8 crore in Q4 FY26, because Q4 included an exceptional DM fee. Antara Noida (340 units) received possession offers in June 2026, with about 75% of dues collected by the call date, though revenue recognition is deferred to Q2 on possession. Management said care home occupancy is improving at 5 of 8 homes and AGEasy's ARR is trending up toward INR120-150 crore, and it reiterated AGEasy profitability by around Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Antara Senior Living (residences)
segments.commentary: Dehradun is profitable and fully occupied; Estate 360 Gurgaon is fully sold out. E361 has sold 154 of 360 units by June end, with 27 sold in Q1 and about 34 in July. Noida possession offers went to 340 residents in June, with INR169 crore demanded and about 75% collected.

segments.name: Antara Assisted Care (Care Homes)
segments.commentary: 485 beds across 8 Care Homes in NCR, Bengaluru and Chennai; occupied bed days up 23% QoQ. Occupancy rose at Bannerghatta to 41% (from 37%), Gurugram to 41% (from 33%), Whitefield to 18% (from 8%) and OMR to 12% (from 3%). Four homes reached ARPOB above INR7,000 in June.

segments.name: AGEasy (consumer products)
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR19 crore in Q1, below INR23 crore in Q4 on post-peak moderation. Online gross margin held at 45% (vs 46%). Marketplace ROAS 3.8 and D2C exit ROAS 2.6; marketplace CM2 improved to minus 17% in July from roughly minus 70-80% historically. Monthly revenue run-rate about INR10 crore in July.

segments.name: Antara Integrated Wellness Clinic
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR15.75 lakh in Q1 with negative contribution margin; average revenue per client INR4,000, client satisfaction 96%, sessions rose from 199 to 307 in June. Will be built into residences and Care Homes, not as a standalone business.

guidance_outlook: AGEasy expected to reach contribution and EBITDA breakeven around Q4 FY27 (management: 'by January or last quarter of this year'), with CM2 improving as ROAS rises.
AGEasy revenue doubling target for FY27 (from INR77 crore to about INR150 crore) reiterated; management expects significant Q2-Q4 top-line improvement.
Management said it will report a smaller EBITDA loss next quarter versus the 63% figure cited for FY26 (loss to revenue ratio).

Two new projects, Bangalore (about 300 units, potential sales value about INR900 crore, in final diligence) and Dehradun (under 150 units, sales value INR850-900 crore), are expected to help meet the 1.5 million sq ft / INR1,800 crore annual sales ambition for the year; definitive documents pending.
Care Home expansion decision timed for October-November 2026, subject to occupancy trends; no new beds added at present.
Incremental capital requirement of about USD20 million over the next two years (reduced from about USD25 million), with the second fund raise deferred.
capex_capacity: Antara Noida (340 units): possession offers issued June 2026; residents expected to move in over 30-45 days; Phase II approval is the next step, with rates cited at INR16,000-18,000 per sq ft versus INR7,000-10,000 earlier.
Care Homes: 485 beds across 8 homes; all 8 operational after DLF Phase II Gurgaon relaunch in July 2026; each new bed costs about INR10-12 lakh including operating losses.
Chandigarh project unwound after height clearance denial near flight paths post Operation Sindoor.
Second tranche of preference issue of INR40 crore received in July 2026; management says the total capital need is unchanged but working-capital credit lines are being used to bridge timing.
demand_pricing: Gurgaon E361 sales velocity slowed in April-June amid geopolitical uncertainty but recovered in July (34 units) and August; management says it has not seen DLF's senior-living entry affect sales.
AGEasy ROAS improved to 2.0 at Q1 exit from 1.8 in Q4; conversion rate rose from 2% to 3.5% after brand spend (Anupam Kher as ambassador).
AGEasy repeat rate is about 10-12% (88,000-90,000 repeat customers); management's directional target is 20%+.
Management noted that logistics and China-sourcing disruption raised COGS and forced some airlifting, depressing margins.
Competition: management said real-estate developers and hospital chains can replicate infrastructure but not services IP; DLF's launch plans in Gurgaon are reportedly small and tied to Medanta.

513375|2026-06.headline: Carborundum Universal Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 21.2% YoY to INR 846 crores; consolidated PAT up 23.4% to INR 76 crores, with Electrominerals up 33%.
513375|2026-06.overview:
Standalone sales grew 21.2% YoY to INR 846 crores, broad-based across Electrominerals (+33%), Ceramics (+15.2%) and Abrasives (+14.7%), and were flat QoQ. Standalone PAT was INR 88 crores, up 14.3% on a like-to-like basis excluding a one-time INR 68 crore subsidiary dividend in Q1 FY26. Consolidated PAT of INR 76 crores was helped by a INR 25 crore gain on leasehold transfer at Sterling Abrasives, while Abrasives standalone margins were squeezed by an oil-linked and fuel cost push of about INR 16 crores. Management raised the consolidated Ceramics growth guidance to 23-25% and kept other segment guidance unchanged, while Foskor divestment and Awuko closure updates are now promised for Q2.</overview>

segments.name: Electrominerals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 282 crores, +33% YoY and +12.2% QoQ, mainly volume and export-led with very little price increase; PBIT rose to INR 39 crores from INR 7 crores. Exports rose to about 40% of segment sales from about 35% last year.

segments.name: Ceramics (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 274 crores, +15.2% YoY but -1.6% QoQ on refractories seasonality; PBIT INR 59 crores vs INR 62 crores YoY as IC gains were offset by fuel, alumina and unabsorbed costs in new semicon and aerospace/defence lines.

segments.name: Abrasives (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 328 crores, +14.7% YoY, volume-driven; PBIT INR 34 crores with margin falling to 10.4% from 13.1% YoY, due to about INR 16 crores cost push (resins, oil, fuel) and INR 8-9 crores volume drop QoQ.

segments.name: Rhodius (Germany, Abrasives)
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 15.6 million, +18% YoY and +1.1% QoQ (INR 172 crores, +33.9% YoY); loss after tax EUR 0.7 million vs EUR 1.6 million a year ago. FY27 guidance of about 5% growth and a small PAT loss is maintained.

segments.name: CUMI Awuko Abrasives (Germany, being wound up)
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 2.89 million, +11.1% YoY; loss after tax EUR 1.69 million vs EUR 0.9 million a year ago. Voluntary winding up is in progress and management aims to complete it in about a quarter.

segments.name: VAW Russia (Electrominerals)
segments.commentary: Sales RUB 1.58 billion, -14.1% YoY in roubles but INR 201 crores, +3.1% YoY in rupee terms; PAT RUB 52.1 million vs RUB 71.5 million a year ago. Business is domestic-focused.

segments.name: Foskor Zirconia (51% subsidiary, Electrominerals)
segments.commentary: Sales ZAR 107 million, -14.7% QoQ; deemed commercially unviable. Q1 consolidated PBIT absorbed a INR 17 crore loss; divestment or exit options are being explored, targeted for Q2.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated sales growth: FY27 guidance of about 4-4.5% reported, or 11-12% excluding Foskor and Awuko; management says it could reach about 15% on a comparable basis given the order book.
Consolidated Abrasives sales growth: guidance of 5.5-6% retained; 11-12% excluding Awuko (about INR 108 crores).
Consolidated Ceramics sales growth: raised to 23-25% from 15-15.5%; management expects the Ceramics margin to be at the higher end of the guidance.
Consolidated Electrominerals sales: guidance of a 6.5-7% decline retained (reported basis); 8-9% growth excluding Foskor, and management says this could be 9-10%.

Margins: Abrasives 9.5-10% and Electrominerals 9-9.5% retained, with Ceramics 20.5-21% maintained. Q1 consolidated Abrasives margin was about 2.5% excluding the Sterling gain, which management attributes to Awuko losses.
Capex of about INR 400 crores for FY27 retained. Rhodius guidance of about 5% growth with a small PAT loss is unchanged.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capex was INR 53 crores in Q1 FY27 against INR 64 crores a year earlier; the FY27 target of about INR 400 crores is unchanged, and management would not give project-wise splits.

FY27 capex covers expansion in advanced ceramics for power electronics (including substrates), metallized tubes, rings and brazed assemblies, brown-fused alumina expansion, an integrated furnace for thermal spray powders and a zirconia furnace.
Metallized substrate facility is being set up with one anchor customer and a technology tie-up; it should be commissioned in FY27, with revenue from FY28.

Semiconductor wafer fab equipment components: small in FY27, picking up in FY28, with a peak targeted for FY30. Aerospace and defence will improve in FY27 with the main ramp from FY28. Powder purity is moving from 5N to 6N.
Refractories capacity expansion is on track, per management.
demand_pricing: Standalone Abrasives growth was volume-driven with very small price increases; management sees early easing of Chinese import competition but says exchange rates and China's export-rebate changes make the trend unclear.
Ceramics: growth was seen across segments; Wear Ceramics returned to growth this quarter after several quarters, and Metallized Cylinders and Engineered Ceramics are growing mainly through exports.

Electrominerals: volume-led, with treated-product mix helping margins; little or no price increase. Export share is rising toward 40%, helped by European duties on Chinese imports, with US and Asia efforts under way.

Abrasives cost push: oil-linked inputs such as resins rose sharply in May and June, with oil reaching about $117 a barrel. Grains (80-85% of COGS) rose only 3-5%. The US-Iran conflict that began end-February 2026 drove the cost pressure.
Management said it will not pass on further price increases until the cost environment is clearer, and will decide one quarter at a time.

533047|2026-06.headline: IMFA Q1 FY27 posted record revenue and profit: output rose to ~80,000 t from ~65,000 t average, blended realisation just under INR120,000/t, FY27 volume guidance trimmed to ~380,000 t.
533047|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the highest-ever quarter for both revenue and profitability, driven by firm ferrochrome prices and tonnage from the KNR-2 acquisition. Production was about 80,000 t against a prior average of about 65,000 t per quarter. Management trimmed FY27 volume expectations to about 380,000 t from 400,000 t, citing transformer loading limits and a gas cleaning plant (GCP) that needs work at KNR-2. KNR-1 first furnace tapping is expected around the third week of August, with a second furnace by end-September/early October. Management guided that Q2 realisations would be broadly similar with a slight correction, and Q2 volume only marginally higher as ferrochrome inventory is built.

financial_highlights.value: INR281 per ton (as cited by analyst on Q1)
Q4 MTM hit of INR32 crore absent in Q1; forex gain booked in Q1

segments.name: Ferro alloys (ferrochrome)
segments.commentary: Q1 volume ~80,000 t vs ~65,000 t average; ~95% exports, mainly to the Far East; domestic ~19% of sales. Expected run-rate of ~120,000-125,000 t/month once all furnaces stabilise in Q4.

segments.name: Captive chrome ore mines
segments.commentary: Chrome ore sourced from captive mines is the largest input and is described as insulated from ore price moves. Stockpile of ~6 lakh t built for next year's additional capacity needs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production revised to ~380,000 t (from 400,000 t indicated earlier) due to transformer and GCP constraints at KNR-2.
FY28 production guided at 475,000-500,000 t; capacity described as a little more than 0.5 million t post Kalinganagar.
Q2 FY27: realisations broadly similar to Q1 with slight correction; volume marginally higher as ferrochrome stock is built.
KNR-1 first furnace expected to tap around third week of August 2026; second furnace by end-September/early October 2026.
Full benefit of Kalinganagar expected from Q4 FY27 once KNR-2's 4 furnaces and KNR-1's 2 furnaces run at higher load.
Management indicated margin uplift of INR1,500-2,000/t once KNR-1 and KNR-2 stabilise at ~500,000 t; no formal per-ton EBITDA guidance.
KNR-2 50,000 t furnace: environmental clearance clarity expected in 3-4 months; additional INR15-20 crore approved in budget.
capex_capacity: KNR-1 greenfield: first furnace refractory heating underway, first tapping expected third week of August 2026; second furnace by end-September/early October.
KNR-2 (acquired): 4 furnaces switched on in March 2026, but loading restricted; 2 sets of transformers plus a spare ordered, to replace doubtful transformers in Q2-Q3 FY27.
Power constraint at KNR-2 cited as ~6-7 MW lower loading plus ~15 MVA load limit; gas cleaning plant work pending to meet emission norms.
Renewable power contract with JSW Energy: corridor available since June, power flow expected August; ~INR1 crore per month benefit indicated.
KNR-2 furnace of 50,000 t awaiting environmental clearance; expected operational around mid-2027, with clarity in next 3-4 months.
Board approved an additional INR15-20 crore budget for KNR-2 environmental and related work.
demand_pricing: Ferrochrome prices at recent highs; management expects Q2 prices broadly similar with slight correction; no Q3/Q4 price guidance.
Met coke prices up a little (currency depreciation in Colombia, high ferrochrome prices); impact expected in Q3 rather than Q2.
Chinese/South African supply: Eskom special tariff ($0.62/unit cited) lifting South African output; management expects chrome ore reallocation to offset, but flagged possible glut risk.
Global stainless steel production growth ~2.5-3% per management.
Domestic demand: management expects Indian ferrochrome demand to grow; duty protection only ~2-3%, so domestic and export pricing near parity.
FACOR capacity expansion (145,000 t to 500,000 t by FY28) noted by analyst; management declined to comment on FACOR plans.
West Asia crisis: no direct impact (no imports or sales to West Asia); freight costs up modestly but offset by prices.

qa_highlights.question: Expected Q2 volume, at least 90,000 t given KNR-2 running at optimum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers; output to rise further, but some ferrochrome stock build (17,000-18,000 t needed at higher output) will limit the increase. Q2 volume increase expected to be marginal.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 EBITDA a base for the coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: No definitive statement. Prices similar in Q2 with slight correction, offset by a slightly higher tonnage; Q3 and Q4 to see much larger tonnage.

qa_highlights.question: Has the KNR-1 and KNR-2 benefit reached EBITDA per ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Not much yet; ramp-up inefficiencies (power consumed without output). Full benefit expected from Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Per-ton EBITDA trajectory and whether FY27 volume will be 360-380k t?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 380,000 t for FY27; per-ton EBITDA guidance not given, with margin uplift of INR1,500-2,000/t expected once 500,000 t is reached smoothly.

qa_highlights.question: Met coke and cost per ton outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Chrome ore cost is insulated via captive mines; met coke has risen modestly, with the impact seen in Q3. Royalty increases a potential risk.

qa_highlights.question: Coke and ore consumption per ton of ferrochrome?
qa_highlights.answer: About 0.65 kg of coke and about 2.5 t of chrome ore per ton of ferrochrome.

risks_watch: KNR-2 transformer replacement (Q2-Q3) and GCP work; any further load restrictions would cut the 380,000 t FY27 target.
KNR-2 50,000 t furnace environmental clearance timing, expected mid-2027.
Ferrochrome price correction in Q3-Q4 as South African supply recovers; management would not give visibility.
Possible domestic supply additions (FACOR expansion) and domestic pricing pressure.
Met coke price rise and currency movements (Colombia) feeding into costs from Q3.
Forex MTM volatility on export hedges (Q4 FY26 precedent of INR32 crore hit).

544140|2026-06.headline: Gopal Snacks Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR 422.3 cr (+31.1% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 7.4%; FY27 EBITDA guided at 8-9%.
544140|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered record quarterly revenue from operations of INR 422.3 crore, up 31.1% YoY and 3.1% QoQ, with the fifth consecutive quarter of sequential growth. EBITDA more than doubled YoY to INR 31.5 crore (7.4% margin vs 4.7%), and PAT was INR 12.8 crore. Rajkot main facility restarted after the Gondal consolidation, though April saw about 5-6 working days of disruption (gas shortage and plant shift) that cost INR 12-13 crore of revenue in core markets. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20%+ growth (INR 1,800-1,900 crore revenue) and 8-9% EBITDA margin with exit near double digits.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 5.3 crore in Q1 FY26
No exceptional items in Q1; prior quarter had insurance gain, so QoQ not comparable
May and June at this level

segments.name: Core market (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Flat sequentially in Q1 due to April disruption that cost INR 12-13 crore; management targets INR 100-plus crore per month from here. Gathiya is the leading product, followed by namkeen, snack pellets and potato wafers; wafers grew 15% YoY in core markets. About 65% of Gujarat Gathiya market is still unorganised.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 41% YoY; 100% of UP top line comes from two SKUs, Champakali Gathiya and Papdi Gathiya.

segments.name: Focus and other states
segments.commentary: Focus-state distributors rose from 440 (Q1 FY26) to 530 (Q4 FY26) to 567 (Q1 FY27); other states rose from 110 to 129. Maharashtra distributors went 194 to 205 to 198, with focus on Marathwada and the Nagpur belt.

segments.name: Other snack products
segments.commentary: Revenue in the other snacks bucket went from about INR 10 crore last year to about INR 23-24 crore per quarter, including Shot Go noodles, rusks, wafer biscuits, wafer rolls, jeera biscuits and washing bar.

segments.name: Alternate channels
segments.commentary: E-commerce was INR 2.79 crore in Q1 FY27 vs INR 2 crore in Q4 FY26. Modern trade was flat at INR 1.85 crore.

segments.name: Nagpur plant
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation is below 30%; 159 distributors were mapped to Nagpur, of which about 60 have moved to Modasa for logistics reasons. Third-party units at Kashipur (about INR 2 crore per month) and Manendragarh support other regions.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR 1,800-1,900 crore (20%+ growth), reaffirmed; management says it has held the stance on 20%+ growth.
FY27 EBITDA margin 8-9% for the full year, with exit run rate near double digits.
FY28 EBITDA margin guided at 10-11% with exit near 11%; sustainable target 11-11.5%; average reaching that level around mid-FY28-29.
FY28 PAT margin around 7-7.5%; minimum 20% revenue CAGR over the medium term.
Insurance claim of about INR 30-40 crore on the fire loss expected in Q2 FY27; management says documents are submitted.
Seven NPIs planned across Q2 and Q3, five of them non-palm-oil with better margins; 6 lakh outlets targeted by end of CY2026 (from 5.25-5.5 lakh).
capex_capacity: Rajkot main facility restarted; production consolidated from Gondal to Rajkot, with expected savings in power, fuel, logistics and operating costs as utilisation improves.
Modasa and Nagpur plants contribute to the network; Nagpur utilisation is below 30%.
Double-service coverage now reaches 38% of outlets; run rate up 14-25% where it has been rolled out. Pilot of ARS (auto replenishment) started; DMS covers most of the distributor network.
Retail touchpoints on DMS at 4.24 lakh; another 60-70k outlets are served but not on DMS.
demand_pricing: Raw material inflation was 5% in Q1; 4.2% passed on through price hikes and grammage cuts, 0.8% absorbed in P&L. Another 0.2-0.3% hit is pending and will be passed through.
Q2 inflation is slightly lower than 100 bps additional, per management.
Management says the company now runs at par or lower grammage than competitors and relies on distribution automation rather than grammage to drive volume.
Management expects roughly 75-80% of growth from volume and about 20% from price in the rest of FY27.
Chana stored till Q3-end; potato stored; palm oil and laminate are bought from the market with no major near-term increase foreseen.
INR 5 price point remains about 60% of sales (down from ~80% in FY22); management says no visible industry shift.
Regional brands in core states (Balaji, Gokul, Shri Hari) remain present; Miraj and Star brands shut, and Miraj has restarted.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 330-350 crore FY27 incremental revenue guidance still intact, and what is the festive run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the run rate is INR 150 crore+ per month, April was lower due to the Gondal to Rajkot shift, and 20%+ growth guidance stands.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin and when will it ramp up?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable target is 11-11.5%. FY27 exit near double digits, FY28 exit near 11%, and an average of that level around mid-FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core market run rate target and how is the Gujarat business growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of INR 100-plus crore per month in core markets. Double service is being scaled up, and more products are planned to lift margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are the A&P and trade spend trends?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P was about 1% of sales in Q1 against a 2.2% annualised budget; trade discount is 2.5% of sales versus about 3.5% earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Nagpur utilisation below 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: 159 distributors were mapped to Nagpur, about 60 were moved to Modasa for logistics, and the 250-distributor-a-year addition is below plan for the 300-400 km catchment.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an FMCG business with no order book, and daily run rate is steady with no month-end billing.

544407|2026-06.headline: Aegis Vopak Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.4% YoY to INR233.8 crore, with liquid terminaling up 31% and operating EBITDA up 15.6% to INR179.4 crore.
544407|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 12.4% YoY to INR233.8 crore, led by liquid terminaling (INR126.5 crore, +31% YoY) while gas terminaling fell 3.5% YoY to INR107.2 crore. Operating EBITDA rose 15.6% YoY to INR179.4 crore (about 76.7% margin) and cash PAT was INR124.9 crore. Management said the board approved a 52,000 MT LPG tank at JNPA and 49,577 cbm of liquid capacity at Kochi, and that the Pipavav ammonia terminal (36,000 MT static) was commissioned. Management framed a $5 billion capex plan through FY2030-31, of which about INR10,000 crore is to be commissioned by March/June 2027.

segments.name: Liquid terminaling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR126.5 crore, up 31% YoY, driven by higher volumes, new capacity and product mix; management cited JNPA plot 1 maturing (about INR6,000 realization per unit vs blended INR3,000) and better-located capacity commissioned last year.

segments.name: Gas terminaling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR107.2 crore, down 3.5% YoY on LPG import disruption from the Middle East; management said volumes held up via diversified sourcing and multi-location distribution. Standard throughput rate about INR1,175/MT, INR1,200/MT for some principals.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow volumes at least 25% YoY every year; management said AVTL delivered 3.9 million MT in the last year and expects more than 25% growth.
Liquid capacity to rise from about 1.7 million cbm to about 2.2 million cbm in FY27 and close to 3 million cbm by FY28 end.
About INR10,000 crore of expansion (JNPA, ammonia, liquid) expected to be commissioned by March 2027 or June 2027 at the latest.
Kochi 49,577 cbm expected by early next financial year; CRL4 at Kandla (about 94,148 cbm) targeted for later next year.

Funding: debt gearing capped at 0.6x and debt/EBITDA at 3.5x; about $3 billion of the $5 billion capex to come from debt, with about $2 billion equity net worth target and mandatory dilution to 25% of equity by 2 June 2028.
capex_capacity: JNPA expansion: 318,100 cbm liquid storage, 77,236 MT LPG capacity and a 35,000 MT LPG bottling plant, total outlay INR1,675 crore; first phase of about 100,000 cbm expected in Q3 FY27.
JNPA: board approved a 52,000 MT refrigerated LPG tank; existing liquid capacity about 101,900 cbm.
Kochi: board sanctioned 49,577 cbm; total liquid capacity to reach 132,122 cbm from 82,545 cbm.

Pipavav: 36,000 MT ammonia storage commissioned; 0.5 million MT/yr 15-year take-or-pay petroleum product agreement to start by year-end via additional liquid rail gantry; VLGC-compliant jetty by APM Terminals expected this year; Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline connection expected in the first half of FY27 (per Q&A, 2-3 months).

Mangalore: 75,000 cbm added last year, total 193,000 cbm; evaluating 60,000 cbm more; LPG rail gantry and bottling investment INR52.5 crore. Haldia: 226,890 cbm liquid storage plus 3 acres of land acquired; Haldia-Panagarh pipeline (HPCL, 60 km) expected October-November 2026.
demand_pricing: LPG throughput is priced per metric ton, not per storage day, and management said there is no escalation; the focus is on volume growth.
Liquid terminaling is charged per cbm capacity, not occupancy, so revenue is not driven by utilization.

Management attributed gas volume resilience to diversified sourcing (ITOCHU partnership, non-Middle East cargoes) and ullage availability; it said domestic LPG shortfall had recovered to about 80-85% of normal by July.
Ammonia realizations described as 2.5-3x LPG realizations; first-year utilization projected at 20-25% of the 36,000 MT static capacity (prorated for an August start).
Pipavav: 15-year take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc for part of ammonia capacity for its DAP plant.

qa_highlights.question: Are LPG throughput charges fixed by counterparty and term, and why haven't terminal charges risen while distribution margins did?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard rate about INR1,175/MT, INR1,200/MT for some principals; charges are per MT with no escalation. Management said terminaling is infrastructure usage, while distribution margins reflect sourcing and inventory risk during the geopolitical disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AVTL gain share versus national LPG imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited non-Middle East sourcing (none of its ships were stuck), a partner in ITOCHU, and wider distribution using freed-up ullage across more locations than Mumbai and Kandla.

qa_highlights.question: Is 25% volume growth sustainable, and what is the Haldia pipeline impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for at least 25% YoY growth; four pipelines are due this year (Jamnagar-Loni done; Kandla-Gorakhpur at Kandla and Pipavav in 2-3 months; Haldia-Panagarh in 2-3 months). Haldia-Panagarh is HPCL's 60 km line; the Panagarh bottling plant is 0.5 million MT/yr and currently about 0.25 million MT is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and liquid capacity path to FY28, and what is the Pipavav take-or-pay economics?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR10,000 crore to be commissioned by March/June 2027; liquid capacity 1.7 to 2.2 million cbm in FY27 and close to 3 million cbm by FY28 end. The Pipavav 0.5 million MT is higher utilization of existing capacity via rail gantry, not new tankage.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth plans beyond the INR10,000 crore phase and the $5 billion program?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing organic and inorganic options, inland depots, strategic storage and industrial terminals, and said binding agreements will be announced as signed. The $5 billion plan through FY2030-31 is reaffirmed, with timing expected to be lumpy.

qa_highlights.question: Why did liquid revenue jump when capacity did not change?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity added last year was only partly in the base year and has now matured, JNPA plot 1 is fully running, and product mix has changed, which takes time.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a mix of debt and equity, with debt gearing capped at 0.6x and debt/EBITDA at 3.5x, about $3 billion of debt, a $2 billion equity net worth target, and mandatory dilution to 25% by 2 June 2028.

544014|2026-06.headline: Honasa Q1 FY27: revenue grew 32% with EBITDA near INR110 crore and PAT INR90 crore; management says FY27 growth will beat the high-teens five-year CAGR.
544014|2026-06.overview:
Management reported 32% growth, EBITDA of almost INR110 crore, PAT of INR90 crore, and about INR83 crore of cash generation, with 30.5% volume growth. Management attributed margin expansion to B2B mix, A&P efficiency, opex leverage (about 100 bps) and a non-recurring one-time opex benefit, and said the one-time item was not recurring. Focus categories grew 35%+ and reached about 85% of sales; Mamaearth accelerated to high-teens growth and the second INR1,000 crore brand (The Derma Co.) was announced. Management also disclosed the entry into fragrances (FIKN) and the Fluence Pharma acquisition under Honasa Health, still pending conditions precedent.</overview>

segments.name: Mamaearth
segments.commentary: Accelerated to high-teens growth in Q1 FY27, driven by focus categories; Rice face wash is now the number one face wash, Rosemary shampoo above INR100 crore ARR, and both online and offline grew at strong double digits.

segments.name: The Derma Co.
segments.commentary: Now the second INR1,000 crore brand in the portfolio and has entered the teens EBITDA club; latest contribution about 80% online and 20% offline (GT plus MT), with presence in close to 50,000 GT outlets.

segments.name: BTM Ventures (acquired January 2026)
segments.commentary: ARR of INR150 crore in the latest quarter, grown almost 100% since acquisition; expanded to Maharashtra, opened a new category and new channels.

segments.name: Young brands (Aqualogica, Dr. Sheth's, BBlunt, Staze, Reginald)
segments.commentary: Growing 30%+ excluding BTM Ventures; Aqualogica relaunched in Q1 targeting Gen Z; Reginald expanding on two marketplaces and into new geographies; specific ARR not disclosed.

segments.name: Fragrances (FIKN) and Honasa Health
segments.commentary: FIKN launched as India's first elixir-based fragrance brand, clinically tested for 12-hour stay; Honasa Health subsidiary formed for nutrition and wellness, with the Fluence Pharma acquisition still in conditions precedent and diligence.

guidance_outlook: Five-year plan: high-teens revenue CAGR and EBITDA margin expansion of 100-150 bps a year to reach 15% EBITDA margin in five years; FY27 expected to beat this CAGR and expand margin by at least 150-200 bps.
Mamaearth expected to deliver double-digit CAGR over five years and to grow better than planned CAGR this year.
Q2 expected to see sequential dip in scale as summer seasonality fades; management said growth-first mindset means reinvestment where needed.
Reported and like-to-like growth expected to converge from Q2 once the Flipkart settlement base is clean; this is the last quarter of the settlement slide.
Packaging and crude-linked cost inflation expected to hit from Q2; calibrated price increases taken at end of Q1 to offset it.
capex_capacity: Honasa Health subsidiary created for nutrition and wellness; Fluence Pharma acquisition pending condition precedent and diligence completion.
The Derma Co. has offline presence in close to 50,000 GT outlets; company tracks reach of about INR3 lakh outlets per AC Nielsen universe, driven mainly by Mamaearth.
Distribution: direct distribution narrowed to focus on 100 cities; distributor inventory tracked and distributor inventory under 30 days.
Q1 cash generation of about INR83 crore with negative working capital; collections at highest levels.
demand_pricing: Market share gains: about 350 bps in face wash and 160 bps in shampoo in modern trade/offline (per management).
Quick commerce share gains tracked at category level via platform data; management says branded search share is higher on quick commerce than e-commerce.
Fragrance penetration in India 3% vs 11% globally; management sees fragrance as a horizon-two category.
Gen Z cited as ~45% of buying cohort in B2C categories, mainly e-commerce.
Packaging price index rising; company says price increases taken late Q1 to offset inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth expectation for the rest of the year, and how does Mamaearth trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated high-teens five-year CAGR and said FY27 will be better than that CAGR, with Mamaearth also ahead of its planned double-digit CAGR this year; no quantified guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin expansion is organic versus seasonal, and does seasonality reverse from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 should see at least 150-200 bps of margin expansion, with a clearly above-average year; the seasonal benefit is expected to fade from Q2 as summer categories normalise.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is the company about no repeat of past distributor inventory build-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is extremely confident: distributor inventories are tracked, collections are at highest ever levels, and distributor inventory is under 30 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Derma Co. split between online and offline, and where is it in offline scale-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Derma Co. revenue is about 80% online and 20% offline (GT plus MT), with GT presence in close to 50,000 outlets; offline effort is about a year old.

qa_highlights.question: Why hasn't fragrance been cracked by large Indian players, and what was the learning from the earlier Mamaearth fragrance experiment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier Mamaearth fragrance extension was shut down because consumer PMF was poor; it argued fragrance needs to be a fragrance-first brand, and built internal R&D over about two years before launching FIKN.

qa_highlights.question: How has the company offset packaging and crude-linked cost inflation in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said inventory management protected Q1 gross margin; the real impact is expected from Q2, which calibrated price increases taken at end of Q1 are expected to offset.

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA guidance too conservative given Q2 seasonality and H2 patterns?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 ex one-time was about 12% margin; Q2 scale dips sequentially and the company remains growth-first, reinvesting where needed; margin target remains 100-150 bps a year over four to five years.

544871|2026-06.headline: Shiprocket Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34% to INR592 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 9x to INR8.9 crore and emerging segment losses narrowing.
544871|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 34% YoY to INR592 crore, with transactions up 36% and GMV up 31%. Core revenue rose 22% to INR412 crore at a 12.8% adjusted EBITDA margin, up 50 bps YoY. Emerging revenue rose 70% to INR180 crore, and its adjusted EBITDA margin improved from -38% to -24%. Loss before tax narrowed to INR13.7 crore from INR18 crore, and management said the emerging share of revenue reached 30%.

financial_highlights.change: vs 18.0% last year; CM amount +43% YoY, +10% QoQ
YoY; gap vs adjusted EBITDA driven by share-based payments

segments.name: Core (shipping)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR412 crore, up 22% YoY; transactions up 31%. Adjusted EBITDA INR52.7 crore at 12.8% margin, up 50 bps YoY. Contribution margin 8.4% vs 8.7% last year.

segments.name: Emerging
segments.commentary: Revenue INR180 crore, up 70% YoY and 14% QoQ; now 30% of revenue vs 24% last year. Adjusted EBITDA margin -24% vs -38%; contribution margin about 15% per CEO vs 9% to 10% last year (39.6% vs 47.3% per CFO's company-level breakdown, which is inconsistent).

segments.name: Omnichannel (within emerging)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 92% YoY, the largest emerging sub-business; driven by quick commerce and PTL (cargo) fulfilment.

segments.name: Cross-border (within emerging)
segments.commentary: Revenue down marginally YoY; management cited global volatility hitting merchant confidence and a focus on higher-margin customers.

segments.name: MarTech (within emerging)
segments.commentary: Youngest and smallest emerging unit, growing very fast at a slightly better margin; checkout (Quikpay), Steal Deal, AI Assist and AI Ads launched this quarter. No revenue split disclosed.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance. Management said core contribution margin should stay around its recent trajectory and gave no timeframe for emerging EBITDA break-even.
Core adjusted EBITDA margin has moved from about 6% to 12.8% over three years, but management said it will keep investing behind growth, so no steady-state margin was given.
Management expects Q3 to be the weakest quarter because merchants shift marketing spend to marketplaces during the festive season.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model: Shiprocket owns no logistics assets and works with 42+ courier partners and 250+ partners overall.
Company has about 1,500 employees, with much of the investment going into emerging products and tech.
No capex or capacity figures were discussed.
demand_pricing: Core transactions grew 31% while core revenue grew 22%, which management attributed to input cost (courier rate) compression passed on to merchants and mix shift toward larger D2C merchants.
Cross-sell: share of core merchants buying emerging rose to 8.8% from 7.3% a year ago; merchants served via emerging rose to about 48,000 from about 30,000.

Power merchant ARPU rose about 25% while the power merchant count was slightly lower YoY, per the analyst's question; management attributed this to top merchants growing faster and a focus on expanding the funnel.
Blended CAC was about INR3,600 this quarter vs INR3,100 a year ago and INR2,800 last quarter; management said it is experimental, not seasonal, and that it breaks even within a short period.
Management said pricing is volume-based and that competition in single-point solutions exists, but its data scale is the differentiator.

qa_highlights.question: Will core contribution margin and EBITDA margin keep growing faster than revenue, and is 12.5% to 13% a steady-state core EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CM improved slightly over revenue growth and should stay around that range. It declined to give a steady-state margin, citing continued investment in growth and operating leverage over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the emerging EBITDA margin trajectory, and when could emerging reach break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: No timeframe was given. Management said MarTech is higher margin and growing fast from a small base, and that growth is the main lever for margin improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core CAC rise to about INR3,600 from INR3,100 a year ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CAC fluctuates with experiments across channels and reactivation, has held steady for years, and is not seasonal. It said the focus is break-even, with CAC of about INR3,000 recovering margin quickly.

qa_highlights.question: Are 3PLs moving into D2C and SMB, and does that threaten Shiprocket?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its model is to integrate with leading 3PLs and that the D2C segment, which makes up most of INR32,000 crore GMV, is its focus. It said data and integrated stack are its advantage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power ARPU rise about 25% while power merchant count fell slightly?
qa_highlights.answer: Top merchants are growing faster, and the company is expanding the merchant funnel to convert more merchants into power merchants over time. Management said near-term results depend on macro conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Q3 is typically weakest, because merchants shift marketing spend to marketplaces during the festive season. No other seasonality was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why has realization per shipment fallen (from about INR96 in FY24 to about INR72 now, per analyst's calculation)?
qa_highlights.answer: The 216 million figure is total unique transactions, not core shipments. Management said the decline reflects the mix shift toward emerging (30% of revenue) and a rise in transactions, while margins as a percentage improved. Core shipment count was not disclosed.

543399|2026-06.headline: Tarsons Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.7% YoY to INR 110.2 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 23.6% on input-cost spikes of 25-50%.
543399|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue grew about 21% YoY to INR 110.2 crore and standalone revenue reached INR 86.1 crore, the company's highest Q1 standalone revenue. Domestic sales grew 17% and exports rose about 29%, with the German subsidiary Nerbe up about 6% in constant currency. Gross margin (standalone) fell to 67.1% on polymer price spikes, and consolidated EBITDA was INR 26 crore (23.6% margin), with new-facility operating costs also weighing. Management said the remaining Panchla lines are due for full commissioning in Q2, with revenue contribution from H2 FY27, and that FY27 profit will stay moderate.</overview>
