segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 5,343 mn, down from INR 6,112 mn; EBITDA margin 6.3% vs 17.9%, hit by deferred order and FX loss.

segments.name: Marketable Molecules (cholesterol, Vitamin D and analogues)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,432 mn, up from INR 968 mn; margin normalised as cholesterol sales outweighed analogues versus a high analogue quarter last year. Vitamin D and analogues sales and margin reportedly rose.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group revenue growth guided to single digits; France and Swiss CDMO growth slower than planned.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected similar to FY26, possibly slightly higher.
Indian entity revenue guided to grow 25-35% in FY27 with operating margin near 10% (analyst's characterisation, not explicitly confirmed by management).
FY28-29: at least double-digit growth in France and India; group revenue growth above 10% YoY; EBITDA margin closer to 25-26% seen before EDQM issues.
No quarterly guidance; management said Q2 is difficult to guide. Net debt expected CHF 140-150 mn (excluding promoter infusion), reducing by about CHF 8-9 mn.
Interest expense guided at about INR 130-140 crores for the full year (about INR 35-40 crores per quarter).
Promoter ECB up to CHF 200 mn at 4% all-inclusive, 10-year tenor, to prepay high-cost India debt; expected in 60-90 days. RBI approval reportedly received.
capex_capacity: Two tech transfers from Carbogen Amcis Switzerland to India: one commercial contract signed with a US company (Switzerland to Bavla, to complete within FY27); a second legacy project approved by a Swiss MNC and already initiated; three more in advanced discussion.
Second co-investment with the Japanese ADC customer is in progress, with operations expected in calendar 2027.
Naroda and Bavla hold certifications from all major international health authorities; Naroda passed a Korea MFDS inspection and is under US FDA observation; two CEPs granted by EDQM.
Restarting some API production at the Netherlands entity.
Inspections scheduled for later in 2026 at Carbogen Amcis sites (no details given).
demand_pricing: New commercial leadership: Angela Ameriks joined as Global CCO; new India sales leadership; hiring in UK, Central Europe and US West Coast (start 1 Sept).
SPRINT early-phase acquisition initiative reported as successful; over 13 late-phase projects in drug substance portfolio, including PPQ campaigns.
Drug product (Saint-Beauzire, France): RFP volumes up and quotation rates raised, though market is challenging; big pharma audits had positive outcomes.
Naroda: CDMO RFPs rising steeply, several in final negotiation; semiconductor and fine-chemical projects in progress.
Biotech funding slowdown is weighing on development revenue; destocking by customers after pandemic stockpiling noted.
ADC-related revenue in the quarter was about INR 150 crores, including linker, payload and hyper molecule.
Specialty business: new wool grease sources at better prices; new markets in Vietnam, Africa and South America.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 revenue and EBITDA margin targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Single-digit revenue growth for FY27; EBITDA margin similar to last year, maybe slightly higher.

qa_highlights.question: How will the high-cost debt be refinanced?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter entity to raise up to CHF 200 mn in foreign currency and infuse it as ECB into the Indian entity, at 4% all-inclusive for 10 years; expected in 60-90 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why does cash stay overseas rather than repay India debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiary-to-parent loans are not permitted, and repatriation via dividends triggers tax leakage, so Swiss cash is kept as deposits to fund overseas needs.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 net debt and interest expense?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about CHF 140-150 mn, falling CHF 8-9 mn; interest expense about INR 130-140 crores for the full year, excluding promoter infusion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 550 crore EBITDA for the remaining three quarters achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not be INR 200 mn each quarter, but expects EBITDA similar to last year, with focus on the top line.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the company swung between profit and loss quarter to quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lumpy B2B shipments tied to new chemical entities, a largely fixed cost base (employee cost about 50% of P&L), and Q4 typically the strongest quarter; each INR 10 mn revenue could add about 70% to EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How much goodwill remains and is it amortised?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated goodwill is above INR 4,000 crores, restated at closing rates and not amortised; standalone goodwill is about INR 550 crores and is amortised; original INR 1,350 crores.

532899|2026-06.headline: Kaveri Seed Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 815 crore from Rs 945 crore (about -14%) on a weak El Nino monsoon, with EBITDA margin held near 35%.
532899|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 815 crore against Rs 945 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA at Rs 285 crore (vs Rs 332 crore) and net profit at Rs 271.3 crore (vs Rs 316 crore) as stated on the call. Management attributed the decline to a delayed, deficient monsoon that shortened the sowing window, cutting maize sales in Karnataka and weakening demand in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat. Cotton was flat YoY at Rs 213.43 crore while non-cotton was Rs 601.57 crore, and new products gained share in cotton and maize. Management said the quarter's margin was helped by lower production cost (down 4-5%) and that inventory is up about Rs 200 crore YoY, prompting lower production next year.

financial_highlights.change: same as last year, management said slightly above
about Rs 265-270 crore as of 30 June

segments.name: Cotton
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 213.43 crore, flat YoY. New cotton products were 37% of cotton sales vs 22% last year; North India (Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan) roughly doubled from a small base, while Gujarat and Maharashtra were hit by low rain and illegal Bt seed.

segments.name: Maize
segments.commentary: Sales fell sharply (about 40% decline per analyst question, not disputed by management); Karnataka sowing was about one-fifth done by mid-June. New single-cross hybrids are over 20% of maize sales.

segments.name: Hybrid rice
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 247.07 crore, the largest non-cotton segment. Two new hybrids KRH7344 and KRH7227 launched this season contributed 62% of new-product sales in rice.

segments.name: Selection rice
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 159.07 crore, marginal YoY growth despite poor rain in rice sowing areas.

segments.name: Bajra
segments.commentary: New hybrids are 65% of Bajra volumes, up from 61%.

segments.name: Vegetables
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 15.08 crore; management called it a small segment with some spillover possible in Q2 if rain improves.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the rest of FY27 quarters to be higher than the prior year's comparable quarters, with Karnataka recovery and Rabi maize supporting H2; the Q1 revenue gap is expected to narrow but no full recovery was committed.
Management said Q2 margins would be lower than Q1 margins, and that the YoY revenue gap would narrow, not turn positive, within FY27.
Karnataka Kharif recovery: about 1,500 tonnes sold this year vs about 2,600 tonnes last year, a gap of 1,100-1,200 tonnes worth about Rs 40-60 crore (figures given inconsistently on the call).
Export target of Rs 100 crore in vegetables and other crops within about 3 years; export margin expected at 25-30%, in line with current levels.
Management reiterated a long-term growth target of 15-18% (earlier referenced as 18-20%) over the next 2-3 years, with growth expected to return to last year's level.
Cash expected to rise only by about Rs 20-30 crore by Q2 to close to Rs 300 crore; any buyback is subject to a Board decision, with no amount decided.
capex_capacity: Inventory is up about Rs 200 crore YoY because production was taken up on expectations of a good El Nino-era season; management said production will be reduced next year.
Cost of production is down 4-5% YoY while dealer-level realisations are down 2-3%; management said FY28 production will be minimal and cost per unit should stay at last year's level.
Product pipeline described as among the best in 10 years, with Madhya Pradesh hybrids newer and not yet at scale.
demand_pricing: Monsoon deficit to June 15 shortened the Kharif sowing window and farmers bought fewer premium products; Karnataka tanks now filling after July rains, which management expects to support maize in Q2-Q3.
Maize price rose to about Rs 27-28 from Rs 16-17 at the start of the season, which management expects to support Rabi demand.
Cotton MRP is government-capped; management said Kaveri realises higher prices than many peers in the top three cotton segments.
Competition: illegal Bt cotton and smaller players have grown; management said no new hybrids from peers have taken share in the last 3-4 years, and that Kaveri has lost cotton share over 7-8 years.
Management said subsidiaries (sales of about 10-12 lakh cotton packets this year) operate as separate competitors, and that their revenue is booked independently.

500271|2026-06.headline: Axis Max Life VNB rose 33% in Q1 FY27 with VNB margin up to 23.2% from 20.3%, while APE grew 15%.
500271|2026-06.overview: Axis Max Life posted 15% APE growth and 19% GWP growth to INR10,610 crore in Q1 FY27, with individual adjusted first-year premium up 17%. VNB margin expanded about 3 points year on year to 23.2%, driving 33% VNB growth despite the residual GST impact, which management says is now behind them. Solvency was 198% after Axis Bank's INR381 crore equity infusion, which took Axis to 19.99%. Management reiterated plans for structure simplification (merger of MFSL into AMLI, subject to NCLT timelines of 6–12 months) and kept the INR1,600 crore QIP enabling approval open, with a sub-debt raise planned to replace the redeemed sub-debt.

financial_highlights.metric: Axis Max Life individual adjusted first-year premium growth

financial_highlights.change: from 20.3% in Q1 FY26 (Amrit cited 20.1% later in call)
improved 185 bps YoY; expense up only 7%

segments.name: Proprietary channel
segments.commentary: APE up 15%; offline proprietary grew 9% with a voluntary cancellation of sourced policies cited as a drag; online proprietary APE up 27%, with ~45% of online sales outside the large aggregator (38% a year earlier).

segments.name: Partnership channel
segments.commentary: APE up 16%: Axis Bank +14%, other partners +21%. Group Credit Life grew 57%, with 45% of GCL sourced from partners added in the last three years.

segments.name: Protection and health
segments.commentary: Grew 44%, with riders up 57%, driven by the self-employed segment proposition.

segments.name: Annuities
segments.commentary: Grew 116% (Q1 low base cited); new variable annuity Smart RISE launched in the quarter.

segments.name: Participating (par)
segments.commentary: Grew 48%, contributing 15% of overall APE; non-par saw sharp de-growth on a high base; ULIP grew 19%.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated guidance to outperform the industry and to grow VNB faster than APE for FY27; it declined to give a numeric VNB margin guidance.
Margin expansion YoY is expected to be sustained through FY27; management attributed about 30% of the margin uplift to protection mix and operating leverage and about 70% to yield curve movement.
Opex growth is expected to normalise in later quarters; Q1 slowdown in opex growth should not be extrapolated.

Solvency is expected to remain above internal risk threshold (around 180% ± a few points) for at least two to three quarters; sub-debt raise planned to recoup the redeemed amount plus Axis infusion capacity.
Structure simplification (MFSL merger into AMLI) timelines: 6–12 months post scheme filing under NCLT; next steps to be communicated later.
Accounting standard Ind AS 117 effective 1 April 2027 and risk-based capital (RBC) framework expected to add capital efficiency; QIP enabling approval valid until May 2027.
capex_capacity: Solvency ratio 198% at end-June 2026 after Axis Bank's INR381 crore infusion (Axis stake now 19.99%); Axis has signalled interest in going up to 30%, subject to its internal evaluation.
INR1,600 crore QIP enabling approval taken at MFSL, valid until May 2027; management said there is no immediate need, and it would be used if RBC framework is delayed.
Sub-debt of roughly INR480–490 crore was called on 31 July 2026; a fresh sub-debt raise is planned to replace it.
Individual new business sum assured up 32% YoY to about INR1,17,000 crore; rank 3 in private sector on this metric.
AI and digital: 30+ AI/ML models in production; mSpace 36,000 monthly active users; customer app 10 lakh installs and 4 lakh MAU.
demand_pricing: Participating products strongest growth; non-par declined on high base, with management expecting the non-par trend to move toward flat or positive as quarters progress.
Management said margins across annuity and non-par are broadly comparable; the proprietary channel margin is higher than company average, so slower offline prop growth is not margin-accretive.
Competition: management cited ~65–70% counter share at Axis Bank and number one at Yes Bank; across seven newer bank partnerships, counter share is 25%+ and it is number one at four of them.
Commission regulation: SEBI/IRDAI draft still awaited; management declined to speculate on impact on Axis Bank or the large aggregator.
Persistency: 13th-month persistency at 83%; decline attributed to discontinuation of a product variant decided in March 2026; 37th, 49th and 61st month persistency improving.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin increase, residual GST effect, and why did solvency stay flat despite protection growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management split the ~3-point margin gain as ~30% protection mix and operating leverage, ~70% yield curve. About 80% of the GST effect was taken in Q4 and no further GST impact is expected. Solvency rose to 198% on the Axis infusion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the structure simplification timeline intact, and how does Axis's potential stake increase affect plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Scheme filing followed by NCLT approval takes 6–12 months and those timelines hold. Management is still doing internal and shareholder consultation; Axis is evaluating going to 30% and both sides will disclose in due course.

qa_highlights.question: Opex-to-GWP improvement despite GST input tax credit loss, and the offline proprietary slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth was held down by productivity gains and cost cuts (travel, advertising, negotiations). Management said some of this will normalise. Offline prop growth was affected by deliberate cancellation of certain sourced policies that did not meet quality standards.

qa_highlights.question: How long can solvency be run before a capital raise is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can stay above its internal threshold for at least two to three quarters comfortably, helped by debt capacity from the Axis equity infusion; RBC and Ind AS 117 clarity expected in the next few months.

qa_highlights.question: Does the annuity push raise any product margin concerns; what is the variable annuity risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Annuity and non-par margins are broadly similar in aggregate. The variable annuity has a fixed return component hedged in line with other products; the equity-linked component is borne by the annuitant, so no additional company risk is claimed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the protection-led margin expansion sustainable given the June yield curve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged that the June curve moved lower and may unwind some Q1 yield benefit, but said repricing is normal and maintained the aspiration of VNB growth outpacing APE growth; it did not accept the 70% yield benefit would fully reverse.

542011|2026-06.headline: GRSE Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 39% YoY to ₹1,815 crore and PAT 44% to ₹173 crore; order book ₹13,596 crore.
542011|2026-06.overview: Management reported total income of ₹1,914 crore (+38% YoY), revenue from operations of ₹1,815 crore (+39%), and PAT of ₹173 crore (+44%) with EPS of ₹15.09 versus ₹10.49. The company said this was its 17th consecutive quarter of upward trend in financials. Order book stands at ₹13,596 crore across 11 projects and 44 marine platforms, and the Next Generation Corvette (NGC) contract is still awaited with management guiding signing within the quarter. Capacity expansion (brownfield and greenfield, roughly ₹4,200 crore combined capex) was the main strategic update, alongside Navratna status granted on 19 June 2026.

financial_highlights.change: First time below ₹15,000 crore in 10 years, per management
Attributed to absence of ship commissioning costs incurred in Q4 FY26
Management called it sinusoidal, tied to delivery phase

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Shipbuilding order book ₹12,980 crore (~95% of total); P-17 Alpha ~₹4,519 crore, NGOPV ~₹3,075 crore, anti-submarine shallow water craft ~₹1,815 crore, Ocean Research Vessel ₹740 crore, Acoustic Research Ship ₹450 crore, Multipurpose Vessels plus Dredger ~₹1,355 crore.

segments.name: Ship repair
segments.commentary: Order book about ₹96 crore.

segments.name: Naval vessel gun
segments.commentary: Order book about ₹219 crore.

segments.name: Bailey Bridge
segments.commentary: Order book ₹158 crore; management says 100% indigenous.

segments.name: Deck machinery
segments.commentary: Order book ₹58 crore; about 90% indigenous per management.

segments.name: Diesel engine plant
segments.commentary: Order book ₹82 crore; co-production with foreign OEM targeting 55-60% indigenization.

guidance_outlook: NGC contract expected to be signed in Q2 FY27; revenue recognition to start in FY28, with eighth ship completion around 2034-35.
Concurrent construction capacity to rise from 28 to 32 platforms by end of calendar 2026; to 43 platforms after Raichak (West Bengal) and western-seaboard facilities.
Management said current quarter's performance can be replicated in coming quarters, citing P-17 Alpha (~₹4,500 crore left) and ASW craft (~₹1,816 crore left) as major execution drivers.
Expects employee cost increase of 15-20% from next pay commission, consistent with past pay commissions.
Bonus or stock split: awaiting directions from administrative ministry and DIPAM.
capex_capacity: P-17 Alpha large ship ~85% complete; delivery targeted by November 2026 (calendar year). First two P-17 Alpha ships delivered ahead of schedule.
Four of eight anti-submarine shallow water craft delivered; remaining four to be delivered in FY27 (fifth ~91%, sixth ~88%, seventh and eighth ~65-70%).
NGOPV: first ship launched, second launched ~11 August 2026; third and fourth launches in Q3 and Q4 FY27; first delivery Q2 FY28, last Q2 FY29.

Expansion capex: ~₹200 crore for two Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port facilities (18-month revitalization, already started); ~₹2,200 crore for Raichak greenfield shipyard in West Bengal (DPR in final stages, 3-5 years to operationalise, infra work from 2027); ~₹2,000 crore for a Gujarat-side total ship solution facility (shipbuilding, green recycling, repair) on PPP model, DPR complete, environmental clearance obtained, ~3 years to operationalise.
demand_pricing: Live defence RFPs ~₹80,000 crore (Navy and Coast Guard): 120 fast interceptor craft ~₹3,500 crore (bid due next month); 31 follow-on water jet FAC ~₹3,500 crore; 22 interceptor boats ~₹1,200-1,300 crore (bids submitted); six NGOPVs for Coast Guard ~₹2,500 crore; P-17 Bravo (DAC AON ₹70,000 crore).
RFPs expected in calendar 2026: mine sounder measure vessel (~₹36,000 crore AON, split between two yards, 8 and 4) and four LPDs (~₹35,000 crore).

Non-defence tenders out via PSU demand aggregation: four MR tankers; six VLGCs and six Aframax vessels (GRSE partnering with a foreign yard and a sister yard); container ship tender expected (partnering with an Indian yard due to lack of dock capacity).
Letters of intent received for four platform support vessels (ONGC) and one green electric tug (SMP Port, Kolkata); GRSE L1 in NGC (~₹ high value, contract awaited).
Water metro opportunity: ₹200-300 crore per metro; ~₹1,500 crore and 30-40 platforms if five states proceed.
Next Generation Destroyer not expected at RFP stage before FY29 per management (no DAC approval yet).
Export strategy: no export orders currently pursued given domestic non-defence demand (~200+ platforms); will consider attractive European orders.
Indigenisation: management says ~80-85% overall by value; weapons ~60%, survival ~70%, float (hull) 100% but ~10% of cost, propulsion engines not yet indigenous; large survey vessel >80%.

540935|2026-06.headline: Galaxy Surfactants Q1 FY27 EBITDA hit a record INR 252.5 crore (INR 35,458/MT), nearly double YoY; FY27 EBITDA/MT guidance raised to INR 24,000–25,000.
540935|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose to INR 252.5 crore from INR 135.1 crore in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA per metric ton at INR 35,458 versus about INR 20,009 a year earlier. Consolidated volumes grew 5% YoY, with India up 11% and Rest of World up 6%, while AMET volumes fell 4% YoY but rose 19% QoQ after West Asia logistics disruptions cut April–May supply. Management attributed the margin jump to reformulation-led volume recovery, a richer specialty mix, commercial execution and feedstock volatility, and said some of these gains may not persist. FY27 volume guidance of 6–8% was maintained, while EBITDA/MT guidance was raised to INR 24,000–25,000 from INR 19,000–21,000; management implied roughly INR 21,000–22,000 per MT for the remaining three quarters.</overview>

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volumes up 11% YoY, led by double-digit growth in performance surfactants and high single-digit growth in specialty products; non-Tier 1 and direct-to-consumer volumes grew near double digit.

segments.name: Rest of World (Americas, APAC, Europe)
segments.commentary: Volumes up 6% YoY; Americas led on tariff clarity and TRI-K premium specialties; APAC grew double-digit. Specialty mix improved, lifting EBITDA/MT.

segments.name: AMET (incl. Egypt)
segments.commentary: Volumes down 4% YoY but up 19% QoQ; about seven weeks of Q1 at the Egypt site were effectively lost because raw materials were stuck at Jebel Ali, Jeddah and Port Said/Suez ports; management called this supply-led, not demand-led.

segments.name: EPC service income (Mexico project)
segments.commentary: Separate business model, not part of performance segment; income recognised in Q1 with amount not disclosed (management said not significant to overall numbers); recognition to complete by end of FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guidance maintained at 6–8%.
FY27 EBITDA per MT guidance raised to INR 24,000–25,000 from INR 19,000–21,000.
Management indicated INR 21,000–22,000/MT for the next three quarters, implying the INR 35,458 Q1 level is not sustainable.
Fatty alcohol expected to trade sideways at INR 2,600–2,800/MT (ex-Indonesia-type range), with no major expected jumps or corrections.
Annual capex around INR 150–200 crore; management referenced about INR 150 crore for this year.
Specialty products targeted to contribute more than 5% of total revenue by 2030 (per management).
capex_capacity: Annual capex of about INR 150–200 crore, with some capacity already front-loaded and commissioned; some more to be commissioned this year.
Capacity in place for petrochemical derivative-based products, but supplies were constrained because the derivative was not available; oleochemical use was prioritised.
No acquisition planned in AMET; any AMET capex will be debottlenecking.
Inorganic growth in Beauty and Wellness under evaluation; management hopes to announce something in coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Reformulation tailwind: oleochemical-based solutions became more attractive as petrochemical availability and cost worsened after West Asia developments; management expects this to persist for some time.
Feedstock: crude averaged above USD 100/bbl in Q1; oleochemical feedstock ranged USD 2,800 to 3,300/MT, then fell below USD 2,500/MT by late June.
Freight rates on exports more than doubled, feeding into CIF-linked pricing; rupee moved from INR 88 to INR 95 per USD (per management).
Price pass-through: management said customers accept increases when transparently justified; contractual business has a cost pass-through methodology; decreases passed on at the first opportunity.
BASF announced closure of its sulfation plant in Dahej; management said it is too early to quantify any demand upside.
Customer restocking was seen ahead of festive and summer demand, plus some extra buying on fears of feedstock availability; management did not quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA/kg at INR 35,000 in Q1, and how much came from inventory gains or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited reformulation-led volume recovery and operating leverage, specialty mix improvement, and commercial opportunities; some may not persist. It did not quantify inventory gains, but said mix and freight also contributed. Without these, it said EBITDA/MT would have been about INR 21,000.

qa_highlights.question: Is the specialty share decline from about 40% to 34% a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said specialty absolute revenue grew strongly; the share fell because performance products grew faster, enlarging the denominator.

qa_highlights.question: Will AMET return to positive volume growth in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was supply-led, not demand-led, with Egypt effectively washed out for about seven weeks; sequential growth of 18–19% and June momentum support a recovery, and it sees AMET returning to growth this year absent a new shock.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of reformulation reversing in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reformulation remains favourable while petrochemical and oleochemical balance holds; it does not see a big risk currently but will monitor coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 22–23/kg gross margin or INR 25/kg EBITDA a steady-state base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed the structure has improved but said it wants at least one more quarter before changing long-term guidance, to avoid overpromising.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the pricing gain is from finished-goods inventory spikes or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said freight costs, mix shift toward dry (100%/95% active) products, and the reformulation mix all lifted realisations; it declined to quantify the ASP increase excluding these.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for fatty alcohol prices and Indonesia's biodiesel mandate?
qa_highlights.answer: Palm oil is around USD 1,100–1,200/MT and the mandate is largely priced in; fatty alcohol expected to hold at INR 2,600–2,800 on a sideways basis, with El Nino a possible supply-side risk for next year.

501423|2026-06.headline: Shaily Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14% YoY to INR281 crore, with Healthcare up 85% to INR142 crore, now the largest segment at 51%.
501423|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14% YoY to INR281 crore and EBITDA rose 18% to INR83 crore, with EBITDA margin up 120 bps to 29.7%. PAT rose 17% to INR48 crore (PAT margin 17.1%). Healthcare drove growth while Consumer fell 24% on softer European and US home furnishing demand. Management flagged sequential gross margin pressure from polymer and freight costs, with pass-throughs lagging into July, and said it expects normalisation by Q3.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue INR142 crore, +85% YoY, driven by pen injectors for GLP-1 and other chronic therapies. Orders received after Semaglutide approvals in Canada and Brazil; two new platform projects signed.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Revenue INR116 crore, -24% YoY on softer home furnishing demand in Europe and US. Management said Q4 to Q1 sequential revenue grew, and the business is expected to stay near FY26 levels in FY27.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue INR23 crore, +25% YoY, supported by new customers and Consumer Electronics and Appliance/Automotive business confirmations; five Consumer Electronics components won from a new customer.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pen injector guidance of 36 million pens; management said it should be able to go beyond 36 million, though it is evolving.
Additional 25 million pen capacity expected operational by end-September 2026, taking installed capacity to ~75 million pens per annum.
Gross margin expected to return to normalised levels by Q3 FY27 as delayed pass-throughs take effect.
Semiconductor revenue expected to start in Q4 FY27.
Abu Dhabi plant must be in production by end-FY28; commercial sales from end-FY28. About 50-55% commitments/indications secured for that capacity.
Management said 24-30 months to reach ~$10 million revenue in Consumer Electronics; stated as projection, not guidance.
Management declined to give UK subsidiary growth guidance; said Q1 UK revenue dip is timing and will recover over the next 3 quarters.
capex_capacity: New pen line: speed raised ~9% so far; additional equipment not yet received, expected to add ~30% throughput; target before end of Q1 FY27 (quarter end). Second line to ship only after supplier reaches 80%+ efficiency and passes FAT.
Additional 25 million pen capacity operational by end-September 2026.
Semiconductor Trays: about INR5 crore investment in existing facility for initial requirements.
Consumer Electronics: planned new plant in south India with investment of INR80-100 crore; land secured (not yet announced). Start-up update expected next quarter.
Consumer Electronics components to be supplied from existing facility, with tooling and automation investment required.
Abu Dhabi plant: sales by end-FY28, aimed at European opening in 2028 and insulin and global markets in 2030-31.
demand_pricing: Healthcare: Management estimates device volumes of ~9 million pens in Q1 (all delivery devices); mix roughly 50-60% GLP-1, remainder insulin and other molecules.
Pricing is volume and market-driven with annual price review, not cost-plus; index references include inflation and polymers, with contract longevity a key factor.
Chinese GLP-1 pens reportedly priced at $1.50-1.70 vs Shaily's above $2; management said some Chinese products infringe patents and it is considering a response.
Gross margin fell sequentially due to post-March commodity and freight cost spikes, premium airfreight, and delayed pass-throughs.
Consumer: softer home furnishing demand in Europe and US; India is ~2% of Consumer sales.
Management said it expects the Canada and Brazil positions to remain majority or significant share; expects Mexico, Turkey and Saudi Arabia to open up.

qa_highlights.question: How many pens were delivered in Q1 and what is the GLP-1 vs insulin mix?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9 million devices in Q1; roughly 50-60% GLP-1 with the rest insulin and other molecules.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new line on track and is FY27 36 million pens guidance beatable?
qa_highlights.answer: Line speed up about 9%, with extra equipment expected to add ~30%; 80%+ efficiency targeted before shipping the second line. Management said it should be able to go beyond 36 million.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline and pricing versus Chinese competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin dip due to commodity and freight costs and delayed pass-throughs (May-July). Chinese pricing at $1.50-1.70 seen as not a major concern; Shaily priced above $2. Contracts are not cost-plus.

qa_highlights.question: Comfort with 36 million guidance given partner issues in Canada and Brazil?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap in supply must be filled and it still holds most approvals in various markets; it remains confident in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Time to reach $10 million revenue in Consumer Electronics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management projected 24-30 months, explicitly not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Consumer Electronics plant and Semiconductor Trays?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial supply started; 5 components to be supplied before FY-end. Semiconductor Trays: INR5 crore initial investment; Consumer Electronics plant INR80-100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Development status of emergency use, reusable and on-body injectors?
qa_highlights.answer: Reusable auto-injector to be tested this month or next and shown at CPHI Milan. Emergency use program ~18 months in, targeted for closure by end-FY27. On-body injector via partnership, developed from the Mira prototype.

532221|2026-06.headline: Sonata Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10.6% YoY to Rs 3,279.1 Cr, but PAT fell 17.1% QoQ to Rs 108.6 Cr on Rs 35.4 Cr forex hit.
532221|2026-06.overview:
International services revenue was flat QoQ in constant currency (+0.1%) at $82 million, while EBITDA margin fell to 15.4% from 20.2% as utilisation dropped to 88.5% on a delayed large-deal ramp-up, a one-time compensation benefit reversed, and AI talent investments rose. Domestic revenue was Rs 2,505.6 Cr with gross contribution up 4.2% QoQ and 14.5% YoY, and management said an OEM direct-billing risk has been partly reversed through contract renewals. Management reiterated an AI-native, engineering-led strategy and an AI order book of $21.4 million, but declined to give a steady-state EBITDA margin or formal guidance.</overview>

segments.name: International services
segments.commentary: Revenue $82M, flat QoQ cc and +2.1% YoY cc; EBITDA 15.4% vs 20.2% in Q4 on utilisation drop, one-time Q4 compensation benefit (~2 pts), ~50 bps forex hit and AI talent investments. Headcount 6,293 (vs 6,283), attrition 13%, offshore mix 70%.

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 2,505.6 Cr and gross contribution Rs 78.5 Cr (+14.5% YoY). SMC and corporate software business grew ~82% YoY. DSO rose to 65 days from 47 days, which management attributed to seasonality.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA to show positive traction each quarter this year, with some one-time items normalising in coming quarters; it declined to give a steady-state EBITDA margin as guidance.
Large-deal ramp-up expected to complete in Q2 FY27; management said margin trajectory should turn positive from next quarter.
Domestic management expects financial performance to keep improving in Q2 and the rest of the year.
Normalised effective tax rate guided at about 25%; Q1 benefited from a one-time US state R&D tax credit.
Medium-term: management expects gradual improvement in revenue and EBITDA, supported by AI pipeline.
capex_capacity: Utilisation at 88.5% vs 91.8% in Q4; attributed to delayed large-deal ramp-up and AI capability incubation.
Forward deployed engineer pool being expanded to about 100 people by August 2026.
Sonata University has trained 93% of workforce in AI.
Workbench agentic AI service delivery platform launched in the quarter; several clients have shown interest.
demand_pricing: AI order book $21.4M (18.2% of total order book) vs $16.9M in Q4; AI-led pipeline $340M; AI-led order wins +27% QoQ and AI-led pipeline +21% QoQ.

About seven new international customer wins in the quarter, including a three-year multimillion-dollar modernisation and managed services deal; a global beverage brand deal (800+ locations, 11 countries) was also won.
Top 10 clients were 51% of international revenue; management declined to disclose absolute top-10 revenue, which an analyst said declined QoQ.
Clients above $5M run rate: 12 (flat QoQ); $3-5M: 9 (flat QoQ); clients above $10M run rate: eight.
Management said 21% of engagements are output-based; cloud share of revenue reported at 62% vs 53% a year ago (per analyst question).
Domestic: some customers in the probable direct-billing list were retained through contract renewals after an OEM moved to direct billing with large customers.

544232|2026-06.headline: Interarch Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20.7% YoY to INR460 crores, EBITDA up 24.6% to INR39 crores, PAT flat at INR28 crores; order book INR1,864 crores.
544232|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 20.7% YoY to INR460 crores and EBITDA grew 24.6% to INR39 crores, with margin stable at 8.6%. PAT was flat at INR28 crores as other income fell because IPO cash was spent on capex. Management raised FY27 revenue to INR2,700 crores for FY28 (from INR2,500 crores) and kept FY27 guidance at INR2,150-2,200 crores. Order book stood at INR1,864 crores as of 31 July 2026, and a QIP was approved at INR250 crores, up from INR100 crores earlier.

financial_highlights.change: up ~9% QoQ per analyst; management said increased over last 3 months
positive; prior-year Q1 had negative operating cash flow

segments.name: Pre-engineered buildings (PEB)
segments.commentary: Core business; capacity about 221,000 tonnes after Kheda (Gujarat) Phase 1 inauguration; FY26 sales 162,000 tonnes (~80% of installed, ~88% of utilisable capacity). Gujarat plant started 9 July 2026; Phase 2 expected by October 2026.

segments.name: Heavy structures (Andhra Pradesh, Pantnagar Kichha line)
segments.commentary: Trial production started; commercial production expected around end-August/early-September 2026. Phase 2 targeted by March 2027 and Phase 3 by December 2027, for a total of about 75,000-80,000 tonnes. Management expects about INR100-150 crores of FY27 revenue from heavy structures.

segments.name: Buildings segment (multi-storey, data centres, hotels)
segments.commentary: Around 10% of Q1 revenue, versus about 0-2% previously, including a data centre order for RailTel in Noida. Management said about 35% of order book comes from new-age industries and new segments.

segments.name: Export / open web steel joist JV (Canada)
segments.commentary: JV with a Canadian partner (ER Steel) for a 15,000-tonne plant; first phase 4,000-5,000 tonnes (~$7.5m, ~INR70-75 crores) with ~20% EBITDA margin targeted. Production expected by July-end 2027. Management targets exports at about 10% of turnover in the short to medium term (1-2 years).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance kept at INR2,150-2,200 crores; management said it is well on track and may beat projections, but will revisit in about 3-4 months.
FY28 revenue projection raised to INR2,700 crores from INR2,500 crores, including about INR200 crores from heavy structures.
EBITDA and PBT targets for FY27 unchanged; FY28 EBITDA margin aim of 9.5-10%.
Quarterly run-rate of about INR600 crores targeted for the next 3-4 quarters, with quarters varying (e.g. INR550-620 crores); about INR1,700 crores needed in the next 9 months.
FY27 volume growth around 18%, to roughly 190,000 tonnes.
Capex planned at about INR129 crores in FY27 and INR133 crores in FY28 (roughly INR250 crores over two years, per management).
Margin expansion expected mainly in FY28 rather than immediately, as new plants carry upfront costs.
capex_capacity: Current capacity about 221,000 tonnes per year including Kheda Phase 1; Gujarat PEB plant (fifth integrated plant) started 9 July 2026, Phase 2 by October 2026.
Heavy structure plant in Andhra Pradesh: trial production underway, commercial production around end-August/early-September 2026; Phase 2 by March 2027; Phase 3 by December 2027.

QIP approved at INR250 crores (earlier INR100 crores approved about six months ago), with use of funds about INR140-150 crores for heavy structure Phases 2-3, INR50-60 crores for Gujarat Plant 2, and INR50-60 crores for the Canadian open web joist export unit. Timing not decided; may be within the next 4 months.
About INR240 crores of capex spent from April 2024 to date, versus INR180 crores raised in the IPO.
PEB new plants are set up only once existing plants reach 80-90% utilisation; heavy structure utilisation expected to be clearer by March 2027.
demand_pricing: Order book INR1,864 crores as of 31 July 2026, including a INR165 crore order from a major energy company in Vadodara; management said orders are booked on a basis of about INR600 crores per quarter.
Order mix: about 35% from new-age industries and new segments (EV, semiconductor, lithium battery, data centres, multi-storey buildings).
Management said execution was affected by site clearances and monsoon in Q1 and Q2; slower first half is seasonal.

Some recent energy-sector orders have 15-16 month execution periods (HVDC valve halls, variable price contracts), against 8-12 months for normal orders, due to longer site clearances (about 6 months).
Cost pressures cited: steel prices and shortages (linked to the Iran war), freight, labour and site manpower; erection prices have risen.
Management said competition is intensifying but pie is expanding; price pressure exists, but management is focused on profitability over revenue growth.

523642|2026-06.headline: PI Industries Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 17,023 million with 57% gross margin and 22% EBITDA margin; FY27 growth guided to lower single digit.
523642|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 17,023 million with gross margin of 57% and EBITDA of Rs 3,693 million (22% margin), amid soft exports and cyclical domestic headwinds. Exports saw volume down 8% and value down 12% YoY, while domestic volume grew 12% but revenue only 3%. Subsidiary losses, driven by global biologicals and pharma ramp-up, were about Rs 100 crore at EBITDA level in the quarter. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth in the lower single digits and expects FY27 to beat FY26 on an export recovery in the second half.

financial_highlights.value: Reduced by 19 days, releasing Rs 300 crore cash

segments.name: Agchem exports (CSM)
segments.commentary: Export volume down 8% and value down 12% YoY; new products contributed 16-18% of CSM revenue in Q1. Management cited soft commodity prices, genericization and tariffs as pressures.

segments.name: Domestic agri
segments.commentary: Volume up 12% but revenue up only 3%, reflecting price pressure; management said it prioritised market share over price. Flagship brands include Nominee Gold, Brofreya and Biovita.

segments.name: Biologicals
segments.commentary: Grew 50% with a three-year CAGR of 15%; global biologicals are loss-making due to market development spend (1,000+ grower engagements, 500+ field trials).

segments.name: Pharma / CRDMO
segments.commentary: Platform across Jaipur, Hyderabad and Lodi (Italy); some orders delayed to later quarters. Management described a long J-curve; company does not disclose molecule names.

segments.name: Electronic and specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: A commercial plant is operational and commercial supplies have started; management said the segment is not yet substantial in revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided to lower single digit, contingent on cycle.
FY27 expected to be better than FY26, driven by export recovery in H2, new launches and scale-up of pharma and global biologicals.
FY27 capex guidance of Rs 700-800 crore; Q1 capex about Rs 250 crore.
ETR for FY27 around 24%.
R&D spend kept at 3-4% of revenue.
Pioxaniliprole (first NCE) expected domestic launch within FY27 pending regulatory approval; other geographies in later years.
Gross margin target to be maintained via optimisation; management gave no explicit EBITDA margin guidance.
capex_capacity: Capex for Q1 about Rs 250-260 crore, spread across existing manufacturing, new verticals and innovation-led geographies/products.
Commissioned one of the world's largest flow chemistry plants.
Commercial plant for electronic chemicals is operational.
QC lab commissioned at Italy (Lodi) site, approved by regulators.
Centre of excellence for drug discovery at Hyderabad CRO facility.
demand_pricing: Management said global crop protection demand is showing early signs of stabilisation, but pricing pressure remains from weak demand and high input costs.
Domestic sowing said to be at par with last year after delays; chemical pre-placement and sales were affected.
Management said price escalation was mainly in generics, while PI focused on market share.
Export pricing and growth pressured by soft commodity prices, genericization pressures and tariffs.
Brazil nematicide market about USD 750 million; company aims for double-digit share over 5-10 years.
Global biologicals market about USD 10 billion, growing double digits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated lower single-digit growth and a positive trajectory, depending on the cycle.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be viewed through the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to sustain gross margins at the best possible levels through optimisation; it did not give an EBITDA margin figure.

qa_highlights.question: When will Pioxaniliprole launch?
qa_highlights.answer: Early start expected this year and India launch within the year, subject to regulatory approvals; other geographies planned for next year and the year after.

qa_highlights.question: Why did currency benefits not reflect in exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said currency benefits are shared with customers under a pass-through model, with some currency risk management, and margins are managed at an optimal level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the subsidiary loss and when does it break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses reflect front-loaded investment in pharma and global biologicals (market development, human resources); management gave no breakeven timeline and said it would try to provide quarterly biologicals numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the pharma guidance intact after order delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said delays are sequential timing shifts from new customers and products; it did not quantify the delay.

risks_watch: Export volume decline (-8%) and value decline (-12%) despite rupee depreciation of around 13% YoY, with management giving limited explanation of the gap.
Subsidiary losses of around Rs 100 crore EBITDA in Q1 from biologicals and pharma; no breakeven timeline given.
Pricing pressure in domestic agri and exports, plus input cost and inventory overhangs.
Pharma order delays and high volatility in CRDMO revenue.
Pioxaniliprole regulatory approvals and efficacy data, which were not disclosed on the call.
Biologicals growth depends on farmer habit change, which management flagged as slow.
523642|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and R&D, but cautious and somewhat evasive on near-term pricing, margins, subsidiary losses and pharma timing. Management repeatedly deferred specifics (molecule lists, efficacy data, the export currency gap) to future launches.
key_quotes: While the quarter witnessed softness amidst cyclical headwinds and global disruptions, we are steadily transitioning towards a growth trajectory.
Despite a challenging operating environment in the domestic market, we delivered a 12% volume growth in this quarter, translating into a 3% revenue growth.

544547|2026-06.headline: Jinkushal Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 37.4% to INR51.29 crores, but consolidated PAT fell to INR2.2 crores from INR6.51 crores.
544547|2026-06.overview:
Standalone revenue grew 37.4% YoY to INR51.29 crores and consolidated revenue grew 15.9% to INR56.57 crores. Profitability fell sharply on a consolidated basis, with PBT at INR3.04 crores versus INR7.26 crores, as shipping costs and employee expenses rose. Africa contributed about 32% of revenue against about 4.47% a year earlier, partly replacing Middle East business disrupted by geopolitics. Management said inventory of about INR96.8 crores, mostly overseas, is being built as part of the international strategy, and that investments in people and systems will weigh on margins for several quarters.</overview>

segments.name: Africa (geography)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 32% of Q1 FY27 revenue versus about 4.47% in Q1 FY26, offsetting lost Middle East revenue. Management said it sees the shipping and business cycle as established.

segments.name: HexL (proprietary construction equipment brand)
segments.commentary: Management said it is in early stages, with heavy spending on marketing, discounting and dealer development. Management cited a long-term PAT target of 12% to 14% (also 12% to 15% in an earlier call) and a 20% to 40% retail price advantage versus global brands.

segments.name: New/customised equipment, used and refurbished equipment
segments.commentary: No segment revenue split was disclosed. Management said new customised equipment demand is strongest near term, and that used equipment and HexL should each grow to a larger share over 2 to 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Long-term revenue target of INR600 crores to INR700 crores, to be reached in 2 to 3 years; management declined to give a FY27 growth figure.
Management expects healthier profitability in 2 to 3 years once shipping, interest and manpower costs settle; near-term profit is being sacrificed for long-term build-out.
Inventory expected to stay at similar levels, plus or minus a few percentage points, in lower double digits, with conversion over about 2 quarters.
Expects to see results from strategic investments in 3 to 6 quarters.
Expects operational manpower costs to keep rising over the next few quarters.
capex_capacity: Consolidated inventory of about INR96.8 crores at June 30, 2026, of which about INR84.4 crores sits at overseas subsidiaries.
Inventory is positioned overseas to shorten delivery times for used and refurbished construction equipment.
Management says the investments are transient (inventory, working capital, manpower) rather than fixed capex or plant machinery.
Post-IPO capital base and enhanced banking facilities cited as capacity to support higher volumes.
demand_pricing: Africa is now a major market; management said the Middle East revenue gap was partly filled by Africa.
Freight and shipping costs rose on geopolitical route closures and longer shipping times, which also lengthened debtor cycles.
Commodity inflation is not expected to be fully passed through; costs are partly absorbed and partly passed to suppliers and customers.
Management said new customised equipment is in highest demand, driven by faster availability and lower breakdown times for end users.
Management said customer collections have generally met commercial timelines, but geopolitical disruptions have led to some customer payment delays.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Africa's growth and can it be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Africa replaced Middle East revenue hit by geopolitics and board capital allocation decisions. Management expects the shipping and business cycle there to be sustainable, and it sees Africa, Latin America and the Middle East as equally important.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR97 crore inventory convert to sales, and how fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business cycle runs at least 2 quarters, so inventory should convert over the next 1.5 to 2 quarters, with inventory levels fluctuating by a few percentage points over the last 2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debtors rise: what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the debtor rise a planned overseas penetration strategy, with longer shipping times keeping receivables high until machines reach customers. It expects working capital cycles to stay elevated for now.

qa_highlights.question: Will freight costs ease and can they be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is taking a substantial hit on shipping costs, partly passing them to suppliers at purchase and to customers at sale. Management said it cannot forecast oil prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs yield operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it plans to add sales and purchase staff and to move from SME to mid-corporate or large-corporate operations, and will keep investing even at the cost of near-term reported margins.

qa_highlights.question: When will returns on these investments become visible, and what will the business look like in 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects results in 3 to 6 quarters. In 2 to 3 years it targets INR600 crores to INR700 crores revenue with healthier profitability, a dominant international business, and roughly equal revenue from the three verticals.

risks_watch: Consolidated PAT fell about 66% YoY, and management is absorbing shipping, interest and manpower costs without a date for recovery.
Inventory of about INR96.8 crores with about INR84.4 crores overseas ties up working capital and raises conversion risk.
Africa accounts for about 32% of revenue; management said it is not viewing any single geography in isolation.
Freight costs depend on oil prices, which management said it cannot forecast; geopolitical route closures are extending shipping times.
Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance and gave no segment-level margin or revenue numbers.

Management said the company manufactures backhoe loaders under contract in China, and an analyst raised natural calamities there as a supply risk; management said the locations it uses are unaffected.
544547|2026-06.management_tone:
Confident on long-term targets and the Africa shift, but cautious and evasive on near-term profitability, FY27 growth and HexL economics. Management repeatedly deferred forward-looking questions because of geopolitical uncertainty.</management_tone>
<parameter name="key_quotes">["We are taking the hit, but we are still able to grow on revenue.","So, the answer would be in 3 quarters to 6 quarters I think we can start seeing results of these strategic investments.","And I believe that INR600 crores to INR700 crores figure long-term revenue targets are still in place.","we don't intend to stop that even at the cost of it reflecting in the numbers."]

540497|2026-06.headline: S Chand Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs1,145m, but EBITDA loss of Rs97m and PAT loss of Rs187m widened the reported loss.
540497|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs1,145m, up 12% YoY, with gross margin improved. EBITDA turned to a loss of Rs97m and PAT to a loss of Rs187m, hit by marketing costs pulled into Q1 from Q2 and a one-time tax rate adjustment. Management pre-bought paper ahead of expected price rises, lifting inventory and slightly raising net working capital days. Net cash reached a record Rs1,182m after Rs141m dividend, and FY27 guidance of 10-15% operating revenue growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin was reiterated.

financial_highlights.change: Wider loss YoY due to one-time tax rate adjustment
vs Rs1,160m in Q4FY26, after Rs141m dividend

segments.name: School Education (K-12)
segments.commentary: Refreshed curriculum brands Mylestone, My Zen, SmartK and Solid Steps received repeat adoptions; Mylestone (650+ schools) and My Zen (about 500 schools) together generated about Rs55-60 crore in FY26. New partnerships with Allied, Jump Maths, Penguin and Speedlabs added to the offering.

segments.name: Content Licensing
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue of about Rs9 crore (Rs91m); about Rs14 crore booked to date. Target is above Rs40 crore for FY27 and growing active clients from 5 to 10.

segments.name: International (CPD Singapore, acquired)
segments.commentary: Q1 contribution about Rs1 crore; target of SGD 1m (about Rs7.5 crore) by year end. Management says it was profitable earlier, currently investing in content and marketing with limited burn; India and Middle East K-12 expansion will take 1-2 academic cycles.

guidance_outlook: Operating revenue growth of 10-15% for FY27.
EBITDA margin guidance of 17-19% for FY27, stated to include a 10-12% paper price increase assumption.
Content licensing revenue target above Rs40 crore in FY27.
Market buyback under consideration; management expects a decision by October 2026, contingent on acquisitions progressing.
Acquisitions under discussion in test prep and school spaces, total size about Rs40-50 crore at most.
Steady-state growth for core business of 10-12% over the next 2-3 years, excluding acquisitions and new segments.
Full adoption of NCERT new-syllabus books expected in FY27; West Bengal new syllabus expected to support growth for about 2 years from next year.
capex_capacity: New printing and binding facility: half to be completed in FY27, full completion in FY28; partial binding and printing to start from the following week, with operations in September-October 2026.
Management says the facility covers requirements for 10-15 years and should improve productivity, quality and output speed.
demand_pricing: Dollar rate cited at about Rs95 versus about Rs85 a year earlier, raising imported paper cost along with logistics and Middle East tensions.
Paper availability is not a constraint; management says the issue is price. About 20-25% of annual paper requirement purchased so far, roughly 3-4 months earlier than usual.
Receivable days stable; collections from the Middle East are being hit by geopolitical instability and are expected to normalise.
Management is cautious on paper inventory due to space and cash limits, so it will not buy the full annual requirement.
Regional board growth (Chhaya Prakashani) was lumpy in FY26 due to West Bengal elections shifting sales into Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company buy paper early and where are paper prices heading?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pre-bought to hedge against higher USD-linked import costs, logistics and Middle East tensions; paper prices may firm up next quarter. About 25% of annual consumption bought, versus the usual August-October purchase window.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 17-19% margin guidance inclusive of paper price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Guidance assumes a 10-12% paper price increase; management said a 40% rise would be a different case.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of buyback and acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: A market buyback is being considered, with a decision targeted by October once acquisitions progress. Two acquisition discussions in test prep and school space, total size Rs40-50 crore at most.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state growth outlook beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Core business steady state is 10-12%, built from 3-4% student growth, 4-5% volume and 4-5% pricing; acquisitions or new segments would add to this.

qa_highlights.question: Will goodwill be revalued or impaired?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not impair now because the acquired investments have intrinsic value. Impairment may be considered in a year with exceptional income, such as a real estate sale or Smartivity listing.

risks_watch: Paper cost inflation versus the 10-12% assumed in the 17-19% margin guidance; further USD-INR weakness or freight disruption would pressure margins.
Working capital: higher inventory from early paper purchases and Middle East collection delays; cash deployment on paper versus buyback.
Q1 EBITDA loss partly reflects marketing timing (Q2 costs in Q1), so the Q2 margin needs watching.
Content licensing must scale from about Rs14 crore to above Rs40 crore; contracts not yet signed.
Large goodwill on the balance sheet weighs on return ratios; no impairment or revaluation planned near term.
Buyback decision and acquisition progress, targeted for October 2026.
540497|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the core K-12 franchise and content licensing, but cautious on paper prices and working capital. Management was non-committal on the timing of the buyback and on content licensing contracts, and deflected goodwill questions.
key_quotes: We took a conscious decision to advance Paper purchases since we are pre -empting higher paper prices, supply disruptions and elongated shipping timelines for imported paper.
The steady state is again 10% to 12%, for the core business.

517035|2026-06.headline: RIR Power Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29.3% YoY to Rs 27.16 crore, EBITDA Rs 3.98 crore, with Odisha epi-wafer output targeted from Q3 FY27.
517035|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 27.16 crore (up 29.3% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 3.98 crore and EPS of 39 paisa. Margin improvement was attributed to passing on raw-material (copper, gold, silver) cost increases to customers, with about 80-85% pass-through, plus procurement and vendor negotiation gains. The Odisha epitaxy facility is nearing commissioning: power connection is nearly done, and epi operations are expected by end-Q2 FY27, with epi-wafer revenue from Q3. Bank loan of Rs 70 crore is at in-principle approval stage, with final sanction expected the following week.

financial_highlights.change: Margin improved vs Q4 FY26 per management; no exact YoY figure stated
Spent so far: ~Rs 58 crore govt subsidy plus ~Rs 70 crore company contribution; Rs 8-10 crore non-capex spend extra

segments.name: Halol facility (silicon power semiconductors: HPD, LPD, equipment)
segments.commentary: Management sees LPD at saturation; growth to come from HPD in India and new equipment-division products. Management aims to grow top line 3-4x FY26 this year; quarterly run-rate of Rs 30+ crore targeted during FY27 excluding Odisha.

segments.name: Odisha facility (SiC epi wafers)
segments.commentary: Epitaxy phase targets epi-wafer sales from Q3 FY27; FY27 second-half epi-wafer revenue target Rs 12-15 crore. Packaging (phase 2 first step) revenue expected from Q2 FY28. Two reactors can deliver 4-, 6- and 8-inch epi; 8-inch mainly for export, 4/6-inch for domestic.

guidance_outlook: Quarterly revenue of Rs 30+ crore achievable within FY27 (excluding Odisha); Rs 50 crore per quarter expected in 6-9 months, per management, though 'it may take some more time'.
Odisha epitaxy operations to commence by end-Q2 FY27; qualification expected to take ~30 days; official inauguration targeted September 2026.
Epi-wafer revenue from Odisha from Q3 FY27; FY27 second-half epi revenue target Rs 12-15 crore.
Management targets at least 3-4x FY26 top-line growth this year, and faster bottom-line growth.
Long-term EBITDA margin aim of 15-17%, but sustainability depends on geopolitical conditions; no firm commitment given.
Epi-wafer expected yield ~85%, with a goal above 90%.
capex_capacity: Odisha power supply via 33 kV line completed; transformer charged; plant and machinery installation expected to finish end-August or mid-September 2026.
Epitaxy clean room completed; two epi reactors installed.
Phase 2 (fabrication) capex of Rs 395-400 crore still under discussion; update expected in next couple of months.
Bank term loan application of Rs 70 crore; in-principle approval received, final sanction meeting pushed a week.

demand_pricing: Price increases taken in Q1; about 80-85% of input cost increase passed on to customers, with older accepted orders lagging. New schedules carry new prices.
Further value-addition price increases seen as difficult while West Asia disruption persists.
First overseas order: 120 units of 125 mm 5 kV SCR thyristors.
Epi-wafer prospects: international customers in US and Taiwan approached; Indian government labs also interested.
Richardson Electronics: ~20,000 SiC chips supplied, under customer review; no update from customer.

qa_highlights.question: Can the core business reach Rs 50 crore quarterly revenue excluding Odisha?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes so but said it may take time; Rs 30+ crore per quarter is achievable this year, with Rs 50 crore possibly in 6-9 months after supply chain and productivity work.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Odisha project status and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Power resolved and transformer charged; epi operations to begin in about 30 days after installation; inauguration targeted September 2026. Government subsidy of Rs 58 crore received to date; company has contributed an equal amount.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Odisha phase 1 capex funding gap and bank loan size?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 130 crore spent (Rs 70 crore company plus Rs 58 crore subsidy), leaving ~Rs 100 crore; application made for Rs 70 crore bank loan.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is sustainable and what drove Q1 margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gain came from price pass-through, procurement savings and redeployed staff; management aims for 15-17% but cannot confirm sustainability given geopolitical factors.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin does epi wafer carry?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected EBITDA 20-25% on epi-wafer sales; SiC devices expected to be higher margin than epi.

qa_highlights.question: What is R&D spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said 8-10% of revenue has been the long-term R&D spend norm; products in development include optically triggered thyristors (5 kV now, targeting 8 kV).

qa_highlights.question: Will RIR enter GaN?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said focus remains on SiC; sees SiC capturing power share of GaN market in about three years.

risks_watch: Bank loan final sanction (Rs 70 crore) expected next week; delay would stall phase 1 funding.
Odisha commissioning timeline: slippage from end-Q2 FY27 epi start and Q3 revenue.
Margin sustainability amid West Asia-driven input cost volatility; only 80-85% of cost increases passed through.
Phase 2 capex (Rs 395-400 crore) funding and timing not yet finalised.
Epi-wafer yield (target 85%, goal above 90%) and customer qualification in US, Taiwan and India.
Richardson Electronics SiC chip review outcome unknown.
Management declined to name products under development, citing competition; limited visibility on new product revenue.

509079|2026-06.headline: Gufic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR260.8 crore and PAT rose 86% to INR22.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 18.09%.
509079|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR260.8 crore versus INR226.9 crore a year earlier and INR252.1 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA rose to INR47.2 crore (18.09% margin) from INR33.2 crore (14.6%), and PAT reached INR22.46 crore (8.61% margin) versus INR12.1 crore. Management said Indore is running to plan, with capacity utilisation expected to reach 40-45% by year-end and the GLP-1 CMO ramp expected to build from Q2 and more in Q3. Management reiterated 15-20% annual growth as a minimum commitment, with EU and US certifications for Indore still pending.

financial_highlights.change: +15% YoY vs INR226.9 crore; +3% QoQ vs INR252.1 crore
+42% YoY vs INR33.2 crore; +6% QoQ vs INR44.7 crore
+349 bps YoY vs 14.6%; +35 bps QoQ vs 17.74%
+85% YoY vs INR16.3 crore; +9% QoQ vs INR27.6 crore
+86% YoY vs INR12.1 crore; +9% QoQ vs INR20.6 crore

segments.name: Critical Care
segments.commentary: Launched monobactam and beta-lactamase inhibitor combination on innovator patent expiry; Sparsh completed a full quarter on the rebuilt channel with outstanding days within trade terms. Focus is on own-manufactured brands and depth within existing hospital groups.

segments.name: Women's health / IVF (Puregraf, Ferticare, Zenova)
segments.commentary: Ferticare retains leadership in recurrent implantation failure; Puregraf entered major corporate IVF chains. Zenova is shifting from injectables to prescription chronic therapies, with two first-mover launches (osteoarthritis, metabolic ovarian) due ahead.

segments.name: Aesthetics (botulinum toxin and fillers)
segments.commentary: Claims to be number 2 in toxin type A in India, made from its own strain. Filler partnership with Revanesse (Prollenium, Canada) expected to launch in India around December-January, subject to registration in Q2 or mid-Q3.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Shifted to a model that earns fee income alongside supply revenue. Licensing progressed in Europe, a contract manufacturing and licensing arrangement was signed with a North American partner, and first CMO orders were received in Australia. Approvals were secured in 8 countries in the quarter.

segments.name: GLP-1 (semaglutide, via Hetero)
segments.commentary: Operates purely as a CMO for Hetero, which received permission in May 2026; Q1 revenue contribution was residual. A 10-15 day plant shutdown in Q1 was for a new machine. Management expects traction from Q2 and the main contribution in Q3, with 70% of capacity targeted for international use.

guidance_outlook: Management commits to 15-20% year-on-year company growth as a bare minimum, with efforts aimed at growing beyond that.
Indore capacity utilisation expected to rise from about 30-35% now to around 40-45% by year-end, with the Indore liquid line targeted at about 80% utilisation within three years.
Margin expansion from Indore expected once EU certification is in place. Management says the 18% operating margin is the start of an improvement trend, not a new normal.
Management expects operating leverage to start around mid-FY28.

Indore revenue potential is INR800-1,200 crore from current capex (about INR300 crore), so combined with Navsari the maximum is about INR1,600-2,000 crore; management also cited INR1,600-1,800 crore with no further capex.
Botulinum toxin and biostimulator in-licensed products are to launch this financial year with no significant capex. Stunnox and Zarbot registrations in SE Asia and Africa take 12-18 months.
capex_capacity: Indore has about 6 lyophilisers (4 at 100,000-vial capacity and 2 at 44,000-vial capacity). Depot and liposomal lines are in installation and qualification, with both targeted to be operational this year.
Indore has four lines: two lyophilisation lines, one suspension/liquid vial line, and one ampoule line. Target mix is roughly 20% liquid, 50-60% lyophilisation, and 20-30% complex injectables.
Indore is fully operational as a unit; new product lines are being added within the existing capex of about INR300 crore, with no major new infrastructure.
Indore utilisation has risen from 18-22% last year, to 20-25%, to close to 30-35% this year.
Navsari is largely capped at about INR800 crore revenue, with toxin and penem blocks not yet saturated.
Toxin plant is WHO Phase 1 with limited capacity; global registrations are deferred until after next year pending cash flow.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per vial is about INR80-100 on current product mix (pantoprazole 10 ml vial at about INR60-80). Management aims to move to INR300-400 and eventually an average of INR500 per vial with depot, liposomal and complex injectables.
Fillers market in India is estimated at about INR200 crore. Management aims to move from number 2 to number 1 in toxin plus fillers within 3-5 years.

International: aims to raise margins from 40-50% under distributor models to 15-20% higher with its own field force in Africa, Southeast Asia and South Asia. Recruitment of a regional team happened in Q1.
CHAI partnership for liposomal amphotericin B gives access to more than 100 markets; bioequivalence study due by August-September, followed by WHO PQ filing.

Employee additions are mainly at Indore (around 50-60 for domestic expansion), with international headcount capped at 20-25. Management says the previous-year contract-to-payroll conversion was one-time.

530655|2026-06.headline: Goodluck India Q1 FY27 standalone revenue up ~23% to INR1,205.9 cr, EBITDA up 15% to INR110.5 cr; Defence expansion delayed 6-9 months.
530655|2026-06.overview: Standalone income from operations rose to INR1,205.94 crore from INR983.29 crore YoY, while standalone EBITDA rose 15% to INR110.53 crore and PAT rose to INR49.66 crore from INR40.14 crore. Management cited 31% consolidated revenue growth, 46% consolidated EBITDA growth and 67% consolidated PAT growth, with EBITDA margin above 10%. Defence (Goodluck Defence & Aerospace) won orders of INR255 crore and INR52 crore for 155 mm shells, but its capacity expansion has slipped 6-9 months due to financial closure. A preferential issue at the Defence subsidiary (about 75 lakh shares at INR375, about INR285 crore) drew heavy shareholder criticism over valuation and the choice over a rights issue at parent level.

vs INR40.14 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR80 crore at about 38% EBITDA margin

segments.name: Defence (Goodluck Defence & Aerospace)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR80 crore at about 38% EBITDA margin. Orders of INR255 crore (about 50,000 shells of 155 mm long-range RTF empty shells, 10-month execution) and INR52 crore (20,000 shells, 3-month execution). DGQA certificate received for 107 RTF artillery shells.

segments.name: Precision tubes / auto tubes
segments.commentary: Management cited EBITDA margin of 12-13%. Hydraulic tube utilisation rose to 60-65% in Q1 from about 50%.

segments.name: Pipes and CR sheet
segments.commentary: Management cited EBITDA margin of 3-5%.

segments.name: Solar structures
segments.commentary: Management cited EBITDA margin of 7-8%.

segments.commentary: Management cited EBITDA margin of 10-11%. Transmission tower capacity about 50,000 tons per year.

segments.name: Forging
segments.commentary: Management cited EBITDA margin of 12-13%.

Defence FY27 revenue target INR300-350 crore at 30-35% EBITDA margin; management reiterated 30-35% margin range, saying it is conservative.
Defence expansion (250,000 shells capacity) delayed 6-9 months; management hopes expansion starts by Q4 FY27, with commercialisation about one year later (around Q4 FY28).
Post-expansion Defence plant capacity 400,000 shells, achievable about 350,000 shells per annum.

Value-added products about 60% of business; GI tube and front fork tube capacity expected in about 6 months; 40,000-45,000 metric tons of capacity addition announced for FY27 (large-diameter pipe ramp delayed by West Asia crisis).
capex_capacity: Defence shell capacity currently 150,000 shells per annum; expansion (plant capacity 400,000) delayed 6-9 months due to financial closure.
Defence capex about INR400 crore; standalone capex INR100-150 crore.
Hydraulic tube capacity utilisation 60-65% in Q1 (about 50% earlier).
Standalone capacity utilisation annualised at 98%.
Plans for aerospace rolling mill to supply outer bodies for space rockets and an aerospace supplier ecosystem; Goodluck Astra land allotted, licence applied for.
Large-diameter pipe and precision tube capacity additions (40,000-45,000 MT) ramping slower due to West Asia crisis.
demand_pricing: Standalone volume 1,22,718 MT, up 8.8% YoY.

Input cost risk high due to petroleum-linked inputs and logistics costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Defence subsidiary being listed separately rather than demerged, and how does that create value for current shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said financial advisers recommended a separate listing; the listing will be based on future numbers. Parent shareholders benefit as a subsidiary's value accrues to the group.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the subsidiary stake sold through a preferential issue instead of a rights issue at Goodluck India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said financial advisers preferred this route and that the company needs funds for growth. Management acknowledged a differing view and said it would consider feedback.

qa_highlights.question: What is the subsidiary's implied valuation from the INR285 crore issue at INR375/share?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-issue outstanding shares about 4.91 crore; post-issue about 5.66 crore shares (about 75 lakh new shares). Implied valuation not explicitly stated; dilution cited as about 10.5% (an investor said 15%).

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Defence expansion slipped and when will it start?
qa_highlights.answer: Delay is due to financial closure of the project and approvals; expansion now expected to start by Q4 FY27, with commercialisation around a year later.

qa_highlights.question: What are Defence margins and revenue in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Defence revenue about INR80 crore at about 38% EBITDA; management is guiding 30-35% sustainable margin, stating it is conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company maintaining its FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained 15-20% revenue growth guidance; volume up 9% in Q1 and expected to improve if geopolitical conditions ease.

532834|2026-06.headline: Camlin Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR5,199 million, but EBITDA margin collapsed to about 4% from 45% last quarter on raw material costs and vanillin under-utilisation.
532834|2026-06.overview:
Revenue reached INR5,199 million, up about 28% YoY and about INR1,000 million QoQ, but margins fell sharply on raw material, freight and logistics costs tied to the West Asia conflict. The company reorganised reporting into Specialty Ingredients, Aroma and Performance Chemicals, with Aroma and Performance Chemicals both EBITDA-negative or near zero in the quarter. Ethyl vanillin ramp-up ran at low utilisation, and FY27 vanillin volume guidance was cut to about 3,000 tons from 3,600-4,000 tons. Management cut FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 10-12% while keeping revenue guidance, and debt was flat at about INR640 crore gross.</overview>

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients (blends and straights)
segments.commentary: Revenue above INR4,000 million with blends above INR3,000 million; EBITDA margin 6.35%. Management says about 4-5% of gross margin was lost to raw material costs and Brazil air-freight, with Brazil's shortfall of about INR8 crore expected to correct in Q2.
