segments.commentary: Sold about 560 tons (350 t ethyl, 200 t methyl from channel stock) against 6,000-ton capacity; produced ~400 tons. Quarterly EBITDA negative at INR4-4.5 crore on fixed cost absorption; management expects positive EBITDA in Q2.

segments.name: Performance Chemicals
segments.commentary: Gross segment revenue about INR175 crore, of which ~INR130 crore is internal transfer, leaving ~INR40 crore external sales. EBITDA margin 2.5% with diphenol plant shut; management expects positive EBITDA from Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance: INR2,200-2,300 crore, versus earlier INR2,000-2,400 crore; management says top line is secure.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance cut to 10-12% (10-11% per CFO/MD), implying about INR220-230 crore EBITDA, versus earlier INR250-280 crore.
Analyst read-back: average run rate of about INR70 crore EBITDA per quarter for remaining quarters; management did not dispute this.
Q3 FY27 expected to return to double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin; H2 margin of 13-15% floated by an analyst, not disputed.
FY28 EBITDA margin in the range of 12-14%.
Vanillin FY27 volume about 3,000 tons (earlier 3,600-4,000); 4 campaigns planned, Q2 volume 500-600 tons, Q3 1,000+ tons. Capacity 6,000 tons, achievable 5,000 tons with 3 campaigns.
Blends growth of at least 20% in FY27; budget assumes 25-30%.
capex_capacity: Vanillin capacity 6,000 tons per year; ethyl vanillin campaign of about 750 tons ran through mid-August, with about 350 tons sold and over 300 tons produced; methyl vanillin campaign to follow after roughly two weeks of changeover.
Diphenol plant shut because phenol and raw material prices are high; hydroquinone secured from China for the next two quarters; decision on alternate use or restart by Q3 FY27.
Working capital cycle about 100 days on a consolidated basis; each INR1 crore of revenue growth needs about one-third as working capital support.
CFS Europe in liquidation with no further cash burn beyond legal costs; China subsidiary liquidation expected to cost INR10-20 million in Q1.
demand_pricing: Channel stocks in the US and China described as cleared; management sees demand picking up and is negotiating quarterly, half-yearly and annual contracts with F&F customers.
US and Europe ethyl vanillin realisations stated at about $13-14/kg; methyl vanillin raw material cost $7-8/kg, with conversion cost about INR7 crore/month fixed.
Management sees a supply gap of about 5,000-6,000 tons in US and Europe that must be imported; Syensqo (Solvay) is the market leader; Chinese imports priced around $15 against Solvay's $18.
Pass-through of raw material increases to blends customers is lagging by one quarter; management expects to recover about half of the cost increase in Q2.
Trade financing (dealer finance) on purchase and sales sides costs an estimated 1-1.5% and is hitting gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 EBITDA guidance achievable given Q1 EBITDA of about INR9 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management restated guidance as INR2,200-2,300 crore revenue with 10-11% margin, which it said is within reach on the current cost structure; it expects about 10% margin over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Aroma EBITDA negative and what is its normalised economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said low utilisation (about 400 tons produced vs 1,500-ton quarterly capacity) left fixed cost unabsorbed. Management said 70-80% utilisation would make the business profitable and gave about 7% EBITDA at $13/kg on 3,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt reduction and what external funding is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is INR640 crore, down from INR670 crore on 31 March. The CFO said INR100-200 crore of working capital lines are expected within 1-1.5 months, and equity or other capital is being considered without a decision yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 vanillin volume cut from 3,600-4,000 tons to about 3,000?
qa_highlights.answer: The ethyl vanillin ramp-up was slower to secure quality, with 95% customer approval. Each campaign switch costs about a month, and four campaigns are planned this year.

qa_highlights.question: What would Q1 EBITDA have been under normal conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4-5% of gross margin was lost, which would have lifted EBITDA to roughly INR37-40 crore, an analyst's figure that management confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Will raw material cost pressure persist into Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects elevated raw material prices to persist through Q2 and guidance assumes about three months of elevated costs, not six or nine months.

500043|2026-06.headline: Bata India Q1 FY27 turnover rose about 4% to INR979 crore, with underlying PBT up about 22% and gross margin up 130 bps.

Cost push of 5-6% expected to be offset by price increases; management expects no margin dilution from cost push in subsequent quarters.
Price-hiked stock expected to reach markets at scale around September 2026.
Product funnel reimagination expected to show more impact in H2 FY27 and H1 FY28; significant portfolio change by March 2027.
Gross margin levers cited: premiumisation and higher full-price sales; channel mix (franchise/e-commerce growth) a partial offset.

Vendor consolidation: from about 100-120 partners 2.5-3 years ago to below 70 (about 60) now; target of 15 core plus 15 satellite partners over 3-5 years, with total margin benefit about 200 bps over that period.
Elevated marketing spend expected to continue for the next couple of years; ZBM 2.0 (Project Elevate) results to be shared next quarter.
capex_capacity: Store network: about 2,000 EBO stores crossed, of which about 1,250 COCO/DOS (incl. about 125 Hush Puppies DOS) and about 750 franchise; management aspires to 3,000 stores over time.
Franchise potential trade areas identified: in excess of 600.
Store clutter: average lines per store at 68% of level two years ago; management sees the optimal level near 60%.
Stock turns at about 2.5+, moving towards 2.7; inventory held at about 140-150 days.
Franchise partner ROI cited at 18-24%.
demand_pricing: Lower price points showing some resurgence after GST rationalisation about three quarters ago; premium segment still growing faster and ASP has risen.
Raw material cost push of about 5-6%, mainly imported synthetics (crude derivatives); similar price increases taken on new and existing products.
Competitive intensity at lower price points too early to call; management believes many peers have not yet absorbed full raw material inflation.
Franchise like-for-like growth close to high single digits for about the last four quarters.
Full-price sales near 89-90% with markdowns falling.

qa_highlights.question: What cost inflation was faced and how is it being mitigated?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost push of about 5-6% from synthetics; not yet visible in Q1 because of 140-150 days of inventory. Price increases taken; margin dilution not expected in subsequent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin not expand more despite higher full-price sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel mix (franchise and e-commerce growing faster) diluted gross margin by about 100 bps. Without it, gross margin expansion would have been about 230 bps versus 130 bps reported; EBIT per pair is the benchmark.

qa_highlights.question: How many COCO stores, and what is the ZBM contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1,250 COCO/DOS and about 750 franchise stores. About 775 ZBM stores generate about 80% of COCO retail revenue; management sees ZBM near saturation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost flat for five quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: VRS was part of the business case; a 24-month organisational restructuring, Blue Yonder merchandising platform and manpower reallocation drove savings. Store manpower broadly unchanged; franchise growth required added manpower.

qa_highlights.question: Franchise store economics and SSG?
qa_highlights.answer: Franchise like-for-like growth close to high single digits for about four quarters. Partner ROI about 18-24%. Revenue per sq ft not disclosed on the call.

qa_highlights.question: A&P trajectory and timing of revenue payback?

risks_watch: Pass-through of 5-6% cost push: price-hiked stock reaches markets around September; watch realisations and volumes in Q2.
Lower price-point competition and consumer pushback as peers absorb raw material inflation.
Gross margin dilution from faster franchise and e-commerce growth offsetting premiumisation and full-price gains.
NorthStar sneakers drag until the rationalised collection arrives over the next couple of quarters.
Rising A&P (about 3-3.5% of sales) must translate into double-digit top-line growth; timeline unspecified.
Store clutter reduction (target about 60% of lines per store) must not hurt conversion.
Senior management transition: a participant wished Gunjan Shah well for future endeavours, implying a possible CEO change; not confirmed on the call.
500043|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on operating levers (full-price sales, inventory, ZBM, franchise, cost restructuring) but cautious on near-term top-line and inflation pass-through, repeatedly declining numeric guidance and deferring to 'wait and watch'. Gross margin and revenue targets were answered qualitatively.
key_quotes: We are reasonably confident that we should be able to neutralise it, but I'll let Amit expand a little more on it.
So broadly, the cost push what we have witnessed is in the range of about 5% to 6%.
So we do see already some signs of it already coming through into the stores with some reasonably good success, so early signs of success on it.
Not so much on stores. Store manpower has actually not changed much.

500575|2026-06.headline: Voltas Q1 FY27 net profit rose to Rs 213 crore (Rs 141 crore) on revenue of Rs 4,765 crore, with RAC market share at 17.3%.
500575|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated income grew to Rs 4,765 crore from Rs 4,021 crore, with PBT of Rs 285 crore versus Rs 203 crore. Segment A (unitary cooling) grew 33%, with RAC volumes up 45% and secondary market share at 17.3% against 15.9% for FY26, widening the lead over the nearest competitor to 4 percentage points. Commodity inflation, rupee depreciation and freight costs were largely passed on (10-12% cost increase, near full pass-through), and UCP EBIT margin improved to 5.3% from 3.7%. Projects (Segment B) was soft on execution issues and delayed new orders in the Middle East, while Commercial Refrigeration and Air Coolers were muted. Management also signed a binding term sheet for a 50-50 compressor JV with Atomberg.</overview>

Channel cautious on stock; July-August demand not yet clear, festive season view too early.

qa_highlights.question: Compressor JV: capacity, capex, timeline and split among the three entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity about 2.8 million compressors; total capex still early-stage. Commercial production about 18 months away; the JV was driven by supply security and QCO import limits.

qa_highlights.question: Voltbek EBITDA breakeven timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier target for this year; West Asia-driven commodity spike meant brands could not pass through all costs, so breakeven may slip by a few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How do QCO norms get met until the JV is operational?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports allowed up to 30% based on FY25 volumes; continued purchases from Highly and GMCC (India capacity blocked), blending with own supply later.

qa_highlights.question: Why UCP margins are 5% in a strong quarter, and what is steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peers saw EBIT fall 3-4 pts; Voltas improved YoY on scale, no factory disruption, cost absorption and cost-out. Aspiration of 7%+ over the next ~8 quarters; CFO said margins vary quarter to quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Calibrated order booking to avoid fixed-price contracts without escalation clauses; shifting to shorter-gestation private, data-centre and MEP jobs.

qa_highlights.question: Channel inventory and July-August demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel cautious; inventory around 4 weeks; too early to judge festive season, with a 4-6 week monitoring window.

qa_highlights.question: Voltbek loss in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Share of JV loss booked at Rs 37 crore; EMP margins to improve in Q3-Q4 after a soft Q2.

590003|2026-09.headline: KVB Q2 FY27: net profit INR788 crores (+37% YoY), NIM held at 4.26%, credit cost 0.43%, and advances growth guided to 18-20% for FY27.
590003|2026-09.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported a strong Q2 FY27 with net profit of INR788 crores, up 4% QoQ and 37% YoY, and operating profit of INR1,162 crores (+14% YoY, +6% QoQ). Total business reached INR2,39,712 crores (+5% QoQ, +18% YoY), with advances up 7% QoQ to INR1,11,589 crores and deposits up 5% QoQ to INR1,28,123 crores. Management guided to 18-20% credit growth, NIM of 4% plus, ROA of about 2% and GNPA below 1.5% for FY27, while flagging that funding costs and loan-yield competition may pressure margins in coming quarters. financial_highlights.change: +INR1 crore QoQ; AS-15 provisions lower by INR28 crores

segments.commentary: Agri loans grew 4% QoQ; agri jewel loans are 92% of the agri book.

ROA for FY27 guided at about 2%, with 2.1% reported for Q2.
GNPA guided below 1.5%, NNPA below 1%, slippages below 1%; cost-to-income expected below 45% over the next 2 quarters.

514448|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY (about 10% volume, 7% price) while EBITDA margin fell to about 14.4% on raw material spike.
514448|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 17% YoY in Q1 FY27, with roughly 10% from volumes and about 7% from price increases taken in April and mid-May. EBITDA margin compressed to about 14.4%, which management attributed to 6-7 percentage points of raw material cost inflation (VAM spike linked to West Asia tensions) plus about 3-4 points of aggressive dealer-meet and sales promotion spend. Management guided back to a 22-25% EBITDA range longer term and said it is too early to commit to 28-29% in Q2. Working capital weakened, with receivables around INR 145-150 crore (debtor days above 150) and inventory higher, and management targets 120 days over the next two to three quarters.

financial_highlights.change: Management estimate; declined to call it revenue loss
Over and above shipments made until the call date; about 70% domestic, 30% export

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Export dispatches slowed as container costs rose three to five times for some geographies versus pre-crisis levels; management says customers are buying only minimum volumes, not cancelling. Export is about 90% of export orders on an ex-works basis per management, and the order book is about 30% export.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic dispatches were slowed by negotiations to pass on raw material price escalation on existing orders, with April and May the worst months and conditions easing since. Management says domestic market is normal versus last year and no lower-margin pressure in lower KV classes; order book is about 70% domestic.

guidance_outlook: FY27 annual outlook unchanged; management says it is on track for the top-line target and expects no problem achieving it, though geographic mix may shift if West Asia persists.
Q2 FY27 business momentum expected to be notably better than Q1; domestic visibility better, exports may stay impacted by shipping costs.
Existing 7,500 MVA capacity to run at near full utilisation in FY27; management targets close to 100% utilisation for FY27.
EBITDA: management does not expect problems achieving EBITDA as Q2 orders are at current raw material prices; expects Q2 EBITDA higher than Q1 but gave no margin percentage.

Phase-3 expansion (about 6,500 MVA) on track for commissioning in April 2027; new facility to drive growth from FY28; bigger-KV transformer orders expected later due to customer audits, approvals and type testing.
Margin normalisation depends on exports returning; if domestic-heavy mix persists, margins could dip slightly. New capacity to carry lower initial margins to build references.
capex_capacity: Phase-3 expansion adds about 6,500 MVA; commissioning targeted April 2027, possibly slightly earlier than projected.
Civil foundation work complete; PEB erection and utility work progressing; all equipment ordered.
Additional about 4.5 acres of land bought adjacent to existing Gavasad site for future expansion; product and KV class not yet disclosed.
Prototyping for larger transformers takes about 3-4 months after production starts; discussions under way with a few customers on bigger units.
Company will not supply state utility companies; plans to focus on exports once domestic references are established.
demand_pricing: Management says underlying demand in both export and domestic markets remains firm; customers are buying minimum volumes due to freight costs and uncertainty.
Export orders being deferred, not cancelled; management says delivery dates pushed by about 1-2 months (e.g., June to July or August).
Only 50-60% of raw material price rise passed on to customers for orders in hand from Q4 and Q1; current orders priced at current market prices.
Lead time for custom transformers is about 10-16 weeks; management says customers prefer Shilchar on quality, service and shorter lead time.
Management says competition is not the issue for exports: customers are not buying from rivals, just holding purchases.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify Q1 revenue loss from shipment delays and whether FY27 Rs 800 crore guidance is being revisited.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to call it a loss but said Rs 30-35 crore could have been done without the crisis; it reiterated FY27 top-line target with no anticipated problem.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material cost increase was passed to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50-60% of the price rise was passed on for orders from Q4 and Q1; current execution is at market prices so EBITDA is not expected to be a problem.

qa_highlights.question: Order book size and domestic/export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book close to Rs 500 crore over and above shipments to date; about 70% domestic and 30% export; mostly for Q2, Q3 and some Q4, with Q2 fully booked.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins stay near 30% EBITDA, and will the 220 KV expansion be lower margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins can match prior years if exports recover; otherwise a slight dip. New 220 KV-class capacity will carry lower initial margins to build references, with better margins later.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 export focus not shifted to domestic earlier, leaving capacity underused?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shipping was normal in April but costs spiked from late April/May; it shifted focus to domestic promptly, but custom orders take time to win and execute, benefits showing in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Q1 capacity utilisation and export/domestic revenue split and receivable/inventory days?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 utilisation was about 60-65%; export/domestic revenue split and inventory and receivable days were not disclosed on the call and will be sent by email.

risks_watch: Persistent West Asia conflict keeping container costs elevated (three to five times pre-crisis for some routes) and delaying export orders.
Q1 EBITDA margin (about 21.7% implied) well below the roughly 30% historically cited; Q2 margin recovery depends on domestic price pass-through and mix.
Phase-3 commissioning slippage in April 2027, and ramp-up of larger KV transformers which need customer approval and type testing.
Management's earlier outlook in the FY26 annual report (prepared early June) assumed normalisation that did not happen; credibility of outlook is a watch item.
Export revenue permanence: management says orders are deferred, not lost, but this is unverified; monitor Q2 export dispatches and order book conversion.
531201|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on medium-term demand and FY27 targets, but cautious and at times evasive on specifics: declined to quantify margins, the export/domestic split for revenue, and inventory/receivable days, and repeatedly referred the latter to email. The tone shifted from the prior view that Middle East normalisation would come quickly.

544248|2026-06.headline: Mach Travel Q1 FY27 revenue rose 538% YoY to INR144.33 crore, with EBITDA margin compressing to 6.09% from 7.17%.
544248|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR144.33 crore versus INR22.62 crore a year ago and INR83.25 crore in Q4 FY26, with GMV of about INR252 crore disclosed for the first time. EBITDA rose to INR8.92 crore and PAT to INR6.17 crore, but margins were lower YoY, which management attributed to investment in new verticals, hiring and technology. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR500-plus crore and said it is working on bank overdraft lines because of working capital pressure from payment cycles. Much of the quarter's growth came from a few large government and MICE programmes, and several answers were vague or deferred.

financial_highlights.change: +538% YoY vs INR22.62 crore; +73% QoQ vs INR83.25 crore
+437% YoY vs INR1.66 crore; QoQ up from INR3.81 crore
+307% YoY vs INR1.52 crore; QoQ up from INR1.8 crore
Management described company as debt free

segments.name: MICE (core)
segments.commentary: Management estimated MICE at about INR100 crore of Q1 revenue in one answer, then said INR50-60 crore in another, so the split is unclear. Oceania programmes worth about INR32 crore were completed, covering 950-1,000 delegates.

segments.name: Corporate travel
segments.commentary: Launched in April 2026 with more than 100 corporate clients signed; management put it at about 10-15% of revenue. Billing cycles run 1st-15th payable on the 20th and 16th-30th payable on the 6th-7th of the next month.

segments.name: Government and institutional (Punjab Yatra)
segments.commentary: Punjab Yatra contract worth about INR92 crore covering 1.85 lakh yatris, at about INR4,950 per person for a 2-night, 3-day trip. Management said about 15% of Q1 revenue came from it; about 1.15 lakh travelled to date and the contract runs to about November.

segments.name: IRCTC
segments.commentary: Empanelled as one of four or five A-listed vendors, with a first order of about INR75 lakh to INR1 crore. Empanelment term was stated as two years, extendable, but the executive director was not certain.

segments.name: B2B and B2C OTA / leisure
segments.commentary: B2B tool lets smaller travel agents book tickets. B2C app Machtravel.com is in testing and its launch was pushed from late August to September 2026. Leisure was described as doing very well, with no figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of around INR500-plus crore, reiterated and described as an average-based figure; management expects to surpass it.
Management said quarter-on-quarter growth will not be substantial because October-December is a festival and Christmas lull for corporate travel; Q2 is seasonally heavier than Q1 overall.
Management would not commit to a date for EBITDA margins returning to the roughly 10% level mentioned by an analyst, and would not say margins will be under pressure in Q2.
Markups may be compressed in aggressive pursuit of business, but management said the company will not burn money.
Next milestones named: INR500 crore, then INR1,000 crore revenue, B2C app launch in September, a possible main board move within 12 months, and new southern offices.
capex_capacity: Operating presence expanded to Noida, New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Bhubaneshwar and Ahmedabad; more southern offices planned.
Investment in technology, talent and offices over the past year is cited as the cause of lower margins; no quantified capex figure was given.
Corporate self-booking tool (SBT) covers booking, approval, ticketing, invoicing and reporting; management said it uses the same technology as large players.
Captive audience of about 1.25 lakh travellers a year is to be moved onto the B2C portal and app.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the growth to the transition beyond MICE into corporate, B2B, leisure, government and B2C, and said the policies were implemented from 1 April 2026.
TTV (total ticketed volume) was about INR259-260 crore versus about INR143 crore in revenue; the call did not reconcile TTV with GMV of INR252 crore.
Management said pricing on the B2C app is at par with large B2C players.
Punjab Yatra daily flows are about 1,100 travellers out and 1,100 back, with about 3,300-3,500 people handled at any one time.
Management said it is not clear whether the Punjab yatra will be repeated; three other Punjab yatra programmes were not won. Management is in talks with other state governments.

qa_highlights.question: How did revenue grow from INR22 crore to INR140-plus crore, and what steps were taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company spent about 1.5 years building new teams and technology and implemented the policies from April 2026. Revenue now comes from MICE, corporate, leisure, government and B2B; TTV was about INR259-260 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be managed to support growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is debt free with about INR3 crore of debt, but payment-cycle issues have created a working capital need. It is working toward bank overdraft facilities and will update the market if availed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between core MICE and the new verticals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was unsure of the exact split. It said about INR50-60 crore came from MICE in one answer and about INR100 crore in another, with corporate at 10-15% and the Punjab Yatra at about 15%.

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margins recover to about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no firm date. It said margins will improve as business scales, buying power rises and markups increase, but that it will be aggressive in the market and may give up some markup.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR500 crore guidance conservative given Q1 was about 29-30% of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is an annual average and cited seasonality. It said it hopes to surpass INR500 crore, but expects no substantial quarter-on-quarter growth in Q2 and Q3 because of festival periods.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Punjab Yatra contract repeatable, and how is it paid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the contract is for 1.85 lakh yatris at about INR4,950 per person and runs to about November. Payment is about 7 days after travel, roughly 15 days in total. It was unsure whether the programme would be repeated.

544396|2026-06.headline: NPST Q1 FY27 revenue about INR 61.42 crore, roughly 75% YoY but down QoQ; management reiterates 60-70% FY27 growth and ~30% EBITDA margin guidance.
544396|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of about INR 61.42 crore, up about 75% YoY, with EBITDA up 66% and net profit of about INR 11.4 crore. Revenue fell sequentially from the record INR 68 crore in Q4 FY26, which management attributed to milestone-based recognition in a shifted business mix, with PPaaS cut to about 5% of projections. Management held FY27 guidance of 60-70% growth and around 30% EBITDA margin, and flagged MDR on UPI as a possible future revenue driver that is not yet quantified. International revenue is about 10-12% of consolidated revenue, and management targets around 50% over about two years.

financial_highlights.change: about +75% YoY; down QoQ vs ~INR 68 crore in Q4 FY26 (analyst-cited, not disputed)
Grew 66% YoY per management; analyst noted EBITDA margin declined QoQ
Management stated increase; exact YoY figure garbled in transcript

financial_highlights.value: About 17-18% (analyst's figure, not confirmed by management)
About INR 19 crore (analyst read) vs ~INR 2 crore last year
financial_highlights.change: Management said purchase cost was grouped into this line; other expenses are about INR 2 crore only

financial_highlights.metric: Changes in inventories / stock in trade
financial_highlights.value: About INR 17 crore vs ~INR 2 crore prior-year quarter
financial_highlights.change: Hardware for turnkey projects, recognised on milestones

segments.name: Domestic TSP / banking
segments.commentary: Remains the largest contributor; management expects its share to decline as other businesses grow faster, while still growing in absolute terms.

segments.name: PPaaS (payment platform as a service)
segments.commentary: Projection cut to about 5% of revenue from about 90% earlier, to reduce risk; management says MDR on UPI could revive it.

segments.name: RegTech / AI risk intelligence
segments.commentary: Order from a large PSU picked up; cooperative-bank deals won; SaaS subscription planned for mid and small banks. Management says about 650 million transactions processed on the product at 98% accuracy.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue now coming in; first global account won in Q1; one telecom super-app order in hand and two more deals in pipeline. Management expects margins above 35% vs 15-20% domestic.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 60-70% YoY reiterated; management indicated about INR 320-340 crore for the year, which analyst Preet Shah stated and management called 'around that'.
FY27 EBITDA margin of around 30% reiterated; management says Q1 and Q2 orders should lift the blended margin later in the year.
Management targets 60-70% annual growth CAGR for the next 2-3 years, implying about INR 850-900 crore revenue by FY29 (per analyst calculation; management said 'tentatively yes').
International share targeted at about 30% in FY28-29 per Ashish Aggarwal and around 50% or more in about two years per Deepak Thakur; EBITDA margin target of at least 35% in about two years.
IPO funds: management expects deployment to start within the next two quarters, mainly product development and three shortlisted opportunities (RegTech, AI solutions, payment infrastructure).
Management said growth will come on a yearly basis and sequential revenue will be milestone-driven; no quarterly phasing given.
capex_capacity: Implementation cycle for international orders runs about 4 to 9 months; full project tenure 4-5 years or longer, with margins rising as milestones complete.
Investments in product, global business development, AI, SaaS infrastructure and skill revival are being made and are expensed, weighing on current margins.
Management says it is moving to an AI-driven organisation, targeting about 30% efficiency gain (per investor presentation); employee cost growth lagged revenue growth.
No specific capacity or capex figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: UPI MDR: Parliament reportedly approved MDR on UPI; management says benefits are expected but no regulator, NPCI or bank guidance has been issued, so no numbers are being given. Management expects direct revenue from acquiring-platform contracts and indirect benefit via TSP spend.
Management said MDR on high-ticket UPI transactions (about 4-6% of volume, mostly large merchants) would be far below card MDR, so merchant shift to UPI is expected; no quantified impact.
Competition: established RegTech products (EFRM, EWS) face competition; management says its AI risk-intelligence product has no direct competitor yet.
Domestic margin 15-20% vs international 30-40%, as stated by management.
Acquisitions: priority is geographic access, product gaps and growth; no timeline (Q2 'early'). Management said growth is not inorganic.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue fell QoQ in Q1 versus 15-20% QoQ growth guidance; is FY27 guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-70% annual growth is unchanged; PPaaS cut to about 5% and milestone timing makes quarterly numbers lumpy; Q4 FY26 at about INR 68 crore is the peak to beat.

qa_highlights.question: How will MDR on UPI benefit the company, directly or indirectly?
qa_highlights.answer: Two routes: indirect (more bank and PSP money for TSP upgrades) and direct (per-transaction revenue on acquiring platforms it deployed). No numbers given until regulator, NPCI or bank guidance is out.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst estimate of MDR quantum (about INR 90,000 crore on 5% of volume at 0.25%).
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quote a number, saying MDR has acquiring, interchange and switching components, and the revenue stack is not yet clear.

qa_highlights.question: International orders, margin and mix target?
qa_highlights.answer: International is 10-12% of revenue; target about 30% in FY28-29 and about 50% in two years; margin 30-40% vs 15-20% domestic. Three first orders, one from a PSP, others from other segments.

qa_highlights.question: Deployment of IPO funds (about 10-15% used).
qa_highlights.answer: Three opportunities identified (RegTech, AI solutions, payment infrastructure); deployment expected to start in the next two quarters, mostly product development.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise to about INR 19 crore while employee cost stayed flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said purchase cost was grouped into other expenses, so the real other-expense line is about INR 2 crore; employee cost is less tied to revenue due to AI adoption.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 60-70% growth CAGR inclusive of inorganic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not inorganic.

risks_watch: Lumpy, milestone-based revenue makes QoQ comparisons weak; Q1 was below Q4 FY26's INR 68 crore peak.
FY27 guidance needs about INR 260-280 crore over the remaining three quarters (analyst math), an average of about INR 90 crore a quarter versus INR 61 crore in Q1.
MDR on UPI is unquantified and depends on regulator, NPCI and bank directions; management says no numbers should be relied on.
Slow IPO fund deployment (about 10-15% used after about 8 months).
International ramp depends on 4-9 month implementation cycles; only one order in hand.
Opaque P&L grouping (purchase cost in other expenses) limits margin analysis; management reclassified the line.

544425|2026-06.headline: AJC Jewel Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 124.69% YoY to Rs 101.38 crore; EBITDA margin 4.58% and PAT margin 2.35%.
544425|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue reached Rs 101.38 crore versus Rs 45.12 crore in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA of Rs 4.64 crore (from Rs 1.58 crore) and PAT of Rs 2.38 crore (from Rs 0.57 crore). Margins expanded, with EBITDA margin at 4.58% (from 3.5%) and PAT margin at 2.35% (from 1.26%). Management announced a proposed 80% stake acquisition in AJC Jewel Manufacturers FZC, Sharjah, via a non-cash share swap valued at up to Rs 9.6 crore, though the Sharjah entity is not consolidated in Q1. Management guided FY27 standalone India revenue of Rs 450 crore and 50% CAGR for three years, on a volume basis. Many answers on utilisation, Esthara economics and FY28 targets were deferred to H1 results.</overview>

segments.name: India gold jewellery (core B2B, casting)
segments.commentary: Capacity 5 kg/day; utilisation about 25% (about 1.2 kg/day). Kerala accounts for 90-95% of revenue. Top 10 customers are about 50% of revenue; about 200 other customers make up the rest.

segments.name: Sharjah UAE (AJC Jewel Manufacturers FZC)
segments.commentary: Gold jewellery capacity 3 kg/day at about 800 g/day (about 27% utilisation). Management cited PAT margin of about 4% and EBITDA margin of about 5%, in a tax-exempt free zone. Not consolidated in Q1; expected consolidation from Q3.

segments.name: Esthara Jewels (silver DTC)
segments.commentary: Three stores operational in Kerala; two more under fit-out, expected to open by end of next month. Silver capacity 8 kg/day with about 1 kg/day production. Management targets about Rs 20 lakh revenue per store per month; first store reportedly about Rs 15 lakh per month. Capex about Rs 4,000 per sq ft; opex about Rs 5-6 lakh per store; breakeven targeted within one year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone India revenue target of Rs 450 crore (management reiterated it is standalone India only; Sharjah additional).
Revenue growth of about 50% CAGR for the next three years, stated as based on volume growth; management said price effects would be added only if gold prices rise.
Current PAT margin of about 2.5% cited for the year.
Sharjah full-year contribution to be updated after H1 results; acquisition completion expected in 3-6 months subject to BSE and regulatory approvals.
Dilution to existing shareholders from the share swap estimated at about 7-8%, per management (uncertain).
Store count and three-year store plans to be updated post H1 results.
Q1 and Q2 seasonally moderate; Q3 and Q4 stronger on festivals and weddings.
capex_capacity: India: 5 kg/day gold casting capacity, upgraded from IPO proceeds to 120% expansion (cited as 5 kg Kerala, 8 kg silver), with about 25% utilisation today.
Silver jewellery production started in India; capacity up to 8 kg/day, currently about 1 kg/day.
Sharjah: 3 kg/day installed gold capacity at about 800 g/day.
At 100% utilisation management cited India about Rs 7 crore/day (about Rs 2,500 crore/yr at 5 kg/day) and Sharjah about Rs 3.6 crore/day; these are indicative and not guidance.
Additional working capital needed to reach peak utilisation; to be funded via internal accruals, debt and possibly equity, gradually.
Design and innovation centre set up; about 20 in-house design staff; library of about 2.5 lakh designs on B2B portal.
demand_pricing: Added 12 independent jewellers in Q1, mainly mid and small Kerala retailers; no new corporate clients after Kalyan.
Management is targeting expansion beyond Kerala, with a marketing team in Chennai; international orders to be served via Sharjah.
Management said gold price moves will not affect margins because it hedges with suppliers and on MCX.
Launched 9-karat and 18-karat products; 18-karat is served to some customers for higher margin at lower caratage. Early response described as encouraging.
Management said no gold metal loan or advance gold loan business; no bullion trading in consolidated revenue.
Receivables growth well ahead of sales (3-year receivables CAGR about 51% vs sales 16%), attributed to recent corporate clients with longer credit periods.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total value and rationale of the Sharjah acquisition, and what margins does it earn?
qa_highlights.answer: 80% stake via share swap, valued at up to Rs 9.6 crore; Sharjah earns about 4% PAT and about 5% EBITDA, aided by free-zone tax exemption. Completion expected in 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 50% growth guidance based on, volume or price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume only; price changes would be added only if gold prices rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected utilisation for FY27/FY28 and revenue at 100% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: No utilisation guidance given. Indicative values at 100%: India about Rs 7 crore/day and Sharjah about Rs 3.6 crore/day. FY27 India target is Rs 450 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is receivables growth far ahead of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to recent corporate clients with longer credit periods, and said it will try to reduce debtors.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow from operations has been negative for six years; when does it turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will try to make it positive in coming years, without a specific timeline; focus is on sales volume and growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a demand impact from the duty change talk and what is the Q2/Q3 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said duty changes have not affected the business historically; Q1 and Q2 are moderate, Q3 and Q4 stronger. No specific Q3 numbers given.

543667|2026-06.headline: INOX Green Q1 FY27 PAT rose 86% YoY to INR41 crore; Wind World India acquisition completion expected in Q2 FY27.
543667|2026-06.overview:
INOX Green reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR101 crore (+17% YoY), EBITDA of INR57 crore (+19%), PBT of INR54 crore (+74%) and PAT of INR41 crore (+86%). Management said the power evacuation business was demerged into INOX Renewable Solutions effective August 1, 2026 (record date), leaving INOX Green as an asset-light O&M player. NCLT Ahmedabad approved the Wind World India acquisition, with completion expected in Q2 FY27. Management reiterated full-year guidance but declined to quantify quarterly trajectory, and the call was largely about the parent's (INOX Wind) revenue and receivables questions.</overview>

qa_highlights.question: Why raise funds for the Wind World acquisition when prior preferential issue funded it, and why not debt against cash flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said these were enabling resolutions and declined further comment citing the silent period.

qa_highlights.question: Is INOX Clean business on the same terms as third-party business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inter-entity contracts are arm's length, INOX Clean is treated as a customer, and there is no preferential pricing for any customer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INOX Green portfolio's revenue per MW and how much of the acquired portfolio is consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended INR9-10 lakh per MW excluding GST on about 4 GW own turbines; the two acquired portfolios (about 6.5 GW) remain investments and are not consolidated until shares are acquired.

qa_highlights.question: Why is legacy O&M EBITDA well below the 50% guided margin, and what about the deferred INR400 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to one-off, infrastructure and life-extension costs, plus value-added services previously not billed separately, which will be billed from this year. On the deferred revenue, management said part was recognised in Q1 and the rest would be covered over FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR600 crore EBITDA guidance for FY27 and does it start from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR600 crore is an annual figure on an annualised basis from Q3/Q4 post consolidation, not a quarterly target, and gave no FY28 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 75% FY27 revenue growth guidance still achievable given flat Q1 at INOX Wind?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the 75% growth target, citing H2-weighting (70-75% of business) and a shift to equipment supply that it expects to show results from Q2-end and predominantly in Q3.

544613|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 125.3% YoY to Rs 13,457 mn; EBITDA margin 18.9%, normalized PAT Rs 1,652 mn after Bawal fire exceptional loss of Rs 1,436 mn.
544613|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 125.3% YoY to Rs 13,457 mn and EBITDA rose 140.6% to Rs 2,548 mn, with margin up to 18.9% from 17.7%. A Rs 1,436 mn provisional exceptional loss from the Bawal facility fire brought reported PAT to Rs 578 mn (4.3% margin), while normalized PAT was Rs 1,652 mn (12.3%). Management raised full-year revenue growth guidance to about 70% from 50%, kept the margin guidance at "sustainable to improve," and added distributors, dealers and two states. Ratlam capacity additions (2 GW solar panel, 2 GW power electronics, 2 GW battery due Q2 FY27) and stake increases in Zayo entities were the main capex and integration moves.

financial_highlights.change: expected to be fully recovered via insurance

financial_highlights.metric: Normalized PAT (ex post-tax fire provision Rs 1,074 mn)

segments.name: Residential rooftop / B2C
segments.commentary: Management said about 90% of revenue comes from the B2C channel. Sales are sold as a package of panels, inverters and batteries; no segment-wise revenue split was given.

segments.name: Off-grid vs on-grid vs hybrid
segments.commentary: Management said on-grid growth was the main driver this quarter, enabled by in-house DCR cells; off-grid is still growing but more slowly. No split was disclosed.

segments.name: Tubular batteries
segments.commentary: Tubular battery output (about 10% of revenue) was lost in the Bawal fire; management estimated the gross margin impact at below 0.5% as batteries are now bought from outside vendors.

guidance_outlook: Full-year revenue growth guidance raised to about 70% from the earlier 50%, with a stated intent to trail it upward in later quarters.
EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 'sustainable to improve' (Q1 at 18.9%).
Insurance claim on the Bawal fire (net carrying value about Rs 1,436 mn) expected to settle by end of FY27; management expects full recovery.
Ratlam 2 GW lithium-ion battery plant on track for commissioning by Q2 FY27.
FY27 gross block (incl. CWIP) expected at about Rs 1,300 cr, up from about Rs 800 cr at start of year.
Channel partner target of more than 15,000 (distributors, dealers, shoppes) by end FY28.
Zayo Energy plant expected to add Rs 400-500 cr top-line in the next financial year; Fujiyama's share of Zayo capex about Rs 50 cr.
capex_capacity: Solar panel capacity: 2 GW added at Ratlam (capitalized 14 May 2026), taking total to 3.5 GW; Ratlam running one shift and ramping in phases.
Power electronics: 2 GW facility at Ratlam commissioned in August 2026, taking total to 4 GW; initial utilization of Ratlam capacity guided at 40-50%.
Solar cell (DCR) plant at 1 GW (some reports say 1.2 GW) running at 80%+ utilization; non-Ratlam panel plants at 70-80% utilization.
TOPCon line: building complete and machine orders placed; target commissioning in about 9 months (within the next financial year per the call).
Zayo Energy/Zayo Cables: stake raised from 19% to 50% each; Zayo Energy capex about Rs 180-200 cr total, with land acquisition under way and production targeted within about one year.
demand_pricing: Management cited current PM Surya Ghar installation run rate of about 1 GW per month; about 50 lakh of the 1 crore household target covered.
Industry rooftop capacity installed to date put at over 30 GW, with about 15 GW under PM Surya Ghar; government target 90-100 GW rooftop of 300 GW solar by 2030.
System pricing quoted at Rs 26-30 per watt (BOM with panel, inverter, battery) at distributor billing level, including GST.
Industry growth rate cited at about 40%; Fujiyama estimates about 10% share of the on-grid market (not officially confirmed).
Distributors rose from 950+ to 1,150+ in the quarter; channel partners rose from about 8,900 to over 10,100 with Odisha and Uttarakhand newly moved to covered states.
Management said DCR pricing and higher realization on Mono PERC DCR panels drove the higher average realization.

qa_highlights.question: How should full-year revenue and profit be modelled after a strong Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to about 70% from 50%, citing demand and Ratlam capacity, and said it will trail the guidance upward as the year progresses.

qa_highlights.question: Will backward integration lift margins or be passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCR cell capacity supports margins but raw material price volatility is a factor, and it will pass on part of the gains; margin guidance remains 'sustainable to improve'.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Bawal fire loss is recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the damaged assets with net carrying value about Rs 143 cr are fully insured, the survey is done, the full loss was booked in Q1, and claim settlement is expected by year end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 26-30 per watt figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an average distributor BOM (roughly Rs 15 panel, Rs 5 inverter, Rs 5 battery), varying with DCR/non-DCR, battery type and system type, with GST included.

qa_highlights.question: Capex funding for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no equity dilution this year; about Rs 200 cr of the Rs 500 cr additional capex will be debt-funded, with Rs 100 cr from IPO proceeds and Rs 200 cr from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the TOPCon line and the lead-acid plant after the fire?
qa_highlights.answer: TOPCon commissioning is targeted within about 9 months. The fire-hit lead-acid plant will not restart until insurance work is done; the company is in talks to lease an operating plant.

risks_watch: Bawal insurance claim settlement (management targets end FY27); any delay or shortfall versus Rs 1,436 mn would hit reported earnings.
Margin sustainability as market share is pushed with price cuts and as module prices fall; non-DCR margins are under pressure.
PM Surya Ghar 2.0 is not yet notified; loan sanction and DCR supply constraints are slowing installations.
Ratlam battery plant (2 GW) commissioning in Q2 FY27 and new power electronics ramp-up at 40-50% utilization.
BIS compliance: 15 of about 500 SKUs were flagged by the authority; management says these are now certified and represent under 1% of stock value.
Revenue is not disclosed by segment, which limits visibility into on-grid, off-grid and hybrid mix.
Zayo Energy stake commitments and capex (Rs 180-200 cr total) plus the lead-acid plant lease.

504380|2026-06.headline: Flomic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.4% YoY to INR120 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 275 bps to 9.34%, but PAT fell to INR2.06 crore from INR2.98 crore.
504380|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations grew 18.4% YoY to INR120 crore, with management attributing most of the growth to higher freight rates rather than volume (shipments up roughly 6-7%). EBITDA rose about 68% to INR11.21 crore and margin improved to 9.34% from 6.59%. PBT turned positive at INR2.73 crore from a loss of INR3.3 crore a year earlier, while PAT was INR2.06 crore versus INR2.98 crore last year. Management said a one-time INR28 lakh lease-related benefit was included, and it cited branch closures, manpower cost reduction and an AI-based back-office system from 1 July as margin levers.</overview>

segments.name: Air & Sea Import Forwarding
segments.commentary: Revenue INR40 crore in Q1; management said all segments improved YoY, but no prior-year split was given.

segments.name: Sea Export
segments.commentary: Revenue around INR33.39 crore in Q1; management said ocean exports are the main incremental profit pool while freight rates are rising.

segments.name: Air Export
segments.commentary: Revenue INR22 crore in Q1; management said some cargo has shifted from ocean to air, adding to this segment.

segments.name: Warehousing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR18 crore in Q1; around 15% of revenue now, with a stated gross margin of 15-16% (15-20% range), targeted at 17-18% and then about 20% of contribution.

segments.name: Air & Sea Import Clearance
segments.commentary: Revenue INR7.42 crore in Q1; management did not give further detail.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth momentum to continue for three to four quarters, but gave no numerical FY27 target.
Management expects ocean and air export benefits to last at least two to three more quarters while freight rates stay elevated.
Management said freight rate-driven growth may not be long-term sustainable.
Warehousing share of revenue is targeted to rise to 17-18% and then about 20%.
Management expects operating margins to improve further from corrective actions, higher freight rates and AI-led cost reduction.
Management says it will stay asset-light, with warehousing expansion mainly leased and customer-backed.
capex_capacity: Warehousing expansion will be selective, leased and customer-backed rather than driven by square footage.
Project cargo vertical is being built with a newly hired team; management called it higher margin but higher execution risk.
AI-based application (back-office documentation, quotation-to-billing) started from 1 July 2026; the company handled about 42,000 shipments last year, previously with manual file creation.
Priorities for FY27 include CFS and air cargo capabilities, presence across key Indian hubs and selectively overseas.
No capex amount or capacity figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth was mainly price-driven: shipment volumes rose about 6-7% YoY, with the rest from freight rates, which rose sharply on geopolitical volatility.
Middle East disruption reduced export cargo volumes, per management.
Management targets mid-sized customers and avoids both very large corporates and small startups, citing margin and payment risk.
Project cargo demand cited from oil and gas, aerospace, energy, pharma cold chain and solar; exports mainly to Africa, imports from Germany and China.
Management did not disclose the customer count beyond an analyst's reference to about 5,000 active customers.

qa_highlights.question: How does management view FY27 revenue growth for Flomic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects revenue to be better on higher freight rates, with momentum for three to four quarters, but gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scale and margin profile of the project logistics business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described oversized, dimensional project cargo needing special equipment and permits, with higher margins than routine freight forwarding and higher execution risk; no revenue scale was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 revenue growth came from volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Shipment growth was about 6-7% YoY; the remainder came from freight rate increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin after excluding the one-time INR28 lakh benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT margin was still significantly higher YoY even after excluding the INR28 lakh, and that manpower cost has already been reduced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the warehousing margin and growth potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said warehousing gross margin is 15-16% (15-20% range), with Ind AS 116 inflating reported segment margin because rent on leased assets is excluded; share of revenue is to rise to about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What annual savings are expected from closing loss-making branches?
qa_highlights.answer: No savings figure was given; management said closed branches were non-performing and located where the company lacked customers.

risks_watch: PAT declined YoY to INR2.06 crore despite EBITDA growth of ~68%, implying higher depreciation, interest or tax; the call did not explain the gap.
Growth is mainly freight-rate driven and management itself said it may not be sustainable; volumes grew only ~6-7%.
Receivable days of 56-57 remain above the company's own 30-60 day comfort range's upper end only partly; any slip raises interest cost.
Execution risk in project cargo and warehousing expansion, and the new AI system's rollout from 1 July 2026.
Middle East disruption is reducing export cargo volumes.
Q1 results include a one-time INR28 lakh lease-related benefit; check the underlying run-rate next quarter.
504380|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margin trajectory and the company's integrated model, but vague on numbers: management repeatedly declined to give FY27 revenue or margin targets and gave no capex or branch-savings figures. Answers on the freight-rate tailwind were candid that it may not be durable.
key_quotes: So effectively, it is 18.4% growth.
Our EBITDA margin also improved to 9.34% from 6.59%, effective increase of 275 basis points.
We are not chasing only turnover. Our focus is on gross profit, margins, working capital discipline, and quality customers and better systems.
The freight growth sustainability may not be very long term.

544457|2026-06.headline: Brigade Hotel Ventures Q1 FY27 PAT rose 140% to INR17 crores on 9% RevPAR growth and lower finance cost, despite a ~INR14 crore West Asia-linked MICE cancellation hit.
544457|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 5% YoY to INR131 crores and EBITDA rose 9% to INR46 crores at a 34.8% margin, with GST 2.0 weighing 1.6 points on margin. PAT more than doubled to INR17 crores from INR7 crores, mainly because finance cost fell over 50% to INR8.7 crores after post-IPO debt repayment. Operationally, ARR rose 7% to INR7,241 and occupancy rose 2% to 75.7%, with management calling the RevPAR growth rate-led. F&B was the weak spot as large MICE events were cancelled or postponed across the city, and management expects a stronger Q2 and H2.

financial_highlights.change: down from INR18.9 crores in Q1 FY26 (over 50%)
no institutional debt after INR468.1 crores repaid from IPO proceeds

segments.name: Bangalore hotels
segments.commentary: ARR grew about 3% and occupancy rose 8%, giving RevPAR growth of about 10%; management is holding occupancy and will push ADR over the next three quarters.

segments.name: Sheraton Grand (F&B-heavy)
segments.commentary: Roughly 50-50 room and F&B revenue mix; it took the largest F&B hit from MICE cancellations, and its ADR was about INR500 lower YoY.

segments.name: Courtyard by Marriott Kochi Infopark (ex Four Points)
segments.commentary: ARR rose to INR4,650 from INR4,200, but occupancy fell sharply (71% in Q1 FY26) due to lost crew business and GDS changes during rebranding; management sees occupancy in the high 60s in Q2 and expects at least 10% ADR growth this year.

segments.name: ibis Styles
segments.commentary: Occupancy was about 40% in its first half-year of operations and is now in the 70s in its second year.

guidance_outlook: Management is trying to hold mid-teens like-to-like revenue growth for FY27, with the Q1 shortfall (about INR14 crores, roughly 10% of top line) expected to be recouped in H2.
July performance described as better and September as very buoyant; management expects Q2 to be much stronger than Q1.
Q4 FY27 expected to be strong on large-scale MICE events, which recur every alternate year (Aero Show year).
ADR target of above INR7,500 for the portfolio and each hotel, to offset GST impact; Q1 FY26 ADR was INR6,761.
Management says the 1,700 upcoming keys take the portfolio from 1,600 to 3,300 keys by FY30/FY31; luxury and upper-upscale mix to reach 31% by FY29 and 38% by FY31.
Internal accruals expected to contribute over INR1,000 crores over the coming years, with the rest from borrowing (about 60:40 mix).
Hotel acquisition from IPO proceeds under discussion, with a transaction targeted in FY27 subject to due diligence.
capex_capacity: Total development capex of about INR3,600 crores; about INR400 crores spent in FY26 and INR500 crores planned for FY27. Q1 FY27 spend was about INR53 crores (INR45 crores CWIP, INR3.5 crores renovation, INR4 crores for the new restaurant Project Grain), with about INR350 crores to be spent over the remaining three quarters.
Courtyard by Marriott Chennai at World Trade Center, 45 keys, launch planned for October / Q3 FY27.

Two Fairfield hotels under construction; Ritz-Carlton Vaikom well underway with designs finalised; JW Marriott Chennai excavation to start soon; InterContinental at Brigade Gateway dependent on the mixed-use township.
Grand Hyatt slightly delayed from FY28 because of pending approvals; Tumkur Road (Bangalore) project waiting for approvals.
JW Marriott Chennai under approval and Thiruvananthapuram still in planning; management expects both to open by 2030.
Renewable energy at 61% of total energy needs; several hotels above 90%.
demand_pricing: Management attributes Q1 weakness to West Asia conflict, which cut foreign travellers (FTAs) from about 40% to about 30% of room arrivals and raised fares and fuel costs.
Cancellations and postponements of large MICE events hit the whole city; the INR14 crore impact was about 60% F&B and 40% rooms. MICE is about 15-18% of room bookings.
Domestic corporate business, locally negotiated rates, staycations, and social events were used to backfill room revenue.
Management says RevPAR growth was rate-led rather than occupancy-led, though occupancy rose in Bangalore and in most hotels.
F&B is about 32% of overall top line.
WTC Chennai expected to open at a minimum starting ADR of INR9,000 with stabilised occupancy of about 80%, backed by captive demand from tenants.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex was spent in Q1 and how will the INR500 crore FY27 plan be phased?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR53 crores was spent in Q1; about INR350 crores is expected in the remaining three quarters, mainly H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the F&B and MICE trend improving for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites July pickup, very healthy September, and larger MICE inquiries, and expects the lost Q1 revenue to be partly recovered in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mid-teens growth target for FY27 hold given the slow start and high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management still aims for mid-teens like-to-like growth, citing the INR14 crore cancellation hit as the main gap; no revised number was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is Bangalore strength driven by domestic demand or business recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic accounts, locally negotiated rates, and staycations replaced lost foreign travellers; management says the portfolio occupancy is about 76% with five of nine hotels above 80%.

qa_highlights.question: Are there delays on live projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly on track; the Grand Hyatt is slightly delayed pending approvals, and the Tumkur Road project awaits approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Should ADR be prioritised over occupancy in Bangalore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants to hold occupancy and grow ADR; it aims for the portfolio and each hotel to cross INR7,500 ADR.

533271|2026-06.headline: Ashoka Buildcon Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 55% YoY to INR292 crores on HAM/BOT monetisation; FY27 revenue growth guidance cut to 10-15% from 20%.
533271|2026-06.overview:
Standalone total income was flat YoY at INR1,320 crores, with EBITDA down 17% to INR126 crores (9.5% margin) and PAT up 3% to INR31.5 crores. Consolidated total income fell 21% to INR1,534 crores, mainly because of BOT and HAM asset monetisation in Q3 FY26, and consolidated EBITDA fell 55% to INR292 crores (19.0% margin). Management cut FY27 revenue growth guidance to 10-15% from 20% and EBITDA margin to roughly 9-9.5% from about 10%. Order book stood at INR15,251 crores as of 30 June, with about INR450 crores added after quarter-end, and the company is pivoting to international, railway and power T&D work as domestic highway awarding stays subdued.</overview>

segments.name: Road HAM

FY27 EBITDA margin about 0.5 percentage points below the start-of-year target of roughly 10%, i.e. around 9-9.5%; margin recovery expected in H2 as new projects ramp up.
FY27 order inflow guided at INR6,000-8,000 crores: INR800 crores won in Q1, plus about INR1,800 crores where the company is L1 (expected to materialise in Q2), with the rest in Q3-Q4.

capex_capacity: Q1 capex about INR25 crores (INR7 crores international); FY27 capex target about INR125 crores.

Purestudy stake diluted from 59% to 39.33%, making it an associate rather than a subsidiary.

543953|2026-06.headline: Khazanchi Q1 FY27 revenue rose 45% YoY to INR586.36 crore and PAT 84% to INR27.83 crore, with EBITDA margin at 6.82%.
543953|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 45% YoY to INR586.36 crore, EBITDA rose 89% to INR39.98 crore and PAT rose 84% to INR27.83 crore, with margins expanding 158 bps (EBITDA) and 99 bps (PAT). Management attributed the quarter to the first full quarter of the new flagship showroom and ERP rollout. The company is migrating from BSE SME to the main boards of BSE and NSE, which management expects to complete in about 2 months, and it reiterated a INR5,000 crore revenue target by FY30 with 25-30% growth and B2C reaching ~40% of revenue. Several answers were vague (volume split, store capex, quantum sold), and the call ran on a mix of expansion plans and operating metrics.

financial_highlights.change: +45% YoY vs INR403.84 crore in Q1 FY26
Management said grams/quantum sold implied by ~15% growth; exact grams to be shared later
Inventory turnover days 73 vs 63 in Q4 FY26
Revenue ~5x and PAT ~10x since FY23 (INR481 crore revenue, INR8 crore PAT)

segments.name: B2B (wholesale)
segments.commentary: Management described B2B as the scale and stability base, with ~1,000 clients, none above 5-6% of revenue, and a targeted 25% growth. Working cycle is ~40-45 days. Higher-margin Kundan Jadau and diamond jewellery were added to B2B.

segments.name: B2C (retail)
segments.commentary: Flagship showroom is targeted at ~INR500 crore annual revenue, with management saying it is achieving 80-85% of that; current monthly run-rate is ~INR30-35 crore. Retail working cycle is ~100-120 days. Target is 40% of revenue by FY30, from a current share the company did not state precisely.

guidance_outlook: Revenue target of ~INR5,000 crore by FY30, with growth of 25-30% per year (management said both revenue and PAT CAGR of 25-30%, clarified in the call).
Management now expects ~30% full-year growth if current pace holds, with B2B growing ~25%.
B2C to reach ~40% of revenue by FY30; plan of 8-10 stores over 3-4 years, initially in Tamil Nadu, company-owned only, with later expansion to other states (Andhra named as next).
Main board migration to BSE and NSE: documents to be submitted shortly; completion expected in about 2 months, subject to regulatory approvals.
Management expects positive operating cash flow in FY27 after a negative FY26, as stock build for new stores normalises.
capex_capacity: 8-10 retail stores planned by FY30, a mix of flagship showrooms and minimal-jewellery boutiques; capex per store not defined until formats and venues are finalised.

543387|2026-06.headline: SJS Q1FY27 revenue hit record Rs 2,610 mn (+24.5% YoY) and adjusted PAT Rs 502.5 mn (+45.2%), with EBITDA margin at 30%.
543387|2026-06.overview:
SJS reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue and profitability since listing, with automotive growing 32.4% against 21.7% for the PV plus two-wheeler industry. Reported PAT of Rs 744.2 mn includes a one-time Rs 241.7 mn gain on sale of the old Bangalore facility; adjusted PAT was Rs 502.5 mn (19.3% margin). Management reiterated 1.5x–2x industry outperformance for FY27 and an export target of 14–15% of revenue by FY28. The new SJS Decoplast Pune plant began commercial operations in August 2026, and a wholly-owned cover glass and display subsidiary was approved, with supplies targeted from Q2 FY28.</overview>

capex_capacity: 15 MW captive solar plant: 12 MW operational since 7 August 2026, balance expected in about 1.5 months; long-term target 40 MW with further expansion planned next year.
Integrated capacity: 2 lakh MT TMT bars and 2,16,000 tons billets; billet plant commissioned in the quarter.
Next-year plan to expand installed capacity, timing and capex amount not disclosed.
Current TMT utilisation ~80% of installed capacity; peak achievable ~90% per management.
demand_pricing: Average TMT selling price per metric ton rose YoY in Q1; management cites a premium of about ₹1,500/ton over local players in tier 2, tier 3 and taluka markets.
Imported scrap is 50-60% of raw material, sponge iron 20-25% (sourced from Gujarat, Raipur, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Bihar) and local scrap 20-25%.
Scrap price spike and rupee depreciation compressed margins; TMT prices lagged the raw material cost rise.
Company focuses on dealer-led retail in Gujarat rather than institutional or infrastructure contracts, citing competition and limited supply for dealers.
Dealer network of 227 dealers and 3 distributors under the Kamdhenu brand; network grows 10-15% annually. Aditya dealers in Saurashtra and Kutch to be added post-merger.

qa_highlights.question: What were Q1 utilisation and cost or margin benefits from billet backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q1 TMT production of 34,400 MT and said the cost benefit came mainly from debt repayment (no fixed debt now). Utilisation is ~80% of installed capacity, which management considers ideal given 24-hour capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What are the solar project progress, timeline, capex and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: 12 MW of 15 MW is live since 7 August with the rest in about 1.5 months; ~30% of power needs covered. Savings of about ₹4/unit after EMI, ~2.7 crore units/yr, giving about ₹10 crore annual savings. Capex and funding structure were not stated.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise to ₹228.35 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher-margin products (including 550D) were added, and monsoon-season sales were lower while production continued. Management expects inventory to fall below ₹200 crore after Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall despite revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported scrap prices rose sharply due to the Iran conflict, and TMT prices did not rise as much. Rupee depreciation also raised the cost of cargo bought at earlier dollar rates. Management expects improvement in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is imported scrap still economically viable versus local scrap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said imports are preferred for bulk buying, GST simplicity and consistent quality; large players continue to rely mainly on imports, with 50-60% of input imported.

risks_watch: Imported scrap cost and rupee-dollar movement, given 50-60% import dependence and a lag of 30-90 days between purchase and payment.
Monsoon-driven weakness in Q2 and a demand slowdown in construction.
Q1 EBITDA and PAT decline; watch for margin recovery in Q3 FY27 as guided.
Aditya Ultra Steel amalgamation pending regulatory approvals; roughly six months for completion after approval.
Utilisation of billet and TMT capacity versus the guided 4-5% annual improvement; solar commissioning on schedule.

530813|2026-06.headline: KRBL Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR261 crores (16.7% margin) on price hikes and investment gains, while exports fell about 50% on Middle East disruption.
530813|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue for operations was INR1,496 crores, down about 6% YoY, as Middle East exports collapsed to INR244 crores (from INR485 crores) after the Strait of Hormuz disruption. Exports to all other regions grew 37%. Domestic revenue excluding power rose 14% to INR1,221 crores, driven by about 9-11% higher realisations, while branded bulk-pack volumes declined. Gross margin (including other income) jumped to 36.3% from 25.7%, and EBITDA margin to 23.8% from 13.9%, helped by INR64 crores of other income including MTM and forex gains. Management called the margins unsustainable and guided FY27 to about 30% gross margin and 17-18% EBITDA margin.</overview>

segments.name: Export - Middle East

segments.name: Domestic (India business)
segments.commentary: Domestic revenue excluding power rose 14% to INR1,221 crores; consumer pack and regional rice performed well, while branded bulk-pack volumes declined on timing of purchases. Modern trade rice volume grew 6.5% and value 13%; e-commerce primary sales grew about 50%.

segments.name: Masala and regional rice
segments.commentary: Masala portfolio grew 74% in value YoY with an annualised run rate of about INR9 crores, targeting INR25 crores by FY27-end. Branded regional rice grew 25%, against a base of about INR270 crores in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 domestic volume growth guided at about 10%, maintained for the next 2-3 years; bulk-pack volumes expected to resume in Q2 and Q3.
Export shortfall described as timing; export volumes expected to recover progressively from Q2 and meaningful full-year export growth maintained.
FY27 gross margin guided at about 30% and EBITDA margin at 17-18%; management says Q1 margins are not sustainable.
No further branded price hikes planned in Q2; pricing for Q3 to be decided after the paddy crop season unfolds.
Gangavathi facility for regional products expected to be operational by end of Q3 FY27.
Plans to buy more paddy and rice inventory this season, citing a comfortable 389,000 tons of rice and 71,000 tons of paddy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Saudi Arabia entity, and are direct bookings continuing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is searching for a distributor after past problems with a wrong partner; 3-4 candidates identified, with finalisation awaiting peace in the region. The direct entity programme is deferred, while wholesaler shipments continue.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 exports be higher, and can restocking absorb high freight costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gulf benchmark prices have risen, letting it pass on freight costs; Q2 export numbers expected to be much better, though container space and equipment shortages are slowing movement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 margins are not sustainable; FY27 guidance is about 30% gross margin and 17-18% EBITDA margin, versus about 15% last year.

qa_highlights.question: How will domestic volume grow, and what is the regional/quick commerce plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 10% domestic volume growth for the next 2-3 years; Q1 volume dip was due to deferred bulk-pack orders. More regional rice varieties will be listed on quick commerce platforms later this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why not buy more inventory given available cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will buy more paddy this season, but purchases depend on market conditions; current stock of 389,000 tons of rice is considered comfortable.

qa_highlights.question: What are the regional rice and overall revenue targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Regional rice is targeted to grow 25% on about INR270 crores; overall guidance is about 10% volume growth, with price guidance withheld because of West Asia uncertainty and the upcoming paddy season.

qa_highlights.question: Will basmati prices rise if the Gulf supply gap reopens?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices would rise if peace returns, but the size of the new crop is uncertain after late rains; crop size clarity expected around 25 August.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gross margin structurally sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 gross margin is not sustainable, driven by price increases and MTM gains; FY27 gross margin guided at about 30%.

537259|2026-06.headline: Suyog Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR710 mn (+6.1% YoY on electricity-inclusive basis), net profit INR145 mn; Vodafone Idea rollout began mid-June with 150 tenancies converted.
537259|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 revenue was INR710 mn, up 6.1% YoY against INR668 mn restated for electricity, with EBITDA of INR420 mn (59.3% margin) and PBT of INR195 mn. From 1 April the company began including electricity reimbursement in revenue after a GST-related guidance change, which lowered the reported EBITDA margin from about 70% to 59.3%. Vodafone Idea orders started flowing around 15-16 June; 95 towers (150 tenancies) were converted in June. Management said most growth will show from Q2 onwards, with the full benefit in FY28. Net profit margin was about 20% against 25% a year ago, which management attributed to a vendor-provision reversal in the prior-year quarter.</overview>

qa_highlights.question: Confidence and breakdown of the 3,000 Vodafone tenancies?

qa_highlights.question: Why is BSNL no longer being pushed in guidance?

qa_highlights.question: What is the 189/186-site BSNL billing status?
qa_highlights.answer: 186 sites are still pending billing; management expects revenue from them to start in Q2.

505537|2026-06.headline: Zee Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR 789 million (4.1% margin) as advertising dropped 11% YoY, while ZEE5 revenue rose 58% to INR 4,571 million.
505537|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 was weighed down by an 11% YoY decline in advertising revenue, attributed to the Middle East conflict hitting April and May, and by a 15% rise in operating costs from FIFA 2026 marketing and new sports channel launches. Subscription revenue grew 16% YoY, and ZEE5 revenue grew 58% YoY to INR 4,571 million, though the digital business posted only INR 44 million EBITDA. Linear network share reached 20% (17.9% for the quarter through week 24), and PAT was INR 743 million. Management said significant FIFA revenue and cost will flow through in Q2, and it declined to give full-year EBITDA margin guidance.</overview>

qa_highlights.answer: Company wrote to the regulator seeking clarification with no response yet and has appealed to the Securities Appellate Tribunal. Management hopes for a quick resolution; preferential allotment approval is valid for one year but the matter is sub judice.

qa_highlights.question: How is the music business accounted for and is a demerger planned?

543748|2026-06.headline: Aarti Pharmalabs Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 42% YoY to INR535 crore, PAT up 49% to INR71 crore, led by record Xanthine sales.

Xanthine derivatives made up 57% of turnover and hit its highest-ever quarterly sales, helped by raw-material pass-through and price increases during the West Asia crisis. CDMO/CMO fell to 7% of revenue, with management attributing this to postponed deliveries and expecting H2-weighted growth. Management said Xanthine prices have eased from peaks in June-July, so the company expects a lower realisation per kg going forward.

CDMO/CMO growth of 40-50% in FY27, H2-weighted; CDMO expected to reach ~20% of revenue this year and 25-30% of sales over time.

CDMO: 37 commercial projects, up from 21 three years ago; one new customer and three net new projects added in Q1.
