qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 gross margin of ~56% sustainable given falling Xanthine realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said absolute gross margin should be sustained as higher volumes from ~9,500 MT capacity offset lower prices; company-level gross margin ~50% plus or minus a few points.

qa_highlights.question: Is CDMO revenue H2-heavy this year and what is the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, FY27 CDMO will be H2-heavy as in prior years; 40-50% growth reiterated. Net +3 projects and +1 customer in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CDMO revenue fall to 7% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited postponed sales due to non-deliveries under accounting standards; expects to build up over the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Can Xanthine FY27 revenue reach INR1,100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a range of INR900-1,100 crore, leaning to INR900-1,000 crore, depending on price normalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Xanthine price rise structural or temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Involution-driven changes are seen as structural for the next few years; raw-material spikes as temporary. Management said roughly 50-50 split.

qa_highlights.question: What would API revenue have been without the steroid shutdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated INR170-190 crore per quarter, with the shutdown having reduced Q1 revenue.

509675|2026-06.headline: BirlaNu Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.6% to Rs 1,174 crores and EBITDA 35% to Rs 80 crores, with Parador still loss-making at Rs 13 crores.
509675|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 10% to Rs 824 crores and EBITDA rose nearly 70% to Rs 97 crores, with margins up over 420 bps, led by Roofs and Pipes. Pipes revenue fell 11% and volumes fell 27% on a sharp PVC resin price swing, yet EBITDA margin expanded 660 bps on mix and pricing. Parador swung to a Rs 13 crore EBITDA loss, which management attributed mostly to timing items expected to normalise in H2. Gross borrowings fell about Rs 100 crores to Rs 758 crores and working capital was cut by about Rs 100 crores year-on-year.

financial_highlights.change: nearly +70% YoY; margin up over 420 bps
vs profit of Rs 5 crores last year
down from Rs 852 crores at March 2026

segments.name: Roofs
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 517 crores, up 17% (volume growth about 10%), a record quarter with market share up about 100 bps and EBITDA margin 18.2%.

segments.name: Walls (boards, panels, blocks)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 14% with margin 10.2%, up 270 bps; management says the current portfolio can reach 12-14%.

segments.name: Pipes
segments.commentary: Revenue down 11% and volumes down 27% after PVC resin prices rose about 60% in March then fell about 30% in April; EBITDA margin still up over 660 bps on mix and pricing.

segments.name: Construction Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue up 11% despite raw material prices rising over 50%; tile and project slowdowns hit demand temporarily.

segments.name: Parador (Europe)
segments.commentary: Revenue flat YoY in euro terms; order book up over 10%; EBITDA loss of Rs 13 crores includes about EUR 1 million of one-time SAP and front-loaded maintenance costs.

segments.name: Clean Coats
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 9 crores in Q1; now reported under Pipes and Construction Chemicals on a consolidated basis.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give numeric FY27 targets but said it hopes to keep beating internal targets, which it has done for the last two quarters.
Pipes: expects moderate growth in seasonally weak Q2, with PVC prices stabilising on government measures.
Parador: expects H2 recovery and says it is looking at more than breaking even this year; BCG cost programme targeted at 300-400 bps EBITDA margin uplift, with full impact around Q4.
Boards: Andhra Pradesh (Nellore) plant to be commissioned by Q4 FY27; new Telangana board plant expected to add Rs 300-350 crores revenue and Rs 75-85 crores EBITDA once ramped up.
Borrowings expected to stay elevated near term, reducing progressively as Nellore board plant starts contributing from late FY27.
Management cites a longer-term aim of doubling the business, about Rs 8,000-9,000 crores revenue over 2-3 years; about Rs 500 crores capex is allocated to named projects.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad (Telangana) greenfield designer board plant approved; capex about Rs 167 crores including land (about Rs 145-150 crores excluding land), asset turn 0.9x, target revenue Rs 140 crores.
Nellore boards and panels plant: Rs 127 crores capex, civil work under way, machinery installation to start from next month; around 90-100% of orders placed.
OPVC capex of Rs 40 crores completed in July 2026.
Boards capacity at 80-90% utilisation, described as capacity constrained.
Solar capacity commissioned at 2 manufacturing facilities.
demand_pricing: Roofs growth driven by rural demand, price support and elevated steel sheet prices pushing demand toward fibre cement; management characterised the quarter as secondary sales.
Board industry is about Rs 1,500-2,000 crores, growing 10-14% a year; 5-7 organised players and 15-20% imports; industry margins in the high teens.
Pipes: sharp April demand drop after resin price moves; management says Q2 indications are positive but PVC pipe market remains volatile.
Parador: commercial and new-market revenue each under 5% today; line of sight to adding Rs 20-30 million (EUR) revenue over the next couple of years, lifting their combined share to about 20%.
Construction Chemicals: raw material inflation above 50% and tile-industry disruption from the Middle East conflict.
Working capital: receivables down close to 30% after tighter credit controls; fibre inventory substantially reduced over 6-8 months.

qa_highlights.question: What covenant breaches were waived by banks and what is the borrowing plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Breaches were on debt-equity covenants; borrowings were Rs 852 crores at March 2026 and Rs 758 crores at June 2026, and they will stay elevated near term until Nellore starts contributing from late FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How does Parador grow over the next 2-3 years and what is the cost upside?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees at least Rs 20-30 million of added revenue from US, India, UK and Middle East commercial channels, DIY expansion in Europe, and Italy and Eastern Europe orders; BCG cost programme targets at least 300-400 bps EBITDA uplift.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Boards market and why is BirlaNu's margin below the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Market is Rs 1,500-2,000 crores growing 10-14%; the company's wall segment blended margin is 10-11% while new standalone board plants target 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Roofs margins and growth one-offs or sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-offs or inventory gains; growth was about 10% volume plus price, and the mix is primarily secondary sales in the season.

qa_highlights.question: Is Parador manufacturing moving to India, and is a rights issue planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Options including India are being evaluated for cost-to-serve and supply-chain diversification, subject to quality; the CFO said debt-equity is 0.68x and the Board decides on any rights issue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Telangana plant's economics and the Nellore capex status?
qa_highlights.answer: Telangana asset turn is 0.9x on about Rs 145-150 crores investment excluding land; Nellore is in civil construction with about 90-100% of orders placed.

522004|2026-06.headline: Batliboi Q1 FY27 revenue rose 80% YoY to INR125 crores with EBITDA margin near 4% and PAT of INR49 lakhs, backlog INR618 crores.
522004|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR125 crores, up 80% YoY and ahead of earlier guidance, with EBITDA margin stated at about 4% and PAT of INR49 lakhs versus a loss of INR2.4 crores a year earlier. Order inflow was INR283 crores and order backlog stood at about INR618 crores at June 2026. Management guided to around 10% top-line growth for the year, and announced the Penta Automation acquisition and a INR52 crore solar-cell pollution control order from SAEL. Analysts pressed on weak operating leverage, the reconciliation of machine-tool trading income, and EBITDA targets; management gave a 7-8% EBITDA aspiration in 1-2 years and agreed to share trading commission figures offline.

financial_highlights.change: stable (management terms it stable; an analyst noted 4% of turnover, management also cited 6% at one point)
vs loss of INR2.4 crores YoY
includes Quickmill; INR34 crores manufacturing, INR149 crores trading per management reconciliation

segments.name: Machine tools (manufacturing + trading + Quickmill)
segments.commentary: Order inflow INR59 crores in Q1; 88 machines installed in machine tool manufacturing and 1 in trading. Quickmill turnover INR45 crores; Quickmill backlog about INR55 crores. Manufacturing capacity up about 30% YoY.

segments.name: Air Engineering group
segments.commentary: Revenue INR21 crores in Q1 with order inflow of INR21 crores in the same quarter.

segments.name: Textile machinery group
segments.commentary: Order inflow INR79 crores and order backlog INR201 crores; revenue INR12 crores in the quarter.

segments.name: Environmental Engineering division
segments.commentary: Order inflow INR76 crores and revenue INR27 crores; backlog about INR134 crores. Secured INR52 crore SAEL order for solar-cell fume pollution control at Jewar, UP, commissioning in 6-8 months.

segments.name: Penta Automation (acquired)
segments.commentary: Industrial automation and robotics integration; FY26 turnover about INR25 crores; management targets 25-30% growth over next two to three years. Customers cited include Gabriel and Schaeffler.

guidance_outlook: Around 10% top-line growth over last year, supported by healthy order backlog and inquiries.
EBITDA margin aspiration of around 7-8% within one to two years, with Penta and Bioconserve expected to add leverage next year.
Machine tool trading orders delivered over 1 to 1.5 years; part of the benefit expected to show in Q4 and next year.
Quickmill expected to deliver consistent performance; new orders booked in Saudi Arabia.
Management flagged that outlook is subject to Middle East conflict and tariff headwinds.
capex_capacity: Machine tool production capacity up about 30% YoY after capex in foundry and machine tool shop; plans to add one or two more machines.
Considering one or two investments, one in machine tool space and another rooftop/factory solar plant.
Existing solar covers about 65-70% of connected load at the factory, with 30-40% spare capacity to be augmented by end of this fiscal.
Surat factory land parcel being marketed for sale; no deal yet.
demand_pricing: Machine tool demand picking up on defence, aerospace and power private-sector participation.
Raw material costs (copper, steel) rising; company partly absorbing and partly passing on to customers.
Textile sector expected to improve on new incentive policy and UK/EU FTAs; focus on retrofit, Africa, South Asia and Bangladesh once stable.
ZLD demand from textile; plan to expand to pharma and food after about a year.
Penta acquisition expected to enable automation/robot-integrated machine offerings across divisions.

qa_highlights.question: How will Penta be integrated and what synergies are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited automation-linked machine tool cells (robot doing work of two machines) and textile handling automation as cross-division opportunities, driven by skilled manpower shortages.

qa_highlights.question: What turnover and growth to expect from Penta?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 turnover about INR25 crores; management expects around 25-30% growth this year and an average of 25-30% over the next two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why has operating leverage not shown with revenue growth, and what EBITDA is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged margin at about 4-6% and targeted 7-8% in one to two years, citing operational efficiency and Penta/Bioconserve scale-up.

qa_highlights.question: Reconciliation of machine tool trading income and commission figures.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figures combine machine tool and textile machinery trading across five divisions; absolute trading commission numbers for Q1 and last year will be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Backlog split between machine tool manufacturing and trading.
qa_highlights.answer: Machine tool backlog INR103 crores in the quarter: about INR55 crores Quickmill, INR34 crores manufacturing, balance trading (per management). Analyst noted INR183 crores figure appears on a different basis.

qa_highlights.question: Power cost and solar economics.
qa_highlights.answer: Power costs about INR10 per unit; solar payback expected after 3-4 years, with cost of finance in early years.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin stuck near 4%; the 7-8% target is not yet backed by numbers.
Raw material cost inflation (copper, steel) and only partial pass-through.
Disclosure inconsistency: machine tool revenue and backlog splits drew repeated analyst questions; management attributed a gap to rounding and agreed to clarify.
Trading commission income not disclosed on the call; offline follow-up pending.
Bioconserve and Penta are recent acquisitions/subsidiaries with limited track record.
Geopolitical risk (Middle East conflict) and tariff headwinds flagged by management.
522004|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, order book and macro tailwinds, but noticeably defensive and vague when asked about margins, trading income and segment reconciliations, deferring numbers to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: This order is valued at around INR52 crores and the project is on track for commissioning within next six to eight months.
We are looking at something around 7% to 8% in next 1 year or 2 years to reach that operating level.

544410|2026-06.headline: Prostarm Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR 76 crore, PAT up 156% to INR 5 crore, with a 25% minimum FY27 growth target reiterated.
544410|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 76 crore, up 38% YoY but down 27% QoQ from INR 104 crore in Q4, which management attributed to seasonality and deferred execution. EBITDA was INR 7 crore at an 8.55% margin (up 126 bps YoY) and PAT was INR 5 crore at a 6.05% margin. Management said the 12-13% margin guidance still holds on a full-year basis, while also guiding FY27 PAT margin to 8.5-9%. Order book stood at about INR 1,085 crore plus INR 5 crore L1, and working capital days fell from 185 to 168.

financial_highlights.change: +38% YoY; -27% QoQ vs INR 104 crore in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: approx INR 1,085 crore plus INR 5 crore L1 (about INR 1,090 crore total)

financial_highlights.change: from INR -49 crore in Q4 FY26
from about INR 254 crore as of March 2026

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage) developer projects
segments.commentary: Order book includes about INR 855-857 crore of developer business (Bihar and Karnataka/KPTCL). Management said no revenue recognition from these in FY27, only EPC billing on the standalone books; Karnataka dispute was resolved in KPTCL's favour and the company is targeting a sale of that project.

segments.name: Solar EPC and EPC orders
segments.commentary: Solar EPC order of about INR 165 crore from Solarium Green Energy, which management expects to execute fully in FY27. Adani EPC billing was largely completed in Q1 (INR 36 crore of deferred work executed); a further solar EPC order of about INR 12 crore (8.36 MWh) was won.

segments.name: Utility vs C&I BESS
segments.commentary: Company has stopped bidding for utility-scale BESS for about 10 months and is shifting to C&I BESS (200-500 kWh installations), where management says margins are better. Adani project gave about 26% gross margin in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target: minimum 25%.
Margin guidance of 12-13% EBITDA is maintained on a full-year basis, with H2 expected to be stronger; Q1 margin is affected by low turnover and high fixed-cost ratio.
FY27 PAT margin expected at about 8.5-9%, not 10%, due to higher costs from new plants, import costs and hiring.
Jhajjar 1.2 GWh BESS plant and Gujarat UPS plant both expected operational in Q2 FY27; SAP and Salesforce expected operational by end of H1 FY27.
Working capital days targeted at about 120-150 by March 2027; management aims for positive operating cash flow by year-end FY27.
Jhajjar BESS utilisation: not more than 20-25% in FY27, 40-50% in FY28 (around INR 500 crore revenue targeted in FY28); steady-state EBITDA margin 14-15%.
capex_capacity: Jhajjar, Haryana: 1.2 GWh BESS manufacturing facility in final stage of commissioning; earlier delayed, management cited cost and logistics movements and a strategy shift to C&I. Commercial operation now expected by end of H1 FY27.
Gujarat: new UPS manufacturing facility progressing as planned, expected to start commercial operations in Q2 FY27.
Existing manufacturing in Pune and Navi Mumbai.

Bihar BESS (developer/rental model): yearly cash flow of about INR 16 crore over 12 years plus capital subsidy of INR 32.40 crore; SBI facility tied up in SPV, LC-backed by Bihar DISCOM, no corporate guarantee.
Karnataka BESS (KPTCL): annual cash flow of about INR 45.72 crore over 12 years plus capital subsidy of about INR 81 crore; management prioritising a sale post-COD.
demand_pricing: Order book approx INR 1,090 crore including L1. Excluding developer orders (about INR 855 crore), in-hand orders are about INR 236 crore, plus dealer business of about INR 10 crore per month, giving about INR 306-307 crore additional order in hand.
Bids under evaluation of about INR 2,000+ crore, including two large orders of about INR 1,800 crore.
Utility BESS margins under pressure: management said bidders quoted below cost assuming Chinese supply negotiations; cited China export restrictions and a 2% battery tax from 1 September.
Q1 FY27 order wins included an INR 11 crore BESS project from a corporate customer and a INR 165 crore solar EPC order.

Trade receivables: about INR 46 crore realised from the CCTNS (Pune) project in Q1, with a large further amount expected by end-August; management said most of the INR 231 crore is government-funded with no realisation risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the deferred Q4 orders (Adani INR 43 crore, SAIL INR 7 crore, South Eastern Railway INR 13 crore) was executed in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 36 crore has been executed. Adani is almost fully billed; SAIL and South Eastern Railway are to be billed mainly in Q2, with some South Eastern Railway work spilling into Q3 pending site clearance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 revenue fall 27% QoQ, and is the margin guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is seasonally low and that the Adani billing was the major Q4 item. It said the 12-13% margin is a full-year target, with H2 stronger, and that Q1 fixed-cost absorption is weak at INR 76 crore turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What are the working capital days targets and cash flow expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital days fell to 168 from 185; target about 120-150 by March 2027. Operating cash flow improved to about INR -16 crore from INR -49 crore, with a goal of turning positive by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and margin should be expected from the Jhajjar plant, and what utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 utilisation not above 20-25%; FY28 40-50% with around INR 500 crore revenue targeted. Steady-state EBITDA margin 14-15%, with C&I focus preferred over utility BESS.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further equity dilution or significant borrowing over the next 1.5-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no equity dilution is planned for at least the next year; the Bihar debt sits in an SPV, and the INR 43 crore warrant issue is for working capital. Any future dilution would be tied to a major expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivables position and realisation timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables fell from INR 254 crore (March) to INR 231 crore (June) and dropped further by mid-August. Management expects about half to be collected by end-Q2, with most of the Solarium EPC realised in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on order inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited INR 1,090 crore order book and bids of INR 2,000+ crore under evaluation, and expects the non-developer order book to grow over the next year as qualifications and bid participation increase.

570004|2026-06.headline: Jain Irrigation Q1 FY27 revenue fell ~2.5% to about Rs 1,500 crore, EBITDA margin dropped ~2 pts, and adjusted PAT was about Rs 3 crore versus Rs 30 crore a year ago.
570004|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was about Rs 1,500 crore, down roughly 2.5% YoY, with Hi-Tech degrowing, plastics flat and Agro-Processing growing on beverages and overseas sales. EBITDA fell on lower standalone India fixed-cost absorption, weaker Hi-Tech volumes and negative forex, while plastics margin improved. Management said April was weak but May, June and July improved, and it expects a stronger second half. Rs 164 crore of EBITDA was converted to cash at about 78%, and net working capital days fell to 183 from 210 a year ago. Rs 680-690 crore of NCDs fall due in September (about Rs 230 crore) and March; management says these will be met from internal cash flow with refinancing and other options in progress.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (ex non-cash NCD interest unwinding)
financial_highlights.change: vs about Rs 30 crore last year
from 210 days in June 2025 and 186 days in March 2026
receivables down about Rs 25 crore vs March

segments.commentary: Revenue down about 22% YoY; retail down 17% (MIS down 16% to Rs 368 crore, tissue culture down 10%) and project down 63%. Margin fell from 16.6% to 14.4%; management guides to double-digit growth for FY27.

segments.name: Plastics
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly flat YoY, with overseas plastics revenue up about 40%. EBITDA margin improved to about 11% from 10%.

segments.name: Agro-Processing (food)
segments.commentary: Grew significantly on beverages (about Rs 60 crore in the quarter) and overseas sales; EBITDA lower on seasonality and margin down about 3 pts.

Hi-Tech expected to deliver double-digit revenue growth in FY27, with solar pump billing to pick up from September.

Dividends expected from next year (FY28) as standalone India business generates positive cash flow.
Tamil Nadu land monetisation expected to be delivered in the current quarter, per management.
capex_capacity: Biochar plant recently started, using agri-waste (corn cob, cotton stalk, mango stones); impact on numbers expected from next fiscal.
Coffee Board first orders received; revenue has started.
Large Pune water-supply project still needs triple-digit billing; other projects about 98-99% complete with about Rs 40-50 crore billing left.
About 10-12 of 72 projects carry O&M over the next two to three years; management says O&M spend is light.
demand_pricing: Polymer prices rose about 50%; management says most increases were passed on to customers, and customers deferred purchases until prices ease.
Delayed monsoon onset in June hit farm purchases; July rainfall was good and July revenue grew versus April-June.

Institutional demand for larger-diameter pipes is being negotiated.

qa_highlights.question: How much legacy government receivable will be collected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about Rs 422 crore for FY27, with Rs 60 crore received in Q1 and at least Rs 380 crore expected in the remaining nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any risk of write-offs on project receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no material write-offs are expected; provisions were made in earlier review and the remaining good receivables will be collected.

qa_highlights.question: Why are standalone working capital requirements higher than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to long-tail legacy project receivables and state-government orders on behalf of farmers, which are paid in six months to one year. Expects improvement from FY28 once project receivables clear.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the delay in the food business IPO?

qa_highlights.question: Why was Hi-Tech margin down and what is the full-year view?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the receivables are over 180 days?

Recovery of Rs 380 crore of legacy government receivables in nine months; about 55% of net receivables (about Rs 1,100 crore) are above 180 days.
Polymer price volatility and oil/geopolitical risk could delay customer purchases.
Monsoon progress in August-September, which management says is critical for H2 volumes.
Food business IPO and PE exit timing with no confirmed date; Tamil Nadu land sale repeatedly delayed.
Whether the H2 margin catch-up materialises; Q1 adjusted PAT was about Rs 3 crore.

543260|2026-06.headline: Stove Kraft Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 41.3% YoY to INR480.6 crore, with EBITDA up 50.9% to INR53.8 crore and margin at 11.2%.

demand_pricing: Induction cooktop demand remains above pre-war levels; management expects traction to continue but not at the initial spike levels.
Cost-plus pricing model: domestic price increases taken and export buying prices revised upward to pass on input cost inflation.
Gross margin improvement attributed to price corrections and a favourable mix, including stainless steel pressure cookers outgrowing aluminium.
Q1 exchange-offer programme (mainly in EBOs and general trade) cited as a regular seasonal driver; GPOs up about 80% and general trade up about 50%.
Festive calendar spread across Q2 and Q3 (Onam in August, Dussehra in early October, Diwali in November).
South region about 50% of general trade contribution; North and West growing faster from a smaller base.
Working capital: inventory build-up for festive season; management plans straight-line production through the year to smooth working capital.

Other expenses rose to about 18% of sales, driven by job work (+1.2 pp), marketing (+1.2 pp; spend about 3.5-3.6% of sales), franchise commission (about 1% of sales; franchise mix 55-56% vs 43%), and CSR front-loading (about INR94 lakh, about 3% of PBT).

532178|2026-06.headline: Engineers India Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 55% to INR109 crores, while turnover fell 7% to INR801 crores on Turnkey decline.
532178|2026-06.overview: Standalone PBT rose about 55% YoY to INR145 crores and PAT to INR109 crores, helped by Consultancy growth of about 22% to INR499 crores. Turnkey turnover fell to INR302 crores from INR449 crores as major projects tapered. Order book stood at INR14,424 crores at 30 June 2026, but Q1 order inflow was only INR514 crores. Management kept the INR8,000 crore FY27 order inflow target and the FY27 operating margin guidance of 16%, and said the Middle East new-mega-project pipeline has slowed.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR104 crores, 11.72% in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR14,424 crores (Consultancy INR10,498 crores; Turnkey INR3,926 crores)

segments.name: Consultancy & Engineering
segments.commentary: Turnover INR499 crores, up ~22% YoY; segment profit margin rose to ~24% from 17% in Q1 FY26, with management targeting 24-25%.

segments.name: Turnkey (LSTK)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR302 crores, down from INR449 crores as major projects tapered; segment margin ~7.5% in Q1 FY27. New Turnkey orders are in early execution, with turnover expected to rise in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: CEIL subsidiary
segments.commentary: Profit INR6.88 crores vs INR2.69 crores a year earlier.

segments.name: Joint ventures / associates
segments.commentary: Contributed INR42.51 crores to consolidated profit vs a loss of INR7.37 crores in Q1 FY26. RFCL contributed about INR42 crores of revenue-linked profit; management expects some dividend from RFCL this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow target of INR8,000 crores maintained; management said it will try to cross it. Current inflow is about INR2,750 crores (about INR1,100 crores overseas, about INR1,500 crores domestic, of which ~INR1,500 crores domestic is LSTK and the rest consultancy).
FY27 consultancy revenue targeted at more than 50%, possibly around 55%, implying consultancy turnover of INR2,300-2,400 crores.
Total FY27 turnover growth target of at least 10% on last year's INR3,850-4,200 crore base; management said guidance could improve.
FY27 operating margin target held at 16%, same as FY26; upside possible if pending change orders are settled.
FY28 revenue target of INR5,000 crores maintained, with an intent to improve it.
Dividend payout of around 100% for the current financial year referenced.
capex_capacity: Company is setting up a CBG plant with its own investment (non-hydrocarbon).
RFCL plant expected to run about 330 days a year; a 30-35 day regular shutdown in December will carry technical work without hitting profitability.
No specific capex amounts or commissioning dates were given for other projects.
demand_pricing: Middle East: new mega projects on hold or slow; existing jobs continuing. Secured about INR500 crores of Middle East business in Q1, including PMC work of INR400 crores under long-term agreements. Aramco contract in place but no major inquiry yet.
Overseas share of current inflow is about INR1,100 crores out of INR2,750 crores.
Nuclear: environmental studies for 3 private projects and 1 government project; engaged with NPCIL on engineering consultancy; SMR work secured last year.
Coal gasification: government VGF support of INR34,000 crores revived feasibility inquiries; an NTPC gas-to-SNG project is ongoing; results expected in a couple of months.
Domestic pipeline: BPCL Andhra execution tender may come by year-end; IOCL Paradip Phase 2 awaits OMC approval; ONGC petrochemical project only at feasibility stage.
Infrastructure about 45% of business in the current year, mostly LSTK/OBE, with a recent data-centre assignment from PowerTel.
Competition described as high in all segments, with most work won through competitive bidding.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR8,000 crore order inflow target still achievable, and how much would be consultancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is unchanged, with about INR2,750 crores in hand now and about two quarters left. Consultancy is about INR1,100 crores of this, with the rest mainly LSTK domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be write-backs or change orders this year, including HPCL Barmer?
qa_highlights.answer: No exceptional change order is in the current quarter and no provision write-backs are expected; provisions reverse only after the defect liability period ends.

qa_highlights.question: How should consultancy growth and margins be modelled for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Consultancy growth target is at least 10%+ overall, with consultancy above 50% of turnover; segment profit is targeted at 24-25%. Operating margin target is 16%, with possible upside from change orders.

qa_highlights.question: Have Middle East clients put projects on hold due to the conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no existing project is stopped; new mega projects are on hold or slow, and routine jobs continue.

qa_highlights.question: How will revenue be recognised on the Dangote Nigeria order?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised on cost-progress basis, with turnover booked as cost progress is achieved over about 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan to distribute surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no plans to distribute the full reserves now, as other investment plans are under consideration, and pointed to about 100% dividend this year.

risks_watch: Turnkey turnover fell 33% YoY; management expects recovery in Q3-Q4 but this depends on execution of new projects still in early phase.
Q1 order inflow of INR514 crores is far below the run rate needed for INR8,000 crores; the target depends on a few lumpy domestic and overseas wins.
Middle East (about 12-15% exposure per analyst estimate) faces slow new mega-project awards; Saudi/Aramco work still at initial discussion stage.
Q1 operating margin of ~14% is below the 16% full-year target, so the guidance depends on later quarters and change-order settlements.
Coal gasification and nuclear inquiries remain at feasibility or EOI stage; timing and value of awards unclear.
Management did not confirm the Turnkey-to-consultancy mix beyond ranges given, and gave conflicting statements on the consultancy share (50-60%, around 55%).
532178|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on consultancy margins, growth and dividends, but cautious on the Middle East and on new mega-project awards. Several answers were vague or shifting, notably on the consultancy mix, the margin target and the order-inflow path.

541974|2026-06.headline: Manorama Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39.5% YoY to INR 404 crore and PAT rose 67.6% to INR 79 crore, with PAT margin at 19.5%.
541974|2026-06.overview:
Revenue grew 39.5% YoY to INR 404 crore, crossing INR 400 crore for the first time, with management attributing growth mainly to volume (about 85% YoY per management). EBITDA rose 42.2% to INR 106 crore at a 26.3% margin, and PAT rose 67.6% to INR 79 crore. Management said the QIP of about INR 500 crore has closed and it has lined up a ~INR 460 crore capex plan spanning India and Burkina Faso, with commissioning targeted around Q3 FY28. Several answers were qualitative or deferred, notably on guidance, Brazil revenue, and subsidiary losses.</overview>

segments.name: Value-added specialty fats (CBE and stearin)
segments.commentary: Management said CBE is about 30% and stearin about 70% of the contribution from these products; per-ton realisations were not shared, but pricing was described as largely stable.

segments.name: Subsidiaries (consolidated vs standalone)
segments.commentary: Consolidated PAT loss narrowed to about INR 3 crore from about INR 8 crore in Q4 FY26, with negligible subsidiary revenue; West African entities are sourcing vehicles and Brazil is in build-out.

guidance_outlook: FY27 utilisation guidance is about 80% (management internal target 80-85%) on expanded capacity of about 52,000 tonnes per annum after 4,500 t debottlenecking; the company declined to restate the INR 1,600-1,800 crore revenue guidance from November, pointing to utilisation metrics instead.
FY27 capex guidance of about INR 225-250 crore; about INR 70 crore spent to date and about INR 220 crore more planned in FY27.

Gross margin expected in a 45-50% range, with EBITDA margin the preferred tracking metric; management said margins should hold broadly stable at current range, with quarter-to-quarter movement possible.

Burkina Faso facility (about INR 120-130 crore) has an estimated payback of about 3 years once operational; the remainder of the ~INR 460 crore plan is for India (solvent fractionation 3 and refinery).
Solvent fractionation 3 and refinery targeted for commissioning around Q3 FY28; full impact expected in FY29 as plants ramp up.
Balance sheet: no further equity dilution planned; working capital to be funded via existing banker lines led by SBI, plus ~INR 150 crore FDR outside the QIP proceeds.
capex_capacity: Current fractionation capacity 47,500 t per annum; additional 7,500 t already operational, with a further 4,500 t debottlenecking targeted around Q3 FY27, taking capacity to about 52,000 t.
Debottlenecking cost estimated at INR 5-6 crore.

Burkina Faso: about 10 hectares (24 acres) land acquired for shea nut and mango nut processing with regulatory approvals pending; facility covers extraction and expelling, solvent fractionation and related capacity, about INR 120-130 crore.
Overall proposed capex plan about INR 460 crore; about INR 70 crore spent to date; Q1 spend about INR 20 crore across Manorama and subsidiaries.
Brazil (LatAm) partner: trial production started in the last quarter; ramp-up expected gradually over the next 2-4 quarters, with production sourced from the Indian plant.
Asset turn currently about 7x; management would not guide to 7x-9x going forward.
demand_pricing: Demand described as volume-led; management attributed about 85% YoY growth to volume.
Pricing described as largely stable for value-added products, in line with the costing model that passes through raw material inflation.
Raw material mix: about 50-60% imported seeds and butters, the rest domestic seeds (sal, mango) and butters.
Contracts are 9-12 months and renew on a rolling basis; no renewal percentage was disclosed.
Nigeria's temporary shea nut export ban was called non-material given sourcing across about 10 African subsidiaries.
Exports to more than 30 countries; export share about 55-60% in Q1 FY25 and 60% in Q1 FY27 per management.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of the 4,500 t debottlenecking and greenfield capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Debottlenecking is due around Q3 FY27; solvent fractionation 3 and refinery are targeted around Q3 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Brazil ramp-up and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production started; gradual quarter-on-quarter ramp expected over 2-4 quarters; no revenue guidance given yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall about 20% QoQ, and is it the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior quarter included a performance incentive provision; run-rate guided at INR 14-15 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline and raw material cost ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin expected at 45-50%; management disputed the 75-80% H1 raw material ratio, saying it has been about 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated subsidiary losses and whether they will narrow?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses reflect operating costs of sourcing vehicles and Brazil build-out; drag expected to reduce as entities scale, with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Utilisation guidance versus the 85-90% cited in the presentation?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal target 80-85%; 80% advised for stakeholders, with upside to be communicated if achieved.

qa_highlights.question: Funding of working capital for the new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Funded by existing bank lines (SBI lead), the QIP of about INR 500 crore and FDR of about INR 150 crore; no further equity dilution planned.

risks_watch: Supplier dispute: a debit note has been raised for the full claim amount against a foreign manufacturer/supplier, with no recovery timeline or confirmation of liability given.
Geopolitical and freight disruption; management said freight and container costs drove the 16% jump in other expenses.
Utilisation target ambiguity (80% vs 85-90%) and withdrawal of the INR 1,600-1,800 crore revenue guidance.
Subsidiary and Brazil losses weigh on consolidated margins; timing of breakeven undisclosed.
Working capital needs for new capacity (analyst estimate INR 900-1,000 crore) and reliance on bank lines.
Hedging policy of 50-60% of net exposure; forex gains formed about INR 13 crore of the INR 16 crore other income, so the earnings quality of other income is a watch item.
541974|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on headline growth and capacity build-out, but evasive on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to quantify margins, revenue guidance, Brazil contribution, subsidiary breakeven, and per-ton realisations, redirecting to utilisation and "business has risk" framing.

538734|2026-06.headline: Ceinsys Q1 FY27 revenue flat at INR158 crore (+1% YoY) but EBITDA rose 27% to INR39 crore, margin 24.4%; order book INR990 crore.
538734|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating revenue was INR158 crore, up about 1% YoY, while EBITDA grew 27% to INR39 crore and margin expanded 505 bps to 24.4%. PAT was INR31 crore, a marginal decline, with PAT margin at 19.6% (down about 59 bps). Order inflow was INR143 crore against about INR157 crore executed, lifting the order book to INR990 crore from INR880 crore. Management withheld forward guidance throughout, citing policy, and focused on receivables recovery (JJM dues), a proposed AI cloud JV, and undeployed funds from the earlier fundraise.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR880 crore in Q4 FY26
broadly flat vs prior two quarters (162-164 days)

segments.name: Geospatial Engineering Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR94 crore, up 30% YoY; majority of the INR143 crore fresh order inflow came from geospatial enterprise solutions. Management said the mix shifts with project execution phase.

segments.name: Technology Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue INR63 crore, down about 25% YoY. Management aims to take this segment beyond 51% of segment revenue.

segments.name: Mobility (incl. international subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Mobility is now a division after the Allygrow merger; management reported improving order book and a top-line increase and margin improvement at the US subsidiary. Mobility is run-rate and not built into the order book.

guidance_outlook: No forward guidance given on revenue, margins or order inflow, citing company policy.
Management said growth should show in the next 2-3 quarters as orders with 3-6 month execution convert, and expects to sustain the growth trend seen over the last 2.5 years.
Management said it is on track with order book milestones and believes margins of around 22-23% are achievable, citing the 24.4% in Q1.
Management expects a better operating cash flow in FY27 than in FY26, without quantifying it.
Expected collection of about INR100 crore of JJM/IoT dues by end of Q3 FY27, with overdues expected to be cleared before 31 March 2027 per the Maharashtra GR.
Management expects one large national-program order (similar to the earlier INR350-400 crore L1 opportunities) possibly in FY27 Q4 or Q1 FY28, and said two L1 positions were pending award.
capex_capacity: Board approved up to INR25 crore investment in a 50:50 JV with AI Fabric USA for a sovereign AI cloud (GPU-as-a-service, model-as-a-service, AI services); first tranche INR5 crore for incorporation, second INR20 crore after due diligence.
JV incorporation expected in about 1-1.5 months; due diligence (technical, market) to take 3-4 months; business model to be frozen after that, with commercial activity indicated for FY28.
Management said it is evaluating acquisitions, aiming for vertical integration and margin-accretive deals; no deal announced. Acquisition multiples cited at 5-10x EBITDA.
Around INR230 crore raised earlier, of which INR130 crore received in March 2026 and INR100 crore in September 2024 (per management clarification).
demand_pricing: Order book INR990 crore; execution timelines range from 3 to 18 months, with some O&M contracts running 2-5 years. Weighted average execution 12-18 months.

Run-rate businesses (mobility, OEM products and services) sit outside the order book; about INR50 crore of Q1 revenue came from these. Management estimated 20-25% of FY26 revenue (of INR660 crore) was outside the order book.

Key Q1/recent wins: INR67 crore Madhya Pradesh PMAY manpower/LoI (over 3 years); INR17 crore Bhandara Municipal Council AMRUT 2.0 smart water meters (12 months); INR4 crore EKS InTec order; INR4 crore US subsidiary order; INR30 crore aggregate T Second purchase orders.

Management said JJM-related bids are being deprioritised in favour of transport (ITMS/ATMS), energy and other geospatial opportunities where budgets are funded. Transport positive developments expected in 1-2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the execution timeline of the INR990 crore order book and the funnel outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution spans 3 to 18 months, with O&M extending to 5 years; weighted average 12-18 months. Management said the funnel is strong and it will not give a numeric funnel figure or guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the order book roll-forward not match inflow minus revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said run-rate businesses (about INR50 crore of Q1 revenue) are not booked in the order book. Net order book increased about INR110 crore after INR157 crore of execution. Reconciliation to be sent via the IR agency.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI cloud JV economics and will Ceinsys be an EPC player?
qa_highlights.answer: The JV is 50:50 with AI Fabric USA, targeting defence and government sovereign cloud. Management said it intends to be an AI solutions company, not EPC, with contractors used for construction.

qa_highlights.question: What are the receivables and JJM dues outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle at 164 days, flat. About INR100 crore of IoT/JJM dues expected by end of Q3 FY27, per the Maharashtra GR. Management said billing is being collected with no new build-up.

qa_highlights.question: Are large orders (INR350-400 crore L1 positions) likely by Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: INR67 crore order already received. Two more in process, with one possibly in Q2. Management declined to commit on timing but said tender pipeline remains strong, and a large national program order could come in 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why not a share buyback given idle funds and low valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said buybacks are funded from surplus operating cash, and the raised funds are for growth. Management said it would not invest only to deploy capital; acquisitions must preserve margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why is unbilled revenue high and when will it convert?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the large unbilled revenue (about INR320 crore at 31 March, per the analyst) is mainly JJM; it is expected to be billed and reduce over the next 2 quarters as government funds come in.

533581|2026-06.headline: PG Electroplast Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 35.2% YoY to INR2,034 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.7% amid commodity and rupee pressure.
533581|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue crossed INR2,000 crore for the first time, up 35.2% YoY, with EBITDA up 12.1% to INR156.2 crore and net profit up 12.9% to INR75.3 crore. Growth came from double-digit volume growth plus a similar ASP increase as copper, aluminium and resin costs and rupee depreciation were partly passed through. Gross margin percentage softened QoQ and YoY, which management attributed to pass-through mechanics rather than per-unit erosion. The company reports a net cash position, and the compressor, refrigerator and washing machine capacity build-out is the main medium-term theme.</overview>

segments.name: Room AC
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,401 crore, up 38.1% YoY; volume up about 20-22% and ASP up about 10-12% YoY. Management guided roughly 20% plus volume growth for the full year.

segments.name: Washing machine
segments.commentary: Revenue INR211 crore, up 67.2% YoY; fully automatic machines grew about 150% YoY. Resin cost pass-through lagged in the quarter, with management calling the margin impact much larger than 20-30 bps.

segments.name: Coolers
segments.commentary: Revenue almost INR19 crore, up 3.4% YoY.

segments.name: Electronics (EMS)
segments.commentary: 5.3% of revenue, up 65.3% YoY; largely job work with stable margins per management.

segments.name: Plastic moulding and components
segments.commentary: Revenue INR294.6 crore, up 7% YoY; job-work style model where customers specify resin sourcing, so limited margin impact.

segments.name: Goodworth Electronics (JV)
segments.commentary: Sales INR177.3 crore vs INR147.5 crore last year; EBITDA INR6.3 crore vs INR4.3 crore.

segments.name: PG Technoplast (wholly-owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Reported sales of about INR1,600 crore for the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Operating margin aspiration of about 8% for full FY27; management stated this is not guidance and the Q1 operating margin was about 7.3%.
Management expects FY27 earnings to surpass FY25 levels if second-half sales are good.
Full-year volume growth of about 20%+ expected in base case, with 4-5% upside versus industry growth if the compressor plant ramps.
Price increases of roughly 10-15% expected for brands post GST cut, with the next pass-through targeted for the December quarter.
Management expects 25-30% growth in FY27-FY28 and sees no growth challenge for the next 2-3 years; FY29 may be a consolidation year.
AC share of sales expected to fall from 60-65% to 50-55% over 2-3 years.
Management declined to give revenue guidance, quarterly guidance, or FY27 capex detail beyond INR400 crore for the year.
capex_capacity: Washing machine plant in DMIC Greater Noida is online with 1.8 million units annual capacity; total washing machine capacity to reach about 3 million. Target utilisation of 70-80% by FY28.

Refrigerator plant at Sri City (1.2 million units) targeted for commercial production in Q4 FY27; anchor customer tied up with about 30-35% capacity commitment. Phase 1 covers direct-cool and side-by-side models; frost-free and multi-door follow in phase 2.

Compressor plant at Supa: first 2 million-unit line on track for mass production in December-January; commissioning took about 6 months. Second line planned for April-May 2027 decision, with about 3-4 months lead time; the land and building can accommodate 4 lines.
Compressor economics: one line at 80% utilisation is about 1.6-1.7 million units at about INR2,850-2,900 per unit; Indian compressor prices cited at INR2,800-3,000.
FY27 capex about INR400 crore, mainly completing compressor and refrigerator projects, plus a new land parcel at Salarpur to consolidate plastic moulding operations from Greater Noida.
PG Technoplast Rajasthan facility is coming online. Management targets fixed asset turn above 4x.
demand_pricing: Industry RAC primary sales grew about 15% YoY in Q1; with ASP growth of 10-12%, primary value growth was about 20-25%. Secondary sales were reportedly better than primary, with channel and brand inventory near normal (estimated 4.5-5.5 million units).
Management expects RAC outsourcing share to keep rising; brands are using outsourcing to protect margins amid high competition.
Price hikes in July-September have had limited success; some brands took and rolled back increases.

Copper above $14,000/tonne versus $7,000-8,000 earlier; rupee around INR95.5-96/USD. Management said commodity pass-through remains incomplete.
Imports of inner grooved copper tubing (IGT) to be restricted from November.

qa_highlights.question: What was the RAC volume and ASP split, and how much of the commodity cost increase has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: RAC volume grew about 20-22% and ASP about 10-12%. Management said pass-through was partial, varied by customer, and a further price increase is expected from the December quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company near normal margins, and can it return to 10% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to a 10% margin, saying the business is per-piece priced. It expects per-piece margins to normalise and operating margins ex-PLI to improve significantly, with a reported margin slightly above last year.

qa_highlights.question: How much is compressor capex and what margin will compressors add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex split by segment would be shared offline, and total FY27 capex is about INR400 crore. Compressors are expected to be margin-additive as the first line mainly serves in-house AC needs.

qa_highlights.question: What was washing machine utilisation before the new plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier capacity ran at about 70% annualised utilisation, with peak months above 100%. Target is 70-80% on the expanded capacity by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of rising inventory values and the working capital build?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5 lakh AC inventory is now about INR940 crore versus about INR700 crore last year, reflecting commodity inflation and strategic stocking of compressors and IGT. Inventory was about INR100 crore lower than planned due to June softness.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order book available?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not share order book numbers. The AC season order book is not yet rebuilt and will start building in September-October for the December season; washing machine volume commitments exist but are not disclosed.

532900|2026-06.headline: Paisalo Q1 FY27: record disbursement of Rs.17,309 million (+128% YoY), PAT up 30% to Rs.613 million, gross NPA 0.70%.
532900|2026-06.overview: Management, represented solely by Deputy MD Santanu Agarwal (CFO unavailable), reported AUM of Rs.67,074 million (+28% YoY) and a record quarterly disbursement of Rs.17,309 million. Total income rose 19% YoY to Rs.2,603 million and PAT rose 30% YoY to Rs.613 million, with gross NPA at 0.70% and net NPA at 0.49%. Management set a three-year ambition to roughly double AUM, income and profitability, and launched a Rs.300 crore NCD tranche under a Rs.900 crore shelf. Sequential metrics were weaker in several places: interest expense rose and opex fell sharply QoQ, and loan-loss provisions jumped, which management attributed to timing and settlement effects.

financial_highlights.change: expected to stay slightly higher short term

segments.name: Lending (MSME / micro-enterprise)
segments.commentary: AUM mix in Q1: food and hospitality about 23%, agri and allied agri about 15%, street vendors about 16%; vehicle, health, education and textile each about 3-6%. Internal cap is 25% per industry.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Touch points rose to 5,995 across 23 states from 5,299 a quarter earlier (+696 over four quarters per management). BC franchise crossed USD 1 billion gross transaction value.

segments.name: New product lines
segments.commentary: Six new product lines added in the last quarter across mobility, industrial, medical, agri equipment and alternative fuel; too early to set mix targets.

guidance_outlook: Ambition to approximately double AUM, income and profitability over three fiscal years.
Quarterly growth may normalise from the high base, but management expects healthy momentum through FY27.
Cost-to-income ratio to stay slightly higher in the short to medium term during the AI transition.
Co-lending with SBI remains at status quo, awaiting compliance on the bank side; treated as optionality not included in guidance.
Three new development products to launch around end-Q3 FY27; AI outbound calling for new-to-Paisalo customers to start around then.
Internal leverage comfort around 3.5x against a regulatory limit of 7x; about $44 million of FCCBs pending conversion, with a committee meeting scheduled.
risks_watch: Interest cost (Rs.115 crore per the questioner's reading, up from Rs.87 crore QoQ) and sharp opex fall (Rs.69 crore to Rs.46 crore) partly unexplained; management cites timing lag between funding and deployment.

New product lines (six added recently) have short track records; risks not yet quantified.

532900|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, distribution and AI; repeated the 'strongest quarter yet' framing. Evasive or deflecting on sequential cost, interest and provision questions, which were answered with timing explanations and without quantified guidance.

544479|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10.5% QoQ to INR161 crore, but gross margin fell 240 bps to 39.5% and EBITDA margin to 14.3% on polymer cost spikes.
544479|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR161 crore (up 10.5% QoQ, up 2% YoY) and polymers processed rose 25% QoQ to 6,323 MT, with utilisation at 64.9%. Raw material costs rose 40-50% from the West Asia crisis, compressing gross margin to 39.5% from 41.9%, with price pass-through partial and time-lagged. Management says the pass-through is largely complete in domestic and is contracted for most exports, with the largest customer's benefit landing in Q2 FY27. Supply-chain disruption (inbound material, containers, logistics) was the main drag, with about INR5.5 crore of sales slipping into July.

segments.commentary: About 19% of Q1 FY27 revenue vs about 12% for FY26; management cites new product inquiries and a further large opportunity under discussion.

guidance_outlook: FY27 utilisation target of about 75% on 41,000 MT capacity for the remaining nine months, described as a working assumption dependent on the geopolitical environment.
FY27 revenue/volume growth of at least 15-20% per CFO, backed by order book; EBITDA expected to improve if growth is delivered, but no margin guidance given.
Gross margin and EBITDA recovery expected once raw material environment normalises; management says Q2 FY27 will show full benefit of largest-customer price revision.

Bamboo: Phase 1 at Guwahati (3,000 CBM) machinery arriving mid-August, installation by end-September, commercial contribution from Q4 FY27; Q4 revenue estimated at about 20% of annual run-rate at 75% utilisation. Capex about INR15 crore for Phase 1, may rise for next phase.
Management says EBITDA margin of 18-19% (FY24-FY25) is sustainable at around 80% utilisation; FY27 margin to be better than FY26 but no specific range committed.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity about 41,000 MT (management also cited 39,000 MT base in opening remarks); utilisation 64.9% in Q1 FY27.
14 new injection moulding machines ordered for about 1,500 MT incremental capacity, arriving Q3 and fully available in Q4 FY27.

A further about 4,000 MT is planned, to be ordered in Q3 with receipt by end of Q4 FY27 if demand confirms; management deferred commitment to pick the right equipment for large-customer projects. Earlier plan was about 6,000 MT in a year.
Bamboo board unit at Madanpur, Guwahati (75,000 sq ft, owned by All-Time Bamboo Pvt Ltd): 3,000 CBM per annum in Phase 1; downstream finishing at Khatalwada, Gujarat.
Khatalwada expansion has raised fixed costs; management says these will be absorbed as utilisation improves.
demand_pricing: Raw material (polymer) costs rose 40-50% over base at peak; management said raw material is about 50-53% of product mix. Selling prices rose about 15% against roughly 20% input impact at a 40% mix.
Domestic: 100% of price increase passed through; largest customer on an eight-week lag, with benefit in Q2 FY27; remaining customers about 50% passed through, with the balance over a longer period.
Management says demand and forecasts have held; supply availability, logistics and raw material inbound were the constraints in April-May, with June improving.
Competition: management views smaller unorganised players under working-capital stress as an opening; large retailers are increasingly focusing on brand and packaging quality.
Bamboo: management says no cannibalisation of plastic business as price points and end consumers differ; bamboo margins are a few points above plastic.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR5 crore of shipment slippage a lost sale or does it carry into subsequent months?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a loss; management quantified about INR5.5 crore (INR3 crore in transit plus INR2.5 crore at factory containers) to be recognised in July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 75% utilisation target on 39,000 or 41,000 MT?
qa_highlights.answer: On 41,000 MT for the remaining nine months of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 employee expense a fair run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, Q1 is a fair base; any increase will be very small.

qa_highlights.question: Why is volume growth only about 5% QoQ on sales volume, and when does price pass-through show up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is not the issue; raw material availability and logistics were. Q2 should show better demand and the pending price pass-through; one quarter of exceptional pricing growth after normalisation is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the remaining 4,000 MT capacity delayed and what is the domestic growth driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a visibility issue; equipment choice depends on customer product lines. Domestic was flat because a full price reset was sought and production was halted, with the largest customer's expansion (20-25 stores in two years, about INR40-50 lakh revenue per store per month) cited as a driver.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15-20% growth achievable, and how will margins move?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said EBITDA will improve if growth comes, but declined to commit to a margin figure; the historical gross margin range is 39-40%.

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margin return to 18-19%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said at around 80% capacity utilisation, which it considers sustainable.

524000|2026-06.headline: Poonawalla Fincorp Q1 FY27 PAT rose 20.8% QoQ to ₹308 crores, ROA 1.98%, GNPA down to 1.37%, AUM ₹67,054 crores (+11% QoQ).
524000|2026-06.overview: AUM grew 11.1% QoQ to ₹67,054 crores, with retail products driving growth and new products reaching 26% of disbursements. Profitability improved: PAT ₹308 crores (+20.8% QoQ, +391.5% YoY), ROA 1.98% (up 17 bps QoQ), and pre-provisioning operating profit ₹785 crores (+12.9% QoQ). Asset quality improved on all measured metrics, with GNPA at 1.37% (vs 1.44% in Q4), NNPA at 0.70%, and quarterly credit cost at 2.4% (vs 2.51%). Management attributed margin gains to a ~50 bps rise in disbursement yield from product mix, and guided to a June 2028 exit ROA of 3-3.5%.

524000|2026-09.headline: Poonawalla Fincorp Q2 FY27: PAT up 22% QoQ to ₹375 crore, ROA 2.18%, credit cost down to 2.19%, AUM ₹74,008 crore.
524000|2026-09.overview:

NIM plus fees rose 16 bps QoQ to 9.26%, while credit cost fell to 2.19% from 2.40-2.41% and GNPA fell to 1.20% from 1.37%. qa_highlights.question: Sensitivity of borrowing cost to a 50 bps repo hike and fixed vs floating mix?

540073|2026-06.headline: BLS International Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25% to INR 891 crores, a record, with EBITDA of INR 252 crores (28.3% margin) and PAT of INR 202 crores.
540073|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a record quarter for BLS on revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with growth coming from both Visa & Consular and Digital Services. Visa application volumes were flat at 11.3 lakh, and growth came from net revenue per application rising 11% to INR 3,521. Digital Services grew 32% to INR 330 crores, with EBITDA up 45% to INR 27 crores. Net cash stood at INR 1,617 crores. Management was firm on a 15-20% organic growth target over five years, but gave no clear answer on buybacks or on the return from past acquisitions.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 330 crores (+32% from INR 250 crores), EBITDA INR 27 crores (+45% from INR 18 crores), margin 8.2% vs 7.2%. Growth led by business correspondent (BC) and loan distribution. BC GTV above INR 29,500 crores vs INR 26,200 crores a year ago.

segments.commentary: iDATA INR 72.5 crores, Aadifidelis INR 225 crores, Citizenship Invest INR 17.5 crores (vs INR 11 crores a year ago), Aadhaar INR 17.5 crores, UK hotel INR 16 crores (vs INR 2.5 crores). Management described the Citizenship growth as partly driven by Middle East NRI demand.

guidance_outlook: Organic growth target of 15-20% a year over the next five years on the increased base; management said Q1 (25% revenue, ~24% EBITDA growth) was ahead of this.
Management intends to hold Visa margin near 40% and Digital margin around 8%; it did not give a separate consolidated margin guidance beyond the 28.3% achieved.

Effective tax rate expected to close FY27 at about 12%. D&A may rise slightly next quarter before stabilising.
capex_capacity: Aadhaar project: about INR 75 crores invested so far against a total of about INR 125 crores; phase 2 in final stages and full investment expected to finish next quarter.
Visa & Consular platform: Belarus visa applications launched in Mumbai; AI-powered 24/7 bot rolled out across missions.
Atyati Technologies acquisition completed (about INR 138 crores). It had about INR 275 crores revenue and INR 20-21 crores EBITDA last year, with BC and bank/NBFC software verticals.
Management said about INR 1,100 crores was invested in acquisitions last year and that M&A remains the first use of cash while the pipeline is active.
demand_pricing: Visa application volumes were flat YoY at 11.3 lakh; management attributed this to the war affecting Q1 and said growth came from other contracts. It said the war is now over and volumes are recovering, but declined to give current-quarter numbers.

Management said it has won contracts with Belarus, Portugal, Slovakia and Italy governments, with multiple tenders at different stages in the pipeline over the next 8-12 months or more.

qa_highlights.question: How is capital allocated between M&A, core growth and shareholder returns, and what return threshold applies?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Amit Sudhakar listed organic expansion first, then M&A that improves ROI, then dividends. He said all M&A to date earns returns of 17-20%, which is the baseline. Management did not quantify the economic value created by past acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Will buybacks be considered given INR 1,617 crores net cash and reserves of about INR 2,500 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said M&A is the first priority, that buybacks and higher dividends are on the agenda, and that the Board will decide. It said a buyback is not currently under consideration but may be discussed at the next Board meeting.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue per application growth slow over the past year, and what revenue is at risk from contracts ending within 12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the step-up over three years came from moving to self-run operations, and that per-application revenue is now stabilising. It said some contracts are ending but new wins offset them, and it still expects 10-15% Visa growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the effective tax rate and D&A rise, and how long before Aadhaar revenue arrives?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax rate depends on the country profit mix; FY27 is expected near 12%. D&A rose mainly from Aadhaar investment under lease accounting. Full Aadhaar revenue is expected from Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Citizenship Invest revenue growth and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue rose to about INR 17.5 crores from INR 11 crores. Management attributed this to Middle East NRIs seeking permanent residency or citizenship in Europe and elsewhere, and said it should be maintainable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Visa gross profit per application fall as a share of revenue sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not reconcile the analyst's calculation (Visa gross profit about INR 400 crores, around 51%) and said it would review the working offline.
