qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance of ~10% EBITDA margin given in June if air freight pressures were already visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said transit times rose from 7 weeks assumed to 9-10 weeks; most air freight was incurred after the early-June call as the situation escalated in late June.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 39% growth came from higher metal prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR100-200 crore of revenue was due to higher metal prices on a consolidated basis; standalone raw-material impact about INR100 crore, with consolidated possibly INR10-15 crore higher.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 and full-year margin outlook and what is the path to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 margin would be between Q1 and H2 levels, with margins improving from Q3 as freight normalises and price revisions are realised; it expects to be confident of the trajectory if conditions hold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aluminium price assumption behind FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the ruling price around INR320/kg (approximately INR32,000 per tonne); raw-material impact estimated at INR200-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can the business reach INR4,000 crore revenue without major capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR4,000 crore plus is achievable with the current setup, with die investments largely recovered upfront from customers except for Maruti and Hero, which pay via piece price.

qa_highlights.question: Will hedging be used to manage aluminium volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company does not bank on commodities; the focus is on passing through raw-material cost via real-time settlements to eliminate the lag.

risks_watch: Air freight and sorting costs (INR12.8-13 crore in Q1) may persist into Q2; recovery from one customer (about 50% of freight) is not yet booked.
Customer settlement timing: 25% of customers not yet on real-time settlement; overseas customers may take longer to accept inflation-related price revisions.
Aluminium price volatility (about 57% higher YoY for a grade) and reliance on customer-led pricing; geopolitical risk (West Asia conflict) could extend shipping times.
Quality correlation issue with a major customer put some parts on hold; rust issues from prolonged sea transit required repacking.
Margin recovery to ~10% for FY27 requires about 12-13% in H2 per analyst's arithmetic; management has not given a quarterly margin figure.
Capex, land monetisation and railway/defence revenue numbers were not fully quantified on the call.

542904|2026-06.headline: Ujjivan SFB's MD and CEO Sanjeev Nautiyal retired early; Carol Furtado is Interim MD and management reiterated FY27 guidance with 29% loan growth.
542904|2026-06.overview: The call was an unscheduled management briefing on the early retirement of MD and CEO Sanjeev Nautiyal, whose health has been poor since mid-July. Whole-time Director Carol Furtado will act as Interim MD and CEO, subject to RBI approval, and the NRC has begun a successor search that the Chairman expects to finish in 3 to 4 months. Management cited Q1 FY27 loan book growth of about 29% YoY, GNPA of 2.2%, CASA growth of 38% YoY and cost of funds of 6.9%, and said FY27 guidance is unchanged. Management also said there is no material factor behind the exit beyond Nautiyal's health, and that El Nino is not currently affecting asset quality.

financial_highlights.metric: Secured book share of loan book

segments.name: Secured loan book
segments.commentary: Secured share of the loan book has moved past 50% as part of the diversification strategy; management said secured asset quality tracked in line with or better than Q1 post-quarter.

segments.name: Unsecured book
segments.commentary: Management said unsecured asset quality has tracked in line with or better than Q1 performance, with no deviation seen as of the call date.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Vikas Agarwal, a Chartered Accountant with over 25 years in MSME, business banking and retail, joins as Business Head, MSME; management said MSME plans are on track for FY27 and more detail will come in the Q2 call.

guidance_outlook: Management said the bank remains on track to meet FY27 guidance, with no change to the strategy previously communicated.
Asked whether a delayed capital raise would affect FY27 growth, Carol Furtado said the bank is well capitalised for FY27 growth plans and that a delay would not affect FY27 performance.
Management said the festive season looks promising, supported by capacity additions and a brand campaign planned for launch during the festive season.
Management declined to give a timeline for the transition to a universal bank, saying it is proceeding with the diversification strategy.
capex_capacity: Management referred to capacity additions supporting the festive-season outlook but gave no figures on capacity, capex or commissioning.
Management referred to strategic spends planned for FY27 without quantifying them.
demand_pricing: Management said liability and asset product performance has gained momentum, and that the market is under pressure on deposits, yet CASA grew 38% YoY.
No figures were given on pricing, yields or competition.

qa_highlights.question: Will a delayed capital raise after the management change affect growth over the next 2 to 3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Carol Furtado said the bank remains on track for FY27 guidance and is well capitalised for its FY27 growth plans, so a delay would not affect FY27 performance.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an early view on the successor, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman B.A. Prabhakar said the search started early, versus a planned October-November start, and names should go to the RBI in 3 to 4 months. He said the timing of joining was too early to say.

qa_highlights.question: Will internal candidates be considered, and will Carol Furtado be a candidate for permanent MD?
qa_highlights.answer: Prabhakar said internal candidates will be considered and that Furtado has expressed interest in a regular MD role.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any material reason for the abrupt exit beyond health?
qa_highlights.answer: Prabhakar said there was no issue with business strategy or bank operations and that the exit was Nautiyal's personal decision.

qa_highlights.question: Is El Nino affecting asset quality or growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Furtado said trends are in line with or better than Q1 for both secured and unsecured books and that no deviations are seen, with nothing material to report.

qa_highlights.question: What profile is sought for external candidates?
qa_highlights.answer: Prabhakar said the profile is still being worked out and will be shared later.

risks_watch: Leadership continuity: the MD and CEO search is expected to take 3 to 4 months to reach RBI submission, and a new MD may not join for several months after that.
Capital raise: the Board has approved a raise, but timing is now uncertain after the management change; management says FY27 is unaffected.
Universal bank transition: management declined to give a timeline, so this remains open.
El Nino and weather risk: management says there is no impact so far, but the issue was flagged earlier as a key monitorable for asset quality and growth.
MSME mix shift: new MSME head's impact on the business mix is not yet quantified.
542904|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on FY27 guidance and capital, but guarded on the succession timeline and the universal bank transition. Management repeated "on track" statements and declined to give detail on external candidate profiles and the transition timeline.
key_quotes: We remain on track to meet our FY27 guidance, and we are committed to delivering a strong performance.
No, absolutely, no. Absolutely no. I think it is his personal call.
Nothing. Absolutely nothing.

542649|2026-06.headline: RVNL Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA nearly doubled to INR 171 crore (margin 3.99% vs 2.08%) on turnover up 9.62% to INR 4,300 crore.
542649|2026-06.overview: Standalone turnover rose 9.62% YoY to INR 4,300 crore and consolidated turnover rose 10.55% to INR 4,321 crore. Standalone EBITDA more than doubled to INR 171 crore, with PAT up 21.72% to INR 155 crore. Order inflow in the quarter was INR 5,417 crore, taking the total order book to INR 93,492 crore as on 30 June 2026. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 15% top-line growth and 15-20% bottom-line growth, and flagged labour shortages, client payment delays and geopolitics as challenges.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 81 crore in Q1 FY26 (~+110% YoY)
vs INR 64.91 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Order book of about INR 58,000 crore, the largest component; management says about 42% of total order book is railway work awarded on management fee basis.

segments.name: S&P (as stated on call)
segments.commentary: Order book of about INR 12,000 crore.

segments.name: Metros
segments.commentary: Order book of about INR 5,700 crore.

segments.name: Power and transmission
segments.commentary: Order book of about INR 4,000 crore.

segments.name: Ports, roads and highways
segments.commentary: Order book of INR 3,651 crore; ports, hydro and highways are named as focus sectors for new orders.

segments.name: Hydro and irrigation
segments.commentary: Order book of INR 1,626 crore.

segments.name: Building works
segments.commentary: Contributed 31.51% of revenue from operations, up 16.63% from the previous year.

segments.name: Subsidiaries and JVs
segments.commentary: Subsidiaries contributed INR 126 crore to consolidated revenue and INR 12.70 crore to PAT; share of JV/associate profit was INR 6.16 crore; dividend income from JVs/subsidiaries was INR 12.07 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at about 15%, and bottom-line growth at about 15-20%; management said it expects to maintain this after Q1 (Q1 PAT growth 19% cited).
Order inflow target for FY27 of about INR 20,000 crore (with one answer citing INR 20,000-25,000 crore), in addition to existing order book; about INR 5,000-5,500 crore already received or entrusted.
Three-year vision: EBITDA margin of 5-7% and ROE of about 12-13%.
Over the next three years, order book targeted to split about 50:50 between railway management works and bidding works; overseas share expected to rise.
Margin expectations: management works 8-10%, PMC work about 7%, domestic bidding works 5-6%, overseas works 15-20% targeted.
Dividend policy follows DIPAM guidelines: 30% of PAT or 4% of net worth, whichever is higher.
No new external borrowing planned for the next two to three quarters; working capital lines available at about 5.5-5.9%.
capex_capacity: BharatNet (INR 13,000 crore, BSNL, 82,000 km OFC, DB-1 model): infrastructure implementation timeline three years, with about six to eight months of extension expected due to ground-level issues; 10-year maintenance follows.

Vande Bharat sleeper (INR 14,400 crore, executed by SPV Kinet Railway Solutions): first prototype trainset targeted for December 2026; 120 sets to be delivered over five years; 35-year maintenance contract.
Rishikesh-Karnaprayag rail project (INR 37,000 crore, 125 km): 78% overall progress, about 97% tunnel excavation complete; completion targeted December 2029.
Hardware for BharatNet was procured at pre-crisis tender prices, per management.
demand_pricing: Management says about 40-42% of the order book is fixed-price-like railway management-fee work; most contracts have price variation clauses covering inflation, so impact is limited.
Q1 revenue mix: about 63% from management (nomination) work and remainder from bidding and PMC work.
NMDC PMC award of about INR 6,500 crore cited as a nomination-basis win; talks ongoing with other PSUs and state governments for similar fixed-margin PMC work.

Overseas pursuits: bids in Africa (power transmission and roads), Nepal (hydro), Israel (Tel Aviv Metro EOI), Georgia and Serbia (rail reconstruction); management names Central Asia, Middle East, Eastern Europe and Southeast Asia as targets.
Management flagged labour availability shortages and client payment delays as key execution challenges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the L1 size and where is business development focused?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets INR 20,000-25,000 crore of order inflow this year, with about INR 5,500 crore already entrusted; focus on ports, hydro, highways and green energy.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is fixed-price and how is inflation handled?
qa_highlights.answer: About 42% is railway work on management-fee basis; contracts generally have price variation clauses, so inflation impact is not very big.

qa_highlights.question: How is BharatNet progressing and how are payments?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution was initially challenged but has improved; work is in full swing in UP West and UP East; some BSNL payments received and others in pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15-20% growth guidance maintained after Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management says it expects about 15% top-line and 15-20% bottom-line growth, with Q1 bottom-line growth at 19%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from overseas projects in volatile regions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says risk assessment is done before bidding and risk premium is built in; it expects margins of 15-20% overseas and cites government support.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further losses on onerous contracts? What is outstanding from Railways?
qa_highlights.answer: Onerous contract provisions are already made and no further provisions are anticipated; railway receivables are about INR 2,500 crore, with bills typically paid within 30 days.

risks_watch: Margin sustainability: standalone EBITDA margin of 3.99% remains thin; management says margins remain a focus area.
Client payment delays, notably BharatNet payments from BSNL, and railway receivables of about INR 2,500 crore.
Labour availability shortages and geopolitical situation affecting execution and overseas projects (Middle East, Israel).
Order inflow must reach the INR 20,000 crore target; the number was given as both INR 20,000 crore and INR 20,000-25,000 crore.
Inconsistent figures on call: order book split by segment, and order book mix (40% vs 42% railway); verify against filings.
Vande Bharat prototype timing (December 2026) and BharatNet extension of six to eight months.

540153|2026-06.headline: Endurance Q1 FY27 standalone total income rose 35.9% to ₹3,194.15 crores, with EBITDA margin at 11.2% after a commodity pass-through headwind.
540153|2026-06.overview:
Standalone total income grew 35.9% YoY to ₹3,194.15 crores, EBITDA rose 17.1% to ₹357.78 crores (11.2% margin) and PAT rose 17.4% to ₹194.62 crores. Management said commodity inflation (RMC at 68.4% of total income vs 64.8% a year ago) compressed margins; ex this pass-through, EBITDA margin would be 13.33%. Consolidated PAT grew 8% to ₹244.52 crores, with Maxwell turning PAT-positive for the first time. Management expects Q2 and Q3 margins to improve as raw material and conversion cost increases are settled with OEMs, and cited multiple SOPs and order wins across 2W, 4W castings, batteries and non-auto solar products.</overview>

512573|2026-06.headline: Avanti Feeds Q1 FY27 consolidated PBT fell 37% YoY to INR 157 crore despite 19% higher gross income, as feed raw-material costs squeezed margins.
512573|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated gross income rose 30% QoQ to INR 1,966 crore but PBT fell 15% QoQ to INR 157 crore and 37% YoY. The Feed division's gross income rose 27% YoY to INR 1,615 crore on 28,287 MT higher volume, yet PBT dropped 45% YoY to INR 114 crore as fish meal and soya bean meal prices surged. Feed PBT margin fell to 7.06% from about 13% in Q4 FY26 and 17% in Q1 FY26. Shrimp Processing and Export gross income fell 7% YoY to INR 350 crore, while PBT rose to INR 45 crore on better realisations and forex. Management took a roughly 10% feed price hike in June 2026 and said industry and government are working on a raw-material price mechanism.</overview>

Shrimp exports estimated at about 19,000 MT in FY27, against 16,976 MT in FY26.
Management expects raw-material prices to stabilise in coming months as fresh crops arrive and monsoon eases El Nino effects, but called FY27 a challenging season for aquaculture.
On the Q2 question, management agreed that Q2 could be another weak quarter before the benefit of the price hike and any government intervention plays out.
Shrimp production estimated at 8-9 lakh MT in calendar 2026, with feed consumption estimated at 11-12 lakh MT.
capex_capacity: Pet food plant: land near Hyderabad converted to non-agricultural use; Consent for Establishment application filed and approval pending, construction to start after approval.

Wheat flour price fell to INR 28/kg in Q1 FY27 from INR 31/kg; current spot prices are fish meal INR 225/kg, soya bean meal INR 71/kg, wheat flour INR 33/kg.
Frozen shrimp exports FY26 were 7,92,647 MT worth USD 5,624.48 million; USA 33% share, China 21%, EU 17%. US volumes fell 17.9% YoY; China rose 24%, EU 36%, Japan 5%.

539682|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 56.9% YoY to Rs 728 million and PAT rose 95% YoY to Rs 117 million, with EBITDA margin at 21.2%.
539682|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 728 million, up 56.9% YoY and 16.3% QoQ, with growth attributed to direct advertiser demand in Quick Commerce, BFSI, FinTech and Retail and to international expansion through agency and reseller models. EBITDA was Rs 154 million (21.2% margin, up 240 bps YoY) and PAT was Rs 117 million (16.1% margin, up 320 bps YoY). Management highlighted the launch of the Mobavenue Neural Engine, the PiiX Apple-ecosystem product, US entry and Singapore/Philippines operations. Direct clients' share of revenue fell to 65.2% from 73.9% in FY26, which management attributed to the agency/reseller route used for international expansion.

financial_highlights.change: +56.9% YoY; +16.3% QoQ (Q1 FY26 Rs 464 mn; Q4 FY26 Rs 626 mn)
+77% YoY (from Rs 87 mn); +15.8% QoQ (from Rs 133 mn)
+95% YoY (from Rs 60 mn); +39.3% QoQ (from Rs 84 mn)

segments.name: Direct advertisers
segments.commentary: Contributed 65.2% of Q1 revenue, down from 73.9% in FY26. Management said the decline reflects the agency/reseller route used for international entry and expects the direct share to recover over the long term.

segments.name: Agency, reseller and platform channels
segments.commentary: Make up the remaining ~34.8% of revenue. Management cited agency and reseller models as an accelerator for international growth.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Contributed 20.7% of revenue, with India as the anchor. Markets referenced include UK (first entered, ramping fastest), Latin America, Philippines, Singapore and US; management expects international share to build gradually over coming years.

segments.name: PiiX (Apple ecosystem)
segments.commentary: Newly launched in Q1 for Apple Search Ads, custom product pages and ASO; management said revenue contribution is negligible today and it will start in India.

guidance_outlook: Long-term 'Rule of 50' framework: sustained annual revenue growth above 30% with EBITDA margin of 20% or higher, with a vision to 2030.
Management said it will maintain a 20%+ EBITDA margin while improving it year on year in basis points.
Expects growth drivers from new geographies and products (US, UK, Apple ecosystem, emerging markets) to become meaningful in the next 12 to 18 months.
Expects a growing share of optimisation decisions to be made by the Neural Engine over the next 12 to 18 months.
FY27 priorities: deepen enterprise and mid-market penetration in India, scale globally on an asset-light outcome-based model, and selective inorganic opportunities.
capex_capacity: Mobavenue Neural Engine launched as a unified AI layer at the core of GMP360; management said core decisioning moved fully to neural network systems in FY26.
Platform processes over 1.3 billion signals per day and reaches about 2.6 billion devices monthly, with decisions in under 15 milliseconds.
Campaign lifecycle (plan, launch, create, report) said to run in under 59 seconds / under a minute per step.
Asset-light model; management said platforms can scale with limited incremental infrastructure investment.
Balance sheet supported by a FY26 preferential raise (about Rs 50 crore per an analyst's reference); capital prioritised for AI stack, international expansion and selective acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Growth led by direct advertiser demand in Quick Commerce, BFSI, FinTech and Retail, plus premium formats such as connected TV and video streaming.
Revenue per outcome of Rs 49.94 on 14.16 million verified outcomes; management said both outcomes and price per outcome are rising.
Top five sectors (FinTech, Quick Commerce, BFSI, Commerce, Retail, Travel) contribute about 70-80% of revenue; management did not disclose top-5 or top-10 client shares.
Data and supply costs are the largest cost line and are largely variable with revenue.
Named global competitors: AppLovin, Unity and The Trade Desk; named India competitors: Affle and InMobi.

qa_highlights.question: Why did direct client share fall from 73.9% to 65.2%, and what is the optimal mix with agency/reseller partners?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift is from the agency/reseller entry route for international markets. It described this as a small-to-medium-term approach and expects the direct advertiser base to return to a normal position over the long term.

qa_highlights.question: What moat protects the Neural Engine from global platforms replicating it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it owns the full stack across all three P3 layers and that proprietary consented signals feed a closed feedback loop, with pricing linked to outcomes. It pointed to rising revenue per outcome as evidence.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is 56.9% growth, and what would normalise it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it optimises for full-year performance and targets 30% growth and 20% EBITDA margin over the long term. It said quarter-to-quarter variation is expected as international markets scale.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 56.9% growth: market or share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said general market growth cannot explain 56.9%. It attributed growth to international markets (UK first, then LatAm, Philippines, US, Singapore) and premium inventory such as streaming, CTV, Apple ecosystem and DOOH.

qa_highlights.question: What is PiiX's revenue contribution and size of opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PiiX revenue is negligible today. It cited Apple's Indian reach at about 6% growing to 8-10%, and said the product will start in India before going international.

qa_highlights.question: How will the preferential raise proceeds be allocated, and what are the key risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said proceeds are mainly for strategic acquisitions with disciplined selection, plus technology investment. Named risks were regulation, currency (revenue balanced between INR and USD), AI disruption and inflation; no near-term inflation impact was seen.

risks_watch: Shift in revenue mix toward agency/reseller channels (direct share down to 65.2% from 73.9%) and its effect on margins.
International execution in US, UK, Singapore and Philippines, which management says drives a large share of growth but is still early.
Regulatory risk, which management named as the primary risk; also currency risk and AI disruption.
Client concentration: top-5 sectors contribute about 70-80% of revenue, and top-5/top-10 client shares were not disclosed.
Deployment of the FY26 preferential raise into acquisitions, which management has not yet named.
539682|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability; the tone was more qualitative when answering questions on client concentration, the scale of PiiX revenue and the acquisition pipeline, where few figures were given.

500350|2026-06.headline: RSWM Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.7% QoQ to ₹1,161 crore and EBITDA to ₹94 crore (8.0% margin), led by a 39.8% gross margin.
500350|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was ₹1,161 crore, up 1.7% QoQ, with domestic sales up to ₹825 crore and exports down to ₹336 crore. Gross margin expanded to 39.8% from 37.4%, lifting EBITDA to ₹94 crore (+10.1% QoQ, +16.1% YoY) and margin to 8.0%. PAT was ₹17 crore against ₹7 crore a year ago, but lower than Q4 FY26, which included a one-time tax benefit. Management gave no full-year guidance; fabric profitability weakened sharply while yarn held up, and new projects (PET food-grade chips, denim garmenting JV, knitting expansion) were outlined.

segments.name: Yarn (synthetic, cotton, mélange)
segments.commentary: Utilisation was about 96% for synthetic, 98% for cotton and 92-93% for mélange. Management said yarn demand held up and cotton/mélange spreads were good in Q1; Q2 is running similarly so far.

segments.name: Denim fabric
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation was about 90%. Management said the segment faced the same cost and demand pressure as knit, with exports and domestic roughly balanced.

guidance_outlook: No full-year growth or EBITDA margin guidance given; management said all quarters should be similar to or better than Q1.

Power cost savings of about ₹40 crore for FY27 at constant utilisation (from renewables and efficiency), with a stated target of around ₹100 crore; renewable share of power rose from mid-20s% to mid-40s%, and about 60% in the current quarter.
Management expects per-unit power cost to fall by more than ₹1 year-on-year on average.
Knitting expansion expected to add benefits from Q3 FY27, with capacity going from 650 tons to about 900 tons per month, including 150 tons of printing.

Food-grade PET chip plant: completion in Q4 FY27, trials and commercial production in Q1 FY28; 50,000 tpa capacity, ₹500 crore revenue expected, about 15% EBITDA (industry norm per management). Utilisation ramp of 75%, 85%, then 90-91% over three years.
Graphene-based fibre (with Birla Cellulose): management expects commercial traction within FY27.
risks_watch: Crude and polyester price volatility, and a possible reversal of Q1 stocking gains.
Export demand recovery, especially knit fabric and Middle East markets; the company said recent inquiries are improving.
Fabric margins near nil; monitor whether fabric EBIT recovers in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
PET plant execution: food-grade certification and trials, no customer tie-ups yet, and a 15% EBITDA assumption that is management's industry norm.
Garmenting JV: stake and capex undisclosed, new skills needed, and a labour-intensive business that is new to RSWM.
Finance costs rising with working capital needs (₹31 crore).
Management gave no full-year guidance; the company's disclosure is limited on volumes and capex amounts.
Investor-presentation timing: it was uploaded about 15 minutes before the call, which an analyst objected to.

500214|2026-06.headline: Ion Exchange Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 49% YoY to INR 32 crore (4.54% margin) on 20% revenue growth to INR 701 crore, with treatment solutions still loss-making.
500214|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating income rose 20% YoY to INR 701 crore, but EBITDA fell 49% to INR 32 crore and PAT was INR 3 crore (0.44% margin). Management split the former engineering segment into Treatment Solutions, Industrial Products and Lifecycle Services, and reported Specialty Chemicals and Consumer Products separately. Treatment Solutions posted a EBIT loss of INR 17 crore on legacy projects, while Industrial Products margin rose to 11.89%. Management said Roha resin capacity is ramping slower than expected and guidance will be reviewed by end of Q2.

financial_highlights.value: INR 112 crore / loss of INR 34 lakh
financial_highlights.change: +33% revenue YoY; loss was INR 45 lakh
excludes Hyundai win of about USD 52 million

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 210 crore (+14% YoY) with EBIT loss of INR 17 crore, hit by legacy projects including the UP project. Dispatches to GCC resumed post-quarter; a Hyundai contract of about USD 52 million (over INR 500 crore per Q&A) was won after quarter end.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 105 crore (+14% YoY) and EBIT INR 13 crore, margin 11.89% vs under 6% a year ago, driven by water treatment solutions and membranes. Institutional products moved here from Consumer.

segments.name: Lifecycle Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 72 crore (+28% YoY) and EBIT INR 7 crore (9.92% margin vs 10.55%), with margin pressure from higher input costs. Includes a 20-year O&M concession in Oman with PDO.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 230 crore (+21% YoY) but EBIT INR 22 crore (-52% YoY), impacted by geopolitics and Roha ramp-up costs; Roha cost drag about 6% of segment margin. FX gain in the prior-year quarter also reversed (about 3-4 pts).

segments.name: Consumer Products
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 112 crore (+33% YoY) with a small loss of INR 34 lakh vs INR 45 lakh a year ago; breakeven targeted in FY27.

Consumer Products targeted to break even in FY27.

capex_capacity: Roha resin plant commissioned and in stabilisation; with Ankleshwar debottlenecking, total resin capacity expected to reach about 5x the pre-Roha level (Phase I doubles capacity, Phase II plus debottlenecking takes it to about 5x).
Pharma resin capacity at Ankleshwar (FDA-approved) to expand 6x, targeted within the next 12 months; described as asset-light, technology-led rather than capex-heavy.
Membrane business: second Goa plant under construction to add UF and MBR capacity; tie-up with MANN+HUMMEL for UF PVDF technology. Management targets 3x business growth over the years.
Standard plants capacity expanded across Hosur, Goa and Wada.
Management would not disclose capital earmarked for BOOT/BOO service projects, saying it will remain asset-light.
demand_pricing: Hyundai contract of about USD 52 million (over INR 500 crore) won post quarter end; supplied to an EPC, FOB Mumbai, kickoff under way.
Bid pipeline stood at INR 9,777 crore as of the call.

Price increases taken across customers and segments, but pass-through lags input cost increases; management sees some moderation in input costs with crude near USD 80 vs over USD 100 in March-April 2026.
Geopolitical situation (West Asia) impacted invoicing and dispatches; Roha volumes expected to lean on overseas markets, including North America after WQA certification.
UP project unexecuted portion is about 11% of June order backlog; receivable exposure said to be broadly unchanged over recent quarters.

517214|2026-06.headline: DiGiSPICE Q1 FY27: continuing-business PAT of INR 9 crore; EBITDA INR 8.6 crore; AePS market share dipped to 17.93%.
517214|2026-06.overview: Management framed DiGiSPICE as a holding company whose only continuing business is Spice Money, a banking-agent fintech serving Tier-3 to Tier-5 India. Revenue was flat on a product-mix shift, but gross margin held at INR 48.1 crore as financial product distribution offset seasonal CICO weakness. EBITDA rose to INR 8.6 crore (about 6.5x QoQ) and PAT to INR 6.6 crore from INR 2.8 crore in Q4. The NCLT merger is in its second motion, with completion targeted by March 2027. Management said there are no formal fundraising plans and it is funding growth from internal accruals.

financial_highlights.metric: PAT (continuing business, as stated by Chairman)

financial_highlights.change: up from INR 2.8 crore in previous quarter

BBPS grew 14.2% YoY; share of GTV 15% vs 9% a year ago

segments.commentary: Management says this is the growth engine: GTV up 16.3% QoQ and margin up 50.7% QoQ. Grahak loan disbursals INR 167.7 crore; 17.8 lakh CASA accounts sold; five new secured card categories; two-wheeler insurance launched in July. Insurance sales moderated in Q1.

UPI Cash Point exit run-rate of close to INR 500 crore in Q2 FY27 (Rohit Sood).

qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Sood said insurance is sold mainly to captive Adhikaris (shopkeeper insurance), which saturated quickly; the company is expanding the product portfolio and changing the distribution construct next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AePS market share fall to 17.93%, and can share gains be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Sood attributed the dip to DBT disbursement skew in southern markets where share is lower; share recovered to 18.3% in July.

qa_highlights.question: Can UPI Cash Point reach 50% of AePS, and how is advantage sustained as entry barriers fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 50% a hopeful target and said Q2 exit could be near INR 500 crore; the BC-agent onboarding requirement was cited as a moat for players with large agent networks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected timeline for the merger and listing, and are there residual costs from discontinued businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Kapoor said the merger is expected by end of FY27; discontinued-business losses are minimal and reported separately, with structures being closed by year-end.

511742|2026-06.headline: UGRO Q1 FY27: total AUM INR 15,013 crore and disbursements INR 2,551 crore (+59% YoY); opex cut to ~INR 119 crore from INR 217 crore in Q4.
511742|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 reflected the completed shift toward Emerging Market LAP and Embedded Merchant Finance (GROx), which together reached 46% of AUM versus 32% in Dec '25. Interest income fell 13% QoQ to INR 363 crore as co-lending and direct assignment income dropped to INR 75 crore from INR 155 crore, though it grew 19% YoY. Quarterly opex fell 42% QoQ to ~INR 119 crore, and reported PAT was lifted by a one-time deferred tax reversal from the move to the new tax regime (pre-tax ROA 2.6% vs reported 2.8%). Management guided AUM flat for FY27 with on-balance-sheet assets growing, and said growth can be funded without incremental equity through FY29. Q&A focused on runoff, GNPA trajectory, the Profectus merger and the weak share price.

financial_highlights.change: Down from INR 155 crore in Q4 FY26; ~14% of total income vs 24% in Q4

Emerging Market and GROx targeted at ~25% CAGR to FY29; defocused Prime book to run down ~20% (actual run-off ~25%). Management indicated ~15% growth overall.

capex_capacity: EM branch network at 317 branches; branch build-out complete, so focus shifted to productivity. Mature (>12 months) branches number 96 (from 81 in March) and produce ~INR 81 lakh per month vs target INR 80-85 lakh.

demand_pricing: Combined EM and GROx share of AUM 46% (from 32% in Dec '25), targeted at 85% by FY29.
GROx partners: onboarding other lenders, with SIDBI as a co-lending partner, and more banks and NBFCs coming. Average EM LAP ticket size INR 17 lakh (range INR 7.5-50 lakh).

July 2026 monthly disbursement crossed INR 1,000 crore for the first time.

532768|2026-06.headline: Fiem Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.6% to INR769.9 crore with EBITDA margin steady at 13.5%; FY27 4-wheeler ramp pushed out to FY28.
532768|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 sales grew 18.62% YoY to INR769.9 crore and EBITDA rose to INR104.06 crore at a 13.5% margin, versus 13.46% a year ago. PAT increased 16.31% to INR65.19 crore. Management said raw material and employee cost increases will be passed on with a lag over the next few quarters, and reiterated FY27 guidance of 15-20% revenue growth and about 14% EBITDA margin. The main negative was the 4-wheeler lighting ramp, which management now expects to slip into FY28 from FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs 13.46% YoY; about 130 bps QoQ compression as stated by an analyst

segments.name: EV lighting
segments.commentary: EV share of 2-wheeler volume is above 9%, up from about 6% a year ago. Supplies commenced for Ather Konarc (sole supplier on the new model), River RX02 and Royal Enfield EV Flying Flea. Hero Vida lamps for its Andhra Pradesh plant will ship from Hosur from next quarter.

capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex INR41.15 crore; FY27 target about INR100 crore, largely Hosur (Kelamangalam and Thally Road) for EV capacity.

demand_pricing: Industry: record Q1 2-wheeler volume of 7.25 million units, supported by GST rationalisation, retail financing and rural demand; exports and EVs grew faster.

Mercedes: samples submitted, with 1.5-2 years of vehicle-level testing before an RFQ/RFI for mass production.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the FY27 4-wheeler lighting guidance (INR100-150 crore in the prior quarter) cut?

qa_highlights.question: How will LED penetration move in 2-wheeler lighting?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Yamaha?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Yamaha to be flat to growing for the year. Exports were weak on the cycle of European and US demand; domestic models such as R15, Aerox and XSR were slower in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin and cost pass-through outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about 14% EBITDA margin for FY27. Raw material cost increases are expected to be passed on with a lag of a couple of quarters; the employee cost run-rate should hold for the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is capital allocation given about INR280 crore cash and no debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited organic and inorganic opportunities, plus possible future 4-wheeler and electronics capex. It will fund capex from internal accruals and would raise debt if needed for a larger opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company disclose wallet share by customer and segment?
qa_highlights.answer: An analyst asked for annual wallet share disclosure by segment. Management declined to share it in advance, citing customer confidentiality, and said it will announce models after customer launches.

risks_watch: 4-wheeler ramp has slipped again; FY28 is now the earliest meaningful scale-up, and analysts questioned competitive share gains.
Yamaha exports and domestic models slowed in Q1; management expects recovery but gave no quarterly targets.
Input cost and rupee pressure: pass-through has a lag, so margin in the next 1-2 quarters depends on recovery.
Employee cost step-up from minimum wage revisions across states, which management expects to persist for the next three quarters.

543547|2026-06.headline: Ddev Plastiks Q1 FY27 EBITDA crossed INR100 crore for the first time (INR101 cr, 10% margin), revenue up 29% YoY on export price gains.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth target about 15%, with the target volume at 231,000 t and about 60,000 t per quarter needed for the remaining quarters.
FY27 revenue growth guidance about 13-14%, built on FY26 average realisation of about INR145/kg with no price increase assumed; management says it expects to beat guidance.
Long-term EBITDA margin target 10-12% (INR16-17/t), but Q1 EBITDA/t of about INR19.6 is not expected to be sustained every quarter.
Bhiwadi plant assumed at about 50% average utilisation in FY27, generating about INR200-250 crore of revenue; FY30 top-line ambition INR5,000 crore.
Resin prices expected to take 3-6 months to normalise after the Hormuz/war situation clears.
Committed capex for FY27 about INR150-175 crore (East MV cable capacity, HFFR expansion to 20,000 t, new Vapi site, BESS); about INR77 crore already spent in Q1.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 316,400 t per annum as of June 2026; management cites 334,400 t by year-end and about 231,000 t planned FY27 tonnage.
Bhiwadi (Rajasthan) greenfield XLPE plant of 48,000 t commissioned April 2026, running at about 20-25% utilisation; expected to ramp over the next couple of months.
HFFR capacity to be expanded to 20,000 t by FY27 end; new Vapi site for product consolidation; PVC addition of about 25,000 t mentioned.

East India (Bengal) plant for medium-voltage cable compounds being set up; the BESS location is being shifted from West to East, delaying timelines by a couple of quarters, with the state incentive policy expected around end-August.
BESS phase 1 about 1 GW / 1 GWh, funded from internal accruals; BOO/BOOT not planned for now.
demand_pricing: Export pricing was the main Q1 driver: freight and raw material uncertainty let the company quote war-risk premiums, and management says export realisations rose about 30%.
Domestic demand softened in Q1 because of high polymer prices; management expects volume recovery once price volatility eases.
Management says the company's cable-customer segment grows about 12-13% a year, which is the basis for the 15% volume target, with the extra 2-3% expected to come from market share gains.
Share gain thesis: the Bhiwadi plant targets Rajasthan and Delhi customers; some western capacity moves to European exports.
Management expects EBITDA/t to stay elevated only for a few months; prices in July were marginally lower and August is 'okay', but orders are spot with 10-20 day visibility.
Cash conversion cycle widened in Q1 due to higher inventory and debtors; expected to return to 55-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: How much Q4 export revenue spilled into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 1,000 t moved from late-March shipments; value rose due to freight, so about INR300+ crore export revenue was reported in Q1, partly from Q4 volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 EBITDA/t sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR19.6/t may not hold each quarter but could last a few months; the long-term target is INR16-17/t or 10-12% margin. The war-risk premium is about INR2.5-3/t.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS business model and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Starts as a supply model at 6-8% EBITDA margin, with EPC adding 2-5 points and system integrator another 2-3 points; long-term target 11-15%. BOO/BOOT not planned now.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance (13-14% revenue) below capacity growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance uses FY26 average prices, assumes about 50% Bhiwadi utilisation and 15% volume growth; management says it expects to beat guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will finance costs and cash conversion cycle improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance costs rose from working-capital borrowing after the March raw material spike; they have eased since July. Cash conversion cycle expected to return to 55-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company gain market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management cites the Bhiwadi plant and importers being displaced by supply-chain disruption. Bhiwadi will serve existing customers, mainly in Rajasthan and Delhi.

543442|2026-06.headline: Brand Concepts Q1 FY27 revenue grew ~11% and EBITDA rose, but PBT loss widened; management expects growth to resume from October.
543442|2026-06.overview:
Management said revenue grew almost 11% YoY and EBITDA grew on lower overheads, while the PBT loss widened marginally on higher depreciation, interest and operating investments. Primary billing took a dent from an e-commerce SKU realignment and channel consolidation, though secondary sales were said to be strong and market share was claimed to be intact. Retail tail-clipping continued: about 75-80% of the store consolidation is done, with completion targeted by September. The new hard-luggage and PP plants are ramping, with the PC unit at 80%+ utilisation on internal consumption only.</overview>

qa_highlights.question: When does consolidation end and when does growth return?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidation about 75-80% done; stores to exit by September, e-commerce reset this month, and growth expected back from October.

qa_highlights.question: Store closure impact and INR1,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reported figures are post-closures, EBO is ~10% of business, and the INR1,000 crore target over 4-5 years remains on track.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory days and Benetton plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory INR123 crore at June-end, about 130 days per management. Benetton had failed strategies; pivoted to e-commerce price-led line and new offline styles next month.

500249|2026-06.headline: KSB H1 FY27 revenue INR 12,920 mn with weak Q1 sales (2–3% growth); management targets double-digit FY growth on H2 export recovery.
500249|2026-06.overview: Management presented at an institutional investor meet (held 19 Aug 2026) covering H1 FY27 (April–June 2026 quarter as described in the call). H1 revenue from sales was INR 12,920 mn, EBITDA INR 1,465 mn and PBT INR 1,279 mn. Management attributed the subdued quarter to Middle East export shipments held up by the geopolitical situation, supply-chain constraints on castings after gas availability issues, a delayed KUSUM 2.0 solar scheme, and slow project-pump order inflow. Management expects a much better H2 and aims for double-digit growth, though it flagged NPCIL test-bed delays on nuclear and continued fixed-price margin pressure.

financial_highlights.change: Management said Q1 sales grew only 2–3% over the prior period
Well below plan due to KUSUM 2.0 delay
Down from mid-teens levels the analyst cited; management called it temporary

segments.name: Order intake mix
segments.commentary: Standard 51%, Engineered 14%, SupremeServ 16%, Valves about 19% of order intake, per management.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Order on hand INR 1,235 crore covering GHAVP 1 and 2, Kaiga 5 and 6 and the Kudankulam safety package; Shirwal nuclear capacity at 80–90% utilisation with a new shed adding about 7,000 sq m (about 20% plant capacity).

segments.name: Valves
segments.commentary: Margin fell to single digits in H1 on commodity prices, product mix, lower exports and lower sales; management expects a return to double-digit margins.

segments.name: SupremeServ
segments.commentary: Management targets 25–30% aftermarket share in India (group target 35%); business growing about 15% per annum.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: Solar pumps are 5–7% of current order book versus a 10–12% target; Maharashtra tender orders expected to help in Q3.

guidance_outlook: Goal is double-digit growth for the full year; management said 15–17% average growth over time is achievable (10–15% volume, about 15% value).
H2 expected to be much better, with export shipments recovering from Middle East disruption and supply chain now around 85–90% stable.
Nuclear GHAVP testing expected to start in September 2026 once NPCIL resolves test-bed issues; first pump needs about 500 hours of testing (2–3 months), with up to six pumps a year possible.
EBITDA target of 13–14% reiterated; gross margin under pressure on fixed-price project business, partly offset by internal cost reduction.
Export order book about 15% of sales, with a target of 20%.
S/4HANA implementation in H1 of next year, with group cost allocation expected in FY28 OpEx; amount not yet decided.
Capex of about INR 80–120 crore per year (sustenance plus growth).
capex_capacity: Shirwal plant is about 115,000 sq m (15,000 sq m added with recently bought land); a new shed of about 7,000 sq m adds about 20% capacity.
Shirwal capacity about 1,200–1,300 pumps across energy, oil and gas and nuclear combined.
Nuclear: first indigenous pump made in 2025, under testing at NPCIL test bed in 2026; ISO-19443 certified.
Reciprocating pumps being developed under BP&CL technology; EIL approval in process, requiring a running pump supplied within 12 months.
Split-case pump of 10,000 cubic metres per hour under development for export and river-linking projects.
demand_pricing: Management sees energy (thermal, nuclear, renewable) and water/wastewater infrastructure as main growth drivers; supercritical thermal boiler circulation pump win broke an import jinx.
Project market (oil and gas, petrochemical) slowed; Dangote refinery expected to contribute later.
Price increases: foundry costs up 12–15%; KSB standard market price hikes so far single-digit, being phased in.
Export demand hit by Middle East war and earlier US tariffs cancelling some orders; US boiler feed pump orders for gas plants noted.
Data centre: orders from KSB Germany's OEM customers and an international OEM in India for liquid cooling; no size quantified.
Pump content of projects estimated at 3–5% of total project value.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 performance subdued, and how much export was to the Middle East?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the war affecting exports (pumps ready but undelivered) and supply-chain constraints; sales grew only 2–3%, and H2 is expected to recover.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Goal is double-digit growth; nuclear test-bed delay is the main risk, which management sees as low risk. 20% top-line is possible but with peaks.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear execution and competition for the next primary coolant pump tender?
qa_highlights.answer: GHAVP testing delayed by NPCIL test-bed issues, with testing expected from September; a new tender for about eight reactors (Mahi Banswara, ASHVINI) expected in a few months, and KSB is the approved supplier.

qa_highlights.question: Why valves margin fell to single digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited commodity prices, product mix, lower exports and lower sales together, and called it temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Why did order intake not improve materially?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard business growing but new-market entry takes time (fire-fighting, marine, mining); project market, especially oil and gas and petrochemical, slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear execution cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard cycle is 24–36 months; deliveries to NPCIL around 48 months from order; management confirmed about 4 years from groundbreaking to first supply.

qa_highlights.question: BP&CL run-rate and scale?
qa_highlights.answer: On track but slow due to PSU referencing and tender requirements; medium-term potential INR 40–50 crore a year.

risks_watch: Nuclear: NPCIL test-bed issues delaying GHAVP testing, which could push back deliveries and revenue recognition.
Gross margin pressure from fixed-price project contracts and foundry cost pass-through lag of 3–6 months.
Export recovery depends on the Middle East situation and shipment clearances; export inventory still held at end-June.
Solar: KUSUM 2.0 delay; solar receivables and state-government payment cycle may keep receivable days elevated.
S/4HANA cost allocation from FY28 onwards; amount not yet quantified.
Q2 results should show whether H2 recovery materialises and whether valves margins return to double digits.
500249|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term nuclear, thermal and data-centre opportunities but defensive on the weak H1; management repeatedly says it expects H2 to recover, with few hard numbers on timing or magnitude.

541967|2026-06.headline: Sky Gold Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 78% YoY to INR2,013 crores, with gross margin at 9.3% and operating cash flow of about INR30 crores.
541967|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q1 FY27 was INR2,013 crores, up 78% YoY, implying an annualised run rate near the FY27 guidance of INR8,100 crores. Gross margin rose to 9.3% from 9.1% in Q4 FY26, driven by a higher share of non-22KT jewellery and studded products. EBITDA was INR157 crores (7.8% margin) and operating PAT crossed INR100 crores for the first time. Operating cash flow turned positive at about INR30 crores, and working capital days edged up to 60 from 59 in March. Management said it will revise FY27 guidance only after Diwali.

financial_highlights.value: Crossed INR100 crores for the first time

financial_highlights.change: Positive vs negative operating cash flow through FY26
QoQ/as stated by CFO; company no longer gives volume guidance

segments.name: Advance Gold model
segments.commentary: Advance Gold share of sales reached 17% in Q1 vs 20% in Q4 FY26 (management says volumes flat, share diluted by higher total volume); contributes about 90-100 bps to revenue and gross margin. Internal FY27 target was 15%.

segments.name: Non-22KT jewellery (18KT, 14KT, 9KT)
segments.commentary: Share rose to 14% of volume from 10.5% in Q4 FY26, contributing about 1.4-1.5% to gross margin.

segments.name: Studded jewellery (natural and lab-grown)
segments.commentary: Share rose to 2.1% of revenue from 1.65% in Q4 FY26, contributing about 0.3% to gross margin. Natural diamonds are about 2% of business.

segments.name: 22KT jewellery
segments.commentary: Gross margin about 6-6.5%; roughly 70% of this is CZ-studded (margin not stated separately), with plain gold at 5-5.5% margin.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export share rose to close to 18% from about 14.5% in Q4 FY26. UAE 6%, Singapore 2%, Malaysia 2% of sales; UK/Europe pipeline of INR30-45 crores, initial UK order of 25-30 kg.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR8,100 crores; management to revise after Diwali (after one more quarter).
FY30 revenue aspiration of INR18,000-19,000 crores, excluding Advance Gold business revenue; PAT target of INR1,000 crores over time.
Gross margin guidance of 8.5-9% blended; PAT margin long-term guidance of about 5.25%.
Operating cash flow to PAT conversion target of close to 20%; revenue growth of 30-35% per year cited for the Sky Gold 3.0 horizon.
Net working capital cycle: reduce by about 2 days YoY, target 52 days by 2030; net debt-free by 2030.
Advance Gold targets: 15% average in FY27, 20% in FY28, 25% in FY29, 30% by 2030. Exports targeted at 20% of sales in coming years.
Zero-salary promoter compensation from FY27; promoter pay linked to dividends paid from operating cash flow, after debt reduction.
capex_capacity: Current capacity utilisation about 60% (stated range 55-57% earlier in the call), against 1.2 tons capacity; management expects utilisation to rise 7-8% QoQ.
Asset-light model: capacity sufficient until 2028. Post-2028 expansion planned on a leased basis, with 120-day lead time to take capacity from 1.2 to 1.10-2.4 tons.
Expansion capex of INR75-100 crores (machinery, furniture and fixtures), about 12-20% of PAT; rent-free period of around 120 days typically available.
Company has 4 facilities; no acquisitions on the table.
demand_pricing: Shift to lower-karat jewellery driven by customer preference and high gold prices; 18KT, 14KT and 9KT gaining share.
Management says gold price volatility has squeezed margins across peers, but Sky Gold maintained margin via back-to-back hedging.
Gen Z brands (CaratLane, Candere, GIVA) growing; 4 large corporates onboarded in 15-18 months, faster than the 24-36 months expected.
Industry organisation: B2C about 40% organised; B2B about 20% organised; management expects 75% organised by 2030.
Seasonality: Q2 (Navratri-Diwali) above Q1; Q3 (wedding season) above Q2; Q4 (March, Akshaya Tritiya deliveries) strongest per management.

qa_highlights.question: Given the Q1 run rate, should FY27 guidance be revised upward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will revise guidance after Diwali; revenue upgrades depend on a greater share of studded and Advance Gold business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory/working capital days rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital days moved from 59 to 60. Cash is being redeployed into higher-margin studded jewellery, which needs slightly more working capital; exports rose to about 18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the rise in payable days sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gold credit is nearly nil while diamond purchases get market-standard credit, so the higher payables are sustainable. Each 1-day change in operating cycle is worth about INR95 crores of operating cash.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt was INR540 crores at quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 60% (55-65% range across standalone and subsidiaries); capacity lasts until 2028, then leased expansion with capex of INR80-100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 growth guidance be given?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 30-35% sales growth under Sky Gold 3.0 and plans to give FY27/FY28 estimates after September.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide PAT margin at 5.25% and gross margin at 8.5-9% when mix is improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance was set at end-2025 for a five-year horizon; volume discounts of 0.25-0.5% on large 22KT orders dilute margins. Management said guidance may be improved.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the July 2026 fraud disclosure on Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: INR10.7 crores involved; about INR3.5 crores recovered, legal proceedings initiated and a favourable order obtained. Management declined further comment as the matter is under legal and investigative process.

544443|2026-06.headline: Travel Food Services Q1 FY27: consolidated PAT up 35.6% YoY to INR1.3 billion on 20.6% revenue growth, despite flat passenger traffic and 0.8% system-wide LFL.
544443|2026-06.overview: Management reported system-wide sales up 18% YoY to INR8.4 billion and consolidated revenue from operations up 20.6% YoY to INR4.5 billion, with net contract gains of 15.9% system-wide. Passenger traffic was broadly flat YoY, with international traffic hit by the Middle East conflict and May's domestic rebound reversed in June. EBITDA rose 11% to INR1.6 billion, but margin moderated to 35.8% on pre-operating and employee costs for new airports (Noida, Cochin, Delhi). PAT was helped by a INR131 million one-time GST provision write-back in other income.

financial_highlights.change: ex-Mumbai, Guwahati and some South India markets about 7%
Adjusted for INR223 million lounge aggregation cost reclassification: INR3.65 billion, about 81%
+35.6% YoY vs 25.3% margin last year; includes INR131 million GST provision write-back

segments.name: Travel QSR and lounges (system-wide)
segments.commentary: 580 outlets and lounges at June end across 21 airports; 153 brands; 87 travel QSR outlets and two lounges added over last 12 months. Noida International Airport commenced operations in the quarter.

segments.name: JV / associate business
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 15% per management's implied figure as questioned by analysts; drag from Western India airports with Middle East exposure. Management said JV ramp-up continues.

segments.name: Passenger services (Elite Assist)
segments.commentary: Launched at Noida International Airport with meet-and-greet and porter services; to integrate into the EATS platform and expand to more airports.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 passenger traffic bounce-back as airlines restore long-haul international routes from September and October 2026.
About 90 units commissioned over last 12 months expected to normalise over next 12 months; benefits to play out in H2 FY27.

Pre-operating costs for Cochin, Delhi and Noida ramp-up expected to normalise in about 12 months, returning to traditional cost levels.

Bhogapuram Airport opened 17 August 2026 with multiple outlets under JV GHL.
capex_capacity: Over 50 outlets under construction or about to start construction across airports including Delhi, Navi Mumbai, Bhogapuram and Noida.
Noida International Airport outlets and passenger services commissioned in the quarter.
Asia focus for international expansion; Dubai entity set up for the Middle East and Indonesia entity set up recently to enable local bids.
Highways wayside amenities (WSA) under evaluation, with government plan of about 1,000 wayside amenities; management says medium-to-long term.
demand_pricing: Passenger traffic broadly flat YoY in Q1: April declined, May rebounded to record domestic month, June softened on renewed conflict. Management says traffic in July-August similar to Q1 trend, with international the drag.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 4.2% LFL came from higher spend per passenger, and what is sustainable LFL?

qa_highlights.question: Lounge aggregation cost and other expenses rise in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: INR223 million of lounge aggregation cost sits in other expenses; excluding it, other expenses rose 22% YoY. Management expects normalisation within about 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why are JV and associate revenues growing slower than consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Some JV contracts are moving to JV structures over time, and Western airports with Middle East exposure, which form a bulk of JV portfolio, were hit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Delhi T3 contract moving to JV in H2?

qa_highlights.question: Are the 50 outlets under development in existing airports?

qa_highlights.question: Highways strategy: is it accelerating?

Chennai and Kolkata renewals due end-March 2027 and early Q1 FY28 may bring cost resets.
PAT growth flattered by INR131 million one-time GST write-back; underlying growth is lower.

544890|2026-06.headline: Skyways Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 90.4% YoY to INR1,216.53 crores, with consolidated PAT margin at 2.2% versus 1.72%.
544890|2026-06.overview: Management reported a strong Q1 FY27, with operating revenue up 90.4% YoY to INR1,216.53 crores and operating EBITDA up to INR50.12 crores from INR27.31 crores. Management attributed much of the revenue jump to per-unit freight cost increases driven by fuel indices, with volume growth of 23% in air cargo and 18% in ocean freight. Employee and other expenses fell as a share of revenue, lifting margins. Five projects are deployed, and the company aims for about INR10,000 crores GDV in Senior Living.

segments.name: Regular housing (Gurugram, Jaipur, Bhiwadi)

FY27 reported revenue indication of about INR2,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable presales trajectory over 3-5 years?

qa_highlights.question: Why ROE expectations changed from 20%+ to 15%?

qa_highlights.question: Units sold fell from 407 to 234 YoY. Deliberate or volume slowdown?

qa_highlights.question: Vadgaon payback and underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Underwriting assumes INR9,000-10,000 per sq ft on 20 lakh sq ft, or INR1,800-2,000 crores of revenue. Sales are planned at about 2 lakh sq ft per year, with a launch in about 18 months. The NCD was issued by the landowners, who keep a 25% stake plus a 6% revenue share.

qa_highlights.question: Capex for the deals in pipeline and IFC partnership status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the FY27 deployment budget is about INR800 crores, including Q1 deals and deals in active discussion. The IFC platform is exhausted or lapsed because of ticket-size caps. There is no active agreement, though discussions on future capital are ongoing.

524091|2026-06.headline: Carysil Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 27% to INR56 crores with margin at 21.2%; management now tracks the upper band of the 18-20% FY27 guidance.
524091|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 16.5% YoY to INR264.8 crores, with EBITDA up 27% to INR56 crores and margin expanding 175 bps to 21.2%. PAT grew 37.7% YoY to INR31.4 crores (PAT margin 11.9%), and EPS was INR11.05 versus INR8.03. Management attributed the margin gain to operating leverage, product mix, US discount rollback and efficiency, and said it maintains 15% revenue growth guidance. Logistics-related container delays pushed some export dispatches into Q2, and the UK business was softer.

financial_highlights.change: +37.7% YoY (vs INR22.8 crores); PAT margin 11.9% (+183 bps)

segments.name: Quartz sinks

segments.commentary: Volume 9.8 thousand units, +12% YoY; about 11.8% of revenue. 53% of appliances sold were made in-house.

segments.commentary: Surfaces about 25% of revenue per management. United Granite revenue grew over 20%, with gross margin said to have risen from 35% to 50% after higher-end stone inventory build.

EBITDA margin guidance of 18-20% maintained; management says it is tracking towards the upper band.
Domestic momentum supported by a funded 90-day festive plan (September-November) and an 8-city celebrity roadshow.
Quartz sink expansion of 250,000 units on track for completion by end FY27 (March 2027).

FY27 capex of approximately INR80-90 crores: granite sinks INR40-50 crores, stainless steel about INR20 crores, faucets and appliances about INR20 crores. Management sees a minimum of INR50-60 crores of capex annually thereafter.
Carysil Blue D2C: first 10 stores in India targeted by end of calendar 2026 or March 2027. Surfaces fabrication unit in India targeted by March 2027.
Expected e-commerce sales in India to grow 3x this year; 180 stores over next two years, with 34 committed in Q2.
capex_capacity: Quartz sinks: 250,000-unit expansion on track for end FY27; management said infrastructure is built for half a million sinks.
Stainless steel: capacity added 70,000 units in Q1 (total 250,000), with 150,000 more by March 2027; new factory construction started on adjacent land.
Factory running close to 7 days a week per management, with utilisation near 90% and focus on productivity.
Surfaces (India) fabrication unit targeted for March 2027, with CNC automated process to be the first in India.
demand_pricing: Export order book described as the highest ever; new SKUs added with Lowe's, Home Depot and Amazon; Home Depot US and Canada partnership extended; Hafele Australia/NZ collaboration; first Amazon USA orders.
Logistics disruption delayed container dispatches at quarter-end, pushing some volume into Q2; management said material supply was not a constraint.
US discount rollback: about 90% completed, booked in the last month of Q1 (June). Lowe's display-sharing cost of USD3-4 million (50% share) expected to reverse, supporting margins.
India B2B is about 20% of India revenue (INR176 crores last FY); new builder breakthroughs include DLF and M3M.
Management cited pricing of INR12% average realisation growth in India domestic sales; stated average price held flat in FY27 guidance.
UK business softer in Q1 per management; new customers such as Bodel, Barwick and JJO added; project/builder segment being entered.
Faucet RO water system: first consignment sold out, about 60-day backlog.

qa_highlights.question: Why was quartz growth single digit and why were international subsidiaries and UK growth weaker?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed logistics disruption and container delays that stopped dispatches at quarter-end despite strong order booking; UK is in a tight phase but new customers should drive recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Any price hikes taken across categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the ASP increase to operating leverage, US discount rollback, and a premium product mix in stainless steel and granite, rather than explicit price hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 94% SS utilisation inclusive of the 70,000 units added in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity came mid-quarter, so utilisation is on a weighted-average days-available basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why was quartz capacity expansion structured as 250,000 units instead of 100,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand from export deals and India momentum required the larger expansion; it considers 20-25% spare capacity necessary at around 90% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% guidance a volume or value number?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said value guidance at 15%, and also stated 15% volume growth for the year, with average prices held; the answer was inconsistent and was not fully reconciled on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the segment revenue and domestic vs export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Quartz sink 51%, steel sink 12%, kitchen appliances 11.8%, surfaces 25%. Domestic INR56 crores and exports INR111 crores in Q1. Segment margins to be provided separately by IR or CFO.

risks_watch: Capacity constraints: factory at near-full utilisation, so volume growth depends on the timing of the March 2027 capacity additions.

UK market softness and dependence on new builder/project channels yet to show results.

Sustaining the 27% EBITDA growth and upper-band margin as the US discount rollback and mix benefits normalise.
Faucet exports not yet started; capability and technology upgrades still in progress.

513023|2026-06.headline: Nava Q1 FY27 consolidated total income hit an all-time quarterly high of INR1,269 crore; Phase 2 thermal (MEL) slips to Q2 FY28-29 commissioning.
513023|2026-06.overview:
Management reported record consolidated total income of INR1,269 crore for Q1 FY27, with standalone total income at a record INR689 crore, helped by lower coal and manufacturing costs and dividend income from Nava Global. The 300 MW MEL plant ran at an 89.3% PLF. Phase 2 thermal commissioning has been pushed by a couple of months to around July 2027 (Q2 FY28, per management wording) due to logistics delays on critical equipment linked to the geopolitical conflict. A 100 MW solar project is slated for commissioning by end-September 2026. Management did not disclose consolidated profit or margin figures in the call.</overview>

qa_highlights.answer: Full commissioning of both units by Q2 FY28 (around July 2027); Phase 2 revenue about INR200 million; margins not disclosed, with tariff described as attractive.

qa_highlights.question: Why are land assets carried at historical cost and what is their current value?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Accounting Standards allow historical cost; management has engaged a third party to study current asset values and options, and declined to give a number.

qa_highlights.question: Is funding available for new power projects (solar, wind, SMR) and is Zambia spin-off planned?

qa_highlights.question: Why has Zambia energy EBITDA margin declined and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower reversal of ECL credit; sustainable EBITDA margin around 45-50%.

qa_highlights.question: How is consolidated EBITDA derived from segment EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Intersegment transfer pricing (power-metals and coal from mines) is eliminated; consolidated EBITDA is around 35-40% of segment EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is Phase 2 finance cost capitalised?

543329|2026-06.headline: Windlas Biotech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% Y-o-Y to a record INR248 crores, with CDMO up 29% and Trade Generics hit by codeine discontinuation.
543329|2026-06.overview: Revenue hit a record INR248 crores, up 18% Y-o-Y, extending the company's record-revenue run to 14 consecutive quarters. Adjusted EBITDA (ex-ESOP) rose 26% Y-o-Y to INR34 crores, with PAT of INR25 crores up 37%. The Generic Formulations CDMO vertical grew 29% to INR207 crores, while Trade Generics & Institutional fell to INR30 crores after codeine-based products were discontinued. Management said Plant 6 is expected to be fully online at end-H1 FY27, targeting around INR1,100 crores of revenue capacity, and repeatedly declined to attribute the CDMO spike to any specific factor.

financial_highlights.change: lower after codeine discontinuation; Y-o-Y decline not quantified

financial_highlights.value: INR13 crores, INR6.30 per equity share

segments.name: Trade Generics & Institutional
segments.commentary: Revenue INR30 crores after discontinuation of codeine-based cough syrups. Management acknowledged a momentum hit and called it temporary, but did not guide on recovery timing. Analysts noted the ex-codeine base has been flat for 3-4 quarters.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR11 crores, +79% Y-o-Y on a small base. Management described it as a higher-gestation business and cited ongoing registrations, new geographies and plant audits.

segments.commentary: Not separately disclosed; now contributing to overall revenue. Management confirmed that injectables are back on track on customer feedback, inquiries and offtake.

Revenue capacity from current plants plus Plant 6 is put at about INR1,100 crores, with management seeing a further INR100-150 crores possible through debottlenecking.
Maintenance capex runs at INR12-15 crores a year. Management does not give formal guidance on growth.
capex_capacity: Plant 6 mechanical completion is done; validations and customer audits are ongoing, with commercialisation targeted for end-H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 29% CDMO growth sustainable, and is injectables adding to it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly growth should not be read as a base, and that injectables have been contributing for some time without a specific quarter-driving factor. Long-term drivers have not changed.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company close the gap in Trade Generics after codeine is removed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to more SKUs (150-200 in the range, with much room to grow), new state and geographic openings, and better execution. It declined to give a growth outlook.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak utilisation, and can revenue go beyond INR1,100 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR1,100 crores is a base level. Efficiency initiatives could add 10-15%, and INR100-150 crores more is possible with Plant 6, while peak utilisation is 60-65%, stretchable to about 70%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise about 17% ex-ESOP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited volume-driven contract manpower, annual increments and a retrospective Uttarakhand minimum wage increase notified about 2-3 months earlier. It said nothing was extraordinary.

qa_highlights.question: Has the API price environment changed the top line?

qa_highlights.question: How long from planning to revenue for the next expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a brownfield oral solids expansion takes about 1 year, a new dosage form takes longer, and it favours incremental capacity over large blocks.

Exports remain small (INR11 crores) and lumpy, and dossier wins are not disclosed.

544913|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs.107 crore, up 36% YoY, led by domestic facade (Rs.62 crore, +93%) and fenestration (Rs.6 crore, +127%), while international fell 12% to Rs.39 crore on delivery timing. EBITDA grew 9% to Rs.23 crore, and margin fell to 21.3% because of lower international contribution and a shift to DDP freight billing at cost. Management attributed about 1.5 points of the margin gap to freight pass-through and said the underlying margin is in line with FY26. PAT of Rs.17 crore grew more slowly than EBITDA due to lower other income (prior-year property sale gain) and higher depreciation from new capacity. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 25% revenue growth, 23-25% EBITDA margin and 18-20% PAT margin, while flagging a weak first half and a heavier Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why has margin risen above pre-COVID levels on lower revenue?

533655|2026-06.headline: Triveni Turbine Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.2% to ₹4.43 bn, but EBITDA margin fell to 18% from 25.8% on export deferrals and low-margin legacy orders.
533655|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations grew 19.2% YoY to ₹4.43 bn, with domestic sales up 27.4% to ₹2.4 bn and exports up to ₹2.03 bn. EBITDA was ₹797 mn (18% margin vs 25.8%) and PBT was ₹697 mn (down 20.1%, 15.7% margin vs 23.5%). Management attributed the margin fall to a higher domestic mix, export deliveries deferred by freight costs rising 3-4x, a near-zero-margin NTPC CO2 energy storage project, and legacy orders priced before commodity inflation. Order booking rose 6.1% to ₹5.68 bn, led by exports and aftermarket, while domestic and product bookings declined.</overview>

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹2.4 bn, up 27.4% YoY, but domestic order booking fell 35.4% YoY and domestic enquiries declined. Management says the domestic market is broadly weak across industries.

segments.commentary: Revenue ₹2.03 bn (48.8% share). Export orders were 68% of Q1 bookings (vs 47%), up 53.4% YoY; exports are 57% of closing order book. Growth is led by Southeast Asia, Africa, Europe and the US.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of top-line and bottom-line growth for full-year FY27, but growth will be back-ended into H2.
Roughly ₹175 mn of NTPC CO2 project execution remained at end-Q4; management said about 40% falls in Q1 and Q2 with the rest in Q3, while the commissioning is expected around end-Q2 or early Q3.
Management reiterated that a PBT margin above 20% is sustainable in the medium to long term; no specific H2 margin number was given.
US subsidiary is targeted to break even in FY27; product sales from the US are expected to be executed mainly in FY28.
Management expects lumpy quarterly results for a couple more quarters, both positive and negative.
capex_capacity: US facility utilisation in FY27 will be adequate but not high; significant Q1 losses at the US subsidiary were attributed to the absence of an order book.
Execution cycle guidance: under 15 MW about 7-8 months; 15-45 MW about 9-12 months; 30-45 MW about 14-15 months; about 18 months for 100 MW.
Management indicated it is ready to manufacture up to 250 MW class sub-critical packages if NTPC introduces such a policy; participation not yet decided.
Heat pump plus MVR combined solution is in early customer deployment with a demo unit and initial MVR orders in execution; ORC enquiries rising, including in the Americas.
demand_pricing: Export share of Q1 order booking rose to 68%. Management attributed the export execution delays to freight rates rising 3-4x and reduced vessel availability; FOB contracts mean freight is borne by clients.

Bought-out items range 30%-70% of order value depending on the order; all contracts are fixed-price, so commodity inflation during execution is absorbed by Triveni.
US data centre demand is rising as gas turbine lead times extend to 3-5 years; US enquiries have been converted slowly (more than 12 months), with product orders expected first.

Management said the domestic margin decline came from legacy orders booked when commodity prices were volatile and competition was intense, and from lower pricing on the current execution mix. Management expects higher order-booking margins going forward and a rupee benefit.
