qa_highlights.question: What is the domestic enquiry trend and reason for the slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give quarterly enquiry numbers, cited weakness in India across industries, flat-to-declining conversations, and longer order gestation periods. Green shoots in Europe and strength in the US and Southeast Asia were noted.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin decline comes from bought-out components and cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Lalit Agarwal said bought-out content varies by order from 30% to 70% of the balance of the order value, and contracts are fixed-price, so commodity increases during execution were absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: What sustainable margin should be expected for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a specific number, but reiterated that a PBT margin above 20% is achievable over the medium to long term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the US aftermarket and product business?
qa_highlights.answer: The US aftermarket contributed less than 10% of the figure implied by analysts because of state-level certification. US product enquiries are closer to commercial discussions, with product sales expected to lead, followed by refurbishment.

qa_highlights.question: How long are execution cycles for different order sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: Under 15 MW about 7-8 months; 15-45 MW about 9-12 months; 30-45 MW about 14-15 months; about 18 months for 100 MW.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on H2 execution of legacy orders and on the rupee and new orders with higher margins; Q1 PBT margin was 15.7%.
Domestic order booking fell 35.4% YoY and domestic enquiries are declining; the 6-12 month gestation means the effect may appear in later quarters.
Freight costs and vessel availability could defer more export dispatches into Q2 and Q3.
The US subsidiary is loss-making with break-even targeted in FY27; the US product conversion timeline is more than 12 months.
The CO2 energy storage project (with NTPC) is a technology-validation order that has limited profit potential in the early years; commissioning is expected around end-Q2 or early Q3 FY27.
533655|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on full-year growth and H2 recovery, but cautious and somewhat defensive on Q1 margins. Management gave few numbers on enquiries, margin guidance and US timelines, and attributed the weakness to geopolitics, freight and legacy pricing.

Kharsang output rose from about 12,300 to 17,400 BOE and crude realisation rose to about $95.5/bbl from $70.8/bbl. Standalone PBT before exceptionals fell to INR12.5 crore from INR30.4 crore, due to inventory-related cost offsets. B-80 output was hit by higher water cut, and the HPCL-stored crude is being resold to third parties at a slower pace than expected, with a further mark-to-market loss expected. Management is relying on debt to fund the B-80 workover and three-well programme.

qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the targets. EBITDA margin was 22.5% (FY23), 22.6% (FY24), 18.4% (FY25) and about 13.5% (FY26), with PBT of 8.8%, 7.7%, 9% and about 5.3%. It guided FY28 EBITDA margin of 22-24% and PBT around 10%, based on project-level build-up and not land sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why is sales value growing 40-50% while collections grow only 26-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Collections follow project progress: 10% on booking, 20% after agreement, then construction-linked. Launches are back-ended to Q3-Q4, so collections ramp in later quarters and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of FY27 launch GDV versus sustenance sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sustenance sales of INR1,400-1,500 crores look right; the balance comes from new launches off about 7.23 million sq ft supply worth about INR6,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kolkata land plan and value?
qa_highlights.answer: About 104-106 acres approved for apartments, villas and plots, with a 3-year build and 5-year handover target. Management estimates INR6.5-7.5 crores net contribution per acre and INR1,200-1,400 crores free cash over about five years; bulk sale at INR3.5-4 crores per acre was rejected as uneconomic.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 PBT margin 10% and what drives the margin recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PBT margin guided at 8-9%. Margins are product-mix driven: Grand One, Shankari and Sunshine One handovers are low-margin, with Sunshine 2 and 3 and post-2019 launches expected to restore mid-20s EBITDA margin and 9-10% PBT, mainly in H2 FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will tax write-backs boost PAT in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tax write-backs cannot be predicted; they arise only from loss-making subsidiaries recognising deferred tax assets. PAT growth guided at 20-25% without a write-back assumption.

532827|2026-06.headline: Page Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 7.9% to INR14,204 mn and PAT fell about 4%, as ~3 days of billing slipped into Q2 on logistics disruption.
532827|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 7.9% YoY to INR14,204 mn and volume rose 5.7% to 61.9 mn pieces, but management said quarter-end logistics and manpower disruptions left about three days of billing undelivered. EBITDA fell 1.9% YoY to INR2,890 mn, with margin at 20.3% versus 22.4% a year earlier, as input costs (cotton, nylon, synthetics) spiked from March–May. PAT declined about 4% to INR1,928 mn. Management said most of the delayed billing and the May price increase (about 2.2% weighted average) should show up in Q2, and it reaffirmed double-digit annual volume growth and the 19–21% EBITDA margin range.

financial_highlights.change: vs 22.4% in Q1 FY26; within planned 19–21% range
from 73 days at start of quarter
from 56 days at start of quarter

segments.name: Jockey innerwear and core range
segments.commentary: Volume growth of 5.7% was ahead of revenue growth of 7.9%-minus-mix, with lower-ASP accessories and socks gaining share due to scheme design. Schemes are now spread across quarters under the ARS model.

segments.name: Groove 3 (street fashion line)
segments.commentary: Launched in June 2026 across close to 500 exclusive brand stores; management said sell-through looks very good.

segments.name: Disney/Marvel character merchandise
segments.commentary: Go-to-market planned for end-June; a large portion of revenue expected in Q2.

Majority of the roughly three days of undelivered billing (seven days vs normal three to four) expected to be reported in Q2.
Full benefit of the mid-May price increase to flow through in Q2 under FIFO billing; difference between volume and value growth expected to widen from Q1 levels.
Annual EBITDA margin outlook retained at 19–21%.
Management intends to hold prices and drive volumes if margins stay within 19–21%; another price action possible if input costs re-escalate.
Marketing spend to remain at 4–5% of revenue.

Odisha and K.R. Pet manufacturing facilities are scaling up progressively.

E-commerce: two fulfilment centres (one South, one North); management prefers outright model over marketplace.
Consumer data platform (CDP) expected to go live by end-August 2026, subject to DPDP Act compliance.
DMS rollout: all distributors targeted on DMS by end-2026 or Q1 FY28 at latest.
demand_pricing: Volume growth of 5.7% was driven by healthy consumer demand across EBOs, e-commerce and wider retail.
Price increases: about 2.5% in January 2026 (product-quality related, not input-cost linked) and about 2.2% weighted average in mid-May 2026 (input-cost linked).
Input cost inflation in cotton, nylon, synthetic fabrics and packaging peaked in May; prices eased by late June but remain volatile.
Management said the May price increase only partially offsets the raw material escalation.
Pricing is uniform across channels with no flash sales or markdowns; quick commerce is on an outright model.
Secondary growth was better than primary in Q1 because of undelivered billing; tertiary and EBO performance was better than Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price increase offset input costs and restore margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The May increase only partially covers input costs; the full benefit flows from Q2 and management said prices have eased below April–May levels, so it is a 'waiting game'.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not intend to reduce inventory further, that Q1 had some lost sales from non-availability, and that inventory is now at an optimum level.

qa_highlights.question: What were the logistics and manpower disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party logistics and labour concerns linked to fuel price rumours, fuel availability and a June SAR drive disrupted last-mile delivery to distributors at quarter end.

qa_highlights.answer: Offline swim consolidation as business moved online; Speedo multi-brand outlets fell to about 700 in Q1, and about 950 counting Q4 and Q1 combined.

Logistics and third-party labour reliability at quarter end.

524332|2026-06.headline: BCL Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore (10.5% margin) despite revenue falling to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore.
524332|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue fell to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore, mainly due to closure of the edible oil unit and exit from packaged oil. EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore, with margin up 370 bps to 10.5%, and PAT rose 6% to INR 36 crore (5.7% margin). Distillery EBITDA margin improved to 12.41%, while ENA realisations fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. A fire at a 200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol tank on 19 June 2026 shut that plant temporarily; management said insurance recovery is virtually certain and no net loss was booked. Management also completed the acquisition of the remaining 25% of Svaksha Distillery and reduced working capital borrowings, but deferred the Fatehabad 250 KLPD project and the Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project.

Portfolio reached 6.94 GW (1.87 GW installed, 5.07 GW WIP). Management guided to 30-40% revenue growth (softened from the chairman's 40-50%) and a PAT margin below the earlier 16-18% for FY27. The CFO Salim Yahoo is leaving and Kapil Kriplani joins as Group CFO.</overview>

segments.name: IPP (Independent Power Producer)
segments.commentary: Portfolio of 2.57 GW; expected to generate more than 390 crore units annually at full run rate; management cites 85-90% EBITDA margin on IPP and 25-year PPAs. Management expects IPP revenue of at least INR1,000 crore once 1 GW is at peak, with peak timing in Q3 or Q4 FY27.

segments.name: CPP (Captive Power Producer) / EPC
segments.commentary: Portfolio of 4.37 GW; CPP order book approximately INR5,000-plus crore. Management said EPC is about 83% of total revenue, and that margins were hit by higher costs for steel, cables, MMS structures, logistics and cranes.

segments.name: Sun Drops Energia (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Management expects Sun Drops to cross INR1,500-odd crore of top line in FY27 across IPP and CPP; Sun Drops IPO is mentioned as upcoming.

segments.name: KP Energy (EPC subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Per analyst, EBITDA margin fell from 22% to 12%; management attributed it to a pure EPC model with greater exposure to cost inflation and shared-cost absorption.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 30-40% YoY for FY27, with management saying it is being conservative given geopolitical conditions; chairman had earlier spoken of 40-50%.
PAT margin for FY27 expected to be below the earlier 16-18% guidance; no specific revised number given.
Management expects the full earning contribution of new IPP assets to build through the rest of FY27, with most projects targeted for energization by September and full stabilisation in FY28.
Long-term debt to net worth targeted at a maximum of 3:1; management said leverage could rise to around 3x as project loans are drawn.

Annual interest cost for the full IPP capacity estimated at around INR450 crore (at about 8.5%); IPP depreciation estimated at about 5% on the building component, with total IPP capex potentially INR5,000-6,000 crore in FY27-28.
Botswana: 500 MW first phase under planning; management said no revenue from Botswana in FY27, with revenue in later years.
capex_capacity: Total portfolio 6.94 GW as of June 30, 2026 (up 71% YoY from 4.06 GW): 1.87 GW installed plus 5.07 GW work in progress.
Commissioned 0.85 GW and booked 2.88 GW of fresh orders over the year.
Land bank 8,657 acres; power evacuation capacity 5.10 GW; 133 sites total after entering Rajasthan.
BESS: 565 MW / 1,130 MWh project executed, financial closure under process.
Floating solar: 142 MW EPC order at Kadana Dam, Gujarat under execution.
150 MW wind for GUVNL: PPA signed and financial closure achieved; 300 MW SJVN-backed wind PPA signing under process.
Botswana: MoU with government for 5 GW; 500 hectares of land acquired (transcript corrected from 500 acres); PPAs at an advanced stage.
Energy trading licences from GERC (intrastate) and CERC (interstate); trading in pilot mode.
UAE: solar plus BESS project for a containerised data centre awarded to subsidiary Sun Drops Energia, under execution.
demand_pricing: Management said data centres are an emerging opportunity with inquiries ongoing, but no order share was quantified.
Growth slowed below guidance because utility-scale billing for customers such as Coal India, Adani Group and Aditya Birla Group slipped into Q2.

Geopolitical conditions raised costs of steel, cables, MMS structures, logistics and cranes; management said costs were partly absorbed and partly passed on to customers, and that sales were not affected.
Inventory built up at end-March to secure materials amid geopolitical disruption; it fell somewhat in Q1 and is expected to decline further as projects complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why was execution slow versus guidance, with growth of 16% against the 40-50% previously cited?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shortfall was billing timing on utility-scale projects, and that it is now guiding to 30-40% growth, being conservative due to geopolitical factors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the sharp fall in CPP and KP Energy gross margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed higher balance-of-plant, logistics and cost inflation from geopolitical conditions; KP Energy is pure EPC with about 17-18% of its revenue from IPP, so it was more exposed.

qa_highlights.question: Will IPP stay at a share of the revenue mix, and is the balance sheet strained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to keep IPP at about 20-odd% of revenue mix; leverage is 'below 3' and may rise towards 3x as loans for projects due by September are drawn, with EPS expected to recover as plants stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What are the annual interest cost, EBITDA and depreciation for the IPP business at full scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest is around INR450 crore a year at about 8.5% on roughly INR5,000 crore of debt; IPP EBITDA is 85-90% with revenue of at least INR1,000 crore once 1 GW peaks, expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27; depreciation is about 5% on the building component.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 PAT margin meet the 16-18% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q3 and Q4 would recover only part of the Q1-Q2 gap, so the FY27 PAT margin would be lower than 16-18%; full benefit is expected in FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: What was Q1 cash flow from operations?
qa_highlights.answer: Salim Yahoo estimated about INR140-150 crore, computed as PAT of about INR94 crore plus quarterly depreciation of about INR45 crore.

500463|2026-06.headline: Black Box Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR1,719 crore (+24% YoY) and EBITDA rose 38% to INR160 crore; FY27 revenue guided at INR7,800-8,000 crore.
500463|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR1,719 crore (+24% YoY), with EBITDA of INR160 crore (+38% YoY, margin 9.3%, up 90 bps) and PAT of INR56 crore (+18% YoY). The quarter included about two months of consolidation from the Brazilian acquisition 2S, which contributed about INR60 crore. Order bookings were US$339 million and the order backlog reached about US$950 million (up 83% since the transformation began). Management reiterated FY27 guidance, with FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 9.3-9.4%, and said growth would be weighted to H2 and spill into FY28.

financial_highlights.change: up 83% since start of transformation; company said up 83% YoY in opening remarks

segments.name: Hyperscale / data center
segments.commentary: Management expects hyperscale to grow about 25% in aggregate across the business, with data center tenures of 24-36 months. A new US hyperscaler order of US$131 million (about INR1,240 crore) was added, with work on site starting from November.

segments.name: Non-hyperscale enterprise
segments.commentary: Expected to grow at modest double-digit, about 10%, lagging the hyperscale cycle, with enterprise spend expected to follow with a lag.

segments.name: Product business (TPS / KVM, Emerald)
segments.commentary: Still loss-making at EBIT level as revenue grows; management expects about 20% growth in FY27 and says the segment is highly accretive once scale is reached.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue INR7,800-8,000 crore (+23-27% YoY).
FY27 EBITDA INR725-750 crore (+27-32% YoY); EBITDA margin 9.3-9.4% (about +30-40 bps). Medium-term aim is 10% or more at scale.
FY27 PAT INR300-325 crore (+38-50% YoY).

FY27 order bookings US$1.3-1.4 billion (about +32-45% YoY); order backlog at March 31, 2027 of US$1.3-1.4 billion (about +65-75%). Management said the backlog figure may be conservative and gave updated detail after Q2.
Tax rate expected at 10-15% in FY27 and FY28, normalising to about 20% thereafter.
Operating cash flow to EBITDA conversion expected to improve meaningfully over FY26.
Long-term aspiration of INR18,000 crore (US$2 billion) revenue by FY30: about INR12,000 crore organic and INR6,000 crore inorganic.
capex_capacity: Plan to onboard nearly 2,000 professionals to support execution.
Large hyperscale sites are gigawatt-plus; deployment and hiring for the new US hyperscaler order start only from November.
Talent and people investment described as largely done; cash flow expected to turn positive from operations.
Management said supply chain, particularly cables and fibre, improved over the last quarter.
demand_pricing: Management says competition is based on execution capability, scale, and the ability to deploy skilled resources, not on lowest price.
Management estimates the addressable opportunity at US$250-300 billion, with about 60-70% of spending in the US.
Management says the company has executed several hundred megawatts, close to a gigawatt, and is now receiving more invitations to bid (pull rather than push).
Data center orders are described as accretive to margin, and expected to be more accretive at scale.

qa_highlights.question: What was organic revenue growth given 2S was included from May?
qa_highlights.answer: The company said INR60 crore of the INR1,719 crore came from 2S, and the balance is organic. June quarter is seasonally weak for 2S.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow improve given the investment needs suggested by the backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said talent investment is largely complete, operating cash flow should be positive, and cash flow should rise with growth. Working capital still needs funding.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance conservative, given backlog growth ex-long-term projects?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said most backlog execution falls in Q3 and Q4, and it will spill into FY28. FY27 growth is about 22-25% and FY28 growth should exceed that. Backlog could end higher as new orders come in Oct-Mar.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook for non-data center businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said non-hyperscale enterprise is expected to grow about 10%, with a lag behind the hyperscale cycle. Overall growth is about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Will TPS / product business reach profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said the product business is expected to grow about 20% in FY27 and focus on mission-critical products such as KVM/Emerald. Losses should narrow with scale.

qa_highlights.question: Does the margin guidance imply depressed Q2/Q3 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said Q4 should be at or above 10%. Investment in training and talent means guidance is kept at 9.3-9.4% for the year, with 10% or more expected at scale.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from hyperscaler capex moderation?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said current pipeline shows new projects being announced and no slowdown in conversations. Shifts between sites would be absorbed across multiple geographies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive moat?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO cited scale, execution capability, customer relationships, and the ability to fund and train staff. He said competition will exist, and the company is aiming to take share.

risks_watch: Guidance depends on H2 conversion: Q1 was described as seasonally soft, and FY27 growth requires about 30-40% sequential or YoY growth in H2.
Margin: management is holding guidance at 9.3-9.4% because of talent and training investment, and 10% is targeted only at scale.
Customer concentration in hyperscalers: any capex moderation or site delay would affect execution and backlog timing.
Product business (TPS) still loss-making at EBIT level.
Working capital and cash conversion needs to improve meaningfully over FY26.
Tax rate is currently low due to carried-forward losses; it is expected to rise to about 20% after FY28.
Transcript notes that several guidance figures were corrected on the call (backlog, bookings, EBITDA, PAT, margin); use the corrected figures stated in the call.
500463|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on demand and backlog, with explicit caution on margins (guidance held at 9.3-9.4% because of investment in talent) and on H2 execution timing. Management relied on the backlog to support the FY27 numbers and gave limited detail on cash flow and on the product business.

539083|2026-06.headline: Inox Wind Q1 FY27 consol revenue INR872 crores, adjusted EBITDA INR237 crores (~27% margin), PAT INR64 crores; FY27 guidance of 75% revenue growth reaffirmed.
539083|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue was INR872 crores with adjusted EBITDA of INR237 crores, PBT of INR95 crores, PAT of INR64 crores and cash profit of INR153 crores. Management said the pivot toward equipment supply (about 59% of third-party order book as of July 2026) is disrupting near-term revenue, with benefits expected from Q2-end and mainly in H2. The order book is about 4.4 GW after a 200 MW NLC India LOA, and an MOU for 1.5 GW with INOX Clean (500 MW firm). Analysts pressed hard on the H2-weighted guidance, flat year-on-year Wind revenue and the pending INR400 crore deferred revenue, and management largely refused to quantify quarterly numbers.

financial_highlights.change: No year-on-year growth cited; management said Q1 is at par with Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR57.9 crores, of which INR50+ crores operational

segments.name: Inox Wind (WTG and EPC)
segments.commentary: Order book about 4.4 GW as of July 2026, with equipment supply about 59% and turnkey 41% for third-party orders. Management says equipment-supply margin and revenue benefits show from Q2-end, predominantly H2.

segments.name: INOX Green (O&M)
segments.commentary: Q1 total income INR101 crores, EBITDA INR57 crores, PAT INR41 crores; machine availability ~96.3%. Own portfolio ~13.3 GW peak (10.5 GW wind operating, rest solar), with ~6.5 GW acquired wind O&M assets still not consolidated. Management guides ~50% O&M EBITDA margin.

segments.name: INOX Renewable Solutions (IRSL / RESCO, EPC)
segments.commentary: Demerger of power evacuation infrastructure business from INOX Green completed; record date August 1, 2026, listing expected in about 2-3 months pending regulatory approvals. Transformer expansion (4.9 MVA, then 8-20 MVA and 100 MVA+), 4 cranes in operation, and USS launch planned in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 75% over FY26 maintained; management reiterated it as an annual, not quarterly, target.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guidance of 20% to 22% for full year FY27 maintained.
H2 heavy: 70% to 75% of annual business expected in H2; H1 about 25% of annual operations.
INR600 crores annual EBITDA guidance for INOX Green maintained, expected on annualised basis from Q3 FY27 once Wind World India (acquisition expected to complete in Q2 FY27) is consolidated.
Deferred revenue of about INR400 crores from Q4 FY26 to be recognised partly in Q1, fully within FY27.
Working capital guidance on annualised basis maintained; receivable days expected to fall over the next 3-4 quarters.
capex_capacity: 4X wind turbine: foundation complete, tower and main components ready; first prototype installation targeted August 2026, commercial launch about a month later.
Management said it is contemplating higher turbine models (5X/6X) if market demand exists.
ALMM and indigenisation: 80-90% of wind turbine components already indigenised; target near 100% indigenisation before end of calendar 2026 for 3X and 4X.
Transformer capacity expansion in IRSL (Jaipur): 4.9 MVA next, then 8-20 MVA and 100 MVA+ units; own crane fleet of 4 with more in FY27; USS and inverters/capacitor systems planned.
INOX Clean plans 3 GW+ annual IPP capacity; management expects ~25-30% of that to flow to Wind and the balance to Green (O&M) and RESCO (EPC).
demand_pricing: Order book ~4.4 GW as of July 2026, visibility of 24-36 months; 200 MW repeat LOA from NLC India in July via tender.
MOU for 1.5 GW with INOX Clean in June 2026; firm orders for 500 MW so far, balance 1 GW to be firmed later.
Indian wind additions of 1.4 GW in Q1 FY27; total installed wind 57.4 GW; management expects 8-10 GW annual additions over next few years.
Blended realisation for INOX Green's ~4 GW consolidated wind portfolio of INR9-10 lakh per MW (excl. GST); acquired portfolios expected to be substantially higher.
Wind World India: ~4.5 GW O&M portfolio, FY26 revenue ~INR580 crores, ~5% contracted annual price escalation; clients include Tata, ReNew, Greenko, Apraava, Hindustan Zinc.
Management said there is no preferential pricing for INOX Clean versus third-party customers.

qa_highlights.question: What was MW execution in Q1 and what is the FY27 estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give MW numbers; it now guides on revenue and margin rather than machine volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue growth of 30% and 20% EBITDA margin be confirmed for next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: No quarterly guidance; management reaffirmed 75% full-year growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin, with significant improvement expected in Q2 and H2 weighting.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue flat YoY and is the company no longer doing EPC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed flat revenue to the pivot to equipment supply causing disruption; it said Q1 is at par with prior-year Q1 and that EPC continues within IRSL with ~40% of third-party orders turnkey plus 1.5 GW INOX Clean MOU and NLC LOA.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables are high versus peers; how are EPC receivables accounted?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables are recognised under Ind AS 115 on risk-transfer basis and remain elevated until commissioning; management said receivable days fell in Q1 (figures not disclosed) and should drop substantially over the next 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR600 crore Green EBITDA guidance annual or quarterly?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual basis, expected from Q3-Q4 FY27 post consolidation of acquisitions; management would not guide on FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Are INOX Clean terms arm's length versus other customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts are arm's length, INOX Clean is treated as a customer, and there is no preferential pricing for it.

qa_highlights.question: Risks to meeting the 75% growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO cited only force majeure events; said the equipment-supply pivot carries no seen risk to deliverables.

533941|2026-06.headline: Thomas Scott Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 66 crore and EBITDA margin was 13.07%, as management chose to hold prices over discounting.
533941|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations was INR 66 crore (+22% YoY), EBITDA INR 9 crore (+43% YoY, margin 13.07%) and PAT about INR 5 crore (+54% YoY, margin 8.21%). Management said subdued price elasticity led it to protect realisations and shift spend from discounts to performance marketing, which it said lifted gross margins. Wholesale-style aggregator sales now make up about 40% of Thomas Scott brand revenue. Finance costs rose sharply on working capital tied to a fire-related insurance claim that is still pending.</overview>

segments.name: Thomas Scott (own brand)
segments.commentary: Revenue close to INR 25 crore, up 34% YoY, driven by online-first approach, rapid launches and data-led merchandising. About 40% of brand revenue came via aggregator bulk orders booked at wholesale prices under marketplace channel.

segments.name: Licensed and other brands
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 38 crore, up 14% YoY, supported by marketplace relationships and premiumisation. Dockers licence agreements expected to contribute meaningfully in coming quarters.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 4 crore, up 33% YoY, on higher capacity utilisation and marquee customer relationships.

segments.name: Women's wear (newer category)
segments.commentary: Piloted for about two quarters; management says most revenue so far came from testing. Cited as a growth pillar at around 13% of Q1 revenue per analyst question, not disputed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: continue the growth pace of the last two years, with similar margins (confirmed on Q&A).

Management expects healthy margins and aims for consistent EBITDA margin improvement through the year, but may reinvest margin in growth; the 12-15% EBITDA margin range was cited by an analyst and not disputed.
Price discounting may return in Q2-Q4, particularly festive H2, where management expects better ROI.
Women's wear could reach 2x to 3x current revenue in about a year, with gradual scaling rather than sudden growth.
Insurance claim (fire incident, about INR 21 crore of stock insured) expected to settle soon; debt and interest cost expected to normalise after realisation.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity is fully utilised for the last few quarters; the company uses job work and rented capacity to meet demand.
Manufacturing footprint across Sholapur, Bangalore and Gurgaon, with fulfilment centres across India.
Target manufacturing mix: about 50% in-house, 35-40% outsourced (per-piece labour charges, with in-house quality control), and about 5% bought-out goods.
Capex is consistent each quarter but described as modest; the main effort is workforce hiring, training and line efficiency.
Offline stores (Bangalore) are EBITDA positive but ROCE is below online opportunities, so capital is directed online; new stores will be selective.
demand_pricing: Price elasticity was subdued in Q1; management says demand exists but price cuts did not earn adequate ROI, so it chose performance marketing over discounts.
Management attributed cautious sentiment partly to global macro conditions, including LPG shortages; said August sentiment is positive.
Customer acquisition cost is about 4-6% of GMV, with the quarter at the higher end; no precise CAC or payback figure was given.
Wholesale-style aggregator sales booked at B2B price, about INR 10 crore in Q1, equivalent to about INR 15 crore NSV per management; management says these are EBITDA-margin neutral.
Management claims demand exceeds supply capability.
Q1 is an end-of-season sale quarter in which the company chose not to discount heavily.

qa_highlights.question: How do women's wear unit economics and repeat purchases compare with men's wear, and what share is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said unit economics are neutral to favourable versus men's wear, with better return-cost control. Core products such as bottomwear and basic tops show repeat behaviour similar to men's; no share target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Quick commerce strategy and economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Main partner is M-Now (Myntra) at neutral unit economics with no extra fee. Broader quick commerce strategy is still nascent; core categories to be evaluated over the next six to nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Bangalore store performance and expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Stores are EBITDA positive but ROCE is lower than online, so capital goes online. Offline may scale in FY28; new stores will be selective.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue growth slow in ROI for licensed and own brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is a margin-pressured end-of-season sale quarter; it chose not to match discounts and invested in marketing instead. Lost revenue could be recovered in festive H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still on track for prior revenue run-rate and margins in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets unchanged: same growth rate as the last few years and healthy margins, with margin improvement sought while reserving margin for growth investment.

qa_highlights.question: Fire insurance claim and finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance claim (about INR 21 crore of stock, fully insured) is in process; elevated working-capital loans raised to fund inventory are expected to fall once the claim is realised. Exception provisions are small (INR 3-4 lakh).

qa_highlights.question: Dockers deal: B2B or B2C, and effect on premiumisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Dockers agreement is B2C-focused; B2B is used for long-run sourcing orders. More than 94% of revenue is B2C. Dockers fits the premiumisation strategy.

risks_watch: Finance cost rising sharply on working capital; normalisation depends on timing of the insurance claim settlement, which is still in process.
Revenue growth is dependent on the timing of price reinvestment in H2 festive; if festive demand is weak, the growth catch-up may not happen.
Rising other expenses (marketing) and a higher CAC in Q1; watch whether gross margin gains hold as marketing spend rises.
Aggregator/wholesale channel share (about 40% of brand revenue) and its effect on reported revenue vs. NSV; the company reports B2B value, which understates headline sales.
Women's wear is still in a test-and-scale phase; scaling could strain returns and inventory.
Capacity is fully utilised, so growth depends on job-work and rented capacity.
533941|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the platform and long-term ambition, but defensive on Q1 growth, which management framed as a deliberate trade-off to protect price and margin. Evasive on specific CAC, payback, and insurance claim timing, citing process constraints.

500201|2026-06.headline: India Glycols Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 9% to INR1,130 crore and record EBITDA of INR170 crore (+13%), with PAT up 32%.

Circulation held steady market by market to protect copy share in English markets.
Other operating income at HMVL roughly doubled to about INR 20 crore (from about INR 10 crore), mainly job work and scrap sales.
Competitive environment described as likely to remain as is for circulation.

qa_highlights.question: Why use a preferential issue at about INR 24 per share, below book value of about INR 70, rather than a rights issue, given INR 922 crore net cash and a 15% dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all the net cash sits in HMVL, while HT Media and DCL are net debt companies. Preferential issue is faster (2-3 months), gives more certainty of raising the amount and avoids underwriter risk; pricing follows the SEBI formula with no premium. Proceeds will retire 30-50% of debt.

qa_highlights.question: Given the 15% dilution, the valuation and the moral/reputational issue, will the company withdraw the preferential issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not agree to withdraw. It said price-to-book is below 0.5x, the promoters are subscribing on the same terms, and it is raising capital to retire debt and improve EPS. A shareholder said he voted against the resolution.

qa_highlights.question: Is the debt position consistent with earlier statements that the company was debt-free?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt has built up at HT Media over the last 3-4 years post-COVID (Print English and Radio); the combined net cash figure hides this, and the number is not new.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of HMVL's other income jump, and is it MTM?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury gains from mutual funds (NAV-based) plus realised profit on sale of assets; no MTM on investments. Treasury gains depend on yield curve movements and are not predictable.

qa_highlights.question: How will newsprint costs affect Print margins, and can prices be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Newsprint is 25-40% of the bill of materials. Management expects a plateau at current levels, so Q1 Print margin of about 13% can be used as a baseline if prices don't rise further; cover price increases are difficult.

qa_highlights.question: What drove ad revenue growth at Print, and what share is government revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly commercial yield improvement with volumes holding; government revenue grew on volume and pricing. Management did not disclose the government share and called it 'substantial' but smaller than commercial.

513097|2026-06.headline: Shivalik Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 33.4% YoY to ₹182.2 crore and PAT rose 44.9% to ₹33 crore, with FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-30%.
513097|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 33.4% YoY to ₹182.2 crore, EBITDA rose 35.2% to ₹43.2 crore and PAT rose 44.9% to ₹33 crore. Shunts grew 18.7% while bimetals grew 7.4%, and management attributed roughly half of the revenue growth to higher silver prices. Management said margin gains came mainly from shunt conversion from strip to finished parts, which it considers sustainable. The company also received consent to operate for Phase 1 of its Pune facility for cell connecting systems and bus bar assemblies, serving one two-wheeler OEM for now.

financial_highlights.metric: Share of growth from value-add in shunts
financial_highlights.value: ~70-75% of shunt value-add growth from conversion to parts; rest from material/commodity

segments.name: Shunts

segments.name: Bimetals (thermostatic)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 7.4% YoY; management says customers are signalling first quantity uptick in 4-5 quarters, mainly domestic. Expects about 44-45% of standalone revenue; utilisation about 40-45%.

segments.name: Contacts (wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Expected to be 30-35% of consolidated revenue; about 60% of contacts revenue goes to switchgear. Silver price roughly doubled YoY, with about half of revenue growth attributed to silver.

segments.name: Cell connecting systems / bus bar and PCBA assemblies
segments.commentary: Minimal revenue in Q1 as full production began only in the last month of the quarter; expected 15-16% of total revenue in first year. Main Pune manufacturing becomes fully operational only in October.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall revenue growth guided at roughly 20-30%, dependent on customer forecasts; management said it is early in the year.
Expects cell connecting systems and bus bar revenue to step up in the current and upcoming quarters, with Pune full operation from October.

Management sees a potential ₹300-400 crore business from the Pune facility in about 3 years, with about 10-15% in year 1, ₹150-200 crore in year 2 and ₹300 crore onwards thereafter; these figures are explicitly subject to change.
Pune incremental capex estimated at about ₹20-25 crore, with the high-capex processes already in place at Solon.
Expects one customer's share to stay below 17-18% in the maximum case, versus 35-40% at its historical peak.
capex_capacity: Pune Phase 1 received consent to operate after the quarter; currently capable of serving only one two-wheeler EV model.
Pune main manufacturing facility expected to be fully operational only in October 2026.

Thermostatic bimetal capacity utilisation about 40-45%; capacity expansion is slow and capex-intensive.
Pune incremental capex about ₹20-25 crore; the Pune facility has room for expansion.
demand_pricing: Large US customer has given expectations for this year that management describes as encouraging; the resurgence is in higher value-added business.
Two-wheeler EV and smart meter applications cited as main growth end-uses for shunts.
Shunt accuracy, not price, is the key buying criterion; a recently patented design by a large resistor customer is winning share, including from some Chinese OEMs.
Bimetal export opportunities with existing customers restarted after the US tariff pause; these are expected to add revenue in about 4 quarters.
Silver prices about double YoY and slightly lower QoQ; copper prices up substantially YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 guidance for top line and margins, split by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave overall revenue growth of about 20-30% and a segment mix: bimetal 44-45%, shunts 54-55% of standalone; contacts 30-35% and assemblies about 15-16% of consolidated revenue in year 1. No margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 33% growth is sustainable excluding commodity prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a 20-30% range going forward and said about half of the revenue growth came from silver, with shunt value-add conversion driving margin gains that are considered sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Pune bus bar opportunity and incremental capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Potential business of ₹300-400 crore in about 3 years, with capex of about ₹20-25 crore since high-capex processes already exist at Solon; figures subject to change.

qa_highlights.question: Are new verticals or inorganic moves planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Two or three opportunities identified (greenfield or technology partnership) in electronics specialty material and automotive fuses; at least one or two may be announced soon, possibly via JV, licence or acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: How concentrated is the largest customer?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak exposure was 35-40%; even in the maximum case this year it will not exceed 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bimetal business turning around?
qa_highlights.answer: For the first time in 4-5 quarters customers signal quantity uptick, mainly domestic, including real estate and infrastructure; export developments restarted, expected to add revenue in about 4 quarters.

risks_watch: Revenue growth is partly commodity-driven: silver roughly doubled YoY and copper rose substantially, and management says about half of growth came from silver.
Pune ramp depends on one OEM's EV two-wheeler model; the ₹300-400 crore opportunity is explicitly subject to change and phase 2 qualifications are still pending.
Bus bar and cell connecting system revenue is still minimal in Q1; watch October full operation and the next quarter's revenue step-up.
Bimetal volume recovery is early (quantities only, one quarter of evidence) and export developments are still in testing.
Management did not give margin guidance, and it cited employee cost increases alongside margin expansion.
513097|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the shunt and value-add story and on Pune's prospects, but evasive on specifics. Management declined to quantify several items under NDA (customer names, JV partners, the precious metal share) and repeatedly stressed that forecasts are early and subject to change.
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 is a strong start to the year and gives us further evidence that Shivalik is progressing higher on the value curve.
So, yes, that part is sustainable, because those parts are here to stay.

531859|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.7% YoY to INR137.6 crore, with EBITDA up 43.7% to INR20.9 crore and margin at 15.2%.
531859|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue from operations was INR137.6 crore against INR117.9 crore a year earlier, up 16.7% YoY. EBITDA rose 43.7% to INR20.9 crore, with margin expanding 286 bps to 15.2%, and PAT rose 83% to INR10.7 crore (7.8% margin). Management attributed the sequential revenue moderation to the US-Iran war and a fuel and gas supply crisis in March-April, which it says is now largely resolved. The consolidated order book stood at about INR1,692 crore as of August 11, 2026, with INR1,526 crore at OFPL wagons and INR166 crore in coach interiors. Management also laid out smart wagon, next-gen wagon, wagon leasing and JV initiatives.</overview>

segments.commentary: About 16% of revenue; the business holds over 30% market share with installed capacity of about 3,600 coaches per annum. Management expects other businesses to grow 8-10%.

qa_highlights.question: How many wagons does the INR1,526 crore OFPL order book represent and what is the execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3,800 wagons, executed at about 200 wagons per month from Q3 FY27 (October-December).

qa_highlights.question: Capacity expansion plans and capex?

qa_highlights.question: Why did freight revenue not grow in FY25-FY26 (INR458 crore to INR409 crore), and what changed?

qa_highlights.question: Debt, cash flow and leverage outlook?

Bookings normalised to INR 105.7 crores (1.26 lakh sq ft) after the exceptional Q4 FY26 launch quarter. Margin gains were driven mainly by the high-margin horizontal Imperia Phase 2 project, which accounted for about 85% of quarterly revenue. Management added a 50+ acre Lucknow land contract and about 15 acres of aggregated land, but gave no firm FY27 sales or booking guidance and was cautious on Faith (Trinity) launch traction.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 37% EBITDA margin in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue mix shifted to Imperia Phase 2, a high-margin horizontal project (about 60% gross margin), while Q1 FY26 was dominated by a lower-margin vertical project; management expects horizontal projects to keep margins higher.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Imperia Phase 2 revenue is recognised, and how much is left?

qa_highlights.question: How much legacy ready inventory remains and how much can be sold in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Why is Faith tower bookings traction weak, and how is the booking figure reconciled with area?
qa_highlights.answer: Faith launched mid-June after war-related delays; the sample flat was ready 10-15 June, with 2-3 bookings and 20-25 in pipeline. Rajiv Khurana said the slides now show area allotted rather than area booked, since allotment follows booking, and the two are not directly comparable.

segments.name: Oleo chemicals (Platinum Oleo Chemicals)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR 5.3 crore. FY27 target of INR 65-70 crore per management, with INR 150-200 crore targeted over three years. Seed marketing is via CDMO, with exports to Malaysia and Turkey, and own manufacturing is planned in about 1.5 years.

segments.name: Rivadu Lifesciences (pharma)
segments.commentary: Business model still being defined. Some revenue began this quarter, with collaborations with overseas companies under negotiation. No figure given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 30-40% reiterated, though management said the Egypt contribution is now lower than earlier planned.
Egypt revenue for FY27 cut to INR 30-35 crore from an earlier INR 50-60 crore estimate.
EBITDA margin guidance of 13-15% and PAT margin of 11-12% for coming months, reaffirmed from the previous call.
Egypt plant (60,000 tpa, about INR 67-68 crore capex) to start commercial production before 31 December 2026; Egypt top line of INR 250-300 crore over three years.
Palghar expansion peak potential of INR 700-800 crore over three years; top-line CAGR of about 35% over three years.
Stearates plant (6,000 tpa) now expected September/October 2026 versus earlier August, due to an equipment delay.
Oleo FY27 revenue INR 65-70 crore (management), vs analyst question of INR 55-60 crore; management said it was 'very positive'.
capex_capacity: Palghar expansion (~60,000 tpa: 24,000 tpa lead-free PVC, 24,000 tpa CPVC, 12,000 tpa lubricants and others) commenced commercial production 21 May 2026; CPVC partial operations from August 2025. Palghar capex about INR 71 crore.
Total Indian capacity expected to reach 85,000+ tpa on full ramp-up of the expanded facility.
Utilisation of the new capacity expected at around 30-35% in Q2-Q3 FY27, per CFO.
Egypt plant (60,000 tpa; mainly lead stabilisers) capex about INR 67 crore (management also cited a total of ~INR 68 crore). Commercial production targeted before 31 December 2026.
Stearates plant (6,000 tpa) delayed to September/October 2026 due to equipment delay. Oleo manufacturing plant planned in about 1.5 years; land already acquired.
demand_pricing: Pipe demand degrew in Q1 across pipe companies, per management; demand has picked up from August and management expects good demand through December as PVC prices stabilised and turned upward.
CPVC: a demand-supply gap exists with supply exceeding demand, so the company pushed sales in Q1. Management expects margin recovery only in Q3 or Q4 FY27.

Raw material supply disrupted by shipping and war-related freight costs; some raw materials bought locally, which pressured margins. Management says the company cannot pass on sudden freight, CFS and transport costs in this environment.
Management said pricing is not under pressure: competitors and the company 'understand the same pricing levels'. Competitors in lead-free: Baerlocher, Reagens; Goldstab mainly lead-based.

Lubrizol/Aditya Birla CPVC resin capacity, plus Reliance and Meghmani resin plans, described by management as complementary to its CPVC additives business. Supply to Supreme and Prince Pipes for 1-2 years.
Sales-related expenses fell sharply as the company skipped exhibitions in Q1; ECL provisions were also lower.

512529|2026-06.headline: Viyash Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to Rs 946 crore, EBITDA margin expanded to 21.6% (up ~530 bps) and PAT more than doubled to Rs 79 crore.
512529|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 946 crore (up 19.5% YoY, 2.9% QoQ), with EBITDA of Rs 205 crore and margin of 21.6% versus 16.2% a year earlier. PAT of Rs 79 crore is after about Rs 19 crore of incremental ESOP cost tied to the post-amalgamation grant. Net debt fell to Rs 86 crore (0.1x EBITDA), and management said the Sequent-Viyash integration is complete. Human API revenue was flat QoQ due to customer deferrals during raw material price volatility, which management expects to reverse in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: vs 51.9% in Q1 FY26 (~+220 bps YoY)
vs 16.2% in Q1 FY26 (~+530 bps YoY)
vs Rs 20.4 crore in Q1 FY26
Net debt/EBITDA 0.1x vs 0.24x last quarter, ~1x a year ago

financial_highlights.value: Rs 25 crore total, of which Rs 19 crore incremental
financial_highlights.change: Grant of 1.3 crore options, 2.8% of post-amalgamation paid-up capital

segments.name: US (Human formulation)
segments.commentary: Grew about 60% per management (about 45% YoY and 6% QoQ in USD per analyst); Rs 126 crore of Q1 revenue is Human formulation. Management said 60% growth will not repeat, but growth is stable, with a 50-55% US market share.

segments.name: Europe (Animal Health)
segments.commentary: Reported roughly 13% growth; analyst computed EUR 16.8 million flat YoY in constant currency. Management guided full-year Europe growth of 18-20% INR, citing phasing across quarters.

segments.name: Emerging markets (Animal Health)
segments.commentary: Grew 36% (about 23% in USD per analyst); volume growth was 25%, led by Turkey, Brazil and Mexico. Management said 25% volume growth will not be sustained every quarter.

segments.name: Animal Health India domestic
segments.commentary: Grew about 60%; management plans to expand field force and portfolio.

segments.name: API (Human and Animal)
segments.commentary: Broadly flat QoQ due to customer deferrals during raw material volatility. Animal API run-rate about Rs 100 crore, with Vizag capacity commercialised from July. API is about 40-45% of total revenue, roughly two-thirds Human and one-third Animal.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q2 to be the best quarter in company history for API, citing a rebound in orders after customers delayed purchases in June.
FY27 double-digit growth, with management citing 13-15% overall (Human API 13-14%, Animal Health 20%+).
Europe growth of 18-20% INR for the full year; Europe double-digit growth in FY27 excluding FX.
ESOP cost of about Rs 150 crore for FY27 (Rs 25 crore in Q1, about Rs 40 crore per quarter thereafter), falling to Rs 25-30 crore in FY28.
Depreciation plus goodwill amortisation of Rs 25 crore per quarter; drops to about Rs 10-11 crore in Q2, and management expects about Rs 15 crore benefit per quarter from Q3 onward.
Minority interest expected at about 16-17% of total profit; minority stakes in the US and Spain to be fully acquired within 1-2 years.
Capex of Rs 250-300 crore per year; companion animal tablet capacity targeted to be ready by January-February 2027.
Bio For Life (Italy) acquisition SPA signed; closing expected in the next few months and within FY27. Bigger revenue expected after 18-24 months.

Human high-potent oncology first product expected in 2029; majority of new product revenue after 2030. Management targets Rs 1 billion (~Rs 10,000 crore?) aspiration by 2032 implying 18% CAGR from FY27 base.
capex_capacity: Companion animal tablet manufacturing: design finalised, construction to start within weeks, target completion January-February 2027 for exhibit batches.
High-potent formulation development lab completed last week; three high-potent API modules built over last 18-24 months.
Albendazole capacity expanded; US approval received for Vizag site, commercialisation started from July 2026.
R&D ramped up for companion animal products; equipment ordered and people hired.
Annual capex of Rs 250-300 crore, described as modest relative to existing business.
demand_pricing: Human API demand deferred in June as customers waited for raw material/solvent prices to stabilise; management says orders are returning after July.
Management noted it raised prices when raw material costs rose and may reduce them if solvent prices fall.
Human high-potent and oncology products expected to face 50-60% price erosion at generic entry versus 95% for general APIs, per management.
Target market share for new products: 10-15% on average, with 25-30% in best cases.
Europe: Spain performing strongly; Benelux and other countries lagging in tenders. Europe volume and pricing are the main growth drivers.
Animal Health portfolio focus shifted to differentiated products; the company has stopped developing mature commodity products.

544122|2026-06.headline: Entero Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38.2% YoY to INR1,940 crore and EBITDA margin reached 5.0%, already meeting full-year FY27 margin guidance.
544122|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 38.2% YoY to INR1,940 crore (40% like-for-like), with organic growth of 17.8% reported and 19.6% like-for-like versus an underlying pharma market growth of 13.8%. Gross margin expanded 147 bps to 11.4% and EBITDA margin expanded 143 bps to 5.0%, with EBITDA up 94% YoY. PAT rose 72% YoY to INR52 crore, but PAT attributable to owners was INR38 crore (up 37%) after INR14 crore of non-controlling interest. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of ~23% revenue growth ex-acquisitions, 5% EBITDA margin and 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion, and said no major acquisitions are planned in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: entirely calendarisation of prior-year acquisitions; no new acquisitions in Q1

financial_highlights.value: INR14 crore (~27% of PBT before minority interest)
financial_highlights.change: Q4 was about INR17 crore per the call

segments.name: Core pharma distribution
segments.commentary: Majority of business is demand fulfilment with lower gross margins; margin gains attributed to scale-driven procurement. Low-margin sub-distribution accounts exited, which reduced reported growth by about 2.5%.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.commentary: Organic MedTech revenue on track to exceed INR1,000 crore in FY27 and carries higher gross and EBITDA margins than core pharma. Management said the business plays a demand-generation role, not only fulfilment.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained: consolidated revenue growth of ~23% YoY excluding new acquisitions (about 11-12 points from calendarisation of prior acquisitions, rest organic).
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 5% maintained; management aspires to improve further and said H2 could beat guidance depending on H1 performance.
EBITDA to operating cash flow conversion of 50% on an annual basis; OCF is after working capital changes.
FY27 effective tax rate guidance of 22.5%; FY28 guidance to be given near FY27 close.
Interest cost expected to stay broadly in the same range as Q1 for the rest of the year.
Employee cost increments fell mainly in Q1 (effective 1 April); no major increase expected thereafter.

Medium-term: management said it can grow at over 20% in the next 3-4 years, organically and inorganically, and modelling 20% is a safe assumption; ROCE of 25-30% was cited as possible in that period; internal aspiration EBITDA margin above 6%.
No revision to working capital days guidance; management will review after H1.
capex_capacity: Platform: 138 warehouses across 475 districts in 19 states; 72,000+ retail customers, 2,300+ hospital customers, 83,400+ SKUs, 3,000+ manufacturer relationships.
Depreciation: Q1 level expected to be the going-forward run-rate, subject to any major new capex; Q4 included depreciation on certain machines given to customers.
No major acquisitions planned for FY27, though a pipeline exists; a small Andhra Pradesh surgical consumables deal (with Sai Pharma) was completed and is immaterial to revenue.
Around INR200 crore of debt was taken for the last acquisition, disbursed late Jan/early Feb 2026.
demand_pricing: IPM growth has moved to double digits in the last two quarters (earlier 7-9%), driven mainly by volume; management could not isolate a specific cause.
Management said it cannot forecast future IPM growth and built its organic forecast on a lower industry growth assumption.
Growth above market is attributed to wallet share gains from better fill rates, product availability, range and more principal collaborations.
Q1 revenue was partly pulled into Q4 FY26 through preponed government/diagnostic PPP billing, which made the sequential inorganic contribution look lower.
Management said MedTech has limited distributor competition and offers more scope for demand-generation contracts with higher gross margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook for the next 3-5 years without acquisitions, and what ROCE is possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes it can grow at over 20% in the next 3-4 years, organically and inorganically, and sees ROCE of 25-30% possible at the end of that period.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the minority interest exist and when will the call options on it be exercised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said call options were agreed at deal signing at a valuation multiple matching the original acquisition, with exercise windows of 2-5 years; the minority is reinvested rather than paid out. Not all options fall due this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the sequential inorganic revenue contribution decline from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of Q1 government project revenue was billed early in Q4 FY26 because of budget timing, so Q1 had a high base effect.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q4 one-off items recurring in other opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only part of the INR11.5 crore one-offs sat in other expenses; run-rate other expenses of about INR55 crore are expected to be sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 5% EBITDA margin be a floor for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained 5% for the full year but said it targets quarter-on-quarter improvement and may revise guidance after H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did minority interest fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said minority share depends on subsidiary profit; Q4 had a revenue preponement at one subsidiary that boosted its profit share (INR17 crore in Q4 vs INR14 crore in Q1).

risks_watch: Growth in IPM has been unusually strong for two quarters and management cannot explain the cause, so sustainability is uncertain.
Non-controlling interest is about 27% of PBT and call-option buyouts (2-5 year horizon) will need funding, possibly from parent or subsidiary cash.
Q1 revenue was partly pulled into Q4 through government billing timing, so quarterly comparisons may be distorted.
Quarterly OCF is not disclosed; balance-sheet items (gross debt, net debt, OCF) will be given only at half-year and full-year, in September and March.
Interest cost is expected to stay at the Q1 run-rate after the INR200 crore debt drawdown.
Further exits of low-margin sub-distribution businesses could reduce reported growth again (about 2.5% impact in Q1).
544122|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the top line and margins, and clear on the strategy to consolidate and grow organically. Management was evasive on IPM growth drivers, on the quantum of OCF and net debt, and on non-controlling interest funding.

543950|2026-06.headline: Yatharth Q1 FY27 revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 3,927 mn with record EBITDA of INR 917 mn; consolidated EBITDA margin 23.3%.
543950|2026-06.overview:
Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR 3,927 mn (up 51% YoY, 15% QoQ) and record EBITDA of INR 917 mn, with PAT of INR 454 mn. Newer hospitals (Greater Faridabad, New Delhi Model Town, Faridabad Sector 20, Agra) contributed 27% of revenue. Faridabad Sector 20 reached EBITDA breakeven in about 9 months, while the group margin was diluted by new-hospital losses (adjusted margin ex-New Delhi and Faridabad Sector 20 was 28.1%). Management reiterated FY27 guidance of upwards of 24% EBITDA margin and ARPOB growth of 8-10%, and announced a maiden interim dividend of 5% of face value.</overview>

segments.name: Existing hospitals (Noida, Greater Noida, Noida Extension, Jhansi-Orchha)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 2,862 mn, +22% YoY; Noida and Jhansi-Orchha at 90%+ occupancy, Greater Noida 74%, Noida Extension 56%. ARPOB: Noida Extension above INR 50,000, Greater Noida ~INR 43,000, Noida ~INR 35,000, Jhansi ~INR 13,000.

segments.name: Newer hospitals (Greater Faridabad, New Delhi Model Town, Faridabad Sector 20, Agra)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 1,067 mn (27% of revenue). Faridabad Sector 20 at monthly revenue INR 12-13 crore, ARPOB near INR 40,000, EBITDA breakeven in ~9 months. Model Town at INR 8 crore monthly run rate, ARPOB near INR 50,000, breakeven guided to Q3-Q4 FY27. Agra at INR 9-10 crore run rate with 20%+ EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Oncology
segments.commentary: Contributing close to 10% of group revenue with one LINAC at Noida Extension; additional LINACs being added at Faridabad Sector 20 and then New Delhi.

guidance_outlook: FY27: management says it is on track for guidance on revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with upside possible on some parameters; EBITDA margin upwards of 24% (guided 24-25%).
ARPOB growth of 8-10% YoY for FY27 and each year thereafter.

Bed capacity: announced capacity above 3,200 beds (incl. 250-bed Gurugram live in Q1 FY28 and ~450 brownfield beds in Noida cluster over ~15-19 months); target of 5,000 beds now expected in about 2.5 years.
New hospitals expected to reach 25%+ EBITDA margin (~27%) within two years; Faridabad Sector 20 and Model Town to reach 15-20% EBITDA margin about 15-18 months after breakeven.
Depreciation guided at ~INR 29 crore per quarter for the next three quarters; no fresh loans planned in FY27.
Dividend: maiden interim dividend of 5% of face value approved.
capex_capacity: Census beds 1,820 vs 1,655 last quarter; 2,555 total beds in existing network per management.
Gurugram 250-bed hospital under construction, expected to go live in Q1 FY28 with ARPOB potential of INR 50,000+; cost ~INR 1 crore per bed.
Brownfield expansion at Greater Noida and Noida Extension (~450 beds): construction delayed by monsoon; capacity coming live in 15-18 months.
Capex per bed guided at INR 75-80 lakh for the remaining ~1,800 beds (greenfield, brownfield, acquisitions, lease models), up from INR 61.4 lakh cited by an analyst over three years.
Agra: 250 beds installed but only 110 census beds operational; plan to increase census beds.
Funding: acquisition partly debt-funded (~INR 80 crore); management says it is comfortable up to ~2x TTM group EBITDA in debt and will use internal accruals going forward.
demand_pricing: Group ARPOB INR 34,758 (+7% YoY); new NCR premium hospitals (Noida Extension, New Delhi) crossed INR 50,000 for the first time in Q1.

Payer mix: government share ~40% at group level (analyst noted 36% last quarter); attributed to ~2% impact from recent CGHS rate revision, with government volumes declining QoQ. Newer hospitals have under 10% government business and 90%+ cash and private insurance.
Average length of stay fell below 4 days for the first time, attributed to lower government mix and surgical mix in new hospitals.
Doctor attrition ~7% group-wide; senior doctor attrition below 3-4%.
Incremental EBITDA margin on additional occupancy (e.g. Faridabad Sector 20 to 70%) estimated at 22-23%.
Regulatory: a panel recommended capping hospital room rents at 3-star hotel levels; management declined to comment in detail and said no framework has been received yet.

544004|2026-06.headline: IRM Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR 326 crore, with EBITDA ex-other income up 139% YoY to INR 62 crore and PAT of INR 34 crore.
544004|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with volumes at an all-time high of 50.9 MMSCM (up 8% YoY). Margin expansion was attributed to sourcing (HPHT and long-term contracts priced below spot), price realisations, and cost control, with management stating there were no one-time items. Industrial PNG volumes were hit by a 9 March 2026 government notification that cut industrial gas allocation to around 80%. Management guided FY27 EBITDA of INR 7-8/SCM for the remaining three quarters and says the current margin level will likely moderate.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 capex about INR 67 crore

segments.name: Banaskantha (GA)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 48% of Q1 volume and about 46% of profitability; CNG is about 51% of vehicle sales here. Station additions limited to 10-15 in FY27 as the GA is nearing saturation.

segments.name: Fatehgarh Sahib (GA)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 38% of profitability. CNG penetration only 6%; volumes hit by the industrial gas cut linked to the NGT order. Plans for 2 new stations in FY27.

segments.name: Diu & Gir Somnath (GA)
segments.commentary: CNG is 60% of vehicle sales; contributed about 8-9% of profitability. Entire commercial segment converted to PNG, with commercial connections now on PNG. Plans for about 5 new stations in FY27.

segments.name: Namakkal & Trichy (GA)
segments.commentary: Q1 volume about 6 MMSCM, up 102% YoY from 2.84 MMSCM; contributed about 5% of profitability. FY27 volume guidance 25-30 MMSCM (vs 14.2 MMSCM in FY26); about 15-17 new stations planned; more than 80 TNSTC buses running, with a target of 200+ buses.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA expected at about INR 7-8/SCM for the next three quarters; management later indicated overall FY27 around INR 7/SCM and said the 19% EBITDA margin may not be sustained.
Revenue growth of about 25% in FY27 guided; management said a safe range is around 20% or more.
Volume growth of 10-12% in FY27, with total volume targeted at about 250 MMSCM by year-end (FY26: 224 MMSCM).
FY27 capex of about INR 250 crore in total (INR 150 crore for Namakkal and Trichy, INR 50 crore each for Banaskantha and Diu & Gir Somnath / Fatehgarh).
Long-term goal of 20-25% revenue CAGR over the next five years.
Management said same-level performance as Q1 will not be repeated every quarter; performance will be subdued going forward, though it expects QoQ and YoY improvement.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR 67 crore; cumulative capex about INR 1,090 crore.
FY27 capex plan about INR 250 crore; management said it will not exceed this, of which INR 150 crore is for Namakkal and Trichy.
CNG stations at 153 as of 30 June 2026 (up 37% YoY), with 564 dispensing points across four GAs.
Station model mix: franchisee (DODO), OMC and company-operated; the company is moving away from daughter booster and LNG-based models toward online stations.
Diu & Gir Somnath: tap-off from GSPL pipeline and hookup with IOC and GAIL in progress; currently drawing LNG from HPCL's Chhara terminal.
demand_pricing: Pricing: Realisations up about 15% YoY and QoQ per an analyst's calculation (not disputed by management); management said price hikes are linked to sourcing cost and it will not pass on further hikes now that Brent is cooling.

Sourcing mix in Q1 FY27: APM and NWG about 32-33% (APM 21%, NWG 11%), HPHT about 35%, long-term (Reliance, GAIL and others) about 32%, CBG blending 1%, spot about 1%. Q1 FY26 was APM 27%, long-term 27%, HPHT 38%.
HPHT gas at about USD 9/MMBtu versus spot of USD 14-20; industrial volumes benefit from GSPC and Shell long-term contracts running to 2030.
Industrial PNG volumes were hit by the 9 March 2026 notification (about 80% allocation); CNG and domestic/commercial PNG not affected.
Customer base: 86,590 domestic PNG (+13% YoY), 589 commercial (+36% YoY), 228 industrial (+5% YoY).
Management said it is a price taker; competitors and alternative fuel prices are high, supporting margins.

qa_highlights.question: Were there one-time items behind the sharp rise in EBITDA per SCM, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-time items; gains came from pricing, gas sourcing and opex optimisation. It guided FY27 EBITDA of INR 7-8/SCM for the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sourcing mix and how has it changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: APM+NWG about 32%, HPHT about 35%, long-term about 32%. Q1 FY26 was APM 27%, long-term 27%, HPHT 38%; Q4 FY26 APM about 26%.

qa_highlights.question: Namakkal and Trichy volumes and FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 volume about 6 MMSCM (up 102% YoY); FY27 target 25-30 MMSCM, towards the upper end, vs 14.2 MMSCM in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan for FY27 and station additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR 250 crore; stations to be added: 10-15 in Banaskantha, 15-17 in Namakkal and Trichy, about 5 in Diu & Gir Somnath, 2 in Fatehgarh Sahib.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the NGT order in Fatehgarh Sahib?
qa_highlights.answer: The NGT order (February 2026) has not been enforced by the Punjab pollution board; supply cuts began 9 March. Management expects ramp-up once enforced and says new industries must use natural gas to get consents.

qa_highlights.question: Is the promoter license fee a concern and how might it change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a 2% license fee disclosed in the IPO document, not profit to promoters, worth about INR 20-25 crore for the year and already included in PAT; it cannot promise the rate will stay unchanged.

544866|2026-06.headline: Molbio Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue ₹408 crore with 25% EBITDA margin and PAT ₹52.7 crore; FY27 guidance ~25% top-line growth.
544866|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was ₹408 crore in Q1 FY27, with 164 devices and 62.4 lakh test kits sold. EBITDA was ₹104 crore (25% margin) and PAT ₹52.7 crore (about 13%). Export revenue was about ₹67 crore (16% of revenue), helped by a catch-up of orders deferred from Q4 FY26 due to Gulf disruption. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of roughly 25% and EBITDA margin of 24–25%, while cautioning that quarters are non-linear and OptraScan will not be profitable in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Export ~₹67 crore (16% of revenue), includes catch-up of Q4 FY26 deferrals

financial_highlights.value: Molbio standalone ~₹399 crore; Prognosys ~₹11 crore; OptraScan minimal

financial_highlights.metric: OptraScan loss (Q1 FY27 and comparable 5-month period FY26)

segments.name: Truenat molecular platform (core)
segments.commentary: Kits are about 75% of revenue; installed base ~12,500 machines in 90+ countries, 43 assays across 30 diseases; 40M+ cumulative tests. Gross margin 60–63% across devices and kits per management.

segments.name: Prognosys (70% subsidiary, digital X-ray)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹154 crore and PAT ~₹12 crore; management expects similar ~19% EBITDA margin in FY27. Q1 FY27 revenue ~₹11 crore; US FDA approval for digital imaging and EU MDR for X-ray products.

segments.name: OptraScan (60% subsidiary, digital pathology)
segments.commentary: US FDA clearance received July 2026 for end-to-end workflow incl. software and AI; ~$30 million fresh equity invested. Not expected to be profitable in FY27; meaningful contribution expected FY28–FY29.

segments.name: Bigtec Labs (100% R&D subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Bangalore R&D entity with 150+ scientists and 220+ total staff; intercompany kit sales to Bigtec are eliminated on consolidation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at roughly 25%.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 24–25%.
Prognosys expected to deliver ~19% EBITDA margin in FY27, similar to FY26.
OptraScan not expected to be profitable in FY27; meaningful contribution expected in FY28 and FY29.
Device sales expected in the 2,200–2,600 range for the year, in line with historical levels.
HPV-related revenue timing and volumes to be guided next quarter; R&D to stay at 5–6% of revenue.
capex_capacity: IPO proceeds ~₹200 crore: ~₹72 crore for automation and ~₹105 crore for an integrated R&D centre in Bangalore consolidating Bigtec staff.
Current utilisation: ~58% for test kits and ~42% for devices; management says minimal capex can allow doubling of top line from FY26 levels.
Facilities: two kit plants in Goa, device manufacturing in Vizag, a small kit facility in Bangalore, and a Pune site for OptraScan.
Any further manufacturing consolidation in Goa to be funded from internal accruals; no major capex planned beyond what is disclosed.
Certifications: MDSAP; EU IVDR for Truenat CT/NG; EU MDR for X-ray; US FDA for Prognosys imaging and OptraScan.
demand_pricing: TB remains the bulk of the Truenat test mix, mainly public health; management says pricing is similar across diseases in public health.

Government of India HPV validation led by AIIMS; recommended for national rollout; health technology assessment found it cost-effective for women aged 30–45. Volumes not yet quantified; WHO prequalification application in progress.
Two-year TB rate contract with the government signed last month.
India molecular diagnostics share cited at ~90%; ~8,000–9,000 of an estimated 25,000–30,000 TB diagnostic centres are on Truenat.
Pricing is contract-based, not MRP-led; realisation moves driven by device variant mix (Uno/Duo/Quattro), geography and dollar movements.
Export business started around 2023; distributors in 90 countries; ramp expected to take longer, with EU and US entry being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on the HPV tender and test kit off-take?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said approvals are in place and a recommendation has been made to roll out the test in the national programme; volumes will be clearer by next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the life cycle of a Truenat device and are consumables exclusive?
qa_highlights.answer: Devices have not needed replacement; early 2017–18 installations are still running. The system is closed, so only Molbio cartridges and chips are used; each test consumes one cartridge or chip.

qa_highlights.question: What R&D and capex are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D at 5–6% of revenue; ₹72 crore automation and ~₹105 crore Bangalore R&D centre are the major capex items; no other major capex planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split and subsidiary profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Molbio standalone ~₹399 crore, Prognosys ~₹11 crore, OptraScan minimal. FY26 Prognosys revenue ₹154 crore, PAT ~₹12 crore; OptraScan loss ~₹9 crore in the period.

qa_highlights.question: Is device volume growing and how will the TB/other-disease mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Device sales expected in the 2,200–2,600 range, in line with history; kit volumes in Q1 were well above Q4 FY26. Non-TB assays such as HPV and hepatitis expected to contribute meaningfully over 2–3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the TB market share sustainable and what is the realisation trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Truenat is the only WHO-endorsed battery-operated point-of-care TB test; remaining centres use microscopy. Pricing is contract-based; realisation moves reflect device mix and FX, with gross margin of 60–63%.

risks_watch: Quarterly lumpiness: management asks investors to track annually; Q1 was helped by export catch-up of Q4 FY26 deferrals linked to the Gulf situation.
OptraScan loss-making in FY27 and ramp dependent on US lab and hospital adoption after July 2026 FDA clearance.
HPV national-programme volumes and timing not yet quantified; next guidance deferred to next quarter.
Inventory days still high at 230 (trailing 12M), though down from 280 in March.
Export ramp slower than expected; past export volumes have been uneven.
Dependence on public-health TB programme for the bulk of domestic revenue under a two-year rate contract.

544901|2026-06.headline: Purple Style Labs Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR119 crores (from INR106 crores), but EBITDA was negative INR11 crores vs negative INR4 crores a year earlier.
544901|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter with the four large-format experience centres opened in FY26 (Fort Mumbai, South Ex Delhi, Linking Road Bandra, Madison Avenue New York). GMV rose to INR193 crores from INR133 crores and AOV rose to INR86,000 from INR66,000. Revenue from operations was INR119 crores, gross margin held at 36%, and EBITDA and PAT losses were wider than a year earlier on the higher fixed cost base of the new stores. Inventory and net working capital fell year on year, but borrowings rose to INR436 crores at June 2026 from INR371 crores at FY26 end.</overview>
