segments.name: Mumbai (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR50 crores from INR28 crores in the first three months of FY26. Mumbai was the largest market in FY26 GMV at INR205 crores.

segments.name: Delhi (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR39 crores from INR29 crores. Delhi FY26 GMV was INR166 crores.

segments.name: Hyderabad (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR16 crores from INR10 crores.

segments.name: USA (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR29 crores from INR20 crores. New York flagship opened in March 2026 and is the first US store; US was online-only before that.

guidance_outlook: No objective margin or profitability guidance given; management said it would refrain from it.
Q1 is the leanest quarter; management said the cost structure set in Q1 will carry into Q2 absent changes, and clearer trends are expected over the next two quarters.
No significant new experience centre expansion is planned near term; the first full year of the FY26 store investments is to be observed.

EBITDA break-even framing: on a P&L basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed for zero EBITDA, with lease-related costs of INR45 crores (lease interest plus ROU depreciation) included. On a cash basis, lease payments of INR29 crores imply a smaller gap.
Lease interest and ROU depreciation are expected to stay broadly flat unless stores change. Other finance cost should decline as operating profit reduces debt.
capex_capacity: Four large-format experience centres opened in FY26: Fort Mumbai and South Ex Delhi (operational since Q2 FY26), Linking Road Bandra (end-March 2026), and Madison Avenue New York (March 2026).
Store footprint is organised by geography, not by store, so same-store sales are not tracked. Mumbai now runs two large-format centres.
The New York lease is a June-end lease with a shorter tenure, so rent can be adjusted after 12-18 months of performance.
Inventory is expected to stay roughly flat at the current level absent further expansion. Management said inventory is around INR160 crores, with breadth-led singular-unit stock.
demand_pricing: AOV rose to INR86,000 in Q1 FY27, from INR76,000 in FY26 and INR46,000 in FY24. Store AOV is about 2.5x online AOV (India online about INR38,000 vs store about INR90,000 in FY26).
Active designer brands fell to 1,109 in FY26 from 1,910 in FY24. Top 100 designers were 67% of sales in FY24.
Average GMV per customer rose to INR108,000 in FY26 from INR67,000 in FY24. Top 50,000 customers contributed INR702 crores of FY26 GMV of INR722 crores.
Women's wear above INR1 lakh grew to INR312 crores GMV in FY26 from INR187 crores in FY24. Women's wear below INR35,000 fell to INR86 crores from INR162 crores.
Gross margin percentage is said to be broadly flat across price points. Management argued that absolute gross profit per piece rises with higher ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow still negative and borrowings rising despite lower inventory and working capital? When does the business become self-funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lower inventory reflects better inventory management after the FY22-25 build-up, and higher customer advances (INR49 crores) helped working capital. Debt is funding interest costs, and Q1 is not operationally profitable. It asked investors to observe the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the higher-ticket strategy improve gross margin or only AOV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said percentage gross margin is similar across categories. The benefit is in absolute gross profit per piece (e.g., at 40% margin a INR2 lakh piece yields INR80,000 vs INR8,000 for a INR20,000 piece), plus lower supply and customer complexity from the long tail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of outright purchase, consignment and backorder inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consignment split is business-sensitive and not disclosed. Outright purchase forms the inventory on the books. Backorder advances are about one month of revenue, and average delivery is 45-60 days, so backorder customer advances are not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for finance costs in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Lease interest plus ROU depreciation (INR45 crores in the P&L) should stay at Q1 levels absent new store changes. Other finance cost should fall as operating profit reduces debt.

qa_highlights.question: What GMV scale, gross margin and operating leverage are needed for EBITDA positivity?
qa_highlights.answer: On an EBITDA basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed. Adding the lease costs of INR45 crores (P&L) or INR29 crores (cash) raises the required gross profit. Management referred to the detailed P&L on slide 20.

qa_highlights.question: What is the New York store's AOV and break-even, and what is the SSG for mature stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a New York store AOV of about INR1.25 lakh (about USD1,500), based on a 2.5x multiple to online AOV. It did not give a break-even GMV. Same-store growth is not tracked because the company reports by geography.

542907|2026-06.headline: Prince Pipes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5% to INR 609 crore and EBITDA jumped 93% to INR 77 crore (13% margin) despite a 7% volume decline.
542907|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 609 crore (+5% YoY) and volumes were 40,729 MT (-7% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 77 crore (+93% YoY, 13% margin, +600 bps) and PAT of INR 34 crore. Management attributed the margin gain mainly to a better product mix (less agri, more plumbing; more CPVC/PPR versus PVC) and better realisations, while April was a destocking washout after a PVC price correction when import duty was suspended. Management said June and July saw recovery in channel restocking, and it reiterated FY27 guidance of 12-15% volume growth and 11-13% EBITDA margin. Inventory days rose to 100, which management attributed to supply insecurity during the war and a volume shortfall, and it expects normalisation to 65-75 days by end-September quarter.

financial_highlights.value: Net cash almost neutral; gross debt around INR 120 crore (30 June)

segments.name: Bathware
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 13 crore with EBITDA loss of INR 5 crore in Q1; management expects around INR 25 crore quarterly revenue run-rate by December quarter, close to breakeven.

segments.name: Agri vs plumbing/drainage
segments.commentary: Agri, typically 30-35% of annual sales, degrew sharply this quarter while plumbing and drainage grew, lifting mix; Q1 project share guided at 25-30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guidance of 12-15% maintained.
FY27 EBITDA (operating) margin guidance of 11-13% maintained; management said it does not guide gross margin.
Inventory days expected back within 65-75 guidance by end of September quarter; described as not structural.
Debtor days target of around 30 days over the next couple of years; channel finance to be used to reduce receivables.
Capex: no change to plan; about INR 40-42 crore spent in Q1 (mainly second tranche of Bhuj plant takeover), remainder over next nine months.
Management expects no significant inventory gain or loss in Q2 FY27.
Medium-term focus is growth with 11-13% operating margin; ROCE target of 15-20% cited as the business norm.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation around 52-53% currently (production basis); management says 60-65% is the level it targets, with growth of 12-15% taking static capacity to about 60%.
Recently completed large capex cycle at Jaipur, Telangana (Sangareddy) and Begusarai, across all three manufacturing facilities; Begusarai plant in East aids freight benefits.
Q1 capex INR 40-42 crore, mainly completion of second tranche of Bhuj plant takeover; rest of capex to flow over the next nine months.
DECILO polypropylene drainage pipe manufacturing started at Haridwar facility, with installations in residential, hospital and hotel projects.
demand_pricing: April was a washout after PVC prices corrected sharply following temporary suspension of import duty on PVC resin till June 2026, causing channel destocking; May and June recovered and July showed good growth per management.
Management cites a PVC price floor (MIP) of USD 766 per ton, reducing distributor destocking incentive; channel restocking now reflects secondary demand.
Q4 FY26 volume growth was about 25%, which management said was driven by heavy channel restocking and was not sustainable.
Management claims industry-leading volume growth via new distributor and retailer additions (organised and unorganised), DMS and SFA digitisation, and direct scheme payouts to retailers.
CPVC price hikes passed on in phases with 1-2 weeks given to channel.
Management says Prince's volume decline (7%) was lower than industry and peers, implying share gain.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin improve sharply, and how sustainable is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited product mix: lower agri share (agri degrew sharply) and higher plumbing, plus higher CPVC/PPR/PP versus PVC, along with better realisations and operating leverage. It declined to guide gross margin, pointing to 11-13% EBITDA guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 see inventory gains given recent CPVC and PVC price moves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to speculate and said no significant inventory gain or loss is expected in Q2, as higher-cost cargo is coming in after the earlier correction.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still sacrificing margin for volume as it did in the prior quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The earlier pass-through of inventory gains was a one-time tactic in a severe price swing and is not expected to repeat every quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company reach 14-15% EBITDA margin, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had not guided 14-15%; guidance is 11-13% operating margin, driven by mix, pricing power, operating leverage and freight benefits from decentralised plants.

qa_highlights.question: What is the appropriate ROCE and the utilisation level for returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Historically 15-20% ROCE, sometimes higher, is the expectation. Management said 60-65% utilisation is where returns are achieved; it is not focused on 70-75%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to reduce debtor days?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtor days were 40 at June end; management targets about 30 days over the next couple of years, using channel finance and a shift to pull-based demand, with no growth at the cost of credit.

risks_watch: PVC price volatility and the MIP floor: any reversal could trigger destocking again, as happened in April.
Inventory at 100 days versus 65-75 guidance; management expects correction by end-September quarter.
Volume growth credibility: Q1 volume fell 7% after 25% in Q4 FY26; FY27 guidance of 12-15% depends on June-July momentum holding.
Bathware loss (EBITDA minus INR 5 crore) and whether revenue reaches INR 25 crore run-rate by December quarter.
Debtor days at 40 remain high versus peers; target of 30 days is a multi-year goal.
Capacity utilisation at 52-53% means margin expansion depends on volume growth to reach 60-65%.
542907|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth and margin levers, but defensive on the April volume decline and the 100-day inventory, which it attributes to temporary factors. Management avoided quantifying July growth and declined to guide gross margin or Q2 inventory gains.
key_quotes: We will stick to our guidance on growth going forward.
We will be back to our stated guidance by end of September quarter.
Any improvement in margins has to be driven from value-added products like CPVC coming in as well as new products like DECILO.

544867|2026-06.headline: Dhoot Transmission Q1 FY27: revenue up nearly 50% YoY, wiring harness revenue Rs 1,090 crore (+44.6%), EBITDA margin ~15%; FY27 growth guided at 25-30%.
544867|2026-06.overview: Management reported a strong first quarter as its first post-listing call, with growth of nearly 50% YoY, wiring harness revenue up 44.6% and non-wiring harness up 67.7%. EV revenue grew 79% and rose to 27% of total revenue from 24% a year earlier. EBITDA margin improved 110 bps QoQ to about 15%, while raw-material (copper, brass) inflation continued and is being passed through to customers with a roughly three-month lag. Management guided to 15-16% full-year EBITDA margin and 25-30% growth for FY27, while flagging a soft comparison in the first half from last year's GST-driven demand.

financial_highlights.change: Ahead of domestic 2W volumes (>20%) and exports (>36%)
+67.7% YoY vs Rs 213 crore; ~3% of overall growth from Multilink (about 20 days consolidated)
Up from 24% a year ago; EV revenue +79% YoY
Expected to turn to net cash after August IPO proceeds; management indicated ~Rs 1,000 crore net cash around end-August

segments.name: Wiring harness
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,090 crore in Q1 FY27, up 44.6% YoY from Rs 753 crore. Management says localisation has cut imported components from 30-35% to 20-25% of the component base.

segments.name: Non-wiring harness (EV components, battery packs, controllers, sensors, switches)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 358 crore, up 67.7% YoY, with Multilink adding about 10-12 points of that growth. Battery packs are the major portion; a second top customer in the South started supply in the last month of the quarter.

segments.name: Multilink (acquired)
segments.commentary: Contributed ~3% to overall revenue growth for the ~20-day period in Q1. Management expects 25-30% growth and margins in line with the group; full integration in about 3-4 months, adding Hero as a customer plus fuel level sensors and relays.

segments.name: EV vs ICE
segments.commentary: EV revenue +79% YoY, ICE revenue +52.6% YoY. EV content per vehicle is 1.5x-2.5x that of ICE for wiring harness alone, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30% YoY, with soft comparison in H1 noted.
Full-year EBITDA margin guided at 15-16%.
Copper and other key raw materials rose further in July and August (~3-4% per management), so gross margin recovery is not expected in Q2; benefit expected in Q3 if prices stay stable.
EV revenue share expected to exceed 30-32% in the next two to three years.
Multilink expected to grow 25-30% at group-level margins after integration in roughly 3-4 months.
Ride Vision (ADAS, Israeli partner) JV formation in process; a passenger-vehicle HV harness JV is at an advanced stage, with details promised in the next earnings call.
IPO proceeds to fund expansion at Jhajjar and Hosur plants, adding ~15-20% capacity this year; IPO utilisation update promised next quarter.
capex_capacity: Expansion at Jhajjar and Hosur plants funded from IPO proceeds, adding ~15-20% to wiring harness capacity this year.
Management says ~75% utilisation is the working ceiling because customers run at full capacity during the 5-6 month Diwali season.
Dhoot Autocomponents (subsidiary) manufactures cables and connection systems, with ~Rs 1,200 crore of business for group companies (self-consumption, not in reported sales).
EV cord set new business for next year: ~40-45% share of the Indian market, per management.
Ride Vision ADAS product: management says it is aimed at two-wheelers first, with regulatory-driven demand expected.
demand_pricing: Management says the EV industry grew ~93% YoY and ICE more than 20% in the quarter, with 2W industry growth of 22.8%.
Copper is ~20-23% of BOM cost. Price pass-through to customers is on a three-month lag; recovery comes when raw materials soften.
Management said the Q1 margin was impacted by a hard commodity cycle, not by mix shift toward battery packs.
Wage-hike cost is recovered from customers through annual discussions, per management.
Management says it has not lost ICE market share, despite an analyst comparison suggesting it had.

qa_highlights.question: How much more margin expansion is possible, and when does copper pass-through normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Kalani said most copper inflation is passed through, but prices kept rising for 4-5 months, so there is some impact. Guidance is kept at 15-16% full-year EBITDA margin; Q2 recovery is unlikely and Q3 is the earliest, if prices are stable.

qa_highlights.question: Cash position and FCF at end-June?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt was about Rs 220 crore at end-June, after the March Bain infusion and part Multilink impact. Post-IPO money (received in August) should turn the company to net cash, with ~Rs 1,000 crore indicated by end-August.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of non-wiring harness revenue and EBITDA margin expectations for Multilink?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakup by product is not disclosed due to single-customer concentration. Non-wiring harness grew 67.7%, with Multilink adding 10-12 points for its ~20-day contribution. Multilink margins are expected to be in line with group margins.

qa_highlights.question: Wiring harness revenue and prior-year split?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: wiring harness Rs 1,090 crore and non-wiring harness Rs 358 crore. Q1 FY26: Rs 753 crore and Rs 213 crore, respectively.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add capacity given 75-80% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion at Jhajjar and Hosur adds ~15-20% capacity this year. Management said 75% is the sustainable ceiling because of seasonal peak demand during Diwali.

risks_watch: Copper and other raw-material prices continued to rise into July-August, which could delay margin recovery beyond Q3.
Soft base comparison in H1 FY27, since the GST-cut-driven demand boost came in H2 FY26.
Customer concentration: battery pack business rests on a single customer, and disclosure is limited under customer agreements.
Multilink integration (3-4 months) and cross-selling targets; the Ride Vision JV and passenger-vehicle HV harness JV are not yet finalised.
Management said ADAS demand is partly regulation-dependent; timing is uncertain.
Goodwill and PPA on Multilink still provisional; management estimates goodwill at ~20-25% of the acquisition price.
Q1 employee cost rose ~16% QoQ; management did not quantify the split between wage-hike and organic hires.

540212|2026-06.headline: TCI Express Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR 312 crore, with PAT up 6% to INR 22.4 crore and volumes up 7.5% to 2.5 lakh tonnes.
540212|2026-06.overview: Income from operations grew about 9% YoY to INR 312 crore and EBITDA rose 11% to INR 37 crore, with margin at 11.7% versus 11.5%. PAT rose 6% to INR 22.4 crore (7.1% margin). Management said the fuel price hike taken in mid-May was only partly reflected in Q1 (June only), so benefits should show from Q2. The company stated it is debt-free with net cash of about INR 118 crore.

financial_highlights.change: up ~6% YoY from INR 21 crore; margin 7.1%

segments.name: Surface Express
segments.commentary: Largest contributor; grew 9% YoY on existing customers, new accounts and industrial growth. Management targets accelerating to double-digit growth.

segments.name: Domestic Air Express
segments.commentary: Grew 29% YoY per opening remarks (CEO-level figure); later cited ~28% on enterprise account wins and airline partnerships.

segments.name: International Express
segments.commentary: Grew 27% YoY on new customers, win-backs and expanded global carrier partnerships.

segments.name: E-commerce Express
segments.commentary: Grew 63% YoY, the fastest-growing vertical, but only ~2-2.5% of revenue; target small-merchant, D2C and e-commerce B2B segments at 16-18% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Rail Express / C2C Express
segments.commentary: Rail added operational branches; C2C added clients, regional branch coverage and a larger dedicated vehicle fleet. No growth figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at 11-12%, with net price realisation of about 3%, implying 13-15% overall revenue growth.
FY27 PAT growth guided at 20-25%.
EBITDA margin expansion of 100-150 bps targeted for FY27; margin benefit from fuel pass-through expected from Q2.
Multimodal share of revenue targeted at 17-18% to 19% in FY27 and 22-25% by 2030.
FY27 capex guided at INR 125-140 crore; management said it expects to cross INR 125 crore, with about INR 20 crore spent so far.
Kolkata hub automation expected by March 2027 or June 2027 at latest; Ahmedabad around mid-2027, taking automated hubs to four by 2027.
capex_capacity: Two hubs automated so far: Tajnagar (North India) and Chakan (Pune); Kolkata and Ahmedabad under construction.
Ongoing construction at four sites: Ahmedabad, Kolkata, corporate office and Lucknow.
Management said it is close to finalising a land purchase in one of Mumbai, Chennai or Bangalore.
Regional branch expansion ongoing across Surface, Air, Rail and C2C; e-commerce regional branches being opened and bikers hired for sub-5 kg deliveries.
demand_pricing: Volume grew ~7.5% to 2.5 lakh tonnes, but management said price hikes were held back until fuel increased in mid-May; diesel and annual hikes together gave a 'handsome' increase, with ~90%+ of customers passed through in June.
Analyst noted peers are taking 3-5% price hikes; management did not give a specific Q1 price-hike percentage.
SME to B2B mix returned to 50:50 in Q1 from 48:52 in FY26.
Management cited pipeline visibility, manufacturing demand and SME recovery; growth expected from both existing customers and new industries.
Analyst raised competitive pricing in certain segments and elevated operating costs industry-wide; management said its service quality and tech investment keep it ahead.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Q1 volumes and price hikes versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was 2.5 lakh tonnes, up ~7.5%. Management said fuel-linked pass-through came in mid-May, with the full price increase reflected mainly in June; the company deferred hikes ahead of expected fuel increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategic rationale for expanding e-commerce given lower margins historically?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is ~2-2.5% of revenue. Management said D2C margins are 16-18% and it is targeting small merchants, D2C and e-commerce B2B, with regional teams and branches to support Surface.

qa_highlights.question: What changed to drive consistent double-digit EBITDA growth and volume acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it strengthened vertical-wise regional teams and built regional structures across Air, International, Rail and C2C. Air grew ~28% on new customers, and a clear pipeline supports growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the volume, pricing and PAT targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 11-12%, net price hikes of about 3%, total growth of 13-15%, and PAT growth of 20-25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of hub automation and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Two hubs are automated (Tajnagar, Chakan); Kolkata is expected by March or June 2027 and Ahmedabad around mid-2027. FY27 capex is INR 125-140 crore, with about INR 20 crore spent so far.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins improve in Q2 as fuel pass-through takes full effect, and what is the multimodal share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the fuel increase was passed on to 90%+ of customers in June, so margins should improve from Q2. Multimodal share is about 17-18% now, targeted at 17-19% this year and 22-25% by 2030.

risks_watch: Realisation: management said price hikes were deferred and partly reflected only in June, so Q2 pricing and margin uplift need to be verified.
Net price hike guidance of ~3% is below the 3-5% peers were said to be taking; the analyst questioned this.
E-commerce last-mile economics: management cited 16-18% EBITDA margin, but the analyst questioned profitability in last-mile delivery.
Capex of INR 125-140 crore against INR 20 crore spent so far; land purchase timing is uncertain.
Management's 11-12% volume and 20-25% PAT growth guidance is ambitious against 7.5% volume growth and 6% PAT growth in Q1.
Domestic Air growth figure inconsistency: 29% in prepared remarks versus ~28% in Q&A.
540212|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, pipeline and margin recovery, but vague on specifics such as the Q1 price-hike percentage and the e-commerce economics. Answers were often loosely structured and repetitive.

532832|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 presales rose 338% YoY to INR868 crore and collections 54% to INR496 crore, but revenue fell to INR217 crore and net loss widened to INR234 crore.
532832|2026-06.overview:
Presales of INR868 crore (up 338% YoY) and collections of INR496 crore (up 54% YoY) led the quarter, while no new projects were launched in Q1 by design. Reported revenue from operations fell to INR217 crore from INR681 crore, EBITDA was negative INR106 crore, and net loss widened to INR234 crore from INR166 crore, as revenue is recognised only on completion and handover. Operating cash flow was negative INR285 crore; management expects collections to pick up from Q2 as launches from H2 FY26 hit milestones. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR6,000 crore owned presales, INR2,000 crore DM presales and about INR3,000 crore collections, and a promoter warrant issue at INR111.51 to repay Embassy Group's INR363 crore shareholder debt.</overview>

segments.name: Residential (owned development)
segments.commentary: Presales INR868 crore in Q1; ongoing portfolio of 11 assets about 70% sold by saleable area; OC-received inventory about 98% cumulatively sold. Construction spend INR276 crore, about 56% of collections.

segments.name: Development management (DM)
segments.commentary: Embassy Terazza (Juhu) received RERA approval just before the call and is slated for Q2 launch; FY27 DM presales guidance INR2,000 crore.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.commentary: Embassy East Business Park is under excavation and may be held as an annuity asset or sold near completion. Embassy Knowledge Park commercial product is in early planning, with timelines targeted by end-FY27; not included in GDV.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales guidance: INR6,000 crore from owned developments and INR2,000 crore from DM projects, reiterated.
FY27 collections guidance of approximately INR3,000 crore reiterated; management says it could be bettered, with more clarity by Q3.

FY27 launch pipeline: 11 projects, GDV about INR19,400 crore (9 owned, INR13,300 crore; 2 DM, INR6,000-plus crore). Four to launch in Q2 (Embassy One North tower, Embassy Knowledge Park villas and apartments, Juhu DM project); the rest targeted for Q3, possibly spilling into Q4.
Management expects a cash-flow inflection around mid-calendar 2027 (April-May) as slab cycles start on Greenshore, Verde and Citadel.
Debt: cost of debt to fall first, with refinancing of the portfolio targeted around March-April 2027; net debt to equity target of 0.3x-0.35x.
Under review: percentage-of-completion accounting, to be assessed over the next couple of quarters.
capex_capacity: Ongoing development of 11 assets about 70% sold by saleable area; Embassy Paradiso and balance towers of Golf City Savroli nearing completion and slated for OC in FY27; Embassy Edge and East Avenue due for completion in FY28.
OC received in Q1 for Embassy One 09 (Gurgaon, Phase 1) and 5 towers at Golf City Savroli.
Embassy Citadel (Mumbai, Worli) has approval for all 81 floors; Leighton appointed as civil contractor; est. INR8,000-9,000 crore of stock to sell over several years.

Beyond 2027: development pipeline of about 20.3 million sq ft, GDV about INR23,470 crore; fully paid land bank of 3,000-plus acres, including 1,400-plus acres at Nashik (MIDC dispute; debonding expected to take 6-9 more months).
Cumulative unsold inventory across launched and under-construction residential and commercial projects: INR13,630 crore.
demand_pricing: Bangalore: about 72% of launch inventory sold within 6 months; management cites this as the cleanest read on demand, with Mumbai's 60% figure skewed by Citadel.
Nearly 60% of inventory launched in FY26 already sold.
Management says Embassy has a pricing premium in Bangalore; Citadel's first tranche priced to build reputation before taking top Mumbai pricing.
Collections-to-presales ratio was about 35% last year; FY27 target implies about 50% (INR3,000 crore vs INR6,000 crore owned presales).
Some Gurgaon landlords have asked about the Indiabulls association; management says the entities are separate and that this is a slow-to-resolve perception issue.

qa_highlights.question: Are Bangalore launch delays (as at Prestige) also affecting Embassy, and can the other 5 Bangalore projects launch within FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q1 non-launch to choice, not approvals; Embassy One North was pushed to Q2 after the Four Seasons branding was dropped. Knowledge Park villas and apartments are targeted for Q2, and Bangalore projects are targeted for Q3, possibly spilling into Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating cash flow outlook, given EBITDA of negative INR106 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 operating cash flow was negative INR285 crore because no launches occurred in Q1; collections from Q3-Q4 FY26 launches should accelerate from Q2. Cash balance started FY27 at about INR1,165 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR19,400 crore GDV split between H1 and H2?
qa_highlights.answer: The four Q2 launches (North tower, Knowledge Park, Juhu DM, plus Embassy One already launched) are in H1; the remaining projects are targeted for Q3, possibly Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the average cost of debt and the cost of the Blackstone debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost of debt is about 14%. Blackstone debt accrues at 18%, added to the gross debt rather than paid out; management is in talks to convert the Blackstone portion to equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why the promoter warrant issue if the promoter debt is accruing rather than paid in cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it brings no new liquidity; it is a confidence signal, priced at INR111.51 (the earlier pre-merger price), and the Embassy Group debt (growing at over 15%) will be cleared. Warrants will convert within 6 months, versus the 18-month maximum.

qa_highlights.question: Can collections of INR3,000 crore be achieved without new launches, and what is the collection schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Most collections are expected from already-launched projects (Greenshore, Verde, Eden). Launches in Q2 and Q3 are expected to yield 10-20% collected in the quarter; management is confident of the INR3,000 crore.

532867|2026-06.headline: V2 Retail Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR997 crore, with PAT up 70% to INR41.9 crore and store count at 381.
532867|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR997 crore (+58% YoY), with reported EBITDA of INR139.5 crore (+60%, 14.0% margin) and PAT of INR41.9 crore (+70%). Pre-Ind AS EBITDA was about INR79 crore (~8% margin, +51%) and PAT INR50 crore (+64%). Gross margin eased to 28.6% from 29.5%, which management attributed to Adhik Maas reducing full-price sell-through to 90% from 92%. Store count reached 381 at June 30, 2026 (56 net adds), and management says it has since crossed 400 stores. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of at least 50% revenue growth, 8-10% SSSG, 170-200 new stores and 29-30% gross margin.

financial_highlights.change: vs 92% in prior-year Q1 per Q&A

segments.name: Store network
segments.commentary: 381 stores at June 30, 2026 covering ~40.7 lakh sq ft; 57 opened and 1 closed in Q1, net +56. Crossed 400 stores after quarter-end. Stores are mostly standalone, 10,000-12,000 sq ft, in 26 states.

segments.name: New vs mature stores
segments.commentary: New stores run ~34% lower sales per sq ft than mature stores (>2 years old at ~INR1,070-1,100/sq ft); new stores at ~INR730-740/sq ft. New-store SSSG is ~2.3 pts above old stores in Q1. Cohort SPSF cited at 886 vs 925 earlier.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance at least 50% for FY27, unchanged.
SSSG guidance 8-10% for the full year, retained despite Q1 at ~7.5%.
Gross margin guided at 29-30% (earlier 28-30% range), dependent on sell-through.
170-200 store openings planned for FY27; no change in plan despite capex inflation.
Targeting ~50% CAGR growth for the next 2-3 years, per CEO.
Price increase of 4-5% in garment MRPs from Q3 FY27 to offset raw material inflation.
EBITDA margin to be maintained despite the new-store expansion; new stores pay back in 2.5-3 years and break even from their first month.
Funding via internal accruals, release of ~INR150-200 crore from normalising creditor days, and bank limit increases; no QIP planned.
capex_capacity: New store capex has risen ~10% to INR1.22 crore from INR1.1 crore, due to input inflation.
Inventory held ~100 days (earlier 90-100 days target) and creditors ~45-50 days; safety stock raised due to geopolitical tension and to be reduced later.
Inventory for new stores is staged ~2 months ahead, with ~INR100-150 crore tied up per quarter of 50-55 openings.
MOU signed for the next 100 stores; ~15-20 store locations finalised each month based on regional data.
Store-level replenishment cut to 2-3 days of sales cover from 10-12 days, with store back-room space converted into selling area.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is inelastic; kids' wear is ~25% of sales. July-August trends described as in line with plan, but too early to judge given festive shift into Q3.
Adhik Maas (30 days in Q1) and fewer wedding dates weakened Tier 2/3 demand and cut full-price sales to 90%.
Price increase of 4-5% on garment cost from Q3; management says past increases reduced volume slightly but were offset by ASP.
Repeat customers within first year rose from ~40% to ~55% over three years, per management.
80% of stores face 3-4 other value fashion retailers in the same catchment.

qa_highlights.question: Will price increases be passed on, and what is the volume impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material inflation to hit from Q3 as H1 orders were placed earlier; a 4-5% rise in garment cost will be passed to consumers. Past price hikes reduced volume slightly but were offset by ASP.

qa_highlights.question: Will the store addition pace slow or need new equity?
qa_highlights.answer: 170-200 openings remain on track with no capex slowdown. Internal accruals, INR150-200 crore from normalising creditor days, and bank limit increases will fund it; no QIP planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin contract, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Adhik Maas cut full-price sales to 90% from 92%. Guidance remains 29-30% gross margin, dependent on season sell-through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new-store productivity gap closing?
qa_highlights.answer: New stores run ~34% below mature stores on SPSF; 10-12 stores are below INR600/sq ft, which management says is too early to judge. Management expects maturity in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why are stores appearing in Tier 1 cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said V2 has long operated in Tier 1 (about 11 stores in Delhi NCR) and that Tier 1 is part of the target market.

qa_highlights.question: Customer experience: are NPS or other KPIs tracked?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not focus on Google reviews; an NPS link is sent after billing to ~40% of customers as a pilot, with store incentives linked to NPS. AI on CCTV flags long checkout queues.

risks_watch: Gross margin at 28.6% is below the 29-30% guided range; the recovery depends on full-price sell-through in the festive season (Q2-Q3).
New-store productivity is ~34% below mature stores, with 10-12 stores below INR600/sq ft; RK Retail acquisition will consolidate from Q2.
Working capital is inflated by vendor prepayments; cash release depends on creditor days normalising to 45-50 days.
Capex inflation (~10%) and rising rent escalation (12-15% every 3 years) could pressure store economics.
Geopolitical risk is driving higher safety stock and raw-material inflation; the timing of 4-5% price pass-through is a watch item.
Customer experience issues (store-level reviews and checkout queues) could weigh on repeat rates and SSSG.
532867|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth and store expansion; cautious and deflective on near-term demand, saying it is too early to call July-August trends ahead of the festive quarters. Management gave few numbers on the post-quarter trend and deferred several questions to the next call.
key_quotes: We delivered an amazing 58% year -on-year revenue growth in the first quarter while maintaining healthy returns.
So we need to have that inventory at least 2 months prior to the opening of the store.

513502|2026-06.headline: Baroda Extrusion Q1 FY27 revenue rose to ₹47.90 crore (vs ₹38.05 crore) and PAT to ₹2.64 crore, with a ₹20 crore order book as of 31 July 2026.
513502|2026-06.overview: Management presented Q1 FY27 against the prior-year quarter, with revenue up about 26% YoY and EBITDA up about 238% to ₹3.68 crore. The company is described as virtually debt-free and cash profitable, and is considering a heavy-capacity hydraulic extrusion press with a stated capex of ₹20-25 crore. Management guided to 35-40% growth for FY27/FY28 but gave no formal numeric guidance. The call was largely qualitative, and several figures were stated inconsistently (the speaker quoted FY25/FY26 labels for Q1 FY27 numbers and gave monthly volume figures that conflicted).

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹38.05 crore in Q1 FY26; +25.87% YoY
vs 2.86% in prior-year quarter (as read out by moderator)

segments.name: Copper and copper alloy products (solid, hollow, sections, nuggets)
segments.commentary: Management cited a sales run-rate of about 150-160 tons per month in one answer and about 430 tons per quarter (~145 tons per month, including job work) in another; these figures are inconsistent. Job work and trading are included in the mix.

segments.name: Ancillary job work and trading
segments.commentary: Company does forging, machining and trading of copper sheet alongside its own production; trading contributed higher income in one recent period, per management.

guidance_outlook: Management expects 35-40% minimum growth for FY27 and FY28 versus the prior year; one answer also cited about 25% already achieved.
EBITDA margin expected to hold, varying by about 1-2% either way, per management.
Capex of ₹20-25 crore for a heavy-capacity hydraulic extrusion press and other machines; post-expansion capacity stated as about 500 tons per month (~6,000 tons per annum), with both plants running.
Management aspires to ₹1,000 crore revenue in 3-5 years and referred to ₹2,000 crore in a later answer; current revenue base is described as about ₹200 crore annualised.
Management said it can accept about 50% more orders right now on existing machines, given limited capacity.
capex_capacity: Heavy-capacity hydraulic extrusion press under evaluation; capex stated at ₹20-25 crore including machines and plant and machinery.
Expansion planned adjacent to the running factory in Vadodara on existing land, to avoid disruption.
Company has 20 drawbenches and extrusion capacity; machines were upgraded, per management.
Management indicated the company was 'a bit late' on expansion after not expanding major capacity for about 35 years.
demand_pricing: Demand drivers cited: electrical infrastructure, transformers, switchgear, data centres, EVs, renewables and power equipment.
Exports: a customer makes copper strips for the US market, where duties have reportedly fallen; export orders are also rising domestically.
Defence: supplies via GeM tenders and to ancillary vendors; large-OD copper pipes for ammunition applications are under development, with no regular volume yet.
Pricing: company does not hedge; it buys raw material against orders and uses LME/BME-linked customer contracts to protect margins.
Customers include BARC and NPCIL-linked government companies for oxygen-free forged and machined components, sourced via GeM; the company says this is currently a minor share of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from BARC and NPCIL, and what products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it supplies oxygen-free material and forged/machined components via GeM, with a minor current share; expansion of heavy presses is expected to capture more volume.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance on revenue and EBITDA margin for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth of 35-40% minimum versus last year, with about 25% already achieved, and margins expected to hold within 1-2%.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue increase from the ₹25-30 crore infrastructure investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Post-expansion, capacity to be above 500 tons per month (about 6,000 tons per annum), with heavy sizes and low-weight items produced at the new unit.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company capture import substitution across EV, renewables, power and data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it already supplies major Indian customers for pipes, flats, rods and bolts, has drawing capacity, and that market is not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the margin improvement and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to rising demand, cost control, an integrated team and some higher trading income in an earlier period; it expects margins to be consistent.

qa_highlights.question: How to reach ₹1,000 crore in 3 years and what capex is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is ₹20-25 crore; management believes the target is achievable in 3-5 years, with volume and margin both expected to grow.

qa_highlights.question: Monthly volume and capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Answers were inconsistent: 120 tons/month implied by ₹200 crore annual revenue, 145 tons/month average, and 430 tons per quarter; management said machine efficiency is below installed capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Open to inorganic growth or acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is open to deals that fit its industry, including production tie-ups, but has no plans for a takeover and will not take financial risk beyond capacity.

risks_watch: Figures are inconsistent across the call (quarterly vs monthly volumes, FY25/FY26 labels for Q1 FY27 numbers); verify against the filed results.
No formal guidance; the 35-40% growth and 1,000-2,000 crore targets are management aspirations without a stated timeline or funding plan beyond ₹20-25 crore capex.
No hedging policy: raw-material price volatility can affect inventory and margins, although management says customer pricing is linked to LME/BME.
Dependence on a small number of large customers and on government/defence orders via GeM, which are not regular in volume yet.
Expansion execution: new press commissioning timeline not given; the company says it has been capacity-constrained for years and carries an operating history of lapses.
513502|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the long-term story, but vague and unstructured on numbers, with frequent restatements. Evasive on the share price and valuation question, which was answered only in general terms about integrity and shareholder returns.
key_quotes: Our object is not simply to increase capacity. Our objective is to create profitable capacity, increase value addition, and build sustainable long-term growth.
The margins are always low, right? So, we have a fixed setup near in Vadodara, we have office here, we have a very integrated team.

539334|2026-06.headline: Shree Pushkar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 280-281 crore and EBITDA rose 9.7% to Rs 31.9 crore, despite volumes falling sharply.
539334|2026-06.overview:
Revenue grew about 10% YoY on higher realisations even though fertiliser volumes fell to 66,527 MT from 76,288 MT and chemical volumes fell to 9,113 MT from 14,837 MT. EBITDA margin was 11.4% and PAT margin 8.2%, with PAT up about 9% to Rs 22.9 crore. Management said acid plants were run at low load due to high sulphur prices and working-capital strain, and Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 are close to trial operation. Management reiterated an FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, which it said could reach Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, with PAT of around 8.5-9%.</overview>

segments.name: Fertiliser
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 142 crore, up 4% YoY, on 66,527 MT volume (down from 76,288 MT). Management said inventory is being held in anticipation of higher prices.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 138 crore, up 17.1% YoY, on 9,113 MT (down from 14,837 MT). Acid plants were put on low load; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, with management saying it could reach Rs 1,300-1,400 crore (Rs 1,350-1,400 crore in one answer), and PAT of around 8.5-9%.
Management expects Q2 to be better than Q1 and better than Q2 FY26 (about 110% higher, per management's reply to an analyst's Rs 250-285 crore comparison).
Unit 6 expected to start trials by end-August or September 2026, giving about 4-5 months of operation in FY27.
Next year (FY28) with a full 12 months of Unit 6 could reach Rs 1,700-1,750 crore, per management's personal view.
Management says peak revenue for all units could reach about Rs 1,700 crore at current prices once Unit 6 is on stream.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of Rs 209 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026 against a total planned Rs 512 crore; about Rs 20 crore spent in Q1 FY27.
Expansions at Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 and Meghnagar are expected to add 450,000 MT per annum of fertiliser capacity and 72,000 MT per annum of chemical capacity.

Unit 5 dyes plant (small vertical, about Rs 37 crore) and 10 MW DC solar project at Nanded are complete or nearing completion; total solar capacity to reach 20.6 MW DC once commissioned. Capitalisation not yet announced.
Acquired about 30,000 sq m of land adjacent to Unit 1 at Lote Parshuram for Rs 9.3 crore in Q1.
Madhya Bharat (Madhya Pradesh) project has Rs 60 crore invested to June; timeline 2028. Plant is about twice Unit 6 capacity and includes an 800 TPD chemical plant for captive NPK integration.
Rs 125 crore in non-lien deposits as of 30 June 2026; capex funded from internal accruals and preferential issue proceeds.
demand_pricing: Management says customers are absorbing higher raw material prices, and demand is recovering after a pause during the West Asia conflict.
Sulphur prices have risen to about USD 1,100/t from USD 250-300 earlier, per management; ammonia and sulphur shortages followed Hormuz closure.
K-acid price moved from Rs 550 to Rs 700-plus per management; company says it is the largest K-acid maker in India and has inquiries for K-acid, H-acid and vinyl sulphone from China.
Dye utilisation has decreased due to the global scenario, per management.
Management says it chose value over volume, with dispatches stopped in mid-March 2026 in expectation of higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 volume weakness mitigating, and is the company on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is optimistic, citing 40 days of data, and expects Q2 to beat Q1; volumes should be met while protecting value.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 not reflect the upside from orders held back from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders retracted in Q4 do not carry over into Q1, and that EBITDA and PAT each rose about 10% YoY, so recovery is visible.

qa_highlights.question: Why were acid plants run at low load?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur requires advance payment while acid is sold on credit, and working-capital stress made the margin unattractive; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company fill existing capacity before expanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Unit 5 and 6 are nearly complete and that the Madhya Bharat expansion is also underway, citing confidence in the team and available cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is DAP substitution affecting NPK and SSP demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management questioned DAP availability and said that if DAP is cheaper and available, farmers will shift, so product availability is the key variable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter battery-grade phosphoric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Not on the agenda for now; the focus is on stabilising current expansions first.

risks_watch: Volumes are down about 17% in fertiliser and about 39% in chemicals YoY, and management has prioritised pricing over volume.
Unit 6 start-up timing depends on long-term raw material contracts, due by August or September 2026; ammonia and sulphur supply and price remain volatile with Hormuz still closed.
Working-capital strain from advance sulphur payments; acid plants at low load.
Management guidance has moved between Rs 1,250 crore, Rs 1,300-1,400 crore and Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, and its PAT target is 8.5-9% versus a remark of up to about 10%.
Inconsistent figures in the call: revenue of Rs 280.1 crore vs Rs 281.1 crore; EBITDA of Rs 31.9 crore vs Rs 31 crore; PAT growth of 9.4% vs 9%. Verify against the filing.
Capex of Rs 303 crore remains to be spent against the Rs 512 crore plan.

543812|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record Rs 141.8 crore (+85% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 29.4%, helped by the Indonesia transfer-case order.
543812|2026-06.overview:
Revenue of Rs 141.8 crore rose 85% YoY and 25% QoQ, with transfer cases up 93% YoY to Rs 76 crore. EBITDA was Rs 41.6 crore (29.4% margin) and PAT was Rs 25.2 crore (17.8% margin). Management framed the quarter as the start of a broader growth phase, citing the Indonesia programme, exports, components, and a planned US greenfield plant (Project Mayflower). EV transmission deliveries were soft in Q1 and management expects a pickup in schedules over the next three quarters.</overview>

capex_capacity: Two existing transfer-case assembly lines (over 20 years old) are being modernised with a German automation partner; the new line is expected to deliver ~400 units/day or ~120,000 units/year at the Shirwal facility.
Land holdings: 25 acres at Sirsi, Karnataka and 10 acres at Shirwal; management says capacity is not currently a constraint.
US: wholly-owned subsidiary set up in Greenville, SC at the International Center for Automotive Research; greenfield plant planned, initial investment directionally ~$5 million.
Management said investment in India will be larger than overseas investment and will take priority.
demand_pricing: Indonesia programme: ~70,000 transfer cases for Tata and Mahindra over 10-12 months; competitors included Toyota, Nissan, Mitsubishi, Isuzu, Great Wall and Foton. Management said the tender saved the Indonesian government ~$500 million.
Principal customer is Mahindra; Tata Motors is number two. Divgi says its export contracts are exclusive, with it as the only supplier of these components into North America.
Global transfer case market cited at ~14-15 million units (management), with a separate analyst figure of 40-50 million that management did not confirm.
Management says FWD-based AWD content can exceed Rs 30,000 per vehicle; two new applications added in the last 4-6 months.
Indian EV transmission market is crowded; Tata is the main localisation leader and Divgi's primary transmission supplier. Korean EV opportunity in discussion.
Management expects exports and global operations to be 25-40% of business and domestic 60-70%, with proprietary products becoming a larger share of domestic business.

544748|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 129% YoY to INR 158.3 crore, driven by first full quarter of Netcom BCC, with EBITDA margin at 24.9%.
544748|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full reporting period consolidating Netcom BCC, lifting consolidated revenue to INR 158.3 crore (up 64.6% QoQ, 129% YoY) and EBITDA to INR 39.4 crore (24.9% margin). Profit for the period rose to INR 16.3 crore, with basic EPS of 0.62 versus 0.36 a year ago. Finance cost rose to INR 8.1 crore from INR 1.9 crore, tied to acquisition borrowing. Management positioned the company as moving from capacity-led outsourcing toward outcome-based AI orchestration through its ResolX platform, while the standalone base business grew 11.6% YoY.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1.9 crore a year ago

financial_highlights.value: ~50% of revenue and ~50% of EBITDA; Netcom margin ~24-25%

segments.name: Global human service engine (incl. Netcom BCC)
segments.commentary: Netcom fully consolidated this quarter, deepening Americas presence; contributes roughly half of consolidated revenue and EBITDA at ~24-25% margin.

segments.name: Base business (standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue INR 61.1 crore, up 11.6% YoY, at 30.4% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Agentic AI engine (ResolX)
segments.commentary: Launched May 2026; 12 live deployments across seven enterprise clients. Revenue described as only just starting to catch up; management expects meaningful revenue in 12-18 months or slightly more.

guidance_outlook: Management said the company should be able to roughly double revenue this year, while acknowledging this was not a one-off quarter.
Management expects EBITDA margins to improve progressively over the coming year as the revenue mix shifts to AI orchestration and outcome-linked models.
Cash generation expected to rise in coming quarters, making debt servicing easier; no equity raise indicated.
Management intends to acquire two more companies over the next three years, targeting firms with Fortune 500 clients in North America.
AI-led revenue expected to show up in quarterly numbers over the coming 12-18 months.
capex_capacity: Netcom BCC acquisition debt carries an effective cost of around 9%; management said total debt is about INR 220 crore and a repayment schedule is planned.

ResolX platform: 12 live deployments across seven enterprise clients (insurance, aviation, banking, automotive, digital assets), including two Central American banks; management said about 6-7 of 12 projects were deployed as of the call.
Management plans roughly 40-plus bots for one Indian insurance client across languages and its 7-8 products.
Management said capacity is not a constraint, with AI expected to free room in accounts for additional work.
demand_pricing: Management expects growth from India and LATAM, with the Americas growing on dollar arbitrage; banking is the leading vertical, with some insurance, healthcare, travel and hospitality.
AI deflection to humans reported at roughly 30-40% depending on use case; one airline deployment cited about 30% of employee-size benefit.
Management claims the company is the only Indian BPO with in-house domain, tech stack and Agentic AI capabilities; other BPOs described as relying on third-party AI.
Conversion rate on active deal pipeline stated at around 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the current quarter's run rate one-off or sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not one-off, as this is the first quarter with full Netcom consolidation, and it expects revenue to roughly double this year.

qa_highlights.question: Split of revenue and EBITDA between Netcom and base business, and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Netcom contributes about 50% of revenue and about 50% of EBITDA, with margins of 24-25%, similar to group margin.

qa_highlights.question: Plan for INR 220 crore debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash earnings will rise, debt servicing will get easier, and repayment is planned; the company is described as debt-free apart from Netcom acquisition borrowing at about 9%.

qa_highlights.question: Does ResolX/Agentic AI generate savings or margin lift yet?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin benefit is visible in a few projects but is too small to be noticeable yet; deflection to humans is about 30-40%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Singapore acquisition and revenue there?
qa_highlights.answer: The Singapore company acquired in 2025 served as the platform later relaunched as ResolX; there is no current revenue in Singapore, with small revenues in the Middle East, Europe, LATAM and India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended cost of debt, and acquisition criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt sits mainly with Netcom at about 9%. Acquisition screen is EPS accretion first, then North American customer access; management said margin accretion is immediate.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and monetisation of resolution-based model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said resolution cost is measured by time and motion across channels, and that single-owner end-to-end handling shortens interactions (e.g. 5 minutes to 2 minutes).

risks_watch: Margin progression: consolidated EBITDA margin 24.9% is below standalone 30.4%, due to Netcom mix; AI-driven margin uplift is still small.
AI revenue timing: management guided to 12-18 months or longer before AI revenue is meaningful.
Debt of about INR 220 crore at ~9% cost on Netcom acquisition; finance cost rose to INR 8.1 crore.
Management's claim of unique positioning and high 10-12% deal conversion has not been independently verified.
Revenue doubling target for FY27 relies on Netcom consolidation plus new customer ramp-ups.
544748|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the ResolX/Agentic AI narrative and growth trajectory, but vague or evasive on AI-driven margin and revenue quantification, which management repeatedly deferred to future quarters. Some answers on competition and differentiation were assertive without supporting data.
key_quotes: Today, I can say that we are the only ones who exist in India who have the domain plus tech stack plus Agentic AI capabilities, which is truly born within the organization.
We are not in the business of creating LLMs, which is your Large Language Models. What we are in the business is on what sits on top of an LLM.

544664|2026-06.headline: KSH International Q1 FY27 revenue rose 108% YoY to INR1,164 crore; EBITDA per ton hit ~INR93,000, with management guiding to a sustainable ~INR75,000.
544664|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR1,164 crore (+108% YoY) and EBITDA was INR74.4 crore (vs INR40.3 crore a year ago and INR56.3 crore in Q4), with a record quarterly PAT of INR42.2 crore. Management attributed the strong EBITDA per ton mainly to a record CTC contribution, higher exports and new OEM customers priced at market-linked value-addition rates, with a weaker rupee also helping. Phase 1 of the Supa expansion is complete, with 14,400 MT of the 30,000 MT phase 2 added so far and full 59,000 MT installed capacity targeted by March 2027. Management signed a five-year framework agreement with Hitachi Energy, though quantity and price are not yet defined.

segments.name: Standard wires (EV, AC compressors, motors, DG alternators)

Some transformer OEMs in capacity expansion delayed picking up orders by a few weeks due to commissioning bottlenecks.

533293|2026-06.headline: KOEL Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 16% to INR1,461 crore, but EBITDA fell 4% and margin contracted to 11.2% on commodity costs and export weakness.
533293|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 16% YoY to INR1,461 crore, led by domestic power gen (+18%), industrial (+19%) and distribution & aftermarket (+20%), while international fell 11% to INR106 crore. Standalone EBITDA declined 4% YoY to INR165 crore and margin compressed to 11.2% from 13.5%, which management attributed to lower export volumes, elevated commodity costs and a lag between cost inflation and price realisation. Standalone net profit fell 9% to INR99 crore. Consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR2,000 crore, with consolidated net profit down 17% to INR111 crore. Management said pricing actions have been taken across most businesses and expects profitability to improve as they flow through over coming quarters.

guidance_outlook: Management says it remains committed to EBITDA delivery for the full year despite international headwinds.
Pricing actions taken across most businesses; realisation staged over different timeframes, expected to flow through over coming quarters.
Management views 3 to 6 months as a reasonable horizon for supply-chain queues and input-cost normalisation.
Long-term aspiration of a $2 billion revenue enterprise by FY30, roughly INR16,600 crore per management; no year-wise breakup given.
Management aims for a higher double-digit EBITDA margin by FY30 but declined to give a specific range; says margins have improved more than 400 bps over three years.
Data center order (~192 MW hyperscale): genset revenue to be recognised in FY27; O&M contract runs at least 5 to 6 years.
capex_capacity: First hyperscale data center order of approximately 192 MW secured in Q1, composite genset supply plus O&M contract.
NPCIL order is milestone-based; execution has started and some revenue expected this financial year; no NPCIL contribution in Q1.
Completed first end-to-end turnkey repowering of a 1,010 kVA high horsepower installation won in direct competition.
Optiprime modular power platform for data centers and mission-critical infrastructure; hybrid architectures up to 2 MW cited.
Largest range of CPCB IV compliant gas gensets claimed; new energy vertical is at programme-management stage (ethanol, methanol, isobutanol, natural gas, hydrogen).
Defense subsidiary Kirloskar Advanced Systems Limited established last quarter; no revenue contribution discussed.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand broad-based; management says market share gains are mostly below 750 kVA and only marginal above 750 kVA.
Pricing realisation varies by segment: power gen and distribution can pass on price readily, industrial and tenders are contract-specific, and fluid dynamics differs; realisation has lagged in Q1.
Middle East, a key export market, operated below normal levels due to West Asia conflict and choked logistics routes.

Employee cost rose about INR31 crore YoY (~40%), attributed to annual increments, ESOP expense, and capability additions; management says some costs are structural and some timing-related.
Inventory days rose slightly to 264 to support business expansion; cash conversion cycle at 25 days.

qa_highlights.question: Customer profile and further pipeline for the hyperscaler data center order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order is a reference point, not an endpoint, with one customer materialised through purchase orders after checks; further orders are proprietary and not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost jump roughly 40% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited a bridge of about INR31 crore YoY from increments, ESOP expense, and capability investments; some costs structural, some timing, not characterised as one-off.

qa_highlights.question: Has NPCIL or defence/marine revenue started?
qa_highlights.answer: No NPCIL contribution in Q1; execution milestone-based, revenue to start this FY. Defence and marine opportunities being pursued without specific Q1 contribution.

qa_highlights.question: Reasons for gross margin decline and pass-through of price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin contraction mainly from global commodity prices; price increases taken, with realisation lagging. Management says KOEL was among the first to start price conversations with customers.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for international business and normalisation timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Weakness mainly Middle East due to logistics disruption; management sees 3 to 6 months as a reasonable normalisation horizon as queues open.

qa_highlights.question: Is Arka being hived off?
qa_highlights.answer: Arka CFO said a hive-off is the long-term plan, to be pursued in stepwise options, with updates to be shared when available.

Data center order execution, further order visibility, and customer experience in hyperscale segment; management declined to disclose pipeline.
Arka hive-off and segment PBT down 31% YoY; Fluid Dynamics export recovery.
Marine and railway growth described as partly execution and billing timing; sustainability uncertain.

544814|2026-06.headline: Knack Packaging Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 40.5% YoY to INR2,647.7 million, with EBITDA up 53.1% and margin at 22.35%.
544814|2026-06.overview:
Knack Packaging reported Q1 FY27 as its first earnings call after listing on NSE and BSE. Consolidated revenue grew 40.5% YoY on 20.9% higher volume (10,940 MT), with EBITDA up 53.1% and PAT up 47.96%. Management attributed margin gains to operating leverage, cost discipline, solar power and a rising share of pinch-bottom bags. Capacity utilisation is about 91%, with a rented plant added to bridge until the IPO-funded plant, targeted for October 2027, takes installed capacity to about 70,000 MT.</overview>

segments.name: Domestic vs export
segments.commentary: Management said about 55-56% of sales are export and about 45% domestic; export margins are about 5-6% gross profit higher than domestic. Operations span 74 countries, up from 71 in FY26.

segments.name: PLWPP and pinch-bottom bags
segments.commentary: Pinch-bottom share of sales rose from 19-20% in prior-year quarters to a current 22.5-23%. Management says about 70% of sales are PLWPP bags. Two pinch-bottom machines (about INR20 crore each) were installed in the last quarter of FY26.

guidance_outlook: New IPO-funded plant targeted for commissioning in October 2027, taking installed capacity to about 70,000 MT from about 43,300 MT at listing.
Management expects Q1 FY27 sales levels to be maintained until the new plant starts, using the rented facilities.
Another rented plant of about 5,040 MT annual capacity was added about a month before the call; trials are under way.
Main construction of the new plant is expected to pick up after the monsoon; machinery finalisation is ongoing.
No explicit FY27 volume or EBITDA per kg guidance was given.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 43,300 MT at listing; operating above 48,000 MT including rented facilities, at about 91% utilisation.
Target installed capacity about 70,000 MT once the new plant is commissioned (October 2027).
Management said it is running at 90-92% utilisation and has no spare space to expand existing sites.
11 MW solar farm at Khedbrahma started in the last quarter; electricity cost fell about 1.1% of revenue YoY from solar.
Gross block rose to INR416 crore, with INR141 crore added over the year; the IPO proceeds are about INR320 crore.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR130 crore cited by management.
Customer retention is about 90%; more than 2,000 customers and over 13,000 SKUs.
Cargill is about 12-17% of revenue (figures varied on the call), with about 600 SKUs and a contract of 2 years plus a 1-year extension, priced as polymer cost plus conversion.
About 45-50% of customers are on fixed conversion-cost pricing with raw material pass-through; the rest are small buyers with pass-through pricing on the day of change.
Management said it passes polymer price changes through to customers on the same day, and that about 50% of input cost changes are passed on, with about 60% retained in some cases.

Management claims about 10% market share in the Indian bag segment (per a Technopack report), and says it is the leader in pinch-bottom bags in India. Management named Polytex (USA) as its only direct listed peer.

qa_highlights.question: Why are ROCE and asset turnover so high versus peers, and how is margin sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset turn is 2.53x on gross block and 4.12x on net block as of 30 June 2026, versus peer averages of about 1.5-2x. It attributed this to specialised machinery and a shift to higher-margin pinch-bottom bags. ROCE is supported by ongoing profits and IPO proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: How is the polymer price rise being managed, and how fast is it passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a SAP S/4HANA forecasting system, buys in cash and in bulk, and passes price changes to customers the same day. It said conversion-cost contracts cover 45-50% of customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Cargill relationship and the FX gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Cargill (USA) business grew from INR4 crore in 2020 to about INR140 crore; it is on a 2+1-year contract and buys finished bags. Management cited the cost of packaging below 1% of product value. FX gain in Q1 FY27 was INR1.6 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How does EBITDA per kg look, and how fast will pinch-bottom volumes move?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited EBITDA per kg of about INR54 in Q1 and INR45 in FY26. Pinch-bottom share is 22.5-23% and is rising; the call did not give a 70,000 MT utilisation timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth be sustained in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q1 sales levels to hold as the rented plants run until the new plant starts in October 2027. It said the onboarding process for new products is long, so marketing is being increased through rented capacity.

risks_watch: Polymer and crude volatility; management said the situation is fully volatile, and pass-through on fixed-conversion contracts shifts cost to the company.
Commissioning timing of the October 2027 plant; construction main phase is after the monsoon.
Dependence on rented plants for interim capacity and on rented facilities until the new plant starts.
Customer concentration: Cargill is about 12-17% of revenue, and figures on the call were inconsistent.
Several figures and facts on the call were inconsistent or corrected (ROCE corrected from 57.73% to 54.73%; Cargill share stated as 12%, 16-17%); verify in filings.
Export share of about 55% and FX exposure; the company reported only INR1.6 crore FX gain in the quarter.
Gross block growth to INR416 crore; management did not commit to maintaining asset turn of 2.5x+ on INR380 crore expansion.
544814|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, margins and customer relationships, with a strong emphasis on the 30-year history and first-mover position. Less precise on peer benchmarking, competitor data and volume guidance, where answers were loose and some figures were corrected during the call.

532683|2026-06.headline: AIA Q1 FY27 volumes rose to 64,644 tons (vs ~60,000 a year ago) with PAT of INR301 crore; management gave no volume or margin guidance.
532683|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was described by management as an uneventful, status-quo quarter, with volumes of 64,644 tons against roughly 60,000 a year earlier, sales of INR1,153 crore and PAT of INR301 crore. EBITDA was INR244 crore (about 21% margin on sales as implied by the reported figures), with reported EBITDA margin near 36% including other income and operating margin near 27.8-27.9%, down from Q4 on lower FX gain (INR25 crore vs INR65 crore), a weaker product mix, and trial and freight costs booked to other expenses. Management kept the NGDS (new generation discharge system) and South America mining conversion trials as the core focus, but declined to share trial outcomes or FY27 volume guidance. Capex guidance was raised to INR350-400 crore for FY27, mainly for a corporate campus land and building.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 volume guidance given; management asked investors to wait one more quarter for specific growth guidance, and declined to confirm 280,000-290,000 tons.
No margin guidance; prior operating margin guidance of 20-22% reiterated as the company's stated range, with Q1 said to be above it.
Realisation guidance of INR160-165 per ton was described as indicative, set about a year and a half ago; management declined to revise it.

FY27 capex now expected at minimum INR350-400 crore (up from about INR130 crore), with exact figure to come in Q2: about INR170-200 crore for a new corporate campus plot and INR50-100 crore for additional land for expansion.
Management said it will hold higher cash for at least a few more quarters before considering capital distribution options.
capex_capacity: Current capacity about 430,000-440,000 tons per year; management said current capacity can reach about 300,000-350,000 tons at 70-75% utilisation.
Q1 capex about INR50 crore: about INR30 crore on hybrid solar-wind renewable project (now operational) and about INR20 crore on maintenance and debottlenecking.

Overseas plants: Ghana site identified and government dialogue ongoing; China has a small lab facility and infrastructure plans are in slow mode. India remains the base for now; South America manufacturing not pursued yet.
demand_pricing: South America is the priority market: management cited about 1-1.5 million tons of addressable opportunity across gold, copper and iron, with South America alone potentially 300,000-400,000 tons for AIA.
Chinese players are gaining share in forged grinding media (about 20 forging companies), but management said high-chrome custom solutions remain limited to few companies.
Freight about USD 8,000-9,000 per container, elevated but easing; transshipment port congestion is a current constraint. Raw materials such as ferrochrome are elevated, with pass-through in pricing.

Realisations rose QoQ, which management attributed to a combination of product mix, freight and raw material pass-through, rupee movement and other factors; management said higher realisation does not mean higher margin.

qa_highlights.question: Has the second South America mine trial concluded, and what was the outcome?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share specifics; trials are ongoing and an outcome may take longer than expected due to technicalities.

qa_highlights.question: Is the QoQ volume decline a timing issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes are tracked annually, and the decline reflects timing, product mix and order execution cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 volumes reach 280,000-290,000 tons and what about Peru copper and Ghana gold trials?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance; growth guidance deferred to next quarter. Management said it has no specific answer on crossing 280,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: Is NGDS a standalone product and what is its TAM and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: NGDS will be sold only as part of a package with grinding media and liners, priced per kg; no standalone TAM was given. Overall lining-system opportunity is about 2-2.5 million tons, narrowing to about 1-1.5 million tons in gold, copper and iron.

qa_highlights.question: Should realisation guidance be revised above INR165 per ton given Q1 levels near INR180?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to revise; the INR160-165 range was indicative and reflects several moving factors including dollar, ferrochrome, scrap and competition.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from Q4 to Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Three factors: FX gain fell to INR25 crore from INR65 crore, weaker value-added product mix, and higher trial and freight costs booked in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Will a plant in South America fast-track scale-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Not for now; the immediate constraint is customer trial acceptance, not supply. Local manufacturing requires an ecosystem, and India remains the base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Chile high-chrome order?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply is going well at about 3,000-3,500 tons per quarter, with no explicit confirmation of further adjacent-mine enquiries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and cash position?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex raised to INR350-400 crore, including INR170-200 crore for a corporate campus; cash of about INR4,500-5,000 crore is being held for at least a few more quarters.

risks_watch: Outcome of South America mine trials (NGDS and high-chrome conversions) remains undisclosed and timing is uncertain.
Margin pressure from freight, raw material costs and product mix; FX gain has fallen sharply QoQ.
Chinese competition in forged media and potential spread into high-chrome.
Capital allocation: about INR4,500-5,000 crore cash, with no near-term buyback or dividend decision.
Overseas plant plans (Ghana, China) are slowed, with no timeline.
532683|2026-06.management_tone: Confident about long-term strategy but deliberately cautious on near-term numbers: management refused to share trial outcomes, volume guidance, or realisation revisions, and repeatedly deferred specifics to future quarters.

543325|2026-06.headline: Rolex Rings Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4.3% to INR304 crore on labour-constrained output, while EBITDA margin expanded to 22.6% and PAT grew 22% to INR60 crore.
543325|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR304 crore, up 4.3% YoY, which management said was short of its guided growth because a shop-floor labour shortage in April to mid-June limited output, not demand. Auto components grew 13.5% to INR163 crore while bearing rings fell 6% to INR118 crore, with softness concentrated in domestic and European industrial bearing rings. EBITDA was INR69 crore at a 22.6% margin (up 100 bps YoY) and PAT rose 22% to INR60 crore, the third straight quarter of YoY margin expansion. Management said operations normalised from June, July 2026 was the highest-revenue month since inception, and it reiterated mid-teen FY27 revenue growth guidance while cutting its margin guidance to 21-22% citing ocean freight costs.

qa_highlights.question: What was the labour shortage reason and was lost revenue deferred or lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited hot summer, vacations, weddings and crop season leave for semi-skilled workers; it said nothing was lost, output was deferred by about a month, and the fix is 3 shifts, overtime and temporary labour for 2-2.5 months at some extra cost.

qa_highlights.question: Will Rolex reach INR500 crore in export auto components in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not INR500 crore but confident of INR425-450 crore, against FY26 exports of INR350 crore; the analyst noted Q1 annualises to about INR450 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be expected, and is 22% possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided conservatively to 21-22% for FY27 because of freight costs, and said a 50 bps uplift is possible in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US duty refund recognised in revenue or other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Some marginal US duty drawback refund was received in Q1 and is included in the numbers; management said refunds will be booked in revenue, not other income, and the major chunk is still pending.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash be deployed given the debt-free balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it may pay dividends or do another buyback after the INR180 crore buyback, and is exploring a JV with an overseas partner (global agency appointed, 6-9 months to outcome) and inorganic options.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic and Timken-linked bearing ring business decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the bearing ring export decline mainly to Timken's reduced business, and said it is diversifying to new customers in the US and Europe; no meaningful share recovery yet, with results expected in a couple of quarters.

risks_watch: Ocean freight and container availability: freight is 2-3x normal and shipping lines are not returning vessels to India, which may spill into Q2.
Timken-linked bearing ring export volumes continue to decline; recovery depends on new customer wins not yet visible.
