Labour availability: recurrence of seasonal shortage and the cost of temporary labour.
Pending US duty drawback refunds: major chunk not yet received, so timing and size are uncertain.
Some US orders under the INR1.75 billion programme are on hold due to tariffs.

Geography mix: West Africa about 30%, Russia/CIS about 22%, Southeast Asia about 20%, Central America about 15%, Europe about 10%, India about 5%.
Customers: about 90% direct brand owners and about 10% traders. Management cited about 98% customer retention.

FDC: management cited LOIs for 70-80% of FDC capacity from Russia, Europe, the US and Southeast Asia (subject to quality and price). Two of these customers are new and five are existing. Global FDC market is about 2,50,000 MT, so 5,500 MT is about 2.2% share.
FDC realisation expected to be 28-32% above spray-dried, which management said is equivalent to a 20-30% EBITDA per kg premium in later exchanges.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4,500 MT capacity contributing revenue in Q1, and what is its utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioned in March 2026 and running at about 90-95% utilisation in Q1; Q1 is seasonally lean, with Q2-Q4 expected to improve.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins keep rising, and what is the FDC start timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expected to rise 0.5-1% from Q1 levels. FDC trials by June 2027 with production from Q2 FY28; 60-65% utilisation over 8-9 months, adding about 2,400 MT in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue potential and the chicory contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the FY27 revenue ballpark is INR850-900 crore on 10,500 MT. Chicory revenue is INR40-45 crore a year, and EBITDA from chicory in Q1 was about INR2.1 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the debt and capex plans for FDC?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt capped at INR450 crore; phase 2 to be funded from FY28 incremental cash flow; no equity dilution planned at present.

qa_highlights.question: Why are working capital days high at 120-130 and when does cash flow improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth inventory is the main reason; CFO said FY27 operating cash flow will be positive, with working capital days around 125 and the FY27 cash-generation capacity estimated at about INR79 crore if growth inventory was not needed.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any hedging or inventory loss risk given production above sales in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said beans are bought back-to-back, with 40-45 days of stock held; surplus Q1 production is expected to be picked up by customers in Q2.

539686|2026-06.headline: K.P. Energy Q1 FY27 total income rose ~126% YoY to Rs 520.97 crore, but gross margin fell to ~20% from 28% in Q4 FY26.

533169|2026-06.headline: Man Infra Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 29% YoY to ₹72 crore on revenue up 8% to ₹218 crore; management reiterates 25%+ FY27 PAT growth guidance.
533169|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong quarter, citing consolidated revenue from operations of ₹218 crore (+8% YoY) and profit after tax attributable to shareholders of ₹72 crore (+29% YoY). Cash and cash equivalents rose to ₹768 crore at June 2026 from ₹686 crore at FY26-end, with borrowings of ₹78 crore, which management said are mostly partner contributions in joint ventures. Pre-sales in the quarter were about 85,000 sq ft, or roughly ₹290 crore, which management acknowledged is low, attributing the gap to launches that have not yet happened (Marine Lines, Berkeley House). Management kept its FY27 PAT growth guidance of over 25% and its target of ₹5,000 crore cumulative pre-sales over two years, and reiterated a ₹35,000 crore group GDV goal by 2031.

financial_highlights.metric: Profit after tax attributable to shareholders (Q1 FY27)

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹686 crore at end of FY26
Mostly partner contributions in JV projects per management
Management noted it is below FY26 run-rate

segments.name: Mira-Bhayendar (Aaradhya Parkwood)
segments.commentary: Towers C and D (2 of 4) received occupation certificates in Q1; the project has 1,000 units, ~5.3 lakh sq ft carpet area, ~₹925 crore sales potential, and is 90% sold. Remaining two towers due by end of next year.

segments.name: Vile Parle (Jade Park, DM project)
segments.commentary: Over 60% of inventory sold on ~3.5 lakh sq ft carpet area; near 100% RCC expected by next year. Held under the cluster redevelopment policy and classified as a DM project.

segments.name: Bandra / Pali Hill (Marina Vista, MS collection)
segments.commentary: Launched June 2026 with ~₹500 crore GDV; 30% sold within two months. Artek Park (BKC) is over 25% sold.

segments.name: Mount Mary (Berkeley House)
segments.commentary: IOA received for an ultra-luxury project with over ₹1,000 crore GDV; demolition and vacation of existing structure underway.

segments.name: Mulund West (Atmosphere Tower G, O2 High Street)
segments.commentary: Atmosphere Tower G (~3.2 lakh sq ft carpet) is 75% sold, with delivery targeted by December 2027. O2 High Street is a new commercial launch on the final phase of Atmosphere.

segments.name: Ghatkopar (Aaradhya OnePark)
segments.commentary: ~5.3 lakh sq ft carpet across 11 towers, over 60% sold; structure complete and finishing underway, with delivery targeted by March 2027.

segments.name: Tardeo (Aaradhya Avaan, South Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Over 306 m tall, ~6.5 lakh sq ft carpet, over 60% sold. Half the building (about 32 habitable floors) to be delivered by March 2028 against RERA commitment of December 2030; 40 floors reached so far.

segments.name: Tardeo 2.0 (South Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Acquired project with over ₹2,000 crore GDV; IOA received and launch now targeted within FY27 rather than Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Marine Lines
segments.commentary: Launch targeted by March 2027 after FSI policy change and additional plot acquisitions; over ₹3,000 crore GDV per management, DM structure. Expected to surpass Aavan in height.

segments.name: US (Miami)
segments.commentary: First two villas completed, one sold and one retained as show house for sale around March next year. Third villa targeted at ~$15 million. Ritz-Carlton branded residences presales ~$25 million, completion targeted December 2030. About $35 million transferred so far.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Management is near final negotiations on a significantly large external EPC order, expected to be announced within two quarters. In-house construction pipeline is ₹9,000-10,000 crore, and a Vadhvan port project is in bidding.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT growth guidance of over 25% over FY26 reiterated; management said it sees this as comfortable at the bottom line.
Cumulative pre-sales target of ₹5,000 crore over the next two years reiterated; management said it might exceed this if markets stay strong.
Group GDV target of over ₹35,000 crore by 2031 reiterated, with management expecting it to be achieved earlier.
Management aims for a bottom line near ₹500 crore in roughly 2-3 years; it said a significant jump would start this year.
Launch pipeline of about 1.1 million sq ft carpet and ~₹6,600 crore GDV planned this year (two launched so far: Marina Vista and O2 High Street).
Management said it expects to add ₹2.5-3,000 crore GDV per ₹200 crore of capital, with ~₹3,000 crore of cash generation over three years.
capex_capacity: Aaradhya OnePark (Ghatkopar) delivery targeted by March 2027 with structure complete and finishing ongoing.
Aaradhya Avaan (Tardeo) half-building delivery targeted March 2028; 100% RCC targeted by August 2027.
Aaradhya Parkwood remaining two towers due by end of next year; Atmosphere Tower G due by December 2027.
Management said DM projects require under 10% of GDV as investment.
Construction is largely in-house (plant, machinery, labour camps), which management says speeds execution.
demand_pricing: Ultra-luxury ticket sizes are ₹1 lakh per sq ft and above; Mount Mary and Pali Hill sell around ₹20,000-25,000 per sq ft depending on inventory (as stated; figures in the transcript are inconsistent).
Management said its underwriting assumes zero price appreciation and a 10-15% discount to market, with a target of about 20% bottom-line margin.
Management cited raw-material inflation of 13-15% (marble, tiles, steel) linked to the Middle East conflict, which it expects to pass through in pricing.
Management said it will not expand outside MMR for the next couple of years, citing margin per sq ft and cyclical risk in other cities.
Management said Q1 pre-sales are lumpy because launches drive sales; it cited a ₹1,000 crore-plus presales month at launch and said Marine Lines and Berkeley House are not yet launched.

504973|2026-06.headline: Chola MS Q1 FY27 combined ratio rose to 120.4% with GWP up 6.7% to Rs 2,130 crore and motor OD loss ratio still elevated.
504973|2026-06.overview:
Chola MS (general insurance arm of Cholamandalam Financial Holdings) reported GDPI of Rs 1,860 crore (+2.6% YoY) and GWP of Rs 2,130 crore (+6.7%), below management's expectations. Claims ratio rose to 85.6% (vs 81.3%) and combined ratio to 120.4%, driven by motor reserve strengthening, elevated motor OD claims and a large fire loss (Rs 12.4 crore net). Profit before tax was Rs 116 crore on operating profit of Rs 71 crore. Management said the OD loss ratio is unacceptable and targets a high-70s level first, while the Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment remains unprovided pending review.</overview>

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Largest line (~70% of book per management); portfolio grew ~5.7% in Q1, mainly commercial vehicles. Mix: private cars 48%, two-wheelers ~9.5%, commercial vehicles ~42.5%. Motor combined ratio 128% in FY26 vs 123% in FY25; OD loss ratio now 80-86% range per analyst framing, not disputed by management.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: Portfolio declined 8.6% in Q1 vs industry fire decline of ~28%; Chola MS fire decline limited to 15.5%. Growth in marine, engineering and liability.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Growth moderate; decline driven by pricing corrections in PSU bank group platform and migration of business to retail platform. Claims settled within 30 days for 99%; NPS 73. Health is being rebuilt from the ground up.

guidance_outlook: OD loss ratio near-term target: bring it to high-70s, then progressively to mid-70s; management said it expects below 80% over time, with a couple of quarters needed for measures to show results.

Corrective measures across motor (new vs renewal mix, NCB focus, ACS control, repair vs replacement analysis) and health (product redesign, pricing revisions, SME push) expected to become visible over coming quarters.
Expects greater property pricing discipline after June NATCAT events; reinsurance market correction more likely at next renewal cycle.
Ind AS / IFRS transition effective April 1, 2027 (one-year IRDAI forbearance granted); no profitability impact estimate yet, preliminary observations possibly next quarter.
Industry CAT loss estimate of Rs 3,000-4,000 crore from multiple events in Gujarat, Assam, Jamshedpur and Maharashtra.
capex_capacity: Reinsurance capacity for fire and engineering secured at start of FY27, described as comparable to leading private players.
Motor issuance platform rolled out across bank channel; workflow enhancements under way in motor claims.
Health network exceeds 13,000 hospitals via PSU bank retail health partnerships.
Readiness work ongoing for Ind AS, Risk-Based Capital (RBC) framework and DPDP requirements.
demand_pricing: Industry GI premium growth ~8.3% in Q1 vs 8.9% a year earlier; motor and health led growth, fire under severe pricing pressure.
Industry combined ratio ~117.8% in FY26 vs 112.6% FY25; Chola MS 115.2% FY26 vs 110% FY25.
Motor TP is tariff-based; premiums do not keep pace with claims inflation and court award trends.
Inward reinsurance growth cited as a driver of GWP outpacing GDPI; sources are commercial-lines participation and group health.
GIFT City reinsurers cited as contributing to soft commercial-lines pricing; management expects limited sustainable lead-line capacity from them.

qa_highlights.question: Has any additional motor TP provision been made for the Supreme Court homemaker judgment, and what is the path for motor OD loss ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: No provision taken in Q1 for the Supreme Court judgment; review petition pending. OD loss ratio not accepted as the new normal; immediate target is high-70s, then mid-70s over time. Management said the 84.4% motor figure cited by analyst was not confirmed in the call, and said OD loss ratio below 80% is achievable over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did retail and group health decline when the industry is growing strongly?
qa_highlights.answer: Group health decline reflects virtually no gross-subsidy business left, standalone accounts required to be individually profitable, and PSU bank group platform pricing corrections with migration to retail platform. Focus shifts to multinational single-mandate clients, SME and GPA cross-sell.

qa_highlights.question: Is the claims ratio rise from new book or from reserve provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase reflects claims inflation assumptions in reserving (expected ULR), not pure reserve strengthening; motor TP is tariff-based so pricing lags claims cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is motor two-wheeler reduced and how does the Supreme Court ruling affect claims?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-wheeler reduction was deliberate given profitability; courts have not uniformly applied the Rs 30,000 threshold and evaluate cases individually. Solvency impact of an adverse outcome not quantified; reserves said to include margin for adverse deviation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IFRS/Ind AS profitability and ROE impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Implementation effective April 1, 2027 after one-year forbearance; no reliable estimate yet, special-purpose financial statements not yet filed with IRDAI. Preliminary observations possibly next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is inward reinsurance growth sustainable and what is the CAT and reinsurance renewal outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inward reinsurance comes from commercial lines participation and selective group health; sustainable only as underwriting appetite allows. Hours-clause structure means separate deductibles per event, so P&L impact could be larger, supporting pricing discipline; reinsurance softness more visible at next renewal.

risks_watch: Motor OD loss ratio (80-86% range) and whether it moves toward high-70s as guided.
Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment: review outcome and possible retrospective provisioning; solvency at 1.93x.
Reinsurance renewal terms after soft market and GIFT City capacity; loss of commissions or higher retention risk.
Health portfolio profitability and rebuilding of retail health capabilities; combined ratio of group health was flagged as a concern.
Ind AS transition from April 1, 2027, with impact on profitability and ROE still unquantified.

544030|2026-06.headline: Flair Writing Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10.6% YoY to INR319.2 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 16.7% on raw material inflation; FY27 15% growth guidance reiterated.
544030|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 10.6% YoY to INR319.2 crore while gross margin held at 50% (down 31 bps YoY, down 151 bps QoQ). EBITDA rose 7.7% YoY to INR53.3 crore with margin of 16.7% (down 46 bps YoY), and PAT grew only 0.5% YoY to INR29.1 crore as other income fell. Management attributed margin pressure to West Asia-driven raw material inflation, and said price hikes, reduced schemes and discounts are working to offset it. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% and an EBITDA margin target of 17-18%.

financial_highlights.value: 49.7% (as stated in Q&A) / ~50% (as stated in CFO remarks)

financial_highlights.change: +7.7% YoY (corrected by errata from 23%); EBITDA margin 16.7%, -46 bps YoY, -116 bps QoQ
+54.3% YoY vs INR13 crore; ~6% of revenue
INR33.25 crore capitalised for Valsad factory building

segments.name: Pens / Writing Instruments
segments.commentary: Revenue INR220 crore, +9% YoY, described as volume-driven; management says domestic revenue grew ~13%. Brands cited are Flair and Hauser; 18 new pens launched. Market share cited as 18% per last CRISIL report.

segments.name: Creative Products
segments.commentary: Revenue INR80 crore, +23% YoY, below the ~50% growth management had previously signalled. Growth was held back by deliberate volume-vs-margin trade-offs in geometry boxes, pencils and some colouring sub-categories; 10 new products launched.

segments.name: Steel Bottles & Houseware
segments.commentary: Revenue INR19 crore, +54.3% YoY. Existing three lines run at ~65% utilisation; the fourth line (INR15 crore investment, expected INR30-35 crore revenue) is due for commissioning by Q4 FY27 and adds ~35% capacity. Management says the existing lines can support ~INR100 crore revenue at current capacity.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% reiterated; management says Pens to grow high single digit, Creatives and Steel Bottles to grow ~40%.
EBITDA margin target of 17-18% for the year (CFO also cited 17.5-18% target); cost pressure expected to ease over the next three quarters as pricing and scheme rationalisation flows through.
Creatives plus Steel Bottles & Houseware expected to rise to ~35-38% of FY27 revenue from ~31% in FY26.
Working capital cycle expected to improve by ~10 days by end of FY27 as inventory normalises.
Three-year outlook: CFO said 15% CAGR is 'easily achievable' but declined to give a higher number.
capex_capacity: Valsad factory building capitalised; machinery and moulds yet to be installed, with commissioning expected around end of Q1 FY27 and full operationalisation over the next two quarters.
Capex to revenue ratio of ~3x maintained for the Valsad unit, which management says covers growth for about 1.5 years across Pens and Creatives.
Steel Bottles: fourth next-generation automatic line ordered, commissioning by Q4 FY27, adding ~30-35% capacity at a cost of ~INR15 crore.
Surat facility has begun 100% operations in the new factory, capitalised in the previous year.
Q1 capex INR43.42 crore in total; Surat capex of INR38.7 lakh for investments and moulds. Company states it is zero-debt and funds expansion from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand growth across key categories; back-to-school season positive. Growth in Q1 described as volume-driven.
Price increases of roughly 10% (management said 10% +/- in household, versus 10-15% raw material inflation), plus rationalised trade schemes and discounts across all three segments.
Exports flat YoY due to West Asia disruption, longer transit times and higher freight; management says export growth turned positive in the current quarter.
OEM business is ~5% of total revenue; domestic OEM fully phased out and legacy OEM reduced to zero.
Management said Reynolds' acquisition by DOMS would not affect its strategy; it plans to stay aggressive in Pens.
Creative distribution remains at ~68,000 stationery outlets; focus is on throughput in existing outlets rather than adding outlets.

532505|2026-06.headline: UCO Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 8% YoY to Rs 656 crore despite a Rs 1,237 crore one-time DTA charge; operating profit up 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore.
532505|2026-06.overview: UCO Bank reported Q1 FY27 with advances up 21.18% YoY to Rs 2,72,768 crore and deposits up 11.28% to Rs 3,32,315 crore. Operating profit rose 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore, helped by Rs 1,018 crore of technical write-off recoveries, of which about Rs 800 crore is from a few accounts management does not expect to recur. Net profit was held to Rs 656 crore by total tax of Rs 1,919 crore, including a one-time Rs 1,237 crore DTA remeasurement on the shift to the new tax regime. Management said most asset-quality and margin metrics were within guidance, and that it would review credit growth guidance only after Q2.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,919 crore (regular ~Rs 625 crore plus one-time DTA Rs 1,237 crore)

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -55 bps YoY; NNPA -20 bps YoY
Was 54.06% last year and 52.66% in March; management expects normalised ~50%

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 27.32% YoY. Home loans grew about 20% and vehicle loans about 65% YoY off a low base; management expects roughly 30% vehicle loan growth and 20-25% home loan growth.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 30% YoY; gold loans are cited as a growth driver.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 18.79% YoY; management expects 19-20% growth to continue. ECLGS sanctions stand at Rs 2,150 crore with Rs 1,700 crore disbursed.

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 25.27% YoY and make up 64.5% of the book, within the 62-65% guidance; management aims to hold around 65%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew about 17%, driven by working-capital limit drawdowns. The bank holds no IBPC exposure and is curtailing low-yield PSU and government lending.

guidance_outlook: Credit growth guidance kept at 12-14%, though management says it aims to exceed this; review after Q2 FY27 results. Rs 15,000 crore sanctioned pipeline awaiting disbursement.
NIM guidance 2.8-2.9%, with management aiming to stay slightly above 2.9%; yield on advances expected to hold.
Cost-to-income expected at or around 50% or below for FY27, despite Q1's 37.49%.
ROA of 0.68% annualised in Q1; management sees it near 1% by year-end as the DTA charge is a one-time item.
Credit cost to stay below the 0.75% guidance; deposit repricing largely complete, so cost of funds expected to stay stable.
Expected Credit Loss (ECL): about 60% of the estimated transition requirement already provided as buffer; remaining 40% to be built over the next 4-5 quarters before the ECL regime starts.
capex_capacity: Around 400 branches in West Bengal under five zonal offices; pan-India network of 3,421 branches.
GIFT City branch to open in the next month; all approvals in place and IT implementation in progress.
Omni-channel platform and corporate cash management service said to launch 'very soon'.
GST smart product to rise from Rs 25 lakh to Rs 1 crore ticket size; pre-qualified personal loan journey to be extended to the call centre.
Digital balance sheet of about Rs 35,000 crore at 30 June, up from Rs 25,000 crore at 31 March; 31 STP journeys live; about 70% of fixed deposits now booked digitally.
demand_pricing: Retail loan rates held steady, as they are linked to the repo rate; MCLR raised 5 bps to 8.80% in July 2026 from 8.75%.
Corporate pricing held steady; management sees demand shifting to loans as bond yields are limited.
Yield on advances was stable, moving only about 3 bps QoQ.
Competition from PSBs, private banks, RRBs and NBFCs; management did not quantify the split and sees it as market expansion.
Management reports no stress in any sector; corporate pipelines in infrastructure, renewable energy, transmission, steel and cement.

532505|2026-09.headline: UCO Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 26.77% YoY to Rs 786 crore; advances grew 24.70%, well above the 12-14% guidance.
532505|2026-09.overview: UCO Bank reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs 786 crore, up 26.77% YoY from Rs 620 crore, with operating profit of Rs 1,872 crore (up 16.04%). Global advances grew 24.70% to Rs 2,87,690 crore, while deposits grew 14.36% to Rs 3,49,590 crore and CASA ratio slipped to 36.77%. Gross NPA fell 60 bps YoY to 1.96% and net NPA to 0.18%, both within guidance. Management said the quarter's slippage rise was mainly agriculture crop-loan marking done half-yearly in September, and that the June quarter had a one-off Rs 785 crore recovery that did not recur.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -60 bps YoY; NNPA -25 bps YoY

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 30.23% YoY; housing loan growth above 20% YoY with average home-loan ticket up from about Rs 35 lakh to about Rs 45 lakh.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri advances grew 29.59% YoY; agri slippages rose to Rs 205 crore in Q2 from Rs 73 crore in Q1, but were below Rs 238 crore a year ago.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 20.32% YoY; management sees scope for more growth here.

segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 24.15% YoY; sanctioned but undisbursed corporate pipeline is about Rs 10,000 crore.

segments.commentary: RAM portfolio is Rs 1,68,736 crore, up 26.92% YoY, and its share of advances has crossed 65% against the 62-65% guidance.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Hong Kong and Singapore branches are operating; GIFT City IBU opened in Q2 FY27.

Deposit growth guidance of 10-12% was exceeded (actual 14%+).
GNPA guidance is below 2% by 31 March 2027; already at 1.96%.
Net NPA guidance is below 0.25% for the year; already at 0.18%.
Global NIM guidance of 2.80-2.90% was exceeded (3.00%); management expects to sustain NIM above guidance with repo pass-through.
Credit cost guidance is below 0.75% for FY27; Q2 is 0.65%.
Cost-to-income expected to be around 50% for the full year and possibly below 50% next year.
ECL transition on 1 April 2027 estimated at about Rs 3,200 crore+ requirement; bank has provided about Rs 2,500 crore over and above existing provisions.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 3,439 after adding 27 branches in the quarter; business per branch Rs 185 crore vs Rs 161 crore a year ago.
Business per employee Rs 30 crore vs Rs 25 crore a year ago.
GIFT City IBU opened in Q2; three international branches (Hong Kong, Singapore, GIFT City).
Digital business balance sheet under Project Parivartan above Rs 48,000 crore as of 30 September 2026.
Seven processes automated via RPA; digital marketing solution onboarded; customer 360-degree portal rolled out in branches.
Recruitment of specialist officers (data analysts, CAs, trade finance officers) in FY27; further recruitment of professional officers and customer service associates planned.
demand_pricing: Advances growth came from all segments; RAM share has crossed 65%, and management expects it to hold around 65% with corporate growth also continuing.
Corporate sanctioned pipeline of about Rs 10,000 crore is undisbursed; disbursement depends on corporates' acceptance of lending rates and capex plans.
About 66% of advances are linked to external benchmark (repo/EBLR); a 25 bps repo hike was passed on immediately to these loans.
Deposit rates unchanged for now; management said no immediate need to raise term deposit rates, with any hike applying only to new deposits and renewals.
Gold loan yield is about 9% (slightly below) and unchanged QoQ.
Housing loan growth above 20% YoY from both volume and ticket size; second-hand car loans are not tracked separately and are small.
Domestic yield on advances 8.11%; global yield 7.79%; cost of funds 4.44%, up slightly.

539056|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR178 crores and EBITDA 24% to INR90 crores (50.7% margin), with footfalls up 22%.
539056|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 20% YoY to INR178 crores, with footfalls up 22% to over 11.5 lakh visitors and parks revenue up 22% to INR161 crores. EBITDA rose 24% to INR90 crores and PAT rose 30% to INR58 crores. Management attributed the soft spots to an extended heat wave that kept Khopoli park non-operational for about two weeks and a shift in some CBSE school holiday calendars, and said it deliberately priced softer to build footfall. Management also announced the acquisition of a 50.002% stake in Mehsana Next Parks (Shanku's Water Park) for INR50 crores and the entry into indoor entertainment via a Hello Park franchise.

segments.name: Mumbai-Pune catchment (4 parks)
segments.commentary: Revenue +18% YoY on footfalls +19%; largest contributor and most affected by heat wave and Khopoli closure.

segments.name: Rest of Maharashtra (Shirdi, Saiteerth)
segments.commentary: Revenue +33% YoY on footfalls +14%; ARPU +17% on better product mix and higher guest spend.

segments.name: Gujarat (Surat, Mehsana)
segments.commentary: Footfalls +32% but revenue only +15%; ARPU lower YoY on visitor mix change and promotional pricing at Surat.

segments.name: Central India (Indore)
segments.commentary: Fastest-growing catchment: footfalls +48%, revenue +44% YoY.

segments.name: Hospitality (Novotel Imagicaa, 287 keys, Khopoli)
segments.commentary: Revenue largely stable despite occupancy at 62%; ARR INR9,657.

Hello Park: plan to add 2-3 indoor centres a year; first centre in Hyderabad (Lake Shore Y Junction Mall) later this year; second at Phoenix Mall, Surat.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no clear reason for a slowdown currently, though quarter-by-quarter volatility remains. Guidance was corrected to 12-15%, not 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Is ROCE weak despite high utilisation, and what is the capex payback threshold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 ROCE was 10.7%, with a target of about 15% through process tweaks and exiting low-value business. Typical capex payback is 3-4 years. Loss-making JLR-linked investments are expected to turn around in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What changed versus past order book claims that did not materialise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said past EV bets had long validation periods and JLR volumes fell or SOPs slipped. Current order book focuses on ICE, hybrid and structural parts with shorter validation, and growth now comes from traditional products.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the development spend went into capacity and what is the non-auto strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Development spend went into larger, heavier parts (28-30 kg vs earlier 12-15 kg), requiring new machines and dedicated teams. Intangible spend about Rs 18-20 crore last year, Rs 3-5 crore per quarter. Non-auto aspiration unchanged but about 2% today; management expects meaningful change by end-FY28.

544008|2026-06.headline: Max Estates Q1 FY27 pre-sales of about Rs 1,100 crore (5x YoY), with consol PAT of Rs 8 crore on Rs 52 crore revenue.
544008|2026-06.overview: Pre-sales rose 5x YoY to about Rs 1,100 crore, anchored by the full sellout of Phase-1 of the Terraces at Estate 361 (about Rs 500 crore) plus Rs 600 crore of sustenance sales. Collections were about Rs 575 crore, and management said these fund construction without incremental debt on residential projects. Consolidated revenue was Rs 52 crore, EBITDA Rs 8 crore, PBT Rs 11 crore and PAT Rs 8 crore, with the P&L reflecting only a fraction of the contracted portfolio. ICRA assigned a first-time A+ (stable) issuer rating on a consolidated basis. Management declined to give FY27 sales guidance, though it did guide collections and deployment figures.

financial_highlights.metric: Lease rental income (Max Towers, Max House, Max Square)
Gross debt (incl. LRD borrowings of Rs 934 crore)

segments.name: Commercial annuity (Max Towers, Max House, Max Square)
segments.commentary: 100% occupancy across three operating assets; lease rental income Rs 40 crore, up 5% YoY. Latest Max Towers lease at Rs 156/sq ft/month vs weighted average Rs 132, a mark-to-market upside of over 50%.

segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 15 crore in Q1, up 16% YoY.

Sector 59 (Golf Course Extension Road, GDV above Rs 3,500 crore) expected to launch in Q3 FY27; management has not decided whether to launch it in phases.

Max Square 2 (1 mn sq ft) OC expected by Q2 FY28, adding about Rs 125 crore to annuity; Max District (1.6 mn sq ft) OC in Q3 FY28 and Q3 FY29, adding about Rs 200 crore; combined annual rental of about Rs 700 crore at peak occupancy.

Under-construction commercial assets: Max Square 2, Max District and Max One.
Annual target of 2 mn sq ft of residential development additions.
Estate 105 (Noida) GDV revised up to Rs 6,000 crore on a residential mix; Phase-2 to launch in FY27.

demand_pricing: Delhi NCR recorded about 8,800 residential launches in Q2 CY26 (Gurgaon about 70%); about 18,500 units in H1 CY26.
Residential weighted average prices broadly stable QoQ; sales volumes across the sector moderated through the quarter.
Delhi NCR office leasing of 4.1 mn sq ft in Q2 CY26.

Pre-leasing at Max District (about 200,000 sq ft) and Max One (about 100,000 sq ft) at 25-30% premium; pipeline above 3 mn sq ft under discussion. Max Square 2 LOI for about 90,000 sq ft at 25% premium; Max District LOI for 200,000 sq ft at 35% premium.

Antara-branded senior living units sell at about a 7-10% (management also cited ~10%) premium to Max Estates units; development management fee to Antara is about 9.5% of topline on the Antara portion.

500219|2026-06.headline: Jain Irrigation Q1 FY27 revenue fell about 2.5% to Rs 1,500 crore; adjusted PAT dropped to Rs 3 crore from Rs 30 crore, with Rs 680 crore NCDs due this fiscal.
500219|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was about Rs 1,500 crore, down roughly 2.5% YoY, with Hi-Tech degrowing, Plastics flat and Agro-Processing growing on beverages and overseas sales. EBITDA fell because standalone India volumes were lower and fixed costs went unabsorbed; Hi-Tech margin fell to 14.4% from 16.6%. Management said April was weak, May-June improved, and July was positive, and it expects a stronger second half. Working capital days improved (consolidated net working capital 183 days vs 210 a year ago) and about 78% of EBITDA converted to cash.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (after non-cash NCD interest unwinding)

financial_highlights.change: from 210 days in June 2025 and 186 days in March 2026

segments.name: Hi-Tech
segments.commentary: Revenue fell about 22% YoY; retail (MIS drip, tissue culture, solar) fell about 17% and projects fell about 63%. Drip (MIS) fell 16% from Rs 438 crore to Rs 368 crore; tissue culture fell 10%.

segments.name: Plastics
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly flat YoY; overseas plastics revenue grew about 40%, and segment EBITDA margin rose to about 11% from 10%.

segments.name: Agro-Processing (food)
segments.commentary: Grew significantly on new beverage business (about Rs 60 crore in April-June) and overseas sales, but EBITDA fell about 3 points on seasonality.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA lost in Q1 to be recovered in H2 FY27 and full-year PAT to beat FY26.
Hi-Tech: double-digit revenue growth targeted for FY27; solar pump sales expected to pick up from September.
FY27 margin guidance: about 14% standalone and about 12-13% consolidated.

Debt: about Rs 680 crore of NCDs due in FY27, about Rs 230 crore in September 2026 and the rest in March 2027; management says internal cash flows will cover them, with refinancing term sheets in hand.
Legacy government receivables target for FY27 is Rs 422 crore (minimum Rs 380 crore for the remaining nine months); Rs 60 crore collected in Q1 and Rs 25-30 crore in July.
Food business IPO deferred; management says it will look at it from September if markets improve.
capex_capacity: Biochar plant recently started (mango stones, corn cob, cotton stalk feedstock); management expects financial impact from next fiscal, with carbon credits taking 6-9 months.
Tamil Nadu land monetisation delayed by elections; management hopes it will be delivered in the current quarter.
Remaining project billing outside Pune is about Rs 40-50 crore; the large Pune water-supply project still has triple-digit crore billing left; Q2 project billing could be below Rs 24 crore.
demand_pricing: Polymer prices rose about 50%; most increases were passed to customers, and some customers postponed purchases until prices fall.
Delayed monsoon onset in June pushed drip sales into the current quarter; July was positive and August-September are expected to be good.
Government-linked and subsidy-driven micro-irrigation sales were deliberately not pursued because of cash flow and long receivables; management estimated Rs 50-60 crore of sales were forgone.
Dam storage was about 67% of capacity; management expects about 85% by monsoon-end, supportive of the rabi season and next summer.

qa_highlights.question: How much legacy government receivables were recovered and how much project work is left?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 60 crore received in Q1 and Rs 25-30 crore in July. Remaining project billing outside Pune is about Rs 40-50 crore, with no working capital needed; about 10-12 of 72 projects carry O&M over two to three years, which management called light.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 674-680 crore of debt due this fiscal be repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited internal accruals first, then legacy receivable collections, asset monetisation (surplus land) and refinancing; it said Rs 1,300 crore of bank debt was repaid over three and a half years and that the company has never missed a payment in four years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Hi-Tech down about 22% and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail fell about 17% and projects about 63%; management called the drip decline a one-off from the delayed monsoon and polymer-driven postponements. Hi-Tech margin was 14.4% vs 16.6%, and management expects margins to recover to typical levels through the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of write-offs on project receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said provisions were made in FY21-22 after a project review and it does not expect material write-offs; net receivables of Rs 1,975 crore in June are largely good, with about 55% linked to government-related items.

qa_highlights.question: Why are working capital requirements higher than listed peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to legacy long-term project receivables and state-government orders paid after 6-12 months, and said the cycle should improve substantially in FY28 once project receivables are cleared.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of refinancing and the food-business IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no pushback from lenders, a couple of term sheets are in hand, and talks are ongoing. The food-business IPO (about Rs 1,000 crore including PE exit) has been deferred due to weak valuations; the company will revisit it from September.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT negative when revenue is flat, and what are the coffee and biochar updates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the loss to higher raw-material costs and lower standalone India volumes, and expects a full-year PAT improvement. First coffee orders have come from the Coffee Board; the biochar business has started, with impact on numbers from next fiscal.

risks_watch: Refinancing of about Rs 230 crore NCD due in September 2026 and about Rs 450 crore due in March 2027 has not yet been completed; management relies on term sheets and internal cash flows.
Legacy government receivables of about Rs 800-900 crore and about Rs 500 crore of agency receivables above 180 days; collection pace against the Rs 380 crore minimum target is key.
Polymer price volatility and geopolitical oil-price movements may keep customers postponing purchases.
Weak Q1 adjusted PAT (Rs 3 crore) and reliance on H2 recovery; Q2 is seasonally muted.
Food-business IPO and Tamil Nadu land monetisation timelines have slipped repeatedly.
500219|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on debt repayment and H2 recovery, but cautious on near-term volumes: Q1 is described as muted and beyond management's control. Answers on receivables and monetisation timelines were broad, and several timelines (Tamil Nadu land, IPO) were pushed out.

500402|2026-06.headline: SPML Infra Q1 FY27 revenue rose 74% YoY to INR286 crore and PAT 87% to INR22.7 crore, with EBITDA margin at 10%.
500402|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 revenue grew 74% YoY to INR286 crore, EBITDA rose 81% to INR28 crore and PAT rose 87% to INR22.7 crore, with EBITDA margin at 10% versus 9% a year earlier. Revenue was flat QoQ, EBITDA rose 17% QoQ, and PAT fell 20% QoQ because Q4 FY26 included a one-time tax reversal. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of more than 25% growth in turnover, EBITDA and PAT, with new-order contribution expected mainly from Q4. The company also highlighted a BESS manufacturing line (2.5 GW, targeting NTPC supply from Q4), a stronger balance sheet, and credit rating upgrades.</overview>

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: Drinking water, irrigation, river linking and sewerage; pipeline of about 134 projects worth INR98,725 crore across 11 states, with irrigation and water supply over 80% of value. Water projects take 3 to 3.5 years to execute.

segments.name: Power substation (power EPC)
segments.commentary: Management cites strong demand from thermal capacity additions and substation modernisation; execution of 15 to 18 months per project. Specific Q1 revenue not disclosed.

segments.commentary: Expected FY27 BESS execution of INR200 to 300 crore, mainly in Q4 subject to NTPC design and container approvals. 2.5 GW assembly line is ready; expansion to 5 GW and 600 container units per year targeted for 1H FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover, EBITDA and PAT growth guided at more than 25% YoY, maintained; to be updated each quarter based on orders and execution.
FY27 order inflow target of more than INR5,000 crore; INR1,293 crore won in Q1 and L1 in INR212 crore.
BESS execution of INR200 to 300 crore in FY27, subject to NTPC approvals; design approvals expected by December and container supply from Q4.
Legacy order book of about INR1,251 crore expected to be executed in FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR3,843 crore new order figure net of JV partner share?

qa_highlights.question: Will margins move toward 12% as new orders come in?

qa_highlights.question: How much BESS revenue in FY27 and when?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR50 to 80 crore FY26 spillover has been billed?

qa_highlights.question: What is the main constraint to achieving more than 25% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited no specific constraint beyond unforeseeable events; design approvals are in hand for new orders, and NTPC approval is pending.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS revenue per GW?

532923|2026-06.headline: Renaissance Global Q1 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR690 crores and PAT jumped 288% to INR26 crores, but management guided revenue down as low-return customers are exited.
532923|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 30% YoY to INR690 crores (ex-bullion) and EBITDA rose 22% to INR50 crores, with PAT up sharply to about INR26 crores helped by a weak prior-year restructuring charge. Owned-brand revenue grew 29% to INR89 crores and owned-brand EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% from 10%. Working capital days fell to 220 from 253 YoY. Management said it will exit low-return customer businesses in the customer brands segment, which lowers revenue run-rate by INR400 crores by year-end, while it targets bottom-line growth above 30% for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: from 7.7% a year ago (management's comparison, ex-bullion)

segments.name: Owned brands (D2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR89 crores, up 29% YoY; EBITDA margin 11.5% vs 10%. Focus on Jean Dousset and WithClarity, which together make up the bulk of owned-brand revenue. WithClarity run-rate about INR220 crores, growing about 20%.

segments.name: Licensed brands
segments.commentary: Management is rationalising licences (exiting NFL, Netflix, Harry Potter and others) to focus on Disney, where it is exclusive licensee for fine jewellery. Management said licensed-brand margin fell from 15.5% in FY24 to 10.9% in Q1 FY27 and expects a return to 14-15%.

segments.name: Customer brands (B2B/OEM)
segments.commentary: Where the planned exits sit. Management expects INR300-400 crores of annualised revenue to be removed, with the revenue run-rate down INR400 crores by year-end. Sequential revenue declines expected from Q2.

guidance_outlook: Bottom line expected to grow more than 30% in FY27, with revenue growth muted by customer exits.
Working capital release of about INR250 crores and operating cash flow above INR300 crores in FY27, to be realised by year-end.

Target of INR1,000 crores direct-to-consumer revenue by FY29 with at least 15% operating margin on that segment; FY27 D2C base is about INR500 crores (INR375 crores owned brands, INR125 crores licensed).
Jean Dousset: 7 stores by end FY27 (3 operating today, 4 more planned), then 6 more in FY28; management says each store should add INR25-35 crores of sales and pay back in under 1 year.
Management expects a minor margin dip during the year from exit costs, with margins comparable like-for-like.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity was reduced to match lab-grown diamond realities, with 24 months of restructuring cutting operating expenses by about INR45 crores annually.
Jean Dousset: company owns 65% after exercising an option up from 38.7%; a further stake increase is possible only if more funding is needed and has not yet been discussed at board level.
Tariff mitigation: some manufacturing subcontracted in the US and Middle East, which generates bullion sales.
Possible tariff refunds under application; amount not yet quantified and customers may share in refunds.
demand_pricing: Customer brands exits: management said the exited customers are low-return, with working capital costs above EBITDA generated; inventory exit cost is negligible because gold and silver prices have risen.
Average order values by tier: licensed brands about USD400, WithClarity about USD3,000, Jean Dousset about USD8,000. Customer brands range from USD50 to USD3,000.
Jean Dousset and WithClarity gross margins are 60-65%; WithClarity EBITDA margin is 11-13%.
Forex loss of about INR13 crores in Q1 (rupee appreciation); a large share of working capital is dollar-denominated, giving a natural hedge.
Metal price exposure hedged, with no inventory loss reported in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth continue at Q1's pace, and what about US tariff refunds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects bottom-line momentum to continue but revenue growth may not hold as low-return verticals are exited. Tariff refunds are being applied for; the amount was not disclosed and management asked investors to wait one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment will the INR250 crore working-capital release come from, and how big is the revenue hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Release comes from inventory and receivables, mainly in customer brands. Exits remove INR300-400 crores of annualised revenue, and the revenue run-rate falls INR400 crores by year-end; the company expects no meaningful bottom-line impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why are licensed-brand revenue and margins declining?
qa_highlights.answer: Management rationalised a wide licence portfolio, exiting NFL, Netflix, Harry Potter and others, with exit costs taken. It expects growth and margin recovery to 14-15% from focusing on Disney.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Jean Dousset's revenue is reported, and what is store economics?
qa_highlights.answer: The company consolidates Jean Dousset in full with a 65% stake, and minority interest is shown in the P&L. Brand revenue grew about 30% after acquisition in FY26; each store should add INR25-35 crores of sales and pay back in under 1 year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin decline and will B2B revenue keep rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Bullion sales are a continuing feature because of tariff-mitigation subcontracting. Ex-bullion margin fell from 7.7% to 7.2% due to exit costs. Sequential revenue should decline from Q2, tapering through Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 finance cost trajectory and forex loss outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give quarterly finance cost guidance but expects meaningfully lower net debt YoY by year-end. The forex loss should ease if the currency stabilises at current levels; other income of INR8-9 crores was described as normal course.

risks_watch: Revenue run-rate falls by INR400 crores by year-end from customer exits; revenue growth may turn negative sequentially from Q2.
Achieving INR250 crores working-capital release and INR300 crores operating cash flow in FY27.
Quality of PAT: the 288% jump is partly base effect from prior-year restructuring costs; Q1 forex loss of about INR13 crores.
Jean Dousset store ramp: 4 new stores in FY27 and 6 in FY28 need funding; a further stake increase or third-party investor is not yet discussed.
Tariff refund amount and how much will be passed to customers remain unquantified.
Licensed-brand margin recovery (10.9% to 14-15%) and rising Disney revenue are not yet shown in numbers.

segments.name: Solar inverters
segments.commentary: Single-phase iUNO (up to 5 kW) reached operational profitability; 3-phase iNEO launched up to 12 kW this quarter, with up to 50 kW due by end FY27 and hybrid inverters in development. FY27 solar target is INR24-25 crore, rising to INR250-300 crore next year per management.

guidance_outlook: EEI guidance held at about 20% top-line growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin for the full year; management said it will try to beat this but did not raise it.
Lumel Alucast expected to reach adjusted EBITDA breakeven for full-year FY27; management sees a path to double-digit EBITDA margin in about 2 years.
US organic revenue target INR45 crore this year and INR100 crore in 2-3 years.
Nashik plant to be fully finished in about 1-2 months; management targets more than 2.5x production over the next 4-5 years.
Mumbai and Delhi TMI Experience Centres to be operational by end of FY27; ~15 new products launched over two years with more than 15 planned for FY27.
CT capacity to rise from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 low-voltage units per day, with medium-voltage CTs to follow.
capex_capacity: New Nashik manufacturing facility partially commissioned; both buildings complete, with full completion expected in about 1-2 months.
Current transformer capacity being raised from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 low-voltage units per day (near-doubling), with added machinery already ordered.
Three SMT lines in PCB/EMS operations; latest is high-end and an older line is being upgraded. A fourth line will be added once the three run on three shifts.
Dedicated automated floor for solar inverter manufacturing in the new facility.
Lumel Alucast capacity is underutilised; management is filling it with higher-value orders.
demand_pricing: Domestic order bookings in Q1 were about 20% above last year, but billing lagged, leaving a backlog to be worked off.
Data-centre wins: first win announced, then 3-4 more; about 10 more quotes outstanding.

Lumel S.A. growth comes from product spread, German grid upgrades (EUR5 mn order executed; EUR3 mn follow-on running to year-end) and radiation-detection gates, with Poland security demand after the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
Lumel Alucast: RFQs in advanced stages of commercial negotiation and customer approval; ramp-up takes about 6 months after award. Management is prioritising value over volume.
Solar inverter pricing is competitive with Chinese imports; EPC contractors are moving away from Chinese-sourced units over after-sales and warranty concerns.
Contribution margin is about 45% on average; solar and EMS run at 15-20%, while other products run at 40-75%.

544454|2026-06.headline: Indiqube Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR428 crore (+37% YoY) and PAT rose 91% to INR35 crore, with PAT margin at 8%.
544454|2026-06.overview:
Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR428 crore (+37% YoY), EBITDA of INR87 crore (+34%), EBIT of INR55 crore (+59%) and PAT of INR35 crore (+91%). Margins expanded, with EBIT margin at 13% (11% a year ago) and PAT margin at 8% (6%). Rent-paying area was flat QoQ, which management attributed to the timing of building handovers, with about 2 million sq ft of annual additions still guided. Q&A centred on VAS revenue (INR39 crore one-time in the quarter), solar capex, a large new Noida centre, and occupancy and margin ranges. Management declined to give quarterly OCF or capex figures ahead of the H1 audit.</overview>
