segments.name: Client mix (revenue)
segments.commentary: GCCs ~52-53% of revenue, startups and unicorns ~23%, Indian enterprises ~28% (of which GCCs ~10-12%). Multi-center clients ~41% of revenue; top five clients 12% of revenue; 855 clients as of June 2026.

segments.name: VAS (DesignQube, IndiCare, Eco)
segments.commentary: VAS is ~17% of revenue and management expects it to rise by about 2-4 percentage points. VAS EBIT margin is guided at ~15% for the next one to two years, as growth takes priority over margin.

segments.name: Solar / sustainability
segments.commentary: About 30 MW of solar capacity is operational. Plan to add 25-30 MW this year at INR100-120 crore capex; solar IRR stated at 18-22%.

guidance_outlook: Annual additions of close to 2 million sq ft (about 44,000 seats) reiterated; about 3.9 million sq ft (about 97,000 seats) of headroom already signed.
Corporate occupancy guided at 80-85% (stated later as 82-86%); mature centres (over 12 months) at 85-90% (stated as 86-90%/88-90%).
Margin ranges guided at EBITDA 19-21%, EBIT 11-13%, PAT 8-10% on a annual basis.
Operational break-even for new centres is 5-6 months at about 52-57% occupancy; steady state around 12 months (9-12 months to reach ~90%).
Around 2.8 million sq ft of area under management not yet rent-paying is expected to become operational in 12-16 months (most signed supply to deliver in 12-18 months).
Large Noida centre expected to go live around mid-2027 (Q2 or Q3 FY28).
Management expects to sign larger spaces in Hyderabad and Mumbai during this financial year.
capex_capacity: Solar: 30 MW operational; plan to add 25-30 MW this year at INR100-120 crore capex.
Capex and OCF for Q1 not disclosed; management said figures would be provided with H1 results after audit and review. Capex is driven by interiors, design-and-build, solar and vendor payment cycles.
Debt increase is attributed to solar investment, not the leasing business (per Vikas Agarwal).
New Noida centre is a large single building; live by mid-2027 (Q2/Q3 FY28).
demand_pricing: Institutional supply share rose to ~20% of portfolio from ~12% a couple of years ago; institutional buildings carry higher rents and CAM costs but management says margins are consistent across supply types.
Tier-2 centres: real estate cost INR50-70 per sq ft; seat pricing INR6,500-7,500 per seat; unit economics said to be similar to Tier-1.
Bangalore is ~60-64% of area; Chennai ~10%. Management expects Bangalore share to fall as NCR, Hyderabad, Mumbai and West India grow.
Attrition is negative (net expansion); client renewal rate ~90%; client notice periods 60-90 days; leases are straight leases with landlords (no back-to-back).
Tech parks are ~20% of portfolio. North Bangalore exposure is under 0.5 million sq ft of ~6.5 million sq ft in Bangalore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no QoQ rise in rent-paying area despite 2 million sq ft annual guidance, and is supply slowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said additions are lumpy and tracked annually; H2 FY26 added ~1.14 million sq ft. No slowdown is seen, and ~3.9 million sq ft of signed headroom is available.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR39 crore one-time VAS revenue and how sustainable is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue came across DesignQube, IndiCare and Eco. Management said it is non-recurring in quarters but will keep recurring over time, with VAS share rising 2-4 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: How much solar capex is planned and what IRR is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan of 25-30 MW more at INR100-120 crore; solar IRR 18-22%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the large Noida centre and is it demand-backed?
qa_highlights.answer: Live by mid-2027 (Q2/Q3 FY28). Management said it was largely proactive supply, not pre-leased, based on NCR micro-market research.

qa_highlights.question: Will new centres dilute margins given slow break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Operational break-even takes 5-6 months at 52-57% occupancy and steady state ~12 months, so no margin pressure expected. The 36 months referred to full capex recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What margin will VAS deliver and will it drive group margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: VAS margin ~15% for the next one to two years; management prioritises scale. Group-level margins are expected to stay within the stated ranges.

risks_watch: Rent-paying area was flat QoQ; the ~2 million sq ft annual addition depends on H2-weighted handovers in Jan-Feb.
Revenue concentration: Bangalore ~60% of area; the Noida site is a large non-institutional asset held by an HNI family group.
Capex and OCF not disclosed for Q1; H1 numbers due after audit.
One-time VAS revenue (INR39 crore) inflates the quarter; the underlying run-rate needs checking.
Interest cost rising with solar-linked debt; watch debt quantum and cost in H1 disclosures.
Occupancy guidance has been stated in different ranges during the call (corporate 80-85% vs 82-86%); clarify the official range.
544454|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, pipeline and margin stability, with specific ranges given. Evasive on quarterly capex, OCF and city-wise revenue-to-rent ratio, deferring these to H1 audited numbers.

532734|2026-06.headline: GPIL Q1 FY27: EBITDA margin 19.1%, PAT margin 12.7%, both flat YoY but softer QoQ on costlier merchant iron ore and imported coal.
532734|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew both YoY and QoQ on higher volumes and better realisations, while EBITDA and PAT were broadly flat YoY and down sequentially on input costs. Iron ore mining volume fell because dumping space was constrained by pending tree-cutting approval on additional land, forcing market ore purchases for pellets. One of the new 2 mtpa pellet plants was shut from around mid-June/July on gas price and iron ore economics, with Q2 pellet output guided to roughly 500 kt. Management shelved the 1 mtpa integrated steel project over water allocation delays and moved the 0.7 mtpa CRM complex to Maharashtra, with commissioning now targeted December 2027.

financial_highlights.change: Stable YoY; softer QoQ due to input costs

financial_highlights.metric: Pellet plant (4.7 mtpa expanded capacity) utilisation

financial_highlights.value: About INR13,000/t now vs about INR10,500/t in Q4 FY26 and early Q1
Up about 40-45% under new PNGRB guidelines
About INR10,000/t currently; low of about INR8,700/t in early July

financial_highlights.change: Broadly stable QoQ and YoY; target 2.4920

segments.name: Iron ore mining (Ari Dongri)
segments.commentary: Mining volume declined YoY and QoQ, constrained by overburden dumping space pending government land approval. Captive mining guidance of 3.4 mt for FY27 is said to be unchanged; management expects mining cost to fall below INR2,700/t from FY28 vs INR3,000-3,500/t now.

segments.name: Pellets (4.7 mtpa expanded capacity)
segments.commentary: Ran at 77% utilisation in Q1 with all three plants operating, and pellet sales jumped in Q1 as surplus pellets went to the merchant market. One 2 mtpa plant has been shut since about mid-2026; FY27 pellet guidance of 4.0 mt is under review and expected to be lower.

segments.name: Sponge iron, billet, rolled products (value-added)
segments.commentary: Management cited healthy YoY growth in value-added production led by sponge iron, billets and rolled products. No segment volumes or revenues were given on the call.

segments.name: Galvanized products
segments.commentary: Volumes declined YoY, attributed to monsoon-season delays in project deliveries. Management described this as seasonal.

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage, Maharashtra)
segments.commentary: About INR500 crore spent. Machine delivery starts December 2026 and first container is targeted for Q1 FY28. Containers are being quoted from August 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume guidance is said to be on track, with Q1 at 16-29% of full-year guidance. Management said FY27 pellet output will be slightly lower, and a revised figure will come later.

Q2 FY27 pellet production is expected at about 500 kt if the plant stays shut for the whole quarter. Q3 is expected at full pellet capacity, with merchant ore purchases at 25-30%, falling below 10% in Q4 and to zero (fully captive) in FY28.

Mining ramp-up is expected from Q3 FY27 once government land approval comes through (targeted end-September), reaching full capacity by end Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28. Beneficiation plant commissioning is expected by Q3 FY27.

Margin improvement is expected from Q4 FY27 once the beneficiation plant enables higher captive pellet use. Management said CRM incentives can add 2-3% to CRM margins, taking them to 10-11% from the earlier 7-8%.
Vision 2030 target (4x revenue, 3x EBITDA and PAT) was restated without the steel plant. Management said the steel plant is on hold and no timeline is set.
capex_capacity: CRM complex (0.7 mtpa, relocated to Maharashtra near Sambhajinagar): capex raised to INR1,100 crore from earlier INR900-950 crore, including working capital margin money; INR80 crore spent so far; land about INR50 crore for 35 acres; construction from October 2026; commissioning December 2027; funded by INR550 crore debt and internal accruals. Land allotment approval is expected by end-August 2026.
BESS (20 GW... as stated in transcript, battery storage project in Maharashtra): about INR500 crore spent; remaining INR700-800 crore to be spent over FY27 and FY28; commissioning targeted Q1 FY28.
Mining and other capex: about INR2,000 crore for the remaining FY27 and the whole of FY28. No FY29 projection has been given.
Ari Dongri beneficiation plant: INR218 crore spent till June 2026; ramp-up from Q3 FY27 and full-scale operation from FY28.

Captive solar: 25 MW commissioned in May 2026; 100 MW under construction, targeted September 2026; 150 MW project in abeyance. Solar storage of 45 MW targeted for Q3 FY27 (management corrected 'Q3 27' to 'Q3 26' and then said Q3 FY27 was intended). Captive solar would reach 290 MW.
Boria Tibbu mine (0.7 mtpa now) expansion to 4 mtpa targeted for FY31, with a 4 mtpa beneficiation plant yielding 1.5-2 mt concentrate (about 40% yield). TOFR filing pending.
demand_pricing: Iron ore prices (global) expected to hover around USD90-100/t; management said it does not expect prices to fall below USD90 soon. Domestic ex-mine iron ore about INR5,500/t.
Pellet prices: ex-Raipur about INR10,000/t now, versus a July low of about INR8,700-9,000/t. Management expects long-term range INR9,000-10,000/t.
Pellet exports: two vessels exported in June-July at about INR9,000/t ex-plant, roughly at par with domestic. Exports have now stopped due to the plant shutdown.
Industry pellet utilisation is about 65%, held back by lower exports, limited high-grade supply and margin pressure. Indian pellet production was about 120 mt in FY26, up from 109 mt in FY25.
Cost: iron ore accounts for about 75% of the raw material cost increase and imported coal for about 25%. Q2 FY27 costs are expected to stay high.
Sensitivity: each INR100/t fall in pellet price reduces annual EBITDA by about INR40 crore on 4 mt of pellets (per management).

544865|2026-06.headline: LEAP India Q1 FY27 total income rose 19% to INR2,134 million, EBITDA up 21% to INR1,141 million at a 53.5% margin.
544865|2026-06.overview: LEAP India, India's largest on-demand pallet pooling company, reported its maiden post-listing quarter with total income up 19% YoY to INR2,134 million and EBITDA up 21% to INR1,141 million. PAT rose 30% to INR247 million (12% margin) and cash PAT rose 23% to about INR812 million. Management reported 48 new customers in the quarter against a normal 15-20, asset count of 14.9 million, and utilisation up to 89.2%. Capex slowed to INR76 million-equivalent (stated as INR76 crores) from INR110 crores a year earlier as raw-material inflation made new crate and pallet purchases less attractive.

financial_highlights.change: up 1.26 million vs Q1 FY26 (13.65 million)
vs INR1.45 in same quarter last year

segments.name: Pallets (pooling)
segments.commentary: Pooled pallet count at around 9.2 million; management targets about 850,000 net additions in FY27 and says pooling growth of 17-18% YoY is achievable. Price increases of 5-6% were taken, linked to the German wood price index.

segments.name: Containers / crates
segments.commentary: Revenue growth of about 13% with asset additions of only 3-4%; management is deliberately slowing crate purchases because crate cost rose from about INR650 to INR1,000-1,200.

segments.name: MHE (TARON)
segments.commentary: 174 new machines added in Q1 and INR35.3 crores revenue (+33%); average monthly MHE pooling turnover rose from INR9.6 crores to INR11.6 crores. Management expects TARON to stay in a 14-17% growth bracket long-term.

segments.name: Middle East (GCC)
segments.commentary: Entities set up in Saudi Arabia (MISA licence), ADGM and Dubai; about five staff and about 20 customer discussions; Q1 capex in the region was held back due to the conflict. Management sees INR150-200 crores revenue in three years.

guidance_outlook: Management guides to about 20% YoY revenue growth (confirmed on the call as YoY, not QoQ), with GCC treated as additive to India growth.
EBITDA margin expected to stay within 47-56% for the next couple of quarters; management sees 100-200 bps potential margin expansion over time, but not a steady quarterly rise.
EBITDA growth expected to exceed revenue growth on a full-year basis, per management's answer to an analyst.
Target of about 3.7 million Movement Hire pallet moves in FY27, with 800,000-900,000 pallets added to the pooling model.
DSO expected to fall 10-15 days per quarter, with working capital normalising within two to three quarters.
Two more warehouses (about 250,000-300,000 sq ft) to be closed in Q2-Q3; a small 40,000-pallet pool may open in Silvassa.
Acquisition opportunities in India and abroad are at an early stage; management indicated updates in Q2-Q3.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 asset spend about INR76 crores vs INR110 crores in Q1 FY26; management is slowing purchases given input cost inflation and is repairing more (1.4 million pallets repaired in Q1 vs 1.2 million a year earlier).
Utilisation target: above 90-91% in the next quarter and 92%+ over the next couple of years; a buffer of about 900,000 pallets is available.
Movement Hire fleet of 400-plus lithium-ion battery forklifts and 140 machines ready for delivery; 1,440 forklifts in total.
Planned 3D printing for inserts and automated crate cleaning by next quarter.
Warehouse network reduced to 28 fulfilment centres after the CHEP integration; 10,500 touchpoints.
demand_pricing: 48 new customers in Q1 (normal run-rate 15-20), including Lear Automotive, Minda Instruments, Havells Logistics, Woodpecker, Green Agri and Sriram Foods; expected to add about 120,000 static-hire pallets.
Beverage and cola demand was extended by a late rainy season (Adhik Maas), shifting demand from March into April-May; this drove positive net pallet additions in Q1.
E-commerce and quick-commerce added about 25,000 pallets (Zomato, Blinkit) and 3PLs added about 30,000 (DP World, DHL, Yusen).
Textile was subdued due to raw-material shortages and cost increases; this reduced Movement Hire volumes.
Pricing: 5-6% annual price increases, linked to the German wood price index, are embedded in 3-5 year contracts; 24 contracts were renewed in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Asset growth was 9% but revenue rose 19%; how is the growth split between asset growth and throughput?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth comes from churn; FY26 moved about 2.8 million pallets and FY27 is targeted at about 3.7 million. Movement Hire rose 8% and textile/other sectors contributed the rest.

qa_highlights.question: Can you guide to EBITDA margins for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins have ranged 47-56% over six to seven years; FY26 was 50.7% and Q1 was 53.5%. Management expects 47-56% for the next couple of quarters and does not expect steady quarterly expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20%+ revenue growth on a YoY basis and is Middle East additive?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed YoY. Middle East is additive. Management expects INR150-200 crores of GCC revenue in three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is container revenue growth modest at 13%?
qa_highlights.answer: No slowdown in demand; management is limiting purchases because crate costs rose sharply, and is retrieving existing assets faster.

qa_highlights.question: Why does pallet 'sales' revenue look up about 3x?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sells pallets only selectively, to customers who will eventually return to pooling; it says this is not a core focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue uplift from static to Movement Hire?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-pallet yield is INR1.54 (about INR562 a year). Management says it could rise to INR600-712 as Movement Hire share increases from about 0.3x toward 0.5-0.6x, with no new assets needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Movement Hire only 0.3x in India and what would lift it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a fragmented truck market (about 1,000 body sizes) and recommended standardising to about 10. It said that when one large player adopts pooling, peers follow.

544831|2026-06.headline: Meenakshi India Q1 FY27 PAT rose to Rs 712 lakh (about 153% YoY), but about half of it came from other income; core garment EBITDA margin was about 3.4%.
544831|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs 3,224 lakh, down about 3.4% YoY and broadly stable. Reported PAT of Rs 712 lakh was driven mainly by other income of Rs 711 lakh, which management said is mark-to-market linked and may not recur. The garment (textile) segment operating profit improved to Rs 343 lakh from Rs 28.24 lakh a year earlier on a similar top line, with management citing better mix, pricing discipline and cost control. The company reports zero leverage, net worth of Rs 142.65 crore and about Rs 80 crore of cash and investments.

financial_highlights.change: -3.4% YoY vs Rs 3,339 lakh; +10.3% vs Q1 FY25 (Rs 2,921 lakh)
+153% YoY vs Rs 281 lakh; +58% QoQ vs Rs 451 lakh (as stated)
vs Rs 2.51 a year ago; Rs 4.02 in Q4 FY26
vs Rs 402.7 lakh a year ago; includes Rs 372.64 lakh unrealised fair value gain, Rs 225.78 lakh forward contract gain, Rs 32.91 lakh realised gains
vs Rs 28.24 lakh a year ago (about 12x)

financial_highlights.metric: Core EBITDA margin (garment, ex other income)
financial_highlights.change: vs marginally negative a year ago
vs Rs 150.65 crore at March 2026 (as stated); book value about Rs 127 per share
due to unrealised fair value gains attracting minimal current tax

segments.name: Garment / Textile (premium bottomwear and outerwear)
segments.commentary: Operating profit Rs 343 lakh on revenue of Rs 3,224 lakh (about 10.6% operating margin including other items in the segment definition as presented). Cost of materials net of inventory change was about 45.7% of revenue vs about 48% last year; employee cost Rs 894 lakh, flat YoY; other expenses Rs 747 lakh, down 7.3% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27: target capacity utilisation of about 70% (vs 65% currently cited on pieces basis); management said Q1 margins are on track to return to pre-tariff levels.
FY27 margin direction: move back towards FY25 EBITDA margins; management said pre-tariff EBITDA margin will not be fully reached but targeted about 17% by FY28.

FY30 illustrative projection in presentation: revenue about Rs 500 crore and PAT about Rs 65 crore; management called these conservative, pending FTA operationalisation (EU FTA hoped operational in Q1 CY27; US situation unclear).
Capacity: plan to go from 18 lakh pieces to 38 lakh pieces; 80% utilisation is the trigger to add capacity.

Capex: about Rs 40-50 crore to FY30 in two phases of about Rs 20 crore each; first factory targeted around FY28 (may slip by a couple of months), second around FY30. Management called these ballpark figures.
capex_capacity: Current capacity cited at 18 lakh pieces, planned expansion to 38 lakh pieces; utilisation of 65% is on absolute pieces produced and can vary with product mix.
About two lines of spare capacity exist in current facilities; two more manufacturing units planned gradually, depending on demand.
First new factory: about Rs 20 crore, targeted FY28 (possible slippage of a couple of months); second factory: about Rs 20 crore, around FY30.
Sri Lanka contract manufacturing MOU in place (not yet used); Nepal flagged as future plan; next factory being considered outside India in Nepal, Vietnam or Sri Lanka.
demand_pricing: Revenue mix by geography: about 50-50 Europe and US historically; management said Europe is now closer to 60%, as US volumes slowed on tariffs and customer overstocking.
US customers retained after tariffs, but volumes reduced; discounts and shipment holds were used to protect customers, which compressed margins.
Customer concentration: top 5 clients about 70% of revenue; 12-20 active customers at any time.
Management positions the company in premium segment vs Bangladesh, Vietnam, Pakistan (mass market); competitors cited for premium are Turkey, Tunisia, Eastern Europe, Guatemala.
Domestic India business is minimal; management said it is less profitable and not planned.
LDP (landed duty paid) model being introduced as a small service with better margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why stay in premium bottomwear, and why were margins hit by tariffs despite premium positioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said premium bottomwear was chosen for quota-era history and competition from Turkey/Tunisia/Eastern Europe rather than mass-market countries; it claimed tariff burden sharing was lower than mass-market peers.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and timing for the incremental 20 lakh pieces?
qa_highlights.answer: Two factories of about Rs 20 crore each: first around FY28 (may slip a couple of months), second around FY30; total about Rs 40-50 crore, described as ballpark.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 utilisation and margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Target about 70% utilisation in FY27 and move towards FY25 EBITDA margins; about 17% margin targeted by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why the Sri Lanka contract manufacturing and overseas plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Sri Lanka MOU is a contingency for US tariff changes (country-of-origin flexibility), not yet used; Nepal, Vietnam and Sri Lanka being evaluated for the next plant. Management said Europe/UK demand is not being moved out of India.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY30 projection of Rs 500 crore revenue and Rs 65 crore PAT conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, conservative given FTAs not yet operational; includes Sri Lanka contract volumes but no quantified share was given.

qa_highlights.question: D2C plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Test marketing started, put on hold due to a patent issue with the SHORTSTOP brand; not much invested in the brand.

qa_highlights.question: Athleisure and women's wear plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Women's wear is an easy extension of men's bottomwear; athleisure needs supplier base development (mainly cotton with some man-made fibre), using similar machines; no separate plant planned.

qa_highlights.question: FY25 base and exceptional income?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 revenue about Rs 155 crore (operational) and Rs 191 crore gross; EBITDA Rs 51 crore including Rs 12.5 crore exceptional gain from sale of agricultural land; PAT Rs 40 crore including exceptional item.

544485|2026-06.headline: Regaal Q1 FY27 operating income fell 18% YoY to Rs 202.15 cr as trading was cut, while value-added margin rose to 39.8% and PAT grew 47% to Rs 13.33 cr.
544485|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a transition quarter: the doubled crushing capacity (825 to 1,650 TPD) was commissioned on 26 May 2026, with operations ramping from early June. Operating income fell 18% YoY to Rs 202.15 cr because low-margin trading was deliberately reduced (3.3% of revenue vs 19.5% in Q1 FY26). Value-added revenue grew 30.3% to Rs 80.53 cr and EBITDA rose 26.6% to Rs 30.98 cr, with margin up 540 bps to 15.3%. Capacity utilisation was 71.4%, with management guiding to progressive improvement from Q2 FY27 and a shift to deleveraging after the capex cycle.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Contribution fell to 3.3% of revenue in Q1 FY27 from 19.5% in Q1 FY26 as low-margin trading was deliberately cut.

segments.name: Value-added products (liquid glucose, maltodextrin, starches)
segments.commentary: Value-added revenue Rs 80.53 cr (+30.3% YoY) at 39.8% margin. Liquid glucose at about 70% of its capacity; maltodextrin powder still ramping, with 2-3 more months needed to reach target.

segments.name: Maize starch / core crushing
segments.commentary: Crushing of 69,689 MT in Q1, with about 5,500 MT of incremental volume attributed by management to liquid glucose and a small part maltodextrin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 crushing expected at about 4 lakh tons (minimum), vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26.
Q2 FY27 crushing guided to 100,000-110,000 tons, contingent on smooth stabilisation and integration.
Value-added share of turnover expected at about 20-22% in FY27 (vs about 3% last year); later guided to about 30-35% of turnover on capacity mix.
Management declined to give EBITDA per ton or EBITDA margin guidance, citing maize and product price dependence; said operating leverage and value-add mix should improve margins at constant prices.
Net interest cost (net of subvention) for FY27 expected at about Rs 39-40 crore, broadly flat vs FY26.
Total project outlay about Rs 664 crore, of which about Rs 552 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026.
Working capital debt expected to decline in H2; management cited a prior pattern of about 40% reduction by Q4.
Dextrose Anhydrous, Dextrose Monohydrate and Hydrol expected by about Q4 FY27; modified starches (cationic, carboxymethyl, pre-gel, spray) trials to be fully online by September 2026.
No new capex decided; management said focus is on stabilising at 90-95% utilisation and deleveraging before considering next expansion.
capex_capacity: Crushing capacity doubled from 825 to 1,650 MT per day, commissioned 26 May 2026; operations started early June; described as largest maize wet milling facility in eastern India.
New liquid glucose facility 180 TPD, maltodextrin powder facility 50 TPD, captive cogeneration expanded from 7.1 MW to 15.8 MW.
Q1 utilisation 71.4%; about 9 shutdown days during April-May integration cost roughly 7,200 MT of output (management estimate).
Planned additions: 50,000 MT storage across two new silos, a 50,000 sq ft maize godown, and a 1.6 MW methane gas-based power plant.
Bihar interest subvention applies to new capex debt; management said the subvention cap was amended to Rs 40 crore but final policy notification was still awaited.
demand_pricing: Management said export share rose to 10.4% and that new markets in South and West India are being developed; no export target given.
Pricing: management said starch margin is a whole-number (per-ton) business rather than percentage-based; a rise in starch prices would not proportionally lift EBITDA per ton.
Maize procurement: about 80% of annual requirement bought in the Rabi season (Apr-Jul), 10-15% from other states; Bihar maize quoted at about Rs 22.5-23/kg delivered vs market talk of Rs 24.
Liquid glucose sold mainly September to March; big MNC customers now billed directly, and white-labelling customer base has grown.
About 70-80% of new modified starch volumes expected to go to existing paper-mill and food customers.

qa_highlights.question: What utilisation is the expanded plant running at and when will it reach a comfortable run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation is rising from the early-June start and expects maximum utilisation within the year; FY27 crushing expected above 4 lakh tons vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 47% PAT jump driven by raw material cost or operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to operating leverage and the drop in low-margin trading from about 19% to about 3% of turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What sustainable EBITDA per ton should be expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide, citing maize and product price dependence; it expects per-ton EBITDA to improve with scale and value-add at constant prices (Q1 EBITDA/ton cited as about Rs 4,450 vs Rs 4,742 FY26).

qa_highlights.question: What is the net interest cost for FY27 after Bihar subvention?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about Rs 39-40 crore, broadly flat vs FY26; subvention runs across multiple project loans, with the Rs 40 crore cap still pending final policy.

qa_highlights.question: When will peak debt occur and when will working capital come down?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said debt is peaking in H1 FY27 because working capital is highest then; debt expected to fall in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What production was lost in Q1 and is the value-added capacity stable?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9 shutdown days (approx. 7,200 MT lost). Liquid glucose at about 70% of capacity; maltodextrin needs 2-3 more months; modified starch trials to be online by September.

qa_highlights.question: Any new capex plans for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management wants to stabilise at 90-95% utilisation and reduce debt before considering the next expansion.

500780|2026-06.headline: Zuari Q1 FY27 standalone loss widened to INR9.5 crore PAT on sugar margin squeeze; Dubai St. Regis repatriation of INR142.58 crore received so far against INR900 crore FY27 target.
500780|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income rose 26% YoY to INR283.9 crore on higher sugar volumes and realisations, but EBITDA fell to INR31.3 crore from INR36.9 crore and PAT swung to a loss of INR9.5 crore from a loss of INR3.9 crore. Management attributed margin pressure to an 8% rise in UP cane SAP (INR370 to INR400 per quintal). Consolidated PAT was a marginal INR0.05 crore, supported by associate income, mainly Zuari Agro Chemicals. Management reiterated the INR900 crore Dubai repatriation target for FY27 and said that sugar prices are at record highs, which it expects to support the next quarters.

vs profit of INR0.9 crore in Q1 FY26
vs loss of INR3.9 crore in Q1 FY26
vs loss of INR0.48 crore in Q1 FY26
down INR1.46 crore from INR63 crore YoY

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: Sales of 4.7 lakh quintal vs 3.6 lakh quintal (+29% YoY) on higher domestic quota; realisation INR4,116/quintal vs INR4,036. Segment revenue INR236.8 crore (+34%) but segment profit fell to INR8.4 crore from INR12.3 crore. Recovery 11.7%; mill ran only six days in April 2026.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Production up 1% to 10,138 KL and sales up 5% to 10,248 KL; realisation INR60.70/litre, described as static. Molasses-route recovery was lower, and outsourced molasses was not economical, so no extra purchases were made.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Power sales of 62.8 lakh units vs 7.7 lakh units in Q1 FY26; R&M is in progress ahead of the crushing season.

segments.name: Real estate (Zuari Infraworld)
segments.commentary: Total income INR33.9 crore (+25% YoY), EBITDA INR24.6 crore (vs INR21.7 crore), PBT loss INR0.7 crore (vs loss INR1.5 crore). St. Regis Dubai reached 100% completion; handovers have started.

segments.name: Engineering (Simon India)
segments.commentary: Executed about INR30 crore of projects in the quarter; about INR70 crore of orders under execution. Management cited deferred capex in West Asia crisis.

segments.name: Financial services and broking
segments.commentary: Zuari Finserv total income INR4.1 crore vs INR5.9 crore. Zuari Insurance Broker brokerage income INR3 crore vs INR3.8 crore; EBITDA INR2.2 crore vs INR3.2 crore; gross return premium INR20.8 crore vs INR33.3 crore.

guidance_outlook: Dubai St. Regis profit repatriation: INR900 crore expected in FY27; INR142.58 crore (AED55 million) received in Q1 and July–August, with about INR750-758 crore balance expected in FY27.
Zuari Agro Chemicals loan of about INR258 crore expected to be repaid in the current quarter (Q2 FY27).
Management expects INR100-110 crore interest saving in FY28 from repaying about INR1,100 crore of debt at 9.73% average cost, per the analyst's calculation accepted on the call.
Sugar prices rose about 10% in the past month to record highs; UP prices INR4,860-4,920/quintal. Management expects festival demand to support realisations; exports are not currently allowed.
Management expects the next OMC ethanol tender in October 2026 and plans to participate; it expects the government may revise ethanol prices in the near term.
Furniture division decision expected by the end of FY27 (revival or other action).
capex_capacity: Sugar facility operating at 100% capacity utilisation; R&M under way for the 2026-27 crushing season.

Ethanol capex on hold because of overcapacity: last tender sought 1,050 crore litres against INR1,800 crore of offers. Management aims at 1,000 KLPD in the long term but will invest only once demand clarity emerges.
Zuari Envien Bioenergy (ethanol JV) stabilised plant operations this quarter and has orders until October 2026.

Gangothri Tribhuja (Hyderabad) saleable area 2.8 million sq ft; sales office complete, marketing under way. DM agreement for 14.8-acre plotted development in Bengaluru with RERA approval; cycle time about 15-18 months.

Zuari Infraworld DM order book about INR6,000 crore (per Alok Banerjee) vs GDV of about INR4,900 crore (per Athar Shahab); aspiration INR10,000 crore GDV. Launches in Hyderabad and Bengaluru expected next month.
demand_pricing: Indian sugar prices up 10% in the past month to record highs; global raw sugar about 16.6 cents/lb, near 1-year highs. Management attributes this to lower FY26 closing stocks (4.3 MMT vs 5.3 MMT).
Ethanol realisation static at INR60.70/litre; management says this weighs on margins.
Cane SAP in UP up 8% (INR370 to INR400/quintal), the main driver of margin compression.
Simon India orders slowed by West Asia-related capex deferrals across sectors.
Zuari Finserv and insurance broking volumes declined as the market weakened (gross return premium down about 38% YoY).

533155|2026-06.headline: Jubilant FoodWorks Q1 FY27: Domino's LFL 2.5% on high base; Popeyes LFL cited at ~45%, EBITDA margin target of 200 bps reiterated.
533155|2026-06.overview: Management described Popeyes as a second growth engine, with LFL growth of 40-45% attributed to product quality, flavour innovation and store execution. Domino's delivered 2.5% LFL in Q1 FY27 against 11.6% in the prior-year quarter, and management expects Q2 FY27 to be better than Q1. Cost pressure rose: LPG, cheese, oil, labour code and minimum wage hikes were partly offset by pricing and efficiencies, leaving the net margin headwind at about 20 bps QoQ. Management held FY27 capex guidance of INR 750-900 crore and the 200 bps EBITDA margin expansion target, with about 100 bps viewed as ahead of track.

financial_highlights.metric: Gross margin (consolidated, as cited by analyst)

financial_highlights.change: vs 11.6% in Q1 FY26; 0.5% in Q4 FY26
Vs ~70-80 bps remaining headwind flagged last quarter after ~110 bps of pricing already taken

segments.name: Domino's
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 LFL 2.5% on a high base; delivery order volumes not impacted by price increases per management. Minimum order value cut to INR 99 (from INR 149 free-delivery threshold) to match aggregators, lowering average order value.

segments.name: Popeyes
segments.commentary: LFL growth 40-45%; about 90 stores, with 7 cities above INR 100K ADS for the full quarter. Target ADS is above INR 100K; gross margin still scaling and marketing spend high (about INR 100 crore revenue base invested to reach INR 1,000 crore).

segments.name: Dine-in / takeaway channel
segments.commentary: Dedicated channel team and regional structure built; 2,500 neighbourhood stores; early reversal of trend seen on Wednesdays via Best Deals Ever Wednesday offer. Goal is to hold LFL flat in this channel.

guidance_outlook: Domino's LFL to reach 5-7% for rest of FY27 as bases correct; Q2 FY27 expected better than Q1 FY27 (2.5%).
EBITDA margin expansion target of 200 bps retained (roughly half from Domino's, half from emerging brands); ~100 bps from Popeyes viewed as ahead of track.
FY27 capex guidance of INR 750-900 crore maintained; capex increasingly tilted to new Domino's and Popeyes stores, dine-in store investment and technology; supply chain capex materially down.
Management will take calibrated price increases if input cost inflation (LPG, cheese, oil, chicken, labour) persists; commodities described as still in flux.
Expects positive free cash flow for the company over time; tracks ROCE and EPS as primary capital allocation metrics.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance INR 750-900 crore, in line with the previous two years; quarterly capex not disclosed.
Mumbai food factory commissioned in March; some commissioning still pending.
Supply chain investments described as past peak; new commissaries are lowering supply chain costs.
Capex mix: new store expansion (Domino's and Popeyes), existing store upgrades (dine-in), and technology.
demand_pricing: Price increase of about 140 bps overall in the quarter per analyst; management said price hikes were 1.5-2% and delivery order volumes were not impacted.
Minimum order value on delivery reduced to INR 99 (and INR 49 on some aggregator platforms) to match aggregators; lower AOV and higher cost per order.
Management said demand is not the constraint; growth is increasingly a question of profitable delivery.
Popeyes competes with fried chicken incumbents; ADS still behind the number one player in the market.
Management declined to disclose AOV; said chicken AOV is higher than pizza and Popeyes can become the highest AOV brand.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Popeyes LFL acceleration from 9.2% to 45%, and where does it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited superior product (marination, fresh chicken, intact pieces), six chicken wing flavours and bun focus, and better store execution with strong openings over the last 3-4 quarters. It declined to forecast normalisation, saying 45% is not a target to hold forever.

qa_highlights.question: Why has per-store employee cost not risen despite minimum wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged per-store headwinds from minimum wages and new stores; productivity gains (orders per labour hour) offset some of the cost, though labour rate per hour has risen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dine-in strategy and expected outcome?
qa_highlights.answer: A dedicated dine-in channel team, store segmentation into dine-in clusters, mall, campus and delivery-first stores, service audits, and offers (Wednesday deals, payment and aggregator partnerships). Early Wednesday results show reversal of trend; first goal is to hold dine-in and takeaway LFL flat.

qa_highlights.question: Can LFL reach 5-7% for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing a two-quarter average of 2.5% (Q1 FY27) and 11.6% (Q1 FY26), which gives over 7%. It said Q2 FY27 will be better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company maximise free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited exits from Hong's and Dunkin' and the supply chain build-out now past peak. Capex is shifting to revenue-generating store investment; the internal focus is ROCE and EPS rather than FCF alone. FCF was positive in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How is the EBITDA margin target progressing given cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 100 bps of the 200 bps is ahead of track from Popeyes. Domino's is on track, with price increases and supply chain efficiency offsetting LPG, cheese, oil and labour costs. Management said a quarter ago LPG alone cost about 120 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to Domino's margins QoQ after the MOV cut and cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost headwinds were about 200 bps against about 100-110 bps of pricing already taken, leaving 70-80 bps. Further pricing, waste reduction and efficiencies cut the net headwind to about 20 bps in the quarter.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (LPG, cheese, oil, chicken, labour code, minimum wages in about 14-15 states) could widen margin headwind; commodities described as still in flux.
Domino's LFL needs to hold 5-7% on a lower base in H2; Q3 and Q4 face tougher base comparisons.
Delivery volume and MAU-to-MTU conversion softness after price increases; lower AOV from the INR 99 minimum order value.
Popeyes EBITDA breakeven still pending; marketing costs high at current revenue scale; gross margin still scaling at about 90 stores.
Dine-in traffic recovery is early; results so far limited to Wednesdays.

544513|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 53.8 crore; standalone revenue up 7.8% YoY to INR 42 crore, Ind AS EBITDA margin 56.3% consolidated.
544513|2026-06.overview:
Standalone workspace revenue rose 7.8% YoY to INR 42 crore, with consolidated revenue at INR 53.8 crore and Ind AS consolidated EBITDA up 14.7% to INR 30.3 crore. Operational portfolio grew to 1.13 million sq ft (17,294 seats, 27 centers, 12 cities) with occupancy at 91.93%. Post-quarter, the company raised INR 100 crore of 11.75% secured NCDs (36 months) and encumbered about 19.65% of equity, with promoter holding stated at 36.81%. Management highlighted a pipeline of 2.31 million sq ft signed for future consumption, though analyst questions on Ahmedabad per-sq-ft economics, lease-inclusive leverage and Q4 margin drop were answered only partially.</overview>

500117|2026-06.headline: DCW Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell 28% YoY to INR41.4 crore as PVC losses (West Asia VCM shortage, duty suspension) hit Basic Chemicals to a negative INR14 crore EBITDA.
500117|2026-06.overview: Revenue rose 14% YoY to INR542 crore, led by Specialty Chemicals (INR177 crore, 33% of revenue, up 38% YoY), but fell 11% QoQ on a one-time Q4 Synthetic Rutile inventory liquidation base effect. Consolidated EBITDA including other income was INR41.4 crore, down 28% YoY and 41% QoQ, with management attributing the drop mainly to PVC disruption. Basic Chemicals EBITDA was negative INR14 crore, while Specialty EBITDA grew about 20% YoY. Management guided that PVC conditions have improved since Q1 and that FY27 should close better than FY26, while also announcing a INR250 crore capex programme and an intent to be effectively net debt free by end-FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +38% YoY (as stated in opening remarks); +6% QoQ

financial_highlights.value: Not stated in INR; margin 29.1% (analyst-computed from Q1 FY26 33.6%)
Negative INR14 crore (-5.2% margin per analyst)

financial_highlights.change: from migration to new tax regime (25.17% vs 34.9%)

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals (CPVC, SIOP)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR177 crore, up 38% YoY with CPVC volumes up 59% and SIOP volumes up about 3%. EBITDA grew about 20% YoY and 35% QoQ; margin about 29% vs 33.6% a year ago, which management linked to PVC-CPVC spread volatility.

segments.name: Basic Chemicals (PVC, caustic soda, soda ash, Synthetic Rutile)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR361 crore, down 18% QoQ on Q4 Synthetic Rutile inventory liquidation. EBITDA negative INR14 crore; management estimated a sequential PVC contribution swing of INR50-55 crore, with caustic soda and Synthetic Rutile margins improving.

guidance_outlook: FY27 expected to close at a better level than FY26, based on current visibility (management).
Basic Chemicals expected to do better than Q1; management says breakeven in Q2 is more than believed if normalcy holds.
Steady-state EBITDA assessed at about INR300 crore, replacing the earlier INR400 crore target.
Legacy long-term debt expected to be fully repaid in FY27 (repayments about INR135 crore); effectively net debt free by end-FY27 before new borrowings.
Targeting minimum incremental ROCE of 20% on new investments.
Expects to borrow slightly more than repayments for the capex, with a 1-1.5% negative carry on cash-to-borrowing.
capex_capacity: INR250 crore programme over 2-3 years; first part is SIOP capacity expansion from about 30,000 tpa to 45,000 tpa, with Phase 1 adding 7,000 tpa by Q4 FY28 and infrastructure sized for a further 8,000 tpa.
Captive power infrastructure at Sahupuram facility, targeted for Q4 FY28, to lower power costs across Specialty and Basic Chemicals.
SIOP expansion is brownfield; expected margin around 35-36% and product price north of INR80,000/ton (management).
Current PVC capacity about 1 lakh tpa; CPVC about 50,000 tpa; SIOP capacity 28 kt fully tied up this year after debottlenecking.
Synthetic Rutile capacity about 48,000-50,000 tpa; caustic soda realistic capacity about 90,000 tpa.
demand_pricing: PVC: West Asia conflict cut VCM availability from traditional Asian suppliers, forcing spot purchases from China at higher prices; import duty suspension let in lower-priced imports. Duties now reinstated and a minimum import price (MIP, about USD/INR80 per ton equivalent) introduced for suspension-grade PVC.
Management said current import parity is about USD820-860/ton, well above MIP, and expects prices to stay at these levels at least this quarter.
PVC/VCM spread was estimated at north of INR25,000/ton; PVC-to-CPVC spread lags because of existing customer orders.
Synthetic Rutile: prices recovered vs last year's inventory-correction slump; customer mix improved and high-priced deliveries are back-ended.

SIOP: around 60% of output exported, mainly to the US; management says no tariff impact on exports. Volumes are seasonally higher in Q3 and Q4. Ammonia cost increases were passed through to customers.
Caustic soda margins expanded QoQ and YoY; chlorine is now fully consumed captively for CPVC, improving caustic ECU realisation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the QoQ revenue decline came from captive PVC use, lower PVC output and the Synthetic Rutile base effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q4 Synthetic Rutile liquidation base effect was the main driver, plus a few days of PVC plant shutdown; it did not quantify the split, but said the Synthetic Rutile effect alone would have exceeded the top-line decline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Specialty margins compress and is about 29% the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins depend on the dynamic PVC-CPVC spread, which is volatile. SIOP margins are robust, and a steady-state margin is hard to pin down because roughly 40-50% of PVC goes into CPVC.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Basic Chemicals' loss came from PVC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave only a directional estimate: a sequential contribution swing of INR50-55 crore in PVC. It confirmed PVC was the only loss-making Basic Chemicals product, with caustic soda, soda ash and Synthetic Rutile profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR400 crore EBITDA target still stand?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It was set when CPVC margins were about 40%. Management now sees steady-state EBITDA of about INR300 crore, subject to the spread holding.

qa_highlights.question: Would a share buyback be considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still considering a buyback and will announce it at an opportune time if it decides to proceed.

qa_highlights.question: How is VCM sourced, and can it be derisked or backward integrated?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply moved from a single Qatar producer to a global distributor sourcing across Asia. Management ruled out backward integration at current scale; storage expansion would add only about 10-15 days of inventory.

543258|2026-06.headline: Indigo Paints Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18.7% to INR350 crore with EBITDA margin up to 17.7%, its best Q1 margin in four years.
543258|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 18.7% YoY to INR350 crore, with double-digit volume and value growth across all four product categories. EBITDA rose 42% to INR61.9 crore (margin 17.7% vs 14.8%), and PAT rose 60.7% to INR42.4 crore, helped partly by a mark-to-market treasury gain. Consolidated revenue was INR369.7 crore (+19.7%), but subsidiary Apple Chemie's margins were compressed by high-cost inventory and limited B2B pass-through. Management said it will spend more aggressively on trade and influencers in Q2 to widen the growth gap versus the industry, and that the Jodhpur capex cycle is complete.

segments.commentary: Value growth 17.5% and volume growth close to 10%.

segments.commentary: Value growth above 17% and volume growth around 12.5%.

No concrete Q2 margin guidance; management called the raw material situation a 'fuzzy' roller coaster and said Q2 is seasonally the weakest margin quarter, suggesting a six-month comparison.
July was a very good month with top-line momentum maintained or slightly better than Q1; August not yet assessed.

A/P spends are to be assessed on an annual basis; brand investment for the full year is 'undiminished'.

Solvent-based Jodhpur plant already in production for several months and ramping up.
Legacy water-based plant to be scrapped and output shifted to the new automated plant; opex expected to be broadly unchanged.
Solar capacity installed 350 kW across Pune and Cochin; a further 1,200 kW planned at Jodhpur.
No significant capex planned for the next three years; free cash flow expected to improve versus the last five years.
demand_pricing: Industry demand has improved progressively from Q3 FY26; management said demand is back near normal growth conditions.
Price increases in March and April were steep and frequent, protecting margins; raw material costs have eased from peaks but remain elevated and volatile.
Channel overstocking not seen at Indigo; management said the market leader may have seen some overstocking.
Distribution: about 19,400 active dealers (up about 800 YoY) and about 12,400 active tinting machines (up about 1,100 YoY).
Wood coatings: two-pack polyurethane launch planned for September and October in phases, in a segment management estimates at upwards of INR9,000 crore; it had no presence there earlier.
Differentiated products are about 29% to 30% of revenue; management said the company is not planning new differentiated launches.
Competition: management said no meaningful change from JSW's acquisition of AkzoNobel or the Birla Opus entry.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Indigo not grown faster versus the market leader, and was the IPL advertising pause a missed opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said steep, frequent price hikes benefit the market leader most. The IPL pause was due to raw material uncertainty after the Iran war, not competitor ad intensity or Dhoni's playing status; it intends to put the money back in the coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is July and August demand holding after Q1 upstocking, and is there a destocking risk for Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel overstocking was not seen at Indigo. July was a very good month with momentum maintained or slightly better than Q1; August was too early to call.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a price cut in H2, and what are the Q2 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No further price hikes are planned for now. A price cut is possible, most likely after Diwali. No Q2 margin guidance was given; management suggested looking at the six-month period.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jodhpur plant opex impact, and what is the competitive intensity after JSW-AkzoNobel?
qa_highlights.answer: The new plant replaces the legacy water-based plant with little opex change. Competitive intensity is unchanged, as JSW and AkzoNobel still operate separately.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new plant be ready for the festive season, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production is about 10 days away and should stabilise in about a month. The legacy plant is a backup. Management said gross margin may drop a couple of points, and EBITDA margin may move about 1 point either way.

risks_watch: Raw material prices remain elevated and volatile after the Iran war disruption; Q2 margin path is uncertain given mixed inventory costs.
Festive-season execution depends on the Jodhpur water-based plant stabilising in about one month after trial production.
Apple Chemie margin recovery depends on consuming high-cost inventory by Q2 and normal margins by Q3.
Management plans to spend more on trade and influencers in Q2, which may pressure gross margin by a couple of percentage points.
Possible H2 price cuts post-Diwali if input costs stay at current levels.
Wood coatings two-pack PU launch in September and October is a new category push that needs a specialised sales team.
Quarter's PAT margin includes a mark-to-market treasury gain, so underlying profit growth may be lower than reported.

544851|2026-06.headline: MV Electrosystems expects propulsion output to ramp from 10 units in September to about 40 per month by January, against an order book of 564 propulsion systems worth about INR989 crores.
544851|2026-06.overview: This was the first investor call after the company's listing, with no reported financials in the transcript. Management said deliveries have been limited to 2 or 3 small batches so far, with none in the prior two months, and that IPO proceeds (working capital) now fund a scale-up. Management targets about INR400 crore of revenue this year and roughly 10% PAT once run-rate is reached, though it conceded margins are negative or constrained during the initial ramp. Growth optionality was discussed across EMU/MEMU/Vande Bharat distributed propulsion, OHE auto fault locators (with PNC Technologies), and marine/electrical adjacencies.

financial_highlights.metric: Supply price per locomotive propulsion system
financial_highlights.value: INR1.67 crore (AMC roughly matches this figure over 3 years)

financial_highlights.metric: Working capital requirement at ~INR1,000 crore turnover

financial_highlights.value: 105 days stated in prospectus; last three cycles completed in 85 days

segments.name: Locomotive propulsion systems
segments.commentary: Order book of 564 units valued at about INR989 crore; ramp planned at 10 units in September, 25 in November, 40 per month by January. Capacity built for 55 per month, with 40 chosen as the stable target.

segments.name: EMU/MEMU/Vande Bharat distributed propulsion
segments.commentary: INR86 crore MCF EMU development order with 24-month supply window; design and development targeted in 8-10 months, then approval taking about 15-16 months in total. A 12-coach EMU is about INR16 crore and a 16-coach Vande Bharat about INR40 crore including electrics.

segments.name: Overhead electrification (OHE) / AFL
segments.commentary: Auto fault locator tied up with PNC Technologies (South Korea). Management pegged unit prices at INR12 lakh (sectioning/sub-sectioning) to INR36 lakh (substation transformer), roughly INR1 crore of revenue per transformer section, with installations expected over 5-7 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR400 crore, described as achievable definitively.
Monthly run-rate of about 40 propulsion systems from January, implying roughly INR70 crore a month and about 480 units a year.
PAT of 10%-plus expected once run-rate is reached; management expects profitability within 2-3 months and margins to improve month over month after stabilisation.
R&D spend to be 3%-4% of revenue over time; R&D team to be expanded with a new centre ready by Q3.
Approximately 15-16 months to EMU propulsion approval including development.
capex_capacity: Capacity built for 55 locomotive propulsion systems per month; company plans to run at 40 for consistency, with spare capacity earmarked for EMU propulsion.
Unit 2 already set up; box fabrication and assembly to start the following Monday after the call.
No further machinery capex planned; only test setups are required, with three more ordered and installations expected in 45-60 days.
Two additional shifts planned in the existing factory, cited as enabling about 4,500 systems.
demand_pricing: Management cited Indian Railways building about 1,600-1,700 locomotives a year, about 15,000 locomotives in service needing rehabilitation, and 300-500 EMUs tendered or to be tendered this year.

Locomotive tenders in pipeline: CLW tender for about 748 locomotives (expected around 31 August), followed by BLW and PLW tenders, expected over the next few weeks; more than 100 EMU propulsion tenders and 200 train-set electrical tenders published by ICF Chennai, not yet bid.

Company said it won about 25-26% of tendered locomotive propulsion quantity, with competitors including Siemens, Alstom, ABB, Medha and BHEL. In the last tender, 7 suppliers were awarded small quantities.
Management said margins were very thin across bidders; company was L2 in two tenders and L1 in one. Bulk purchasing (200-300 sets) was cited as offsetting electronics price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the PLW/CLW propulsion tender cancellation affect the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was unaware of any cancellation and noted an active CLW tender for 748 locomotives. Tender-to-order conversion typically takes 45 days, sometimes up to 90.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company meet the December 26 order deadline, and what is the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply obligations extend to March and into next financial year. Output is planned at 10 units in September, 25 in November, and 40 in January; extensions are typically granted for capacity-constrained suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: What margins apply given rising electronics costs and no price-escalation clause?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 10%-plus PAT at full run-rate; early months will have constrained or negative margins. Bulk procurement of 200-300 sets is offsetting global price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle and requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement lead times range from 7 days to 6 months, averaging about 45 days. Payments were received within 15 days on all three dispatches. Working capital of about INR200 crore needed for roughly INR1,000 crore turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realisation per propulsion system?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply price is INR1.67 crore per locomotive propulsion system; AMC over three years roughly matches that figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EMU/MCF approval process and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Three-month validation at the MCF commissioning depot, performance trials on Delhi-Ambala Road, then a four-month trial covering about 30,000 km before approval.

risks_watch: Execution risk on the ramp from 10 units in September to 40 per month by January, with management admitting near-term margins are negative or constrained.
Gross margin pressure from electronics price inflation with no price-escalation clause, and bids were won at thin margins (L1/L2).
Working capital intensity: about INR200 crore required; management quoted a 105-day cycle in the prospectus and 85 days on the last three cycles, with inconsistent figures raised by analysts.
Competitive intensity from Siemens, Alstom, ABB, Medha, BHEL and new entrants; the company holds about 25-26% share of tendered quantity.
EMU/Vande Bharat revenue depends on approval about 15-16 months out and an MCF delivery window of 24 months.
Unverified tender cancellation reported by an analyst on GeM (CLW, 127 sets); management disputed knowledge of it.

Evasive or vague on several points, including tender cancellation, the 238-day working capital figure, and the timing of the first-year PAT. Several answers were long and repetitive.
key_quotes: We see about 10% plus PAT margin comfortably coming in from this order.
Completely in-house. It'll be designed and developed completely with our own IPR, with our own technology in-house.

517498|2026-06.headline: Websol Q1 FY27 revenue rose 70% YoY to INR373 crore and PAT grew 16% to INR78 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 34% from 47% on module mix.
517498|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations was INR373 crore, up 70% YoY and down about 7% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR126 crore (+21% YoY, margin 34% vs 47%) and PAT of INR78 crore (+16%). Cell output rose to 259 MW (92% utilisation) and module output to 103 MW (81% utilisation), with module volume doubling and driving the margin dilution. The company repaid the INR110 crore IREDA term loan on 4 August from internal accruals, with promoter pledge set to fall from 80% to 16% of promoter holding once released. Phase 3 expansion is being relocated from Andhra Pradesh to West Bengal, with land approval awaited; management says capex, cost and timelines are unchanged.</overview>

segments.name: Solar cells
segments.commentary: Production 259 MW vs 126 MW in Q1 FY26, utilisation 92%; average cell efficiency 23.3%. About 153 MW sold externally in Q1, with the rest consumed captively for modules.

segments.name: Solar modules
segments.commentary: Production 103 MW vs 50 MW, utilisation 81% vs 39%. Module margins are lower than cell margins, and module-led mix is the main driver of the margin decline.

guidance_outlook: Cell utilisation of about 92% to be held; management expects close to full run-rate utilisation across lines except TOPCon upgrade downtime.

TOPCon upgrade of 600 MW mono PERC line to 750 MW TOPCon, lifting total cell capacity to 1.3 GW (about 55% TOPCon), expected by March 2027 at about INR270 crore, funded from internal accruals with possible debt.
Management expects payback of 2 to 3 years on the TOPCon capex; cell efficiency expected around 25% post-upgrade.

Phase 3 (4 GW total, cell and module, two phases of 2 GW each): land approval expected in August; construction targeted mid-September; equipment lead time 4 to 6 months; trial run after about 2 months post installation; management says no change in timelines or capex.
Margins: management expects cell margins to fall somewhat but not aggressively, and believes current margin levels can hold for a year or two.
Silver consumption cut 20% in FY26, with a further 10% reduction target for cells.
capex_capacity: Current capacity: cells about 1.2 GW pre-upgrade, rising to 1.35 GW (per management, with 750 MW TOPCon) after the TOPCon upgrade; the upgrade adds about 150 MW of cell capacity.

Phase 3: 4 GW of additional cell and 4 GW of module capacity in two 2 GW phases; location moved from Andhra Pradesh (Naidupeta) to West Bengal (land shortlisted near Falta facility, approval pending).
Expected timeline: land approval in August 2026, construction from mid-September, equipment ordered around December, arrival April to May 2027, about 9 months to complete, then 2 months of trials.
Module utilisation of 81% described as close to full effective utilisation; industry comfort range cited at 70-75%.
demand_pricing: Prices softened in the previous quarter; management says prices rose in the current quarter on ALMM-related expectations, but the ALMM cell mandate was deferred from June to December 2026.
Current cell price quoted at about USD0.13 per Wp and module at about INR21 per watt, against Q1 levels of about USD0.125 and INR20.50.

Demand is mainly DCR (PM-Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM); management sees no decline. Inventory rose about 7% QoQ and management attributes it to monsoon-season offtake slowdown and captive cell blocking in modules.
Input costs: silver prices have eased but imported paste carries a lag; wafer prices are flat. The West Asia conflict has raised BOM costs for modules, not cells.
Management said Q1 margin decline reflects lower cell prices and higher silver and BOM cost, alongside mix shift.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company moving Phase 3 from Andhra Pradesh to West Bengal, and does it change timelines and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited synergies in skilled manpower, supply chain and infrastructure, with no change to capex, project cost, funding or timelines; no financial outflow had occurred on the AP land.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trend and is margin pressure expected to persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to module-heavy mix plus lower cell prices and higher silver/BOM costs; it expects cell margins to fall but not aggressively and to hold current levels for a year or two.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory rising, and what were Q1 realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose about 7% QoQ, which management attributed to monsoon-led offtake slowdown and cell cost blocked in modules; Q1 realisations were about USD0.125/Wp for cells and INR20.50/W for modules.

qa_highlights.question: What returns does the TOPCon upgrade generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects incremental revenue from higher Wp per cell (7.6-7.7 Wp for PERC to about 9.5 Wp for TOPCon), higher capacity (600 MW to 750 MW) and a price premium; it expects a 2-3 year payback on the INR270 crore capex.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company targeting a larger order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book reports only firm purchase orders and repeat business, and the company is not targeting a higher order book; it sees regular DCR-market inquiries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ability to execute and ramp Phase 3 at the same pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the TOPCon conversion will serve as practical training before the greenfield expansion; it cited the mono PERC installation timeline as precedent.

risks_watch: Margin compression as module mix rises: EBITDA margin fell 13 percentage points YoY to 34%, and management expects further cell margin softening.
Phase 3 execution: relocation to West Bengal depends on pending land approval (targeted August 2026); no incentive terms disclosed yet.
Inventory build (about 7% QoQ) and monsoon-season offtake; watch whether it clears in Q2.
ALMM cell mandate deferred to December 2026 and dependence on domestic cell capacity; price direction after that date.
Investor-communication concerns raised by several participants (valuation, share-price moves, lack of disclosure). The company said it is increasing investor interactions.
Pledge release: promoter pledge reduction from 80% to 16% depends on lender formalities; timing unconfirmed.
517498|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on operations and utilisation and on the debt repayment, but defensive and vague on valuation, share price, Phase 3 incentives and cost savings, where it declined to give figures and said it would disclose later.

543829|2026-06.headline: Global Surfaces Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% to Rs 65 crore and EBITDA turned to Rs 8 crore, with PAT at break-even, despite 27% utilisation.
543829|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 65 crore (up 44%), EBITDA of Rs 8 crore versus a Rs 19 crore loss in the prior quarter (margin 12.69%), and PAT break-even versus a Rs 2 crore loss. Overall capacity utilisation was about 27% (Dubai 20%, India 36%), held back by shipping disruption via Hormuz in March–April. The Bagru natural stone unit was discontinued from March 31, 2026 and is being wound down, with asset disposal targeted within FY27. Management declined to give FY27 revenue or utilisation guidance, citing US tariff and geopolitical uncertainty, including a US ITC safeguard recommendation on quartz surfaces.

Freight costs in UAE have not normalised from Q1 levels; about 30–40% of the cost increase has been passed on to customers.
India domestic launch in Q2 FY27 via a dealer/distributor model; sales team to grow from about 9–10 to 25–30 people over the next quarter, with about 15 added in India.

Marquartz Technology (patented, one of only two global manufacturers) launched; it is cited as driving Dubai product mix.
demand_pricing: US tariffs: 50% effective in Aug 2025 (25% reciprocal plus 25% Russia-linked); interim framework in Feb 2026 cut reciprocal tariff to 18% and removed the Russia-linked tariff.

US ITC found quartz surface imports a substantial cause of serious injury under Section 201 (petition April 2026); recommended a four-year TRQ with 25% in-quota and 50% above-quota tariff in year one. Final measures pending.
Management said there has been no major change in product demand, and the order book is strong.
Freight/trade costs rose to nearly twice normal levels; resin-linked raw material costs rose in India and the Middle East.
Diversification: GCC (UAE focus), European markets (sales team deployed, results awaited), and India. Named domestic peers: Asian, Classic Marble and Spectrum.
Most US clients are distributors (including big-box retailers and fabricators); no residential/commercial split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Dubai utilisation, US shipping and tariff hurdles, and the raw material cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Dubai utilisation was 20% and India 36% in Q1, because of shipping disruption in March–April. Raw material costs rose globally with freight and resin; some costs were passed on, and management expects stability once geopolitics settles.

qa_highlights.question: Planned India domestic model and marketing spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Distributors will be appointed in major cities, selling to B2C end customers under the Global Surfaces brand. A marketing budget is set for the next two quarters but the amount was not disclosed; some international fairs were dropped to offset cost.

qa_highlights.question: Margin aspiration once utilisation improves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said break-even was reached at about 28–30% utilisation and profitability should scale significantly once utilisation rises, subject to geopolitics.

qa_highlights.question: Dubai revenue and peak revenue split between facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Dubai revenue was about Rs 160 crore in FY26 at 44% utilisation. Peak split across Dubai and India is roughly 65:35, described as a ballpark figure.

qa_highlights.question: Freight normalisation and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: UAE freight has not normalised from Q1 levels. About 30–40% of the cost increase has been passed on to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Bagru asset disposal timing and cash proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: A valuer has been appointed and buyers are being approached; no number has been set. Management expects disposal within FY27.

Persistent Hormuz/Middle East shipping disruption and elevated UAE freight; only 30–40% of cost increases passed on so far.
Low utilisation (20% Dubai, 36% India) and dependence on the recovery in volumes for margin sustainability.
Execution risk and marketing burn in the India launch scheduled for Q2 FY27 (sales team scaling from 9–10 to 25–30 people).
Bagru disposal value and timing; no sale price has been identified.
Clarity on the Q1 revenue growth basis: the company said +44%, but an analyst's question cited a 12% YoY decline. Verify against the filed results.

544914|2026-06.headline: Steamhouse Q1 FY27 PAT rose 80.25% YoY to INR18.34 crore on 16.7% steam volume growth; EBITDA margin 24.05%.
544914|2026-06.overview:
Steamhouse reported record quarterly steam volumes of about 3,05,816 tons, up 16.7% YoY and 11.52% QoQ, with revenue from operations up 13.35% to INR128.62 crore. EBITDA rose 60.08% to INR30.93 crore, lifting margin to 24.05% (up 702 bps), while PAT rose 80.25% to INR18.34 crore. 533217|2026-06.headline: HMVL Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 15% to INR 497 crore and EBITDA nearly 3x to INR 90 crore, while a preferential equity issue at ~INR 24.7 drew shareholder pushback.
533217|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 15% YoY to INR 497 crore, with EBITDA up nearly 3x to INR 90 crore (margin up 12 points) and PAT of INR 47 crore (9% margin). Print drove growth, with advertising up 15% to INR 295 crore and operating revenue up 16% to INR 376 crore, while Digital revenue fell about 28% and Radio stayed flat with negative EBITDA. Management also announced a preferential issue at the SEBI-formula price (~INR 24.7 per share) in HT Media and Digicontent Ltd, not HMVL, to retire 30-50% of debt; this drew sharp objections from minority shareholders on dilution and pricing. Treasury gains and asset-sale profit lifted other income in HMVL.

segments.name: Print
segments.commentary: Advertising up 15% to INR 295 crore and operating revenue up 16% to INR 376 crore, with EBITDA margin of 13% despite high newsprint costs. Growth attributed mainly to yield (pricing) improvement in commercial, plus government rate hike from November 2025.

segments.name: Radio
segments.commentary: Topline flat YoY with negative operating EBITDA of INR 3 crore. Company surrendered licences for certain non-viable stations to run a leaner footprint.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Operating revenue down about 28% and operating EBITDA negative INR 3 crore (margin -12%), reflecting a deliberate portfolio reset toward leaner offerings.

segments.name: OTTplay / incubating businesses
segments.commentary: Management said a decision on OTTplay was taken around 31 March 2026, and incubating businesses that do not turn profitable will be reviewed; no figures were disclosed for the discontinued operations.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or earnings guidance given; management said it does forward planning but is 'very hopeful' of sustaining current numbers.

Newsprint (25-40% of print bill of material) at about USD 650-700 per metric ton, seen as a peak that should plateau; management said 13% Print EBITDA margin can be used as a modelling baseline if prices and USD do not worsen.
Q2 FY27 newsprint price slightly higher than Q1; margin outcome depends on ad category mix and pricing.
Government revenue rate increase (November 2025) will continue to support the next two quarters as prior-year pricing is lapped.
Preferential issue proceeds expected to retire at least 30-50% of HT Media/DCL debt, described as EPS-accretive and supportive of interest coverage and credit rating.
capex_capacity: Radio surrendered licences for certain non-viable stations, moving to a leaner footprint.
No capex or capacity figures were disclosed in the call.
demand_pricing: Commercial ad revenue: volumes held and yield improved; yield improvement programme cited as a key driver.
Government ad revenue grew on a combination of volume and pricing after the November 2025 rate hike (first in seven years).
English circulation revenue (INR 13 crore, +14%) driven mainly by pricing and mix; copy levels described as steady state.
Cover price hikes seen as difficult: Hindi papers already well priced, and most peers have taken increases.
Newsprint has no forward market, and a stronger USD (at a lifetime high) adds to cost pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Ranga Prasad: why raise equity via a preferential issue at ~INR 24 when net cash is INR 922 crore, diluting public shareholders by 15%, and why not a rights issue? Asked for withdrawal.
qa_highlights.answer: Piyush Gupta said net cash sits in HMVL, while HT Media and Digicontent are net debt companies; the issue is priced on the SEBI formula (higher of 10-day or 90-day VWAP) with no premium, and P/B is below 0.5. Anna Abraham said a preferential issue is faster (2-3 months) and gives more certainty than a rights issue, which carries underwriting and under-subscription risk.

qa_highlights.question: Mehul Pathak: the issue price is unjustifiably low versus book value and intrinsic value; ROE is under 10% even at current profits, and other options should be considered.
qa_highlights.answer: Gupta said the market values HMVL at about one-third of book, the promoter is subscribing on the same terms, and all options (including OTTplay decision) are being discussed at Board level. Pathak said he voted against the resolution.

qa_highlights.question: Mehul Pathak: management previously said the company was debt free and used debt only for treasury, but now debt is being retired.
qa_highlights.answer: Gupta said HT Media has carried debt for three to four years, built up post-COVID from English Print and Radio operations, and that the combined net cash figure hides this.

qa_highlights.question: Rohan Agarwal: what is the nature of the other income jump at HMVL?
qa_highlights.answer: Anna Abraham said it comprised treasury gains (mutual fund NAV-based, driven by yield curve movement at quarter end) and realised profit on sale of assets; no MTM on equity investments. Future levels cannot be predicted.

qa_highlights.question: Rohan Agarwal: outlook for newsprint costs, hedging, and whether the 13% Print margin is a baseline; would cover price hikes help?
qa_highlights.answer: Gupta said newsprint is 25-40% of costs, peaked near USD 650-700/MT, and there is no forward market; 13% margin can be used as a model baseline. Anna Abraham said Q2 newsprint is slightly higher and cover price hikes are difficult given existing hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Yash R.: what drove 15% Print ad growth, and what was the government share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Anna Abraham said commercial volumes held with yield gains and government revenue grew on volume and pricing. Gupta said growth was largely pricing-driven; government share is 'substantial' but not disclosed, with commercial the bigger block.

qa_highlights.question: Yash R.: why did consolidated employee cost fall and other operating income rise at HMVL?
qa_highlights.answer: Gupta attributed lower employee cost (about INR 99 crore vs INR 111 crore) to right-sizing across HT Media and HMVL. Anna Abraham said other operating income (job work, scrap sales) roughly doubled to about INR 20 crore.

543732|2026-06.headline: Radiant Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA margin fell to 13.5% from 15.9% on manpower costs, with standalone revenue up 7% on the IDBI mandate.
543732|2026-06.overview:
Standalone revenue rose about 7% YoY, driven mainly by the newly commenced IDBI Bank mandate, while the retail cash management business grew 5.5%. Standalone EBITDA margin fell to 13.5% from 15.9% a year ago because of gunmen costs, minimum wage hikes and southern-state licensed gunmen shortages. Management is pinning margin recovery on price revisions it expects to complete in Q2, plus revenue growth and cost control.</overview>

segments.name: Standalone cash management

guidance_outlook: Price revision: company has sought substantial cumulative price increases from banks; IBA committee formed and negotiations expected to complete in Q2 FY27; management expects it to reflect in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the core business growing below inflation excluding IDBI and RVL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged that non-IDBI, non-RVL growth is low, citing bank pullbacks and points moving to payments banks, and said the RVL impact is too small to matter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the big picture for Acemoney and its breakeven?

qa_highlights.question: Payment aggregator licence status?

Manpower cost inflation (own employee costs rising about 8%-9% a year) and gunmen shortages.
Acemoney breakeven slipping beyond September/Q3, and RBI payment aggregator licence timing (queries outstanding).
Management's own guidance has slipped repeatedly; an analyst noted six quarters without a settlement on the growth and cost levers.
