544304|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 12% YoY to ₹5.97 cr, with occupancy up 2 pts to 45% and RevPAR up 9% to ₹4,763. EBITDA declined to ₹1.69 cr from ₹1.81 cr and margin compressed to 27% from 32%, partly from new-property ramp-up costs and a ₹0.52 cr exceptional charge tied to the discontinued Parsili project. PAT fell to ₹0.47 cr from ₹1.13 cr. Management outlined Devprayag and Palash Kothi (42 rooms combined) as FY27 additions, Mathura (105 rooms, IHG Holiday Inn Express) and Sheopur Fort (35–40 rooms in phase 1) for FY28, and a debt build-up to about ₹50 cr by FY28.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹1.43 cr in Q1 FY26; includes ₹0.52 cr exceptional expense

financial_highlights.value: Total income ₹23.28 cr, EBITDA ₹7.48 cr (30% margin), PAT ₹4.22 cr, occupancy 40%, ADR ₹10,418, RevPAR ₹4,210

segments.name: Pench
segments.commentary: 39% of Q1 FY27 room revenue (36% in Q1 FY26); FY26 ADR ₹9,248 per management.

segments.name: Kanha
segments.commentary: 17% of Q1 FY27 room revenue (30% in Q1 FY26); FY26 ADR ₹9,500 per management.

segments.name: Tadoba
segments.commentary: 38% of Q1 FY27 room revenue (38% in Q1 FY26); highest portfolio occupancy at 57%; FY26 ADR ₹12,300.

segments.name: Rukhad (leased, 10-yr from MP Ecotourism Board)
segments.commentary: 4% of room revenue in both periods; highest ADR at ₹12,573 in Q1 FY27; FY26 ADR ₹11,800.

segments.name: Bison Highway Retreat (leased)
segments.commentary: 2% of room revenue in both periods; 8 rooms, FY26 ADR ₹3,500 per management.

segments.name: Palash Kothi (Bandhavgarh, 5-yr management contract)
segments.commentary: 20 rooms, soft-opened in 2026; operates October to June; ADR guided at ₹8,000–12,000; fee of 13% of revenue to Jungle Camps.

segments.name: Peepal restaurant (Jaipur, leased from RTDC)
segments.commentary: Restaurant added FY25; management said first six months were setup/stabilisation and EBITDA contribution should improve in FY27.

guidance_outlook: ADR expected to be better in October–March than the current run-rate; management said it is 'quite hopeful' of ~5% ADR growth for FY27 but gave no formal number.
Second half (October–March) margins expected to be better than the same period last year.
Devprayag (Uttarakhand, 22 rooms, leased from UP Tourism Board) to start in Q2 FY27; ADR guided at ₹5,000–6,000; capex up to ₹1 cr; lease rental ₹28,000 per year.

Mathura (IHG Holiday Inn Express, scaled to 105 rooms) targeted for FY28 opening; revenue estimate ₹18–20 cr/yr, with management comfortable even at ₹12 cr; project cost ₹49 cr with ₹32 cr HDFC debt at 8.14%; lease rental 5% of gross revenue or ₹54 lakh, whichever higher.

Sheopur Fort (60-key heritage hotel, 90-year lease, competitive bid) to open 35–40 rooms in 1H FY28 with the rest in FY29; budget ₹25 cr (₹10.5 cr internal, ~₹17.5 cr HDFC loan); first-year revenue expected at least ₹12 cr.
Kukru Jungle Camp (Melghat, 15–20 tents, ₹7–7.5 cr capex) expected operational by end-FY28 (March 2028).
Debt expected to reach around ₹50 cr by end-FY28 per Q&A; Mathura and Sheopur loans have 2-year moratorium then 7-year repayment, combined EMI about ₹53 lakh/month (~₹6.5 cr/yr).
Management expects EBITDA margin around 30% over time, but new properties dilute margin until stabilised; new properties take roughly 4–6 months, up to 6 months, to stabilise.
capex_capacity: Current portfolio 8 operational properties with 137 keys (3 owned, 5 leased/managed); 4 pipeline properties.

Mathura: planned capacity expanded from 60 to 105 rooms plus banqueting and dining; project cost ₹49 cr; partly funded by ₹11.5 cr IPO component and ₹32 cr HDFC loan; ₹8.79 cr already invested in subsidiary Madhuvan Hospitality.
Sheopur Fort: development commenced; ₹3.5 cr spent on Sheopur and Pench renovation under CWIP; ₹7 cr standalone tangible assets increase YoY largely CWIP.
Parsili project discontinued after regulatory constraints; ₹1.22 cr premium refundable, ₹0.50 cr performance security to be returned; IPO proceeds redeployed to Sheopur.
Panna, Satpura, Sariska and Jawai at advanced/exploration stage; Ratapani land held, construction expected to start shortly.
demand_pricing: Seasonality: safari season October–March drives ADR and revenue; April–June slower; park closed June/July–September, properties remain open with discounts.
Management said occupancy ceiling is about 60% in wildlife, citing Tadoba at 57%; FY26 occupancy 40%.
Management said competition has not yet hurt ADR or margins, positioning on naturalist-led experience rather than five-star luxury.
Holiday Express brand chosen for Mathura; IHG fee structure of around 7–8% of revenue across four or five components.

504903|2026-06.headline: Rathi Steel & Power Q1 FY27 total income rose 24.6% to INR193.67 crores, PAT up 84.5% to INR3.48 crores, with volumes up ~30% to 28,372 MT.
504903|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed strong volume growth, driven by TMT bars, which more than doubled to about 18,677 MT from about 8,200 MT a year earlier. Total income reached INR193.67 crores (+24.6% YoY), EBITDA INR7.77 crores (+24.83%), and PAT INR3.48 crores (+84.5%), taking PAT margin to 1.8% (+58 bps). Stainless steel volumes were soft, down roughly 10-12% YoY to about 9,000 MT, mainly due to export-linked end-users hit by freight costs and West Asia disruption. Management reiterated a rolling mill utilisation target above 60% for FY27 and a 20% revenue CAGR aspiration, while the TMT 550D direct-charging integration is still in trial and expected to ramp post-monsoon.

financial_highlights.change: vs 21,864 MT in Q1 FY26, ~+30% YoY
vs ~8,200 MT in Q1 FY26, more than doubled
Q1 and Q4 respectively; not disputed by management

segments.name: TMT bars
segments.commentary: Volumes more than doubled to ~18,677 MT; roughly 47-48% of revenue, sold ~100% in NCR, largely to real estate. Brand portion is only 48-50% integrated; 550D integration trial runs done, full ramp expected post-monsoon.

segments.name: Stainless steel
segments.commentary: Volumes ~9,000 MT, down 10-12% YoY on export-linked end-user weakness; roughly 52-53% of revenue. Management says it is more margin-accretive due to higher integration; 80-90% of range is 200 series.

guidance_outlook: Rolling mill utilisation expected above 60% in FY27 (FY26 was ~51-52%); management says it is on track.
Target of 20% revenue CAGR over the next two to three years, measured from FY25 base; management says achievable.
EBITDA margin improvement of 2-3 percentage points over about two years (FY27-FY28) cited as aspiration, from a range-bound 4-4.5%.
Expected FY27 capex of around INR15 crores plus, against INR4-5 crores spent so far, excluding new value-added projects.
Full-scale TMT 550D direct-charging ramp expected by Q4 FY27 after monsoon and pollution-related construction halts.
Melt shop expansion considered once utilisation exceeds 70-75%; refinancing with existing lenders being discussed to lower borrowing cost.
capex_capacity: Installed melting capacity ~85,000 tpa and rolling capacity ~2,00,000 tpa at Ghaziabad (~12.5 acres); rolling utilisation ~51-52% in FY26.
FY27 capex to date estimated at INR4-5 crores; full-year maintenance capex INR10-12 crores normally, with FY27 expected at INR15 crores-plus before debottlenecking/modernisation projects.
Direct-charging/melt-shop integration for TMT bars is in trial; teething issues being resolved across TMT sizes.
Rooftop solar still under feasibility assessment with suppliers; new sheds designed to accommodate it; no capex committed.
Renewable power ~20-25% of consumption via open access and exchanges, adjusted to price.
demand_pricing: Management expects softer steel realisations, volatile energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty to persist.
Stainless steel demand hit by export-oriented end-users due to high ocean freight and West Asia issues; management expects this to persist for a few months.
Competitive supply rose in stainless steel after several IBC acquisitions of similar units ~2 years ago; management says this is normalising.
Raw materials sourced ~100% domestically in Q1 to limit currency exposure; ferro alloys hedged against order book.
Credit period to customers ~30-40 days on average; order book held at about one month of orders.
Monsoon (Q2) and pollution-related construction halts (Q3) expected to dampen TMT demand; management cites the North-India and NCR construction pipeline as supportive.

qa_highlights.question: What monthly dispatch run rate in July-August, and is Q1 momentum sustaining?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose monthly figures but hopes to maintain Q1 momentum; the equal split between construction and B2B segments helps offset monsoon weakness.

qa_highlights.question: Stainless steel volumes and Q2 trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Stainless volumes were ~9,000 MT, down 10-12% YoY, due to export-linked end-users hit by freight costs and West Asia disruption; management aims to recover to last year's level.

qa_highlights.question: Rolling mill utilisation and exit rate for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 utilisation was ~51-52%; management maintains guidance of above 60% for FY27 and says it is on track.

qa_highlights.question: Capex spent so far and full-year plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR4-5 crores spent in FY27 so far; around INR15 crores-plus expected for the year, mainly from internal accruals, excluding new projects.

qa_highlights.question: Margin levers and EBITDA target?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are 20% growth, cheaper working-capital lines after refinancing, and 550D integration; management aspires to a 2-3 percentage-point EBITDA margin gain over about two years, with FY27 as an aspirational target.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital funding for the 30% volume increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Met mainly through extended supplier credit; management plans refinancing with existing lenders to get cheaper bank limits.

risks_watch: Stainless steel volumes down 10-12% YoY; recovery depends on West Asia freight and export demand.
Thin EBITDA margin (4-4.5% range-bound for three to four years, per analyst) despite volume growth; PAT margin only 1.8%.
Working capital dependence on supplier credit; bank limit enhancement contingent on refinancing at lower rates.
Monsoon (Q2) and NCR pollution-related construction halts (Q3) may slow TMT demand; full 550D ramp only expected by Q4.
Increasing stainless steel domestic supply from acquired IBC units.
Management did not disclose top-5/top-10 customer concentration or receivables outstanding; IR follow-up pending.
Revenue-based FY26 base (~INR700 crores per analyst) includes some past trading sales per management; 20% CAGR target needs sustained manufacturing volume growth.
504903|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on volumes and the TMT ramp-up, but cautious on stainless steel and margins. Management was evasive on monthly run rates, customer concentration, receivables and the rooftop solar timeline, and gave no firm date for the solar decision.

543965|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to Rs 3,335.2 crore and adjusted EBITDA rose 34% to Rs 232.2 crore, but ISCS margin fell to 8.1%.
543965|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue grew 28.7% YoY and 10% QoQ, with both ISCS and GFS posting double-digit growth. Adjusted EBITDA margin was about 7%, up 30 bps YoY. ISCS margin slipped to 8.1% from 9.3% in Q4 on onboarding costs for new contracts and no Q4-style price corrections, while GFS margin rose to 4.1%. New business wins of Rs 543 crore were an all-time quarterly high and the pipeline reached over Rs 7,500 crore.</overview>

segments.name: ISCS (Integrated Supply Chain Solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 2,417 crore (+21.9% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA Rs 196.3 crore at 8.1% margin, down from 9.3% in Q4 FY26 due to implementation costs on new contracts. Management targets a return to above 9% in Q2.

segments.name: GFS (Global Forwarding Solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 918 crore (+50.6% YoY), driven by ocean freight volumes in India and higher freight rates. Adjusted EBITDA Rs 38 crore at 4.1% margin, versus 2.1% a year ago; management said it wants at least 5% over time.

guidance_outlook: Aspiration of mid-teen percentage revenue growth for FY27; management expects profit to grow faster than revenue.
Target of about 4% PBT margin; management called FY27 an aspiration and said FY28 will definitely reach 4%.
ISCS EBITDA margin expected to return to about 9% in Q2 FY27 and reach 9.5% to 10% by Q4 FY27.
GFS EBITDA margin expected at 4.5% to 5%, with management wanting at least 5%.
Early-teens EBITDA margin target referenced by an analyst; management said first 45 days of Q2 are on similar lines to Q1.
ALA JV expected to contribute revenue in H2 FY27, targeting about Rs 2,000 crore in year 5 of operations; H2 expected to be stronger than H1.
capex_capacity: Warehousing footprint about 25 million sq ft per analyst; utilisation around 85%, with room to improve through racking and automation investment.
Warehouses are largely project-driven and backed by customer contracts; depreciation on right-of-use assets rose to Rs 114 crore from Rs 93 crore YoY due to additional space for new wins.
Acquired Swamy & Sons 3PL; its results were included for 40 days of Q1 and integration is on track.
Joint venture with ALA Group for defence and aerospace: warehouse finalised, staff being trained in Italy, and warehouse certification pending before business can start in India.
Oracle ERP implemented for the India ISCS business.
demand_pricing: New business wins of Rs 543 crore in Q1 (Rs 524 crore in Q4); about two-thirds from existing customers and one-third from new logos.
Order pipeline above Rs 7,500 crore, up from Rs 6,100 crore; management expects 20-25% conversion over 12-18 months, in line with track record.
Fuel and freight cost increases are passed through to customers under contracts with some time lag; container and air cost increases also passed on.
Management expects ISCS steady-state EBITDA margin of about 8.5-9% on new contracts.
India geography revenue grew 44% YoY on record new business wins and freight volumes.
Management sees recession and geopolitical disruption as the main risk, but said it has not yet seen this playing out in customer volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ISCS EBITDA margin decline despite revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited transition and implementation costs on new contracts onboarded in Q4 and Q1, plus the absence of the Q4 customer price corrections. Management called it a one-time effect and expects margins to recover.

qa_highlights.question: How long do new ISCS contracts take to reach stable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1 to 2 quarters, depending on the contract: about 2 quarters for implant and sub-assembly work and about 1 quarter for aftermarket or finished-goods work.

qa_highlights.question: Was the GFS margin improvement due to one-offs linked to the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth came from new wins and cost optimisation through vendor consolidation, and it expects margins to stay around current levels with high double-digit growth ahead.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ALA JV revenue potential and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to about Rs 2,000 crore revenue in year 5, with first revenue in H2 FY27. It expects the JV to be margin accretive given high entry barriers and a regulated sector.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FIT 3PL merger going ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FIT 3PL will remain a separate legal entity due to GST mechanisms for certain FMCG customers. It said the entity was never part of the announced merger.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Middle East and Africa be entered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is in discussions with Middle East companies and prefers a partnership route. It said it will announce once something crystallises and is taking extra precautions due to the war.

risks_watch: ISCS margin recovery to about 9% in Q2 FY27 is the key test; management has committed to this.
Recession, geopolitical events and supply-chain disruption, with the war cited as a factor.
Container and air capacity constraints and freight rate volatility; management said costs are passed through, though with time lags.
Manpower availability across geographies.
Warehouse depreciation and lease costs rising with new space (other expenses up on short-term rentals).

500245|2026-06.headline: Kirloskar Ferrous Q1 FY27: castings sales up 18% to 41,345 t, tube sales down 14% to 41,512 t, and power and fuel costs rose about INR58 crore YoY.
500245|2026-06.overview: Pig iron and castings output rose in Q1 FY27, while tube output and sales fell on weaker high-value oil and gas and export orders. Power and fuel costs rose sharply, with about INR58 crore of the INR100 crore YoY jump in other expenses coming from power and fuel, half of it from rate increases. A change in green-power rules (8 hours instead of 17) and the end of power trading (about INR10 crore a year) cut the expected solar and wind savings to about INR80 crore a year from about INR100 crore. Management guided to recovery in pricing and volumes from Q2, and said Q1 EBITDA margin was 12-13%.

financial_highlights.change: -3% YoY vs 132,392 t; management attributed to higher internal consumption
Company level; steel and tube margins cited at 14-17%

financial_highlights.metric: Power and fuel cost increase in other expenses
financial_highlights.value: INR58 crore of ~INR100 crore YoY jump
financial_highlights.change: About INR50 crore sequential jump in other expenses; about INR30 crore from rate increases

segments.name: Castings
segments.commentary: Sales of 41,345 t, up 18% YoY; pricing passed through to customers, with further price increases still being concluded. Rajpura foundry is fully sold out at about 2,200 t per month.

segments.name: Tubes
segments.commentary: Sales of 41,512 t, down 14% YoY, with a weaker product mix as more line pipe was sold in place of high-realising export and oil and gas tubes. Management is in a wait-and-watch stance due to Chinese dumping and subdued demand.

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: Realisation improved YoY and QoQ (about INR42,400/t vs INR39,000/t base, as cited on the call); about 30,000 t exported at slightly better than domestic prices. Pig iron EBITDA is expected to support the company margin.

segments.name: Steel (alloy)
segments.commentary: Management expects external sales of 100,000-110,000 t this year vs about 84,000 t, but cost pass-through is still under discussion.

guidance_outlook: Castings volumes expected to rise to about 162,000 t gross sales and then about 188,000 t, implying roughly 17-20% growth.
Overall volume growth of at least 15% across products in the remaining three quarters, with tube volumes up at least 10% YoY and steel external sales up more than 20%.
Pig iron output close to 700,000 t this year, possibly slightly less.
Price-increase and cost pass-through benefits expected from Q2 and Q3 onward.

Medium term: about INR14,000 crore revenue aspiration with 300,000 t castings, 300,000 t casting sales and 400,000 t tube sales. Management said castings reach 270,000 t realisable capacity in this year plus two more years, with tubes at 350,000 t in 3-4 years.
Capex of INR600-700 crore this year, rising in the following years; about INR3,000-3,500 crore over the next four years.
capex_capacity: 35 MW solar plant in commissioning stage; 12 windmills of 2.1 MW each; both expected to be commissioned between June and September 2026.
Solapur two-part (no-bake) foundry, 15,000 t per annum, with commissioning expected by October 2026. Management said it has capacity of about 1,250 t per month.
Rajpura expansion: first phase to 40,000-50,000 t per annum within about 8 months; second phase to 70,000 t per annum. Total realisable castings capacity across six foundries is 270,000 t per annum.
Koppal oxygen plant and enhanced pulverised coal injection in blast furnaces 1 and 2, expected to complete by February-March 2027. Hiriyur pig iron upgrade to 360,000 t, taking about nine months.
Jejuri rolling capacity to rise from 15,000 t to 25,000 t per month (about 3 lakh t per annum), with about 240,000 t saleable; about 18-month timeline.

Premium couplings plant in Baramati, order expected within weeks. Koppal steel plant (about 2 years) and Baramati expander mill (2 years to build) are at early stages. Iron ore mines and pelletisation at Koppal are in progress.
One blast furnace to move to steelmaking, with government clearances in place; decision expected within 2-3 months, commissioning in about 2 years.
demand_pricing: Castings demand described as strong across tractors, automobiles, earthmoving equipment and stationary engines; management expects realisation improvement.
Tube demand subdued by oil and gas slowdown and export disruption; Chinese dumping is pressuring pricing. Management expects the tube market to recover.
Coke dumping into India has reportedly eased, which supports domestic pig iron prices. Pig iron exports are running at about 30,000 t.
Fuel costs rose sharply: LPG cost in Solapur roughly doubled versus pre-war levels. Coking coal cost is expected to peak in June-August because of a three-month coal inventory.
Monthly pig iron sales plan of about 58,000 t including internal sales (about 48,000 t external); foundry grade about 20,000-25,000 t of that.

544469|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 pre-sales rose 83% YoY to INR470 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR107 crore at a 39.9% margin.
544469|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong Q2 and H1 FY27 growth in pre-sales, revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with margins above 38%. Three redevelopment projects were added in the quarter, adding an estimated INR2,700-2,800 crore GDV, taking the pipeline to 24 projects and about INR20,000 crore GDV. Collections were weaker at INR60 crore in Q2 and INR209 crore in H1, which management attributed to construction-linked billing and expects to improve in H2. Analysts focused on collections, the INR300 crore business development outflow, Prabhadevi sales traction and project timeline slippage.

segments.name: Lotus Trident (Andheri West, luxury commercial)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR178 crore pre-sales in its first full quarter after end-June launch, about 35% of sales sold within three months per management. Management guided EBITDA margin of 33-35%.

segments.name: Residential luxury projects
segments.commentary: Celestia reported 36% sales within six months of launch. Lotus Aquaria (Prabhadevi) reported healthy inquiries, but Lotus Prabhadevi (GDV ~INR800 crore) contributed no pre-sales in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance reiterated at INR1,800-2,000 crore.
FY27 revenue and PAT growth guided at 55-60% over FY26.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 35-40% and PAT margin at 25-30%.
Four H2 FY27 launches planned: Lotus Aurelia, Lotus Sky Plaza, Lotus Portofino and Lotus Odyssey, combined GDV INR3,500-4,000 crore; about 90% approvals in place.
Project-level surplus estimated at about INR9,500 crore over the development cycle; projects expected to complete over the next 4-4.5 years.
Management expects H2 collections to be much better than H1 as projects reach plinth level; FY28 collection guidance to be given at the start of FY28.
Amara and Athena expected to receive OC in FY27 (Amara within the quarter or by March; Athena before March).
capex_capacity: Pipeline of 24 ongoing and upcoming projects, aggregate GDV ~INR20,000 crore, of which 19 are redevelopment-led.
Business development: Lotus Impressa (Shivaji Park, Dadar West), Lotus Stellar (Versova) and Lotus Supremus (Juhu) added in Q2.
INR550 crore of IPO proceeds earmarked for subsidiary (Amalfi, Arcadian, Varun); INR305 crore deployed as of 30 Sep 2026 of INR732 crore net proceeds.
Upfront premium paid to government for new projects in Q2, which management said is to save costs and secure supplier discounts; new projects typically need 8-10% of project cost to start.
GIFT City plot of 5.5 acres on Sabarmati riverfront; expected 1.3-1.5 million sq ft mixed-use development subject to town planning scheme approval.
Lotus Monarch timeline pushed out by one year due to society, trust, Charity Commissioner and government approvals; Ghatkopar (Salona) timeline also extended.
demand_pricing: Management says the luxury segment is less sensitive to RBI's 25 bps repo hike to 5.5% (first hike since early 2023); buyers rely less on home loans.
Mumbai H1 CY2026 sales of homes priced above INR10 crore reached a record INR18,500 crore; prime residential prices up 6.2% YoY per management.
Management says prices have risen across almost all projects in H1 and will rise further as construction progresses if the market supports it.
Management says it is the only suburban player to have completed a commercial redevelopment (Arc One), and has 2-3 more commercial redevelopment projects; about five commercial projects in portfolio.
Prabhadevi (Lotus Aquaria) pricing set at a premium, with 270-degree sea view and ~200 m Art Deco tower; management says no pushback, pre-sales expected to show in next two quarters.
Collections as a share of pre-sales: management said completion-stage projects carry 90-95% balance due, and expects 95-100% collection on three projects completing next year.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins above 35% during expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited net debt-free status (no interest burden), minimal marketing spend, a 2.5-3.5 year project cycle that speeds fund deployment, and premium pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected for Trident and what is the commercial redevelopment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided Trident EBITDA margin at 33-35%, in line with guidance. Management expects commercial redevelopment to carry sustainable margins and cited 2-3 more projects.

qa_highlights.question: How will collections catch up with pre-sales?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said collections are construction-linked: about 5-10% at launch and about 25% at plinth. Of about INR800 crore H1 pre-sales, INR200 crore was collected, and H2 should improve as two of three recent projects move past basement.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term growth beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gives annual guidance only. It pointed to ~INR20,000 crore GDV and ~INR9,500 crore project surplus, with completion over the next 4-4.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did timelines shift for upcoming projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Lotus Monarch moved out by one year due to multiple approving bodies. Ghatkopar (Salona) timeline also extended. Management says overall guidance is unchanged and new projects will replace slipped ones.

qa_highlights.question: Why no Prabhadevi pre-sales, and will the business development outflow constrain the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Prabhadevi is a new micromarket with marketing under way and results expected in two quarters. The INR300 crore outflow was upfront government fees and discounted supplier payments; management said cash is sufficient. Operating cash flow will stay negative in launch periods, though Arcadian is working-capital positive.

543626|2026-06.headline: Electronics Mart Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39% to INR 2,419 crore and PAT to INR 121 crore, with reported EBITDA margin at 9.9%.
543626|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter to date, driven by a strong AC season, healthy footfalls and conversions, and 34.2% same-store sales growth. Gross margin expanded to 17.2% from 14.6%, aided by cooling-product mix and temporary price-increase gains in IT hardware. Working capital days fell to 42 from 73 and working capital borrowings dropped to INR 97 crore from INR 658 crore at the start of the quarter. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 18-20% and a post-Ind AS EBITDA margin of 7.5-8%, and said the margin tailwinds are partly temporary.</overview>

Standalone EBITDA margin was about 10.1% and consolidated 9.6%, hit by raw material inflation (alloy, sulfuric acid, poly), brand spends including IPL, Amaron Assist pilot, Factory of the Future costs and higher warranty provisions. Management took ~3% price hikes in June with a further 2-3% planned in the current month, but B2B pass-through lags. Automotive international volumes fell about 20% on Middle East disruption, and management expects recovery in subsequent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Are other expenses non-recurring, and what is the BESS economics?

qa_highlights.question: Break down the ~0.9% margin hit and how other expenses will trend.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 16 GWh lithium plan still on track after the Gotion setback?

qa_highlights.question: What is the lead acid growth outlook and is the price hike volume-driven?

qa_highlights.question: How will the holding company fund new energy capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial risk capital of ~INR2,500 crore to complete five facilities; holding company cash generation of INR700-800 crore post-tax and post-dividend. Future debt-to-equity decisions to be made per business case.

538268|2026-06.headline: Wonderla Q1 FY27 income rose 41% YoY to INR252 crore and EBITDA 39% to INR122 crore, with Chennai Park adding INR45 crore revenue in its first year.
538268|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as one of its best quarters, with income of INR252 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA of INR122 crore (+39%) and PAT of INR72.79 crore (29% margin). Existing parks grew revenue about 15% on 7% footfall growth and 8% ARPU growth. Chennai Park, in its first year, contributed INR45 crore revenue and 2.42 lakh visitors, and management said it is tracking like a mature park for a Q1-type quarter. Management kept the new-park pipeline vague, saying an announcement on at least one park is expected before FY-end.

segments.commentary: Contributed about INR45 crore revenue and 2.42 lakh visitors; EBITDA contribution INR21.86 crore, 64% of EBITDA growth. Management said about 40-50% of land is developed (around 30 of 61.87 acres).

segments.commentary: Added about INR3.19 crore EBITDA (9% of growth); best-ever quarter for both resorts along with Hyderabad park. Resort EBITDA is not disclosed; resort-related 'other' segment revenue was about INR63-64 crore per the segment data queried.

qa_highlights.answer: Footfall is unpredictable, but the year has started strongly. Chennai margins should converge to other parks over time, and Q1 is tracking similarly to larger parks.

qa_highlights.question: Will Chennai reach 1 million visitors this year?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it would take a couple of years to reach 1 million visitors.

qa_highlights.question: How many parks will be added over the next 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans about 1-2 large parks and 1-2 small ones, with an update expected before FY-end. Parks will be picked based on land and government offers, and no closures were named.

qa_highlights.question: Is ARPU growth at Bangalore and Hyderabad a new base?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium cohorts and in-park experiences drove non-ticket spend, which is the main ARPU driver. Management said the base is now high, so similar growth may not repeat each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Monsoon effect on Q1 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said monsoon had little effect because June is weak and May had no unseasonal rain. Management also cited the Kerala and Tamil Nadu elections and inflation in F&B as factors.

qa_highlights.question: Will the resort model be replicated and is timeshare planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans to take the resort model to other cities, including standalone resorts such as Goa, but will wait a full year before deciding. Timeshare was ruled out in favour of retail.

Hyderabad trailing-12-month footfall flat YoY, which management attributes to a lagged marketing investment.
Overhead growth (+INR6.5 crore) and marketing spend, which may recur; management did not call them one-off.
Monsoon and regional rain or disruption risk, including Kerala heavy rain and drought.
Timing and terms of new park announcements, which were not named and remain uncertain.

540743|2026-06.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 10% to INR2,852 crore; Crop Care fell 16.2% on delayed monsoon, while management still targets double-digit FY27 PBT growth.
540743|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales grew 10% YoY to INR2,852 crore despite a delayed monsoon and geopolitical-driven inflation. Animal Nutrition (revenue +12.6%, reported segment result +29%) and Oil Palm (revenue +28.9%, segment result +14.4%) carried the quarter. Crop Care revenue fell 16.2% on a dry June and slower kharif sowing, and Dairy margins were squeezed by milk procurement costs and packaging inflation. Astec reached EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago. Management reiterated FY27 double-digit consolidated PBT growth (versus earlier mid-teens guidance) but deferred a firmer view on Crop Care until end-September.

Segment result +14.4%; EBIT margin ~17% vs 19% a year ago (per analyst)

segments.name: Animal Nutrition
segments.commentary: Revenue +12.6% on robust demand and better realisations; cattle feed volume +15% and overall segment volume +7%. Poultry volumes deliberately reduced in unprofitable geographies. Cattle feed is about 55-56% of the segment; fish feed about 7%.

segments.name: Oil Palm
segments.commentary: Revenue +28.9% on higher CPO and PKO realisations and volume; FFB volumes broadly flat versus a strong early-monsoon base. Segment result +14.4%, with margin down on a pricing-formula effect that management calls one-off.

segments.name: Crop Care
segments.commentary: Revenue -16.2% as a dry June and slow kharif sowing hit cotton herbicide volumes, with margin contraction. Ashitaka and Takai together contribute about 18-20% of Q1 sales; Ghassnash soybean herbicide launched.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago; revenue moderately lower on product mix. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of more than 20%, with an 8-9% Q1 dip to be recovered; CDMO dissilience around 50-52%.

segments.name: Dairy (CDPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue +11.4% and volume +8%, but profitability hit by elevated milk procurement prices and packaging inflation. Route-to-market reconstitution (about 18-20 months) under new CEO Gaurav is starting.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: Revenue broadly stable as live bird trading is planned to fall 15-20% a year and go near zero over 3-4 years. Branded B2C (Yummiez, Real Good) volume +28% and about 32% of the Foods business; profitability hit by input costs.

segments.name: Bangladesh JV (ACI Godrej Agrovet)
segments.commentary: Returned to growth, with double-digit growth in volume, revenue and PBT.

544853|2026-06.headline: Juniper Green Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79% YoY to INR 324 crore and EBITDA 86% to INR 294 crore, with 601 MWp commissioned in the quarter.
544853|2026-06.overview:
First results call as a listed company: total income INR 324 crore (+79% YoY), EBITDA INR 294 crore (+86%) at a 91% margin, and PAT INR 33 crore (+54%). Fleet CUF rose to 30.2% from 28.2% and generation grew 72% to 944 million units. Management reported record commissioning of 601 MWp in the quarter and won new SECI FDRE/thermal-mimic and GUVNL wind tenders after quarter end. Net debt-to-equity was 3.24x before IPO proceeds of INR 1,800 crore; net worth is now stated at INR 5,200 crore.</overview>

543711|2026-06.headline: Sula Q1 FY27 revenue rose 3% to INR121 crore, but gross profit fell 5% as wine-grape mix and adverse market mix cut margins by ~350 bps.
543711|2026-06.overview: Net revenue from operations grew 3% YoY to INR121 crore (INR118 crore in Q1 FY26), the sixth consecutive month of positive sales growth per management. Elite & Premium grew 6% and Own Brands grew 2%, while Economy & Popular stayed under pressure from competitor discounting. Gross profit fell 5% on a ~150 bps hit from a shift to wine grapes (near 100% of harvest 2026 procurement vs 80% earlier) and a ~200 bps hit from adverse geographic mix. Management says the grape-cost headwind should ease from Q4 FY27 and fully normalise from Q1 FY28, and expects EBITDA margins to recover to last year's levels before FY27 end.

532626|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 56% YoY to INR931 crore and PAT 32% to INR36 crore, while lead volumes fell on supply-chain disruption.
532626|2026-06.overview: Revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew 56%, 30% and 32% YoY to INR931 crore, INR56 crore and INR36 crore, with EBITDA margin about 6%. Copper volumes more than tripled YoY to record levels and copper EBITDA per ton rose 66% to INR48,488. Lead volumes moderated as shipping delays via the Strait of Hormuz constrained scrap imports, and management chose to prioritise value-added products (85% of lead revenue), giving a record lead EBITDA of INR21,595 per ton. Management says demand is intact and the constraint is supply, not demand.

segments.name: Lead
segments.commentary: Volumes moderated due to supply constraints; value-added products were 85% of segment revenue. Export mix 55% of lead sales. Management guides sustainable lead EBITDA of INR18,000-20,000 per ton.

segments.name: Copper
segments.commentary: Production and sales volumes each rose more than 3x YoY to record levels (about 4,000 tonnes in the quarter per analyst); export mix 25%. Copper expected to be about 45% of FY27 revenue. Existing capacity about 75% utilised.

segments.name: Plastics
segments.commentary: Turned profitable in Q1 with net profit of about INR15 lakh on about 800 tonnes of volume.

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Small production of about 200 metric tonnes in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Lead value-added mix for FY27 targeted at 65-70% (FY26 about 63%).
Lead EBITDA sustainable at INR18,000-20,000 per ton as volumes rise; Q1 INR21,595 was driven by 85% value-added mix.
Copper EBITDA per ton before value-addition guided above INR40,000 (earlier guidance INR35,000-40,000); cathode blended EBITDA guided INR60,000-65,000 per ton.
Management reiterated earlier FY27 lead volume guidance of about 1.25-1.3 lakh tonnes, saying it expects to close near that level, though it did not give a revised number.
2030 roadmap: over 15% volume growth, 20%+ CAGR in revenue and profitability, EBITDA margin above 8%, ROCE above 20%, over 60% revenue from value-added products.
FY27 capex about INR175 crore: maintenance INR20-25 crore, balance INR140-150 crore for copper plant. Management did not give volume guidance for FY27/FY28 by product yet.
capex_capacity: 36,000 tpa copper cathode plant at Thervoy Kandigai, Tamil Nadu, total investment about INR200 crore, funded from internal accruals; about INR25 crore spent so far.
Phase 1 (18,000 tpa) on track for commissioning in December 2026, trial runs in Q4 FY27; machine installation from end-September, Phase 2 (18,000 tpa) targeted for Q3 FY28.
Incremental 6,000 tpa copper recycling capacity commissioned in Q4 FY26 (copper recycling total about 12,000 tpa, in Andhra Pradesh); about 75% utilised. Target utilisation about 75% through FY27.
New 72,000 tpa lead (TKD) capacity utilisation below 50% because of the focus on value-added pure lead.
CRISIL upgraded outlook to A positive from A stable, rating reaffirmed.
demand_pricing: Management says there is no demand softness; the constraint is delayed shipments and supply-chain disruption.
Lead exports go mainly to Southeast Asia, not Europe; Middle East procurement below 5% of sourcing, with the main issue being shipping routes via the Strait of Hormuz.
Lead sourcing about 97% international in Q1; domestic prices were too high for profitable domestic buying, though management has started looking at domestic procurement.
Copper pricing was supported by tight availability, enabling a premium on copper sales.
Copper sourcing: mostly imports, with plans for 25-30% domestic sourcing going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Can lead volumes reach the 1.25-1.3 lakh tonne FY27 guidance given the current run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of closing up to the committed numbers but will see how supply chains evolve over the next 1-2 months; no revision given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there demand softness in lead, given exposure to Western and Middle East markets?
qa_highlights.answer: No demand softness; exports are mainly Southeast Asia. Only supply delays are affecting volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 16% YoY and 44% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Logistics is a small part; the major driver is fuel prices and some additive prices that rose over the last three months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the record lead EBITDA per ton one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a sustainable level is INR18,000-20,000 per ton; Q1 was high because of the 85% value-added mix.

qa_highlights.question: Capex split for FY27 of about INR175 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance INR20-25 crore; the balance of INR140-150 crore is for the new copper plant.

qa_highlights.question: Copper EBITDA per ton outlook before value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects above INR40,000 per ton going forward, aided by capacity efficiencies and a premium in the current tight market.

qa_highlights.question: EPR credits and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: EPR benefit minimal this quarter as most purchases were imports; unmonetised EPR credits remain on the books. Working capital not stretched because payments are made about a week before arrival at port.

risks_watch: Lead volume shortfall from shipping disruption (Strait of Hormuz) could put the 1.25-1.3 lakh tonne FY27 guidance at risk; monthly production fell in May and early June.
Cost inflation from fuel and additive prices, with other expenses up 44% QoQ.
Copper cathode commissioning slipping beyond December 2026 would delay margin uplift; the cathode blended EBITDA of INR60,000-65,000 per ton is not yet proven.
Copper scrap security as global supply tightens and more countries retain scrap; reliance on imports for most copper sourcing.
Lead EBITDA per ton could normalise toward INR18,000-20,000 as the value-added mix falls from 85%.
Lead volumes fell sharply YoY, with analysts noting a much steeper decline than a competitor; management declined to comment.
532626|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the copper ramp-up and margins, but noticeably cautious and vague on lead volumes, where it repeatedly said it would wait 1-2 months before giving a firm view. Several answers were defensive or repetitive when pressed on FY28 copper volumes and recycling capacity.

544309|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY (12% constant currency) to INR893 crores, with reported EBITDA of INR294 crores at 33% margin.
544309|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached about INR893 crores, up 21% YoY and 12% in constant currency, with forex gains neutral versus Q4. Reported EBITDA was INR294 crores (33%); management says it was about 35% after adding back roughly INR20 crores of one-time TruBridge acquisition costs. PAT was INR193-194 crores, up about 28% YoY. TruBridge closed on July 10, 2026, so Q1 figures are legacy IKS only; management reset TruBridge's steady-state revenue to about $300 million a year (from $340 million pre-close) while keeping its roughly $68 million EBITDA, and reaffirmed a FY30 EBITDA True North of at least INR3,000 crores without further dilution beyond ESOPs.

~+28% YoY; higher if adjusted for acquisition costs

demand_pricing: Legacy IKS cross-sell into large health systems showing early land-and-expand wins: Advocate Health Care (top-five US health system, >$35 billion revenue) expanded in RCM and coding; a large California system is moving regions to Epic; a national musculoskeletal aggregator signed a significant RCM deal; StrideCare (vascular) partnership.

qa_highlights.question: What organic constant-currency growth is healthy over the medium term, and is margin expansion coming from currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin growth is not from currency: revenue grew 12% CC on 4.2% headcount growth; adjusted EBITDA is 35% with neutral forex. Aspiration is 12%+ CC on legacy IKS, not guidance; TruBridge growth to be set in two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How does SLM fit with LLMs, and where does glass-box/explainable AI sit?
qa_highlights.answer: Three SLM approaches: standalone SLMs, LLM-distilled SLMs, and hierarchical SLM-plus-LLM. Explainability comes from knowledge graphs acquired via ARAI. Management would not commit to a 60% token-usage reduction, saying it will emerge over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire TruBridge and what criteria govern acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Chosen because the rural market is large, TruBridge holds 30%+ share as one of two dominant rural EHRs, and its service mix resembles ambulatory. Criteria: strategic thesis first, leverage tolerable relative to EBITDA, and accretive price; $68 million EBITDA bought for ~$550 million.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge's margin of 22-23% fixable, and does the INR3,000 crore target rule out M&A?

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge still EPS accretive for FY27 after revenue reset?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; EBITDA is unchanged, so management says EPS accretion is absolute and possibly a bit higher than previously expected.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: About 10% of Q1 revenue, seasonally weighted to H2 (Latin America, mainly Brazil). Q1 hit by raw material constraints, order slippage to China, and Brazil credit and liquidity concerns. Expected to be about 20% of mix over 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Management expects around 15% growth rate, with EBITDA growing 13-14% over the next 2-3 years (earlier in the call, EBITDA margin guidance of 12-13% was given).

Management expects the Q2 season to track anticipated growth; PAT in Q2 is expected to be a similar share of full-year PAT as last year (Q2 FY26 was about 60% of full-year PAT), with the absolute number higher.
Management expects Brazil demand to recover from September for H2 ahead of the October season.
Management targets a domestic market share rise from about 3-3.5% to 7-8%.

Management says patented product share of the portfolio will double in 2-3 years, with about 12 products launched in the last 3 years and two to three new patented formulations and one or two technicals a year.
capex_capacity: Technical capacity utilisation is about 70-75%, with room to grow and scope to swap high-value, low-volume products in multi-product plants.
Formulation plant utilisation is about 25-30%; management says formulations are sized for peak season and are not a bottleneck.
Backward-integration technical plant at Dahej and Saykha was capitalised after the prior quarter, raising depreciation.
Technical plant can run 12 months to supply H2 export demand from Latin America.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices were volatile in Q1 due to geopolitical events and petrochemical-linked inputs. Rupee depreciation of about 10-11% also raised input costs. Management said B2B prices can be passed on, while B2C has a lag covered by inventory.
Demand was held back by price volatility, with farmers, channel partners and formulators delaying purchases. Management cited El Nino forecasts and crude volatility.
Monsoon rains from July were good; cotton and soybean acreage is up and chillies are increasing. Management expects insecticide and fungicide demand to benefit.

Brazil demand is weak with customer liquidity and credit issues, and some orders moved to China on logistics. Management is cautious and is focusing on established B2B partners and second-tier distributors in Argentina and Uruguay.
Management says farmers are moving to specialty molecules and preventive spraying. It cited West Bengal as an example.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mix between technicals, formulations and branded patented products?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel mix is about 45% B2C, 45% B2B and 10% export. Formulations are about 75% and technicals about 25%. Patented products are about 20-22% of B2C, with a target to double over 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of IPO fund utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The loan repayment object has been fully met during the quarter. A small residual amount remains pending bank settlement of brokerage, which may take 2-3 months, before the IPO account can be closed.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material costs affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expansion is mainly from product mix. Rupee depreciation of 10-11% and petrochemical-linked price volatility raised input costs. B2B passes costs through, and B2C is covered by inventory for now.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Q1 export business faring and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Brazil orders were delayed by pricing volatility and some shifted to China. Management expects destocking, with demand returning from September for the October season. It is pursuing Argentina and Uruguay via second-tier distributors and new registrations.

qa_highlights.question: How is Kharif progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: July rains were good and key kharif acreage is up. Management said South India (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka) is still a wait-and-watch situation based on monsoon. No material shortage is seen currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Technical utilisation is about 70-75% with scope to add high-value products. Formulation utilisation is about 25-30%, which management says is by design for peak-season capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The company plans one or two new technicals a year, with data generation taking 4-5 years, and two to three new patented formulations a year, with a pipeline covering the next 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off nature of other income and the outlook for it?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR5.7 crore of the INR8.3 crore other income is the land-sale gain. No further other income is planned for the remaining quarters. Management said the land sale is a one-off.

risks_watch: Other income of about INR5.7 crore from a one-off land sale inflated Q1 PAT. Excluding it, management's PAT growth looks much lower, and the analyst cited roughly flat PBT.
Raw material volatility and rupee depreciation of 10-11% could compress B2C margins if pass-through lags.
Brazil credit and liquidity stress, plus loss of orders to China on logistics, puts export recovery at risk. Export is about 10% of Q1 revenue.
South India (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka) depends on monsoon, and the El Nino forecast adds uncertainty.
Management guidance is inconsistent: EBITDA margin 12-13% in one answer, EBITDA growth 13-14% in another, and PAT growth expectations are not quantified. Monitor Q2 delivery against these.
544733|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on domestic patented product growth and the mix shift, but cautious on export, particularly Brazil. Management was less precise on margin and growth figures, sometimes giving different numbers across answers.

505726|2026-06.headline: IFB Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.65% to INR 1,529 crore, with PAT up to INR 38.06 crore, but commodity and forex costs were not passed on.
505726|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.65% YoY to INR 1,529 crore and PBDIT rose 26.46% to INR 88.46 crore, with margin at 5.79% of revenue versus 5.34%. PAT was INR 38.06 crore (2.5% of revenue) against INR 25.36 crore a year earlier. Management said commodity and forex headwinds are not behind the company and that it has not been able to pass them on in price, relying instead on cost initiatives (INR 42-43 crore in Q1). Home Appliances (HAD) revenue grew about 18%, with July described as good, while gross margin fell about 160 bps.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 vs Q1 FY26; FY26 HAD growth was about 9.8-10%
FY26 full year: about INR 67 crore
Attributed to raw material price increase of about INR 4,125 per tonne in the quarter

segments.name: Home Appliances (HAD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 18% in Q1; front-load volume up 9-10%, top-load volume up over 20%, AC volume up 6-8%, and IFB-branch refrigerator volume up 14% per management. Gross margin down about 160 bps on material costs.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: Sales up 17% YoY and above budget; EBITDA in line with budget. Management expects similar growth going forward, with festive season supportive. Stated FY ambition of about INR 2,000 crore revenue; current base about INR 1,000-1,100 crore.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Loss-making in Q1 due to steel price increases, which management expects to recover from customers in coming quarters. Management cited ROCE of about 20%.

segments.name: Services (HAD)
segments.commentary: Growth of about 17% in the quarter per management. Profitability described as double-digit at PBT level; management did not give a figure.

segments.name: IFB Refrigeration (associate, 41.40% stake)
segments.commentary: Company PBT INR 80 lakh; IFB share INR 0.33 crore (INR 33 lakh) in Q1 versus a loss last year. Company revenue growth stated at 2%. Management declined to discuss it in detail.

guidance_outlook: Management expects about 20% growth, with Q1 at 18% and July described as good; it said it is 'working towards' 20%.
Cost initiatives target of INR 120-150 crore for FY27, with INR 42-43 crore already in Q1; the company said it is not cutting counters or in-store promoters.
Management has no near-term view that commodity and forex pressure is over and did not expect to pass it fully through.
PBDIT should be early double digit in the long term, per the CEO (in response to an analyst question on margin aspiration).
Engineering expects growth similar to Q1. The INR 2,000 crore target depends partly on a battery project (LOI about INR 150 crore from Tata) that is now under review after Tata Sons' decision.
Full-year capex is about INR 110 crore; the Engineering stamping capex plan is about INR 400 crore.
AC aspiration: 7-10% market share, with no timeline given.
capex_capacity: AC capacity about 75,000 units per month; peak month utilisation about 85%. Debottlenecking and automation planned to reach 75,000-80,000 per month without adding shifts.
Management said there is no current capacity constraint in HAD and that new products for unserved capacities are expected within 3-6 months.

Engineering acquired land in Gujarat for EV and stamping. Stamping capacity expansion planned in Gujarat, Gurgaon and Bangalore, with a business target of about INR 1,000 crore against about INR 400 crore stamping capex.
Tata LOI (about INR 150 crore) for battery project under review; land already acquired, and machinery not yet ordered.
demand_pricing: Price increases taken across all HAD categories in the last quarter, but not enough to cover commodity and forex; management said it had led some price increases where the market had not.
Management said it has not been able to pass commodity and forex cost increases to customers in full; pricing is constrained by competitiveness.
Front-load washer share estimated to be top-2 by management, but no published market-share data is available. Top-load may be lower.
Trade schemes and discounts of about INR 1,800 crore were questioned by an analyst; management said it is an industry practice and under review for leakages.
RAC transition: old-rating AC stock was run down by about January, and the company did not build older-rated stock. Management said the new-rated models are 10-15% more expensive than the market.

qa_highlights.question: Has the commodity and forex headwind (about INR 170 crore across Q4 and Q1) been passed on, and is it behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Not behind us. Management said it has not passed commodity or forex costs to customers; savings came from efficiency initiatives instead.

qa_highlights.question: Why did RAC growth (about 10%) lag the industry (20%+)?
qa_highlights.answer: The company chose not to carry older-rated AC stock through the BEE rating change, so it lost the price advantage. It is focusing on higher-capacity models.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company sustaining 20% growth and what drove the Q1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 HAD revenue grew 18%, and management said distribution fixes (counters, displays, promoters) drove growth; it says the trend should continue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 2,000 crore Engineering target still achievable given the battery project uncertainty?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR 250 crore of business is near closing, and that the existing business grows about 20%. The battery project is under review, and other projects are being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Was the company's cost-savings guidance lowered from INR 150-200 crore to INR 120-150 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is INR 120-150 crore for FY27, after INR 67 crore in FY26; SKU rationalisation is expected to add benefits.

qa_highlights.question: Why did IFB refrigeration company growth (2%) differ from IFB-branch refrigerator sales growth (14%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 14% is IFB Industries branch volume and that the company's own figure could differ because of branch structure; it declined to discuss the associate.

risks_watch: Commodity (steel, copper and others) and forex pressure with no pass-through; gross margin down about 160 bps.
Steel division loss in Q1 with recovery depending on customer price pass-through in coming quarters.
Engineering growth target depends on OEM business wins and the Tata battery project, which is under review.
Trade-scheme spend of about INR 1,800 crore (per an analyst) and its scrutiny by management.
Motor division loss; management deferred the question to an offline discussion, so the cause is unclear.
Inconsistent Fine Blanking Q1 FY26 revenue figure (INR 185-186 crore vs INR 176 crore) in the presentation; management said it would revert.

522074|2026-06.headline: Elgi Q1 FY27 revenue grew about 23% (7 points from exchange), EBITDA up 28%, with EBITDA margin held flat year on year at prior-year level.
522074|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue growth of about 23%, of which about 7 points were exchange-related, with growth across all geographies. EBITDA grew about 28% and EBITDA margin was maintained at last year's level despite raw material inflation, tariffs and adverse product mix. PAT margin was about 9.7%, roughly flat YoY, after exceptional reorganisation costs in Australia, Europe and the US. Management said price corrections to offset metal cost inflation would take effect towards the end of Q2 and more fully in Q3, so the Q1 margin does not yet reflect them.

financial_highlights.value: Maintained at prior-year level, management said slightly better
Up about 12%, mainly rental premises for motor plant and US facilities sold and leased back
About 1.6-1.8 million of approx. 4 million approved; balance pending

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Grew about 28%, described as primarily volume-driven, with growth across industrial, portables, aftermarket and vacuum. Growth cited in EV ecosystem, renewables and semiconductor supply chains; water well segment picked up in the quarter.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Grew about 37%. Distribution business underperformed, mainly on service side; other businesses performed well.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew about 21%. Run as a P&L play now, targeted at breakeven; plans to enter Germany and expand in Eastern Europe, with tighter cost control.

segments.name: Australia
segments.commentary: Grew about 17% but described as muted; service and distribution operations being reset, with recovery expected by Q3-Q4.

segments.name: Southeast Asia
segments.commentary: Described as a challenge for an Indian brand; not a significant contributor; longer-term play.

segments.name: Vacuum (Italian JV product)
segments.commentary: Locally produced and selling since indigenisation; management described Q1 growth as phenomenal in percentage terms from a small base, with no figure given.

guidance_outlook: Price corrections to recover raw material inflation expected to kick in towards end of Q2 FY27 and fully in Q3 FY27; management said Q1 under-recovered on raw material costs of 5-6% versus 3-4% planned.
Management expects EBITDA margin to keep improving, citing operating leverage, product launches, constant cost reduction and fixed cost rationalisation over 3-4 years.
Medium-term EBITDA margin target of 20%; prior guidance of 18% by 2031 was mentioned in Q&A.
Tier 4 entry-level compressor range to launch formally in September 2026 (Hyderabad exhibition); first orders already received; marginal contribution to top line this year.
Demand=Match to be introduced in rest-of-world models during 2026; management expects all products to carry it within about a year.
Some reorganisation costs in Australia, Europe and the US expected to continue into the year.
capex_capacity: Capex mainly for MK2, the programme to shift the campus from the city factory to a new campus; about half of capex.
Land purchased in Italy under a commitment made six years earlier, plus routine factory equipment.
Motor plant moved to rented premises; US facilities sold and replaced with rental facilities.
Insourced motor manufacturing cited as a significant cost-saving driver.
demand_pricing: Inquiry levels described as very strong, though deal finalisation timelines are longer than normal.
Price correction only marginal in Q1; growth described as primarily volume-driven.
Demand=Match technology, launched September 2025, is embedded in tier 1-3 models as standard and cited as a key driver of new-customer wins in India.
Aftermarket parts are about 28-30% of India revenue and about 15-16% globally (parts only); management said global service benchmark is about 38%.
Warranty cost stated as below 1% of revenue; management said competitors are higher, though not publicly reported.
Steel sector capacity utilisation weak; management said steel is bleeding capacity utilisation before new investment.

qa_highlights.question: How much of India's 28% growth was volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Primarily volume-driven, with only a marginal price correction in Q1; raw material costs rose 5-6% versus the 3% planned, and management expects to recover this in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is Elgi gaining Indian market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it thinks so but would prefer competitors confirm it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aftermarket share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Parts are about 20-23% of group revenue, about 28-30% in India and about 15-16% in the rest of the world; service is a small part in India and is left largely to dealers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the warranty cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Less than 1% of revenue; competitors are believed to be higher than 1%, though not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What drove margin improvement in international subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: North America growth, restructuring to lean the organisation, cost reduction including in-house motor manufacturing, and price holding in Q1, with price corrections expected to add from Q2-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee and operating costs rationalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost ratios should fall as revenue grows; a process-layer project over 3-4 years is expected to identify lower-cost locations for specific jobs.

risks_watch: Tariffs at 25%; outstanding tariff refund balance (approx. 4 million approved, 1.6-1.8 million received) and future US tariff policy.
Raw material inflation: management said price corrections lag cost inflation, so Q2 margins could be pressured before recovery.
Australia service and distribution reset and Southeast Asia challenges.
Reorganisation costs expected to continue into the year, which may keep PAT margin under pressure.
Distribution build-out in the US and globally is slow; management said adding distributors takes a long time.
Tier 4 launch in a segment where low-cost Chinese compressors compete on price.
522074|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and product technology, but cautious on near-term price recovery timing and on Australia, Southeast Asia and US distribution. Management declined to give several figures (segment mix, semiconductor share, warranty cost, vacuum sales).
key_quotes: We grew by about 23% and after that 7% was exchange related.
So even this quarter, we have maintained our EBITDA percentage same as last year.
Demand=Match is a technology that gets embedded in all our products, right?
So, we are confident that there will not be any impact.

500940|2026-06.headline: Finolex Q1 FY27: volume fell 27% YoY to ~68,000 MT, while EBITDA rose 14% to INR107 crore and margin widened to 12%.
500940|2026-06.overview:
Volumes fell 27% YoY to about 68,000 MT as PVC price volatility triggered channel destocking, with April the weakest month and May and June growing per management. Revenue fell 27% to INR884 crore from INR1,043 crore, but EBITDA rose 14% to INR107 crore and margin improved from 9% to 12%, which management attributed mainly to top-line realization rather than cost. PAT was about INR107 crore and cash stood at INR2,636 crore. Management said July was the best month of the four, with a minimum price floor from the MIP and customs duty withdrawal, but declined to give full-year volume or margin guidance beyond reiterating the sub-15% margin view.</overview>

segments.name: Agri pipes
segments.commentary: Agri was 69% of volume; agri volume fell 27% YoY. Fittings were 5% of agri and 11% of total volume.

segments.name: Non-agri / plumbing
segments.commentary: Non-agri was about 25% of volume (fittings 25% within non-agri per management); volume fell ~24% YoY, versus ~18-20% industry peers per management.

segments.name: CPVC
segments.commentary: CPVC was about 7% of volume in Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: No full-year FY27 volume guidance; management said it is too early and will revisit after Q2 trends.
Margin: reiterated the Q4 FY26 view of sub-15% EBITDA margin, with no revision.
Management expects a somewhat better Q2 on realizations after the MIP-driven price floor; said it was hopeful H1 volume could be flattish YoY, with a plus possible if July's pace holds.

Capex: capital outlay of INR125-200 crore per year for expansion and debottlenecking, unchanged. Installed capacity 520 (unit as stated), FY26 volume 333, headroom for 10-12% growth over roughly the next 1-1.5 years.
Other income of ~INR75 crore in the quarter is mark-to-market and driven by bond yields, so it is not guaranteed to recur at that level.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity stated as 520 (units not specified); FY26 volume 333. Management says there is headroom to grow 10-12% over the next 1-1.5 years.
Growth is coming through debottlenecking, replacing lower-capacity extruders with higher-capacity ones, rather than large greenfield or brownfield projects.
Capex outlay remains INR125-200 crore, unchanged.

Ratnagiri PVC: EDC-based line running without interruption. VCM-based line does not run during the June-September monsoon months because the Ratnagiri jetty is fair-weather only. VCM availability is constrained by Middle East force majeure and Northeast Asia feedstock constraints.
CPVC extrusion capacity is considered sufficient for near-term CPVC growth, according to management.
demand_pricing: Average PVC price in Q1 was about USD875/MT versus USD707/MT a year earlier (ICIS), carried over from elevated Q4 FY26 levels. A sharp intra-quarter correction in April triggered channel destocking.
Management cited INR96 to INR92 to INR82/kg as the PVC price path through April. Analyst cited a INR12-13/kg hike in the last 15-20 days after the MIP and duty changes.
Customs duty exemption on PVC resin was withdrawn in mid-July, and a minimum import price (MIP) was imposed. Management said these should support price stability and channel inventory.
Pass-through: management said almost all of the recent price increase (barring INR1-2) has been passed to customers.
Demand: July was the best month of the four, with a strong pickup; August to date was described as moving in the right direction.
Channel inventory is near normal, with some room left. A lot of stocking occurred in July in anticipation of price increases. Quantification in days was not given.
PVC-EDC spread was ~USD501/MT in Q1 FY27 versus ~USD522 a year earlier, and ~USD490 currently. PVC-VCM spread was INR122/kg in Q1 FY27 versus INR163 a year earlier.
Pricing: management said Finolex prices ~10-12% above Supreme-type peers in the market (ballpark only).
Market share: management said FY26 share of the top 5-6 reporting companies was about 22%, and it sees no change in Q1. An analyst cited FY23 share of about 27%.
JJM 2.0: management said the outlay is about INR67,000 crore, not higher than JJM 1.0. All sales go through channel partners, so there is no direct correlation to volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did realization not rise QoQ when peers reported 7-9% jumps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realization per kg was up ~15% vs the same quarter last year and was in line with peers. It said Q4 FY26 was an aberration with a sharp price rise, and that falling PVC prices in April drove the QoQ result. Discounts and incentives also affect net realization.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the volume decline was agri vs non-agri, and what were the monthly trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri fell 27% and non-agri fell ~24% YoY. April was the weakest month, May grew and June was normal. Management did not give monthly figures and said it would reach out separately.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion despite falling volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin was largely top-line driven, with costs range-bound. It cited backward integration and the timing of raw material procurement as a cushion. It did not quantify inventory gains or losses.

qa_highlights.question: Will full-year volume decline? Can H1 be flat YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide full-year volume. It said July was a good month and that flattish H1 YoY is possible, with a plus if July's pace holds, while August and September are still to be seen.

qa_highlights.question: Why not deploy the INR2,636 crore cash into CPVC capacity and shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CPVC extrusion capacity is sufficient and CPVC is about 7-8% of the PVC pipe market, which Finolex matches. It said the Board decides on cash deployment or returns and will announce when a decision is made.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin guidance sub-15% when Q1 delivered 12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is holding the sub-15% guidance from Q4 because of volatility in Q1 and wants another quarter of data before revising it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VCM supply situation and the PVC plant utilization outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: VCM availability is limited by Middle East force majeure and Northeast Asia feedstock constraints. The VCM line does not run during monsoon months (about June to September) because of the fair-weather jetty. Management said efforts to secure supply are ongoing and H2 is uncertain.

505160|2026-06.headline: Talbros posted a record Q1 FY27 with total income of INR242 crores (+15% YoY) and EBITDA of INR43 crores at a 17.6% margin, with management guiding FY27 group revenue growth of 18-20%.
505160|2026-06.overview: Talbros reported record quarterly revenue of INR242 crores, up 15% YoY from INR211 crores, with EBITDA of INR43 crores (17.6% margin) and PAT of INR30 crores (+35% YoY). Gasket and heat shield revenue grew 21% to INR164 crores, while forging recovered only modestly to INR78 crores (+4%) amid weak European demand and manpower issues. Management said input-cost inflation (steel, aluminium, labour) temporarily compressed margins and expects to recover this from OEMs in coming quarters. New growth lines cited include data-centre generator gaskets (about 5% of gasket revenue) and a Stellantis chassis/forging programme that started production in Q1.

financial_highlights.change: +15% YoY (vs INR211 crores in Q1 FY26); record quarterly high
Margin under temporary pressure from commodity and labour costs
vs INR13 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR12.5 crores in Q1 (about 3.27% of sales)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR10 crores in Q4 FY26 and INR9 crores last year (as stated)

segments.name: Gasket & heat shield
segments.commentary: Revenue INR164 crores (+21% YoY), EBITDA INR29 crores (+32%). Claims nearly 50% share of domestic gasket market and is probably the largest heat shield (NVH) player in India; growth from Hyundai and Kia heat shields and data-centre gaskets.

segments.name: Forging
segments.commentary: Revenue INR78 crores (+4% YoY), EBITDA INR14 crores. Export-oriented (US, UK, Europe); Q1 hit by European demand softness, manpower shortages and lost Meritor business (INR30-40 crores p.a.).

segments.name: Marelli Chassis Systems (JV)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR105 crores (+43% YoY), EBITDA INR17 crores, driven by passenger OEM volumes and value-added products. Management expects 30-40% growth for FY27 for this JV; Q1 margin dipped on lower other income and new manpower and rental costs.

segments.name: Talbros Marugo (JV)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR40 crores (+31% YoY), EBITDA INR6 crores (+57%), citing strong customer demand and efficiency gains.

segments.name: Lohum Talbros (JV)
segments.commentary: Circular-economy venture recovering carbon black and devulcanised rubber; described as progressing as planned, no financials disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group revenue growth guided at 18-20%, with EBITDA margin around 17-17.5% as inflation impact is still being assessed.
Gasket division expected to grow about 17% in FY27, with FY27 gasket revenue of about INR680-700 crores.
Forging expected to grow 15-20% in FY27 to about INR340-350 crores, with Q2 at double-digit growth and Q4 the strongest quarter; July and August reported as improving on June.
Longer-term targets: gasket about INR850-900 crores and forging about INR600-700 crores by FY30; export share target 35% by FY28.
Sustainable EBITDA margin cited at around 17%. Capex planned at about INR103 crores for FY27 across gaskets, forgings and heat shields.
Management expects OEMs to pass through steel, aluminium and labour cost increases in coming quarters; Marelli margins expected to recover by year-end.
capex_capacity: Planned FY27 capex of about INR103 crores across gaskets, forgings and heat shields, to meet OEM demand.
Forging equipment is in place; manpower and leadership issues reportedly resolved, with new CEO Ashish (appointed April 1) spending about 50% of time on forging.
Stellantis programme in the chassis division started production in Q1 FY27 after about 2 years of design changes and start of production.
Plastic EV components for JLR at about INR25 crores in orders, maturing from next financial year; JLR EV rubber components worth INR15-20 crores p.a. with supply from Q1/Q2 CY27.
Possible chassis plant in Gujarat under discussion with Tata Motors (management to meet Tata Motors chief within 90 days).

Data centres: about 5% of gasket revenue today; estimated INR30-40 crores annual potential, rising toward INR100 crores in 2-3 years; Cummins sales of INR25 crores in Q1 vs INR90 crores last year.
Management said 7 OEMs are looking to shift supply chains from China to India; BMW giving more business, Volvo a potential new gasket customer, and Stellantis opened for Marelli.
Cummins America expected to contribute INR30-40 crores by FY27-28 (wire harness, aftermarket and data-centre gaskets).
Forging orders: about INR500 crores over 5 years (about INR100 crores p.a.) cited; Marelli and Dana/Carraro orders maturing in Q3-Q4.
Gasket pricing: management said data-centre gaskets are the same product as regular gaskets, with pricing unchanged; margins not separately disclosed.
Management stated pricing pass-through of input costs from OEMs is expected in coming quarters.

500368|2026-06.headline: Patanjali Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to INR11,337 crore, with operating EBITDA of INR543 crore (4.80% margin).
500368|2026-06.overview:
Management reported the fourth consecutive quarter of record revenue, led by edible oils (INR8,505 crore, record) and oil palm (INR740 crore, up 25% YoY). FMCG revenue was INR2,938 crore at a 6.45% EBITDA margin, with biscuits and HPC growing strongly while staples were loss-making at INR-59 crore EBITDA. Input inflation from delayed monsoon and West Asia conflict was a net positive for edible oils (long positions) but a headwind for FMCG. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, while flagging caution on staples demand and margins.</overview>
