540692|2026-06.headline: Apex Frozen Foods Q1 FY27 PAT rose 138% YoY to INR22 crores on 15% higher shrimp realisation (INR930/kg), despite 13% lower volumes at 2,624 MT.
540692|2026-06.overview: Revenue was flat at INR257 crores against INR258 crores a year earlier, while EBITDA rose 79% to INR33 crores and margin expanded to 12.7% from 7.1%. Shrimp sales volume fell to 2,624 MT from 3,015 MT, hit by April-May labour shortages, container and equipment shortages, and EU shipment clearance delays that spilled into Q2. Management kept full-year production guidance at around 12,000 MT and said Q2 volume should recover, subject to global transport normalising. Realisation was guided to hold near INR900 per kg in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: flat vs INR258 crores in Q1 FY26

segments.name: USA
segments.commentary: Accounted for 70% of shrimp sales in Q1 FY27 vs 54% a year earlier; sales rose 13% YoY and 121% QoQ. Pricing includes a 10% tariff plus ADD/CVD (about 9%).

segments.name: EU and UK
segments.commentary: Contributed 25% of shrimp sales vs 39% in Q1 FY26, hit by war-led transport disruption and origin-side testing and certification requirements; management said EU volumes spilled into Q2.

segments.name: Ready-to-Eat (RTE)
segments.commentary: 16% of Q1 volume vs 15% last year; management targets at least 18-20% of volume in FY27, with RTE margin about USD 0.50/kg above RTC at minimum.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 production guided at around 12,000 MT, reiterated from the start of the year; management said the earlier 14,000 MT figure was not a company guidance.
Q2 volume recovery expected, subject to global transport normalisation; order book covers sales until about mid-Q3 FY27.
Realisation in Q2 expected near INR900/kg, similar to Q1.
Margins expected to stay broadly stable, with partial pressure from higher ocean freight (more than doubled since Q4 FY26) and rising farm-gate prices.
Capacity utilisation targeted at 35-40% through FY27; next growth stage of 14,000-15,000 MT considered for FY28-29, not yet firmly committed.
Japan business initiated; Russia expected to start by end-Q2 or Q3 FY27; Australia still at audit stage.
capex_capacity: Volume capacity utilisation 38% in Q1 FY27 vs 39% in Q1 FY26; management targets sustained 35-40% through the year.
RTE capacity utilisation 16%, similar to prior year.
Labour shortage in April-May due to summer heat was resolved toward end-Q1 per management.
Raw material supply tightness expected to ease as new crop comes in.
No capex plans were announced in the call.
demand_pricing: Realisation of INR930/kg is up about INR80-90/kg YoY, helped by higher USD unit values, a weaker rupee and a higher RTE mix.
US buyers placed more orders after tariff uncertainty eased; the 10% tariff has been stable since the start of the year.
Farm-gate prices rose about 6-7% over the 3-4 weeks before the call; Q1 prices were described as stable.
Management said realisations above a certain level would hurt consumption and volumes, as in FY22-23.
UK-India FTA effective 15 July 2026, but non-tariff barriers such as 50% testing of Indian shipments remain; EU FTA expected around December 2026 or January 2027.
Ocean freight costs have more than doubled since Q4 FY26 due to war-led disruption.

qa_highlights.question: How are fish meal and feed price increases affecting farmers and the company, and are they temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said feed manufacturing is not part of the business. Farm-gate prices rising gave farmers comfort; margins should stay stable, with freight and farm-gate price increases as partial offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume below the 12,500-14,000 MT run-rate, and what growth is expected for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is about 12,000 MT. Q1 was hit by labour shortage and container shortages, and EU shipments slipped into Q2, which made US volumes look high. The order book is firm to mid-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RTE contribution and its margin premium over RTC?
qa_highlights.answer: RTE was 16% of Q1 volume and is expected to reach at least 18-20% in FY27. The margin premium is at least USD 0.50/kg over RTC, with some products higher.

qa_highlights.question: Will US tariff refunds be received?
qa_highlights.answer: No refunds have been received yet. Timing and outcome are unclear because of ongoing US legal proceedings.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 realisation a new high versus history, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Similar levels were seen in FY22 during COVID phase 2, but those were driven by panic buying and hurt volumes. The company aims for a sustainable level through a richer value-added mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US CVD and ADD outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: ADD is at 3.4%, up from 1.35%, with a final determination around September 2026. CVD could fall by about 5.77% in December 2026 if duty drawback and RoDTEP are accepted as non-subsidies.

qa_highlights.question: What new adjacent products are being commercialised?
qa_highlights.answer: Proprietary customer-developed RTE and RTC products are already being shipped, estimated at 3-4% of sales (about 300-400 MT on 12,000 MT), rising to about 500 MT annually.

risks_watch: Ocean freight costs have more than doubled since Q4 FY26 because of war-led disruption; freight is the main risk to margin stability.
EU and UK volumes dropped to 25% of sales; watch whether shipments normalise in Q2 and whether testing or certification delays persist.
Full-year volume of about 12,000 MT requires roughly 9,000+ MT in the remaining three quarters versus 2,624 MT in Q1 FY27.
Capacity utilisation of 38% is well below the 14,000-15,000 MT next-stage ambition.
Possible US tariff refunds are unclear; the CVD review in December 2026 and the ADD determination in September 2026 could change pricing.
Farm-gate price increases and tight raw material supply could pressure costs.
540692|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on profitability and pricing, but cautious and hedged on volumes, freight and the timing of FTA benefits. Management avoided committing to FY28-29 volume figures and said it was too early to say.

544679|2026-06.headline: Amagi Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR 437 crore, a record, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 11.5% versus 5% a year ago.
544679|2026-06.overview:
Revenue reached INR 437 crore, up 32% reported and 21% in constant currency, and almost 10% sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA rose from INR 17 crore to INR 50 crore, with margin expanding to 11.5% despite the seasonally weak Q1 from annual increments. PAT rose to INR 34 crore (7.5% margin), and would have been about INR 40 crore excluding a one-time non-cash FX charge. Management reiterated operating leverage, highlighted AI product wins, and said gross margin will be kept in a 67% to 69% range for this year.</overview>

segments.name: Streaming Unification
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 249 crore, +39% YoY, driven by existing customer expansion, ~10,000 channel deliveries and 451 distributors (+21%).

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 110 crore, +30% YoY, volume-driven; monetized ad impressions a record 13.6 billion, +59% YoY and +21% QoQ.

segments.name: Cloud Modernization
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 17% reported; management said ~32% excluding the prior-year rev rec benefit from a large deal.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin to be kept in a 67% to 69% range for this year, with Q3 seasonally strong; management described it as not structural deterioration.

Management is focused on full-year profitability rather than quarterly margins; H1 was ~47% of FY26 revenue and ~37% of FY26 adjusted EBITDA, indicating back-half EBITDA weighting (historical context, not guidance).
Q2 YoY comparison carries ~600 bps headwind from prior-year rev rec timing benefit; management said Q2 may not be the best marker for growth.
Broader AI product suite to be announced at flagship industry conferences in Q2 FY27; AI revenue contribution expected more visibly in late FY27.
Aspiration to maintain growth rates through the year, without explicit guidance.
capex_capacity: Cloud cost optimisation delivered ~USD 282,000 monthly run-rate gross margin savings in Q1, reinvested into AI initiatives.
Live event delivery supported 104 FIFA World Cup matches on Amagi infrastructure for key customers; one US broadcaster received 100% on-air availability across 325 events and 450 hours.
Q1 is the weakest cash quarter each year due to incentive payouts, increments and software renewals.
Since January, 33 M&A opportunities evaluated, 23 passed on, 10 under active evaluation; management said this is not a signal of an imminent deal.
demand_pricing: Content processed reached 959,000 hours, +43% YoY; deliveries reached 9,900+ endpoints; distributors ~451, +21%.
Ad impressions 13.6 billion in the quarter, +59% YoY; management said FIFA did not add ad insertion upside and growth is organic (CTV penetration).

AI: 10+ active pilots; a major US news network selected Newspulse (agentic newsroom platform) after an earlier first paying customer; AI credit model introduced for some media operations, with outcome-based pricing possible later.
Pricing: one customer received a price adjustment but volume run-rate is >30% growth, a net revenue tailwind; management sees no material AI-driven deflation to revenue or pipeline yet.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the sequential gross margin improvement and will it recover to 69%? What is AI's impact on gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided gross margin to 67% to 69% for this year, citing mix, live events, pricing and AI costs. AI is a small base with no substantial margin impact yet; a 2 to 3 year S-curve with a possible initial dip is expected. Gross margin was ~64% three to four years ago.

qa_highlights.question: Do distribution platform additions drive customer growth, and is in-sourcing a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Several distribution platforms (Vodafone, Kogan TV, Virgin UK) became customers, but it is not a prerequisite. Management sees platforms outsourcing rather than in-sourcing and is not aware of in-sourcing impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross retention (GRR) disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: GRR is not disclosed; management pointed to logo churn in low single digits and top 10 customer vintage of ~5 years as stickiness indicators.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI being priced and how is cost inflation protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Early stage; AI credits model mirrors a cost-plus approach for agentic media operations, with telemetry built with Newspulse customer to measure cost and revenue benefit. Business model not yet settled; a few more quarters needed.

qa_highlights.question: Is NRR constant currency and what is the growth impact of last year's one-time item?
qa_highlights.answer: NRR is in reported currency on a TTM basis, as in the DRHP; full-year NRR to be disclosed at Q4. The prior-year rev rec benefit affected growth by ~450 bps. Management aspires to sustain growth but Q2 will still lap the base effect.

qa_highlights.question: Can channel deliveries be split between new channels and additional deliveries on existing channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Not tracked internally; directionally growth is from existing channels going to more deliveries. Net revenue retention contributed ~26 points of the ~31% growth from existing customers.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from live event mix, customer pricing and AI costs; guided to 67% to 69%.
Cash burn remains negative in Q1 (operating outflow INR 65 crore reported), with DSO improvement of ~8 days QoQ still needed.
Q2 FY27 faces a ~600 bps headwind from the prior-year rev rec base; growth optics may be weaker.
Monetisation of AI products (Newspulse and broader Q2 suite) is still early; revenue contribution expected late FY27.
Capital deployment: active M&A pipeline (10 opportunities under evaluation) against INR 1,616 crore cash.

543969|2026-06.headline: Pyramid Technoplast Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to ₹222 crore, but EBITDA margin was about 10% and capacity utilisation only 62%.
543969|2026-06.overview:
Revenue grew 36% YoY to ₹222 crore, driven mainly by price pass-through of raw material increases, while volumes were 1,292 MT against 20,936 MT per quarter installed capacity (about 62% utilisation). Gross margin compressed to 23% and EBITDA grew 50% YoY at about 10% margin; PAT rose 32% YoY to ₹10.5 crore at about 5% margin. Management said EBITDA per ton was ₹16,380 versus ₹11,252 a year earlier and ₹15,053 in Q4 FY26, but also said the figure reflects a temporary price spike that is expected to normalise. 539889|2026-06.headline: Parag Milk Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR945 crores (record Q1), but EBITDA margin slipped to 7.4% from 7.7% and PAT fell 20%.

Gross profit rose 11% to INR258 crores with gross margin stable at about 27.3%, which management attributed to calibrated pricing and mix. Distribution target of more than 1.5 million outlets within three years.

532443|2026-06.headline: Cera Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.5% (volume-led) to INR 486 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.1% on one-time factors management says reverse from Q3.
532443|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations grew about 19.5% YoY to INR 486 crore, with Sanitaryware up 14%, Faucetware up 25% and growth mainly volume-driven. EBITDA excluding other income fell to INR 49.2 crore (10.1% margin vs 13.1% a year ago), which management attributed to a wage settlement, under-absorption from single-kiln operation in April-May, project-order foreclosures and delayed price pass-through. PAT was INR 45 crore vs INR 47 crore. Turnover discounts were reclassified from expenses into revenue deductions, lowering reported revenue by about 2.5-3% with no absolute profit impact. FY27 guidance of 18-20% revenue growth and 13.5-14% EBITDA margin was maintained.</overview>

segments.name: Sanitaryware
segments.commentary: 47% of revenue; grew 14% YoY (volume ~10%, price ~2%, mix ~2%). Capacity utilisation 61% in Q1, roughly 80% across both plants from June.

segments.name: Faucetware
segments.commentary: 40% of revenue; grew 25% YoY (volume 18%, price 4%, mix 3%). Utilisation 96%; gross margin severely hit by brass cost inflation.

segments.name: Tiles
segments.commentary: 11% of revenue; grew 22% YoY.

segments.name: Wellness
segments.commentary: 2% of revenue; declined 7% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 18-20% reiterated.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 13.5-14% maintained; management says it will be met on a full-year basis, implying a recovery after Q2.
Q2 expected to carry some residual impact as project orders still at old prices; project price revisions to flow from Q3.
Gross margin expected to return to ~51% from Q3 if brass and gas prices hold; Q1 gross margin was ~46%.
FY27 wage cost add-on of INR 18.3 crore (INR 6.3 crore one-time arrears plus INR 12 crore for the year); FY27 staff cost guided at ~INR 300 crore.
FY27 capex outlay ~INR 43 crore, mainly Faucetware brownfield expansion (capacity expected from Q4 FY27), efficiency, digital and infrastructure.
FY27 brand-building and marketing budget ~INR 85 crore, which management says can be increased.
Management declined to guide FY28 margins; said it would revisit at year end. Long-term margin of 16% not committed to a timeline.
capex_capacity: Sanitaryware utilisation 61% in Q1 FY27 (one kiln run in April-May; second kiln started June); both plants running from June at ~80% of total capacity.
Faucetware utilisation 96% in Q1; management says it can go beyond 100% via in-house and outsourced supply until brownfield expansion comes in from Q4 FY27.
Greenfield sanitaryware project (earlier INR 130-150 crore, deferred) to be reviewed by year-end; would take ~18 months to build once decided.
Internalising higher-selling SKUs from Morbi outsourcing partners; incremental casting-line investment of INR 2-3 crore.
Long-term in-house/outsourced split about 50:50; Sanitaryware skewed more towards outsourcing recently due to bought-out parts.
demand_pricing: Cumulative price increases (March and May 2026): ~12% in Sanitaryware, ~16% in Faucetware; management says absorbed well by the market.
Price hikes reflected mainly in retail; project contracts (43% of Q1 revenue vs 39% in Q4) to move to revised pricing from Q3.
Brass prices rose from INR 665 (Dec) to ~INR 880 (June) and ~INR 900 (July) per management; further hike possible if prices go to INR 950-1,000.
Product mix: premium 44%, mid 37%, entry 19%. Tier 1 and Tier 3 at 38% each, Tier 2 at 24%.
Management described growth as volume-driven and broad-based across retail and project, with Sanitaryware demand up from ~10% growth in prior quarters to 14%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 19.5% growth was volume vs price, and what was the Senator/Polipluz contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanitaryware: volume ~10%, price ~2%, mix ~2%. Faucetware: volume 18%, price 4%, mix 3%. Management would not split out Senator and Polipluz numbers, saying they are in build-up phase and FY27 targets are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What was the one-time wage settlement and what is the staff cost run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 6.3 crore arrears for Sept 2025-Mar 2026 booked in Q1, plus INR 3 crore for the current quarter. Full-year wage impact INR 18.3 crore. Staff cost expected ~INR 300 crore for FY27 excluding the one-off.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the margin drop, and how much is one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 4.35 percentage point one-time impact: wage arrears 1.3%, under-absorption from single kiln 0.75% (INR 3.7 crore), accelerated project order closures 0.8% (INR 4 crore), and delayed retail price pass-through 1.5%. Ex-these items EBITDA would be ~14.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Morbi and SKU internalisation need capex, and how many flagship stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Internalisation needs only INR 2-3 crore of casting-line changes. Senator stores to rise from 35 to ~50 by year end, on track.

qa_highlights.question: Who leads Senator and Polipluz after Mr. Baliga's resignation?
qa_highlights.answer: The existing national head under the succession plan will lead them. Baliga stays until 30 September. Management says targets are unchanged and no execution impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Should the greenfield sanitaryware plant be revived?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand improving (Sanitaryware growth 14% vs ~10% earlier). Review by year end; if approved the plant takes ~18 months. Some capacity remains available.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further price hikes and where does gross margin go?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin ~46% in Q1 (Faucetware hit hardest); expected ~51% from Q3 if brass and gas hold. Further hike to be evaluated if brass goes beyond INR 900-950.

544476|2026-06.headline: Jeena Sikho Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to INR224 crore, with EBITDA of INR92 crore (41% margin) and PAT of INR65 crore (28%).
544476|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR224 crore (up 29% YoY), EBITDA of INR92 crore (up 17% YoY, 41% margin) and PAT of INR65 crore. Government hospital business was cut sharply (INR15 crore to INR5 crore YoY per management), while private Panchakarma and product sales grew. Management attributed part of the cost base to one-off items: about INR4 crore extra advertising, about INR2 crore software implementation and audit fees. Other income of INR14 crore included about INR7 crore one-time gains (warrant valuation and capital gain), per the CFO. Management guided to 30% annual growth and INR3,000 crore turnover within about 3 to 5 years, but gave no quantified FY27 guidance beyond 3,000 to 3,500 operational beds.

Q1 FY27 PAT of INR51 crore was also cited by an analyst and management in the Q&A; treat PAT figure as inconsistent in transcript
Up from INR4 crore in Q4 FY26; about INR7 crore one-time (INR5 crore warrant valuation, INR2.5 crore capital gain)
Panchakarma revenue +13% YoY; private Panchakarma INR78 crore to INR100 crore (about 30% YoY)
Products business grew 47% YoY; INR80 crore in Q1 FY26 per management comparison

segments.commentary: Pre-launch; 108 rooms plus 22 villas, guaranteed 35 rooms under a 3-year lease renewable 3+3+3. Management expects little FY27 contribution, with launch around Sep-Oct 2026 and better season from March; guided year-one EBITDA 35-40%+ and year-two 60% occupancy at ADR INR35,000-37,000.

guidance_outlook: Target of 30% YoY growth annually and INR3,000 crore turnover in about 3 years (maximum 5 years); INR1,000 crore PAT ambition over the longer term.
Operational beds to rise from 2,400 to 3,000-3,500 in FY27; 7,000-10,000 beds targeted in 3-5 years; occupancy target 75-80%.
Plans for 3-4 more luxury wellness centres in India, each guided at INR3-5 crore net profit (management).

Ayushman Bharat/insurance claim inclusion for Ayurveda expected but timing unclear (2-6 months per management); discounted admissions for BPL and Ayushman patients to begin within about 10 days, with 500 beds mentioned.
Entero OTC product listings expected to start across its distributors within about 15 days.
capex_capacity: Operational beds 2,400 as of Q1 FY27, up 100 in the quarter; bed occupancy 59% on 2,400 beds per management.
Panvel hospital currently 49 beds pending OC/fire approvals; to scale to 250 beds, which management says could multiply its revenue 4-5x.
Manali luxury wellness centre: launch around Sep-Oct 2026 after Himachal Pradesh NOC process; 108 rooms and 22 villas, 35 rooms guaranteed under lease.
Management said about INR15 crore revenue from a single Meerut centre.

Ticket size fell as discounted admissions were introduced for lower-income patients; management said realisation per patient will be lower on the discount segment.
Government business deliberately shrunk because of receivable risk; management says it will re-engage only once NHA panel payments are reliable (3-6 months).
Advertising expense up about INR4 crore YoY tied to TV integrations (Colors TV shows, Khatron Ke Khiladi), with benefits expected in subsequent quarters; ad budget up 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue flat QoQ and what is the advertising cost run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QoQ patient/volume growth was about 10% and government business was cut to one-third; advertising was up INR4 crore in Q1 with benefits expected in later quarters under a 6-month TV tie-up.

qa_highlights.question: Why do IPD (+33%) and OPD (+22%) volume growth not translate into similar revenue growth (+11-13%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the government-business decline (INR10 crore drop), discounted pricing for lower-income patients, and a lag in OPD-to-Panchakarma conversion; the CFO said incremental ticket size has fallen.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 other income (INR14 crore) is one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR7 crore is one-time (INR5 crore warrant valuation, INR2.5 crore capital gain); recurring other income about INR4-5 crore plus treasury/FD income.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off costs in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly INR4 crore extra advertising, about INR2 crore software implementation instalment, and about INR0.5 crore extra audit fees; management said these expenses will continue.

qa_highlights.question: Manali luxury wellness economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 35 rooms guaranteed under a 3-year lease; year-one occupancy 50% at ADR INR32,000-35,000, year-two 60% at ADR INR35,000-37,000, with 35-40%+ EBITDA in year one. Minimal operating cost since the lessor bears utilities and most staff costs.

qa_highlights.question: Pet Shuddhi price gap versus Pet Saffa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its manufacturing cost is about four times the competitor, citing a multi-shot formulation and liver/spleen/metabolism claims.

531548|2026-06.headline: Somany Q1 FY27: EBITDA margin up 3.6 pts YoY to 11.6% on standalone utilisation of 83% (vs 72%), with volume growth only ~3%.
531548|2026-06.overview: Management attributed the margin expansion to higher in-house capacity utilisation and a swing in JV performance from a loss of INR10 crore to a profit of INR3 crore YoY. Sales grew about 3% while value grew about 24%, with a few percent of sales lost in April when Morbi supply was shut for roughly 1.5 months. Price hikes of about 16-17% were passed through to the market, and gas costs rose 16-18% in the current period. Management guided to single-digit to mid-single-digit volume growth, maintained margins of 11%+, and announced a 9-plus million sq m South plant (about INR220 crore capex) due around end-Q3 FY28.

Gas prices rose 16-18% in the current period; management said the company has passed through increases to date, and July and August gas prices are marginally higher.
capex_capacity: South plant: 9-plus million sq m greenfield, about INR220 crore outlay, operational around end-Q3 / start-Q4 FY28.
Balancing equipment in own plants and JVs (Bahadurgarh, Gujarat, Morbi, South) to add about 3-4 million sq m (also cited as 4-5 million) by Q4 FY27; no new line in FY27.

demand_pricing: Price hike of about 16-17% taken in Q1 FY27; management said margins come from efficiency, with pricing being a pass-through.
Morbi was shut for about 1.5 months, with a 20-day ramp-up to full output from May. Management said about 15-17% of Morbi capacity has not restarted and will not restart.
Morbi exports are down 50-60% from peak due to geopolitical issues and freight; this may persist until freight stabilises.
Channel inventory was built up in March ahead of the April shutdown, is now back to normal but lean, as dealers wait for gas-price cuts.
Retail project share is about 7-8% and government about 10-11%; management expects this to rise by 3-4 percentage points.
Management said July demand was affected by rain but sales were still pushed; it said demand was 'perfectly fine' overall.

Management said that in the Q1 volume growth shortfall versus the industry leader, the leader benefited from in-house Morbi production in polished vitrified tiles (PVT), which Somany is fully exposed to via outsourcing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion and will it sustain from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to standalone utilisation rising to 83% from 72% and JV profit of INR3 crore vs a loss of INR10 crore YoY. It said margins are driven by efficiency rather than pricing and expects them to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: Gas pricing across Morbi, North and South?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended natural gas cost is about INR68/unit. South and Morbi are around mid-INR70s (South partly on spot), and North is about INR68-69. Management did not give a blended fuel cost incl. biofuel.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth outlook and why guidance is only mid-single-digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is currently mid-single-digit. It said the leader's higher growth came from in-house PVT production. It has been cautious after missed high-single-digit targets in the past.

qa_highlights.question: Is the price premium over Morbi narrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Morbi raised prices by roughly double Somany's 16-17%, narrowing the gap. Morbi units are now on GEL gas, and their accounting is being rectified, which narrows landed-cost differences.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 capex and funding plans?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR275 crore to end-FY27 including the INR220 crore South plant and balancing equipment, with 65-70% from internal accruals. JV loan is without corporate guarantee from Somany.

qa_highlights.question: Is 2%-3% volume growth affected by outsourcing from Morbi, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Morbi outsourcing is not needed beyond a point because of freight. Own plants are targeted at 100% utilisation, with capacity located in North, South and West.

533269|2026-06.headline: VA Tech Wabag Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.8% YoY to INR 887 crore, PAT up ~37% to INR 90 crore, order backlog record INR 19,400 crore.
533269|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue from operations was INR 887 crore (+20.8% YoY), EBITDA INR 116 crore (+21.7%, margin just over 13%) and PAT INR 90 crore (+~37%, 10.2% margin). Order intake exceeded INR 3,400 crore, 77% from international markets, taking the order book to a record INR 19,400 crore (over 4x revenue). Management said the company stayed net cash positive for the 14th consecutive quarter, and new wins included a 60 MIGD Kuwait desal plant and the third phase of Ajman STP in the UAE. Management guided 15-20% revenue growth for the year and reiterated a 13-15% medium-term EBITDA margin band, with FY27 more likely at 13-14%.</overview>

segments.name: Revenue mix by business
segments.commentary: EPC 82% and O&M 18% of revenue. India 48%, overseas 52%.

segments.name: Order intake
segments.commentary: Q1 order intake over INR 3,400 crore: EPC ~INR 2,960 crore, O&M ~INR 470 crore. International 77%, India 23%.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: Record INR 19,400 crore: 66% EPC, 34% O&M; roughly balanced India vs international. Management put Middle East at about 35-40% of backlog. Two framework orders (~INR 600 crore) were removed as not yet effective.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: O&M revenue grew about 7% YoY in the quarter. Management said it will grow in line with project completions moving into O&M phase (Ghaziabad, Digha-Kankarbagh completed; Perur next year).

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guided at 15-20% for the year; management said it expects to meet it and to deliver above guidance.
EBITDA margin: medium-term blended band 13-15%; FY27 expected at 13-14%, with a stated aspiration of 15% by year end.
Working capital guided to stay in the 100-110 day range despite growth; long-term Wriddhi 2.0 strategy to be presented at the May FY27 investor meet.
Backlog expected to execute over about 36 months; international EPC cycles 24-30 months, India about 36 months.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model: management said no capex is needed to take orders and there are no capacity constraints.
Perur desal project (Chennai, JICA-funded): about 75% complete, 1 lakh cubic metres of concreting done, marine works finished; commissioning over the next few quarters.
Kodungaiyur: agreement signed, DPR submitted to the PE; refurbishment (1.5 years) to start any time, followed by 18.5 years of operation.
Kuwait 60 MIGD SWRO (with HEISCO) and Kutaisi (Georgia) project started; Ajman STP phase 3 is a design-build sewage biorefinery.
demand_pricing: Order intake was dominated by international wins: Kuwait desal (first project there), Ajman STP phase 3 in UAE, Vienna Water Works high-end drinking water, plus repeat Indian orders in Bengaluru and Delhi (Byramangala, Bellandur, Mitraon/DJB).
Bid pipeline: management cited about USD 2-3 billion across MEA and India (about INR 20,000-25,000 crore), with India about USD 1-1.5 billion. No order inflow target was given.
Management said the Middle East conflict has had no material impact on projects; it has written force majeure letters to customers covering price and time impacts.
Domestic traction is returning in industrial and municipal segments; management still sees larger deal sizes overseas.
Industrial share of backlog is about 12-13%, with an aim of 20-25% over time; traditional industrial is ~90% oil and gas.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall YoY, and were there one-off provisions in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed margin differences to project mix (more EPC vs EP). It said other expenses included standard provisions for delay or anticipated default under a tighter policy, which can be reversed on collection. No one-off was described.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share-of-profit from associates (~INR 5.5 crore) and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: It is mainly from HAM projects that moved from construction to O&M. Management said it includes construction-phase risk releases, so it may not recur at the same level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the forex gain operational and how does it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said forex gains arise from transactions (invoices, collections, payments) and are treated as operational; translation gains go through reserves. It said it has a natural hedge and uses PCFC for residual exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Will the order backlog execute faster outside India?
qa_highlights.answer: International EPC cycles are 24-30 months versus about 36 months in India; the backlog is expected to execute over about 36 months overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the TSGENCO receivable (~INR 140 crore) recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is sub-judice, the Supreme Court verdict is in its favour, and it would not give a timeline.

risks_watch: Forex gains formed a significant part of Q1 profit; management says they are operational, but the standalone operating margin excluding forex fell from 15.8% to 8.9% (as cited by an analyst).
Middle East geopolitical exposure: 35-40% of backlog is in the Middle East; execution risk around logistics, imports and prices, with force majeure notices issued.
Rising provisions for delays or defaults in other expenses under the new, more stringent policy.
O&M growth slowed to about 7% YoY; recurring revenue growth depends on project completions moving into O&M.
TSGENCO receivable (~INR 140 crore) still in arbitration with no timeline; Kodungaiyur refurbishment start awaits PE approval.
533269|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and defensive. Management pushed back repeatedly on margin, forex and geopolitical questions, calling forex operational and the Middle East impact minimal. It was evasive on the Perur revenue recognised and on the EPC/EP split for the quarter.
key_quotes: Importantly, we remained net cash positive for the 14 th consecutive quarter, reinforcing the strength of our balance sheet and our disciplined approach to the growth.
Our order book position reached a historic high of INR 194 billion, that is INR 19,400 crores, almost $1.8 billion, which is over four times of our revenue base
So we have a natural hedge when it comes to it. Whatever is the small component of difference between the revenues and the cost, that is anyway covered through a PCFC.

544526|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR 5,110 mn (from INR 9,157 mn YoY) on 334 MW sales; EBITDA margin rose to 8.33% while confirmed order book stands at ~6.35 GW.
544526|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a weak quarter: sales of 334 MW were down from 579 MW a year earlier and 1,050 MW in Q4 FY26, as customers deferred procurement and management chose to execute only margin-accretive orders. Revenue fell to INR 5,110 mn and PAT to INR 54 mn. Management said the EBITDA margin of 8.33% was better than the 7.25% in Q4 FY26. The Odisha cell line (2.4 GW) is near ramp-up with ALMM-2 inspection planned for September 2026, and management is pinning margin recovery on cell volumes in H2 FY27. Management kept FY27 guidance unchanged, but the call contained no numbers for Q2.

FY28 guidance to be discussed in Q3 FY27. Management called FY28 a 'milestone year' as utility DCR demand starts from April 2027.
Encapsulant capacity to rise from 2 GW to 5 GW; the announcement on equipment is expected next quarter.
capex_capacity: Odisha Phase 1 (57 acres): 2.4 GW cell and 4 GW module. About INR 1,000 crore of capex incurred so far; Phase 1 total is about INR 1,850 crore.
Phase 2 (27 acres): 3.6 GW cell, taking total cell capacity to 6 GW. Site work to start by end-Q2 FY27, completion by end-FY28, capex about INR 1,600-1,700 crore.
Phase 3: 6 GW ingot and wafer, targeted for FY29 and aligned with ALMM-3. Planning has started.
Total capex across the programme is roughly INR 3,500 crore. Peak net debt is expected at INR 2,200-2,400 crore.
Cell line ramp-up expected by end-August or early September 2026, with ALMM-2 inspection planned for September 2026.
demand_pricing: Confirmed order book of about 6.35 GW (about 132% of 4.8 GW module capacity), valued at about INR 8,200 crore per management, with execution over 12-18 months.
Mix: about 70% utility and 30% C&I/open access. About 30% of orders are DCR. Retail is excluded from the book and runs at about 20% of monthly sales.
Pricing: about 30% of C&I orders are fixed-price. In utility, about 30-40% are variable-price (cost pass-through) and the rest fixed-price.
New orders: INR 138 crore module order in July 2026 (execution by December 2026) and about INR 400 crore accepted by a subsidiary on 11 August 2026 (execution by March 2027).
DCR cell margins are quoted at 18-20%. Management said spot cell-purchase orders are not in the order book.
Customers deferred purchases amid the Iran war, cost volatility and ALMM-1 vs ALMM-2 uncertainty. Management said demand was weak in May-June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp YoY EBITDA margin compression despite a strong order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a crowded module market, higher commodity, freight and forex costs from the geopolitical situation, and weak customer demand. It also said it declined to execute orders where input costs could not be passed on. Q1 margin of 8.33% was better than Q4 FY26's 7.25%.

qa_highlights.question: When does cell manufacturing start and what utilisation is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up is expected by end-August or early September 2026, with 200 MW per month from the 2.4 GW line. Management expects about 80% utilisation by Q4 FY27. Full ramp-up is expected in about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Debt peak and capex needs for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is about INR 1,250 crore. Capex incurred is about INR 1,000 crore out of a roughly INR 3,500 crore programme. Net debt is expected to peak at INR 2,200-2,400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did demand slow in Q1 when the ALMM transition was expected to pull volumes forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said developers waited because input costs rose after the Iran war began on 20 February, and force majeure notices and expected DCR extensions pushed projects out. Two tariff regimes (before and after 30 June) also encouraged waiting, which left demand subdued in May and June.

qa_highlights.question: Could you give the FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY28 numbers until Q3 FY27. It said large utility projects tendered from December 2025 (18-24 month cycles) will drive DCR demand from April 2027, making FY28 a milestone year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-module business plan and transformer opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-module business is 4-5% of revenue, targeted at 7-8% in FY27 and 15% next year. Melcon was acquired mid-Q1. Management targets 8-10% of a transformer market of about INR 30,000 crore (INR 55,000 crore by 2031) and INR 1,000-1,500 crore revenue in 3-4 years.

540704|2026-06.headline: Matrimony.com Q1 FY27 PAT rose 127.5% YoY to Rs 19.1 crore on consolidated revenue of Rs 130.5 crore (+13.2% YoY).
540704|2026-06.overview: Consolidated billing was Rs 136.0 crore (+7.8% QoQ and +7.8% YoY) and revenue Rs 130.5 crore (+11.7% QoQ, +13.2% YoY), with consolidated EBITDA margin of 20.1% versus 12.4% in Q4 and 11% a year ago. Matchmaking EBITDA margin rose to 26.9%, helped by deferred revenue from last year's introduction of a one-year package. Management guided Q2 matchmaking billing and revenue to double-digit YoY growth and PAT to triple-digit YoY growth, with profit similar to or slightly above Q1. The non-matchmaking wedding services business remained loss-making (EBITDA loss Rs 3.8 crore) and is being shifted from subscription to a commission model.

financial_highlights.change: vs 12.4% in Q4, 11% a year ago
vs 22% in Q4, 17.6% a year ago
vs Rs 43.5 crore in Q4, Rs 46.7 crore a year ago
vs loss of Rs 5.7 crore in Q4

segments.name: Matchmaking
segments.commentary: Billing Rs 135.3 crore (+8.0% YoY) and revenue Rs 109.5 crore (+13.6% YoY); EBITDA Rs 34.9 crore at 26.9% margin. Management said EBITDA would have been about Rs 40 crore had billing equalled revenue.

segments.name: Marriage services and other businesses
segments.commentary: Billing Rs 74 lakh (-13.8% YoY, +0.5% QoQ) and revenue Rs 96 lakh (-24.3% YoY, +13.1% QoQ); EBITDA loss Rs 3.8 crore. Q4 included an impairment, which management said drove the higher loss.

guidance_outlook: Q2 matchmaking billing and revenue to grow double digits YoY.
Q2 PAT to grow triple digits YoY; profit expected at a similar level to Q1 or slightly better.
Marriage services billing expected to be higher in Q1 than in the current quarter (management said Q2 billing would exceed Q1).
Revenue-to-billing conversion expected at roughly 96-99% in a given quarter, depending on billing mix.
Wedding services targeted at a Rs 100 crore run rate before it contributes to profit; management said clarity likely in about a year.
capex_capacity: Marketing spend to be held and slightly stepped up to support growth and new initiatives such as love.com and Malayalee Love.
Manyjobs remains focused on Tamil Nadu; national expansion not planned until next year or later, and it needs a run rate before breakeven.
Goodwill impairment was taken in Q4; further impairment depends on the performance of the newer businesses.
Rs 4 crore invested in an AI astrology startup (Bharat Ek Khoj) as a long-term investment.
demand_pricing: Paid subscriptions added: 2.72 lakh in the quarter (+15.9% QoQ, +3.7% YoY).
Matchmaking ATV fell 6.7% QoQ but rose 4.2% YoY; management said ATV should not be read too much into, citing package mix, discounts and the Jodi and love.com low-price products.
No ASP or ticket price increase planned; pricing handled through segmentation and analytics.
One-year package is a small share of users; management said it is individual choice and not an incentive lever.
Over 25,500 success stories in the quarter.
Management said it is not seeing a reduction in competitive ad intensity but is not fully slowing down; plans to slightly step up marketing.

qa_highlights.question: How is revenue recognised and how big is the billing-revenue gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised over the membership period (3 months to 1 year). The gap was about Rs 5 crore in Q1 and is expected to be Rs 3-5 crore on an ongoing basis, mainly due to the one-year package introduced last year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the triple-digit profit growth sustainable, given flat revenue in recent quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the jump to continued growth plus deferred revenue from the one-year package introduced last year, and guided Q2 PAT to a similar or slightly higher level than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for AI, growth and investor presentation data?
qa_highlights.answer: AI is used for profile and photo validation, chatbots and product work. Growth comes from profile acquisition, conversion and launches such as love.com and regional versions. Management agreed to update the investor presentation data.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ATV falling and will ASPs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ATV is not in a steady state, citing segment, package and discount mix plus low-priced Jodi and love.com products. There are no plans for a ticket price increase.

qa_highlights.question: Wedding services: break-even timeline and ad spend outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is focused on reaching a Rs 100 crore run rate rather than breakeven, with a commission model being piloted. It expects marketing to be held or stepped up slightly rather than cut.

qa_highlights.question: Legal fees increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Sushanta Swain said the rise is from registering a large number of trademarks to prevent misuse.

risks_watch: Revenue quality: Q2 profit guidance depends on deferred revenue from the one-year package, and ATV fell 6.7% QoQ.
Marriage services: still loss-making, with the commission model unproven and a Rs 100 crore run rate target about a year away.
Marketing intensity: matchmaking marketing spend rose to Rs 46.5 crore and management plans a slight step-up.
Impairment risk on the newer businesses after the Q4 goodwill impairment.
Management declined to disclose business split, geography mix and whether there will be any cash deployment (acquisition or shareholder reward).
540704|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on matchmaking profitability and Q2 guidance, but evasive on pricing, geography, segment split and capital deployment, citing competitive reasons. Cautious on wedding services, described as still in piloting with no firm breakeven timeline.
key_quotes: I am pleased to report that we have delivered on that guidance with the PAT increasing by 127% year-on-year.
So, I think Matchmaking has reached a certain level of threshold in terms of EBITDA margins.
We changed the model which we communicated some time back. We moved from the subscription business model to a commission-led model.

519126|2026-06.headline: Hindustan Foods Q1 FY27 PAT rose 33% YoY to INR42.8 crore, a record, while footwear cost pressure of ~INR6 crore weighed; FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore reaffirmed.
519126|2026-06.overview: Total income rose 18% YoY to INR1,207 crore and EBITDA rose 26% to INR106.3 crore, with PBT up 33% to INR56.6 crore. Footwear absorbed about INR6 crore of raw material, freight and minimum-wage cost pressure, with the Haryana wage hike the main driver. Management reaffirmed FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore and announced INR190 crore of new projects, taking FY27 commitments to INR340 crore plus INR150 crore carried forward. A Silvassa plant disruption from July rains is expected to be fully resolved by end-August.

financial_highlights.metric: Footwear cost pressure (raw material, freight, wages)

segments.name: Home & Personal Care
segments.commentary: Running at maximum capacity with a record quarter; Aurangabad personal care integration complete. Silvassa brownfield expected to start in Q2 FY27 and Lucknow greenfield later this year. INR50 crore Lucknow project (bar and liquid lines) announced.

segments.name: Food & Beverages
segments.commentary: Coimbatore, Nashik and Mysuru at record production; beverages had an excellent season. INR210 crore of beverage projects across Coimbatore, Mysuru, Goa, Aurangabad and Hyderabad, expected online by Dec/Jan. Greek yogurt facility being added in Goa.

segments.name: Ice Cream
segments.commentary: Strong summer with record volumes; Panipat facility commissioned in Q1. INR80 crore Panipat expansion announced; Nashik cone and ice cream utilisation improving with new customers.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Q1 utilisation was poor due to imported material and freight disruption, and cost pressure hit margins. Management says utilisation is about 80-90% from August; order book full from Q2 FY27 and the business is expected to pay off in H2 FY27. Price pass-through now being achieved from Q1 onward per management.

segments.name: Healthcare / OTC Pharma
segments.commentary: Baddi site approved; commercial production started for 2 more multinational companies. Management expects Baddi to reach 100% utilisation within 6-12 months. Class III medical device certification started at Chennai.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore reaffirmed; management said it is too early to signal the lower end and will revisit in a couple of quarters.
Capacity commercialisation of more than INR500 crore expected in FY27 including carry-forward projects.
Management expects footwear to return to profitability in coming months and to pay off in H2 FY27.
Profit growth expected to outpace revenue growth because customers increasingly supply raw and packing material, so only conversion cost is booked as revenue.
Continued 1:1 debt-equity funding for projects; growth to rely on internal accruals with ROCE threshold of 18%.
capex_capacity: FY27 new project commitments of INR340 crore (INR190 crore newly authorised), plus INR150 crore carried forward from FY26.
Breakdown: Food & Beverages INR210 crore; Ice Cream INR80 crore (Panipat); Home & Personal Care INR50 crore (Lucknow).
Silvassa flood disruption from July rains: partially restored, fully operational by end-August; management says it is insured and has no material long-term impact.
Lucknow greenfield facility due for commissioning later in FY27; Silvassa brownfield to start in Q2 FY27.
Pipeline of inquiries about INR1,000 crore, not yet confirmed; policy is to announce capex only after signing.
demand_pricing: Footwear raw material prices rose ~50-60% (polymer, fabric) and freight rose up to 4x; footwear pricing is fixed 6-12 months ahead, so costs could not be passed through in Q1.
Haryana/NCR minimum wage hike of ~30% hit footwear and was described as a local, one-off issue; other contracts have pass-through clauses.
Footwear order book full for Q2 FY27 onward, with new domestic and multinational customer wins and some lapsed customers returning.
HPC demand has improved materially over the last three months per management, with liquid home care volumes growing near double digits.
US personal care order is on hold due to tariff ambiguity and freight; product development, trials and mould investment are complete.
Middle East export discussions (UAE, Saudi Arabia) put on hold; Dr. Scholl portfolio exported to UK, EU, Australia, NZ and Japan.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company negotiate better terms with customers given GST inversion and weakening competition, and is there any asset revaluation planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Sameer Kothari said GST inversion is not the main driver of outsourcing and that the company is better placed to handle it. Assets have not been revalued and the business model does not depend on it; the value sits on the balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Can footwear raw-material cost increases be built into contracts structurally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shoe contracts are set 6-8 months ahead with fixed prices, so mid-season changes are not industry practice. Brands have agreed to absorb some cost for the coming season, and pass-through is now being achieved.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the INR340 crore of new projects by segment.
qa_highlights.answer: Food & Beverages INR210 crore across five units, Ice Cream INR80 crore at Panipat, and HPC INR50 crore at Lucknow for a bar and liquid line.

qa_highlights.question: Footwear utilisation and order book quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 utilisation was poor; utilisation is about 80-90% from August with a full order book and new logos, with the business expected to pay off in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Footwear employee cost share and profit impact of INR210 crore beverage capex at 18% ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Footwear employee cost is about 35-40% of Q1 total. Beverage units are expected online by Dec/Jan on anchor-tenant basis; the analyst's ROCE maths was corrected to EBIT, with 1:1 debt-equity funding implying interest outflow.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block growth outlook over 3-5 years versus sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross block will grow faster than sales because customer-supplied raw material means only conversion cost is booked as revenue. It expects to fund growth from internal accruals at 1:1 leverage with an 18% ROCE threshold.

risks_watch: Footwear margin recovery depends on brands absorbing cost and on Middle East-driven material and freight costs easing; ~INR6 crore hit in Q1.
Silvassa restoration by end-August and insurance recovery; watch for any Q2 output shortfall.
Execution of INR500 crore capex this year, and whether Lucknow and Silvassa start on time.
US tariff ambiguity keeps personal care export orders on hold.
Management declined to give plant-level utilisation for shared sites; footwear ROCE is below the 18% threshold, per management.

540602|2026-09.headline: GTPL Hathway Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose 19% YoY to INR11,464 million, but reported EBITDA was flat at INR1,103 million (9.6% margin).
540602|2026-09.overview:
Consolidated total income grew 19% YoY and 12% QoQ, led by subscription revenue of INR3,455 million (up from INR3,024 million). Reported EBITDA was flat at INR1,103 million, with management attributing the gap to ACT acquisition synergies not yet realised and to forex and transponder costs. Consolidated PAT was about negative INR0.5 million after INR75 million of one-off-type impacts (INR45 million forex loss, INR30 million transponder amortisation). The company closed the ACT Group cable TV acquisition on September 15, 2026 for INR35.55 crore, adding roughly 6 lakh digital TV subscribers, and it appointed a new broadband CEO.</overview>
