segments.name: Digital TV (CATV)
segments.commentary: Digital cable TV base reached 11 million at September 30, 2026, with 1.5 million added in the quarter and 10.30 million paying subscribers; ACT contributed about 6 lakh of these. Business partner network is above 51,000.

segments.name: Broadband
segments.commentary: Active subscribers reached 1.07 million, up 10,000 QoQ; homepass stood at 6 million. ARPU was INR470 and average monthly data use was 436 GB per user (up 6% YoY).

segments.name: ACT Group cable business
segments.commentary: Acquired September 15, 2026 for INR35.55 crore cash across seven companies in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha and Karnataka. Current operating margin is about 12%, with a target of 25-26% after integration.

segments.name: DL GTPL Cabnet
segments.commentary: Company is acquiring the remaining 74% stake (INR83.25 million) having held 26%. It has about 1.5 lakh CATV subscribers in Gujarat, Maharashtra and parts of MP.

guidance_outlook: Operational EBITDA margin expected to rise 150-250 bps by end FY27 from the 20-21% level, as ACT synergies and HITS delivery-cost benefits come through.
Digital TV net additions of 1.8-1.9 million for FY27 (1.65 million added so far this year).
Double-digit subscription revenue growth expected in both digital TV and broadband.
Medium term: digital TV base of 13-14 million and broadband base near 1.2 million in about three years; subscriber growth of 7-8% a year.
All integration of ACT expected by end FY27; existing network migration to HITS expected by December or January.
capex_capacity: Entire broadband network migrated to GPON, now a full FTTH network, per management.
Seven new transponders added; INR30 million amortisation impact booked in standalone financials this quarter.
No incremental capex or opex so far from higher data consumption; management said future increases would need only about 10% of the proportional cost.

Over 60% of existing digital TV network already moved to HITS (Headend in the Sky, launched November 2025); full conversion targeted by December or January, after which cable-dark, rural and semi-urban expansion starts.
demand_pricing: Broadband homepass-to-paying conversion rose from 13-14% earlier to 17-18%, with a target of about 20%.

Broadband net adds were about 10,000 QoQ versus the historical 25,000-40,000 per quarter; management attributed the slowdown to the FTTH migration and cleanup over the past 1-1.5 years and expects a return to about 20,000+ per month.
ARPU rise attributed to existing subscribers moving to higher plans.
Management says it is at parity with telcos on pricing and sees competition as healthy.

qa_highlights.question: What changes are expected in ARPU and margins in ACT markets versus established markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ACT is accretive; it has about 1.25 lakh primary subscribers at higher ARPU, and synergies will come over the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did broadband net additions slow, and what is being done to revive them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the FTTH migration and cleanup over the last 1-1.5 years; it appointed Vivek Raina as broadband CEO three months ago, launched the TrueFiber brand, and targets 20,000+ monthly adds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ACT integration status and margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: ACT revenue is consolidated from September 15; current operating margin is about 12%, expected to reach 25-26% after integration into GTPL systems.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the digital TV subscriber growth came from ACT?
qa_highlights.answer: About 6 lakh of the 1.5 million quarterly additions came from ACT; management did not split the rest.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA not grow in line with revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said acquisition synergies are not fully realised; operating EBITDA was about 20-21% versus 22% last year, and PAT was hit by forex and transponder costs.

qa_highlights.question: What drives ARPU growth and what is the mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Subscribers are moving to higher plans, lifting broadband ARPU to INR470; management expects double-digit subscription growth in both businesses.

risks_watch: Operational EBITDA margin fell to 20% from 22%; the 150-250 bps recovery depends on ACT synergies and HITS delivery-cost savings landing by year end.
Broadband net adds of about 10,000 in Q2 are well below the historical 25,000-40,000 per quarter; the recovery target depends on a new CEO and a new brand still at an early stage.
Forex loss of INR45 million and transponder amortisation of INR30 million weigh on PAT; management called these notional and expects them to ease over time.
Digital TV industry is facing technology and delivery-medium change; management flagged it as increasingly challenging for FY28.
Several ACT and DL GTPL Cabnet integration milestones were not quantified; management gave no ACT revenue or EBITDA split.

505255|2026-06.headline: GMM Pfaudler Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR 925 crores, but EBITDA fell 7% YoY to INR 94 crores on pricing pressure and organisation-building costs.
505255|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16% YoY to INR 925 crores and PAT more than doubled to INR 22 crores, while EBITDA fell 7% YoY to INR 94 crores (up 25% QoQ). Order intake was flat YoY at INR 1,007 crores, and the order backlog reached a record INR 2,289 crores (+20% YoY, +4% QoQ). The company moved to four global technology divisions (CRT, PPT, HET, PST) and disclosed segment results for the first time. Management said debt reduction (about EUR 7 million by end-Q2) and refinancing are under way, with no numeric debt target given.

segments.name: CRT (Corrosion Resistance Technologies)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 466 crores (+10% YoY); order intake INR 502 crores (+23% YoY). Glass-lined pharma and chemical demand described as stable; large aftermarket and service base.

segments.name: PPT (Process Performance Technologies)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 255 crores (+23% YoY); order intake INR 367 crores (+64% YoY). Covers mixing, filtration, drying, and sealing; pharma and food & beverage adoption cited.

segments.name: HET (Heavy Engineering Technologies)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 74 crores (flat YoY); order intake INR 58 crores (up more than 700% YoY). India-led, oil and gas, petrochemicals, with nuclear and power entry and EIL approvals.

segments.name: PST (Process System Technologies)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 131 crores (+46% YoY); order intake INR 80 crores vs INR 363 crores in Q1 FY26, which included one large defence order. Skids and engineered systems for semiconductor, defence and pharma.

guidance_outlook: Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 15%, described as a minimum target; management said current verticals are roughly around this range, with no timeline given.
Management expects improvement YoY across all businesses but declined to give a specific margin number; quarter-on-quarter margin tracking was framed as the approach.
Debt: about EUR 7 million to be repaid by end of Q2 FY27; further reduction via refinancing over 12 to 18 months. No year-end debt target disclosed.
Tax rate: work with around 30%, possibly slightly lower in the long term, expected within 18 to 24 months after refinancing and entity restructuring.
Most of the Q1 order intake and backlog is in 10 to 12 month execution projects, expected to be largely executed in FY27.
Possible investor day around Q2 FY27 (management said 'hopefully').
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.
Global engineering centre (GEC) with about 12 people in place; Poland and India being developed as low-cost engineering hubs.
Workforce reductions in UK (prior year) and factory workforce in Germany (last year) expected to flow through to costs in coming quarters.
demand_pricing: India pharma improving, driven by CDMO and API investment in Hyderabad; glass-lined inquiries and conversion rates up vs 12 months ago. Management says Q1 and Q2 look strong for glass-lined.
Chemicals flat in India and remain challenging in Europe; no structural change seen.

International pharma improving in Europe and Americas; US has large glass-lined pharma orders; China back with glass-lined orders; Europe still slow overall though several large glass-lined orders won.
Peptide investment is a new pharma driver, with a large peptide order supplied last year and two large Hyderabad system orders.
Pricing pressure in a shifting business mix cited as a reason for lower YoY EBITDA. Management expects pricing to improve as markets recover.
Opening backlog for FY27 was about 30% higher than a year earlier, which was partly flattered by a large defence order (~EUR 30 million) in the prior-year base.

qa_highlights.question: Are there signs of recovery in chemical and pharma markets, and is competition easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Pharma is improving in India (Hyderabad CDMO), the US and Europe; chemicals remain flat. India traditional markets are better than 12 months ago.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India standalone margins decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from HET (lower-margin, longer-cycle project business); a mix shift plus investment in people for the new organisation. Management expects margins to recover over the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the target EBITDA margins and debt levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 15% EBITDA as the aspiration and said margins would be tracked quarter-on-quarter. It declined to give a year-end debt target.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book executes within 10 to 12 months, and what is the debt repayment schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Large majority of the roughly INR 1,000 crore Q1 intake is executable in 10 to 12 months. Debt repayment of EUR 7 million now, with a further reduction over 12 to 18 months; no amount was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state tax rate and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 30%, possibly slightly lower long term, achieved in 18 to 24 months after debt refinancing and entity rationalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is there severance cost in Q1, and will employee costs keep rising?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-off severance in Q1. Management aims to lower employee costs over time by shifting non-critical work to low-cost locations, though some sales hires will be added.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost and order intake outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Average interest cost of 6% to 7%, mostly hedged SOFR/EURIBOR-linked debt. Order intake is flat YoY but with a different profile, with most Q1 orders at 10 to 12 month cycles.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin recovery depends on three or four underperforming units; management did not give a timeline beyond 'a few quarters'.
Investment in people and organisation raises employee costs ahead of the revenue benefit.
Debt of about INR 835 crores (March 2026) with refinancing and entity clean-up (24 to 25 entities) still incomplete; tax rate depends on this.
Chemicals demand remains weak in India and Europe.
Q1 order intake was flat YoY and the prior-year base contained a large defence order, so the YoY comparison is not like-for-like.
Whether Q2 order intake is strong enough to sustain the backlog and build momentum.
505255|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on strategy and the new divisional structure, but cautious and often non-committal on numbers: no margin timeline, no debt target, and no tax timeline beyond 18 to 24 months. Management repeatedly asked for 'a few quarters' of consistent results before giving more detail.

544777|2026-06.headline: CMR Green Q1 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR3,122 crore and PAT 22% to INR68 crore, with EBITDA/kg at about INR12.40 but operating cash flow negative.
544777|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 65% YoY to INR3,122 crore, EBITDA rose 27% to INR139 crore and PAT rose 22% to over INR68 crore, with aluminium volumes up 25% YoY. Management stressed EBITDA per kg (about INR12.40) over percentage margin because aluminium is largely a pass-through. Operating cash flow was negative due to a roughly 40% rise in average realisation (from about INR226-230/kg to INR350/kg), which raised working capital; inventory days fell to 40 from 45 and the cash conversion cycle to 65 days from 69. Management kept INR12/kg EBITDA and 25% FY27 volume growth as internal targets, while the Odisha plant ramps up.

financial_highlights.change: slightly up; management says per-kg is the right measure
+25% YoY total sales volume; aluminium +32% YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Gross profit per kg (CFO's per-kg figure)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR26,000/ton in FY26 per management
cash flow hedge accounting entry, not a hedging cost per management

segments.name: Aluminium (recycled alloys/ingots and liquid metal)
segments.commentary: Aluminium volumes grew 32% YoY in Q1; liquid aluminium now exceeds 50% of aluminium sales, and management expects liquid metal growth to outpace ingot growth. Liquid metal margins are higher but management did not quantify the gap.

segments.name: Recycled billets and UBC
segments.commentary: Billets volume +149% YoY and UBC volume +333% YoY, both in ramp-up mode. Management cites construction, renewables, electrical and industrial demand beyond automotive.

segments.name: Non-ferrous (other metals) mix
segments.commentary: Aluminium to other non-ferrous sales mix held at about 80:20. FY26 volume mix was 66% automotive alloys, 10% non-automotive and 24% other metals; target rebalancing to 60:20:20 over the coming year.

guidance_outlook: Internal target of 25% volume growth in FY27, which management says is based on Tirupati and Odisha ramp-up, brownfield expansion and existing auto customers.
EBITDA guidance held at INR12/kg on a sustainable basis; management said it could do better but is not guiding above that.
Installed recycling capacity to exceed 7 lakh tons per annum by end FY27 (about 6.15 lakh tons currently), per management.
Expects to reach full utilisation at the Odisha (Hindalco) plant within FY27; current run-rate about 6,000 tons for the quarter, targeting about 4,000 tons a month.
Expects to return to positive operating cash flow once aluminium prices stabilise; debt to fall as inventory days and working capital cycle reduce.
Plans to bring debt-equity back toward its historical 0.5 ratio; currently about 0.86.
capex_capacity: INR53 crore invested in the quarter in greenfield projects at Shoolagiri and Bawal, with brownfield and technology projects at Tirupati and other locations progressing as planned.
Odisha plant (48,000 tpa capacity, built for Hindalco) is ramping up.
Capacity utilisation is about 65%; traditional range of 70-75%.
Hindustan Zinc: MoU signed, nothing definitive, and no construction started; management says it will take a while.
demand_pricing: Passenger vehicle and two-wheeler sales grew about 26% and 20% YoY in Q1 FY27; EV penetration was 8.26% of registrations in FY26. Ather Energy is a new customer.
Auto customers are on cost-plus pricing; management says hedging is used to manage the balance on the un-passed-through portion.
Exports were about 3.4% of FY26 turnover, focused on niche products to Japan, Europe, Southeast Asia and some China.
Management says volumes are independent of aluminium price movements; scrap availability is not price-dependent.
Management says scrap sourcing is getting harder as some countries restrict scrap exports; the company is widening its sourcing base and buying more domestically.

Regulatory tailwinds: proposed EPR framework to lift minimum recycled aluminium content from 5% in FY28 to 10% over time; EU CBAM cited; India's aluminium extrusion industry expected to grow at 12% CAGR through FY29.
Recycled aluminium is about 40% of India's aluminium consumption, growing about 13% a year versus about 7-8% for primary, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How does hedging work for secondary aluminium given peers say it cannot be hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said secondary prices follow primary with a lag and auto customers pay cost-plus, so part of exposure is left to cost-plus pricing and part is hedged on LME. The CFO added that operating cash flow is negative because average realisation rose about 40%, from INR226-230/kg to INR350/kg.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 20% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR36 crore was loaded for a cash flow hedge entry under accounting standards, not a hedging cost; other expenses were broadly flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow turn positive and what will debt be by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects positive operating cash flow once prices stabilise. The CFO said D/E is about 0.86 against a historical 0.5 target, which should fall as prices stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Why does reported EBITDA differ from the earlier presentation for Q4 and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company reclassified foreign exchange gains and the ineffective portion of commodity hedging from other income into EBITDA as they are operating in nature, though accounting standards require other-income classification.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% FY27 volume growth still on track after Q1 aluminium volume growth of about 8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 25% is an internal target, not guidance; Q1 volume grew 25%, and growth is expected from the Tirupati and Odisha plants and existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Do GP and EBITDA per kg move with utilisation, and how should hedging costs be treated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management held INR12/kg EBITDA as guidance despite utilisation of about 65% versus 70-75% historical. It said hedging costs are minimal (broker and LME fees) and that hedging works against physical profit or loss.

532782|2026-06.headline: Sutlej Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose to INR47.2 crore (6.7% margin) from INR5 crore, with PBT of INR4.2 crore versus a loss a year ago.
532782|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income rose 17% YoY to INR704 crore, marginally ahead of Q4 FY26. Gross margin expanded about 370 bps to 46.8%, with raw material cost falling to 53.2% of revenue from 56.9%. EBITDA margin has now expanded for five consecutive quarters (0.8%, 2.7%, 3.9%, 5.3%, 6.7%). Management said the quarter was clean with no exceptional items and that all three business clusters and six manufacturing units delivered positive EBITDA. Value-added yarn share is still only about 10-15% against a 30-35% target.

financial_highlights.change: +17% YoY; marginally ahead of Q4 FY26
from 17.7% a year ago; includes annual wage revision
vs INR5 crore (0.8%) in Q1 FY26 and 5.3% in Q4 FY26
vs INR17 crore in Q4 FY26
vs loss of INR38.6 crore in Q1 FY26; no exceptional items (FY26 had INR22.5 crore)
vs loss of INR25.7 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Segment revenue INR640 crore, up 16% YoY; segment EBITDA INR34.4 crore vs INR6.5 crore a year ago. Management attributes about 60% of the 2.5% raw-material-to-sales improvement to moving up product categories and the balance to operational efficiency.

segments.name: Sutlej Green Fibre (recycled PET)
segments.commentary: Gross sales roughly INR400 crore; about 70-75% is consumed internally by the group's own units. Management is adding performance properties to recycled polyester and discussing collaborations with brands.

segments.name: Home textiles
segments.commentary: Revenue up 22% YoY and profitability held versus a loss a year ago. Sequentially softer on order phasing, not demand. Management targets doubling the business in about two years.

guidance_outlook: No formal quarterly guidance. Management said it will maintain or better Q1 numbers in Q2 and Q3, but declined to give a clear outlook.
Long-term aim is a double-digit EBITDA margin, described as the near-term benchmark; no timeline was given.
Finance cost in absolute terms expected to rise to about INR75 crore this year from about INR67 crore last year, due to capex, even though the cost-of-borrowing percentage is down about 40 bps.
Rationalization programme is not complete; remaining cost benefits expected through the balance of FY27.
Employee cost expected to decline in coming quarters, per management, with no quantified target.
Southeast Asia and Latin America market entries are expected this financial year.
Technical textiles (Protech) and protective textiles are expected to contribute in FY28, not FY27.
capex_capacity: Capex is mainly upgrading existing assets rather than new capacity; funded from internal accruals and existing facilities with no additional equity, per management.
Maintenance capex is proceeding as planned.
Protech technical textiles has moved from qualification into sampling and trials; some protective textile products have qualified.
Home textile growth plans are underway, with the business in investment mode for technical and protective textiles.
demand_pricing: Global demand described as relatively stable; management said legacy yarn makers benefited from China-driven demand in cotton-grade yarn, which Sutlej does not directly target.

Export markets: Far East and Africa, opened last year, have moved from trial volumes to repeat orders. Core markets Latin America and Europe are steady; Bangladesh demand is stable but below levels of two years ago. Exports go to about 60 destinations.
Customers are rebuilding inventories cautiously from very low levels.

Raw material outlook: cotton expected flat to slightly higher, with parity emerging between international and Indian prices; polyester/synthetics expected to ease over the long term, but a return to pre-war levels is uncertain.
Cotton is about 30% of fibre consumption by quantity; synthetics about 70%, of which about 30% of the total is recycled.
Value-added yarn is about 10-15% of yarn products against a 30-35% target. Customer trials take 3-6 months, and first containers of new specialty SKUs have shipped for testing.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the yarn portfolio is value-added now, and what EBITDA margin can the business reach at 30-35% value-added?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added share is about 10-15% of yarn products, with a pipeline and new SKUs under customer evaluation. Management would not give a margin number for the steady state but said double-digit EBITDA is the minimum target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the yarn EBITDA gain came from spread expansion versus mix and integration?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60% of the raw material-to-sales improvement (about 2.5 percentage points) came from moving up product categories; the rest came from operational efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost (15-17% of revenue) so far above peers, and will it fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ratio is not at target and will fall in coming quarters. It attributed the gap to melange and dyeing layers, job processing in home textiles, and low realisations, and said absolute costs have not risen.

qa_highlights.question: What will the interest outflow be this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost is expected to rise to about INR75 crore from about INR67 crore last year, because of capex, even though the cost-of-borrowing percentage is down about 40 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scale and EBITDA potential of Green Fibre and home textiles?
qa_highlights.answer: Green Fibre gross sales are about INR400 crore, of which 70-75% is consumed internally. Home textiles are to be doubled in about two years, with no margin target given.

qa_highlights.question: How will debt be structured, and how do raw material prices affect working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital borrowing will rise for the same number of days because of higher raw material prices. Long-term debt is mainly for capex, which is secured. Credit lines will be rebalanced as results move.

qa_highlights.question: Is there Q2 and Q3 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific guidance. Management said it will try to maintain or better the Q1 numbers.

543324|2026-06.headline: Gretex Q1 FY27 call gave no financial figures; management cited 3 new advisory mandates and guided to 3-4 IPO listings in the current quarter.
543324|2026-06.overview: Management (MD and CFO Alok Harlalka, WTD Arvind Harlalka) described a weak primary market in Q1 FY27, with 53 issues mobilising about INR 6,895 crores, of which 8 mainboard IPOs raised about INR 5,000 crores. The company reported 3 new advisory mandates, a listing mandate with a West Bengal ferroalloy company, and a DRHP filing for Sky Alloys and Power Limited. Bahutex received registration for a Category-II AIF with Gretex as a partner. The call contained no revenue, profit, or segment financials, and no quantified guidance.

segments.name: Merchant banking / advisory
segments.commentary: Signed 3 new advisory mandates in the quarter, secured a listing mandate with a West Bengal-based ferroalloy company, and filed DRHP for Sky Alloys and Power Limited on NSE and BSE.

segments.name: Broking and market-making (Gretex Share Broking Ltd)
segments.commentary: Subsidiary is preparing for a proposed listing; management called its contribution this quarter strong but gave no figures.

segments.name: Alternative investments
segments.commentary: Bahutex received registration for a Category-II AIF during the quarter, with Gretex as a partner in the fund.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a minimum of 3 to 4 IPO listings in the current quarter (Q2 FY27).
Management said it will build scale across merchant banking and broking in a measured and sustainable manner, with no quantified targets.
Management said the operating environment remains favourable, but gave no numerical outlook.
demand_pricing: Indian primary market in Q1 FY27: 53 issues mobilised about INR 6,895 crores; 8 mainboard IPOs raised about INR 5,000 crores and SME platform issues made up the balance across 45 issues.
Mainboard activity slowed sharply from FY26, when 108 mainboard companies raised over INR 1.76 lakh crores.
Secondary market liquidity described as stable, which management said supports broking and market-making.
Growing interest in mutual funds, PMS and alternative investment platforms noted; geopolitical uncertainty cited as a headwind.

qa_highlights.question: How many IPOs can be expected in the coming quarter? (submitted via chat)
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a minimum of 3 to 4 IPO listings in the current quarter.

risks_watch: No revenue, PAT or segment numbers were disclosed on the call; the results document must be checked for these.
Mainboard IPO activity has decelerated sharply from FY26 levels, and geopolitical volatility persists.
Timing of the Gretex Share Broking Ltd listing is not specified.
Whether the Sky Alloys and Power DRHP and the 3-4 expected IPO listings convert into fee income this quarter is unclear.
Management did not quantify the contribution of the Bahutex AIF partnership.
543324|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the long-term outlook and origination pipeline, but vague on numbers: the call gave no financials and used qualitative terms such as 'measured' and 'favourable'. Management acknowledged the sharp slowdown in mainboard IPO activity without quantifying Gretex's exposure to it.
key_quotes: we remain confident in the long-term growth prospects of the Indian capital markets, and these structural trends remain well aligned with Gretex's integrated business model.
for the current quarter which is going on, we expect a minimum of 3 to 4 IPO listings should happen.

532522|2026-06.headline: Petronet Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 33% to INR 1,133 crore despite company LNG volumes falling to 207 TBTU, aided by trading and inventory gains.
532522|2026-06.overview:
Standalone PBT rose 33% YoY to INR 1,514 crore and PAT to INR 1,133 crore, with consolidated PBT of INR 1,491 crore described as the highest ever Q1. Volumes fell: company LNG processed was 207 TBTU versus 220 TBTU a year earlier, and company utilisation was 58% versus 76%. Management attributed the profit resilience to trading gains of INR 301 crore and inventory gains of INR 193 crore, as Qatar supplies remained under force majeure and tolling cargoes from other sources replaced most of the gap. Dahej's nameplate capacity was raised from 17.5 to 22.5 MMTPA on 31 March 2026, which lowers reported utilisation.</overview>

segments.name: Dahej terminal
segments.commentary: Processed 192 TBTU in Q1 FY27 versus 207 TBTU a year ago and 201 TBTU in Q4; utilisation 66% on 22.5 MMTPA expanded capacity (65.6% per call) versus 92% a year ago.

segments.name: Kochi terminal
segments.commentary: Utilisation 23.27% in Q1 FY27 as stated on the call; pipeline connectivity expected to be mechanically complete by end of the quarter.

segments.name: Company overall
segments.commentary: Processed 207 TBTU (vs 220 TBTU YoY, 219 TBTU QoQ); utilisation 58% vs 76% in both prior periods.

guidance_outlook: Capex budgeted at INR 9,064 crore for FY27, with similar levels expected for FY28.
Utilisation expected to improve slightly: April was low, May and June ran at the rate that continues into the quarter, and recovery depends on reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
Contract talks with offtakers on tariffs or renewal expected to close in the next 2 to 3 quarters; no tariff revision discussion currently.
New Qatar contract to start in 2028; it will be on DES basis, with a formula-driven price that includes shipping.
Petchem project is on schedule, about 40% complete on physical progress; propane contract signing expected in 2027.
capex_capacity: Dahej nameplate capacity increased from 17.5 MMTPA to 22.5 MMTPA on 31 March 2026; Dahej utilisation 66% on the expanded base.
Kochi utilisation 23.27% in Q1; Kochi pipeline connectivity expected to be mechanically complete by end of Q1 FY27 (end-June quarter per management).
Petchem project about 40% complete physically; capex INR 472 crore in the quarter, cumulative INR 679 crore.
FY27 capex budget INR 9,064 crore; FY28 expected at a similar level.
Petchem: 600 KTPA ethane handling contract and a Deepak Phenolics contract signed; equity IRR not disclosed for now as commercial contracts are still being finalised.
demand_pricing: Term volumes fell sharply; third-party regas and tolling volumes filled the gap, and management said more than two-thirds of the missing Middle East volume is being replaced by these customers.
Qatar force majeure is declared month by month, and was declared for end-August at the time of the call; offtakers are booking volumes on a month-to-month basis.
Spot trading was small (about 6 TBTU in the quarter per management), yet produced material trading gains when spot prices were well above long-term prices.
Deepak Fertilizers contract (about 0.5 MTPA expected at Dahej) began May 2026 with 2 cargoes brought so far; ExxonMobil volume increase at Kochi also started.
Tariffs at Dahej around INR 69 and at Kochi around INR 98 for the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Has the term-versus-third-party volume mix persisted into Q2, and should it hold until the Gulf conflict resolves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pattern continued into Q2 so far; it hopes Qatar volumes resume soon.

qa_highlights.question: Where did the margin improvement come from; is there an inventory gain and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Trading gains INR 301 crore and inventory gains INR 193 crore; management described trading gains during spot-price spikes as the established business model over the past 5-6 years, without committing to a Q2 figure.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation by terminal and the FY27/FY28 trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahej 65.6%, Kochi 23.27%; recovery depends on Hormuz reopening, and May-June run-rate is slightly better than April.

qa_highlights.question: Use-or-pay treatment of tolling cargoes?
qa_highlights.answer: Tolling cargoes from non-GAIL offtakers can offset use-or-pay after current-year commitments are met; GAIL has no use-or-pay, and the long-term take-or-pay contract is separate.

qa_highlights.question: Ind AS impacts for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin impact positive INR 14 crore, forex loss INR 5 crore, other expenses positive INR 8 crore, depreciation INR 66 crore, finance cost INR 48 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Are time-charter vessel costs being paid during force majeure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said time-charter vessel operations have been suspended under clauses other than force majeure, so charter costs are not being paid.

risks_watch: Strait of Hormuz closure and Qatar supply: no timing given; FM declared month-to-month.
Dependence on spot-price spreads for trading and inventory gains, which management did not say would persist into Q2.
Utilisation at Dahej (66%) and company level (58%) against the enlarged capacity base.
Tariff renewal with offtakers, expected in 2 to 3 quarters.
Petchem project economics: IRR not disclosed; commercial contracts still pending.
Ongoing time-charter cost treatment and the contracted vessel fleet after DES shift.
532522|2026-06.management_tone: ["Confident on earnings resilience and the trading business model, with the Q1 PAT and PBT growth framed as a strong start.","Cautious and non-committal on volumes: Hormuz timing is unknown, and management repeatedly said recovery depends on geopolitics. Evasive on petchem IRR and the Q2 margin outlook."]
key_quotes: Overall, I would say it has been a strong start to the year, while volumes were somewhat lower, we have delivered a healthy financial performance supported by commercial and operational efficiencies.
Inventory gains are at INR193 crores and trading gains are at INR301 crores.

517206|2026-06.headline: Lumax Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32.6% y-o-y to INR 1,223 crore, with EBITDA margin flat at 9.2% as commodity recoveries slipped into Q2.
517206|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 32.6% y-o-y to INR 1,223 crore and EBITDA rose 34% to INR 113 crore, with margin held at 9.2%, in line with Q1 FY26. PAT including associates rose 41.2% to INR 51 crore, at a 4.2% margin. Management said OEM price recoveries for West Asia-driven commodity and electronics costs were not realised in Q1 (about 150 bps margin drag) and are expected in Q2. FY27 capex guidance was raised to INR 200-250 crore from INR 100-150 crore on new order wins.

financial_highlights.change: +34% y-o-y (vs INR 85 crore in Q1 FY26); margin flat y-o-y
+41.2% y-o-y (vs INR 36 crore); margin +30 bps y-o-y

segments.name: Passenger Vehicles
segments.commentary: 64% of Q1 revenue. Tata Motors Tiago headlamps and VW Taigun rear lamps launched during the quarter.

segments.name: 2 and 3-Wheelers
segments.commentary: 31% of Q1 revenue. Won Suzuki Burgman Street front turn signal orders; management said 2-Wheeler growth at HMSI is expected to be significant.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles and others
segments.commentary: 5% of Q1 revenue, unchanged y-o-y per management; won Force Motors Traveller 2 headlamp orders. The 'others' category grew 133% y-o-y, mainly Skoda/VW from Chakan 3.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Front lighting 68% of revenue, rear lighting 23%, other products 9%.

segments.name: Customers
segments.commentary: Maruti revenue +43% y-o-y and Tata Motors +68% y-o-y, both driven by new-model SOPs. TVS also grew; Hero share declined y-o-y per analyst.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 10.5-11% maintained; Q2 margin expected to be above 10%, with Q1 recoveries expected to be realised in Q2.
FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% (full year), with growth slowing in H2 on high base after GST rationalisation.
Medium term: 15-20% revenue CAGR over 3-5 years, targeting about INR 9,000 crore+ revenue by FY30-31 from INR 4,500-5,000 crore base; EBITDA of about 13% in 3-4 years.
FY27 capex raised to INR 200-250 crore (from INR 100-150 crore); maintenance capex INR 40-50 crore. FY28 capex indicated at INR 150-200 crore, but management called it premature.
FY27 mould sales targeted at INR 250-300 crore vs INR 180-185 crore in FY26, mostly in H2 (Q3/Q4) depending on SOP timelines.
Order book about INR 2,500 crore (about 90% LED); about 60% (roughly INR 1,500 crore) to enter SOP in FY28. Maruti wallet share expected to rise from under 30% to 35-40%.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex raised to INR 200-250 crore from INR 100-150 crore, driven by order wins over the last four months; FY26 capex was INR 410 crore.
Bengaluru plant expansion for Maruti and Toyota models is on track, with commissioning from Q4 FY27.
Brownfield projects underway at Sanand and Bawal to support new order wins at those locations.
Localisation: SMT already 100% localised; bare PCB localisation expected to rise from 40-50% to 70-80% and connectors from about 24% to 40-50% over 2-3 years; projected gain of 70-90 bps.
demand_pricing: Industry Q1 production per SIAM: total 93.5 lakh units (+22% y-o-y); PV +17%, 2W +23%, 3W +39%, CV +15%.

Commodity recoveries: OEMs have not agreed to monthly amendments for most of the industry (only aluminium accepted); still quarterly or six-monthly. About 150 bps Q1 margin impact from unrealised recoveries.
Management expects competition intensity to rise as new players enter, but says top OEM concentration (4-5 players, 80-90% share) limits new entrants' share.
Content per vehicle for a passenger car currently INR 15,000-20,000 (outliers up to INR 30,000); management expects at least 50% growth over 4-5 years.
Honda HVAC business was about INR 18-20 crore annualised vs an estimated peak of INR 35-40 crore; Honda volumes weaker than expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin still below 10% despite LED penetration and localisation, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Anmol Jain said OEMs have not agreed to monthly price amendments, so recoveries slipped; margin was hit about 150 bps in Q1. Realisations expected in Q2 could lift margin to about 10.5-11%, in line with FY27 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why are CV and tractor orders not yet visible, and how is the company positioned on EV content?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Jain said CV lighting tech is standardised and the company is in talks on new platforms. Anmol Jain said CV is about 5% of revenue and grew 30-35% annualised. Lighting is powertrain-agnostic; EV content is higher in value per vehicle. 12% of order book is EV.

qa_highlights.question: Why did M&M revenue stay flat when the company holds a 40-50% wallet share?
qa_highlights.answer: Anmol Jain said the XUV700 EV platform, where Lumax is not present, drove Mahindra volumes; management expects full-year growth in line with Mahindra.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mould revenue outlook and FY27 capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Mould sales are targeted at INR 250-300 crore (vs INR 180-185 crore), mostly in Q3/Q4. Maintenance capex is INR 40-50 crore; the rest goes to new business and capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins expand 50-100 bps a year, and can 30% growth continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed about 100 bps expansion in FY27 (9.8% in FY26 to 10.5-11%). It said 30%+ quarterly growth will not persist due to high base; full-year growth guided at 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the localisation plans and tooling sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Jain said localisation is a priority but not all in-house; tooling remains imported, with tool localisation possibly by 2030. China sourcing continues for cost, with a new China office set up.

532906|2026-06.headline: Maan Aluminium Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR232 crore and EBITDA to INR7 crore, with margin near 3%.
532906|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations was INR232 crore, up 10% YoY from INR211 crore but down from INR255 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA rose to INR7 crore from INR5 crore sequentially, with margin about 3% versus about 2%, and PAT was about INR3 crore (EPS INR0.52 vs INR0.29). Management said exports fell to about 45% of manufacturing revenue (from 60-70% earlier) due to duties, and freight and Middle East shipping disruption continue to weigh on volumes and costs. Capex of about INR166 crore over three years is planned, with Dewas precision tubing and Pithampur Italian press ramp-up the key near-term items.</overview>

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Q1 manufacturing turnover above INR70 crore with about 40% exports (management also cited ~45% export share of manufacturing revenue in prepared remarks). Production about 1,558 MT against 24,000 MT extrusion capacity. Anodizing utilisation ~45-50% and machining ~55%.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Described as opportunistic and pass-through; the remainder of the INR232 crore revenue (about INR160 crore implied) comes from trading. Management expects trading to decline as manufacturing mix rises.

guidance_outlook: Volumes expected to stay flattish QoQ and for FY27; ramp-up possibly toward end of FY27 or start of FY28.
Manufacturing revenue guided flattish; management would be 'okay' with FY26 level of ~INR300 crore manufacturing top line.
Pithampur Italian press: management targets ~35%/50%/75% ramp in a three-year plan; currently ~25% ramp-up; significant contribution expected by mid-FY28.
Dewas aluminium precision tubing plant: online targeted within 6-8 months, before mid-FY28 (no firm date given); capex mostly in H2 FY27.
Recovery of gas/energy cost increases: about 50% passed to customers over last two quarters, balance expected to be recovered in one to two quarters as contracts renew.
Management said no new debt planned for capex; company is deleveraging and has sufficient cash. Employee expenses expected not to rise materially as technical team is already hired.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity: foundry 12,000 TPA; extrusion 24,000 TPA; anodizing 3,600 TPA; machining 1,400 TPA.
Three-year capex plan of ~INR166 crore cumulative, including Pithampur, new dials and general capex, and new plants under development; ~INR90 crore allocated to new plants.
Dewas precision tubing project: total capex ~INR45 crore, of which ~INR15-20 crore spent to date; aimed at aerospace, defence and automotive; expected asset turn at least 2-3x at peak utilisation.
Capex spend in Q1 FY27 was less than INR5 crore; overseas visit planned to finalise extrusion press and other machinery for Dewas; majority of capex in H2 FY27.
Pithampur capacity was expanded from 1,200 MT to 12,000-24,000 MT near end of last year; Italian press now online.
demand_pricing: Export share has dropped from around 60-70% to about 45% (about 40% in Q1 per call Q&A) because of duties hitting the export business; management aims to shift volume to domestic high-value business, which is slow to convert.
Freight rates up 5-10x on Strait of Hormuz and Middle East disruption; customers in GCC and East Asia holding back orders; delays and backed-up shipping persist.
Conversion margins: plain extrusion 6-10% (management cited 6-8% and 6-10%); value-added processing (powder coating, machining, anodizing) targeted at 15%+.
Commodity exposure: most manufacturing volumes hedged via LME/MCX on order basis; unhedged positions kept under 5%; management says commodity moves impact margins by less than 5%.

Trading is a pass-through business at metal prices; management said EBITDA per ton is reported on a blended basis only, with manufacturing EBITDA per ton not readily available (last quarter's USD340/ton reference not updated).

qa_highlights.question: What was the capacity volume this quarter and EBITDA per ton (last quarter USD340/t)?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA is reported only on a blended basis; manufacturing per-ton figure not available. Total extrusion production was about 1,558 MT in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any ramp-up in volumes sooner than expected?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management reiterated flattish volumes, with any ramp-up toward end FY27 or early FY28. The export loss from duties is being replaced by slow-converting domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: How are aluminium prices hedged and how do margins change with value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging is order-linked on LME/MCX, with under 5% unhedged; plain extrusion margins are 6-10%, rising to 15%+ with value addition. Management said absolute EBITDA per ton is the right metric for conversion.

qa_highlights.question: Dewas project status, timing and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR15-20 crore of INR45 crore spent; online targeted within 6-8 months, before mid-FY28, with no firm date. Asset turn at least 2-3x; no margin figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company take on debt for capex, and how will employee costs move?
qa_highlights.answer: No debt planned; management said the company is deleveraging. Employee costs are not expected to rise materially as the technical team is already on payroll.

qa_highlights.question: How has other expenses fallen and how are energy costs being recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses fell from INR18 crore to INR13 crore over four quarters. About 50% of the gas cost increase was passed to customers, with the rest to follow as contracts renew.

505010|2026-06.headline: Automotive Axles Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin rose to 13.6% (from 12.4% QoQ) on revenue of Rs 5,168 mn and PAT of Rs 455 mn.
505010|2026-06.overview:
Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 5,168 million, EBITDA of Rs 702 million (about 13.6%), and profit for the year of Rs 455 million (about 8.7%, EPS about Rs 30). Management described EBITDA as one of the highest margins the company has achieved, helped by mix, a one-off, and lower employee costs versus the high-volume Q4. Management now sees the FY27 M&HCV industry down 5-10% versus last year, against an earlier 15-20% decline assumption, with Q4 expected to be a peak quarter. Capacity expansion (Phase-1 and Phase-1(a)) is about 40% complete.</overview>

segments.name: M&HCV on-highway axles (India)
segments.commentary: Management says demand is driven by replacement cycle and the shift from 6x2 to 10x2 or 4x2 tractor-trailers; heavy-duty (40 t and above) is the core focus. Overlap with American Axle described as minimal.

segments.name: Exports (to Meritor/CDBS global plants)
segments.commentary: Exports were about 13% of the quarter's revenue, versus a traditional 8-12% range; management guides to 8-12% for the year, with sea freight the main logistics challenge.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Defence contributes about 5-10% of revenue depending on tender timing; long gestation of 3-10 years from RFQ to SOP.

segments.name: Bus axles and new products
segments.commentary: Low-floor bus axle launch is still in validation, and is being reworked for upcoming pass-by noise norms. A 160 tandem axle is entering production with a large customer.

guidance_outlook: Management's FY27 industry view is a 5-10% decline versus last year (about 480,000 M&HCV units), against an earlier 15-20% decline assumption; best case is flat with last year.
Q2 expected to be reasonable, Q3 to see increasing demand, and Q4 to be another peak quarter, subject to geopolitical and monsoon risks.
Management guides to a steady-state PAT margin of 7.5-8.5% for the coming quarters and frames it as an overall band.
Capacity additions of roughly 25-30% are planned to cover the next two to three years of market growth, with Phase-1 and Phase-1(a) about 40% complete.
Management says it will not give specific volume guidance but expects better conversion and margins if volumes exceed the prior year.
capex_capacity: Phase-1 and Phase-1(a) of the capex programme are about 40% complete, with some production started.
Capacity improvement of roughly 25-30% is planned, depending on product mix (called a Rs 120 crore programme by the analyst).
Capex is aimed at upgrading or replacing lines with more automated equipment, to cover peak-month volumes and export opportunities.
A furnace was electrified, which helped production despite lower LPG availability.
Management says capacity must also be matched by supply chain readiness.
demand_pricing: Q1 M&HCV industry volume was about 110,000 units, down about 30% QoQ from the Q4 peak but among the highest Q1s in several years.
Steel and other commodity cost increases are fully passed through to customers on a back-to-back basis.
Conversion cost increases (LPG, tooling, consumables) were absorbed in Q1 with price negotiations ongoing with customers.
Management says the delayed monsoon is supporting freight and replacement demand.
Management says share of business with Ashok Leyland was maintained; the company confirmed it is a single source for some new products, with dual sourcing common at OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex breakup and growth versus replacement components of the Rs 120 crore programme?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the split is hard to separate. Capex is for upgrades, automation and capacity for the next 2-3 years, roughly 25-30% capacity improvement.

qa_highlights.question: How are exports and OEM opportunities split between Automotive Axles and American Axle (Bharat Forge)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two are competitors, that it cannot comment on the competitor's plans, and that exports go mainly to CDBS global entities.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company lost market share at Ashok Leyland?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a loss of share; the gap reflects product mix and seasonal/segment shifts. Confirmed Ashok Leyland share was maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How was the cost of steel and gas handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel and other commodities are passed through fully. Conversion cost increases were absorbed in Q1 with recovery from customers being negotiated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised industry outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry down 5-10% versus the earlier 15-20%; best case is flat with last year, Q4 a peak quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the regulatory outlook for bus axles and new product launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Bus axle product launch is in validation and is being reworked for pass-by noise regulations; a 160 tandem axle is entering production.

risks_watch: Geopolitical tension and freight/LPG cost increases, with conversion cost recovery from customers still under negotiation.
Monsoon timing: a weak monsoon could push the industry toward the lower end of the 5-10% decline.
Pass-by noise and HPFE Phase-1B regulations could require design iteration and delay bus axle launch.
Competitive overlap with American Axle (now Bharat Forge-owned) in larger truck axles.
Sea freight rate volatility affecting export logistics.
Defence revenue lumpy with tender timing (5-10% of revenue).
505010|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on Q1 margins and on the Q4 peak outlook, but cautious on FY27 volumes, with several answers deflecting share-of-business and competitor questions. Management avoided quantitative volume guidance and framed the margin range loosely.
key_quotes: If I can recall, this is probably one of the highest EBITDA percentage we ever achieved.
Overall, the EBITDA stood at Rs. 702 million, which is at about 13.6%.
We do see minimum impact on our product lines because of those recent changes.
Otherwise, in this industry, if you don't put the capacity, you cannot even go after any potential new opportunities.

532395|2026-06.headline: Axiscades Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 42% YoY to ₹346 crore, but reported PAT loss of ₹14.8 crore; normalized PAT ₹20.2 crore.
532395|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first quarter of the divestment-led transition: Engineering Services is shown as discontinued operations (₹163 crore revenue), leaving continuing operations at ₹183 crore, up 94% YoY. Reported EBITDA for the combined business was ₹27.9 crore, with one-offs of ₹13.1 crore (including ₹9.62 crore receivable provision on an aged defence transaction and ₹3.5 crore hedge provision) and ₹21.81 crore divestment transaction cost below EBITDA. Management says normalized EBITDA was ₹41 crore (11.8% margin) and normalized PAT ₹20.2 crore. Guidance was reaffirmed: FY27 continuing revenue of ₹1,377 crore, EBITDA of ₹270 crore and PAT of about 50% of that, with acquisitions and divestment proceeds central to delivery.

financial_highlights.value: ₹183 crore (₹180.7 crore cited in Q&A segment overview)

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹20.9 crore PAT in Q1 FY26
mainly ADD Solutions (EBITDA -₹4.8 crore, PAT -₹6.7 crore)

segments.name: Defence (continuing)
segments.commentary: Record ₹125 crore revenue, up 112% YoY, with underlying EBITDA of ₹13 crore (up 15% YoY). Reported EBITDA ₹2.6 crore after ~₹9.6 crore one-time costs; management cites underlying 9.7% margin. Assured forecast visibility ₹4,557 crore after 8 wins since April.

segments.name: XiDA (ex-ESAI, US-headquartered)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹49.5 crore, up 63% YoY, at ~33% EBITDA margin (EBITDA ₹14.7 crore cited, ~30% in another remark). Added two large global technology customers via a business transfer.

segments.name: Aerospace manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹6.1 crore in Q1 with negative EBITDA; 30-member leadership team built ahead of acquisitions.

segments.name: Mistral
segments.commentary: Delivered ₹122 crore revenue at ~14.5% EBITDA margin while absorbing its own provisions.

segments.name: ADD Solutions (non-core, European)
segments.commentary: EBITDA loss ₹4.8 crore and PAT loss ₹6.7 crore; exit targeted by Q4 FY27 with a sale process that could realize over FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 continuing operations revenue guidance reaffirmed at ₹1,377 crore on an annualized pro forma basis.
FY27 EBITDA target of ₹270 crore; PAT expected at roughly 50% of EBITDA (~₹135 crore), could be higher with lower interest after debt paydown.
Defence revenue expected to grow over 75% YoY in FY27 and over the following years; ESAI/XiDA expected to grow over 100% this year.

Power 930 targets (FY30 PAT of ₹960 crore) stated as unchanged.

LUH Maritime order visibility of ₹150-170 crore this year, stated as backed by confirmed orders.
MBDA test bench programme: about 5 test benches per year for 3 years; launcher maintenance expanding with a Rafale-linked order.

BrahMos NG seeker: prototype in advanced stage; seeker business expected from next financial year (FY28).

531768|2026-06.headline: Poly Medicure Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 30.3% to INR525 crore (12.4% organic), with consolidated EBITDA margin at 24.1% and standalone at 28%.
531768|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 30.3% to INR525 crore, of which INR72.3 crore came from acquisitions, leaving organic growth at 12.4% to INR453.1 crore. Standalone revenue rose 12.3% to INR431 crore and standalone EBITDA was INR120.8 crore (28% margin), above the 25-27% FY27 guidance, helped by price hikes and inventory gains. Middle East sales fell 32% due to West Asia logistics disruption, while renal degrew 3.8% amid Chinese pricing pressure. Management maintained FY27 guidance and launched a "PolyMed 3.0" target to double revenue by FY30.

financial_highlights.change: +12.3% YoY; domestic INR146 crore (+16.2%), international INR281.8 crore (+10%)
Flagged as above historic 68-69% trend; partly price hikes and inventory gain
From INR2.9 crore a year ago, led by PendraCare plus domestic scale-up

financial_highlights.value: Standalone working capital debt about INR250 crore (revolver); Citieffe loan about EUR 9 million, EUR 1.5-2 million repaid annually

segments.name: Infusion therapy
segments.commentary: Revenue INR259.2 crore, +11.1%, led by domestic growth of 20%+ from higher value-added products and price increases.

segments.name: Orthopedics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR49.2 crore, largely reflecting consolidation of Citieffe.

segments.name: Cardiology
segments.commentary: Revenue INR28.6 crore versus INR2.9 crore a year ago, driven by PendraCare acquisition and domestic scale-up.

segments.name: Renal
segments.commentary: Revenue INR43.2 crore, -3.8%; pressure from Chinese dialyzer imports, with company choosing price hikes over volume defence. Anti-dumping probe on China and Malaysia dialyzers initiated, 20% injury margin claimed.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Revenue INR141.9 crore, +18.5%, forming the balance of the consolidated mix.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated FY27 revenue guidance INR2,300-2,400 crore including full-year PendraCare and Citieffe; maintained after Q1.
Standalone FY27 revenue guidance INR1,900-2,000 crore; domestic expected to grow over 20%, international over 15%.
Standalone EBITDA margin guided at 25-27% for FY27, with management expecting to close near the upper end; standalone gross margin guided at 67-69% going forward.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 23-25%; consolidated gross margin expected at 71-72%.
FY27 capex INR200-225 crore; asset turns 1.2-1.4x.
Renal FY27 growth targeted at 15-18%, possibly close to 20%, contingent on anti-dumping outcome expected by year-end.
Long-term aspiration to double consolidated revenue by FY30 (PolyMed 3.0, 'Ascent'), roughly 80% organic and 20% inorganic; margins expected to be held at similar levels rather than expanded.
Faridabad (Palwal) plant expected online by March 2027, focused on orthopedics, transfusion and extra infusion capacity; Noida plant commercial from Q1 FY28, focused on cardiology.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at INR200-225 crore, with cash earmarked partly for two plants under construction.
Faridabad (Palwal) facility targeted online by March 2027 for orthopedics, transfusion and infusion capacity expansion.
Noida facility targeted for commercial operation in Q1 FY28, for cardiology expansion.
Asset turns of 1.2-1.4x expected to continue on the balance sheet.
PendraCare and Citieffe manufacturing shifts to India are in progress and at regulatory approval stage.
demand_pricing: Middle East: 32% decline due to West Asia crisis; orders are piling up at ports as ships are not calling and containers are hard to find. Management expects 20-25%+ growth once normalised.
Europe: +17.6% organic growth, back to the 17-18% planned rate after adding new customers; Southeast Asia also growing well.
US: exports expected at USD 3.5-4 million for FY27; current duty 10%.
Price hikes taken at start of FY27 to offset raw material increases; management sees raw material peak as past, with only minor further changes.
Renal faces pricing pressure from Chinese players importing duty-free via ASEAN FTA; company raised prices rather than defend volume.
PendraCare had about 20% Middle East exposure and is currently not growing; Citieffe growing in mid-to-high single digits.

qa_highlights.question: How will standalone revenue reach INR350-400 crore incremental growth, given about 12% growth in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is seasonally the lowest and early-year price hikes slowed sales, with recovery later in the quarter; momentum should lift Q2 onwards to meet guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What will the INR850 crore cash be used for?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic and inorganic expansion, including Brazil direct sales, technology in cardiology, oncology and orthopedics, adjacent technologies, and capex at two plants under construction.

qa_highlights.question: Will Middle East exports resume and will Q2 gross margin be affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Shipping remains disrupted and orders are stuck at ports. Standalone gross margin is guided at 68-69%, so some correction from Q1's 71.5% is likely, with EBITDA broadly held by higher revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the 2x revenue goal and the implied gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated 2x is the target and standalone will grow faster than the subsidiaries; did not provide a precise breakdown.

qa_highlights.question: Gross debt and repayments?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone has only about INR250 crore working capital revolver; PendraCare has no long-term loan; Citieffe has about EUR 9 million loan with EUR 1.5-2 million repaid annually.

qa_highlights.question: Will the working capital cycle improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash conversion cycle remains around 140 days, same as March; management declined to give forward guidance given geopolitical delays.

524735|2026-06.headline: Hikal Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 403 crore, EBITDA margin 9.2%, PAT Rs (-7) crore; management guides FY27 revenue growth 14-16% and EBITDA growth 25-30%.
524735|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 403 crore with EBITDA of Rs 37 crore (9.2% margin) and PAT of Rs (-7) crore, aided by Rs 9 crore exceptional income from reversal of a Labour Code provision. Pharma grew year-on-year despite a planned shutdown for US FDA remediation, while Crop Protection was mixed, with domestic own-product volumes improving but CDMO export orders deferred. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 14-16% revenue growth and 25-30% EBITDA growth, with momentum expected to build in H2. Net debt was cut to Rs 685 crore by FY26 end (from Rs 815 crore in FY24), and debt-to-equity was 0.53.

financial_highlights.change: Reversal of excess Q4 FY26 provision for new Labour Codes

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 233 crore, EBIT Rs 8 crore (3.2% margin); Panoli and Bangalore plants ran at about 55-60% utilisation including Q1 shutdown. Management expects pharma to grow 18-19% CAGR going forward.

segments.name: Crop Protection
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 170 crore, EBIT Rs (-6) crore. Own products grew sequentially on domestic demand; CDMO exports subdued as some orders deferred to H2. Management expects flattish-to-marginal growth this year and mid-to-high single digit growth longer term.

segments.name: Animal Health
segments.commentary: Annual turnover above Rs 100 crore in FY26; management targets Rs 400 crore plus by FY30 and 20%+ EBITDA margin at scale. Completed US EPA and Canada PMRA filings for one molecule in Q1.

segments.name: Personal Care (new)
segments.commentary: Dedicated line at Panoli commercial production commenced; revenue expected by end of this year (launch year, small volumes). Management targets over Rs 200 crore revenue within about three years post-FY27 at over 20% EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at approximately 14-16%, with strong growth in pharma and marginal growth in crop.
FY27 EBITDA growth guided at approximately 25-30%.
Q2 expected to show substantial YoY growth in revenue and EBITDA; H2 FY27 momentum expected to accelerate.
FDA remediation costs weigh on fixed costs in FY27; benefit expected from next year, with FY28 described as substantially better.
Management expects 15-16% CAGR to continue beyond FY27.
Crop Protection: Q2 expected better than Q1 (Kharif), Q3 further improvement (Rabi and Latin America); crop margins to stay under pressure near term.
capex_capacity: Over the last 4 years, about Rs 900 crore capex: Rs 300 crore maintenance (about Rs 75 crore a year across 6 sites) and Rs 600 crore growth.
Rs 300 crore agrochemical plant partly impaired in Q4 FY26 is being retooled into a multipurpose pharma and Animal Health CDMO facility, cutting execution timelines by about 12 months.
New cGMP pilot plant at Pune R&D centre and Panoli pilot plant commissioned; DMF filing capacity expected to rise from 2-3 to 5-7 filings per year.
Q1 capex of Rs 45 crore for de-bottlenecking, regulatory upgrades and new capacity; capex in crop business kept minimal.
demand_pricing: Crop Protection: global channel destocking largely complete, but distributors still buying just in time; crop pricing under pressure from Chinese oversupply.
Raw material and energy costs rose on Middle East geopolitical tensions; crop Q1 margin hit of about Rs 7-8 crore from raw material increases.
Some crop contracts have pass-through clauses; others only partially compensate for cost increases.
Pharma: customer ordering patterns normalising; zero lost customer contracts in last 12 months per management; 86+ customer audits re-approved facilities.
Pharma CDMO pipeline of around 8-9 NCE/intermediate molecules; repeat campaign orders from innovators; discussions with a leading Japanese innovator progressing.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be expected for Animal Health?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 20%+ EBITDA margin for Animal Health once operating leverage is reached.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3-year outlook for Crop Protection?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects marginal growth now, moving to mid-to-high single-digit growth; no significant new capital going into crop, and new CDMO contract margins are lower than 3-4 years ago.

qa_highlights.question: Is Hikal positioning as a pharma company over the next five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management expects pharma, allied pharma and Personal Care to be about 70-80% of revenue in 2-3 years, with crop about 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Why aren't FY27 margins higher given pharma and Animal Health growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is a transition year with FDA remediation costs in fixed costs; the meaningful margin improvement is expected in FY28 and beyond.

qa_highlights.question: How will FDA clearance affect FY28 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Pending filings awaiting FDA approval are expected to be executed after re-inspection, ramping revenue in FY28 at better margins.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of clearing the US FDA re-inspection this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes for re-inspection by end of FY27, with possible delays of a few months; a few open issues remain to be closed in the next few months.

risks_watch: Timing of US FDA re-inspection (targeted by end FY27, may slip a few months); remediation costs continue to weigh on fixed costs.
Crop pricing pressure from China and raw material/energy volatility linked to Middle East geopolitics; management said costs could rise again if the conflict resumes.
Deferred CDMO orders in crop and pharma shifting from H1 to H2, increasing dependence on H2 execution.
Personal Care and Animal Health ramp-up depends on new contracts and validations; Personal Care revenue only from year-end.
Q1 PAT loss of Rs (-7) crore despite Rs 9 crore exceptional gain; watch for underlying profitability.

500655|2026-06.headline: Garware Hi-Tech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR633 crore and EBITDA margin hit a record 30.30%, with FY27 guidance reaffirmed.
500655|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR633 crore (+28% YoY), EBITDA of INR192 crore (+56% YoY) at a 30.30% margin, and PAT of INR133 crore (+60% YoY). Management attributed the margin to product mix (Sun Control and high-IR products, architectural share) rather than one-offs, and said Q3 will be seasonally lower. Tariff refunds were excluded from Q1 and about 30-40% had been received by the call date, with the balance expected in Q2. FY27 guidance of over INR2,500 crore revenue and 25% plus/minus 2% EBITDA margin was reaffirmed; management also flagged Middle East shipping disruption that delayed some Q1 volume into Q2.

segments.name: Sun Control Films (SCF)
segments.commentary: About 55% of Q1 FY27 revenue versus 48-50% in FY26; management calls it the largest product. A new robotic SCF line (INR192 crore, about 1,200 lakh sq ft annual capacity) is due for commercial production in H1 FY28.

segments.name: Paint Protection Film (PPF)
segments.commentary: About 20% of Q1 revenue versus about 25% last year. Old PPF line runs near 100%; new line at about 60%. Some volume slipped to Q2 due to a ship stuck at Jebel Ali. Five OEM relationships including M&M.

segments.name: Architectural films
segments.commentary: Management says architectural now exceeds 25% of revenue (vs about 5% earlier, as stated) and is the highest-margin product set on like-for-like basis, per management.

segments.name: Garware Home Solutions (D2C)
segments.commentary: 9 studios operational, target 50 by end FY27. 100% direct-to-consumer; Q1 sales described as very small with no figure given. Management said D2C could exceed INR100 crore.

segments.name: Garware Application Studios
segments.commentary: Network over 250 locations in India; 14 international studios across Middle East and US.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance reaffirmed at over INR2,500 crore; EBITDA margin guided at 25% plus/minus 2%. Management said 27-28% looked logical but kept the guidance.
Medium-term revenue CAGR of 15-20%; management indicated about INR3,000 crore by roughly two years out and INR3,500 crore in three to four years.
TPU line (PPF backward integration, about 75% for PPF, 25% for new products) to commission in Q3 FY27; company guides an additional 1.5-2% EBITDA margin after stabilisation in FY28.

Tariff refund: about 30-40% received by call date (July-August), with full refund expected in Q2; management estimated net INR50 crore-plus to the company after sharing with US customers. Excluded from Q1.
Margin seasonality: Q1 and Q2 strong, Q3 lower, Q4 recovers.
capex_capacity: TPU line commissioning in Q3 FY27; management said it could support about INR500 crore revenue potential over three years with possible further capex.
New SCF line (INR192 crore, robotic, about 1,200 lakh sq ft/yr) commercial production expected H1 FY28; management cited INR500-550 crore peak revenue potential for this line.
Management said cash deployment priorities are inorganic growth (under evaluation), more capex for backward and forward integration, and a return-of-capital decision to be announced in coming months.
Over INR700 crore invested in strategic expansions over recent years.
demand_pricing: US e-commerce PPF sales rising; dealer and distributor order flow described as strong in Q1.
Middle East demand described as strong, but supply chain disrupted by war; shipments delayed.
Raw material pass-through: management said direct correlation of consumer product raw material to revenue is about 10-12%, and cost increases are passed to customers through negotiation.
TPU addressable market in India described by management as easily above INR1,000 crore, but it requires market creation.
Antidumping duty recommended by DGTR on TPU-based PPF imports from China.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~60% gross margin sustainable or will it normalise to 54-55%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-offs, including tariff refunds. Margin depends on product mix (high-IR Sun Control and architectural). Q1 and Q2 are seasonally strong, Q3 lower, Q4 recovers.

qa_highlights.question: Tariff refund status and balance?
qa_highlights.answer: No refund in Q1. About 30-40% received in July-August, with full refund expected in Q2. Net benefit estimated at INR50 crore-plus after customer sharing.

qa_highlights.question: TPU line margin uplift and FY28 expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 1.5-2% margin uplift after the TPU line stabilises. Three TPU products are in the target list; the line is expected to add no material volume in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation of PPF capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Old PPF line near 100%; new line about 60%, with volume lost to Jebel Ali shipping delay expected to be recovered next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow faster than 15-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the constraint is consumer and authority education and niche product positioning, not top-line demand or capacity; it does not want to commoditise Sun Control.

qa_highlights.question: Where is cash being deployed given INR850 crore balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities in order: evaluate inorganic growth, more capex for integration and reliability, then growth capex. No dividend or buyback was announced; details promised in coming months.

risks_watch: Middle East shipping and war-related supply disruption affecting deliveries and Q2 volume recovery.
Sustainability of 30% EBITDA margin: management said Q3 will be lower, and guidance remains 25% plus/minus 2%.
Tariff refund receipt: balance of about 60-70% expected in Q2; quantum and timing to be confirmed.
Garware Home Solutions execution: 9 studios to 50 by FY27 end, channel partner friction, and the unquantified revenue contribution.
TPU and SCF commissioning timelines (Q3 FY27 and H1 FY28) and ramp-up.
Management did not disclose the Q1 revenue or margin split for D2C, nor geography-wise CPD sales (deferred to IR).

Europe: growth from Mango (Spain), CCC (Poland); Gerry Weber's bankruptcy replaced by new German accounts.

540061|2026-06.headline: Bigbloc Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~40% YoY to ~INR 79 crore and EBITDA to ~INR 6 crore (~8% margin), with net loss narrowing to ~INR 70 lakh.
540061|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as an inflection point, with sales volume of 2,21,545 cubic meters (+32% YoY) and plant utilisation of about 69%. Revenue was about INR 79 crore (+~40% YoY) and EBITDA about INR 6 crore versus INR 1 crore a year earlier. The net loss narrowed to about INR 70 lakh from about INR 6 crore. Management said margin gains will come from utilisation (target 75%+), price hikes in some markets, and construction chemicals, and it deferred the Madhya Pradesh plant to FY28 commercial production.

financial_highlights.change: rooftop solar ~3.3 MW across four plants

segments.name: AAC blocks
segments.commentary: Majority of turnover; ~69% utilisation across installed AAC block capacity. Three plants are block-only, and one plant with ~250,000 cbm fungible block/panel capacity runs at ~40% utilisation.

segments.commentary: ~5% of Q1 revenue. Projects cited include ITC, L&T bullet train stations and data-centre and metro talks.

segments.name: Construction chemicals / mortar
segments.commentary: Mortar plant began operations in May 2026; Q1 utilisation about 20-25%, to be scaled over the next couple of quarters. Previously traded under the company brand via manufacturing partners.

Electric forklifts being rolled out across plants.

Transport radius limits growth outside western India; MP plant timing depends on utilisation reaching 75%+.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to contracted licences with escalations timing; it hopes margins hold, expecting only steady fluctuation based on contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt trajectory and restructuring progress?

qa_highlights.question: Executable portion of the INR210 crore order book in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Share of profit from associate (LSN Diffusion) of INR4.4 crore: anomaly or steady?

qa_highlights.question: FY27-28 revenue and margin outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone margin fall from ~18% peak to ~13%, and is Q1 the bottom?

533259|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR440 crores, but EBITDA was still a negative INR15 crores (-3.4% margin) and PAT was INR2 crores.
533259|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew over 58% YoY to INR440 crores and about 16% QoQ from INR378 crores, with gross profit up 64% YoY to INR34 crores. Gross margin improved to 7.8% from 7.3% in Q4 FY26, and EBITDA loss narrowed to INR15 crores from INR20 crores. PAT of INR2 crores compared with a loss of INR13 crores in Q4 FY26 but remained below the INR26 crores reported in Q1 FY26. Management said July revenue was about INR150 crores (subject to audit) and that it does not expect EBITDA positivity for the next two to three years at group level.

financial_highlights.change: from loss of INR20 crores (-5.5%) in Q4 FY26
from loss of INR13 crores in Q4 FY26; below INR26 crores in Q1 FY26

segments.name: RetailerShakti
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 48% YoY and remains the principal growth engine; gross margin about 7.8% and EBITDA close to break-even, with management targeting positive EBITDA in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: SastaSundar (B2C via Health Buddy franchisees)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 44% YoY; management attributes about 90% of its EBITDA loss to technology build-up and says the model spends about 15% of revenue on building it. Segment P&L is not disclosed.

segments.name: JITO private label
segments.commentary: Sales rose from about INR25 lakhs in Q4 FY26 to about INR79 lakhs in Q1 FY27 (about 200% growth), with gross margin said to be above 50%; still a very small share of revenue.

guidance_outlook: Entire FY27 gross margin to be maintained at 8% plus; medium-term industry gross margin of about 12% cited as target.
RetailerShakti expected to reach positive EBITDA in Q3 FY27.

Company not expected to be EBITDA positive for the next two to three years; focus stated as cash flow and capital efficiency.
RetailAir AI-monitored SaaS for retailers scheduled to launch in Q2 FY27.
Existing plus side-extension fulfilment capacity said to support revenue up to about INR3,000 crores; existing capacity described as running at about 90%.
capex_capacity: New warehouses: Noida operational (new facility starting 17 August); West Bengal partly done; Guwahati 75,000 sq ft rented, owned construction to start in about 6 months.
Udaipur construction started; Patna and Lucknow to start in about 2-3 months; Ranchi warehouse planned in Jharkhand.
Management says it intends to own fulfilment infrastructure rather than rely on third-party warehouses; no capex quantum disclosed.
JITO conversions: 19 Health Buddies converted to JITO, 25 in pipeline; about 50% of Health Buddies expected to convert within 3 months.
demand_pricing: Customer base: about 75,000 retail pharmacies served, 40,000 active in last 30 days; average wallet share about 2%.
Order-size mix: 69.4% of RetailerShakti business from orders above INR2,500 and 42.4% above INR5,000; 69.2% of SastaSundar orders above INR1,000.

Geography: about 67% of RetailerShakti and 78% of SastaSundar business from tier 2 and tier 3 markets; West Bengal share about 70% per analyst question, with management citing about 30% now from West Bengal in the call.
Expansion into Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, UP, Rajasthan; Northeast cited as the fastest-growing region.
Sourcing: over 95% of purchases direct from pharma companies; purchase returns below 1%; more than 50,000 SKUs from over 1,000 vendors.
Management estimates current market share in Kolkata and West Bengal at about 3-4%, with a target of about 7% in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are gross and EBITDA margins for RetailerShakti in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin about 7.8%; EBITDA close to break-even, with positive EBITDA expected in Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 revenue aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give annual projections; July revenue was above INR150 crores (subject to audit), which it said investors can extrapolate.

qa_highlights.question: How will gross margin ramp, and what is the JITO contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects blended B2B and B2C gross margin to move toward about 12%, driven by volume, wallet share and private label; it declined to give a JITO share target but said internal projections exceed analyst scenarios of 5-6% of revenue within three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SastaSundar burn and its split?
