qa_highlights.question: Why has the EBITDA break-even timeline moved from one or two years to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied any postponement, saying RetailerShakti is near break-even and that break-even at group level was never promised for the current year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the warehouse and fulfilment capacity status?

500710|2026-06.headline: JSW Dulux Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.8% to ₹965 crore on ~25% volume growth, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% with PAT lifted by one-offs.
500710|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 18.8% like-to-like to ₹965 crore, with volume up about 25% (about 18-19% after price). Gross margin was 37.4%, which management says was depressed by roughly 2 points of high-cost inventory and about 2.5 points from reclassifying promotional spends to gross revenue; underlying gross margin was put at 39.5-40%. EBITDA rose 14.7% to ₹115.1 crore but margin diluted about 50 bps to 11.9% after headcount additions (~160 people) and R&D investment. Reported PAT of ₹135.5 crore includes one-offs: ₹55.9 crore dividend from ICICI R&T and ₹108 crore income tax refund (incl. ₹21.5 crore interest) for AY 2013-14.

financial_highlights.change: Management: underlying ~39.5-40% before inventory and reclassification effects
Other income; linked to real estate monetisation

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Grew double digits (management cites ~20% volume growth) and is ~60% of business; premium is ~45% of decorative and led growth, with premium and luxury growing high double digits. Mass and economy grew lower.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: All sub-segments grew upwards of 25%; automotive grew strongly with premium OEM and refinish wins (Porsche, Mahindra, MG via JSW group, Sikkens body shops).

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected in 13-15% range going forward, as reinvestment costs normalise and input prices ease.
Management expects Q2 growth in a similar band to Q1 despite a weaker July due to late rains; target is double-digit volume and value growth.
Strategic ambition: become number two in decorative and number one in industrial coatings, with a 2030-31 vision; decorative aim is market share gains while protecting absolute EBITDA.
Project Akshaya cost programme targets synergies with JSW Paints; ₹2.4 crore savings realised in Q1 and a 3-year roadmap set.
ERP migration from AkzoNobel systems planned by end of calendar year; TSA period is limited.
capex_capacity: Active towns about 3,400-3,500 out of 5,000+ presence; target to lift to about 4,500 this year, focusing on towns above 20,000 population.
Shift to direct/hybrid model in about the top 20 high-share towns; distributor model retained elsewhere.
Cross-manufacturing: JSW Paints made at Gwalior; JSW Dulux products made in JSW Paints plants; some JSW Paints products made in Mohali.
Headquarters moved from Delhi to JSW Centre, Mumbai during Q1.
demand_pricing: Volume growth ~25%, with price contributing ~6-7 points; growth driven by value per outlet from existing outlets, broadly secular across outlet types.
Gross-to-net reclassification of promotional spends (~2.5% of blended revenue) reduced reported gross margin; management says this aligns with industry presentation.
Management says decorative pricing has stabilised but competition from new entrants, with discounting, will persist for 1-2 years.

Discount ratio includes distributor commission (~4.5-4.7% of revenue), which management says makes dealer commissions otherwise modest; company benchmarks pricing to the market leader, not new entrants.
Benefit expected as high-priced inventory bought at end-March is consumed; lower-cost stock now entering August.

qa_highlights.question: What execution changes are driving better decorative performance, beyond headcount?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-market segmentation by share tiers; reinforced Velvet Touch and WeatherShield; focus on undercoats such as primers in weak states; digital lead management, AI/analytics and an architect/painter programme. Hybrid direct model being tested in top 20 towns.

qa_highlights.question: How does volume-value gap reconcile with mix improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three factors: high-cost inventory, ~2.5% gross-to-net reclassification, and faster growth in lower-margin industrial and other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Target for top-three position and inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined JSW Paints and JSW Dulux revenue is about ₹6,000 crore. Aim is to become number two; industrial to be number one in 1-1.5 years and wider ambition by 2030-31. No explicit M&A mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity and discounting vs. new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition to remain intense for 1-2 years; company does not match new entrant discounts and benchmarks against the market leader.

qa_highlights.question: Decorative outperformance vs Asian Paints and Berger (8-9% volume growth)?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to premium-led growth, distribution expansion, digital tools and recovery in smaller dealers after new-entrant pressure; no single driver cited.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for July-August?
qa_highlights.answer: July was weaker due to late rains, but management expects Q2 in a similar band and targets double-digit growth in volume and value.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery to the 39.5-40% underlying level as high-cost inventory is consumed; crude-linked raw material costs.
EBITDA margin trajectory versus the 13-15% guidance as headcount and R&D costs continue.
Persistent discounting by new entrants in decorative; mass and economy segment growth lagging.
One-off income (₹55.9 crore dividend, ₹108 crore tax refund) inflates Q1 PAT; underlying profit is lower.
Execution risk in Project Akshaya, ERP migration and exit from AkzoNobel TSA; related-party governance with JSW Paints.
500710|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volume growth and market share ambitions, while openly explaining margin shortfall via inventory, reclassification and reinvestment. 544885|2026-06.headline: Gaja AMC Q1 FY27 PAT rose 35% YoY to INR27.2 crores; total income up 26% to INR51.8 crores.
544885|2026-06.overview:

segments.name: Fee income

qa_highlights.question: Share of carry vs fee income and whether pure fee income will grow faster?

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of performance income into carry and sponsor gains?

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Fund III carry given low gross IRR?

qa_highlights.question: Q4 to Q1 jump of about 594% in carry fee; is it realisations?

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to AI deals such as Fractal and Sarvam and entry valuations?

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost rise from Q4 to Q1 (INR6.7 crores to INR10.3 crores)?

543539|2026-06.headline: Modis Navnirman Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27.92% YoY to INR58.26 crore; PAT up 25.81% to INR8.54 crore, though EBITDA margin fell to about 20%.
543539|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 27.92% YoY to INR58.26 crore and 13.15% QoQ, with EBITDA up 14.25% YoY to INR11.65 crore and PAT up 25.81% YoY to INR8.54 crore. Management attributed the margin squeeze to war-related material and labour cost spikes in April-May, which it said have since stabilised. The company added Khar (Rashmi Icon/redevelopment) to its Mumbai footprint, bringing the portfolio to 25 projects (six ongoing, 14 completed, five upcoming). Management gave no quantified FY27 project-addition target, only that two to three projects are likely in FY27.

segments.name: Mumbai redevelopment projects
segments.commentary: Six ongoing, 14 completed, five upcoming; 25 projects in total across Malad, Kandivali, Borivali, Dahisar, Goregaon, Khar. Revenue recognised on percentage-of-completion (Ind AS 115).

segments.name: Rashmi Square / Rashmi Signature
segments.commentary: Together about 60% of Q1 revenue per analyst's question, which management did not dispute. Square at 22 slabs and roughly 80% of inventory booked; Signature at 20th slab and roughly 50-70% booked (figures varied within the call).

guidance_outlook: Management expects two to three new redevelopment projects in FY27, with no guarantee given tender uncertainty.

Four pipeline projects with aggregate GDV above INR800 crore: Rashmi Paradise to start in Q1 FY27 (this quarter), Rashmi Gold and Shectal in Q3, Khar in Q4; Govind Dalvi on hold due to a government stay on a 500-metre area.
Management cited healthy margins of around 20-30% expected per project, and 19-20% margins on upcoming projects.
Square and Signature margins are slightly below underwriting due to war-time material purchases, but not expected to be majorly hit over a two to two-and-a-half year timeline.
Management has not yet set a leverage ceiling or capital-employed framework per project.
capex_capacity: Under construction: about 12.11 lakh sq ft; upcoming pipeline about 10.5 lakh sq ft (per analyst's question, not disputed).
Rashmi Square completed 22 slabs; Rashmi Signature 20th slab; Rashmi Delight 14th slab; Rashmi Manorath 13th slab; Rashmi Icon and Rashmi Avenue at plinth stage.
Rashmi Signature and Square expected to be handed over with occupancy certificate in Q3 FY27.
Asset-light redevelopment model: partners with societies rather than buying open-market land.
demand_pricing: Management said pricing trends are similar to before, with no significant volatility; pricing is micro-market and project specific.
Management views Mumbai demand as stable with no decline expected over the next few years, though supply has risen due to government moves on MHADA and SRA land.
Demand exists for both luxury and affordable segments; product positioning varies by micro-market (larger homes in Kandivali/Borivali).
Labour availability and cost were described as not an issue at any project now, after war-time shortages in April-May.
Expansion limited to Bombay; Parle in tender, Ghatkopar under discussion, nothing finalised. Other Indian cities open in principle.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from about 22.3% to about 19.8% despite 28% revenue growth?

qa_highlights.question: How many new projects in FY27 and what is the pipeline?

501455|2026-06.headline: Greaves Cotton Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31% YoY to INR975 crores, but margins fell 2-2.5 percentage points on investments and commodity costs.
501455|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 31% YoY to INR975 crores and core businesses grew 16% to INR710 crores (19% like-for-like after portfolio exits). Margins came under pressure by 2 to 2.5 percentage points, which management attributed to about 1.5 points of deliberate Greaves.Next investments and commodity inflation (platinum, aluminium, steel, fuel) that pricing has only partly offset. Management said Q2 will be marginally better than Q1 and H2 better than H1, and that it remains committed to full-year FY27 margin targets. GEML revenue was about INR270 crores, roughly double last year, with market share reported at 5.6% in June.

segments.name: Mobility Solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 18% YoY; automotive engines grew 36% YoY. Retail aftermarket pruning is complete (2-wheeler spares, lead-acid batteries, multi-brand EV retail, farm equipment exited). Excel grew 14% YoY.

segments.commentary: Reported revenue flat YoY and 9% growth after portfolio rationalisation. FM-UL compliant firefighting engine exports started and a large defence order was completed.

segments.name: Greaves Electric Mobility (GEML)
segments.commentary: Record Q1 volume growth of 101% YoY vs industry 75%. Market share rose to 5.6% in June from 4.5% exit FY26; 2-wheeler revenue up ~120% and 3-wheeler up ~80% YoY. Dealer network expanded from ~300 to 600.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin drop is investment versus commodity cost?

qa_highlights.question: Is GEML's growth sustainable and when does it turn EBITDA-positive?

qa_highlights.question: Why does GFL, an EV financing NBFC, exist in a pruned portfolio, and is it brand-agnostic?

qa_highlights.question: Is there enough cash for the investee investments?

qa_highlights.question: Is motorcycle entry planned for GEML?

532509|2026-06.headline: Suprajit Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24% to INR1,070 crore and operational EBITDA 57% to INR129 crore, while standalone EBITDA was flat at INR60 crore.
532509|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue hit a record INR1,070 crore (up 24% YoY) and operational EBITDA reached INR129 crore (up 57%). Global Cables and Mechatronics (GCM) drove the gain, with EBITDA margin rising from 5.8% to 12.6% after the global restructuring. Standalone margins were squeezed by raw material and wage inflation in ICM (margin ~15% to ~13%) and by delayed price pass-through in PLE (margin 6.7%, down 2.8pp); management calls both timing issues and expects recovery in Q2-Q3. Management reiterated FY27 guidance from the 25 May 2026 release.

segments.name: Global Cables and Mechatronics (GCM, formerly SCD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~27-28% reported, ~23% after adjusting for two months of SCS Canada/China tranche not in base; EBITDA margin 12.6% vs 5.8%. Management says 12%-plus is current, guidance 10%-12% retained.

segments.name: India Cables and Mechatronics (ICM, formerly DCD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~21%, broad-based across OEM and aftermarket; EBITDA up 4.2% with margin down from ~15% to ~13% on raw material and wage costs. CBS revenue up 110% and brake shoes/pads up ~80% off a small base.

segments.name: Phoenix Lighting and Electricals (PLE, formerly PLD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 5.4%, EBITDA down 45%, margin 6.7% (down 2.8pp) on delayed aftermarket price increases; new prices now in effect. Ramp-up with a large US retailer; Middle East Trifa sales soft.

segments.name: Sensors, Electronics and Displays (SED)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 48%, EBITDA up 100%, margins close to double digits, led by digital clusters and electronic throttle grips. July was reported as the division's highest-sales month.

GCM: new product launches in China (one of the largest Chinese EV OEMs, about 25 cable projects won, 5-6 launched) and India (lines for a large US OEM building a resilient supply chain). Business wins across India, Mexico and China.
SED: about six launches in the plant this month and next, across instrument clusters, actuators/sensors and throttle position sensors.
US retailer PLE programme: store count expected to roughly triple or go 4x next year.

Global automotive and non-automotive demand described as flat to muted; GCM growth attributed to new contract wins replacing lost business.

Three large GCM contract wins announced about a month earlier: largest EV cable contract (USD 5m annual, USD 37m lifetime); European luxury OEM (USD 2m a year, USD 12m lifetime); Japanese OEM (USD 1.2m a year, USD 6m lifetime).
Management described the business as very competitive globally but consolidating, which may favour stronger players on margin.
Braking: CBS customers include TVS and HMSI; management says validation cycles are long for this safety-critical product.

qa_highlights.question: Were there one-offs or FX benefits in GCM margin, and is 12% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no material one-offs; margin gains came from restructuring, leaner operations, cost projects and top-line growth. It is at 12%-plus, but guidance of 10%-12% is retained and depends on product mix.

qa_highlights.question: Can SCS be disclosed separately for Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No. SCS was disclosed separately only until March 2026; it is now folded into GCM as entities were merged or restructured.

qa_highlights.question: Was the GCM 27% growth flattered by FX or acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reported 27% overstates growth; excluding April-May from the second SCS tranche, growth is about 23%. The USD/INR rate has been stable at about INR95-96 over the period.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Last year's gains came from large favourable currency moves on loans, debtors/creditors and forward covers, plus a Morocco subsidy not repeated. Currency has been stable since March, so the Q1 figure is much smaller.

qa_highlights.question: What drives SED growth and the EV exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is in instrument clusters, actuators/sensors and TPS, across multiple customers, with ICE as well as EV demand. Mahindra throttle ramp-up used a rare-earth-free design. Management expects strong growth for at least 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin shortfall in ICM/PLE temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as a timing issue: price pass-through is still being negotiated, with recovery expected in Q2 and Q3 and cost reduction under way.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for PLE run-rate and the European insolvency?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes are declining in the old business; the European insolvency is unresolved. Management expects more clarity in the next quarter and sees opportunities over three to six months, with US retailer business growing.

Chinese landed cell price cited at ~4 cents/W before 27.5% BCD.
Tender pipeline: ~35–40 GW of fresh utility tenders post-August 2025; FY27 AC market estimated at 30–35 GW utility, ~15 GW C&I, 14–15 GW PM Surya Ghar plus KUSUM.

544421|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to ₹987 mn and EBITDA margin reached 39%, with PAT up 87% YoY to ₹350 mn.
544421|2026-06.overview:
Ellenbarrie posted a strong Q1 FY27, with revenue from operations of ₹987 mn (+18% YoY, +13% QoQ), driven mainly by ramp-up of the Kurnool and Uluberia 2 plants. EBITDA rose to ₹387 mn (+21% YoY, +50% QoQ) at a 39% margin, which management attributed mainly to new power-efficient capacity, cost control and higher production rather than argon pricing. PAT of ₹350 mn was helped by lower finance cost and a lower effective tax rate. Management reaffirmed FY27 capex of ₹250 crore and FY28 capex of ₹200 crore, and said the East India 320 TPD on-site plant should start contributing revenue in Q2 FY27.</overview>

segments.name: Core gases (bulk and on-site)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹973 mn, up 20% YoY, driven by merchant plant ramp-up; segment margin 38%, supported by volumes, cost efficiency and argon volumes and pricing.

segments.name: On-site vs bulk split (per Q1 investor presentation, as cited)
segments.commentary: On-site revenue about ₹14 crore and bulk about ₹70 crore, so on-site is about 20% of revenue, though on-site is a significantly higher share of capacity than 20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guidance unchanged at ₹2,500 mn (₹250 crore); FY28 capex guidance ₹2,000 mn (₹200 crore).
East India 320 TPD on-site plant under commissioning; revenue expected from Q2 FY27.
Long-term EBITDA margin target of 40% or higher as new capacity unfolds; management said this is a target, not a quarterly guarantee.
Merchant capacity in North India (220 TPD, not yet operational) and West Central India, together about 450–500 TPD, under construction; the West site is an ASU merchant plant.
Merchant plants assumed to take 18–24 months to ramp to 80–90% utilisation; payback described as about 18 months build plus 18–24 months ramp plus about three years.
risks_watch: Argon price volatility, which management said can move quarterly margins materially.
Ramp-up pace of Uluberia 2, Kurnool and the East India 320 TPD plant, and whether Q2 revenue from East India starts on time.
Power cost, which management called the largest cost; renewable PPA progress is key.
Competitive intensity in new merchant markets, where capacity is not pre-contracted and ramp takes 18–24 months.
Concentration in on-site contracts: one customer for the East India plant, and multiple large inquiries not yet signed.
544421|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on operating momentum and margins, but cautious on argon pricing, which management repeatedly described as cyclical and not guaranteed to support quarterly margins. Answers on on-site customers and specific plant economics were guarded.
key_quotes: We expect this business to stabilize at 40% or higher EBITDA margins.
the growth in our EBITDA margins, however, has not been primarily on account of Argon pricing.
So, this entire 450, I mean, whatever residual amount that there is of this 450 crore will be towards these two merchant plants.

500877|2026-06.headline: Apollo Tyres Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 74bn (+12.8% YoY), EBITDA margin 11.7% (down ~150bp) on ~17% raw material inflation.
500877|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 12.8% YoY to INR 74bn but was flat-ish sequentially, with consolidated EBITDA margin down about 150bp YoY to 11.7% on raw material cost pressure. India delivered its highest-ever revenue of INR 54.6bn (+15.6% YoY, +4.3% QoQ), largely volume-led, with India EBITDA margin at 12% versus 13.6%. Europe revenue was EUR147m (+0.5% YoY) with EBITDA of EUR13m (8.9% margin), hit by Enschede closure transition and agri revenue loss. Management said price increases lag raw material inflation and that most of the catch-up flows into Q2 and H2.

financial_highlights.change: India capex INR 500 crore in Q1

financial_highlights.metric: Raw material cost increase in Q1
financial_highlights.change: Rubber INR 225/kg, synthetic INR 250, carbon black INR 125, steel cord INR 165 (as quoted)

segments.name: India operations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 54.6bn (+15.6% YoY), double-digit growth across all segments; volume growth Replacement 13%, OEM 10%, Exports 15%. TBB was the only category without double-digit growth. Price increases ~3-4% realised in Q1 versus 7-9% taken.

segments.name: Europe operations
segments.commentary: Revenue EUR147m (+0.5% YoY) and EBITDA EUR13m (8.9%). PCR replacement grew double digits; agri revenue fell high-teens QoQ and small single digits YoY. Without Enschede overlap costs, margin would have been ~11%.

segments.name: Reifen
segments.commentary: Revenue EUR43m in Q1 with ~3% EBITDA margin, as disclosed on the call.

guidance_outlook: Raw material inflation of ~8% sequentially expected in Q2 for India; Europe RM basket up 8% in Q1 with hit mainly in Q2.

India needs ~15-16% total price increase to cover commodity inflation; ~11%+ currently in place (9% TBR, 11% other categories); at least 1-2 more hikes needed; July hike 1-2%, similar hike expected in August.
Europe needs ~10% price increase across Q1-Q2; only 3-4% implemented so far.
Europe full-year EBITDA target: high teens margin once manufacturing footprint transition completes.
Net debt/EBITDA expected to rise slightly this year as company becomes a net borrower; capex to rise in Q2 and Q3.
Rubber expected to cool from Q3 as seasonal impact fades; crude-linked cost relief expected with a quarter lag.
capex_capacity: Enschede (Netherlands) plant stopped production in June 2026; ~750,000 tyres/year shifting largely to Hungary, completion Sept-Oct 2026; financial benefits from H2 FY27.
Hungary PCR capacity rising from ~17,000 to ~21,000 car tyres per day, starting H2 FY27; Hungary expanding by 4,000 PCR tyres/day, AP (India) plant expanding double that.
Lower-end 14-15 inch tyres moving from Hungary to India; Spacemaster spare tyre production now in Baroda; India new capacity to start towards end of FY27 and ramp through FY28.
High-end agri (OHT) capacity limited at Kalamassery (Kochi); no economic small-scale alternative; offtake partner identified near Asia-Europe cusp, midterm plan is offtake.
India capex was ~INR 1,200-1,300 crore annually in recent past; FY27 group capex guided above INR 3,000 crore.
Management says India running in the 90s on capacity utilisation and will stay tight through FY27.
demand_pricing: India replacement momentum strong; July started strongly and Q2 YoY growth expected to be good though QoQ muted due to rains and seasonality.
Europe: anti-dumping duty on Chinese tyres expected to help Apollo brand at lower end; Vredestein PCR does not compete with Chinese.
Exports growth driven by Europe; West Asia impacted by war and US underperformed due to dealer inventory issues.
Competition has broadly followed price increases of similar magnitude, per management.
Management market share estimates (internal): TBR replacement upwards of 30% (regained lost share); PCR replacement 21%+.
UHP mix in Europe stayed at around 40%, per management recollection.
Advertising and sales promotion spend cut by roughly 50% QoQ; management said no further reduction expected.

qa_highlights.question: India volume growth by channel and outlook; Europe anti-dumping and capacity shift timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Replacement +13%, OEM +10%, exports +15% volume growth; Q2 seasonal. Enschede-to-Hungary shift to complete Sept-Oct 2026; Spacemaster already in Baroda.

qa_highlights.question: How much India and Europe price hikes have been taken vs needed?
qa_highlights.answer: India: 7-9% implemented in Q1 (only 3-4% flowed into revenue), 11%+ now against 15-16% needed. Europe: 3-4% implemented against ~10% needed.

qa_highlights.question: Europe margin without overlap costs and steady-state target?
qa_highlights.answer: ~11% margin without overlap; full-year Europe target high-teens EBITDA margin after footprint change.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and net debt trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 consolidated capex INR 650 crore; India INR 500 crore; capex to step up in Q2-Q3; company to become net borrower with slight rise in net debt/EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses and staff cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P cut ~50% QoQ but no further reduction expected; minor increments effective June 1 with full impact from Q2, no further increment planned.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material outlook: rupee, rubber, crude?
qa_highlights.answer: ~7-8% of RM inflation from rupee depreciation (from INR 88); ~50% of RM imported; domestic rubber ~50-50 mix; rubber expected to cool from Q3; crude relief with a quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive pricing behaviour and market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition has followed price increases of similar magnitude; TBR share back above 30%, PCR replacement 21%+ (internal estimates).

532305|2026-06.headline: Ind-Swift Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 2.85x YoY to ₹33.32 crore, a 17.91% margin, with management guiding to 20%+ from Q3.
532305|2026-06.overview: Operating income grew 21.16% YoY to ₹186.08 crore and operating EBITDA reached ₹33.32 crore (17.91% margin, up 1258 bps). PAT excluding exceptional items was ₹24.68 crore (13.26% margin vs 4.99%). Management attributed the step-up to exit of litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business after the merger, and to a higher own-brand export mix. CDMO contracts with Viatris, Manx and Arrotex were commercialised in the quarter but contributed only about ₹5-6 crore so far, with ramp-up expected from Q2 and Q3. Management reiterated FY27 export sales of about ₹750 crore and ₹1200 crore revenue by FY29, and declined to revise targets at this stage.

segments.name: Export own-brands
segments.commentary: 57.20% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 48% in Q1 FY26; management cites this mix shift as a key margin driver. Export gross margin was stated at about 55%.

segments.name: Export contract manufacturing (CDMO)
segments.commentary: 26.64% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 29% a year earlier. Viatris, Manx and Arrotex partnerships commercialised in the quarter, with about ₹5-6 crore booked from Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) so far.

segments.name: Domestic segments
segments.commentary: Branded generics 6.41%, ethical 6.14% and domestic contract manufacturing 3.61% of Q1 FY27 sales, all lower than a year ago. Management describes these as a stable cash-generation base; domestic sales are seasonal.

segments.name: Product portfolio
segments.commentary: Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin was about ₹25 crore in Q1 FY27 per management, partnered with Tiffen-Becker. FY26 revenue: Atorvastatin ₹85.50 crore, Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin ₹80.78 crore, Fexofenadine ₹74.32 crore, Quetiapine ₹19.75 crore, Famciclovir ₹18.64 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 export sales target of about ₹750 crore, with roughly 45% from CDMO (per management).

FY29 revenue target of ₹1200 crore; management said it is not revising this yet and will revisit by year-end. Mentioned FY27 expectation of about ₹900 crore and a longer-term aspiration of ₹1500 crore revenue and ~₹200 crore net profit by FY30.
EBITDA margin of 18% described as sustainable; management expects to move above 20% from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally targeted), potentially 21-22% with sequential sales growth.
Viatris CDMO volumes expected to double in Q2 versus Q1; Arrotex Macrogol push expected in Q2, and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules to contribute in Q3-Q4.
Medium-term growth of 20-25% CAGR referenced, with EBITDA margins above 18% (management answered 'yes').
Dossiers to reach 400+ additions, taking the total from 2,100 to about 2,500 by Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: About ₹250 crore of cash to be deployed in capex over roughly 2 to 2.5 years across a new warehouse, capacity enhancement at the existing facility, and the Jammu facility (EU-GMP/PIC/S audit under way).
Samba facility upgrade to EU-GMP and PIC/S standards in progress as planned.
Capacity utilisation for Ibuprofen and granules about 70% in Q1 per management; management expects 90% utilisation of planned FY29 capacity over time.
Capex for a potential new CDMO customer deal estimated at ₹50-75 crore, with revenue of ₹150+ crore expected.
R&D working on 5-6 molecules for FY27-29; capex to follow only after filings are completed. New R&D land bought in Panchkula area.
demand_pricing: CDMO economics: Viatris paid about USD 2 million for development work, to be reimbursed through orders.
Selection criteria for new products include a minimum 50-55% gross margin and customer confidence in R&D delivery. Candidate molecules include Rosuvastatin, Mirabegron, Sitagliptin and Empagliflozin.
Tiffen-Becker arrangement: transfer-priced supply with about 43% of the customer's margin shared with Ind-Swift.
Management expects no dearth of capacity for the planned growth; new partnerships under discussion with 3-4 existing overseas customers, not expected to contribute this year.

512068|2026-06.headline: Deccan Gold Q1 FY27: Jonnagiri sold 59 kg gold for ~Rs87 Cr revenue, Rs6.35 Cr share of PAT; Rs137 Cr fundraise approved by Board.
512068|2026-06.overview: Management said the June quarter established the company as a producer, led by Jonnagiri (Geomysore Services) gold production and first dore output from Altyn Tor (Kyrgyzstan). Jonnagiri sold about 59 kg of gold for about Rs87 Cr revenue and Rs25 Cr PAT, of which Deccan's share was Rs6.35 Cr; about 80 kg of gold equivalent sits in inventory. Management framed the company as having two verticals, gold and battery-metal critical minerals, and said Rs137 Cr of CCDs, equity and warrants is pending shareholder approval. Management said the next quarter should be much bigger, but margins were low in Q1 and the company asked for another quarter before giving clearer guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: Gold inventory at quarter end (incl. dore)
financial_highlights.value: About 80 kg gold equivalent (40 kg gold + 60 kg dore)
Rs137 Cr via CCDs, equity shares and warrants

segments.name: Jonnagiri (Geomysore, gold, India)
segments.commentary: Q1 sales of 59 kg gold for about Rs87 Cr revenue and Rs25 Cr PAT; Deccan's share Rs6.35 Cr. Production about 1 kg/day, with 2,500 tpd expansion planned, targeting up to 2 tonnes/yr around FY29-30.

segments.name: Altyn Tor (Kyrgyzstan, gold)
segments.commentary: Dore production started via Merrill-Crowe; gravity circuit and leach circuit added. Full-scale commissioning expected soon; tailings of about 0.6 Mt at about 1.3 g/t for first 4-5 years of output.

segments.name: Kalevala (Finland, gold)
segments.commentary: Drilling to start around Sept 15; about 1,500 m planned. Kuikka mining lease pending; feasibility targeted in 2027; production seen 2028-29 or later with about 800 tpd plant.

segments.name: Critical minerals (Chhattisgarh nickel-copper-PGE, Bhalukona)
segments.commentary: 2,500 m drilled, 1.3 km mineralised zone identified; resource estimate and mining lease application targeted next year; 3,000 tpd plant considered.

segments.name: Logrosan tungsten (Spain)
segments.commentary: About 3,000 m drilled; full Dehesa results expected mid-September, resource model by early October; 1,000 tpd plant considered.

segments.name: Mozambique lithium-tantalum
segments.commentary: About 150 sq km, three licences; 200 tpd concentrator targeted by end-2027 or Q1 2028 for concentrate.

guidance_outlook: Jonnagiri FY27 production 500-600 kg (earlier guidance retained); FY28 750-800 kg. Management will confirm after next quarter.
Altyn Tor: about 150-160 kg in FY27 and 300-350 kg thereafter, per management comments.
Jonnagiri EBITDA margin expected to stabilise at 65-70% within one to two quarters; Q1 margins were significantly lower.
Altyn Tor revised mine design and life-of-mine plan by October 2026; underground resource above 5 Mt could extend mine life by 6-7 years.
Dividend from Geomysore unlikely in FY27 per management; may come next year, not guaranteed.
Capex: about Rs400-500 Cr per 1,000 tpd plant; Bhalukona 3,000 tpd about Rs650-700 Cr; Altyn Tor underground Rs150-200 Cr in 3-4 years; Jonnagiri shaft work possibly above Rs400 Cr in 4-5 years.
capex_capacity: Jonnagiri processing approvals of 1,010 tpd, with expansion to 2,500 tpd being sought; Bhumi Puja done for expansion.
Altyn Tor leach circuit and new tailings dam (10-year life) under construction; commissioning date to be announced after Chairman-level visit next week.
Finland: about 1,500 m drilling from mid-September; Kuikka pit targets about 70 kg gold; underground mines planned.
Chhattisgarh: 15th drill hole under way; plan 3,000 tpd plant; process flow sheet by mid-next-year.
Spain: Dehesa first-phase drilling complete; Maria drilling from end of this month; 40 sq km Maria licence plus 30 sq km pending.
Mozambique: 1,500-2,000 m drilling from September; 200 tpd concentrator by end-2027.
demand_pricing: Management said gold price in Q1 was about Rs1,50,000 per 10 grams and improved in the current quarter, supporting holding inventory.
Tungsten prices up 622% and tantalum up 196% over the last year; lithium up 108%; graphite up 5% (management figures).
Management plans to sell Jonnagiri stock in the coming quarter; Q1 sales lagged production because the inauguration was on June 24.
Dore from Jonnagiri is refined in-house at a small refinery (cost about Rs4-5 Cr); Altyn Tor dore must go to a government refinery at LBMA price.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Jonnagiri profit margin well below the expected ~65% EBITDA, and what is the outlook for Jonnagiri and Kyrgyzstan revenue and profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said low Q1 sales (59 kg) and initial expenses explain the low margin; 65-70% EBITDA margin expected in one to two quarters. Further clarity expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex estimate and funding plan for the project pipeline (about Rs2,000 Cr)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than Rs1,000 Cr is needed for the next two or three projects; funding via offtake arrangements for critical minerals, combined debt and equity; gold projects possibly 50:50 or 40:60 equity to debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bhalukona be funded by a rights issue like the earlier Rs80 per share issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm a specific route; said the Rs137 Cr raise is a bridge and a larger QIP may follow once drilling outcomes are clearer.

qa_highlights.question: Will Hutti Gold and Ganajur progress, and what is the legal position?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganajur is a mining lease with court proceedings pending; management cited recent judgments on restoring pre-2015 rights. Hutti is a prospecting licence, so it is more tedious; focus remains on Ganajur.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be dividends from Jonnagiri, and is a strategic promoter being sought?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend depends on Geomysore board; management doubts dividends this financial year. No decision yet on a large strategic promoter; the company remains professionally run.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the company not refine dore in Kyrgyzstan?
qa_highlights.answer: Kyrgyz law requires dore to be sent to a government refinery, which settles at LBMA price; no in-house refinery is possible there.

544496|2026-06.headline: Vikran Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 28.2% YoY to INR204 crore and PAT 209.9% to INR17.5 crore, while consolidated PAT was only INR4 crore.

506655|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs.2,642 Cr and business EBITDA Rs.247 Cr for One Sudarshan; FY27 guidance held pending Q2 review.
506655|2026-06.overview: Management reported a strong Q1 FY27 for One Sudarshan, with revenue from operations of Rs.2,642 Cr, business EBITDA of Rs.247 Cr and reported EBITDA of Rs.266 Cr, cited as roughly 60%+ YoY EBITDA growth and about 5% revenue growth. The acquired (Heubach/Clariant pigments) group delivered business EBITDA of Rs.128 Cr versus Rs.65 Cr a year ago, while RIECO was weak with revenue of Rs.38 Cr on customer readiness and subcontractor labour issues. Net debt fell to Rs.531 Cr from a Rs.922 Cr peak. Management kept the acquired-group guidance of EUR 700 Mn turnover and EUR 35 Mn EBITDA unchanged, citing geopolitical uncertainty, and will review it after Q2.

financial_highlights.change: from Rs.78 Cr; inventory overhead impact Rs.18 Cr

financial_highlights.value: ~6% (modest growth, per Rathi), ~5% (per Rathi's acquired-group remark)
financial_highlights.change: YoY; prior-year Q1 base included only partial post-acquisition sales
management: movement of ~2% QoQ, sustained at 50%+

segments.name: Acquired group (pigments, ex-RIECO)
segments.commentary: Business EBITDA Rs.128 Cr vs Rs.65 Cr YoY; reported EBITDA Rs.146 Cr after Rs.18 Cr inventory overhead impact. Management says business margin has been consistently double-digit historically, and sees a 6-7% level as a stepping stone to high single or low double digits.

segments.name: RIECO
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.38 Cr, with EBITDA down on execution delays (customer readiness, subcontractor manpower shortages). Management expects normalisation from Q2 and a positive EBITDA before year end.

guidance_outlook: Acquired group FY27 guidance unchanged: turnover EUR 700 Mn and EBITDA EUR 35 Mn; management will revisit after Q2 despite a stronger Q1.
Legacy Sudarshan growth expected at roughly 12-13% in the near term.
Value capture and cost reduction are expected to drive most EBITDA growth, mainly in FY27-FY28, with some flowing into FY29.
FY29 consolidated targets (about 16-17% revenue CAGR at higher end and EBITDA near doubling vs FY27) are described as previously stated, not new.
Revenue of Rs.12,000 Cr+ cited as the long-term projection from the investor deck (slide 9).
Gross margin expected to stay above 50%; seasonality expected in Q3.
capex_capacity: No new capex needed for volume growth in guided numbers, per management; existing capacity is sufficient.
Possible moderate capex for backward integration or special projects, to be approved only on acceptable ROI.
Global capability centre set up in Pune; second global headquarters opened in Frankfurt.
Project Integra (One SAP) targeted to go live within FY27; currently running more than four SAP instances and 130 applications.
Management cites 55-60% of assets located in Asia.
demand_pricing: Customers delayed purchases amid geopolitical uncertainty; logistics cycle lengthened by about two weeks.
Energy, raw material and logistics costs rose in Europe and India; price increases so far passed on cost increases only, with management committing to reverse pricing if raw materials soften.

Coatings: US decorative and automotive subdued; plastics demand choppy on polymer price spikes and hand-to-mouth buying; volume printing inks declining while specialty inks, agro and digital inks grow well.
Management says a meaningful part of growth will come from recapturing business lost post-integration (lack of focus, insolvency issues), not from market growth.
Pigment pricing is contract-driven; switching pigments takes 1-2 years, up to 5 years in automotive, and pricing is generally negotiated quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 growth reflects underlying volume after FX translation and price increases; can growth be 2-2.5x industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the volume-decline inference, citing ~6% growth and a weak prior-year Q1 base with partial post-acquisition sales. It said growth will come from winning back lost business and value capture.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA path to FY29 is volume versus cost/value capture?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is substantially cost reduction and value capture.

qa_highlights.question: Capex needs in the next 12-18 months?
qa_highlights.answer: No volume capex needed; only moderate capex on backward integration or special projects if ROI is good.

qa_highlights.question: Is ~54% gross margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin moved about 2% QoQ on yields, utilities and production cost cuts, plus minor one-offs; management expects 50%+ to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Debt repayment plans and RIECO hive-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Some acquisition debt has been prepaid, with faster repayment planned as net debt falls. RIECO is in transformation with no hive-off mentioned; management expects a positive EBITDA before year end.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the acquired group's stake in Sudarshan Colorants held indirectly, and what is the restructuring provision after June 30?
qa_highlights.answer: The indirect holding was for financing reasons, with a plan to hold directly from the parent, so this is group restructuring with no business impact. The restructuring charge is not yet quantifiable, with clarity expected by end of Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance conservative given Q1 run-rate, and is 6-7% margin the steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not revising guidance until Q2 review. It does not expect 15%+ margins; the target is high single digit to low double digit.

risks_watch: Unquantified restructuring charge tied to a post-June 30 employee agreement at a European subsidiary; quantification expected by end Q2.
FY27 guidance not revised despite a strong Q1; Q2 result is the next checkpoint.
RIECO execution: revenue Rs.38 Cr and EBITDA decline in Q1; recovery depends on labour and customer readiness.
Raw material and energy volatility (Middle East crisis) and logistics delays; pricing may need reversal if raw material costs fall.
Delayed customer purchasing and subdued US/EU coatings demand.
Project Integra (One SAP) go-live and value capture delivery within FY27.

540404|2026-06.headline: Prime Fresh Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15.7% to INR81.71 crore and EBITDA jumped 51% to INR6 crore (9.83% margin), which management says is not fully sustainable.
540404|2026-06.overview: Prime Fresh reported Q1 FY27 sales of INR81.71 crore (vs INR53.34 crore), EBITDA of INR6 crore (9.83% margin vs 7.53%) and PAT of INR4.35 crore (vs INR2.89 crore). Management attributed part of the jump to one-off recoveries of pending service-business billings, inventory gains from rising F&V and onion prices, and strong service volumes, and guided that margins may not be sustained. Forward guidance is EBITDA margin of 7% to 7.5% and volume growth of 15% to 25%, with value growth of 25% to 30%. The company is pursuing the Nashik cluster development project under the National Horticulture Board, expected to be awarded in August 2026, and a Bank of Baroda working capital limit increase to INR20 crore.

financial_highlights.metric: Bank of Baroda cash credit limit
financial_highlights.change: Raised from INR7.8 crore at 8.5% cost

segments.name: F&V business (B2B)
segments.commentary: Management stated FY23 sales of about INR275 crore, of which about INR245 crore plus came from F&V and the balance from service business. B2C is 1% to 2% of business; exports stopped post-COVID.

segments.name: Service business
segments.commentary: Q1 saw good volume growth and strong margins, plus recovery of old pending billings that aided the quarter. Management said this contribution is not expected to recur at the same level.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Florens Farming Ltd is the key focus for own farming and land tie-ups; management said it contributes about 10% of F&V and could pay off from next year. Prime Fresh Retail India Pvt Ltd is held for strategic partners; B2C entry deferred.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 7% to 7.5%; net profit margin guidance stated as 5.5% to 5% (as transcribed, likely a typo).
Volume growth of 15% to 20% minimum in one answer and 15% to 25% in closing remarks; value growth of 25% to 30%.
Internal aspiration of 9.5% to 11% EBITDA margin in 2 to 2.5 years (around 2029) and a vision of INR2,000 crore revenue by 2031; longer-term EBITDA margin of 14% to 16% in 4 to 5 years.
Operating margin expected to rise slowly from mid-FY28.
Debtor target of 88 to 94 days of sales, debtors below 25% of sales, and no single rupee of working capital or equity needed for an incremental INR60 crore sale by FY29.
Product portfolio to add three to four more categories within a year (currently 9 to 12 F&V products).
capex_capacity: Nashik (Sinnar) cluster development programme under National Horticulture Board: company as implementing agency; expected award in August 2026; INR75 crore investment (excluding INR5-6 crore preoperative spend), of which INR50-52 crore eligible for 40-50% grant (about INR24 crore grant expected on milestones).
Capex to start around end-October to end-November 2026 over 18 to 20 months; Phase 1 INR6-9 crore, Phase 2 INR12-15 crore, balance in Phase 3, funded from own balance sheet including debt.
Project debt peak about INR35 crore against INR42 crore sanctioned, falling to INR18-20 crore after grants.
Farmer component of about INR60 crore with around 35% government subsidy; target of 15,000 farmers and 15,000 tons incremental sourcing in year 1, scaling to 2 lakh tons in six years.
Sourcing capacity close to 2.5 lakh tons vs FY sales of about 65,000 tons.
demand_pricing: Customer mix: about 20 large modern trade and e-commerce accounts, around 90 APMC partners, 10 to 15 food processors, 20 to 30 exporters; added four to five food processing customers in Q1.
Price pass-through of 4 to 8 days on procurement changes for most business; HoReCa about one month; 5-star and tender business up to 3 months, which is under 4% of business.
Pomegranate: about 13,000 farmers and 40 plus local area aggregators; onion prices rising sharply, benefiting inventory gains.
Procurement advantage of direct farm sourcing stated at 3% to 15% on price, with 10% to 15% operational cost initially; long-term advantage 5% to 8% over supplier purchase.
Company is positioned as a pan-India supplier to modern trade and e-commerce across 10 cities for onion, pomegranate and orange.

qa_highlights.question: Can receivables (about one-third of revenue) be reduced and can trade payables be extended?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a client credit exposure system, stricter onboarding with PDCs and security cheques, and about INR12 crore debtor reduction in Q1. It aims at 88-94 debtor days and a 25% of sales cap; a BoB limit rise to INR20 crore plus INR20 crore for Nashik was cited; payables to farmers are expected to rise to INR10-15 crore on credit by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What does the Nashik Sinnar project add beyond the asset-light model?
qa_highlights.answer: Prime Fresh is implementing agency for a farmer component (subsidy-led) and an IA component of INR75 crore with 40-50% grant on eligible capex; it aims at order-book model, farm-gate packhouse and cold chain, and a separate call was offered.

qa_highlights.question: Cumulative capex, revenue/tonnage and margin impact, and replication to other cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex over about 18-20 months with phased balance-sheet spend; quantified margin uplift not given. Replication via subsidiary or SPV route is open, with full equity payback in up to 5 years targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Lag between procurement price changes and customer price resets?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 4 to 8 days; HoReCa up to one month; tender business up to three months, under 4% of business.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q1 trading and direct expenses up faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the numbers and said it would respond by mail.

qa_highlights.question: Why not enter B2C given the city footprint?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C needs heavy upfront investment; an earlier franchise attempt cost INR55-75 lakh in 2021-2023. Management decided not to pursue it now, with B2C at 1-2% of business.

530007|2026-06.headline: JK Tyre Q1FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell to Rs.268 crore (6.8% margin) from Rs.424 crore, as raw material costs rose ~20% QoQ.
530007|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 2% YoY to Rs.3,956 crore, while EBITDA dropped about 37% YoY to Rs.268 crore and PAT was Rs.43 crore. India domestic volumes grew 25% YoY, led by 42% OEM growth, but India revenue growth was about 14%, implying weaker realisations. Mexico (JK Tornel) was hit by input shortages and a productivity-related slowdown, and net debt rose Rs.500 crore QoQ to Rs.4,945 crore. Management guided to margin recovery from the second half, with 10-11% FY27 operating margins as the working assumption.

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to equity / Net debt to EBITDA

segments.name: India domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes grew 25% YoY across replacement and OE; OEM volumes grew 42%, TBR OE +18% and TBR replacement +15%. Net sales realisation rose about 5% QoQ and about 4% YoY on a standalone basis.

segments.name: Passenger lines (PCR)
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 10% YoY, led by OEM. Sixteen-inch and above rim sizes make up 35% of PCR sales volume.

segments.name: Farm
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 31% YoY, with OEM +35% and replacement +25%.

segments.name: 2/3-wheeler
segments.commentary: OE volumes grew 17% and replacement volumes grew 48% YoY.

segments.name: JK Tornel (Mexico)
segments.commentary: Output was constrained by input shortages (bead wire largely from China, shipping disruption) and a productivity-negotiation slowdown, since resolved. An analyst cited a decline of about 82%, which management did not dispute.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth expected at good double digits (about 10-11%), driven by price hikes and volume, with new capacity running fully by Q3 FY27.
FY27 operating margin guided at about 10-11%, which management said may be below FY26; margins expected to improve progressively from H2 FY27, returning to 11-13%.
Further price increases of 8-9% planned; cumulative increase of about 11% taken in the replacement market to date.
Raw material costs expected to rise a further 8-10% in Q2 from higher-cost inventory, then stabilise; natural rubber expected to stay range-bound after some softening.
Total debt expected to rise by Rs.500-700 crore in FY27 to fund capex and working capital.
Mexico expected to deliver better results than Q1 in the remaining three quarters.
capex_capacity: Expansion plan worth Rs.4,980 crore for PCR and TBR at the Chennai tyre plant (about 24% capacity addition over roughly four years, per management).
Capacity additions in the next financial year to be mainly TBR and passenger car, plus balancing at Banmore; expected to add about 7% to current installed capacity.
Indian capacity utilisation about 95%; consolidated utilisation about 80%. TBR and 2/3W near full; PCR about 95%; LCV and farm above 95%.
Upgradation and modernisation project under way at JK Tornel, Mexico.
demand_pricing: Indian auto retail sales grew more than 15% (FADA source); PV +23%, CV +14%, 2/3W +14%, farm +22%.
Price hike of about 5% taken in Q1, applied in monthly staggered steps; 8-9% more planned, with OEM price increases flowing with a lag.
Natural rubber (RSS4) prices softening in India; management hopes for a fall by next quarter.
Export volumes from India rose 2% QoQ.
Product mix at consolidated level: truck and bus 56%, passenger line radial 27%, 2/3W 5%, others 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Vijay Kumar (Axis Capital): India volume growth of 25% versus India revenue growth of about 14%; does this imply lower pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic volumes grew 25% YoY; net effective price increase was about 4% YoY on a standalone basis and NSR rose about 5% QoQ. OEM prices lag, so the full effect will show in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Vijay Kumar: What drove the Mexico weakness, and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Bajoria cited constrained inputs (bead wire from China, shipping disruption, container shortages, NR up about 18%) and productivity negotiations with workers; these are resolved and management expects better results in the remaining three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Bhagnani (Living Root Analytics): What margin and revenue trajectory for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins to improve progressively from H2 FY27 once raw material costs stabilise; price hikes should cover the RM increase except 1-2%. FY27 revenue growth guided at about 10-11%; operating margin about 10-11%.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Bhagnani: Will debt rise this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, net debt is expected to rise by Rs.500-700 crore in FY27 due to capex disbursements and working capital, partly offset by repayments and internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: Krish Jain (NAFA): What capacity utilisation and additions are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: India utilisation about 95%, consolidated about 80%. Capacity additions of about 7% by next financial year, mainly TBR and PCR, with the full run-rate expected by Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Digant Shah (DAM Capital): Will Mexico production normalise to Q3/Q4 revenue levels? What is the USMCA status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected the record: it was a slowdown, not a strike. Production has resumed and is near normal, with similar topline expected. USMCA has been renewed for 10 years.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on RM cost stabilisation after a further 8-10% increase expected in Q2 FY27 from high-cost inventory.
Mexico output recovery and the sustainability of the bead wire supply from China amid US-China tensions.
Net debt rising to about Rs.5,400-5,600 crore by year-end (Rs.500-700 crore increase) with net debt/EBITDA at 2.56x in Q1, against a margin recovery that is not yet visible.
Price hike realisation (8-9% planned) versus volume response, with OEM price lags.
EV tyre replacement life: management cited about 5-10% shorter life due to higher torque, with the degree depending on usage.

544238|2026-06.headline: Premier Energies Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34% YoY to INR2,508 crores, PAT up 53% to INR472 crores at an 18.8% margin.
544238|2026-06.overview: Management reported record Q1 revenue and profit, with EBITDA up 27% to INR759 crores at a 30.3% margin and PAT up 53% to INR472 crores; results include consolidation of the 51% stake in Transcon. The 5.6 GW Seetharampur module plant is operational, while the 7 GW TOPCon cell line is in late commissioning with trial runs expected later in August. Order wins were INR3,011 crores in the quarter, taking the total order book to INR15,000 crores including transformers. Management said the ALMM extension to December triggered a surge in non-DCR module orders, while DCR is sold out through FY28 per management.

financial_highlights.value: INR18 crores (17% PAT margin, 27% EBITDA margin)
About INR1,500 crores (INR1,250 crores solar, INR250 crores Transcon)

segments.name: Solar cells and modules
segments.commentary: Cells were about 24% of Q1 revenue and about 58% of the order book per analyst figures cited on the call. Modules are mainly DCR; management said DCR is sold out and selling only for FY28, while non-DCR realisations softened on oversupply.

segments.name: Transformers (Transcon, 51%)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue INR110 crores, PAT INR18 crores; management expects business to roughly treble over three years, with transformer capacity going from 4 GVA to 16.25 GVA by FY28. Last year's revenue was about INR400 crores.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Land acquired and construction started on a 12 GWh plan, with Phase 1 at 6 GWh; technology partner for containerised solution expected to be finalised in 2-3 months.

guidance_outlook: Margins guided at 29-30% (plus or minus 100-150 bps), supported by 7 GW cell line, transformer scale-up and ingot-wafer backward integration.
First revenue from 7 GW cell line targeted in September; about 50-60% utilisation by November; at least 70% targeted by March quarter.
Depreciation expected to rise to about INR240-250 crores per quarter in Q3 and Q4 FY27 as Seetharampur and Naidupeta lines are capitalised.
Transformer revenue ramp expected to be slightly below analyst's INR600-700 crore FY27 estimate given certification and type-testing lead times; revenue expected to rise substantially over two years.
Management expects at least 40-45% of the INR15,000 crore order book to execute in FY28.
Management sees no concrete plan to raise primary capital in the near future; enabling resolution is precautionary.
Europe export office being opened; US cell manufacturing JV expected to produce output in 24-30 months.
capex_capacity: 5.6 GW fully automated solar module plant at Seetharampur is operational.
7 GW TOPCon cell line (Naidupeta/Tirupati) in advanced commissioning; trial runs expected later in August 2026; first revenue targeted in September.
Telangana operational cell plants ran at a record 92% utilisation in Q1.
Transformer capacity to rise from 4 GVA to 16.25 GVA by FY28; ingot-wafer lines under way.
BESS 12 GWh plan with 6 GWh Phase 1 under construction.
demand_pricing: Analyst-cited estimates: about 12 GW of solar capacity added in Q1 CY/FY across market; management expects about 6-8 GW AC (over 8 GW possible) of KUSUM installations over next nine months, with blended DC overloading of 1.2-1.25x, plus 1.2-1.3 GW per quarter from PM Surya Ghar.

Non-DCR orders surged after the ALMM extension to December; management says non-DCR business is not profitable currently with over 200-250 GW module capacity against about 30 GW non-DCR demand, though prices improved slightly for the coming quarter.
DCR module realisations stable: Surya Ghar about 24-24.5 cents/W, KUSUM about 22 cents/W, C&I slightly lower; no change expected over 12-15 months as orders are booked.
Cell pricing (mono-PERC) stable; long-term cell contracts have variable wafer, silver and FX pass-through. Most orders are USD-linked.

Management said the cell-to-DCR-module mix will shift steadily over the next 18-24 months; cell sales expected at about 50-50 internal vs external split historically, skewing to internal use as ALMM Phase 2 and DCR demand grow.
US minimum import price proposal on cells and modules cited as making US manufacturing attractive; Europe tenders in Italy and France and expected in Germany.

qa_highlights.question: How much DC overloading should be assumed for PM KUSUM, and what is the demand outlook for the next nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended overloading of 1.2-1.25x (KUSUM B at 1.0x, KUSUM C at 1.3-1.5x). Management expects about 1.2-1.3 GW per quarter of rooftop and 6-8 GW AC (possibly more than 8 GW) of KUSUM over nine months; total about 23-24 GW DC over nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Why sell cells rather than convert them into DCR modules and capture the margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legacy cell contracts signed earlier must be honoured; as the 7 GW cell line starts, DCR module output will rise and cell sales will fall. Q1 module orders were mostly for modules.

qa_highlights.question: Will C&I demand be deferred by the ALMM extension, and is DCR capacity blocked?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said C&I clients are already blocking capacity for FY28 and are not deferring; DCR is sold out with FY28 sales underway.

qa_highlights.question: Is 29-30% EBITDA margin sustainable over the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets maintaining 29-30% (plus or minus 100-150 bps), citing 7 GW cell line, transformer scale-up and backward integration into ingot-wafer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the transformer revenue ramp for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the initial ramp to be slightly below the analyst's INR600-700 crore FY27 estimate; business to treble over three years versus last year's INR400 crores; margins targeted slightly above the historical 15% EBITDA / 8-10% PAT cycle average.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses and employee costs jump sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to advance hiring for Seetharampur and Naidupeta, power costs of Seetharampur built up before July ramp-up, and corporate hiring tied to acquisitions. Per-GW manpower at Seetharampur is expected about 40% lower.

532482|2026-09.headline: Granules pivots to four growth engines; plans ~2,000 crore organic capex over 3-4 years after warrant-funded move to net cash.
532482|2026-09.overview:
Management, at an IIFL-hosted "Granules India 2.0" webinar, framed FY27 onward as a shift from building capabilities to scaling them, after a return to growth in FY26. Four growth engines were named: controlled substances, complex generics/early market entry, oncology, and peptide CDMO (Senn Tides). The CFO said the company is now in a consolidated net cash position following September 2026 preferential warrant proceeds, and plans about 2,000 crore of organic capex over three to four years. Management was candid that gross margin gains (about 15 pp over four years) have not yet fully flowed to EBITDA, and that the peptide business is currently loss-making. No quarterly financial figures for Q2 FY27 were given in the call.</overview>

segments.name: US (anchor market)
segments.commentary: About 75% of overall revenue; currently retail-focused across OTC and Rx, with first specialty/institutional launch expected in FY29 and a B2C division in Canada next year.

segments.name: Controlled substances (US Rx)
segments.commentary: Now the third-largest US controlled substance manufacturer by value per IQVIA (eighth in July 2025). Top-three position in six of seven ADHD products marketed; Adderall XR share rose from 5% (2024) to 29%.

segments.name: Complex generics / first-to-file
segments.commentary: Two sole first-to-file ANDAs filed (generic Lumryz and generic Dyanavel, combined US market above $350 million, potential 180-day exclusivity); four to five further first-to-files planned for FY30-34 commercialisation.

segments.name: Oncology
segments.commentary: Shifted from broad conventional oncology generics to selected molecules; two products filed, one extended to about 15 countries; about six more filings planned this year and early next year. Commercialisation begins FY29.

segments.name: Peptide CDMO (Senn Tides India / Senn Chemicals, Switzerland)
segments.commentary: Acquired about 18 months ago; currently EBITDA-negative with target to turn profitable in FY27. Targets about $50 million revenue run-rate in three years and above $100 million in five years. About one-third of about $20 million revenue is development-based.

segments.name: Europe and ROW (API and PFI-led)
segments.commentary: Management plans a meaningful Latin America and other international presence by FY30 using B2B and B2C channels.

532735|2026-06.headline: R Systems Q2 CY26 revenue rose 4.7% QoQ to Rs 601.7 crore ($63.6M) with adjusted EBITDA margin at a record 20.1%.
532735|2026-06.overview:
Revenue grew 30.2% YoY in rupees and 17.7% in dollars, with 1.2% QoQ dollar growth, aided by rupee depreciation and the Novigo acquisition. Adjusted EBITDA reached Rs 120.7 crore (20.1% margin), but adjusted PAT fell 17.1% QoQ to Rs 62.9 crore because Q1 included a one-time hedge-accounting benefit of about Rs 18 crore. Management pointed to higher sales and marketing spend and a wage hike cycle, and declined to give numerical guidance. Constant-currency organic growth remained muted, and management argued that ACV bookings and pipeline quality would convert into revenue in the second half.</overview>

segments.name: Geography: Americas
segments.commentary: Rose to 71.5% of revenue from 69.3%.

segments.name: Geography: APAC
segments.commentary: Fell to 15.3% as larger projects in the prior quarter ended.

segments.name: Geography: Europe / MEA
segments.commentary: Europe at 9.7% and Middle East and Africa at 3.6%, both broadly flat.

segments.name: Client concentration
segments.commentary: Top client 6.0% (from 5.8%); top 10 clients 24.4% (from 24.0%).

guidance_outlook: Management does not provide formal guidance.
Sustainable adjusted EBITDA band of 18-19%, with excess margin reinvested in AI, sales and marketing.
Constant-currency growth of 3-4% is tracked, though management said it could slip to about 2% when decisions are delayed.
Wins in H1 are expected to convert to revenue in H2; sales and marketing spend is intended to build ACV wins for the following half.
No quantified deal-win guidance; deal wins will continue to be reported on a trailing 12-month basis.
capex_capacity: Utilization 80.5-81%, which management said is the target band; bench investments made over the last 2-3 quarters are now being deployed to revenue-generating work.
Headcount broadly flat YoY despite the 18% QoQ revenue growth; productivity gains attributed to AI-led delivery (EXIQO AI Studio cited at about 2x productivity and 55% faster turnaround).
Biannual wage hike cycle; first cycle implemented in Q2 and already in the reported margins.
Novigo acquisition integrated by end of Q4 CY25 and fully consolidated in Q1 CY26.
demand_pricing: Trailing-12-month ACV bookings $82.9 million in Q2 vs $82.3 million in Q1, roughly flat.

Q2 wins included a global telecom analytics deal, a small-business lender GCC set-up in India, a BFSI AI quality-engineering win, a market-access firm's Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM programme, and an ad-tech platform modernisation.
Data, AI and cloud now above 50% of revenue (no explicit figure given).
Management says it does not face AI-driven price deflation because AI productivity is built into bids and multi-year renewal contracts are not common.
Billed DSO about 55-56 days; billed plus unbilled about 75 days.
Novigo faces a Middle East geopolitical headwind but is winning deals across markets, including the Middle East.
Wallet share has risen in top-50 clients, mainly in BFSI through AI business operations.
GCC revenue share not disclosed; management described GCC as a growth vector.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SG&A rise about USD 2M QoQ, and is there added sales hiring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a Chief Revenue Officer hire, more sales bandwidth, AI and domain experts in sales, and marketing spend around the EXIQO brand launch, with the investment described as deliberate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year organic growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given. Management said trailing-12-month numbers are positive, H1 bookings flow into H2 revenue, and the company is confident in its momentum.

qa_highlights.question: Why was ACV flat QoQ in Q2 after a strong Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TTM wins are at least as high as before and Q2 had a few large deals that offset a large Q2 last year, with pipeline quality improving.

qa_highlights.question: Is Novigo adding to growth and how is its order flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Novigo integration added inorganic growth through Q1 CY26. Management said Novigo's earlier organic cliff is now matched, and it is winning deals including in the Middle East.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wage hike and near-term margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: A biannual wage hike was implemented in Q2 and is already in the numbers. Management reiterated an 18-19% sustainable adjusted EBITDA band, with FX a non-controllable tailwind.

qa_highlights.question: When will CC growth return to 3-4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said decision delays drive the timing; it expects consistent growth as the pipeline converts, but gave no date.

risks_watch: Adjusted PAT down 17.1% QoQ on the Q1 one-time hedge benefit of about Rs 18 crore; quality of earnings depends on rupee moves.
Q2 forward-cover book of $43.32 million at an average rate of 93.27; realised hedge loss of Rs 9 crore and exchange loss of Rs 2.1 crore weighed on other income.
Rupee-driven margin uplift management called uncontrollable; the 18-19% EBITDA band is the stated floor for reinvestment.
SG&A up Rs 23.8 crore QoQ; sales investment must convert to ACV, as TTM ACV was flat.
Constant-currency organic growth is muted and was about 2% in the period discussed; watch whether it moves to the 3-4% range.
Novigo's Middle East exposure given the geopolitical situation.
Annuity revenue remains small; deal durations are project-based.

532875|2026-06.headline: Allied Digital Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs. 260 crore, but PAT fell to Rs. 12 crore from Rs. 14 crore on higher tax and margin pressure.
532875|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 19% YoY to Rs. 260 crore and PBT rose 19% to about Rs. 17 crore, while EBITDA was Rs. 25 crore at a 10% margin. Trailing 12-month revenue crossed Rs. 1,000 crore (Rs. 1,009 crore). Management said the audit report is now unmodified, with all earlier auditor qualifications resolved. Management acknowledged competitive pricing pressure in the US and India hardware-linked deals, and said margins are under pressure across the industry. Management also said revenue declined quarter-on-quarter, which it attributed to cautious deal-making and delayed large government and hardware-linked orders.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY26 had net tax benefit of Rs. 0.3 crore
vs Rs. 14 crore in Q1 FY26 (decline)

guidance_outlook: Long-term aspiration of 10x growth over 10 years, about 20% CAGR, with some quarters varying with macroeconomic conditions.
Management expects EBITDA margin of 10-11% currently, and says margins could reach 12-13% once large deals kick in over a couple of quarters.
Management expects new deal announcements from the pipeline in the next one to two quarters (Q2 or Q3 FY27), once hardware prices bottom out and RFPs are issued.
No specific FY28 guidance given; management said timing of margin recovery is uncertain.
capex_capacity: Management says it is investing in AI, people, mid-level leadership and governance, which weighed on margins.
Finance costs rose modestly due to higher working capital deployment as large projects moved into execution.
demand_pricing: Order book: orders of Rs. 120-plus crore booked in the quarter, including new wins and multiyear renewals.

Key wins included a US NYSE-listed electronics company (application maintenance on ServiceNow, Jitterbit and Boomi, entry into US Enterprise Application Services), an Australian mutual bank (workspace services), a Punjab government command and control centre, a Ministry of Commerce body (managed services), an international property consultant (IT asset management) and an Indian FMCG company (IT infrastructure support).
Management said customers are more measured, procurement cycles are longer, and it sees a timing shift rather than weaker underlying demand.
Railway orders of Rs. 180-200 crore were lost after product (hardware) prices rose 25-30% during bidding; the company withdrew to avoid losses.
Competitive pressure in the US market with margin-reduction demands from clients over the last 4-8 quarters; customers seeking discounts in anticipation of automation.
Management said it stayed away from low-margin customer acquisition in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 due to hardware price volatility, and that revenue declined quarter-on-quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why have EBITDA and PAT margins been declining for 3-4 years, and how can they improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited competitive pressure over the last 4-8 quarters, especially in the US, and investments in hiring, leadership and AI. It expects margins to improve in the next few quarters as automation is rolled out to clients.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI a threat or benefit, and is it causing revenue deflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called AI an opportunity and a boon. It said revenue pressure comes from two causes: hardware price increases in India and the company's choice to avoid low-margin deals. Exact AI impact will be clear only once automation is implemented at client level.

qa_highlights.question: When will margin pressure bottom out, and what is the FY28 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot give a timeline because the market is in flux, and that margins are under pressure across the industry as customers seek discounts. It pointed to 10x growth in 10 years (about 20% a year) as the guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What constraints are delaying revenue conversion, and when will growth inflect?

544917|2026-06.headline: Karamtara Q1 FY27 revenue rose 72% YoY to INR1,581 crore, EBITDA INR174 crore (~11% margin), PAT INR87 crore; FY27 growth target 60-65%.
544917|2026-06.overview:
Karamtara's first call as a listed company reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR1,581 crore (+72% YoY), EBITDA of INR174 crore (+45% YoY, ~11% margin) and PAT of INR87 crore (+45% YoY). Management said the quarter was hit by elevated freight and tariff-related costs, which it expects to ease, and reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 60-65%. Transmission was flagged as the next major growth driver, with new Bhachau capacity ramping and a Saudi Arabia plant targeted for trials around December. Management gave no FY28 numbers and no explicit margin guidance.</overview>
