capex_capacity: Sotanala project: total about INR200 crore (INR50 crore formulation, INR150 crore technical); about INR70 crore invested to date. Formulation expected around April-May 2027, technical production by Diwali 2026, with 5-6 products in phase 1.
Dahej: about 50-60% of equipment utilised for the new plant; new power connection and a new boiler upcoming. Management sees at least INR200 crore of potential addition to technical production.
Chopanki expansion completed; Dahej more than 70% commercialised, with the remaining 20-30% expected soon.
Udhampur: investment to separate herbicide and insecticide plants, expected to complete within 2026.
IIL Crop Solutions: plots to be doubled from 36 to cover 14 states and 4 crops (rice, cotton, chilli, soybean).
Management expects to tighten power and steam costs through solar, wind and solid fuel, with benefits from end-Q2 onwards.
demand_pricing: Monsoon: delayed and uneven, with channel activity starting early in March. Management said August rains were good, but rice sowing lagged in South India (about 40% pending in Karnataka, Andhra and Tamil Nadu) and MP and some eastern states were dry.
Volume fell about 13% YoY in Q1, with value up about 2%, implying price/mix gains of about 2%.
Price hikes: one in March, two in April, and one attempted in May but rolled back as demand weakened; no significant price increase was realised through July.

Raw material pressure: solvent prices moved 25-30% week to week and some doubled; plastic, HDPE, emulsifiers and some technicals rose sharply, with freight and container scarcity worsening supply chains.
Management said inventory was slightly elevated in June and is expected to decline sharply in Q2 quarter.
Management said gross margin bands by product type: generics about 10-15% (up to 20-25% in some cases), Maharatna about 30% (20-25% in some), FM 35%+ (up to 40%+).

qa_highlights.question: Will sales returns recur as in last year (INR200 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects returns to fall to at least half of last year's level, citing lower placements, a variety of generic and new products, and only one or two herbicides failing.

qa_highlights.question: What was Q1 volume and value growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume fell about 13%, with value up about 2%.

qa_highlights.question: Kaeros growth and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 100% CAGR initially, moderating to 50-60%. Normalised margin is single-digit at present, and management does not expect it to reach double digits soon.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin expansion to 31.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 2% price rise, specialty product mix, and some benefit from older inventory, while noting volatile input prices. It said the net effect was mixed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sotanala investment and product plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Total about INR200 crore (INR50 crore formulation, INR150 crore technical); about INR70 crore spent to date. Phase 1 will transfer 5-6 existing insecticide and fungicide molecules from Chopanki; new AIs in phase 2.

qa_highlights.question: Granuvia and Spinoace revenue expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Granuvia crossed about INR5 crore in Q1; Spinoace INR25 lakh. Gross FY27 target INR30-35 crore combined, about INR25 crore net.

544210|2026-06.headline: Emcure Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, with EBITDA of INR 508 crore (19.7% margin) and PAT up 35-36%.
544210|2026-06.overview:
Revenue grew 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, led by international markets (up 34.2% to INR 1,485 crore) while India grew 10.2% to INR 1,095 crore. EBITDA rose 25.8% to INR 508 crore with margin up 50 bps to 19.7%, and PAT grew about 36% to INR 292 crore. Gross margin fell to 58.4% on geographic and product mix, and net debt rose to INR 1,103 crore. Management reiterated low-to-mid teens FY27 revenue growth (now toward the higher end) and 70-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion. Board changes were announced: Chairman Berjis Desai retires at AGM and CEO Satish Mehta becomes Chairman; Samit Mehta becomes COO and CEO of Gennova, which is now 100% owned.</overview>
<parameter name="financial_highlights">[{"metric":"Revenue from operations","value":"INR 2,580 crore","change":"+22.8% YoY"},{"metric":"Domestic (India) revenue","value":"INR 1,095 crore","change":"+10.2% YoY; ~+12% vs Q4 FY26"},{"metric":"International revenue","value":"INR 1,485 crore","change":"+34.2% YoY"},{"metric":"Gross profit","value":"INR 1,507 crore","change":"+16.1% YoY"},{"metric":"Gross margin","value":"58.4%","change":"Declined YoY (mix-driven)"},{"metric":"R&D expense","value":"INR 90 crore (3.5% of revenue)","change":""},{"metric":"EBITDA","value":"INR 508 crore; margin 19.7%","change":"+25.8% YoY; +50 bps"},{"metric":"Profit after tax","value":"INR 292 crore; PAT margin +110 bps","change":"+35.4% to +36.2% YoY"},{"metric":"Depreciation & amortisation","value":"INR 110 crore","change":"from INR 99 crore in Q1 FY26"},{"metric":"Interest cost","value":"INR 32 crore","change":""},{"metric":"Effective tax rate","value":"25.6%","change":""},{"metric":"Gross debt (30 June)","value":"INR 1,291 crore","change":""},{"metric":"Cash and equivalents","value":"INR 189 crore","change":""},{"metric":"Net debt","value":"INR 1,103 crore (CFO also cited INR 1,560 crore in Q&A)","change":"Up QoQ"}]

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,095 crore, +10.2% YoY. Ex-Sanofi OAD and Roche in-licensed brands, growth was about 6-7%. Price contributed about 4-5%, new launches 1-2%. Management says no channel filling in the quarter.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 537 crore, +32.8% YoY, driven by base business and liposomal amphotericin B (Ampho). Ampho is introduced in pretty much all countries, but tender-based procurement means lumpy orders.

segments.name: Canada
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 427 crore, +24.6% YoY, on new launches and share gains. Semaglutide filing expected in the next few months; Quebec launch via Dr. Reddy's is uncertain.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 522 crore, +44.8% YoY, led by ARV. About two-thirds of ROW was ARV this quarter; management expects ARV at about 50-55% of ROW for the full year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at low-to-mid teens, with management now more comfortable at the higher end of that range, driven by ARV order book visibility.
EBITDA margin expansion of 70-100 bps for FY27 reiterated.
FY27 gross margin guided at about 59% (earlier 60-61% framing), as higher international and ARV mix dilutes gross margin while EBITDA is accretive.
R&D for FY27 guided at 4-5% of revenue; spend expected to pick up in the rest of the year.
India growth expected in line with industry in Q2 FY27 and faster than industry in H2 FY27 as the Zuventus base effect eases.
Net debt expected to rise to about INR 1,450 crore by end-Q2 FY27 after the Mantra and Gennova payouts (INR 450-500 crore), then turn net cash by end-FY28.
Management expects sequential improvement each quarter.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were given on the call.
Gennova consolidated to 100% after acquiring a 12.05% minority stake; Mantra acquisition payout completed in July 2026.
demand_pricing: International constant-currency growth about 12% (about 12-13% per later answer), against about 6-7% FX tailwind at company level.
India price growth about 4-5% YoY; new launches 1-2%; the remainder is volume.

Poviztra (semaglutide biosimilar with Novo Nordisk) is growing month on month, but management says 40-50 brands have launched in the market and it is hard to separate channel stocking from consumption. Pricing was set very competitively.
Gross margin pressure reflects B2B-type international businesses (lower gross margin, higher EBITDA contribution), with Europe and ARV growing faster.
Management says Zuventus is stabilised and consolidated, now moving to acceleration.

qa_highlights.question: Is India's double-digit growth clean, or is there channel filling after Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no channel filling this quarter; growth is normalised and expected to improve further in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What share of ROW is ARV, and does FY27 base make FY28 harder?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds of ROW is ARV this quarter; full-year ARV share is expected at about 50-55% of ROW, with growth in both ARV and non-ARV.

qa_highlights.question: When will domestic growth be back in line with the market, and what is organic growth ex-in-licensed brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 FY27 is expected to be in line with industry and H2 faster. Ex-Sanofi OAD and Roche, growth was about 6-7%. Poviztra is a new launch; OAD moves into the base next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is constant-currency international growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-level FX impact was about 6-7%; international growth would have been about 12% in constant currency (12-13% in later answer).

qa_highlights.question: Why is Canada semaglutide a second-wave filing, and what is the Quebec launch timing with Dr. Reddy's?
qa_highlights.answer: Filing expected in the next few months, delayed because semaglutide was pursued as a global development. Quebec timing depends on Dr. Reddy's supply; management will defer to them.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline and where does it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix from Europe and ARV growth; FY27 gross margin guided at about 59%. Management says B2B international businesses are EBITDA-accretive despite lower gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: When will net debt turn to net cash and how does it trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt expected at about INR 1,450 crore by end-Q2 after acquisition payouts; net cash by about end-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 R&D spend?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is guided at 4-5% of revenue for FY27.

544870|2026-06.headline: Behari Lal Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR151.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR29.7 crore (19.6% margin) and high-value share at 60.4%.
544870|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's first earnings call as a listed entity, following its IPO (INR301 crore issue, listed 19 August 2026). Revenue from operations grew 18% YoY to INR151.7 crore and PAT rose 24.5% to INR19.2 crore, though both EBITDA and PAT fell sequentially against Q4 FY26, which carried INR5.9 crore of one-off state incentives. Mix improved: high-value products (rolls, castings, specialty alloys) reached 60.4% of revenue and EBITDA per ton rose to about INR13,500. Management guided to about INR80 crore of FY27 capex, with Unit 3 (centrifugal/foundry for ICDP and HSS rolls) targeted to start in Q1 FY28, while defense revenue is expected to become meaningful from FY28.

segments.name: Alloy steel products (bars 6-230 mm, valve/tool/die steel)
segments.commentary: 47.7% of Q1 revenue (FY26 share ~46%); includes recently introduced valve, tool and die steel grades.

segments.name: Metal rolls
segments.commentary: 25.8% of Q1 revenue (FY26 ~26%); supplied to steel majors such as SAIL, JSW, Tata Steel and Vizag.

segments.name: Engineering castings (500 kg to 25 t single pieces)
segments.commentary: 19.8% of Q1 revenue (FY26 ~20%); demand from power sector, crusher OEMs; recent 22-23 t single-piece casting for a thermal power customer.

segments.name: Forging ingots and shafts
segments.commentary: 1.9% of Q1 revenue, down from 4.4%, as management deliberately shifts steel into finished high-value grades.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex target of about INR80 crore; INR5 crore spent in Q1 and INR75 crore planned over the next three quarters. Funding split: IPO proceeds plus internal accruals.
Unit 3 (foundry, centrifugal casting for ICDP/HSS rolls) targeted to commence in Q1 FY28; exact capex amount not yet disclosed pending exchange filing.
High-value product share targeted at about 70% in the near future (currently ~60%).
Operating EBITDA margin expected to grow 20-25% over the next two to three years per management; prior-year operating EBITDA margin cited as around 25%.
Inventory days to be held at 90-100 days as high-value mix grows.
Defense revenue expected to become meaningful from FY28; no quantified mix target given.
capex_capacity: Melting capacity is 1.5x FY24 levels; last melting addition was in FY24, and management plans a considerable melting addition next year with Unit 3.
Unit 3 shed under construction and most machinery ordered; centrifugal casting (vertical and horizontal) planned to make ICDP and HSS rolls; commencement targeted Q1 FY28.

IPO net proceeds of INR93 crore fresh capital: INR56 crore for equipment and civil work at both facilities, ~INR7 crore for rooftop solar, small debt repayment and ~INR19 crore general corporate purposes. Management said part of GCP was already used for working capital within 15 days of receipt.
Planned investments in CNC machining, shot blasting, painting, NDT, finish machining and a NABL-accredited lab to make castings ready-to-use.
Solar power project funded from internal accruals to lower power cost.
demand_pricing: High-value share rose from ~47% (two-three years ago) to 57% in FY26 and 60.4% in Q1 FY27; EBITDA per ton rose from ~INR9,100 (FY25) to ~INR11,500 (FY26) and INR13,457 in Q1.
Order book INR162 crore / 13,138 t at 30 June (over one quarter of revenue), skewed to high-value products.
Thermal power sector demand is rising; management cites customer visibility to 2035 and orders for CNC machines to support castings.
Defense: orders from Bharat Dynamics and Nuclear Power Corporation of India plus private suppliers to defense customers; prototype revenue started; long approval cycles.
Automotive share fell to 33% (from 38.7% in FY26) as low-margin commodity alloy bars for forging customers are being redirected; infrastructure rose to 26.4% from 20.7%.
Imports of ICDP and HSS rolls about 3.5 lakh tons in FY26 per management; management says it is the first domestic player to add capacity for these grades.
Management attributed the export decline to timing of casting shipments and order phasing, and said the trend is not changed.

532976|2026-06.headline: Jai Balaji Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,683 crore; adjusted EBITDA up 46% to INR154 crore, PAT up 21% to INR85 crore.
532976|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 24% YoY to INR1,683 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 46% to INR154 crore (about 9% margin) and PAT up 21% to INR85 crore (about 5% margin), attributed to price normalisation and operational efficiency. Ferroalloy and pig iron realisations rose sharply YoY, while DI pipe demand stayed subdued on slow government ordering and fund releases. Management declined to give volume or EBITDA guidance, citing uncertainty, but said pipe prices are at the bottom and cannot fall further. Expansion capex was revised up to INR1,112 crore from about INR1,000 crore, with completion expected by Q3 FY27 and the balance by end-2026.

financial_highlights.change: Net term debt was INR3,408 crore in FY21

segments.name: Ductile iron pipes (DI)
segments.commentary: About 15% of Q1 turnover; utilisation about 30% of the enhanced 5.5 lakh tpa capacity. Order book about four months at current dispatch rate. Management said pipe margins were similar to pig iron margins in Q1.

segments.name: Specialised ferroalloys
segments.commentary: About 27% of revenue; utilisation above 80% in the last quarter. Ferroalloy prices up 46% YoY. Management guided a long-term margin of 15-20%, and exports go to more than 42 countries.

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: About 19% of revenue; realisations up 16% YoY.

segments.name: TMT bars
segments.commentary: About 14.8% of revenue. Management expects West Bengal sales to rise to 50-70% of TMT volume from 15-20% previously.

segments.name: Commodity mix (sponge iron, billets, coke, scrap, fines)
segments.commentary: Sponge iron 7.4%, billets 3.5%, coke about 7%, scrap and fines about 1% of revenue. Sponge iron and billet realisations were broadly stable.

guidance_outlook: No volume guidance for DI pipes or ferroalloys for FY27; management said demand visibility is too uncertain.
No EBITDA-per-tonne guidance for pipes; management said prices are 25-30% below levels of a year and a half ago and 'cannot get worse'.
Ferroalloy utilisation expected at 80-90% once the new module is commissioned around December-January.
Management indicated revenue of INR7,000-7,500 crore in a normal market once expanded capacity is complete by end-2026; no FY28 or FY30 targets were given beyond this.
Post-monsoon recovery in DI dispatches and payments expected, with improvement from Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: DI pipe capacity raised from 5 lakh tpa to 5.5 lakh tpa.

Specialised ferroalloy capacity rising to 1.9 lakh tpa from 1.66 lakh tpa; blast furnace to 7.5 lakh tpa from 6.3 lakh tpa; sinter to 12.08 lakh tpa from 9.08 lakh tpa. All expected commissioned by Q3 FY27.

Expansion outlay revised to INR1,112 crore from about INR1,000 crore (cause: equipment shipment delays, inflation, rupee depreciation, technical upgrades). About INR1,076 crore already spent, mostly from internal accruals; INR35-40 crore balance by end-2026.
Three railway sidings in operation; about 400 acres of land largely occupied for new capacity.
Management said the INR20 crore trial plastic-alternative pipe plant has sold no pipes and is in abeyance.
demand_pricing: Government DI pipe ordering is slow. Management said INR10,344 crore has been released by the Centre this year, and a FY26 backlog (only INR1,560 crore released in the budget) remains the constraint.
Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 extended to December 2028 with outlay of INR8.69 lakh crore (including INR3.5 lakh crore central assistance); AMRUT 2.0 also cited as a driver.
Competition intense while pipe utilisation stays at 25-35% industry-wide; management said intensity eases above 65-70% utilisation.
Jal Jeevan Mission receivables: management estimated 25-35% of outstanding dues collected, with the rest expected over the next 2-4 months.
Ferroalloy demand described as strong with repeat orders; management said 80-85% capacity is utilised.

qa_highlights.question: When will increased government spending translate into DI pipe dispatches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a post-monsoon recovery in dispatches and payments, with improvement from Q3 FY27, after central fund releases and state matching shares.

qa_highlights.question: Will pricing pressure persist given competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition will persist until industry utilisation reaches 65-70%. Management said pipe prices are at rock bottom and Q1 pipe margins were similar to pig iron margins.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give DI pipe EBITDA per tonne guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management called pipe EBITDA guidance speculative given the 25-30% price fall and said it would reassess next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin profile of specialised ferroalloys versus conventional steel?
qa_highlights.answer: Conventional steel margins are 5-7%, specialised ferroalloys 15-18%. Long-term ferroalloy margin guidance is 15-20%, with a 1-2% swing from raw materials or freight.

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex rise to about INR1,100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase was about 7-8%, from delayed equipment shipments from China, inflation, higher freight, rupee depreciation, and technical upgrades.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DI pipe order book?
qa_highlights.answer: About four months at current dispatch rates. Q1 DI production was 41,000 tonnes, about 30-33% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is current debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayable term debt is INR188 crore. Working capital is INR375-400 crore, sanctioned limits about INR525-550 crore, and net utilisation stays below INR500 crore with INR70-80 crore cash or unutilised limits.

risks_watch: Government fund releases and state payments: DI demand depends on clearing the FY26 backlog and recovering dues.
Pipe pricing at 25-30% below a year and a half ago, with management saying no further downside yet giving no guidance.
Capex overrun risk: budget rose to INR1,112 crore from about INR1,000 crore, and commissioning by Q3 FY27 depends on imported equipment.
Ferroalloy margins (15-20%) depend on raw material costs and freight; management said margins could move 1-2%.
Management did not give FY28 or FY30 capacity or profit targets; the INR7,000-7,500 crore revenue figure is conditional on a normal market.

532804|2026-06.headline: Technocraft Q1 FY27: Drum Closure EBIT margin near 43% on record volumes and rupee depreciation; management targets sustainable 30% for drums, 15% for scaffolding and engineering services.
532804|2026-06.overview:
Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong quarter, with Drum Closure posting its highest-ever revenue and EBIT margin (about 43%) on higher export volumes and a weaker rupee. Scaffolding volumes rose year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter on US demand, with realisations broadly stable. Mach One (aluminium formwork) volumes fell year-on-year but edged up sequentially, which management attributed to site and project readiness rather than competition. Management repeatedly declined to treat the current margins as the new normal and kept its sustainable-margin guidance unchanged. No significant new capex is planned for FY27.</overview>
<parameter name="financial_highlights">[{"metric": "Steel Scaffolding revenue (consolidated)", "value": "Rs 240 crore", "change": ""}, {"metric": "Mach One (aluminium formwork) revenue (consolidated)", "value": "Rs 165 crore", "change": "Year-on-year volume growth declined; small sequential increase"}, {"metric": "Drum Closure EBIT margin", "value": "about 43%", "change": "Highest ever for the segment, per analyst; management confirmed record revenue and EBIT"}, {"metric": "Plastic drum closure sales (previous quarter)", "value": "Rs 14.5 crore", "change": "Growing consistently"}, {"metric": "Textile Yarn business EBITDA margin (last quarter)", "value": "about 13%", "change": ""}, {"metric": "Unallocated MTM gain", "value": "about Rs 27 crore", "change": ""}]

segments.name: Drum Closure
segments.commentary: Almost 100% export. Volumes and rupee depreciation drove record revenue and EBIT. Management targets a sustainable margin of 30% or more. Non-seasonal, not order-book based.

segments.name: Scaffolding (Steel)
segments.commentary: Volumes up year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter on US demand (data centres, semicon, AI chip plants, energy). Operating at about 95% utilisation. Sustainable margin guidance of 15%. Middle East is 2-3% of sales and declining.

segments.name: Mach One (Aluminium Formwork)
segments.commentary: Volumes down year-on-year, up marginally quarter-on-quarter. Utilisation about 75-80%. Order book of 3-5 months. Aluminium extrusion plant at over 95%-100% utilisation and helped EBIT amid higher aluminium prices.

segments.name: Engineering Services
segments.commentary: Growing fast on US outsourcing demand, including AI-based vision, embedded systems and automation. Sustainable margin target about 14-15%, which includes ongoing tech investment.

segments.name: Textile
segments.commentary: Fabric business shut down and machinery sold for Rs 25-30 crore. Yarn business profitable. Garment business loss-making, with breakeven targeted within two quarters. Working capital released about Rs 15-20 crore (figure varied during the call).

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: JT Cooler approved by DRDO and an Israeli sensor maker, with export orders from Israel of about Rs 20 crore at roughly 15% margin. Missile canister repeat orders. Confirmed order book about Rs 20-21 crore.

guidance_outlook: Drum Closure: sustainable margin of 30% or more; similar volumes expected in the immediate quarter.
Scaffolding: volumes expected to be maintained or improved for the next two quarters; beyond that not guided due to volatility. Sustainable margin 15%.
Engineering Services: sustainable margin 14-15%, inclusive of ongoing investment.
Capex: no significant new capacity capex in FY27, only maintenance. Phase 2 of CSN plant and Aurangabad Mach One Phase 2 expected next year.
US tariff refund of close to $3 million expected in the Scaffolding segment, not yet received; timing not stated.
Middle East scaffolding sales expected to stay volatile for one to two quarters.
capex_capacity: No significant new capacity capex planned for FY27; only maintenance capex across divisions. The last major capex (CSN plant, FY25) is fully operational.
Aluminium extrusion plant running at over 95% (management said 100%) utilisation since the March quarter; 100% backward integrated for Mach One.
Mach One utilisation about 75-80%, after a recent Aurangabad capacity expansion. Phase 2 expected sometime next year.
Scaffolding utilisation about 95%. Management says it can add capacity within about 3 months using space in Mumbai and China plants, and is studying options.
Next year: CSN Phase 2 and extra extrusion capacity plus forward integration.
demand_pricing: US scaffolding demand strong since January 2026, driven by AI chip, semicon and energy construction; realisations stable as steel prices did not rise sharply.

US tariff on Chinese scaffolding is 75% (50% Section 232 plus 25% Section 301) vs 50% for India and others. Management says Chinese steel costs are 20%+ lower, but Technocraft is only about 5% higher on cost.
Management says it does not compete on price; it competes on inventory availability, distribution and a 150+ component mix.
Indian project launches strong across 7 major cities; demand also from commercial, GCCs and data centres.
Drum Closure: no price cuts planned; competitive position as the world's second-largest producer. Rupee depreciation lifted realisations.
Europe scaffolding sales started in the last two quarters (CE certification), still small due to weak construction in Germany.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Mach One volumes decline year-on-year, and how is competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to site and project readiness, not competition or demand. Volumes rose slightly quarter-on-quarter. Focus is on quality customers and profitability, not rapid volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 43% Drum Closure margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the sustainable margin is above 30% and 43% is not the new normal, given volatility in freight, tariffs and geopolitics. Rupee depreciation and volumes drove the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Defence JT Cooler opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Export orders from Israel of about Rs 20 crore at around 15% margin. Management said quantum is hard to estimate because defence procurement is slow and product-specific.

qa_highlights.question: What are the scaffolding tariff and competitive dynamics in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariff is 50% for India, 75% for China. Chinese prices are sometimes lower, but Technocraft does not sell on price. Its US subsidiary and inventory-led distribution are its edge.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant capacity capex this year; only maintenance. Phase 2 of CSN and Mach One expansion next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Textile plan after the fabric exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Fabric shut and machinery sold for Rs 25-30 crore. Yarn profitable; garment loss-making, with breakeven targeted in two quarters. No active plan to sell the rest of the business.

risks_watch: Drum Closure margin normalisation from 43% toward the 30% guidance if the rupee strengthens or freight and tariff costs move.
Scaffolding volume visibility limited to about two quarters; US tariff regime (50%/75%) and Chinese price aggression.
Middle East scaffolding disruption from war and shipping problems.
Garment business breakeven within two quarters; restructuring execution.
Timing of the approximately $3 million US tariff refund.
Defence order timing is slow; JT Cooler export scale is small so far.
Mach One volume recovery depends on site readiness; Y-o-Y decline.

542830|2026-06.headline: IRCTC Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.1% to INR1,370 crore, but EBITDA fell 2.77% to INR386 crore as catering margins and internet ticketing spinoffs weakened.
542830|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations rose 18.1% YoY to INR1,370 crore, led by catering (INR732 crore, +33.8%) and tourism (INR168 crore, +13.5%). EBITDA was INR386 crore (28.17% margin), down 2.77% YoY, and PAT was about INR330 crore. Margins were pressured by a one-time HR/gratuity charge of about INR20 crore, proof-of-concept costs on six trains, a West Asia-driven resin cost spike in Rail Neer, and lower non-convenience fee income in internet ticketing. Management said the catering and HR effects are non-recurring and that the proof-of-concept trains will wind down by November.</overview>

segments.name: Internet Ticketing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR361 crore (+0.5%); EBIT margin fell to 80.33% from 84.12%, attributed to NGET infra refresh, about INR10 crore maintenance booking, and lower marketing/ad and agent income. About 89% of reserved tickets are booked online.

segments.name: Tourism

About 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains expected over the next year, with licence fee of about INR6 crore per train (up to INR120 crore).
Management aims to bring non-convenience fee back toward INR150 crore over time via iPay, e-wallet loyalty and agent business changes; no quarterly run-rate given.

Catering services in 81 Vande Bharat trains run by IRCTC; other Vande Bharat catering is outsourced to empanelled licensees via limited tenders.
Payment aggregator (IRCTC Payments Ltd): final RBI application submitted by 4 August 2026 with SAR and MVP; RBI response expected within this financial year; TSP already engaged.

UPI share of tickets 51.22% vs 48.72% a year earlier.

Catering revenue bridge: onboard sales INR413 crore (INR301 crore), licence fee from prepaid and other trains INR224 crore (INR192 crore), static units INR33 crore (INR20 crore), e-catering INR22 crore (INR9 crore), election specials INR41 crore (INR5 crore).
Opt-out for catering on prepaid trains estimated at roughly 25-30% (management said unconfirmed); complaint ratio about 0.0008% of 18 lakh daily meals.

544320|2026-06.headline: Carraro India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR5,447 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.4% on pass-through lag from commodity and freight inflation.
544320|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 10% YoY to INR5,447 million, driven by domestic growth of about 26% that offset a roughly 14% fall in exports. EBITDA rose 6% YoY to INR579 million, but margin was 10.4% as higher energy, raw material and freight costs, plus supplier-side labour shortages, were not yet recovered from customers. Total income included a one-time INR88 million provision write-back linked to a customs reassessment, which flatters other income and PAT. Management expects the price pass-through gap to close over about 12 months and targets full recovery of price increments for the full year.

financial_highlights.change: +12% YoY; includes INR88 million one-time provision write-back (customs reassessment)
Affected by energy, raw material costs and labour constraints

segments.name: Agriculture (total)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,559 million, +15% YoY; domestic agri INR2,135 million, +32% YoY Q1-on-Q1 per management. Export agri INR424 million.

segments.name: Construction (total)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,264 million, +4% YoY; domestic construction INR1,393 million, +20% YoY. Export construction INR871 million.

segments.name: Other / domestic other sales
segments.commentary: Domestic other sales INR267 million; export 'other' category INR357 million.

segments.name: Exports (by segment)
segments.commentary: Total exports INR1,652 million, ~-14% YoY, hit by logistics (container and vessel shortages) and West Asia disruption; management calls the quarter unrepresentative.

guidance_outlook: Management expects volumes and exports to be back on track from Q2 FY27, per CFO.
If the situation stabilises, FY27 revenue growth of up to about 10% YoY is targeted.
Full-year EBITDA margin: CFO says EBITDA could be about half a point above last year if the pass-through gap is fully bridged; no firm margin range given. Analyst-proposed 10.5-11% was not confirmed.
Target to recover all commodity and freight price increments over the full financial year; gap expected to close in about 12 months.
Long-term aspiration: revenue of INR3,500-4,000 crore by FY30.
Export mix expected to remain about 65% domestic and 33-35% export.
Localisation to return to 86-88% target over coming months; currently ~74%.
Serial production for a Turkish higher-horsepower customer started in Q1; Indian higher-horsepower programme SOP targeted for FY28.
capex_capacity: Construction of new paint shop facility started in Q1 FY27.
Additional portal axle capacity and sub-assembly operations commissioned in the quarter.
Capacity expansion underway for domestic agriculture (4WD demand) and for export tele boom handler and backhoe loader demand.
Capex planned for growth; management said returns must be adequate.
Raw material localisation at ~74% (vs ~78% earlier), with imports used to cover local supplier shortages.
Two prototypes under development, which management links to new projects 1.5-2 years out.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as resilient across agriculture, construction and off-highway; Carraro's backhoe loader sales to Indian OEMs grew ~18% vs ~14% for the market; driveline sales to OEMs up ~18% YoY.
Volume growth was about 8-10% per management (not verified in numbers); the rest of the 10% revenue growth is said to be little price impact because pass-through lags at least four months.
Export demand: Turkey volatile due to inflation with order flow weaker this quarter; Europe agri subdued; US decisions delayed by inflation; Latin America showing modest positive signs.
Export tele boom handler and backhoe loader demand said to be stable and rising; a major export customer's trend was described as step-by-step higher.
Customers have agreed in principle to pass-through of commodity costs, but several are in wait-and-watch mode. Transport cost pass-through is not contractually fixed, but OEMs are taking positions.
Management expects possible OEM price hikes of 3-6% in construction vehicles, citing cost pressures.
Carraro supplies all Indian backhoe loader OEMs except JCB; 36 customers in total.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue growth split between metal price increase and organic volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price pass-through is at least a four-month lag, so the price component is small; volume growth is estimated at about 8-10%, with exact numbers to follow.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic agri and construction revenue, and YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic agri INR2,135 million (+32% YoY Q1-on-Q1); domestic construction INR1,393 million (+20% YoY); other domestic sales INR267 million.

qa_highlights.question: Will the EBITDA margin reach 10.5-11% for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO declined to give a range: if the price gap is fully bridged, EBITDA could be about half a point above last year, with more guidance next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is China a meaningful market for Carraro India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said China exposure is hardly 1% of revenue, with only occasional small orders (50-100 axles); the product range differs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the labour availability constraint and does it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: Carraro India said it had no internal manpower constraint; shortages are at Tier-3 suppliers (migrant casual labour), which added overtime and conversion costs that are being passed to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why do exports fall and how predictable are they?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 was hit by logistics issues (container and vessel shortages) and is unrepresentative; exports should return to FY25-FY26 levels from Q2.

risks_watch: Pass-through gap: management says the runway to recover costs shrinks if inflation persists for another 4-6 months, meaning a quarter or 4-5 months left to recover.
Export volatility, especially Turkey (inflation, lira), US decision delays and European agri weakness; logistics constraints.
Supplier-side labour and material shortages, with overtime and ad hoc supplier payments adding costs.
Localisation at 74% against 86-88% target; reliance on imports for some higher-technology components.
Monsoon and El Niño risks; government subsidy and contractor cash-flow issues affecting construction demand.
Working capital and funding of capex while maintaining profitability.
544320|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious on near-term margins and export volumes, but confident on medium-term demand and recovery. Management was candid that Q1 margins are depressed by a pass-through lag, and gave no firm full-year EBITDA range. Some answers were evasive, notably on non-farm split, customer count and China exposure. Management said the worst is over.

543254|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6% YoY to ₹269 crore, but EBITDA fell 27% to ₹45 crore (16.8% margin) and PAT dropped to ₹0.7 crore after one-offs.
543254|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 6% YoY to ₹269 crore on higher volumes and tariff escalation. EBITDA margin compressed to 16.8% from 24.4% a year ago, driven by higher transport/hiring costs at the CIDCO site, employee costs rising to 34% of revenue, and about ₹10 crore of deferred Q4 FY26 disposal work. The PCMC WtE plant was shut after a July 8 landslide of legacy waste that killed nine people, and management flagged a ₹22-24 crore impairment (before insurance) as an exceptional item. The company also refinanced ₹140 crore of Antony Lara's term loan from 10.25% to 8.25%, with a ₹7 crore prepayment charge.

financial_highlights.change: vs 24.4% in Q1 FY26 and 22.8% in Q4 FY26
vs ₹23 crore in Q1 FY26; includes ₹7 crore one-time prepayment expense
Expected to trend lower post refinancing

segments.name: Collection & Transportation (C&T)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹156 crore, up 10% YoY; share of revenue 62% vs 60% a year ago. Management said margins are under pressure from repairs and maintenance and ageing contracts.

segments.name: MSW Processing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹75 crore, up 3% YoY; share 28%, flat. Growth slowed because the CIDCO bio-mining contract ended, and processing volumes rose 5% to about 0.85 million tons.

segments.name: Waste-to-Energy (PCMC)
segments.commentary: Plant suspended after the July 8 incident. Over 20 million green units generated in the quarter before the shutdown; restart expected by first/second week of October. Fixed costs of ₹2.5-3 crore per month (about ₹7 crore total) will run through the quarter.

segments.name: Construction & Demolition recycling
segments.commentary: Running at 600-650 tons per day against 600 tons per day capacity (±10%), with a 96% recycling rate, after BMC policy required large builders to send waste to the plant.

guidance_outlook: Management calls the Q1 margin compression transitional. It expects margins to recover toward the historical trend, with C&T margins improving after transport renegotiation and the labour-cost escalation pass-through.
Employee costs were 34% of revenue vs a historical 30-31%; management expects normalisation within about three quarters, so FY28 margins should be back at historical levels.
New volumes: the BMC contract adds about 1,500 tons per day from Q3 (only one ward live so far); the Atkoli project adds 600-800 tons per day from Q3/Q4. Q4 is the test of the full run-rate.
Growth from the existing portfolio is estimated at 6-9%, with new contracts adding 10-15%. Revenue from new contracts typically takes 2-3 quarters after LOA to reach the P&L.
Greater Noida EMS road sweeping contract: ₹243 crore over 5 years plus a 2-year extension option; starts Q3 FY27 with about ₹46 crore revenue in year one.
Andhra Pradesh (Kadapa and Kurnool) projects: land possession obtained, civil work under way, financial closure near final; the company says it is on schedule.
Impairment of ₹22-24 crore on the WtE assets is expected, before any insurance recovery; more detail is due with Q2 results. Auditors have flagged the plant-damage cost as an open item.
capex_capacity: PCMC WtE plant: suspended after the July 8 event; restart pending structural/safety assessment and OEM/Hitachi certification, expected by early October. The MRF and composting operation restarted on July 28 at about 400 tons per day.
Andhra Pradesh WtE projects (Kadapa and Kurnool): land possessed, civil contractor mobilised at Kadapa, Kurnool expected to start in about two weeks; the company said the project is on schedule.
Atkoli processing project in Thane: operational by Q4 FY27, adding 600-800 tons per day in processing.
Borrowings rose about ₹22 crore QoQ at gross level, for the AP WtE project and the new BMC C&T contract.
RDF sales of about 40,000 tons fell 28% YoY, partly because the CIDCO bio-mining project has been completed. Compost sales were stable at about 6,000 tons.
demand_pricing: Processing tonnage was 0.85 million tons (+5% YoY); C&T tonnage 0.55 million tons (+6% YoY); total about 1.4 million tons (+5%).
RDF net realisation is above ₹300 per ton, up from about ₹250 a year earlier.
Tipping fees range from ₹1,800 to ₹4,200 per ton, depending on scope, vehicle count and contract duration. Some C&T contracts (Thane, Jhansi, Varanasi) are billed per household or trip, not per ton.
Management says about 80% of operating costs are covered by escalation clauses, but the escalation lags cost increases by about six months.
Cost headwinds cited: fuel volatility, repairs and maintenance, additives and gases (linked to the Gulf/Hormuz conflict), plus a new Maharashtra DA revision and a Labour Code restatement.

543514|2026-06.headline: Veranda Q1 FY27 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR150 crore and PAT to INR34 crore, with commerce demerger listing guided for September 2026.
543514|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 42% YoY to about INR150 crore and enrollments rose 35% to about 1.03 lakh students. EBITDA was about INR54 crore with a margin near 36% as stated, but management acknowledged the reported EBITDA growth of 10% was flattered by a INR17 crore one-time other income in Q1 FY26; excluding it, EBITDA grew about 30%. PAT rose to INR34 crore from INR5.9 crore, helped by a INR7.35 crore tax reversal tied to an intra-group merger. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about INR670 crore revenue, INR260 crore EBITDA and INR144 crore PAT, and said the Commerce demerger NCLT order is expected shortly with listing before end-September 2026.

financial_highlights.change: +10% YoY reported; ~30% excluding Q1 FY26 one-time other income of INR17 crore
+472% YoY from INR5.9 crore; sixth consecutive PAT-positive quarter
+53% YoY; EBITDA INR42.7 crore (+58% YoY), margin ~40%
+41% YoY; EBITDA nearly INR4 crore vs near breakeven prior quarter
Post refinancing; debt cost ~9-9.5% vs 17.5% last year

financial_highlights.value: Commerce INR125 crore; non-commerce INR145 crore

segments.name: Commerce Test Prep
segments.commentary: Revenue INR108.6 crore (+53% YoY), EBITDA INR42.7 crore (~40% margin). Offline revenue about INR330 crore and online about INR120 crore annualised, offline margin ~35% and online ~45-48%. Managed commerce colleges at about 17 now, to add 15 more this year.

segments.name: Government test prep
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.5 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA nearly INR4 crore vs near breakeven last quarter. Target of INR95-100 crore EBITDA over four to five years; Karnataka expansion planned in FY27.

segments.name: Academic / K-12
segments.commentary: Revenue INR12.2 crore (+22% YoY), EBITDA INR9.2 crore (+53% YoY). Manages six schools with over 5,400 students; preschool managed operations to be entered in FY27.

segments.name: SNVA Veranda (associate stake)
segments.commentary: Vocational/higher-ed businesses (Edureka, Six Phrase) were moved into SNVA Veranda; management expects value unlock, with the stake to sit in the non-commerce entity post demerger. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: revenue about INR670 crore (FY26: INR482 crore), EBITDA about INR260 crore (FY26: INR204 crore), PAT about INR144 crore (FY26: INR130 crore).
Commerce FY27: revenue about INR450 crore, EBITDA about INR215 crore, PAT about INR110 crore.
Non-commerce FY27: revenue about INR220 crore, EBITDA INR46 crore, PAT INR34 crore.
Management cited EBITDA margin of about 38.8% for FY27 (per analyst reading of guidance); expects margins to recover in Q2 and Q3 as college and marketing spends mature.

Commerce demerger: NCLT order expected imminently after July 20 hearing (orders reserved); next NCLT hearing 17 August 2026; listing targeted by end-September 2026. Shareholders receive 1 JK Shah Commerce Education share per Veranda share.
Commerce long-term aspiration: revenue above INR1,000 crore by FY30.
capex_capacity: Offline commerce network at over 105 centres; 50 new commerce colleges under management in pipeline; plan to add 15 managed commerce colleges in FY27 (doubling from about 17).
Commerce Virtuals (live and recorded digital format for Class 11-12) recently launched for pan-India reach without physical infrastructure.
Government test prep: Group 1 offline programmes, junior IAS, subscription magazines; expansion into Karnataka in FY27.
Planned offline presence in UP, Bihar, Rajasthan and Gujarat to reduce regional concentration.
Managed schools: six schools, 5,400+ students; preschool managed operations to start in FY27.
demand_pricing: Enrollments +35% YoY vs collections +27%; management attributed gap to subject-wise commerce classes, which raise enrollment counts with lower per-enrollment billing.
Q1 collections INR165 crore vs revenue INR150 crore; about INR15 crore of advances deferred under Ind AS 11 to later quarters.
Managed school revenue jump attributed to ~10% student growth plus start-of-year book and service sales (~20% uplift in Q1).
Guided ARPU increase of 7-8% a year and 10% student growth in FY27 as EBITDA drivers, plus 15 new colleges.
Commerce positioned as number one across CA, CS, CMA, ACCA; management claims undisputed leadership in pedigree, alumni, centres and ranks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable quarterly finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohasin Khan guided INR7.5-8 crore per quarter after refinancing; EBITDA excludes finance cost, so no finance savings sit in the EBITDA bridge.

qa_highlights.question: Why did tax swing to a credit of about INR3 crore from about INR8 crore a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Following an intra-group merger of a subsidiary into the parent, management reversed INR7.35 crore of tax related to earlier years; described as current tax, not a DTA write-off.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline QoQ and how will FY27 38.8% margin be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited doubled college expansion spend, pre-demerger advertising for the commerce brand, and initial work on 15 new colleges, all expensed in Q1; expects benefit in next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and timing of the NCLT approval and listing?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders were reserved at the 20 July hearing; affidavit filed on the appointed date query; next hearing 17 August. Management expects order within about a week, then ROC filing in 3-4 days, a record date one week later, and listing before end-September.

qa_highlights.question: Will non-commerce be valued lower because it carries all the debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the commerce entity to command the highest sector multiple as the leader; government test prep should earn a good multiple, K-12 less so. No numbers provided on valuation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the offline/online split and margins in commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline about INR330 crore and online about INR120 crore (roughly 3:1 offline to online per management); offline margin ~35%, online ~45-48%.

543441|2026-06.headline: CMS Info Systems Q1 FY27 services revenue hit a record INR625 crores (+9.3% YoY) despite a INR25 crore currency-supply hit; FY27 EBITDA margin guide raised to about 27%.
543441|2026-06.overview: Services revenue reached an all-time high of INR625 crores, up 9.3% YoY and 2.6% QoQ, but was INR25 crores below the company's internal run-rate target of INR650 crores because banks supplied only about 70% of indented currency. EBITDA rose 8.9% YoY to INR173 crores with margin up 170 bps QoQ to 27.2%, while EBIT fell to INR32 crores (10.3% margin) on higher depreciation from HAWKAI/ALGO capex and the FSS acquisition. Management trimmed FY27 services revenue guidance to INR2,650-2,750 crores (from INR2,700-2,800 crores) and raised the EBITDA margin guide to about 27% (from 25-26%). Currency fulfilment has since recovered to roughly 80-85% of indents, and management expects normalisation by end-Q2.

financial_highlights.change: vs 14.1% margin a year ago; would be ~15% excluding INR18 crore BLA revenue impact
-10.6% YoY, +5.8% QoQ; PAT margin -170 bps YoY, +70 bps QoQ
lower due to deferred tax gain from Securens turnaround

financial_highlights.value: 49.39 lakh shares at INR340, INR168 crores total

segments.name: ATM / BLA (brown label, transaction-linked)
segments.commentary: Revenue impact of about INR18 crores from currency shortage; ATMs at about 70% supply saw transactions fall 27% YoY while well-supplied ATMs were flat. This segment is about 12% of revenue and management will not invest incremental capital in it.

segments.name: Cash Logistics (work for other MSPs)
segments.commentary: Revenue impact of about INR7 crores from the currency shortage.

segments.name: Technology and Payments (HAWKAI, ALGO MVS)
segments.commentary: Now 18% of services revenue in Q1 (7% in FY22, 16% in FY26), with a target of above 20% by end-Q4 FY27. Guided to grow 35-40% in FY27; ALGO MVS deployed at SBI and due to go live at ICICI in Q3.

segments.name: FSS acquisition
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR20 crores of accrual in Q1 with contracts still being novated; synergies expected from H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 services revenue raised? No: trimmed to INR2,650-2,750 crores from INR2,700-2,800 crores; total revenue INR2,750-2,850 crores.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided to about 27%, up from 25-26% guided in May.

Platform growth FY27: ATM Management and Retail & Currency Logistics 11-14%; Technology and Payments 35-40%; combined services revenue growth 15-19%. Another remark cited 10-13% for ATM and retail platforms.
FY27 capex INR100-125 crores (vs peak INR350 crores in FY26 and ~INR200 crores average); could rise but should not exceed INR200 crores if tech opportunities materialise.
Depreciation ratio expected to improve in H2 FY27 and be better in FY28.
Currency fulfilment expected to normalise by end-Q2; IBA committee update on PSU repricing expected by end-Q2; private sector repricing targeted to close by Q2.
Cash conversion of 65-70% of EBITDA maintained; about INR400 crores cash on books, with surplus to be returned via dividend or buyback at year-end review.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was INR350 crores, mainly for order execution and HAWKAI/ALGO product development; FY27 guided to INR100-125 crores, mainly tech.
Tech spend held at 1.5% of revenue.
Around 70,000 ATMs and 65,000 retail touchpoints; more than 50% of ATM touchpoints now under end-to-end integrated contracts.
Won INR500 crores of orders in Q1, including HDFC Bank (6,000 ATMs over 5 years, TCV INR400 crores); 2 ATM recycler RFPs (about 1,000 recyclers) to be executed by year-end.
demand_pricing: Currency supply to banks fell to about 70% of indents in April-May; recovered to about 80-85% now. Currency in circulation up 12% YoY, which management reads as a supply rather than demand problem.

Steep state minimum wage increases (6% to 60% in certain large states) and fuel costs up 8%; management expects larger-than-average price increases, with private banks and retail customers in progress.
Market share: 60% in ATM cash management and 38% in retail solutions, retained from last year.
Outsourced ATM market share rising to about 60-65% (from about 50% 10 years ago); PSU in-house ATMs about 70,000-75,000 of the roughly 100,000 bank ATMs.
Competition broadening in AI and payments as new entrants arrive; management argues full-stack hardware and software ownership is a moat.
Management stated it will not enter merchant acquiring; it has no plans for a payment aggregator licence.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cash crunch transient or structural, and could banks have deliberately under-supplied low-potential ATMs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the worst is past (supply went from about 70% to 80-85%) and rejected the idea that banks chose which ATMs to starve, describing geographic imbalances instead. Demand is not the problem; the end-Q2 result will show it.

qa_highlights.question: What changes are being made to forecasting after repeated shocks?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Kaul said FY22-24 met or exceeded forecasts while FY25-26 fell short, and the team will keep setting realistic stretch targets. He called the criticism fair and said Q1 shortfall was flagged early.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue came from FSS in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly INR20 crores of accrual, with contracts still being novated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of possible UPI MDR and polymer notes?
qa_highlights.answer: MDR of 30-50 bps is being discussed; cash costs merchants about 10-20 bps. Polymer notes are planned for lower denominations, with limited direct impact as ATMs are not configured for them; possible CIT and processing upside.

qa_highlights.question: How was the INR4,00 crore TAM for HAWKAI derived?
qa_highlights.answer: BFSI: about 400,000 ATMs and branches, with 100,000-120,000 outsourced today, over 5-7 years. Non-BFSI is based on use cases and pilots (gold loan branches, dark stores, warehouses), with a healthy BFSI RFP pipeline over the next 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBIT margin recovery path and capital allocation view?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation ratio to improve in H2 FY27, with FSS synergies and HAWKAI/ALGO revenue returns expected; full normalisation in FY28. Buyback not revisited until year-end; surplus cash (about INR400 crores) to be returned via dividend or buyback.

541302|2026-06.headline: Dhruv Consultancy Q1 FY27 net sales fell to INR15.55 crore with an operating loss of about INR3 crore, while Q1 order inflow reached about INR90-100 crore.
541302|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 net sales were INR15.55 crore and total income INR15.95 crore, with management attributing the operating loss to estimate corrections, tax reversals and a fixed-cost base ahead of revenue conversion. Management said Q1 order inflow was about INR90-100 crore, including a INR40.92 crore OBCC order, the largest ticket the company has booked. Unexecuted order book is stated at INR300 crore, with the company also citing a total order book of INR600 crore in a later answer. Management guided that billing on new orders starts around Q3 and that the company is entering wayside amenities through a 55% SPV. Management gave no numeric FY27 guidance, citing SEBI LODR constraints.

financial_highlights.change: Management said operating loss reduced more than 50% vs Q4

Company is building AI dashboards to track 65-70 assignments and aims to handle around 120 assignments a year.

Wayside Amenities site: fuel pump installation (4-5 months) is the critical path; sites are 50-60% constructed by NHAI and concessionaires.

Q2 to date additional orders of about INR60-65 crore cited.

Company rated 9th among about 100 consultants by NHAI; management said the new rating framework gives technical scores more weight.
Lender's engineer fees cited at about INR2 lakh per month in India vs INR4-5 lakh per month internationally.

qa_highlights.question: What FY27 revenue guidance can the company achieve given Q1 income of about INR16 crore and new mandates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined numeric guidance citing SEBI LODR; said Q1 and Q2 typically make up 30-40% of annual revenue and Q3-Q4 are higher due to monsoon and award timing.

qa_highlights.question: What share of Q1 orders will convert to FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 15-20% of the order book converts to revenue annually; based on INR250-300 crore unexecuted book, around INR200 crore is expected over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q1 operating margin negative and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the loss largely a paper loss from estimate corrections after NHAI removed network survey vehicle scope; said the correction was about INR30-35 crore (under 5% of order book), and margins should improve as billing starts in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: When will Wayside Amenities contribute revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: First site possession given 4 August 2026; fuel pump installation takes 4-5 months and revenue is expected from around February 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivable cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 60-90 days; up to 120 days in Northeast or difficult-access states.

qa_highlights.question: Will new orders be billed in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said billing on new assignments starts after two quarters, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be better on margins.

Management's inconsistent order-book figures (INR250 crore, INR300 crore, INR360 crore, INR600 crore) need reconciliation.

Q2 FY27 order inflow of about INR60-65 crore to be confirmed; Wayside LOAs expected in September 2026.

544239|2026-06.headline: ECOS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,113.7 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.3% and FY27 margin guidance was cut to ~10%.
544239|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 16.7% YoY to INR2,113.72 million and trips rose 27% YoY to about 1.48 million, with 61 new clients added. EBITDA was flat YoY at INR218.47 million, and margin fell to 10.3% from 12.0% a year ago and 11.7% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the drop to higher operating costs, a higher ETS mix and more intense pricing pressure, especially in ETS. The FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was lowered to around 10% from the earlier 11-13% range, while revenue growth guidance of 15-18% was retained.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR219.18 mn in Q1 FY26 (flat); vs INR241.53 mn in Q4 FY26
vs 12.0% in Q1 FY26; vs 11.7% in Q4 FY26
vs INR81.54 mn in Q1 FY26; decline as one-time doubtful-debt provision did not recur
vs INR186.68 mn in Q1 FY26
vs INR132.87 mn in Q1 FY26 (~+9.5%)

segments.name: ETS (employee transportation services)
segments.commentary: 59% of revenue (up from 40% share implied by mix of prior year's 60:40 comparison noted on call; management said mix moved slightly toward CCR YoY). Pricing pressure is most intense here; management said margin erosion is more evident in ETS. 15 new ETS clients added in the quarter, described as one of the highest ever for ETS.

segments.name: CCR (chauffeur-driven car rentals)
segments.commentary: 41% of revenue. Management cited healthy recovery in corporate and travel mobility demand, though inbound international travel remains subdued. 46 new clients added, the majority by number.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin now expected around 10%, versus the earlier 11-13% range; management hopes to maintain margins at this level through the year.
Revenue growth guidance of 15% to 18% for FY27 was reiterated.
Employee cost expected to grow around 20% in FY27.
Operating leverage expected to kick in at a scale of over INR 1,000 crore of revenue; no timeline given.
B2C app launch expected this quarter; management set no high target for FY27 and promised guidance from next year.
Management is evaluating acquisitions after hiring a senior strategic finance professional last month; no buyback or shareholder return decision announced.
capex_capacity: Domestic footprint expanded to 151 cities, adding 20 in the quarter, from 130+ at end FY26.
Owned and vendor-operated fleet of about 19,500 vehicles as of June 30, 2026; the vast majority is vendor-supplied, keeping the model asset-light.
Management said 10,000-11,000 vehicles are used daily, with the rest held for demand spikes.
EV fleet increased to 460 vehicles from 390 at end Q4 FY26; EV adoption remains measured.
New CCR technology rolled out this quarter to automate contact centre, dispatch and billing; transition expected to settle within the quarter, with productivity gains to follow.
Upgraded proprietary technology platform completed this quarter; direct web booking portal launched in Q4 FY26.
demand_pricing: Trips of about 1.48 million in the quarter, up 27% YoY and ~7% QoQ; revenue grew slower than trips because of price reductions.
Active enterprise client base of about 1,400, up ~18% YoY; 61 new clients added vs 53 in Q1 FY26.
About 51% of revenue comes from customers with more than five years' relationship with ECOS.
Pricing pressure more intense than anticipated, particularly in ETS; management has set internal thresholds below which it will not bid, but did not disclose the level.
Gross margins declined as lower client rates were absorbed partly from vendor margins; management said it would negotiate harder with vendors.
Online/app bookings were about 14% of bookings in Q1, similar to 15-16% in Q4 FY26.
Management said few clients were lost to competition this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What changed since the 11-13% margin guidance, what is driving pricing pressure, and at what margin will the company walk away from business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition and pricing pressure were higher than anticipated, especially in ETS. It has set internal client-level thresholds below which it will not bid, and did not disclose a level; company-wide margin is expected to be held at around 10%.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost savings and productivity be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Automation of CCR contact centre, dispatch, billing and booking, expected mainly to reduce employee expense and improve vehicle utilisation; management said it would also negotiate harder with vendors. Savings were not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive edge given low entry barriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three elements: long-standing enterprise relationships, a large reliable vendor supply base built over decades, and processes and people. It said the market is only 15-20% organised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margins decline and how low can they go?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower rates given to win business are absorbed partly from vendor margins, most evident in ETS. Management declined to specify a floor but said it has internal thresholds.

qa_highlights.question: When and by how much will margins expand?
qa_highlights.answer: No timeline given; management said it is guiding to maintain margins because competition duration is uncertain, with operating leverage expected at a much larger scale (over INR 1,000 crore revenue).

qa_highlights.question: Will ETS and CCR EBITDA margins be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said costs are shared across the organisation, so a segment EBITDA split is not practical to provide.

risks_watch: Margin trajectory: FY27 guided to ~10% after Q1 at 10.3%; 11-13% range has been withdrawn, and further cuts are possible if pricing pressure persists.
Employee cost growth of ~21.9% YoY vs revenue growth of 16.7% is compressing operating leverage; watch whether productivity from automation offsets it.
Gross margin erosion in ETS from new competitors entering the market.
Credit risk and client quality: management stresses high-quality enterprise wins, but pricing reductions may affect contract economics.
Capital allocation: INR1,558 mn cash with no clear acquisition or shareholder return plan; watch for M&A announcements.
Guidance credibility: an investor criticised the sudden guidance change within one quarter, and management said competitive behaviour is hard to predict.
Other expenses fell only because a prior-year one-time provision did not recur, so the base is not a structural saving.

544328|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14.98% YoY to ₹104.93 crore, driven by tractors (+36.29%) while cranes were flat at ₹52.86 crore.
544328|2026-06.overview:
Standalone revenue from operations grew 14.98% YoY to ₹104.93 crore and EBITDA rose 10.84% to ₹13.09 crore. Tractor revenue grew 36.29% to ₹52.08 crore, while crane revenue was flat at ₹52.86 crore, which management attributed to the Tier III to Tier V emission norm transition and full utilisation of the existing crane plant. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 20–25% overall revenue growth and 12.5–13% standalone EBITDA margin. The new Bhud plant is targeted for commercial production by end-November 2026, with tower crane production planned for the new line.</overview>

segments.name: Tractors
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ₹52.08 crore, up 36.29% YoY. Management guides 25–30% FY27 growth; utilisation of ~12,000-unit capacity is about 35–40%, and no capacity addition planned. Dealer network about 225.

segments.name: Cranes
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ₹52.86 crore, flat YoY. Existing plant at full capacity (~1,000–1,200 units); guidance 15–20% FY27 growth from existing plant. Dealer network about 25, stagnant for three quarters. New Bhud plant capacity 3,600 units.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall revenue growth maintained at ~20–25% (existing plant only; new plant contribution mainly assumed in Q4).
Tractor revenue growth ~25–30% in FY27; management says 30%-plus over 3–5 years.
Crane revenue growth ~15–20% in FY27 from existing plant.
Standalone EBITDA margin 12.5–13% for FY27; consolidated margin said to be similar to last year (~14–15% per analyst’s reading).

New Bhud plant: commercial production targeted by end-November 2026; machinery expected in October. First year utilisation ~30% (Q1 of operations), 35–40% next quarter, ~40–45% average in FY28 (1,500–1,800 cranes).
Crane price hike taken; further price hike planned in coming months; management expects cost pass-through from Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: New Bhud crane plant: 3,600-unit capacity; civil work in progress; almost all major machines ready; commercial production targeted by end-November 2026.
Tower crane: first prototype passed testing; first lot of 10 machines targeted within Q2 FY27, subject to imported components; some tower crane numbers to be built at the old factory.
Capex funds: ~₹45 crore still held in bank; management says it will be fully deployed by March, possibly by buying 6–8 of 10 planned machines and deferring the rest by up to three months.
Tractor capacity ~12,000 units; no addition planned. Crane machine shop utilisation ~80–85%; crane assembly ~30–35%.
demand_pricing: Crane dealers ~25 (stagnant for three quarters vs. 50-plus target cited by analyst); management plans ~20–25 more dealers within six to12 months of new plant start; Shubham cited a roadmap of ~60-plus dealers nationally, taking one to one-and-a-half years.
Some existing dealers being replaced to match performance expectations; management says working in only ~20–25% of the addressable area.
Tractor dealers ~225; growth tied to dealer development, retail financing, and village-level demos.
Barota Finance finances ~20% of new Indo Farm tractors; refinances old tractors of all brands.
Crane competitors cited: Escorts Construction (premium pricing) and one Faridabad-based peer at similar pricing. Peer ACE grew more than 20% per analyst.
Management says tractor price hikes will follow industry; crane price hike already taken.

qa_highlights.question: Has the crane input cost increase been passed on, and will margins normalise from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should hold from Q2 as demand improves; the Tier III to V transition took about three quarters to stabilise, and cost increases can now be passed on.

qa_highlights.question: Why is crane dealer count stagnant at 25, and what is the plan to absorb new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Dealers to be added once capacity is in place; some dealers replaced. Roadmap of ~60-plus dealers nationally, taking one to one-and-a-half years. FY28 needs ~20–25 dealers to sell 1,500–1,800 cranes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the crane sales volume and YoY volume growth in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Not provided on the call; management said figures would be shared by email via the Finance Head.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tractor utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Tractor utilisation ~35–40%; assembly ~30–35%; machine shop ~80–85% because many crane components are made in-house.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA margin on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone guidance 12.5–13%; consolidated said to move on similar lines to last year, which the analyst interpreted as 14–15%; management confirmed the analyst’s reading.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ₹45 crore capex cash be used by Q3 to start commercialisation by January?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it may buy 6–8 of 10 machines and defer up to three months; full deployment by March. Commercial production still targeted for November.

qa_highlights.question: Can crane growth of 15–20% be achieved with existing capacity before the new plant starts?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management confirmed existing capacity is sufficient for 15–20% growth until the new plant starts.

risks_watch: Crane growth: Q1 flat; FY27 guidance 15–20% depends on July–August demand recovery and dealer additions.
Bhud plant timing: November commercial production depends on machinery arriving in October and on imported tower crane components.
Dealer quality and ramp-up: management says new dealers take 6–18 months; utilisation of new plant guided at 30% in year one.
Tractor volume growth of 25–30% contingent on dealer build-out, financing, and village-level demand; utilisation still ~35–40%.
Price hikes: crane price increase taken; further hikes depend on demand and input costs; tractor pricing follows industry.
Volume disclosure: Q1 unit volumes not disclosed on the call; to be shared later by email.
544328|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on tractors and the new plant timeline, but evasive on specifics: crane dealer targets, unit volumes, and consolidated margin were deferred or loosely answered. Management repeatedly tied crane recovery to Q2 demand without quantifying it.
key_quotes: From this quarter onwards, because demand has increased, I think everything can be passed on to the customers.
We expect to complete these 10 machines within this quarter, subject to receipt of the few components we are expecting from outside.
The new capacity is 3,600 cranes, yes.
Over three to five years in the tractor business, we are very sure that 30% -plus growth will continue.

539876|2026-06.headline: Crompton Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.8% YoY to Rs 2,235 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 20 bps to 10%, despite roughly Rs 200 crore of lost primary sales.
539876|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 11.8% YoY to Rs 2,235 crore, with EBITDA up 14.2% to Rs 224 crore and PAT up 15.2% to Rs 143 crore. Management attributed the quarter to commodity cost and availability disruptions, which led to about Rs 200 crore of lost primary sales, mainly in fans and partly in lighting. Pricing actions of high-single to low-double digits covered about 80% of inflation. Management said supply constraints were largely resolved by end-June and Q2 has started well.

financial_highlights.change: Management cited ~12% growth on the Rs 200 crore supply-loss basis

Five new BLDC fans launched in the quarter

segments.commentary: Revenue +10.6% YoY; BLDC portfolio grew ~45%; market leader in ceiling fans with share gains; pumps gained share; domestic appliances grew double digits led by water heaters, which now lead General Trade in volume. Management cited ~Rs 200 crore of lost primary sales, mostly fans.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 269 crore, +15.4% YoY, on B2B and B2C growth; EBIT margin 12%. B2C margins expanded while B2B margins contracted because of pre-contracted prices.

segments.name: Butterfly Gandhimathi Appliances
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 214 crore, +14% YoY; EBIT +19.5% with margin 4.2%. Growth +18% excluding internal mixer-grinder sales to Crompton; share gains in mixer grinders, pressure cookers and glass tops.

segments.name: Solar rooftops and solar pumps (renewables)
segments.commentary: Rooftop order book about Rs 500 crore, of which about Rs 450 crore to execute over 6-8 months, mainly Andhra Pradesh (~38,000 rooftops for SC/ST homes). Revenue recognised on installation, expected to pick up in Q2; EBITDA margin said to be similar to company EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: A&P as a percentage of sales over the year expected to be similar to last year, per management.
Q2 started well; management is optimistic as volatility has settled.
Solar rooftop order book expected to see the bulk of execution in Q1 and Q2 FY27.
Management does not give formal forward guidance; no price increases seen as necessary at present, with cost measures and operating leverage expected to help margins.
Greenfield manufacturing plant planned over 2-3 years at about Rs 350 crore including a large warehouse; otherwise regular capex trends to continue.
Brand launch event on 18 August 2026 and capital markets investor event on 20 August 2026.
capex_capacity: Baddi plant capacity was raised by about 50% at a very low investment of about Rs 50 lakh, per management.
Greenfield manufacturing plant planned over the next 2-3 years at about Rs 350 crore, including a large warehousing unit.
No plan currently to manufacture wires; wires are sourced via outsourced manufacturing.
Wires business launched in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, present in about 14 towns and cities.
demand_pricing: Pricing actions of high-single digits to low-double digits taken across segments, covering about 80% of inflationary pressure; management said the market has accepted them.
Management attributed Q1 slowdown to supply disruption (~Rs 200 crore lost primary sales, mostly fans, also some lighting) and price-induced sticker shock, not demand suppression.
Butterfly core categories grew in line with competition; core channels grew above 20%; induction cooktops not a significant contributor yet. Gas cylinder shortages hit gas stove sales in the quarter.
Management said channel inventory is not a concern; some replenishment from other sources expected.
Competitors did not follow with the same pricing, per management, possibly due to low-cost inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Was volume growth in ECD modest given the price increases, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply disruptions cost about Rs 200 crore or more of sales; the company runs a lean inventory model and prioritised revenue maximisation within available supply.

qa_highlights.question: Will A&P and other expenses normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P is an active investment year for the Crompton brand; management expects A&P as a percentage of sales over the year to be similar to last year.

qa_highlights.question: Solar rooftop order book, execution and payment cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 500 crore order book with Rs 450 crore to execute over 6-8 months; government pays 40% upfront on product demonstration, with the balance on installation. B2C solar rooftop revenue has started.

qa_highlights.question: Would the Rs 200 crore loss come back?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a mix; some channel replenishment will occur, but Crompton expects to claw back share as supply normalises. CFO said some Q1 impact is seasonal and will not recover quarter-on-quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further price hikes needed given copper costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no sharp set of additional price increases appears necessary currently; cost measures and operating leverage should help. For solar, panel prices are falling and the company's scale improves negotiation.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of Butterfly growth vs competitor TTK's 34%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said core category business (about 85% of Butterfly turnover) grew in line with competition; induction cooktops were not a major contributor, and gas stove sales were hit by LPG cylinder shortages.

risks_watch: Recovery of the ~Rs 200 crore lost primary sales and sustainability of supply after the June-end stabilisation.
Copper and other commodity costs remain high; competitors have not matched price increases, which may lead to share shifts or later pressure.
Solar rooftop revenue depends on installation timing (recognised on installation); the Q1 execution gap may extend into Q2.
Solar pumps payment delays from government were seen earlier but reportedly improved; monsoon can delay installations.
Butterfly's EBIT margin of 4.2% is thin; competitive intensity in kitchen appliances is high.
Lighting B2B margins contracted due to pre-contracted prices.
539876|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and Q2 momentum, but defensive when probed on the Rs 200 crore lost sales and channel inventory. Management deflected segment and sub-segment detail, repeatedly citing non-disclosure.

543389|2026-06.headline: Sigachi Q1 FY27 revenue INR121.27 cr with EBITDA margin 13.6%; management reiterates FY27 guidance of INR650-675 cr revenue and ~18% EBITDA despite run-rate gap.
543389|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 total operating income was INR121.27 crore, with EBITDA of INR16.5 crore (13.6% margin) and PAT of INR8.14 crore (6.76% margin). MCC contributed INR82.74 crore, API INR21.68 crore and O&M INR13.06 crore. Average MCC realisation rose to INR241.36/kg from INR216/kg in Q4, while capacity utilisation was 76.8% across plants. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR650-675 crore revenue and ~18% full-year EBITDA margin, but the Q1 run-rate of ~INR121 crore implies a steep H2 ramp that the call did not fully reconcile.</overview>
