Standalone exports from India declined due to geopolitical and shipping disruptions; Middle East remains affected and buyer sentiment muted by higher landed costs.
Q1 demand was patchy in North and East India due to uneven weather; no secondary sales expected in the coming quarter, only primary off-season buying.
Coolers in the US are used outdoors and as whole-house or window-mounted units, sold through Home Depot and Lowe's; management said US and Mexico sales were helped by a hot Southwest summer.

544495|2026-06.headline: NIS Management Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 15.68% YoY to INR115.44 crore, with EBITDA up 36.24% to INR9.22 crore at a 7.99% margin.

544088|2026-06.headline: Medi Assist Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 24.1% YoY to INR236.5 crore, with operating EBITDA margin at 20.3% and retention down to 90.2%.

FY28 growth guided at 25-30% with 25% as minimum; target of about INR1,000 crores revenue at 29-30% EBITDA margin, and INR1,500 crores by FY30 (management also said FY29 possible if hormone and biologics register on time).
Gross margin expected to improve each quarter to 49-51% at INR700 crores+ revenue and about 47% once BE and niche injectables scale.
Bioequivalence programme of 40 oral solid molecules: 6-7 commercialisable by end FY27, remaining 32 filed by Q1 FY28; INR80-100 crores from BE in FY28 and INR400-500 crores in FY29.
Keytruda biosimilar: pre-clinical to start Dec 2026, clinical trials 1-1.5 years, commercialisation targeted before end CY28.
New global auditor KPMG expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27, pending software upgrades and an EGM.
capex_capacity: Capex breakup given: hormone about INR70 crores, oncology INR50 crores, BE INR25-30 crores, working capital INR20 crores, biosimilar R&D INR10-15 crores; total INR185-190 crores.
Biosimilar clinical trials need about INR150 crores between Q3 FY28 and Q4 FY29.
Hormone plant to finish November 2026; oncology expansion capex to finish by March 2027.
Extended loan sanctioned but unused; INR15-20 crores might be drawn only if cash flow is disrupted.
Capacity utilisation: general facility 75-80%, oncology existing facility 75-80%, cephalosporin and beta-lactam 20-25%, biologicals not commercialised.
demand_pricing: Revenue mix: about 35-40% from ROW markets currently; FY30 mix envisaged at 35% LATAM, 15-20% MENA, 10-15% GCC, 10-15% Europe, with India returning after biosimilar trials.
Management claims low competition in LATAM for injectable registrations and a 200-250 product portfolio target across 70-80 countries.
Raw materials: 80-85% domestic API procurement, 15% from China; no major disruptions reported.
Receivables: about 40% of revenue at 165-170 days; payment cycles from MENA, CIS and GCC improving with recent collections.
Related party: Deepak Bansal (business associate) and Mana Pharma/SD Biopharmaceuticals linked; Kaler Biopharma's proposed oncology plant on hold and the associated land may be sold or re-arranged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did oncology fall to 20% of mix from 26%, and is the 30% target still in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Oncology guided to 25-30% as registrations slipped to Q4 FY27; general-facility registrations from MENA and LATAM were received in the last two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 40% growth continue into FY28, and what margin path leads to 30% in FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 25-30% annual growth with 25% as the floor, targets about INR1,000 crores at 29-30% EBITDA margin and doubling of revenue by end FY30.

qa_highlights.question: How will the BE programme, hormone plant and biologics convert into revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: BE: INR80-100 crores in FY28 and INR400-500 crores in FY29; hormones INR70-80 crores in FY28 and INR200 crores by FY29; FY30 totals exclude biologicals and hormones in the guidance base.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin 53%, and where will it go?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix reflects 35-40% ROW sales; management expects 49-51% at INR700 crores+ and about 47% as BE products scale.

qa_highlights.question: How will capex be funded and what is the breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Funded from internal accruals with extended loan undrawn; INR185-190 crores total including INR70 crores hormone, INR50 crores oncology and INR150 crores for biosimilar trials through FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Governance: when will the new auditor be appointed?
qa_highlights.answer: KPMG to be appointed in Q3 or Q4 FY27 via EGM, pending software upgrades; agreement already filed.

544709|2026-06.headline: Gaudium IVF Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.1% YoY to ₹19.4 crore, while reported EBITDA margin fell to 12.5% from 29% on expansion and marketing costs.
544709|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations grew 9.1% YoY to ₹19.4 crore against ₹17.8 crore in Q1 FY26, with management attributing the slow growth to seasonality and pre-launch work. Reported EBITDA fell 52.96% to ₹2.4 crore and PAT from continuing operations fell 42.27% to ₹1.8 crore, which management tied to front-loaded expansion costs and a one-time pan-India marketing push for the SiD and ERICA AI embryology tools. The South Extension (New Delhi) hub became operational on 16 July 2026, with Gurgaon and Nagpur guided to open in about 10 and 25 days. Management reiterated FY27 targets of about 30% revenue growth and 10 new hubs, but the quarter's growth rate is far below that target.</overview>

segments.name: IVF (core)
segments.commentary: Anchors the business; management says the Janakpuri (Delhi) flagship is growing about 30% YoY. Pharmacy and hospital services are described as lower-margin and complementary, with no separate figures disclosed.

segments.name: Pharmacy and hospital services
segments.commentary: Supply fertility medications and allied women's health services (gynaecology, obstetrics, minimally invasive procedures). No revenue or margin split given on the call.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of about 30% revenue growth for FY27 by year-end, after an analyst challenged whether 40%+ was achievable; it said the growth rate would pick up over Q2 and Q4.
Adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to return to FY26 levels by year-end, per management's answer to a direct question.
Target of 10 new hubs in FY27, then 8 in FY28 and 1 in FY29; South Extension is the first of the 19-centre IPO-funded expansion.
Breakeven for new hubs is said to come in about three months historically, against a six-month industry-type benchmark.
Lucknow Women Hospital project of up to ₹15 crore, funded from internal accruals, with commercialisation expected in FY28-FY29.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex of about ₹25 crore for 10 new hubs at about ₹2.5 crore per hub (₹1 crore construction, ₹1.5 crore lab machinery), funded from IPO proceeds and internal accruals; described as on track.
South Extension, New Delhi hub operational 16 July 2026, with the Gaudium Signature Lab (AI embryology).
Gurgaon hub expected to be operational about 10 days after the call; Nagpur (Tier 2) about 25 days after the call.
Patna centre relocated to Kankarbagh medical hub and became operational about three days before the call.
Mature hub volume benchmarks: about 30 cycles a year for a Tier 2 hub and about 50 for a metro hub.
demand_pricing: Q1 is seasonally weak (heat) and Q3 is weak (festivals); management said Q2 and Q4 make up for it, and that historically growth has been about 30% YoY against an industry CAGR of 10-12%.
Initial IVF package starts at about ₹2 lakh per patient and can go up to ₹20 lakh for complex cases; per-cycle cost cited as about ₹2 lakh.
International patients are about 25-30% of the patient mix; three international spokes have begun in Paris, Nigeria and Sydney.

Management says the organised segment is about 30% of the market versus 70% unorganised, and expects consolidation as the ART Act is implemented; it also said full implementation may take about another year.
HDFC Bank patient financing tie-up is aimed at Tier 2 and Tier 3 patients.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 growth only 9%, and is 30-40% FY27 growth and FY26-level margins achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q1 seasonality and build-up work on centres under construction; it said South Extension is already contributing and reiterated 30% growth and FY26-level adjusted margins by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly does a new hub break even, and at what scale is it profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said breakeven historically comes in about three months, and its centres have broken even within that period wherever they have opened.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter hospital business in Lucknow, and is it funded from IPO proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Lucknow was already on the IVF expansion list, that the women's hospital is a step toward women's health beyond IVF, and that it is funded from internal accruals, not IPO money.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unit economics per hub (capex, package size, cycles)?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex averages ₹2.5 crore per centre; initial package ₹2 lakh up to ₹20 lakh; mature Tier 2 hubs target about 30 cycles a year and metro hubs about 50.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin decline from a one-off expense?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin decline mainly to a one-time pan-India marketing push for SiD and ERICA, expected to pay off over the rest of the year.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue growth be split into patient volume and revenue per patient?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a volume versus price split; it repeated the seasonality explanation and did not address the service-mix question directly.

qa_highlights.question: How are the AI tools differentiated and what is the benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SiD (sperm selection) and ERICA (embryo assessment) are the first such tools in India, certified by IVF 2.0, and show early results of about 8% higher first-attempt success; these are early results and not yet validated over a longer period.

risks_watch: Revenue growth of 9.1% against a 30% full-year target; delivery depends on Q2 and Q4 recovery and on new hubs ramping.
EBITDA margin of 12.5% versus the guided return to FY26 levels; management calls the drag one-off, but it needs verification next quarter.
Early AI-tool success-rate data (about 8% improvement) is not yet validated over a longer period; management said this would need time.
Competitive intensity and the pace of ART Act implementation across states, which management said could take about another year.
Execution on hub openings (Gurgaon, Nagpur) and on the balance of the 10 FY27 hubs; the Lucknow hospital adds a new business line and capex of up to ₹15 crore.

540047|2026-06.headline: DBL Q1 FY27 standalone revenue Rs 1,930 crore and EBITDA margin 10.32%; consolidated PAT fell to Rs 128 crore from Rs 271 crore.
540047|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue was Rs 1,930 crore with EBITDA of Rs 199 crore (10.32% margin, up from 10.11%), and standalone PBT rose about 26% YoY to Rs 72 crore. Standalone PAT fell to Rs 39 crore from Rs 123 crore, but the base quarter included a Rs 98 crore divestment gain. Consolidated revenue dipped to Rs 2,378 crore from Rs 2,620 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of Rs 429 crore (18.05% margin). Management reiterated FY27 guidance (revenue growth 30-40%, EBITDA margin 10-12%, debt reduction Rs 600-800 crore) and announced a stake sale in under-construction transmission and solar projects (about Rs 8,400 crore project cost) to Alpha Alternatives.

financial_highlights.change: margin up from 10.11% in Q1 FY26
vs Rs 123 crore in Q1 FY26, which included ~Rs 98 crore exceptional divestment gain
vs Rs 2,620 crore in Q1 FY26
vs Rs 271 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Completed three HAM packages worth Rs 1,700 crore on Bengaluru-Vijayawada Expressway (AP), all ahead of COD. Management says revenue from large new projects (transmission, roads, solar, water) has not yet started and will ramp from Q2-Q3.

segments.name: MDO (Mining)
segments.commentary: Q1 coal production 4.79 MT; MDO revenue about Rs 362 crore in the quarter per analyst calculation. Siarmal planned 27 MT and Pachhwara 7 MT for FY27; FY29 target 57 MT retained. Pottangi Bauxite production not yet started.

segments.name: Multi-asset platform (InvIT/HAM)
segments.commentary: Holds units worth about Rs 1,521 crore (Rs 1,314 crore Anantam Highway Trust plus Rs 207 crore Shrem InvIT). Next tranche of 11 HAM assets to be transferred to Anantam InvIT by March 2027, expected to yield about Rs 1,700-1,800 crore of units for <Rs 81 crore incremental equity.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 10-12% (reconfirmed; analyst noted 11-12%).
Revenue growth guidance of 30-40% for FY27 reiterated; ramp-up expected from Q3, stronger in Q4 and into Q1 FY28.
Standalone debt reduction guidance of Rs 600-800 crore for FY27 reiterated; standalone net-debt-positive target by FY28 reaffirmed.
FY27 order inflow guidance of Rs 10,000-12,000 crore reiterated; bids worth Rs 15,000-20,000 crore pending opening.
Working capital days expected to reach about 120 by year-end and about 90 next year; from 131-133 days currently.
Finance cost for FY27 targeted at about Rs 350 crore.
Standalone capex guided at under Rs 100 crore for FY27, unchanged.
Coal production target of 57 MT by FY29; coal handling plant (CHP) expected to take about 1.5 years, with Siarmal at 27 MT (FY27), 35 MT (FY28), 50 MT after CHP.
capex_capacity: Siarmal total original capex Rs 2,730 crore, about 40-45% spent; more than 50% of equity already invested; around Rs 300 crore cash sitting at Siarmal SPV; Rs 235 crore residual equity to be funded from SPV accruals.
Siarmal debt sanction Rs 2,000 crore, Rs 60 crore drawn as of 30 June; around Rs 300 crore remaining to draw.

Transmission and solar stake sale to Alpha Alternatives: total equity requirement about Rs 1,600-1,650 crore; Alpha to co-invest 49% during construction; about Rs 900 crore structured equity already raised.

Anantam InvIT: 11 HAM assets, 4 to be flipped in August; 4 CODs done and 3 more by September; all 18 assets targeted for transfer by FY27 end or Q1 FY28, subject to NHAI NOC after six months of first annuity.
Other pipeline: 1977 MW solar mandate, Mekhali interstate transmission (Karnataka), water HAM, oil and gas portfolio to be considered for a future InvIT structure.
demand_pricing: NHAI FY27 pipeline: 54 highway/expressway projects, 2,442 km, about Rs 1.80 lakh crore (26 EPC, 21 HAM, 7 BOT). Awarding in Q1 was soft, particularly in national highways.
NHAI monetisation: 17 stretches (~1,693 km) targeted for FY27 via TOT/InvIT, expected proceeds Rs 30,000-35,000 crore.
Bid pipeline about Rs 1.5 lakh crore per Rohan; management later cited Rs 2.5-3 lakh crore across sectors, of which roads about Rs 1.25 lakh crore.
Declared L1 for Sikasar to Kodar Reservoir Link Canal Pipeline (Chhattisgarh), lump sum about Rs 2,524 crore.
Mining balance contract value about Rs 1.03 lakh crore; MDO reported order book about Rs 5,224 crore (3-year rolling).
Coal MDO pricing: Siarmal about Rs 550-600/t; Pachhwara about Rs 1,150-1,200/t; Siarmal coal fee currently 78%, moving to 100% after CHP.
Input costs: diesel bought at about Rs 140 and bitumen prices roughly doubled during the recent disruption; government reimburses 60-65% of fuel and bitumen cost increase.

544321|2026-06.headline: Consolidated revenue rose 7% to INR554 crores, but EBITDA fell about INR16 crores as Maldives diesel costs spiked; India grew 16% at INR74 crores.
544321|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 7% YoY to INR554 crores and consolidated EBITDA was INR205 crores at a 37% margin. The decline in EBITDA was attributed almost entirely to Maldives fuel and ancillary costs, which rose to INR38 crores from INR19 crores as diesel prices roughly doubled from pre-war levels in April-May. India delivered 13% revenue growth and 16% EBITDA growth, with occupancy and ADR both up. Reported PAT of INR124 crores was inflated by a INR102 crore deferred tax reversal following the tax regime switch.

financial_highlights.change: YoY decline of about INR16 crores
Broadly flat; about 3% growth adjusted for one-off transaction costs
Includes INR102 crore net deferred tax liability reversal from tax regime change; tax rate cut from 34.94% to 25.17%

financial_highlights.value: INR2,095 crores (India INR1,329 crores; Maldives USD81 million / INR766 crores)

segments.name: India hospitality
segments.commentary: Revenue INR203 crores (+13%) and EBITDA INR74 crores (+16%); occupancy rose about 7% to 67% and ADR about 8%, giving RevPAR growth of about 20%. Adjusted for a one-off electricity benefit in the prior year, EBITDA growth would be 18%.

segments.name: Maldives resorts
segments.commentary: Revenue INR218 crores (+5%) but EBITDA INR32 crores (-32%); fuel and ancillary costs rose to INR38 crores from INR19 crores. Excluding the fuel spike, management says EBITDA would have grown about 10%.

segments.name: Annuity (commercial/leased assets)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR128 crores (+3%) and EBITDA INR111 crores at 87% margin; committed occupancy 98%. Narmada Estates in Pune was recently added.

segments.name: Hospitality total
segments.commentary: Hospitality EBITDA declined 4% YoY to INR106 crores; adjusted hospitality EBITDA growth was about 14%.

544912|2026-06.headline: Prasol Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.7% YoY to INR433.6 crores and EBITDA to INR90.3 crores, helped by one-off inventory gains of about INR25 crores.
544912|2026-06.overview:
First earnings call after the 16 September 2026 listing. Revenue from operations was INR433.6 crores (up 35.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin of 20.8% and PAT of INR61 crores (14.1% margin). Management attributed about INR25 crores of gross profit to a sharp rise in selling prices from West Asia-linked supply disruptions and inventory bought at lower prices, which it called partly non-structural. FY27 guidance of INR1,550-1,650 crores revenue and INR240-250 crores adjusted EBITDA excludes these gains, and management described a 15-16% year-end EBITDA margin. A Phase 1 capex of INR250-300 crores for existing products (about 60,000 tpa of added capacity) was outlined.</overview>

segments.name: Acetone-based specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: About 40% of Q1 FY27 revenue; about 43% of FY26 revenue per management.

segments.name: Phosphorus-based specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: About 40% of Q1 FY27 revenue; described as the fastest-growing category, about 38% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Other specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Balance about 20% of Q1 revenue; customised products built around specific customer needs.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 27% of Q1 FY27 revenue, stated as stable or growing despite West Asia disruption to Dubai and Africa shipments.

segments.name: Mahad plant
segments.commentary: About 19,900 tpa capacity; utilisation rose from about 13% in FY24 to 44% in FY26, and management says it was EBITDA and PBT positive in Q1 (about 60% utilisation cited).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,550-1,650 crores and adjusted EBITDA of INR240-250 crores, excluding price fluctuation from geopolitical supply issues and forex gains/losses.
Year-end FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 15-16%.
Normalised gross margin expected at about 30-32%, supported by mix, debottlenecking and captive intermediate consumption.
Management expects pricing to normalise from Q1 elevated levels, with margins moving toward a more sustainable range.
Five-year aspiration of INR2,800-3,000 crores revenue.
Lubricant additive debottlenecking expected to lift capacity 50-70% within 2-3 months; antibacterial product mechanical completion around January, with commercial ramp in the coming year.
Mahad utilisation targeted at 70%-plus by year-end.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity about 98,000 tpa across Khopoli (about 78,800 tpa, near optimum utilisation in FY26) and Mahad (about 19,900 tpa).

Phase 1 capex of INR250-300 crores over about two years for existing products, including INR50-60 crores for land and infrastructure; expected peak revenue of INR500-550 crores. Funded by internal accruals and possibly more debt.
Phase 1 adds about 60,000 tpa; 10-14 projects to come over the next 12-18 months, with the antibacterial product due in about 6 months and lubricant volume expansion before March.
Phase 2 of INR250-300 crores for new R&D products with better margins; site, product and regulatory work still in progress.
INR25 crores floating-roof acetone storage tank planned, plus more than INR25 crores in the next year for adjoining Khopoli land.
Application testing lab and additional 4,000 sq ft R&D space being built, with investments of about INR15-20 crores for application lab.
demand_pricing: Management says volume grew in the mid-single-digit range in Q1, with demand strong across sectors.
Q1 realisations were lifted by a sharp rise in acetone and petrochemical prices after the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption; the company says it does not speculate on raw materials.
Largest customer is about INR55-60 crores of revenue, against the FY27 revenue target; top 10% of customers are about 24-25% of turnover; more than 1,600 customers.
Management says export volumes to Europe were rising to offset weaker shipments to Africa and the Middle East, and that the West Asia war cost up to about 10% of potential export growth.
Antibacterial product: new technology cuts steps from 10 to 3-3.5; management expects more than 100 tons a month once samples are approved (NDA signed with MNC).
REACH registration for six or seven products; mining chemicals approved in US, with commercial volumes expected in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Phase 1 capacity additions (about 60,000 tpa) mainly extensions of existing products, and is the approach application-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said it builds new streams once existing capacity reaches 75-85% utilisation and customer visibility is 3-4 years; it has 10 streams for one client and five hydrogenation reactors.

qa_highlights.question: Will the acetone sourcing diversification need storage or logistics investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR25 crores is set aside for a floating-roof storage tank and more than INR25 crores will go into adjoining Khopoli land over the next year, with barge-based shipping expected to cut transport costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 EBITDA guidance (INR240-250 crores) only modestly above the Q1 run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance excludes about INR25 crores of inventory and forex gains, and it is deliberately conservative given geopolitical uncertainty; it expects Q2 to be near complete.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Mahad outlook and how much EBITDA did it contribute in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahad is PBT and EBITDA positive; the exact EBITDA number was not given and will be revert-back. Utilisation is about 60%-plus, targeted at 70%-plus by year-end; the extra 20 acres will share overheads.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory higher at quarter-end and how is it managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stock is built from January-February for the April season, with raw materials bought at pre-war prices, and that it does not speculate on raw material prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for additional capex for the R&D pipeline, and on what land?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15-20% of about 40 pipeline products typically get commercialised; the newer chemistry will use the land already bought, and environmental clearance for one or two products is in an advanced stage (9-12 months typical).

544181|2026-06.headline: Awfis Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR425 crores and cash EBITDA reached INR44 crores, while blended occupancy held flat at 76%.
544181|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 27% YoY to INR425 crores and reported EBITDA rose 28% to INR162 crores (38.2% margin), with PBT of INR24 crores. Management introduced cash EBITDA as a new metric: INR44 crores (10.1% margin), up about 34% YoY. Occupancy was flat at 76% QoQ, though the mature cohort dipped to 83% from 84% after one enterprise client with about 3,000 seats across five centres exited. Management guided to FY27 cash EBITDA of INR190-200 crores, with H2 expected to outperform H1.

segments.name: Co-working and allied services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR352 crores, up 27% YoY. GCCs contribute 24% of rental revenue from 100+ unique GCC clients across nine cities.

segments.name: Transform (construction and fit-out)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR73 crores, up 25% YoY. Third-party share about 92% this quarter; management says blended margin is around 17-18% (15% on landlord-partner work, 18-20% on third-party). Over 200 crores of mandates won for FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 gross seat additions of 22,000-25,000.
Co-working revenue growth of 23-25% YoY for FY27.
Transform growth of about 20%; total FY27 revenue to exceed INR1,800 crores.
FY27 cash EBITDA of INR190-200 crores, with H2 better than H1 and Q4 expected to show a meaningful improvement in occupancy and margins.
FY27 capex of roughly INR200-210 crores.
Premium mix expected to move from about 85:15 to about 80:20 by end FY27, as about 10 of 13 pipeline properties are premium (Gold/Elite).
capex_capacity: Operational seats about 159,000 across 242 centres in 18 cities; 9 centres under fit-out (total 251); pipeline of 267 centres including LOIs.
Total capacity including fit-out about 170,000 seats; including signed LOIs over 185,000 seats.
Q1 gross seat additions about 4,600 against about 1,800 seats exited in portfolio consolidation.

Malpani Estates developer partnership (Pune, two Grade A+ assets, 1.4 lakh sq ft). Developer partnership centres expected to go live in 9-15 months; company contributes about 50% of fit-out value upfront as a security deposit; 9-year agreements.
Seven premium properties in the portfolio (two live, five under construction), priced 30-50% above the existing portfolio. Elite centres rose from 8 to 10; Gold held at 27.
Management expects over 12,000 seats on track in H1 FY27 across the three multiformat pillars.
demand_pricing: Active clients over 3,600; corporates and MNCs about 64% of base. Weighted average client tenure 38 months; average lock-in 26 months.
Mix by sector: technology 39%, professional services 21%, BFSI 13%, manufacturing 12%, healthcare and life sciences 5%. Domicile: 52% India-headquartered, 43% North American or European.
Clients with 500+ seats make up 37% of portfolio. Q1 sold 13,000 seats.
Blended occupancy 76% (flat QoQ); mature cohort (over 12 months old) 83%, down from 84%.
Pricing: 4-7% contractual escalation within same client; management says price per seat has risen every quarter over eight quarters. No exact figure given.
Replacement of vacated capacity: significant part pre-committed, some at higher pricing than the exited client paid.
Industry: H1 2026 flex leasing 8.4 million sq ft (+55%); GCC leasing 16.5 million sq ft (+38%).

qa_highlights.question: Why did rental payments jump from about INR85 crores in Q4 to about INR130 crores in Q1, and is the company shifting toward straight lease?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the cash-flow rent figure excludes rent booked in other expenses (MA profit shares and out-of-lock-in leases not under Ind AS 116); that line was flat, so combined growth is in line with indices. Management said MA is 57% of current supply (down from 62%), and the mix is opportunistic, not a shift away from MA.

qa_highlights.question: How do developer partnerships work: construction stage at signing, delivery timing, capital contribution and access period?
qa_highlights.answer: Centres could go live 9-15 months after signing. Company contributes about 50% of fit-out value on day one as a security deposit until go-live. Nine-year agreements start at signing, with the nine years counted from OC and possession.

qa_highlights.question: What is per-seat revenue trend given chargeable area growth versus revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 68% vs 65% comparison, because chargeable area includes unlive fit-out seats. Net operational seats rose 59% from about 100,000 to 159,000 against 65% revenue growth. Price per seat rises through 4-7% escalations and premium mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Transform's third-party share about 92%, and what are its margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Transform has shifted to third-party work; the 92% reflects this quarter's delivery mix and is expected to stay structurally high. Margins: about 15% on landlord-partner work and 18-20% on third-party, blending to 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the implied FY27 cash EBITDA margin only about 10% when occupancy is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the exit of one large client, where the company kept fixed costs on five centres to refill them, and a timing gap of 3-4 quarters between landlord rent resets (many 2021 leases) and customer repricing. H2 is expected to be better, with Q4 showing a meaningful improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the portfolio is premium, and is the new supply institutional?
qa_highlights.answer: About 37 of 242 live centres (about 15%) are Gold/premium. Of the 13 properties in LOI or fit-out, about 10 are premium. The premium mix is expected to reach about 80:20 by end FY27. All pipeline assets are institutional.

543936|2026-06.headline: Senco Gold Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 67% YoY and EBITDA margin fell to 7.0% (INR213 crores) on gold-price, discounting and one-off cost effects.
543936|2026-06.overview:
Senco crossed INR3,000 crores of sales in a single quarter, with consolidated revenue up about 67% YoY and retail up 50%, same-store sales growth around 39%. April was the strong month (about INR1,500-1,600 crores), while May and June moderated to roughly INR500-600 crores a month amid West Bengal elections, Adhik Maas and heat wave. Reported EBITDA was INR213 crores at 7.0% margin and consolidated PAT INR101 crores at 3.3%, with margin pressure from other expenses (about INR195 crores vs about INR80 crores a year earlier), a gold-price decline, discounting and GML-related finance cost. Management retained FY27 guidance of 20%+ value growth and a 7.5%-7.8% sustainable operational EBITDA margin, and said July and August are running about 25% YoY ahead.</overview>

523301|2026-06.headline: TCPL Packaging Q1 FY27 PAT rose ~79% YoY to INR 40 crore on 16% total income growth, and the company announced a INR 125 crore lithium-ion battery separator film venture.

Cash profit rose 56% to INR 76 crore and PAT rose nearly 79% to INR 40 crore, helped partly by a normalised interest cost versus a forex/mark-to-market hit in the prior-year quarter. Growth was domestic-led (good double-digit domestic growth, export growth positive but lower) with volumes up high single digits. Management announced a proposed subsidiary to enter lithium-ion battery separator films (INR 125 crore over 18 months, commercial production targeted Q4 FY28) and a ~30% expansion of flexible packaging capacity (INR 50-60 crore).

544342|2026-06.headline: Stallion Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.78% YoY to ₹124.68 crore while PAT jumped 79.15% to ₹18.57 crore; management says margins are partly one-off.
544342|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached ₹124.68 crore (+12.78% YoY), EBITDA rose 75.85% to ₹25.27 crore and PAT rose 79.15% to ₹18.57 crore. Management attributed the margin jump to a mix of better product mix (higher HFO share), earlier logistics planning and inventory gains, splitting EBITDA roughly 50:50 between inventory gains and operations. The high-purity helium plant at Khalapur (1,200 MTPA) is complete with commercial operations expected next quarter, while the 10,000 MT R32 plant at Bhilwara slipped from a July 2026 target to end-December 2026, and Mambattu (HFO blending) is now due by year-end. Management reiterated 30-35% revenue CAGR guidance but cut the FY27 contribution expectation from the R32 plant and opened the door to dilution or debt for expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30-35% revenue growth guidance still intact after the R32 delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said the 30-35% is intact, while acknowledging the FY27 R32 contribution will change slightly from ₹250 crore; Q4 R32 revenue expected around ₹125 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the R32 plant delayed and what funding was used?

qa_highlights.question: What are the helium volumes and how is supply secured given Middle East shipping disruption?

543489|2026-06.headline: Gateway Distriparks Q1 FY27: ICD volumes stagnant YoY on West Asia war disruption; management still targets double-digit FY27 growth; no financial figures disclosed on call.
543489|2026-06.overview:
Management said ICD market has de-grown in its operating markets since April due to the West Asia conflict, but Gateway's market share is intact. Volumes were flat YoY, with June and July trends similar to Q1 and July hit by weather-related port and double-stacking restrictions. Snowman Logistics reported 5-7% warehousing price increases and guided 10-15% top-line growth, with about 24,000 additional pallets by end FY27. The call did not disclose quarterly financial figures in the transcript.</overview>

segments.commentary: Management cited ~6-6.5 million pairs contract volume at ~Rs 60 per pair (~Rs 36 crore revenue, 10-12% operating margin); branded target of 2 million pairs in two years at Rs 200-250 per pair.

segments.name: Handbags (Ahikoza, via Brahm Lifestyle)
segments.commentary: About 600 bags sold this year at ~$1,200 retail; target of 2,000 bags at ~$2,000 in two years (~$2 million sales).

segments.name: Brahm Fresh (seafood/meat D2C, Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Run-rate ~Rs 1 crore per month; management targets ~Rs 100 million FY-end sales at ~10% EBITDA margin; app launch mid-September.

segments.name: Skill by Brahm (fitness/wellness, Pune)
segments.commentary: Targeting Rs 5 crore sales in first year via memberships; online launch planned November in Pune.

segments.name: Restaurant and spas (Pune, Bengaluru)
segments.commentary: Pune Club restaurant breaking even; three spas in Bengaluru operated under Unwind by Brahm. Described as small-scale with no significant capital need.

guidance_outlook: Socks: branded plus contract revenue of ~Rs 100 crore and EBITDA of Rs 20-40 crore in two years (management's own projection).

Lord Walker: target of ~1 million pairs in calendar 2027, with 5-year plan toward a global lifestyle brand.

Spare capacity cited as the rationale for branded and DTC expansion, with contract manufacturers in the Gujarat ecosystem available for support.
Brahm Fresh app launch mid-September; Skill by Brahm online in Pune in November.
Handbag production: leather sourced from Indonesia, assembly in India; apparel tie-ups in Kolkata, Coimbatore and Bengaluru.

demand_pricing: Virat exports to UK and Switzerland; UK FTA operational from 15 July 2026 removes 11% import duty on Indian socks, per management.
Customers include John Lewis, Waitrose, Barbour, FootAsylum, Umbro, Castore, Sudu, Kukri, Migros (~300 stores) and Galaxus (Switzerland).

qa_highlights.question: How mature is each business and how will management bandwidth be handled across multiple businesses?

qa_highlights.question: Where will the Rs 95 crore be deployed?

qa_highlights.question: Can management provide revenue, EBITDA or ROCE guidance for 12-24 months?

qa_highlights.question: Will Virat expand into products beyond socks, such as gloves or knitwear?

risks_watch: Related-party style transaction: Rs 95 crore primary raise into a promoter-linked entity, with ambiguity on valuation, pricing and minority-shareholder protection (management said near book value).

Management bandwidth across many new businesses, with the group management focus on the lifestyle platform.
Execution milestones to track: ROC approval of name change, Brahm Fresh app launch in mid-September, Skill by Brahm launch in November, Lord Walker volumes against 1 million pairs in CY2027.
Regulatory check on the NSE trading permission; the company clarified it is not yet listed on NSE, only permitted to trade.

517544|2026-06.headline: Centum Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 11% YoY to INR205 crore; order book ~INR1,800 crore (+31% YoY), with overseas exit adding a INR94 crore one-time gain.
517544|2026-06.overview:
Standalone revenue grew about 11% YoY to INR205 crore with EBITDA margin of 11.28% and PAT margin of 6.59%, which management said was held back by lower BTS contribution and project phasing. Consolidated revenue was INR204 crore (+14% YoY), and consolidated PAT of INR106 crore includes a one-time INR94 crore deconsolidation gain from the overseas subsidiaries; profit from continuing operations was INR11 crore. Management asked investors to judge the year on a full-year basis, citing stronger execution expected in later quarters.</overview>

segments.name: BTS (build-to-spec, defence and space)
segments.commentary: Order book grew ~40% YoY and order inflow was INR120 crore (+150% YoY), but quarterly revenue was held back by project execution schedules. About two-thirds of the ~INR210 crore advances are from BTS.

segments.name: EMS (electronic manufacturing services)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 20% YoY and order book rose 23% YoY. EMS EBITDA is benchmarked at about 10-11% on a cost-plus model.

segments.name: Semiconductor equipment (within EMS)
segments.commentary: Revenue was practically zero in FY25, exceeded INR100 crore in FY26, and management targets USD25-30 million in the next 1-2 years, with a global OEM as customer.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth of about 25% for FY27 and sees similar visibility for FY28.
EBITDA margin aim is above 13% for FY27 (FY26 reported about 12.5%), with stability or slight improvement expected in FY28; FY28 commentary is preliminary.
Export share of revenue expected at about 50-55% or slightly higher.
BTS to EMS revenue mix expected at roughly 70:30, possibly marginally tilted toward BTS over 1-2 years.
Standalone capex at KIADB Aerospace Park: about INR50-70 crore estimate, with spend largely starting toward the end of FY28; no Centum capex this year because the land is held by a group company.
Export BTS margin target is around 20-plus percent.
Management expects a strong SBS (space-based surveillance) order intake this year.
capex_capacity: KIADB Aerospace Park (Bengaluru): design complete, construction to start soon on land owned by a group company; Centum outlay is nil this year, with capex flow expected toward the end of next fiscal.
Full factory, MEP/HVAC, clean room and plant machinery ordering to follow after shell completion.
Engineering team ramp-up in BTS for system integration, with new talent being hired.
NPI process initiated for electrification and grid automation products, expected to contribute meaningfully in about 2 years.
demand_pricing: BTS demand is strong in space, radar, electronic warfare and air navigation; management expects continued strong order intake through the year.

EMS semiconductor equipment: products in serial production after full qualification; new part numbers are being added. Customer IP sits with the customer, which limits selling the same product to rivals.
Competition in EMS is mainly in Southeast Asia (Malaysia); management says it is the main EMS supplier in India for this customer.
A new INR55-odd crore export order was won for complex test systems in aerospace and defence; management says test-system revenue is lumpy and not recurring.
Management says it is in early preliminary talks with other semiconductor customers for India sourcing.

qa_highlights.question: Will BTS revenue recognition accelerate given the order book has nearly doubled since FY24 and project cycles exceed 2.5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects clear strong BTS revenue growth this year and in coming years, with quarterly variation because of lumpy contracts. About two-thirds of the ~INR210 crore advances are from BTS.

qa_highlights.question: Semiconductor equipment: who are the customers, and what are the margins?
qa_highlights.answer: A key global OEM is the customer, ramped over the last year. Revenue was over INR100 crore in FY26 against about zero in FY25, and the target is USD25-30 million in 1-2 years. EBITDA is about 10-11% on cost-plus.

qa_highlights.question: Will BTS revenue mix move sustainably beyond 70:30 in favour of BTS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BTS may be marginally higher over 1-2 years, but not hugely different from the 70:30 split.

qa_highlights.question: Will India revenue growth stay at the medium-term target of 25%-plus this year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company is confident of reaching about 25% and will maintain that target for now.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27/FY28 guidance for revenue, margins and export mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth about 25% for FY27 with similar visibility for FY28. Margin aim is above 13% in FY27. Export share is about 50-55% or higher.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the KIADB Aerospace Park facility and the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Design is complete and construction is starting soon on group-owned land, so no Centum capex this year. Capex of INR50-70 crore could start toward the end of next fiscal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope of the export BTS opportunity and its margin?
qa_highlights.answer: An export electronic-warfare BTS opportunity is at an early stage. Margin target is around 20-plus percent, and export system-level deals may carry higher margins because they are not tender-based.

risks_watch: Q1 was described as muted; the full-year growth and margin targets depend on a sharp pick-up in BTS execution in Q2-Q4.
Margin was 11.28% standalone EBITDA, below the >13% FY27 aim, so H2 execution must lift the mix.
Semiconductor-equipment revenue depends on a single global OEM and on semiconductor capex cycles; management flagged possible variability.
Test-system and certain BTS revenues are lumpy and volatile, per management.
Consolidated PAT of INR106 crore is inflated by INR94 crore one-time gain; continuing-ops PAT was only INR11 crore.
Monitor SBS and EW order conversion, and first deliveries for UHM, Virupaksha and TACAN programmes.
Watch for direct armed-forces system-level orders and first DLM (design-led manufacturing) wins.
517544|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on full-year growth and the order book, but candid that Q1 was muted on growth and margins. Management was evasive on specific customer names and on FY28 margins, and it said these would be updated as opportunities mature.

513519|2026-06.headline: Pitti Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to ₹529 crores, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 16.8% and Lamination FY27 volume target raised to 82,000 tons.

Adjusted PAT was ₹32 crores versus ₹26 crores a year earlier. Lamination and assembly volume grew 19% to about 19,200 tons, and management raised its FY27 Lamination target to 82,000 tons from 78,000 tons. 543992|2026-06.headline: Yatra Q1 FY27 gross bookings rose 17% to INR21,007 million, but adjusted EBITDA fell 39% to INR151 million on MICE disruption and Kanoo build-out costs.
543992|2026-06.overview: Gross bookings grew about 17% YoY to INR21,007 million and gross margin rose 6.1% to INR1,227 million, while revenue from operations fell 10.4% to INR1,879 million as MICE top line dropped about INR300 million. Adjusted EBITDA declined 39.4% to INR151 million (12.29% of gross margin) and PAT was INR3.4 million. Management attributed the margin squeeze to temporary MICE disruption, air margin pressure from delayed Middle East airline PLB deals, and pre-revenue people and platform costs for the Kanoo partnership. No FY27 guidance was issued; management said it expects to provide guidance next quarter.

544432|2026-06.headline: Indogulf Q1 FY27 revenue fell 11% YoY to Rs 168.5 crore on delayed monsoon, but gross margin rose to 28% from 22%.
544432|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue from operations declined 11% YoY to Rs 168.5 crore, though it rose about 12% QoQ from Rs 150.8 crore in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the weakness to delayed and uneven southwest monsoon, which pushed sowing and crop protection applications into later periods, along with cautious dealer stocking and softer prices from Chinese supply. Gross profit rose 12% to Rs 46.6 crore and gross margin widened to 28%, while EBITDA fell about 4% to Rs 9.6 crore with margin up to 5.7%. PAT fell to Rs 2.4 crore from Rs 3.9 crore as finance costs rose about 19% YoY. Management declined to give FY27 growth guidance.</overview>

511034|2026-06.headline: Jindal Drilling Q1 FY27: ONGC awarded a rig contract at ~INR45 lakh/day fixed; order book INR1,310 crore, with three rigs to dehire later in FY27.
511034|2026-06.overview:
Management described Q1 FY27 as fairly good and broadly in line with expectations, with total revenue flat over the previous couple of quarters. EBITDA was stable; the variation in other expenses was driven by forex, which was more pronounced in Q4 FY26 and less so in Q1 FY27. The key development was a new ONGC contract for Jindal Pioneer, which is under refurbishment in UAE with deployment targeted for October 2026. The order book stands at INR1,310 crore, and three rigs are expected to dehire within FY27, which management said will reduce H2 revenue. The call also disclosed a JV loss tied to Pioneer refurbishment and an update on a long-running ONGC legal dispute.</overview>

543227|2026-06.headline: Happiest Minds to merge into ITC Infotech; promoter Soota sells 22.1% for ~INR 1,330 crore cash, ITC to hold ~73.4% of combined entity.
543227|2026-06.overview: This special call covered the proposed combination of Happiest Minds with ITC Infotech, not a quarterly results update. Promoter Ashok Soota will divest 22.1% of his 44.2% stake in two cash tranches (about INR 1,330 crore total) to ITC Infotech. Happiest Minds will be amalgamated into ITC Infotech, with its shareholders receiving 25 ITC Infotech shares for every 81 Happiest Minds shares. Management targets USD 1 billion revenue by FY28 (earlier FY31) and a combined operating margin of about 18.1-18.3%. Management declined to give detail on integration, leadership, client overlap and AI revenue, citing the pending CCI approval.

financial_highlights.metric: ITC Infotech revenue FY20 to FY26

segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA margin 17.3%; valued at 15.1x FY26 EBITDA; brings AI, digital, product engineering, cloud, data and cybersecurity capabilities. Management said it sustained similar growth to ITC Infotech over the last one to two years.

segments.name: ITC Infotech
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 4,718 crore, roughly 2.17x Happiest Minds; EBITDA margin 18.3%; valued at 13.6x FY26 EBITDA. Strengths in SAP, PLM, Industry 4.0, enterprise applications and transformation. ITC Limited wholly owns it and it is unlisted.

Synergies around 10% were referenced by an analyst; management did not quantify synergies in the call.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or utilisation figures were discussed.

Both entities continue operating separately until all regulatory approvals are received.

qa_highlights.question: Who will lead the combined entity and what are incentive and continuity plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Leadership, roles and incentives will be discussed only after CCI approval; both sides committed to retaining all people. No contracts exist for top management beyond meeting of minds.

qa_highlights.question: Client overlap between the two entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no overlap among large customers and very limited overlap in tail accounts; full 800-customer analysis to follow in a couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14% ITC Infotech CAGR organic or inorganic, and what are the near-term targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Largely organic per financial due diligence; only Blazeclan (cloud) and an earlier PTC acquisition. Near-term focus is cross-selling and turnkey large deals after CCI approval; no quantified synergy targets given.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the open offer not triggered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the trigger is above 24% stake; the sale happens in two 11% tranches (about 22% total), so no open offer.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the promoter retain about 7.5% post-merger and why was merger structured this way?
qa_highlights.answer: Partial liquidity was the aim; the remainder shares in future growth. Minimum public shareholding (25%) rules meant ITC cannot take 100%, so Happiest Minds merges into ITC Infotech rather than the reverse.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Happiest Minds carry a higher valuation multiple (15.1x vs 13.6x)?
qa_highlights.answer: Independent valuers cited the AI-led positioning, recency of business mix, growth record over five years and listed status, versus ITC Infotech's customer list.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR 395 transaction price different from INR 405 implied value?
qa_highlights.answer: Tranche 1 at INR 390 and Tranche 2 at INR 400 average to INR 395; INR 405 is the valuation-exercise value used for the swap ratio, about INR 10 higher.

qa_highlights.question: How will margin expansion of 100 bps occur and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Via scale (SG&A absorption over a base about 2.17x larger), office consolidation, and better bench utilisation and deployment; no timeline provided.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the ITC rights issue into ITC Infotech?
qa_highlights.answer: ITC, as sole owner of ITC Infotech, will fund the share purchase through a rights issue; management said this was factored into the swap ratio with no valuation impact.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify AI revenue contribution and visibility beyond USD 1 billion.
qa_highlights.answer: No AI revenue figure given; management will track cross-sell index, large-deal proposals and conversion, TCV and order book, with details expected in a few months.

527001|2026-06.headline: Ashapura Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19.2% to INR1,616 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR188.9 crore and margin fell to 11.7%.
