SEM onboard charger and multifunction unit lines to be commissioned by end of Q2 FY27; samples then need about 4 months of on-road trials (around 50,000 km), so supplies expected around December 2026 or January 2027.
STML fully automated facility in Bangalore; current capacity about INR140 crore on 3-shift basis; commercial supplies from Q2 FY27.
SEM current capacity over INR300 crore without further investment.
Total invested capital in subsidiaries about INR100 crore (STML about INR50 crore, SEM about INR48-49 crore).
demand_pricing: Steel price increases in Q1 created cost pressure; lower-cost inventory largely consumed, so impact expected to be more visible in the coming quarter.
Steel pass-through negotiations typically take 2-4 months; management says customers are positive on compensating for inflation this year.
Industry: PV sales +25.9% to 1.27 million, 2W +20.3% to 5.63 million, CV +18.3%, 3W +29.7% YoY in Q1 FY27 per management.
SEM: LCV, HCV and public transport bus programs gaining traction; EV demand supported by high oil prices.
Integrated units for heavy bus and truck platforms priced at about INR3-3.5 lakh per unit.
Two new 2-wheeler programs at advanced stage with one OEM response expected in coming months; management sees second-sourcing opportunity at incumbents.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin rise about 270 bps while EBITDA margin rose only about 40 bps in standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited steel price increases plus broad inflation (chemicals, tungsten, minimum wages up to 35% in some areas), partly offset by shop-floor efficiencies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fasteners capacity utilisation and when will new capex be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation at 90-95%, described as fully utilised given product mix; most of the INR88 crore capex expected to commission in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How should standalone EBITDA margin be considered for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect EBITDA to weaken further and expects to hold full-year margin structures, based on price increases at an advanced stage.

qa_highlights.question: What are breakeven levels and timeline for SEM and STML?
qa_highlights.answer: Both expected to break even in FY28; SEM at about INR175 crore revenue and STML at about INR70 crore, combined about INR225-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak revenue capacity of the subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: SEM over INR300 crore and STML about INR140 crore on current capacity, total about INR440 crore (corrected from INR400 crore plus).

qa_highlights.question: Will the fasteners capex take capacity to INR1,000 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, if markets support it, with a further INR25-30 crore of investment next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new SEM onboard charger and multifunction line contributing soon?
qa_highlights.answer: Lines commissioned by end of Q2; customer trials of about 4 months mean supplies around December 2026 or January 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why is SEM loss-making and what is the R&D spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Loss due to revenue collapse after anchor customer in-sourcing (FY25 revenue of about INR380 crore falling by about INR280 crore) and continuing R&D; about 130 people, more than half in product or application engineering.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ADAS regulatory opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulation for medium and heavy CVs, about 0.5 million units a year, from October 2027, possibly pushed to January 2028; a Chinese partner signed.

535789|2026-06.headline: Sammaan Capital posted Q1 FY27 PAT of INR243 crores, with cost of funds falling from 10.5% to 10% and AUM at INR56,239 crores.
535789|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 as the first quarter under IHC ownership, with PAT of INR243 crores after last quarter's balance-sheet markdowns. Disbursements were about INR3,875-3,900 crores across five products to roughly 12,000 new customers, and net NPA is 0.15%. Cost of funds declined through the quarter, helped by rating upgrades (domestic AA to AA+, international B+ to BB-) and repricing of existing borrowings. Management reiterated a shift from portfolio management to growth, a build-out of branches, tech and senior hiring, and multi-year targets for cost of funds, cost-to-income, ROE and ROA.

financial_highlights.change: Following balance-sheet markdowns and provisions taken in the prior quarter; no YoY comparison stated
Stated as in line with guidance; no QoQ figure given
Home loans about INR664 crores; loans against property about INR2,000 crores
Described as standard in normal course of business
Down about 50 bps during the quarter
International rating upgraded from B+ to BB-

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: About INR664 crores disbursed in Q1; mortgage remains the anchor product this year.

segments.name: Loans against property (LAP)
segments.commentary: About INR2,000 crores disbursed in Q1, the largest product by disbursement; micro LAP planned as a mainstay.

segments.name: Loans against securities / unsecured / credit-fund deal
segments.commentary: Loans against securities INR262 crores and unsecured about INR100 crores in Q1; one INR840 crore co-lending deal with an Asia-based credit fund (20% Sammaan, 80% fund).

guidance_outlook: Disbursements: INR10,000 crores in H1 FY27 (Q1 on target) and INR20,000 crores in H2, total INR30,000 crores for FY27; INR40,000-50,000 crores in FY28.
Cost of funds: 9.6% by September, 9.3% by end-FY27, and 7-8% range over the next 2-3 years; management said below 8% over three years.
Cost-to-income: about 50% in FY27, declining from H2 FY28, targeted at 30-35% by FY29.
Branches: about 240 at end of H1 FY27, rising to 270, with 800 branches targeted by end of FY28.
Five-year targets cited on the call: ROE 6.8% to 18.7%, ROA 1.8% to 8.1%, NIM 3.5% to 8%, as put out on May 20.
Inorganic growth to be considered from FY28; the bias for now is to build.
capex_capacity: Branch network to rise from about 240 at end-H1 FY27 to 270; 23 master service centres across 20 states; management targets 800 branches by end of FY28.
Digital-first app to go live in H2 FY27, integrating a new Salesforce-based CRM and a new loan management system, plus a data lake.
Digital personal loans to launch on the app in H2 FY27; gold loans, two-wheeler loans and BNPL-type e-commerce tie-ups targeted by end-FY28.
53 AI use cases under implementation, with about 60% to be implemented in FY27; about 66% of identified use cases reportedly in motion.
Hiring: mid-level and ground-level offer-to-join cycle is 90-120 days; senior management hires expected to be announced towards the end of Q1/start of Q2.
demand_pricing: FY27 disbursement mix: about 75% mortgage-backed (two-thirds retail, one-third wholesale AUM with about 20% kept on balance sheet), 25% new products; about 90% secured and 10% unsecured in FY27, moving to 80:20 in FY28.

Securitisation and asset-light model: at least 30% of origination to be securitised or sold down, with 60-70% kept as a backup option; assets below 9.5% to be sold down via direct assignment, above 9.5% sliced between balance sheet and securitisation.
Asset yield universe cited from 8.5% (prime) to about 20% (unsecured); LAP 11-12% and affordable loans 12-13% also eligible for securitisation.
Fee income expected to rise, with direct assignment fee income kicking in around October 2026 with about a six-month lag.
97% of Q1 disbursements and 97% of AUM are secured.

qa_highlights.question: Raghav Garg (Ambit): Will lower cost of funds be passed on to customers for acquisition, or will spreads be retained?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy rides on lower cost of funds plus asset-light model; sub-9.5% assets to be sold down via direct assignment and higher-yield assets kept or securitised, balancing fee and spread income.

qa_highlights.question: Bhanu Chauhan (Barclays): How much upfront opex and what is the cost-to-income path?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex will rise in absolute terms, offset by fee income with a lag of a quarter or two; cost-to-income around 50% this year, declining from H2 FY28, reaching 30-35% by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Abhiram Iyer (Deutsche Bank): What is the asset-class breakup of the roughly INR3,000 crore per half target?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 mix about 75% mortgage-backed and 25% new products; disbursement breakdown to expand from 4-5 boxes to at least 8 by end-FY27 and 15 by end-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Vinit Agarwal (Bajaj Alternates): What tangible benefits has IHC delivered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 90 bps saving on about INR50,000 crore borrowings (about INR450 crore annualised), targeting a further 70 bps; software procurement at 30-50% of earlier costs; and senior talent additions.

qa_highlights.question: Sanket (DAM Capital): What is IHC's larger vision beyond lending in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Dalia Khorshid (IHC) said the group is open to opportunities in India across fintech, digital, AI and financial services, with Sammaan seen as a platform; management said FY27 is for stabilisation and other fee businesses will be evaluated later.

qa_highlights.question: Niharika (CapGrow): Are the five-year ROE, ROA and NIM targets achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident, citing rating upgrades, lower cost of funds, asset-light model and tech, with governance as the enabler.

qa_highlights.question: Nilesh Sharma (Monomer): What are disbursement targets for this and next financial year?
qa_highlights.answer: INR30,000 crores in FY27 (INR10,000 crores H1, INR20,000 crores H2) and INR40,000-50,000 crores in FY28.

506879|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.1% YoY to INR43.8 crore and EBITDA margin hit 47.5%, while the company pursues a debt- and equity-funded acquisition of MicroBiopharm Japan and Sanofi brands.
506879|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR43.8 crore (up 22.1% YoY) on higher sales volumes, with EBITDA up 49.4% to INR20.8 crore at a 47.5% margin and PAT of INR11.1 crore (up 22.1%). Management described the business as sold out in capacity for years and said the expanded fermentation capacity (about 540 KL, roughly doubling capacity) starts full operation by end-August 2026. The call focused mostly on the strategic pivot to a fermentation-based CDMO, the MicroBiopharm Japan (MBJ) acquisition, and the Sanofi brand portfolio, with funding (up to INR1,000 crore equity, debt mix undecided) and deal timing left open.

financial_highlights.change: from about INR62 crore in FY23; about INR370 crore added in 3 years

segments.name: Standalone GTBL - fermentation and API (Rifamycin-S, Rifapentine, Rifaximin)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue has been stuck around the historic INR40 crore run rate; API block bookings are in Rifapentine, Rifaximin and Rifamycin-S. Management said API output began only recently because intermediate capacity was the constraint.

segments.name: MicroBiopharm Japan (MBJ) - to be acquired
segments.commentary: MBJ is about 100% API CDMO, with roughly 4-5% formulations; 60% of its business is CDMO, and revenue is 60% Japan and 40% outside Japan. Revenue by vertical was not disclosed. ADCs are patented but have no CDMO project yet; other platforms are commercialised.

segments.name: Sanofi brands (13 anti-TB and anti-infective brands)
segments.commentary: Branded generics sold in 55 countries across Europe, Middle East and Africa. Revenue and margin figures were not disclosed. Manufacturing will move to CMOs over a 3-year transition services agreement.

guidance_outlook: Expanded fermentation capacity to be fully operational by end-August 2026; output to start partly in Q2 and fully in H2 FY27.
Base-case growth target of high-teens percentage per annum over the next 3-5 years; no revenue number given.
Base-business capex for FY27 about INR20 crore including maintenance, with INR10-15 crore of last-mile capex.
MBJ closing targeted around end-August 2026 with funding largely secured; Sanofi closing long-stop date June 2027, needing approvals in over 50 countries.
Hybrid power Phase 1 expected to go live in September 2026, Phase 2 about two months later; management expects EBITDA margin improvement.
Management expects some synergy projects with MBJ within the first year.
capex_capacity: Fermentation capacity has been roughly doubled (additional 540 KL); some capacity is for R&D and cGMP pilot facilities. Management said utilisation is effectively 0 or 100 and all output must be commercialised.
API block output started only recently, with fermentation constraints having delayed it by about two years versus the November 2023 guidance of FY25.
Gross block incremental INR370 crore over three years, of which about INR200 crore is fermentation and API facilities (asset turn 1.4-1.5x).
Hybrid power project is in progress and expected to lower power costs.
demand_pricing: Management said FY26 was stable and that the company was sold out on capacity; one year saw a dip due to excessive rains and power fluctuations.
Rifampicin to Rifapentine market shift is slower than hoped; management said Rifa-S demand is unaffected because GTBL is ready with both APIs.
A dispute with Optimus Drugs, a major customer, has been resolved and business is restarting; management said other buyers were available and capacity was sold out during the suspension.
Management said the company aims to sell intermediates to other Indian and global API makers to reduce customer concentration.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there nearly a three-year gap in earnings calls, and why was the API block revenue delayed from FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business was flat but sold out; capex was late by about a year. API could not start because intermediate capacity was fully contracted to long-term customers.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR3,000 crore acquisition make sense given interest costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Sanofi deal is expected to close later, with long-stop June 2027, and that interest rates in the target geographies are much lower than 10%. It said the business is cash-flow positive from the start.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding structure for the MBJ and Sanofi deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity raise of up to INR1,000 crore is planned; the debt component is undecided and will depend on the optimal mix, with options kept open.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for the base business in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR10-15 crore of last-mile capex remains, and total base-business capex including maintenance is about INR20 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path from Sanofi brands to manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: A 3-year transition services agreement will move marketing authorisations country by country, with manufacturing moved to CMOs; management hopes for faster transfer, with tech transfer complete in year 1.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Themis Medicare merger withdrawn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an external strategy review led it to focus on a fermentation-based CDMO and avoid diluting focus with predominantly domestic businesses.

risks_watch: Funding and leverage: INR1,000 crore equity planned; debt amount undecided. Interest and dilution implications are open.
Integration and bandwidth risk from two acquisitions across different geographies, plus a promoter pledge that management said should fall significantly within 12-15 months.
Sanofi closing timing depends on approvals in more than 50 countries, with long-stop June 2027. MBJ closing around end-August 2026 still needs final approvals.
ADCs have no CDMO project yet; MBJ revenue by vertical is undisclosed.
Sanofi margin uplift depends on integrating GTBL's own API; management said margins would return to current levels after stabilisation.
Customer concentration and the Optimus Drugs dispute; the settlement terms were not disclosed.
506879|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and strategic on the long-term CDMO vision, but evasive on specifics: MBJ and Sanofi revenue, debt quantum, Optimus dispute details and promoter pledge data were withheld or left vague. Management also sounded defensive about the three-year gap in calls and the earlier API delays.
key_quotes: from a fermentation perspective, it's 0 or 100. So basically, we will be running capacity at full scale.
So MicroBiopharm is 100% API CDMO.
We are simply bringing in the synergies in both the places, which can add value, whereby 1 plus 1 is equal to more -- significantly more than 2.

544044|2026-06.headline: India Shelter Q1 FY27: PAT up 23% YoY to INR 143 crore and ROE 17.5%, but Stage 3 rose to 1.5% and reported AUM growth slowed to 24%.
544044|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR 143 crore (23% YoY, 4% QoQ) with ROE of 17.5% and net worth of INR 3,353 crore. Gross AUM reached INR 11,284 crore, up 24% YoY, after a one-time switch to recognising disbursements on cheque realisation rather than handover, which cut reported disbursements to INR 641 crore. Stage 3 rose to 1.5% (up 30 bps) on seasonal and early-bucket delinquency, and management guided Stage 3 to stabilise in Q2 and recover from Q3. Management reiterated FY27 guidance for 25-30% AUM growth, 40-50 bps credit cost, more than 6% spreads and 40-45 branch additions, though analysts questioned the credit trend and the disbursement ask rate.

financial_highlights.change: bank clearance ~INR 1,040 crore, ~18% YoY on like-for-like basis
stable QoQ; marginal cost of funds 7.9%

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: About 57% of AUM and about 57% of disbursements; GNPA about 1.48%, versus about 1.52% for LAP.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP)
segments.commentary: About 43% of AUM and disbursements; average LTV about 45%; GNPA about 1.52%.

capex_capacity: Operating in more than 300 branches; plan to add around 40-45 branches in FY27, mostly from Q2 onwards with none added in Q1.
Around 1,000 collection employees across 300+ branches; total headcount about 4,700-4,800, with about 160 added in Q1 across collections and head office (AI and tech).
Liquidity above INR 800 crore and undrawn sanctions above INR 1,500 crore; ALM positive across all buckets.
demand_pricing: July 2026 disbursement was about INR 400 crore on the cheque-realisation basis, which management said was above the March figure.
Management expects disbursement growth above 20% for FY27 and says Q2 could reach about INR 1,200 crore; analysts noted last year's disbursement growth was about 11-12%.

Incremental disbursement yield about 14.9%, up 20-30 bps versus Q4 as the company passes on higher borrowing costs; bankers are asking 20-25 bps more, with the overall cost-of-funds impact expected to be limited to about 10 bps, likely in H2.

Borrowing mix: over 30 counterparties; NHB share 15% (up 230 bps YoY); INR 172 crore drawn from NHB in June at 7.3%; average tenure above 8 years; about 20% fixed, about 33% repo/T-bill linked, rest MCLR/PLR-linked.
Loan book: about 15% variable, 35% semi-variable and 50% fixed rate; fixed rate carries about a 50 bps premium over variable.
guidance_outlook: AUM growth of 25-30% for FY27, reiterated despite Q1 AUM growth of 24%; management expects catch-up over the remaining nine months.
Credit cost of about 40-50 bps for FY27; management aims for about 50 bps in Q1 and Q2.
Spreads to be maintained above 6% in the medium term; incremental spreads are higher than portfolio spreads.
Branch additions of about 40-45 in FY27.
Stage 3 expected to stay around the Q1 level (about 1.5%) in Q2 and fall from Q3 as SARFAESI actions take effect; 30+ DPD expected to decline from Q2.
Cheque-realisation accounting change is one-time; management expects normalisation over 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% AUM growth guidance still achievable given the cheque-realisation disbursement change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the change is one-time and disbursement growth above 20% is still expected, supported by July's INR 400 crore; AUM growth of 25-30% is retained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 3 and 30+ DPD rise, and is it company-specific?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonality and stress in the self-employed, sub-INR 7 lakh ticket cohort (above 2% Stage 3 versus 1.4-1.45% three years ago), and to the cohort's 16%+ yields. It said there was nothing internal, and that April collections were 96.2-96.4% and June slightly above 97%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company hold credit cost at 50 bps with Stage 2+3 at multi-year highs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of holding 50 bps, citing low LGD on this cohort and management overlays. Stage 3 is expected to stay flat in Q2, with recovery from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no branch addition in Q1 and why is disbursement growth only about 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said branch openings are phased by strategy, with most of FY27's 40-45 coming from Q2. It said peers' Q1 numbers were on a different base and that the full-year target is what matters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is incremental yield up 30 bps while incremental cost of funds is stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bankers are asking 20-25 bps higher cost of funds, with the overall impact limited to about 10 bps, so the company is passing on some cost to new disbursements. Incremental yield is 14.9%.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the gap in the Q1 FY26 AUM base?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap is about INR 450 crore of co-lending book, which was not previously included in AUM. From March 2026 it is included, so the correct YoY AUM growth is 24%.

risks_watch: Stage 3 at 1.5% and 30+ DPD trend; management expects Stage 3 to stay flat in Q2, but analysts noted that Stage 2+3 is at a four-year high.
Credit cost guidance of 40-50 bps versus ECL of INR 93 crore, which is above the regulatory threshold of INR 52 crore, and analysts questioned whether buffers will be added.
Disbursement ramp: Q1 growth was about 18% on a like-for-like basis; the 20%+ and 25-30% AUM targets rely on Q2 disbursements of about INR 1,200 crore.
Cost of funds pressure, with bankers seeking 20-25 bps higher rates and an expected impact of about 10 bps in H2.
Seasonal rainy-season effects and the reset of semi-variable home loans starting in Q4 FY27.

543482|2026-06.headline: Eureka Forbes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15.3% YoY to INR701 crore, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell 46 bps to 10.5% on a 131 bps gross margin drop.
543482|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 15.3% YoY to INR701 crore, led by water purifiers (high-teens growth on double-digit volume growth) with broad-based strength across retail, direct and e-commerce. Adjusted EBITDA rose 10.5% to INR74 crore, but margin slipped 46 bps to 10.5% as gross margin fell 131 bps to 58.4% and A&SP spend was front-loaded. Service revenue growth was similar to Q4 FY26, while AMC bookings softened after price increases of roughly 3% to 12%. Management guided to a clear step-up in full-year growth and to FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26.

financial_highlights.change: +44% YoY; includes one-time INR19.5 crore gratuity reversal gain

segments.name: Water purifiers
segments.commentary: Grew high-teens on double-digit volume growth, with market share gains driven by economy range, stainless steel range, and premium Hot/UTC/IoT models. Management says growth was ahead of the category.

segments.name: Product business (overall)
segments.commentary: Grew late teens, broad-based across retail, direct and e-commerce, each with strong double-digit growth.

segments.name: Emerging categories (robotics, softeners, air purifiers)
segments.commentary: Strong growth across all emerging categories; robotics driven by premium mix (fully automatic cleaning station), softeners by volume. Robotics campaign launched with Shraddha Kapoor.

segments.name: Service (AMC and filters)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth similar to Q4 FY26 levels, but AMC bookings growth moderated after price increases; filter portfolio grew well. Filter gross margin is slightly below AMC but still high.

guidance_outlook: Clear step-up in FY27 full-year growth expected, supported by strong Q1 start.
FY27 full-year EBITDA margin aimed to be broadly in line with FY26 (FY26 exited with ~55 bps expansion).
Service revenue growth in Q2 FY27 expected to be similar to Q1; beyond that depends on AMC bookings and filter scale-up.
A&SP spend expected to grow ahead of revenue growth in FY27, focused on in-store presence and consumer finance.
ESOP expense expected at INR25-26 crore for FY27.
FY30 ambition reiterated: 2x revenue vs FY25 and 3x EBITDA; robotics targeted at INR1,000 crore by FY30.
Price increases to be calibrated; no plan for further consumer price hikes while momentum holds.
demand_pricing: Water purifier category penetration about 7%; high perceived cost of ownership cited as key barrier.
Price increases in products taken at start of quarter; peers followed with about a 30-day lag, and price parity now restored.
AMC price increases in the 3% to 12% band (single-year vs multi-year) led to deferred AMC renewals and softer bookings.
Four-year filter-life water purifiers (Glow 4X at ~INR22,000, Ritz Pro 4X at ~INR25,000) launched in e-commerce about 45 days before the call; competitors followed more recently.
Simplified filter range cut from ~65 SKUs to five universal filters; filter awareness campaigns stepped up.
Management says no supply-side help from competitors' disruptions; market share gains attributed to own initiatives and point-of-sale investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why is service growth not picking up despite pricing, and when will it reach double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said service revenue grew in line with Q4 FY26 levels; AMC bookings were deferred by customers after the 3-12% price hike, with an 18-month AMC tenure creating a lag into revenue. Filters are being used to offset.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 15% growth came from pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was mainly volume-led for water and softeners, while robotics growth came from premium mix. Pricing had some impact in water; management did not quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the service liability (deferred revenue) help FY27 service growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it helps FY27 revenue. However, in-year bookings must sustain growth, and the softness in AMC bookings is expected to show more in the later part of the year. Q2 service growth is expected to be similar to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins be maintained in FY27 with A&SP rising faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 margin decline reflects upfronted growth investment. Management cited COGS and opex efficiency workstreams and operating leverage, with the aim to hold FY26 margins; it noted FY26 ended with ~55 bps expansion after a similar Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Could the company reverse price hikes if commodity costs fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said that if costs correct, it would pass benefits to consumers to stay competitive and grow share, rather than retain them.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 2x revenue ambition by FY30 hold for products vs services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects products and emerging categories to grow faster than services, with filters growing ahead of AMC. It reaffirmed 2x revenue vs FY25 (about 17-18% CAGR) and 3x EBITDA by FY30.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from commodity and forex; management says no meaningful input cost relief yet.
AMC bookings softness after price hike may weigh on service revenue in H2 FY27.
A&SP rising ahead of revenue growth; margin hold depends on cost programmes.
Increasing competition from new entrants and 3-4 year filter-life offers from peers.
Ongoing geopolitical crisis and currency volatility.
Q1 PAT growth of 44% is flattered by INR19.5 crore one-time gratuity reversal; underlying PAT grew 6.1%.
543482|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on product growth and market share, but cautious on margins and service bookings. Management repeatedly flagged the year as "extremely unusual" due to commodity, forex and geopolitical pressure, and was evasive on the exact A&SP split and service growth targets.
key_quotes: I'm pleased to share that we delivered a solid start to FY27.
we expect full year EBITDA margins to be broadly in line with last year.
We have, as you're aware, a number of initiatives going on driving our service revenue.

532808|2026-06.headline: Pearl Global Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24.5% YoY to INR1,528 crore, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 10.7% (up 140 bps) and PAT of INR99 crore.
532808|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR1,528 crore grew 24.5% YoY, the highest ever Q1, driven by volume growth (20.8 million pieces vs 17.2 million). Adjusted EBITDA excluding ESOP was INR164 crore (up 44.1%), margin 10.7%, and PAT INR99 crore (up 51.4%). Standalone (India) EBITDA margin fell to 6.6% from 7.3% because of Haryana wage revisions. Management reiterated double-digit full-year EBITDA margin and said FY28 INR6,000 crore revenue target could be reached earlier.

financial_highlights.metric: Dividend received from Pearl Global Hong Kong

segments.name: Bangladesh
segments.commentary: Largest geography at about 45%+ of group volume; business growing with existing and new customers. Capacity expansion of 6-7 million pieces expected operational in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Vietnam
segments.commentary: About 27% of group volume; key for high-value and outerwear products; management evaluating further capacity expansion and land acquisition completed.

500153|2026-09.headline: Ganesh Benzoplast to divest JNPA, Goa and Cochin liquid tank farms plus Daund rail for INR1,154 crore, with INR500 crore due around January 2027.
500153|2026-09.overview: Management, on an investor call held October 7, 2026, outlined the sale of the LST (liquid storage tank) businesses at JNPA, Goa and Cochin, together with the JNPA-linked Daund rail business, for INR1,154 crore plus an exit-linked consideration. Payment is staged: about INR500 crore by January 2027, about INR300 crore by March 2027, and the balance INR354 crore over 12 to 18 months tied to port approvals and tank commissioning. Of the first INR500 crore, about INR190-200 crore goes to tax and bank-limit closure and about INR200 crore to a buyback and special dividend, with INR100 crore for chemical expansion and EPC book growth. Management guided chemical PAT to about INR18 crore in FY26 rising to INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years, and EPC PAT to about INR150 crore by around FY30. Much of the Q&A probed the rationale for exiting the higher-margin LST business and the lack of quarter-wise numbers.

financial_highlights.metric: Divestment consideration (JNPA, Goa, Cochin LST + Daund rail)
financial_highlights.change: plus further consideration linked to investor exit valuation (not quantified)

financial_highlights.metric: Planned shareholder return from first tranche (buyback + special dividend)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR5 crore PAT in FY24 (full year)
management says profit up ~1,000% over last 2 years
management now expects above INR200 crore

segments.name: LST (liquid tank farm) – divested
segments.commentary: JNPA, Goa and Cochin liquid tank farms and JNPA-linked Daund rail are being sold for INR1,154 crore. JNPA expected in books until about Dec 2026/Jan 2027, with Cochin and Goa removed gradually over the next calendar year. Company retains a small stake in a Kandla terminal, described as insignificant; a non-compete applies.

segments.name: Chemical (benzoic acid, sodium benzoate)
segments.commentary: Two plants, each about 1,000 tons/month; utilisation about 70-80%. One plant is being doubled, with completion expected July 2027. REACH certification obtained for UK and EU; orders over 600 tons received, expected to reach about 2,000 tons/year. Management targets chemical PAT of INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years.

segments.name: EPC (tankage, pipeline, petroleum)
segments.commentary: Order book expected to be about INR500-600 crore next year, with EPC revenue of about INR250 crore per annum from FY28 onward per management. Targeted 5% share of a INR70,000 crore 5-year petroleum-related EPC opportunity implies about INR150 crore PAT. EBITDA margin assumption 7-8% on a conservative basis, PAT margin basis not clearly specified.

guidance_outlook: Chemical PAT expected to be INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years (from INR18 crore in FY26); management says chemical profitability to rise 3-4x in 4-5 years.
EPC PAT of about INR150 crore targeted by around 2030, assuming 5% share of INR70,000 crore 5-year petroleum EPC pipeline.
Total PAT target of about INR210 crore in 3-5 years versus about INR70 crore currently; FY28 PAT growth target of 15-20% YoY.
Chemical revenue to rise about 20-25% in the year after capacity commissioning and about 70-80% in the following year, per management.
Debt expected to stay at minimum; company does not expect to need significant bank debt, although bank limits are needed for guarantees.
Further tranche proceeds to be used for expansion or shareholder returns, decided by the board based on capex visibility.
capex_capacity: Chemical capacity doubling at one plant (of two, about 1,000 tons/month each), targeted completion July 2027.
Stage 1 capex across chemical and EPC of not more than about INR150 crore.
New agro and specialty derivative plants planned with technology and licence partners; to be funded later, with back-to-back buyback arrangements with customers under discussion.
Management says no balance capex remains on the JNPA port asset, and that about 43 tanks are under construction at JNPA (per management answer on LST growth capex).
Capex to continue over the next 1-2 years; first stage expected to be complete by FY28.
demand_pricing: REACH certification enabled UK and EU exports; over 600 tons of orders received.
Management says the chemical business profit grew from INR5 crore (FY24) to INR15-16 crore (FY25), INR18 crore (FY26) with turnover broadly flat.
Crude-linked raw material costs: management says it passes through fluctuations to customers but cannot rule out margin impact at high crude prices.
Chemical EBITDA margin cited by analyst at 11-12%; management expects to sustain or improve it without a firm number.
EPC contract wins include KKR (about INR300 crore), GACL/NALCO JV pipeline, ANA Oleo, Allana, Adani MPL and Jindal projects.

544898|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 7.28% YoY to INR 133.66 crore and PAT grew 14% to INR 29.28 crore, while growth depends on GPU capacity going live from Q3.
544898|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 133.66 crore, up 7.28% YoY but down 20.20% QoQ, which management attributed to design services booked in a subsidiary (SPOCHUB) in Q4 FY26. PAT rose about 14% to INR 29.28 crore and EBITDA was INR 559 million at a stated 42% margin. Management said the step-up depends on the Sharon AI GPU deal (8,200 B300 GPUs in Sydney), now expected to bill from Q3 FY27 after a delay from the earlier mid-September target. Management declined to give any forward revenue or profit guidance.

financial_highlights.change: +7.28% YoY; -20.20% QoQ (Q4 FY26 included subsidiary design services)
vs INR 1,257.21 million in Q1 FY26
vs INR 910.39 million in Q1 FY26
vs INR 346.82 million in Q1 FY26
vs INR 89.96 million in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 51% of Q1 FY27 revenue; includes cloud IaaS, GPU IaaS and co-location. Mostly GPUs are leased from partners; no significant owned GPU capacity went live in Q1.

segments.name: Managed Services
segments.commentary: 31.31% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management said FY26 growth (about 157% YoY to about INR 76 crore) was driven by one-time technical design services for the Sharon AI cluster classified here.

segments.name: Software-as-a-Service (SaaS)
segments.commentary: 17.55% of Q1 FY27 revenue; includes Swaraj Cloud and dozens of software products. Management said SaaS was historically the higher-margin segment.

segments.name: SPOCHUB (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Recorded about INR 85 crore revenue and INR 54 crore PAT in FY26 versus near-nil in FY25, from one-time technical design services for the GPU cluster at Sharon AI. Management said this will not recur.

guidance_outlook: Management said it cannot give full-year FY27 or FY28 guidance; numbers will be disclosed quarterly.
Sharon AI GPU capacity (8,200 B300 GPUs, Sydney SYD1 data centre) expected to go live by early November 2026 per the Kunal Bajaj reply, with billing from Q1 FY28 per another reply.
Own GPU target of about 1,500 GPUs to be deployed by January-February 2027 (mid-to-end Q4 FY27).
Management targets PAT margins of 15% to 20% on GPU leasing deals.
Planned FY27 capex of about INR 1,500 crore, with a further INR 1,500 crore stated as additional capex for FY27.
Management expects the seasonality of Q4-heavy revenue to fade over the next 2-3 years as AI factories are delivered.
capex_capacity: Sharon AI deal: 8,200 latest B300 GPUs deployed in the GreenSquare SYD1 data centre in Sydney; lease locked for 7 years; the 'September 16' target slipped about 1.5 months; management now targets early November 2026 go-live.

Own GPU build-out: target about 1,500 GPUs by January-February 2027; India setup funded by IPO proceeds, customer advances and some debt in a 30:30:30 split (management said 'balance of 30-30-30' with the remainder unclear).
Management says it is not signing customers for the new India capacity yet and will buy GPUs at current prices, targeting to lease when prices rise around January.
Capex funding: customer advances of about INR 1,177 crore plus about INR 720 crore from the IPO, plus partial debt (per analyst question, confirmed by management).
Employee count 993; about 100 additions expected from the Sharon deal, with the company aiming to stay under 1,000 through churn and partner staffing.
demand_pricing: International funnel is more than 50,000 GPUs; management said customers are waiting for supply.
Domestic order book about INR 3,000 crore over a 3-year duration (per Anmol Garg question); management said domestic demand is growing at 30% to 40% CAGR.
Target lease pricing of about USD 5 to 6 per GPU per hour, in line with industry; management said pricing of B300 contracts is locked, and H100/A100 customers still pay USD 3.5 per hour.
International customers pay 12 to 18 months of advance, and management says the company prefers them for higher prices and larger down-payments.
Management says GPU supply is constrained, with delivery delays of 4 to 9 months from OEMs.
Sharon AI has reportedly leased to direct customers and now demands 50% advance per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Sharon AI go-live delayed from mid-September, and when will revenue start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the date slipped by about 1.5 months, with billing starting now. It targets early Q3 or mid-Q3, and later said November first week go-live, with billing from Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the quarterly revenue growth (7-8%) inconsistent with a 30-40% order book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality with Q3 and Q4 stronger historically; Q1 growth of about 8% was called appropriate given domestic deliverables. Growth is expected QoQ from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GPU pricing locked for the Sharon deal and can its rate be fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the Sharon GPU purchase cost and the customer revenue are both locked at pre-decided rates, with a 7-year contract.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1,500 GPUs be deployed by Q4 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the target as correct, with deployment by January-February 2027 (mid-to-end Q4).

qa_highlights.question: Are there capex subsidies (PLI) or any client concentration risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not eligible for capex subsidies such as PLI. On concentration, management said advance-funded contracts reduce risk, and it did not name the clients or confirm any China exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be any deal-related guidance for FY27 or FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management declined to provide forward-looking revenue or profit figures.

543390|2026-06.headline: PB Fintech Q1 FY27: consolidated operating revenue up 40% to ₹1,888 Cr and PAT up 92% to ₹163 Cr, with insurance premium up 41% to ₹8,372 Cr.
543390|2026-06.overview: Management reported broad-based growth in Q1 FY27, with insurance premium up 41% YoY to ₹8,372 Cr and new health and term premium up 53%. Consolidated operating revenue grew 40% to ₹1,888 Cr, core insurance revenue rose 46% and core credit revenue rose 25%, while PAT margin improved from 6% to 9%. Management repeatedly stated that growth, not margin expansion, remains the priority, with acquisition spend being increased. Management also said Q1 is seasonally weak and flagged that the GST-related health and term demand tailwind is already fading.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating expenses excluding contribution, % of revenue

segments.name: Insurance (Policybazaar)
segments.commentary: Core new insurance premium incl. savings grew 39%, excluding savings 48%. New health grew 59% and new health and term grew 53%. Management says 82% of business is from customers new to insurance.

segments.name: Credit (Paisabazaar)
segments.commentary: Core revenue grew 25% and core disbursals 33%, with total disbursals at ₹4,366 Cr. Operating EBITDA broke even in Q1 and contribution margin was 41%; management expects FY27 EBITDA about half of the ~₹100 Cr previously discussed.

segments.name: PB Partners (POSP)
segments.commentary: Active partners rose 55% YoY to 1.13 lakh and 78% of GWP comes from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Top 100 partners account for 16% of premium; POSP premium is about ₹1,600 Cr and corporate about ₹500 Cr.

segments.name: UAE / Dubai
segments.commentary: UAE insurance premium grew 31% YoY, about ₹500 Cr in the quarter, mainly health and life.

segments.name: PB Health
segments.commentary: Quarterly loss about ₹7 Cr. Second hospital got billing approval; internal target is ~₹500 Cr annual run rate and break-even by March 2027.

segments.name: PB Connect
segments.commentary: Revenue about ₹12 Cr from retail. Wholesale consolidation business was discontinued, so the line is down 73% YoY and was zero from wholesale in Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects renewal growth to exceed fresh growth over the next 12 months, with renewal growth upwards of 50% for some time.
Management says long-term target of about 30% growth remains; margin efficiency is deferred in favour of growth, with efficiency expected later.
Management says the GST-driven insurance demand tailwind is fading in Q1 and it may be lucky if it persists in Q2.
PB Health targets ~₹500 Cr annual run rate and break-even by March 2027.
Paisabazaar FY27 EBITDA expected at roughly half of the previously discussed ~₹100 Cr; Q1 at break-even.
Several launches planned for end-August 2026, including bonds via PB Money entity and daily SIP platform on Paisabazaar.
capex_capacity: Hiring: about 5,000 gross hires in Q1 FY27 despite seasonal weakness.
Call-centre talk time for health transactions reduced from about 2 hours at IPO to 35-40 minutes now.
AI touches 30-40% of about 10 crore monthly customer interactions; 20-30% of service interactions are automated.
Second PB Health hospital received billing approval; more hospitals in pipeline.
demand_pricing: Health and term growth is attributed to demand creation spend, product features like monthly mode (over 30% of health business) and a 3-month maternity waiting period, and claims service (CSAT above 90%, ~70,000 health claims supported in the quarter).
Tier 2 and Tier 3 account for 65-70% of direct online business and are growing faster than metros; South has grown faster than North and West over three years.
Motor plus two-wheeler direct grew over 30%; motor POSP grew close to 50%. Retail direct TP is about 25% of premium value; POSP motor is about half TP.
Waiver of Premium (WOP) share in domestic savings has crossed 60% in some centres in July; savings fresh business grew over 20%.
Management views the Supreme Court TP-extension judgement as a potential upside via enforcement, but says it is too early to quantify.
Management said Q3 FY26 was an above-trend quarter, making the H2 base high, and said the goal is above-market growth.

qa_highlights.question: Where is health and term growth coming from (Tier 2/3 vs urban) and is the user base different from peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed outgrowth to demand investment, relevant tailored products, and claims service; 82% of business is from customers without prior insurance, and port-in is a small share.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins evolve as renewals grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said renewal growth will beat fresh growth for ~12 months but will keep reinvesting in acquisition for lifetime value; margin improvement is secondary to fresh growth.

qa_highlights.question: Regulatory commission changes and the worst-case manufacturer scenario?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not anticipate changes, pointed to legal effort requirements on brokers, and said insurance requires heavy enquiry and conversion spend, with platform cost the smallest part.

qa_highlights.question: Paisabazaar EBITDA and Tier 2/3 mix in online business?
qa_highlights.answer: Paisabazaar broke even on an operating basis in Q1 and is expected to be about half of the earlier ~₹100 Cr full-year number. Tier 2 and Tier 3 are 65-70% of direct business.

qa_highlights.question: Dark patterns and H2 growth base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denies deception in phone-number collection and said Q3 FY26 was above trend; aims to keep above-market growth. On AI, management said productivity gains may mean hiring less for the same business, while growth remains the goal.

qa_highlights.question: Expense ratio decline and call-centre cost classification?
qa_highlights.answer: Expenses excluding contribution fell to 58% of revenue from 61%; management said costs grew about 35% against 40% revenue growth and that efficiency drives have not started. All call-centre employee costs sit in employee benefit expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Savings business softness and reputation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says fresh savings grew over 20% and persistency is about 100 bps below its best; it said ULIPs are sold through verification calls and are low-cost.

524494|2026-06.headline: Ipca Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 21% to INR2,788 crores and EBITDA margin reached 22.88%; FY27 growth guidance raised to 14-16%.
524494|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 21% YoY to INR2,788 crores, with consolidated EBITDA of INR638 crores (22.88% margin) versus INR425 crores (18.39%) a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA rose about 34% to INR557 crores. Management raised FY27 guidance: revenue growth to 14-16% (from 12-13%) and consolidated EBITDA margin to around 23% (from around 22%). Exports (+34%), domestic formulations (+13%) and institutional generics (+107%, helped by about INR40 crores of shipments slipping from March to April) drove the quarter. Management said margin gains came mainly from lower personnel and manufacturing costs as a share of sales, not material savings.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR425 crores, 18.39% in Q1 FY26 (+4.49 pp)

financial_highlights.value: about INR193 crores; zero short-term borrowings
financial_highlights.change: Dollar loans of about USD50 million fully repaid

segments.name: India formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR1,082 crores, +13%; IQVIA-tracked growth about 11.7%, chronic +17.2% and acute +8.9%. Market share about 2.08%, rank about 16. Antimalarials fell about 24% and are now about 1% of business.

segments.name: Exports / ROW branded
segments.commentary: Export business about INR603 crores (+34%). Promotional branded ROW about INR143 crores (+16%from INR124 crores).

segments.name: Europe / UK generics
segments.commentary: European business up about 70%, from INR33 crores to INR137 crores, the main growth driver. US shipments up about 8%; Canada saw a minor decline.

segments.name: Unichem (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: US business up about 27%, with Ipca-portfolio sales to Unichem up about 37% and Unichem's own portfolio up about 9%. Brazil up about 52%. Unichem API rose from about INR33-34 crores to about INR58 crores.

segments.name: Lyka Labs (associate)
segments.commentary: Revenue flat and EBITDA reported negative. Management cited animal health, critical care and IVF as growth areas, with some divisions still below breakeven.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth raised to 14-16% from 12-13%.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin raised to around 23% from around 22%.
Institutional business to grow in single digits, with annual sales of about INR260-300 crores.
Unichem guidance (10% portfolio growth, 13% EBITDA margin) not revised yet; to be reviewed after more quarters.
FY28 guidance to be given with Q4 results.
Medium term: Ipca standalone margin could reach about 30% and consolidated margin about 25-26% in 2-3 years.
Long-run US growth of about 15-17% seen as possible.
FY27 capex of about INR700-800 crores; about INR100 crores extra for biotech pilot facilities and R&D.
capex_capacity: Pithampur: capacity additions for controlled-release and extended-release formulations under way.
API: new plants at Dewas and Wardha (intermediates) as Ratlam runs out of capacity; continuous-process conversions of existing intermediates.
Biotech: about 7 candidates in pipeline and capacity for 3-4 products a year; 2 products at engineering-batch stage, with results in line with expectations.
Sales force of about 7,000 medical reps; about 200 more to be added mid-year for new divisions.
demand_pricing: Domestic growth split: volume about 5%, price about 4.5-5%, new launches about 2%.
Management said there are no price renegotiations downward; prices are rising because costs are rising.

Freight costs rose sharply: South America containers from about USD3,000 to USD9,000-10,000; US from about 7,000-7,500 to 12,500-13,000; Europe from 3,000 to about 5,500. Container availability is also constrained.
Rupee depreciation (dollar up about 11% YoY) added about 5 pp to the 21% revenue growth; about 25% of that benefit was offset by higher material cost.
Materials cost moved up about 21%, in line with sales; management said material cost to sales would fall slightly relative to sales growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did acute underperform, and what is the India outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed underperformance, citing IPM growth of 4.5% vs Ipca's 8.9% acute growth. Antimalarials fell about 24%. Pain management grew about 13%, CV and diabetes about 17%, CNS about 19%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 12-13% guidance hold, and what is the institutional outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance was raised to 14-16%. Institutional growth is expected to be single digit, since the Q1 spike was largely about INR40 crores of delayed shipments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the US launch plans, and can growth reach 20-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3-4 Ipca launches and 7-8 combined Ipca and Unichem launches a year. Mid-teens growth (15-17%) is possible; source-change approvals are progressing.

qa_highlights.question: Will material cost pressure hit margins in the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: No margin pressure expected; material cost should fall slightly relative to sales. Q1 margin gains came mainly from personnel and manufacturing cost ratios.

qa_highlights.question: Is rupee depreciation or price renegotiation affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices are rising, not being renegotiated down. FX adds to revenue and is partly offset by dollar-linked costs such as freight, testing, salaries and non-trading offices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and interest position?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term debt about INR193 crores with a INR70 crore term loan at year-end, repaid next year. No short-term borrowings. Interest cost to fall further.

qa_highlights.question: Where will margins settle over 2-3 years, and what are the biotech plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated margin about 25-26% in 2-3 years, with Ipca standalone up to about 30%. About 7 biosimilar candidates, mostly off-patent. Clinical revenue expected in FY29-30.

risks_watch: Freight and container availability: rates up about 3x and still rising in July-August; South America is hardest hit.
Malaria decline (about 24%) and institutional shipment timing, which can swing quarterly growth.
Unichem margin and guidance are not yet revised; Europe approvals take about 1.5 years after filing.
Biotech and biosimilar spending (about INR100 crores this year) could weigh on EBITDA before revenue arrives in FY29-30.
FY28 guidance is pending until Q4; rupee moves affect both revenue and dollar-linked costs.

500128|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 DI pipe volumes fell 27% YoY to 1.20 lakh tons; consolidated EBITDA Rs 139 crore at 9.5% margin, guided to 12-13% by Q3-Q4 FY27.
500128|2026-06.overview:
Standalone and consolidated volumes fell sharply on weak domestic DI pipe demand, with export volumes also hit by Middle East tensions. Management reported consolidated EBITDA of Rs 139 crore (9.5% margin) and PAT of Rs 48.4 crore, while standalone PAT was only Rs 5.9 crore. Management pointed to JJM 2.0 sanctions and irrigation/river-linking pipelines for an H2 FY27 recovery, cut FY27 DI volume expectations to about 5.75 lakh tons, and announced diversification into industrial paints, valves and railway rubber components. Consolidated net debt was Rs 876 crore at 30 June 2026, down about Rs 1,100 crore in FY26.</overview>
