segments.name: DI pipes and CI pipes (standalone core)
segments.commentary: Q1 volume 1.20 lakh tons, down 27% YoY; FY27 volume now guided at about 5.75 lakh tons versus earlier 6.5-7.0 lakh tons. Order book about 3 lakh tons (about five months), roughly 50% from JJM.

segments.name: T.I.S. Service S.p.A. (Italy, acquired)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about EUR 10 million with EBITDA margin about 13-14%. FY27 exit target EUR 42-45 million revenue, 14-15% EBITDA margin, about 8% PAT margin.

segments.name: Valves
segments.commentary: Valve revenue about Rs 400 crore; Q1 growth stated at 18% on last year's Q1. Target to double in four years; Indian valve facility to start by end of FY27. Exports from Italy plant to shift partly to India.

segments.name: Industrial paints and protective coatings (new)
segments.commentary: Initial investment about Rs 100 crore for 17,000 kilolitres capacity via brownfield expansion in West Bengal; long-term target Rs 800-1,000 crore revenue and Rs 250-300 crore capex over 4-5 years. Commercial production expected from Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Railway rubber components (gasket plant, Andhra Pradesh)
segments.commentary: Board approved entry today; railway registration expected in 4-6 months; some additional equipment under installation, expected in about three months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 DI pipe and CI pipe volume about 5.75 lakh tons (management said close to last year's level), with better revenue and margin per ton.
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected at 12-13% in Q3 and Q4 FY27; Q2 FY27 expected to be at least similar to Q1 levels.
Export share expected at 22-25% of total volumes by end FY27.
Growth expected mainly in H2 FY27 as JJM 2.0 disbursements pick up; management said the Rs 70,000 crore JJM outlay may drive a significant uplift in Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28.
FY30-FY31 aspiration of consolidated revenue Rs 7,000-8,000 crore at 13-13.5% EBITDA margin.
Dependence on DI pipes to fall from about 85% to about 55% in four to five years.
capex_capacity: Industrial paints: about Rs 100 crore initial investment for 17,000 kilolitres in West Bengal; phased capex Rs 250-300 crore over four to five years.
Valve plant in India to commence operations by end of FY27, first phase in West Bengal; Asian subcontinent expected to contribute 40-45% of valve business in three to four years.
Ferro alloy: second plant planned adjacent to existing unit at brownfield site; capacity increase in ferroalloy business under consideration.
Management said about Rs 200 crore to be spent in West Bengal over the next year; greenfield Odisha site put on hold; about Rs 700 crore of capital available for investment including acquisitions.
Term debt about Rs 340 crore, scheduled to fall to about Rs 230 crore.
demand_pricing: Central JJM allocation Rs 67,670 crore for FY27; about Rs 10,344 crore sanctioned to states year to date versus Rs 1,560 crore released under JJM in the previous year. Management said about Rs 6,000 crore released so far.
Q1 FY27 production about 1.0-1.1 lakh tons versus about 1.8 lakh tons in Q1 FY26, per management.
Management expects about 12-13% of JJM outlay to come to Company (stated for DI industry share), and 5-7% of irrigation project volumes to convert into DI pipes.
Saudi Arabia accounts for about 2-3% of sales; management expects 1-1.5% to be lost, to be diverted to other GCC and African markets.
Export mix: about 60-70% Western markets (Europe, UK), remaining 40% Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia.
Management called current DI realisation levels rock bottom and the worst DI year in India since 1994.
States active under JJM 2.0: Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Tamil Nadu; UP and Rajasthan expected to pick up.

507552|2026-06.headline: Foods & Inns Q1 FY27: export dispatches slowed by vessel shortage and freight spikes, though frozen segment grew ~20% and no order cancellations were reported.
507552|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 mango production was good in quality and price, but export dispatches slowed due to vessel non-availability and sharply higher ocean freight, with customers delaying call-offs rather than cancelling. Exports are 35-40% of sales and domestic about 55%; management expects domestic demand, aided by an El Nino-driven juice and drinks season, to offset export softness. Frozen food is the growth engine: about USD3 million in Q1 (up ~20%) and USD12 million last year, with a target of USD30-plus million in three years. Realisations fell ~18.5% YoY in the quarter, and management flagged working-capital blockage from delayed shipments, with a CFO resignation pending replacement.

financial_highlights.metric: Frozen food segment revenue (last full year)
financial_highlights.change: Frozen grew ~30% CAGR over last 2 years (stated)

financial_highlights.value: Down 18.5% YoY (as cited by analyst, not disputed)
Growth of 14.7% YoY (as cited by analyst)

segments.name: Frozen food (pulp, vegetables, snacks)
segments.commentary: About USD3 million in Q1 with ~20% growth; ~USD12 million last year. Target USD30-plus million in 3 years. Absorbing higher freight better than other segments; capacity expansion in process.

segments.name: Pectin
segments.commentary: Commercial production started; audits ongoing. Brand consumer testing underway, with opportunity expected from October/November (H2 FY27).

segments.name: Spices (Kusum) and spray/spice lines
segments.commentary: Kusum showed better Q1 performance; focus on HORECA, with slow retail build-out. Spray line and spice division run 24x365.

segments.name: Vegetables / tomato and guava pulping
segments.commentary: Vegetables have steady demand but depend on raw material cost. Tomato is the largest non-mango pulping utilisation, followed by guava.

segments.name: B2C brands (Kusum, Madhu, Green Top)
segments.commentary: B2C is a new initiative; now on Zepto and BigBasket in some geographies, with Swiggy and Blinkit in talks. Not on Flipkart, Amazon, Myntra as of the call.

guidance_outlook: Management expects lost export volume to be caught up over the remaining nine months, assuming freight normalises within a couple of months.
Domestic volume growth of around 20% is expected on El Nino-driven juice and drinks demand; export volume depends on freight.
Value growth in Q1 may be flat or negative due to lower mango realisations; September 2026 vs September 2025 realisations expected at +/-10%.
Mango realisations may dip slightly this year, with recovery possibly in the latter part of FY27 and H1 FY28.
Frozen food: 20%-plus growth expected this year; USD30-plus million in 3 years.
capex_capacity: Company is expanding frozen food capacity to meet India and export demand; no capex amount or commissioning date given.
Frozen pulp: trial runs completed for West Asia opening; order booking described as very encouraging.
Pectin: production capacity ready; sampling and consumer testing are the gating items.
Export logistics: air freight is about 30x ocean cost, so not viable; routing shifted between Chennai and Mumbai ports and from South factory to Mumbai.
demand_pricing: Order book described as encouraging; Maaza (Coca-Cola) order higher than last year. No order cancellations, but delayed call-offs.
Shipping lines restricting capacity; clients paying 2-3x freight, with mgmt expecting softening.
Mango raw material prices are down sharply: one category was ~INR25/kg in 2024 vs ~INR8 today (as stated by management).
Export shipments of about 1,800 (unit as stated) finished goods overdue; clearance timeline 45-50 days, not in company control.
Frozen food demand in US, UK and Canada remains strong; company says frozen is the only segment absorbing high freight.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of loss for perishable products because of shipping delays, and how should the next nine months be guided?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said finished goods are processed foods with a 2-year shelf life in drums or cans, so no loss risk; delays are expected but no cancellations. It expects domestic demand to offset export softness and sees pent-up export demand later.

qa_highlights.question: How big is frozen food and what is the scale target?
qa_highlights.answer: Frozen was ~USD12 million last year and ~USD3 million in Q1 with 20%-plus growth expected. The target is USD30-plus million in 3 years, across frozen pulp, vegetables and snacks.

qa_highlights.question: Overdue export shipments: what is the clearance timeline and working-capital impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Clearance is slow; management estimated 45-50 days but would not commit. Working capital is blocked, adding interest cost. Air freight is about 30x ocean and ruled out.

qa_highlights.question: Pectin growth and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial production started and audits are underway. Brand consumer testing is needed before procurement orders, with opportunity expected from October/November.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 20% volume guidance be met, and is value growth possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic volume growth of ~20% is seen as achievable; export depends on freight. Value growth may not come in Q1 given lower realisations; the company expects +/-10% from September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why is top line stagnant, and will promoter holding rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Top line fell because mango raw material prices dropped (cost-plus model). Promoter says holding is just over 25%, plans to look at market purchases or a preferential issue to raise stake and reduce debt, with no decision yet.

risks_watch: Freight normalisation timing: export dispatch recovery depends on it; management hopes for improvement within a couple of months.
Working capital is blocked by delayed export shipments, adding interest cost; watch overdue shipment clearance.
Realisation decline: mango realisations are down, with value growth at risk in Q1 and possibly until H1 FY28.
CFO position vacant after Anand Krishnan's resignation (last day 11 August 2026); replacement to be announced.
Pectin commercialisation depends on customer consumer testing, with no firm timeline beyond H2 FY27.
507552|2026-06.management_tone: ["Confident and bullish on frozen food, domestic demand and the El Nino-driven season. Cautious and non-committal on export timing, freight, and the overdue shipment clearance timeline."]
key_quotes: So we are expecting that though there may be some challenges in the export segment, but domestic segment may compensate that for us.
As of today, on the domestic market, yes. But export market, it depends on how the situation moves in international market on the freight.

500067|2026-06.headline: Blue Star Q1 FY27 consolidated PBT before exceptionals fell 23.7% to Rs125.6 Crore on 13.3% revenue growth, as Segment II EBIT margin dropped to 2.9%.
500067|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 13.3% to Rs3,378 Crore, but PBT before exceptional items fell 23.7% to Rs125.6 Crore as commodity costs, rupee depreciation, a late summer and channel inventory squeezed margins. Segment II (Unitary Products) margin fell to 2.9% from 5.8%, as the company chose to defend room AC market share through consumer finance and trade schemes while only partly passing on cost increases. Management guided Segment II FY27 EBIT margin to over 6.5% and called the data-center MEP order book (Rs7,764 Crore total carry-forward order book) the key positive. Net cash rose to Rs900 Crore from Rs371 Crore a year earlier, driven by working capital release.

financial_highlights.change: +13.5% YoY; vs Rs6,923 Crore on 31 Mar 2026

segments.name: Segment I - Electro-Mechanical Projects & Commercial AC
segments.commentary: Revenue +15.1% to Rs1,625 Crore with margin of 6.8% (down ~112 bps YoY), hit by commodity and FX costs. Order inflow Rs2,435 Crore (+24%), driven by data centres; commercial office, factory and infrastructure orders were sluggish.

segments.name: Segment II - Unitary Products (RAC, Commercial Refrigeration)
segments.commentary: Revenue +12.8% to Rs1,689.3 Crore, margin 2.9% vs 5.8%. Management says Jan-Jun 2026 margin was ~7% when discretionary timing is normalised. Commercial refrigeration degrew ~15%, mainly deep freezers from ice-cream OEMs.

segments.name: Segment III - Professional Electronics & Industrial Systems
segments.commentary: Revenue -9.7% to Rs63.6 Crore, mainly from continued MedTech weakness; segment margin rose to 15.1% from 10.8%.

guidance_outlook: Segment II FY27 EBIT margin guided at over 6.5%; management says it is 'certain' of 6.5% but its aspiration is 7-7.5%, which it does not yet have a view on.
Segment I FY27 margin outlook unchanged at 6.5% to 7%.
Management expects only marginal improvement in Q2 FY27, better Q3 and a 'defining' Q4 once product portfolio rejig is complete; revival expected from late August/September with festive season.

Data-centre MEP: FY27 order inflow guided at ~Rs3,000 Crore and revenue ~Rs1,350-1,400 Crore; FY28 order inflow ~Rs4,500 Crore and revenue ~Rs2,100 Crore; data centre MEP revenue ~Rs4,000 Crore by FY29 (~20% of revenue).
Commercial AC revenue growth of ~10% seen as achievable; 15% not predictable.
Growth-related spend (capex, R&D, digital) of Rs300-350 Crore in FY27 if plan holds; Q1 capex about Rs60-70 Crore.
Export target of additional USD100 million per annum from FY28 over FY26 base; FY26 exports about USD80-85 million.
Management said it remains cautious on FY27 overall.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about Rs60-70 Crore; full-year growth-related spend (capex, R&D intangibles, digital) guided at Rs300-350 Crore.
Data-centre MEP capacity constrained by manpower; company is investing in hiring and specialised professionals and modernising execution, with some infra/building resources diverted to data centres.

Product portfolio rejig under way: cutting some models, outsourcing some portfolio, alternate component sourcing, and redesigns at Sri City and Himachal plants; an alternate/product launch previously planned for six months later is being expedited.
International: product approvals in place with a few customers under CDM route (air-to-air and air-to-water heat pumps); trial orders completed two seasons; scaling awaits US tariff resolution.
Management said manufacturing capacity for RAC industry is about double the market size.
demand_pricing: Management estimates Q1 RAC industry volume grew ~21% and Blue Star ~18% on primary sales; revenue industry ~25% vs Blue Star ~21%. These are management estimates, not audited data.
Tertiary (GFK) RAC market share: lost ~50 bps in April, gained ~10 bps in May and ~50 bps in June; Q1 net loss ~30 bps; Blue Star primary share lost ~65 bps. Year-end share ~14.25%.
Price pass-through: company sought ~13% (cost increase), realised ~5% (3-5% by model); further ~8% needed per management in May.
Trade channel inventory not normalised but 'not alarming'; normal stock estimated at ~60 days overall or ~45 days for trade alone. Energy label change led the trade to over-stock old-label products.
Commercial refrigeration demand muted (deep freezers, ice-cream OEMs, cold rooms, QSR); management says market share held.

500336|2026-06.headline: Surya Roshni Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to INR2,046 crore and PAT 77% to INR60 crore, but steel EBITDA/ton of INR4,006 sits well below the FY27 INR4,600-4,700 guidance.
500336|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR2,046 crore (up 28% YoY), EBITDA of INR120 crore (up 46%) and PAT of INR60 crore (up 77%) were driven mainly by Steel Pipes & Strips, where volume hit a record Q1 of 2.28 lakh tons. Management attributed the EBITDA/ton shortfall to ocean freight (about INR800/ton on total volume) and coating, gas and ORM cost increases (about INR200/ton), and expects recovery as new orders are booked at higher freight rates. Lighting & Consumer Durables grew 15% to INR456 crore with margin up to 7.9%. The company remains debt-free with net cash of about INR155 crore; buyback and demerger decisions were deferred with no firm timeline.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA +17% YoY (from INR31 crore); PBT +12% YoY (from INR21 crore)

financial_highlights.value: About INR155 crore (B.B. Singal cited INR154 crore) as of 30 June 2026

segments.name: Steel Pipes & Strips
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,590 crore (+32% YoY) on record Q1 volume of 2.28 lakh tons (+21% YoY); section, ERW API, spiral, cold rolling and GP pipes led, galvanized soft on delayed government fund releases. Capacity utilisation about 82%, value-added products 47% of volume, exports 20% of segment volume.

segments.name: Lighting & Consumer Durables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR456 crore (+15% YoY), best-ever Q1, led by LED bulbs, battens and downlighters; EBITDA INR36 crore with margin 7.9%, passing through about 7% input cost increase. Professional lighting order book about INR150 crore.

segments.name: Wire & Cables
segments.commentary: Management said Q1 sales nearly matched FY26 full-year volume; FY26 revenue target INR250 crore, against a 3-year INR500 crore goal. Electrician loyalty program enrolments reached 36,000.

guidance_outlook: FY27 steel volume about 11 lakh tons (+20-22% volume growth); quarterly path of about 2.6-2.65 lakh tons in Q2, 2.8-2.9 lakh in Q3 and about 3.2 lakh in Q4.
FY27 steel EBITDA/ton guidance of INR4,600-4,700 reiterated; management expects about INR4,400-4,500 in Q2 and INR4,600-4,700 full year, implying above INR5,000 in H2 per Q1 analyst math.
Company FY27 EBITDA guided at INR670-680 crore on revenue of INR9,400-9,500 crore; Q2 EBITDA about INR150 crore and H2 about INR400 crore.
Lighting FY27: revenue about INR2,200 crore (vs INR1,809 crore FY26), value growth 19-22%, volume growth about 25%, EBITDA about INR200 crore.

Steel value growth 30%+ expected for FY27; US market contribution 10-11% of volume (about 1.2-1.25 lakh tons in FY27), total exports about 3 lakh tons; export share of steel to rise from about 20% to 25%.
Ocean freight: new orders booked at higher rates, with July impact described as very low and no freight impact expected in the next two months; break-bulk shipping arranged for US volumes.
Full-year API/spiral EBITDA/ton expected to recover from Q1 INR3,420 to about INR5,000 (vs INR5,500-5,700 in FY26).
Per-ton cost reduction target of about INR1,100 and manpower cost reduction of about 20% over the next year; 15-18% CAGR targeted for the next five years.
capex_capacity: Capacity 14 lakh tons currently; target 16 lakh tons by end-FY27 with three DFT mills commissioning between August and December 2026 at Gujarat, Malanpur and Bahadurgarh; about 2 million tons by FY28-29.
Adding 2-3 lakh tons of capacity every year; capex about INR100 crore for the 14-to-16 lakh ton expansion, funded from internal accruals.

Hindupur (South) greenfield-style expansion on 10 additional acres: first mill about January 2027, total 4-mill plant adding about 15,000 tons initially, about INR60 crore investment, roughly 3 lakh tons overall.
Greenfield projects under evaluation with clarity promised by next board meeting; expansions focus on DFT and section pipes.
demand_pricing: Steel order book INR800 crore (export API orders include 78,000 tons for the US) vs INR1,000 crore at end-March; management said about 75-80% of business is distribution-type and fixed.
Ocean freight rose sharply; Q1 exports carried about INR3,800/ton higher freight, costing about INR800/ton of blended EBITDA. Management says new orders are priced at the higher freight.

US market opened for ERW API pipes, with realisation EBITDA/ton of about INR7,200 in Q1; Middle East orders fell (roughly one-third of usual 15,000-20,000 tons per quarter now able to ship), and API orders down about 50%.
Steel prices rose INR3,000-4,000/ton in April, then fell in May-June, leaving the quarter roughly neutral on inventory; steel now seen stable within INR1,000/ton.
Q1 API/spiral EBITDA/ton of INR3,420 cited with coating material as a significant drag; water pipe faces higher competition.
Lighting: about 80% of production in-house, about 20% outsourced, with the outsourced share largely made exclusively for Surya.

544517|2026-06.headline: Shankara Buildpro Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to Rs 1,890 crore; steel volume grew 10% to 2.5 lakh tons and EBITDA margin was 3.26%.
544517|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 21% YoY to Rs 1,890 crore and PAT rose 12% YoY to Rs 35.8 crore, led by steel volume growth and a recovery in non-steel. Management said April-May were weak due to West Asia-linked energy inflation and steel price volatility, with conditions improving through June and July. EBITDA was Rs 62 crore (3.26% margin), which management said included about Rs 10 crore of inventory erosion (roughly 50 bps) from a price correction in May-June. Management reiterated the 1.2 million-ton steel volume target, 20% steel and 25% non-steel volume growth, and a 3.5% steady-state EBITDA margin, and proposed a 1:5 stock split.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 35.8 crore (also cited as Rs 35.9 crore)

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Volume of 2.5 lakh tons (+10% YoY) and revenue of Rs 1,725 crore (+21% YoY); pipes, tubes, flats and roofing all grew in volume. Management said the 1.2 million-ton FY27 target is intact.

segments.name: Non-steel
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 165 crore (+15% YoY). Fittings and sanitary ware, the largest category, grew 32%; accessories and electricals grew about 40% on a smaller base; tiles were hit hardest in April.

guidance_outlook: FY27 steel volume target of 1.2 million tons, with 20% steel volume growth and 25% non-steel growth reiterated.
Steady-state EBITDA margin target of 3.5%+; management said about 3.8% would have been reached without the Rs 10 crore inventory erosion.
Medium term (FY28 onward): EBITDA margin of around 4%, while maintaining 20% steel and 25% non-steel volume growth.
Target of 2 million tons in around 4 years; the 20% growth path is the baseline, with new territories and stores as upside.
About 5 more fulfilment centres or stores planned in the coming quarters, taking FY27 additions to roughly 8-9 (3 added in Q1).
Proposed 1:5 stock split (face value Rs 10 to Rs 2), pending shareholder and regulatory approvals; total paid-up capital unchanged.
capex_capacity: Three fulfilment centres/stores added in Q1 FY27 (Mangalore, Mumbai, Thrissur), plus 34 customer touchpoints across 45 towns and cities in 10 states.
About 5 more fulfilment centres planned in the coming quarters.
Planned investment in value-added steel infrastructure (cut-to-length, laser cutting) and warehousing.
Cash use priorities: private-label products (with promotion spend), value-added steel investment, and reducing acceptance-based borrowing. Acquisitions are 'on the table' but none named.
demand_pricing: Steel prices spiked in March-April, then corrected sharply in May-June, causing inventory erosion of about Rs 10 crore; prices have stabilised over July and early August.
Management said the Q4 FY26 inventory gain was about Rs 15 crore.
Volume recovered in June (about 1 lakh MT of rebound cited) and management said the momentum continued into July.
Non-steel tile demand was near zero in April (Morbi gas/energy shock) and recovered in May-June; PVC/UPVC roofing uptake is good.
Competitive intensity from well-funded enterprise-focused players has eased in the last couple of quarters; management is de-prioritising TMT and focusing on flats.
Retail accounts for about 50-55% of total volume. Ticket sizes range from Rs 500 to Rs 1.5 crore across 25 verticals, 75 categories and over 100 brands, with over 2 lakh SKUs.

qa_highlights.question: Can 22-23% volume growth be achieved for the rest of FY27 to reach 1.2 MT, given the high H2 base?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukumar Srinivas said June volume growth was very positive and July continued the trend, and he is confident of 1.2 MT barring unforeseen headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: What were the margin impacts from fixed-price contracts and inventory, and what is the steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts carried over from March into April forced supply at high prices, and the May-June price drop eroded about Rs 10 crore (about 50 bps). Ex this, margin would have been about 3.8%; steady state 3.5%+ is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company guiding for 25% non-steel growth when peers are not showing similar optimism?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 32% growth in CP and sanitary ware, a tile recovery from May-June, and PVC/UPVC roofing traction; the CP/sanitary segment is expected to drive most of the growth.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the interest cost, given about Rs 75 crore of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Alex Varghese said about Rs 500 crore of acceptances (LCs opened and discounted, with the company bearing interest) bring total borrowings to about Rs 575 crore; the interest cost mainly comes from acceptances.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% revenue growth achievable at a 3.5% EBITDA margin, and is there margin expansion in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhananjay Mirlay Srinivas said the company is on track for 20% volume growth at 3.5% margin, and medium-term aims for about 4% EBITDA margin with 20% steel and 25% non-steel volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: How long to reach 2 MT, and what new categories are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is about 4 years to 2 MT via new territories, stores and market share gains; new steel infrastructure for cut-to-length and value-added products, and expanding white-label private labels in retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume/price split of the 21% revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukumar Srinivas said price played little part; steel prices were high and then softened, so the effect was largely neutral. He said a detailed split would be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company guiding for a 3.5% margin when adjusted Q1 margin is about 3.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukumar Srinivas said management is taking a cautious path because steel inventory gains and losses are outside its control, and it prefers to be prudent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steel business profitability and outlook for flats?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-steel has an 8-10% EBITDA margin, so steel is trending above 3% overall; diversifying into flats and multiple steel products should help grow EBITDA.

543597|2026-06.headline: Virtuoso Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 85% YoY to INR 376.6 crore, with PAT up about 103% to INR 9 crore; FY27 guidance of 35-40% growth and 9-10% EBITDA margin maintained.
543597|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR 376.6 crore, up about 85% YoY and about 18.7% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at about 9.3%, similar to Q4 FY26. PAT rose about 103% YoY to about INR 9 crore from INR 6.4 crore. Management said raw material (copper, aluminium, imported compressor inputs) and logistics pressure squeezed margins, with pricing expected to stabilise over the next couple of quarters. Commercial refrigeration was slower in Q1 as buyers deferred purchases after price hikes. Management kept FY27 guidance of 35-40% growth and 9-10% EBITDA margin, and said an upward revision depends on Q3.

financial_highlights.change: ~103% YoY vs INR 6.4 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue mix Q1 FY27: deep freezers
financial_highlights.change: Similar to EMS; balance from components

segments.name: Room AC (ODM)
segments.commentary: About 70% of Q1 FY27 revenue; FY27 expected at 55-60% of revenue. Largest AC customer (Voltas) about 40-45% of AC segment, expected 25-35% in FY27; AC capacity going from 1.0 mn to 1.8 mn units over 12-15 months. Margins are under pressure; management expects improvement from FY28.

segments.name: Compressor
segments.commentary: Production began late Dec 2025 and runs at over 50% utilisation; capacity going from 2.8 mn to 6 mn, targeted Dec/Jan. Expected ~15% of FY27 revenue; EBITDA margin about 6-7% currently. Captive use only 2-3% of sales; works with 8-9 customers, with no single customer above 20-23% expected.

segments.name: Commercial refrigeration
segments.commentary: Q1 slower due to price increases and deferred buying; management says Q2-Q3 projections have been pushed out, not cut. Capex INR 20-25 crore this year; capacity 400,000 units, with a potential INR 360 crore revenue at 60% utilisation.

segments.name: EMS
segments.commentary: Capacity going from 4 lakh to 12 lakh cph; first 8 lakh cph phase expected by mid/end September, commercial production by end Q3. About 10% of FY27 revenue; little top-line impact this year, with revenue expected from FY28.

segments.name: Deep freezers
segments.commentary: Capacity going from 1.5 lakh to 2.5 lakh units by mid/end Q3 FY27; second phase to 4 lakh units in FY28.

segments.name: Components and washing machines
segments.commentary: Expected ~5% of FY27 revenue; Chennai and Sanand picking up. Washing machine work is mainly with one anchor customer this year.

guidance_outlook: Maintains FY27 revenue growth guidance of 35-40%; management said an upward revision depends on Q3 performance, with an update at end of Q3.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 9-10% maintained; management said Q1 margin of 9.3% is healthy and margins could move closer to 10% once pricing stabilises.
Net margin guidance of 2-3% (answering a 2.5-3% query), with tax timing noted.
Margin improvement expected mainly in FY28 as raw material pressure eases over 6-12 months.
Long-term ambition of 35-40% revenue CAGR over the next three to five years; peak revenue at current expansion estimated at INR 3,500-4,000 crore within 12 months.
Total FY27 capex INR 80-100 crore at VOEPL; commercial refrigeration capex INR 20-25 crore.
capex_capacity: EMS: 4 lakh cph moving to 12 lakh cph in two phases; first 8 lakh cph expected mid/end Sept 2026, commercial production by end Q3.
AC: 1.0 mn to 1.8 mn units in two phases (1.0 to 1.3, then 1.3 to 1.8) over 12-15 months; 27-28 season expected to utilise 50-60% of the increased capacity.

Compressors: 2.8 mn to 6 mn units, targeted Dec/Jan with commercial production by Q4 FY27; compressor utilisation target above 75% by next year; INR 500 crore total project, INR 150 crore raised via OCD, first phase funded by equity issue; 22-acre land bought for consolidation.
Deep freezers: 1.5 lakh to 2.5 lakh units by mid/end Q3 FY27; 4 lakh units in FY28.
Vertical capacity is generally expanded only after 50-70% utilisation for seasonal products and 70-80% for non-seasonal ones; new capacity needs 12-24 months to reach target utilisation.
demand_pricing: RAC industry growth expected at 8-10% in the coming season; management said prices have stabilised and inventory levels are normal.
Market is absorbing price hikes slowly in commercial refrigeration; B2B buyers deferred purchases in Q1.
Import restriction on compressors at 40% per government policy, expected to ease in 1-2 years; management sees this as an opening for market growth.
Raw material pressure (copper, aluminium, imported compressor components, logistics) persisted; PCB/chip cost impact limited so far.
PLI benefit worth about 1% of EBITDA, mainly in AC; management is negotiating with customers to share the impact over the next 12 months.
Customer concentration: top AC customer at over 60% in FY26, expected 25-35% in FY27; AC customer count is four.

544339|2026-06.headline: Laxmi Dental Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% y-o-y to about INR75 crore, a record, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and PAT up 23.8%.
544339|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with consolidated revenue from operations of INR74.7 crore against INR65.6 crore a year earlier. Gross margin was 78.6% and EBITDA rose 20.6% y-o-y to INR14.4 crore at a 19.2% margin, helped by favourable mix and a scanner trading contribution. Dental lab grew 23.5% y-o-y, with international up 37.4%, while aligners grew 28.6%. Management flagged a new US CEO hire, a planned Palghar land purchase to replace rented facilities, and FY27 scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units. The company remains debt-free.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR65.6 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +13.9% y-o-y)
vs INR12.5 crore in Q1 FY26; driven by freight, ECL provisions and AI automation
vs INR14.8 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Dental lab
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23.5% y-o-y across domestic and international. Domestic lab excluding scanners grew about 12% y-o-y in Q1, per the analyst's question and management's confirmation.

segments.name: International (within dental lab)
segments.commentary: Grew 37.4% y-o-y. CFO said USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y currency tailwind, so constant-currency growth is lower but still strong.

segments.name: Aligner solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 28.6% y-o-y. Bizdent grew 27.8% and Vedia grew 29.3%. Management linked growth to the iScope at-home monitoring launch and dentist education.

segments.name: Kids-e-Dental (paediatric)
segments.commentary: Grew 54.4% y-o-y in the quarter. The company holds 60% of its PAT in its adjusted EBITDA calculation.

segments.name: Scanners (trading)
segments.commentary: Sold at about INR3 lakh average to dentists with a trading margin of about 15% to 20%. Scanner mix causes quarter-to-quarter margin swings.

guidance_outlook: Aspiration: 15% to 20% revenue growth and 18% to 20% EBITDA margin. Management said it expects to be in that range, after FY26 margins of about 15.6%.
Domestic lab growth expected to accelerate in Q2, Q3 and Q4 FY27 as satellite labs and scanner-linked customers mature.
Scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units targeted for FY27, with the company saying it is on track.
AI-led automation costs are elevated this year and expected to fall next year as scale rises.
Margin expected to be maintained or improved through the year; gross margin should stay stable excluding scanner mix effects.
capex_capacity: Planned FY27 investment in new machinery to modernise and expand manufacturing capacity; no amount disclosed.

Letter of intent executed to acquire land in Palghar, Maharashtra, to replace two rented domestic facilities (Illusion Dental Lab and aligners). Rent is about INR2 crore a year; management said a 3x-size owned facility could otherwise cost INR5 to 6 crore in rent.
No disruption to revenue or productivity expected during the transition, which will be phased. Management cited a 2020 export-unit move from Kandivali to Boisar as precedent.
Aligner capacity utilisation about 70%, with reasonable headroom. Lab utilisation is at a constant 90% to 95% because of custom work.
Digital penetration in domestic network about 75% to 80% (dental lab and aligner combined); international is mostly digital.
demand_pricing: Domestic lab growth slowed to about 12% y-o-y ex-scanners, which management attributed to scanner-led adoption maturing with a 6-month to 18-month gestation period.
Scanner penetration in the industry estimated at about 7% to 8%, with management saying the adoption curve (J-curve) has not yet clearly started.
Management said competition in aligners persists but declined to detail it, citing counter-strategies such as cross-selling.
Aligners are sold only through dentists, not B2C. Management targets general dentists and orthodontists alike.
Branding push includes a brand ambassador, in-clinic branding and social media. Management described itself as the only branded player in crowns.

qa_highlights.question: What differentiates Laxmi Dental products for dentists after the iScan Pro scanner, given no exclusive tie-ups?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 36 years of trust, global quality standards and ISO-certified systems, and innovation, and said it is the only branded crown player.

qa_highlights.question: What is scanner gross margin and how lumpy will margins be?
qa_highlights.answer: Scanners are a trading item with a 15% to 20% margin. Excluding scanners, margins are stable and rising; Q1 margin was 19.2% vs about 15% in the previous quarter and 18% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity and utilisation for lab and aligners?
qa_highlights.answer: Aligners at about 70% utilisation. Lab runs at a constant 90% to 95% because of custom work.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire Palghar land and will there be disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Goal is to move from two rented sites to one owned facility to cut about INR2 crore rent and gain room to expand. Management expects no revenue disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why is domestic lab growing only about 12% and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was 12% y-o-y, attributed to satellite labs adding customer proximity, and expects faster growth from Q2 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the international growth is currency?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y, with the rest from existing DSO and retail business. Management expects the tailwind to persist for some quarters but is unsure beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Scanner deployment and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 800 to 1,000 scanner deployments in FY27 and an 18% to 20% margin aspiration; it said Q1 margin supports that range.

risks_watch: Scanner mix drives quarterly gross margin swings; a strong scanner quarter dilutes margin.
Domestic lab growth at about 12% ex-scanners is below the company's 15% to 20% aspiration; Q2 to Q4 acceleration is unproven.
FX tailwind on international growth (USD from about INR85 to INR95) may reverse.
AI-led automation and ECL provisions raised other expenses to INR15.9 crore; cost pressure may persist this year.
Palghar land and facility transition: timing, capex size and rent savings not yet quantified.
Aligner competition, which management declined to detail.
Share price weakness after results drew analyst and retail investor questions; management had no explanation.

544420|2026-06.headline: Raymond Realty Q1 FY27 booking value rose 129% YoY to INR700 crore; FY27 guidance of 20%+ presales growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin reiterated.
544420|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 booking value of INR700 crore (up 129% YoY), customer collections of INR550 crore (up 47%) and total income of INR536 crore (up 37%). EBITDA rose 70% YoY to INR70 crore, with margin expanding from 11% to 13%, which management attributed to upfront costs from four projects launched in Q4 FY26. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20%+ presales growth, 20%+ revenue growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin and 20%+ ROCE. JDAs now account for about 52% of INR52,000 crore total GDV, and a new Parel JDA with INR8,500 crore GDV was signed.

financial_highlights.change: Gross debt INR1,095 crore; cash INR271 crore
management said FY27 interest INR100-120 crore

segments.commentary: Eight JDA projects with combined GDV of INR27,000 crore (52% of total GDV); 64% of Q1 presales came from JDAs. Four launched projects (Bandra East, BKC, Wadala, Sion) carry INR11,500 crore revenue potential, INR2,900 crore cumulative sales and about INR692 crore collections.

segments.name: Owned land (Thane, 100 acres)
segments.commentary: 65 acres under active development with 6.7 million sq ft RERA carpet area and INR16,500 crore revenue potential; INR9,400 crore sold and INR7,460 crore collected to date. Contributed 36% of Q1 booking value; 11 towers (about 4,000 homes) delivered. Management expects own-land margins of 25-26%.

500040|2026-06.headline: Birla Estates Q1 FY27 collections rose 31% YoY to Rs 713 crore while net sales were muted at about Rs 329 crore, with no launches in the quarter.
500040|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 collections of Rs 713 crore, up 31% from Rs 445 crore a year earlier, and net debt reduced to nearly zero after the Century Pulp and Paper sale to ITC. Net sales were about Rs 329 crore (booking value referenced as Rs 3.3 billion), held back by cancellations and terminations, mainly at Birla Niyaara, with no fresh launches in the quarter. Management added the Vashi redevelopment (GDV about Rs 2,600 crore, 90:10 revenue share), taking the residential redevelopment portfolio to about Rs 4,300 crore. Business development remained slow versus the Rs 10,000–15,000 crore annual target, which management reiterated for FY27 and a Rs 15,000 crore pre-sales ambition over three years.

financial_highlights.change: after Century Pulp and Paper divestment

financial_highlights.value: Rs 437 crore total, of which construction cost about Rs 226 crore

segments.name: Birla Taranya (MMR, Thane)
segments.commentary: Booking value above Rs 1,000 crore within the first three months of RERA approval. MMR plotted development at Birla Mrida (Boisar) and Taranya together delivered Rs 150 crore sustenance booking value.

segments.name: Pune
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs 119 crore booking value from Birla Punya Phase-2 and Birla Evam.

segments.commentary: Vashi project added with GDV about Rs 2,600 crore; total redevelopment portfolio about Rs 4,300 crore. Margins guided at 25-30%.

Birla Niyaara large-format launch: RERA expected by end Q2, launch early to mid Q3 FY27.

Birla Niyaara Tower C launch price tentatively Rs 100,000–120,000 per sq ft; Tower-1 possession targeted 2027 Q3 within RERA deadline of March 2028, with margins about 40%.
Commercial development of about 1.3 million sq ft at Birla Niyaara to start approvals/construction before end FY27; leasing in about four years, at least Rs 800 crore annual leasing when stabilised.
capex_capacity: Birla Niyaara commercial block: about 1.3 million sq ft; institutional/PE partner under evaluation (IFC or MUFG named by analyst, not decided).
Birla Niyaara large-format launch with fungible options planned, following the Silas format.
Birla Aurora and Birla Centurion together give about Rs 140–150 crore annual rental income, 100% occupied.
Handover of Birla Tisya and phases of Birla Navya in FY27; Birla Niyaara Tower-A possession next year.
Noida Sector 150 land is out of the picture; company is bidding in Noida land auctions and looking at Gurgaon auctions.
demand_pricing: Management said Mumbai premium demand is stable and growing in both price and volume; NCR (Gurgaon, Noida) and Bengaluru are being added.
Pipeline of term sheets and advanced deals above Rs 60,000 crore, split across NCR, Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru, with a Mumbai tilt from redevelopment.
Total GDV pipeline about Rs 74,000 crore, of which about Rs 32,000 crore launched and about Rs 42,000 crore unlaunched.
Price increases taken at Birla Niyaara and Silas Tower-A; Worli premium segment cited as commanding strong premiums.
BD challenges cited: pricing, location, clean title, risk-managed structure, and competitive overbidding.
Most deals are outright acquisitions; more than 50% of portfolio is outright development, with JVs making up the rest.

qa_highlights.question: Why was net sales of about Rs 329 crore weak when absorption was healthy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to cancellations and terminations for non-payment, mainly at Niyaara, with no launches in the quarter. Gross sales were above Rs 700 crore, and cancelled units were being rebooked at higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 9,600 crore FY27 launch plan on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was largely on track, with most launches planned for Q3 and Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Vashi margins and structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Economic interest is 90% with a 10% partner, who handles society negotiations and approvals. Margins are expected at 25–30%, with sales at Rs 38,000–40,000 per sq ft on about 1 million sq ft saleable area.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Rs 283 crore cash outflows on the cash flow statement?
qa_highlights.answer: Land payment about Rs 125 crore (Thane), net deposit outflow about Rs 151 crore (including a Noida auction EMD and a Khar redevelopment deposit), and capex about Rs 7 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much construction spend is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Keyur Shah said FY27 construction cost would be about Rs 1,200–1,300 crore, against Rs 226 crore construction cost in Q1 out of Rs 437 crore total spend.

qa_highlights.question: Why has BD lagged peers over the past 1.5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a robust risk framework, due diligence, pricing, title and competitive bidding, and said deals negotiated for 18–24 months are close to closing. It described its stance as prudent rather than conservative.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax impact on the ITC proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax outflow is expected on the proceeds, but the amount is still being worked out. The balance about 5% of consideration is subject to conditions and working capital adjustments.

542580|2026-06.headline: Aartech Solonics Q1 FY27 revenue rose to Rs 728 lakh from Rs 433 lakh YoY (~68%), with PBT up to Rs 119 lakh from Rs 73 lakh.
542580|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 728 lakh versus Rs 433 lakh a year earlier, which it attributed to an order book of about Rs 7 crore carried over from FY26 and executed in the quarter. Material cost was about Rs 3.36 crore, employee cost about Rs 119 lakh, and PBT rose from Rs 73 lakh to Rs 119 lakh with no exceptional items. Management said Q1 is seasonally subdued and that Q3 and Q4 are heavier, and expects healthy revenue and margins in the coming quarters. Management described the balance sheet as near debt-free, with only non-fund-based liabilities. The Q&A focused on pipeline conversion, ultracapacitors and defence approvals, CRP margins versus peers, R&D spend, and new customer segments.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 433 lakh in Q1 FY26 (about 1.7x)
marginally up YoY; includes annual increments and performance bonus paid in Q1
vs Rs 469 lakh a year earlier; management said expense ratio is broadly flat as % of revenue
vs Rs 73 lakh in Q1 FY26

segments.name: CRP (control and relay panels)
segments.commentary: Described as the bread-and-butter product; management said pricing carries a margin of around 100% plus. Peers in higher-rated relay segments earn higher margins. Management is pursuing OEM tie-ups to move into 415 kV to 750 kV ratings.

segments.name: Defence projects
segments.commentary: Revenue of about Rs 156 lakh in Q1 per management. Ultracapacitor and energy storage programmes for the Army, with technical evaluation taking about 18 to 24 months.

segments.name: Other diversified segments (electrical engineering services, plastic enclosures, lubricant-related)
segments.commentary: Management cited about Rs 40 lakh from the plastic enclosure segment and about Rs 181 lakh from the trading segment, which totalled about Rs 7 crore on its own basis. The description of these segments was partly unclear in the transcript.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the next quarters to be very healthy in terms of both revenue and margins.

Management said inquiries worth around Rs 100 crore are in the pipeline and expects a near-about number by this financial year or around the same time next year, while being conservative on project delays.
Management said the roadmap to 415 kV and above depends on OEM or manufacturing partners and on possible in-house relay manufacturing in future.
No specific revenue or margin numerical guidance was given.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity, or utilisation figures were discussed in the call.
Management said it is working on partnerships with relay manufacturers to move from 220 kV to 415 kV and above, with own manufacturing possible later.
Type-test certification from PGCIL, CPRI or similar bodies is required for new products; no timeline was given.
demand_pricing: Management said data centres are beginning to develop in India and that its energy storage products (flywheels, ultracapacitors, rectifiers) are being positioned for them.
Bus Transfer System demand is widening from GENs to refineries, process industries and cement; oil and refinery was named as a sunrise opportunity.
Management said the supply chain for some newer EPC-linked business segments is slightly stagnant, with unclear delivery timelines, though margins are good.
Management said the stock price has not reflected the improved performance, and that the market will eventually price it in.

qa_highlights.question: How will ultracapacitors and defence products such as Faradyne/AAPM be industrialised, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share product details, citing proprietary work and customer commitments. It said ultracapacitor work spans more than 15 years, with applications in railway locos, Army tank engine starting and missile nano-ultracapacitors.

qa_highlights.question: Is CRP pricing lower than peers, and are margins being cross-subsidised?
qa_highlights.answer: CRP is the core product with pricing around 100% plus margin. Competitors in higher-rated segments earn more, and the company's long-term aim is 415 kV to 750 kV via OEM partnerships.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 100 crore pipeline convert into orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the inquiries are still active and are long-gestation projects. It expects good numbers this financial year, or around the same time next year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the approval timelines for ultracapacitors and who gives approval?
qa_highlights.answer: Technical evaluation typically takes about 18 to 24 months, and the approval involves the Army and other agencies. Breaking into the market takes much longer.

qa_highlights.question: How is R&D spend low relative to development activity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it runs R&D on a frugal basis, excludes most overheads from R&D, and capitalises most R&D spend into assets. The FY25 R&D figure cited by the analyst was about Rs 45 lakh.

qa_highlights.question: Are Indian Railways and oil and gas target markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said oil and refineries are a process industry where the Bus Transfer System fits. It cited prior supply to Dangote and Reliance and said Indian Railways was not addressed in detail.

risks_watch: Revenue is seasonal, with Q1 typically subdued. Q1 profit in absolute terms is small, so Q3 and Q4 execution matters.
The Rs 100 crore inquiry pipeline is long-gestation and may slip because of policy and ecosystem changes.
Ultracapacitor and defence commercialisation has long approval cycles (about 18 to 24 months for technical evaluation), with uncertain timing and no disclosed revenue visibility.
Expansion into 415 kV and above depends on partners and certifications (PGCIL, CPRI). Supply chain for some EPC-linked segments is described as stagnant.
R&D expense disclosure is low relative to the claimed product development. Investors should watch the FY26 annual report for disclosures.
542580|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the top-line growth and near-term outlook, but reticent on product details, citing proprietary and customer-confidentiality constraints. Answers on pipeline conversion and timelines were hedged and general.

544497|2026-06.headline: Anlon Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin fell to ~17% (PAT ₹8.28 cr) on raw-material spikes and Remember India consolidation; management targets 25-27% for FY27.
544497|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 total income was ₹87.62 cr versus ₹33.31 cr in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA of ₹15.65 cr (vs ₹6.26 cr) and PAT of ₹8.28 cr (vs ₹3.55 cr). EBITDA margin moderated to about 17%, which management attributed to a sharp rise in solvent and petrochemical raw-material prices after the geopolitical conflict and to operating costs of the newly acquired Remember India Health links being consolidated. The company completed the 63.98% acquisition of Remember India on 8 May 2026, has acquired Apiqo Organics and Bizotic Lifesciences, and is moving into finished dosage formulations. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of ₹350-400 cr and a ~30% three-year revenue CAGR, but gave limited quantitative detail on Remember India.

financial_highlights.change: moderated; management earlier guided ~24-25% floor for Q1

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue contribution, Q1 FY27 - Anlon standalone
financial_highlights.change: management cited standalone sales of ₹30 cr vs ₹33 cr in analyst question

segments.name: Anlon Healthcare (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ~₹30-32 cr, down from ₹33 cr YoY per analyst; management says it is at peak utilisation and expects FY27 standalone revenue of ~₹180 cr. Production cycles of 30-45 days mean some output lands in Q2.

segments.name: Apiqo Organics (68% stake, moving to 100%)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ~₹45 cr, described as the most profitable unit; FY27 revenue expected ₹120-150 cr. Business is fully booked in industrial and fine chemicals; share-swap to make it a 100% subsidiary to complete by end-Q2.

segments.name: Bizotic Lifesciences (57% stake, moving to 100%)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ~₹12 cr; FY27 expected ~₹60 cr. Management says it is profitable and that committed partner business exists; share-swap to 100% also targeted by end-Q2.

segments.name: Remember India Health links (63.98%)
segments.commentary: Finished dosage formulations (tablets, capsules, ointments) with access to 30+ dossiers; in investment and turnaround phase. No revenue assumed for FY27 until at least Q4 FY27; WHO-PQ approval expected by end-CY2026. Margin expected above 25%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of ₹350-400 cr reiterated; management said H1 comparison is the right lens, and the guidance range was re-confirmed as ₹380-400 cr in one answer.
EBITDA margin: ~17% in Q1; management expects margins to improve from Q2 (said 'better than the first quarter') and target 25-27% for FY27 on consolidated basis; earlier comment of 22-25% in H1.
Gross margin expected to hold at 40-45%.
FY28 revenue indicated at ~₹700 cr if Anlon-site expansion (~₹130 cr capex, ~1,200 MT additional) is commissioned on schedule by Q1 FY28; management flagged possible delays from statutory approvals.

Working capital: receivable days expected to fall toward 60-70 days over time (current ~130-135 days vs 90-day terms); management expects positive operating cash flow in FY27, 'lower but positive'. Management also said H1 operating cash flow positive is targeted before year-end.
Biologics subsidiary (Anlon Biologics) revenue expected from Q4 FY28; Anlon Medicare from Q2 FY28; Remember India peak revenue/EBITDA to be detailed in Q2 call.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity after three acquisitions stated at ~1,400-1,600 MT per annum; management clarified Anlon standalone is ~400 MT and is at peak.
Anlon-site expansion: ~₹130 cr capex adding ~1,200 MT (standalone to ~1,600 MT); commissioning targeted by Q1 FY28 subject to statutory approvals.
Funding: ~₹70 cr debt at ~8.5-8.6% interest; balance from internal accruals.
Eight new cleanrooms planned at the new facility to run eight APIs in parallel; initial planning assumes 50-60% utilisation.
Bizotic and Apiqo utilisation can rise gradually from ~65% toward higher levels; no 65-to-85% jump expected within this year.
Anlon Biologics (peptides, biosimilars) construction to begin within ~2 months; in-house peptide manufacturing targeted by FY28.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices: management said solvent/methanol-linked inputs rose 2-3x since pre-war (methanol cited at ₹22 to ₹58-60/kg); not yet normalised. Around 40% of API manufacturing cost is solvents and petroleum-linked inputs.

Price pass-through: price increases on finished products have been initiated and customers have agreed; management expects this to reflect over the next one to two quarters, but earlier orders at old prices weighed on Q1.
Customer base is concentrated: 10-15 B2B customers, which limits ability to reprice frequently.
Fine/specialty chemicals (Apiqo): fully booked, described as 'overbooked'; management estimates ₹120-150 cr contribution in FY27.
CDMO: expected commercial supply of first molecule by Q3 and others by Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28; process validations ongoing.
Seven new APIs/DMFs planned for filing within FY27; compilation under way.

540575|2026-06.headline: Star Cement Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR203 crore (INR1,497/t) from INR230 crore, with PAT at INR74 crore versus INR98 crore on subsidy cuts and fuel costs.
540575|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue rose to about INR902 crore from INR847 crore, but EBITDA declined to INR203 crore and EBITDA per tonne dropped to INR1,497 from INR1,774. Management attributed the fall to lower Assam incentive accruals (GST cut from 28% to 18%), higher packing and fuel costs, and a kiln shutdown. Cement volumes grew about 7% to 13.02 lakh tonnes, but Northeast volume was flat, and management cut FY27 cement volume growth guidance to 8-9% from 11-12%. Management also updated the Rajasthan (Nimbol) and Haryana (Jhajjar) expansion plan, with capex now about INR2,700 crore (INR2,900 crore incl. GST).

segments.name: Northeast cement
segments.commentary: Sold about 8.71 lakh tonnes vs 8.67 lakh tonnes YoY, essentially flat; management attributed the weakness to April Assam elections and monsoon, not competition.

segments.name: Outside Northeast (Bihar, West Bengal)
segments.commentary: Sold 4.31 lakh tonnes vs 3.55 lakh tonnes YoY (up ~21%), the main volume growth driver this quarter.

segments.name: Building Solutions (AAC, RMC)
segments.commentary: Management said the INR150 crore revenue target is a revenue (not EBITDA) estimate; current run-rate is below it, with ARR expected to reach that level by Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 cement volume growth revised to 8-9% from 11-12%; Northeast growth target 8-9% vs industry about 7%.
FY27 clinker sales expected flat to down 5-10% vs FY26 as clinker is now sourced externally in the Northeast.
Q2 FY27 EBITDA per tonne guided at about INR1,400, with INR1,500-1,600 for the full year.
Fuel cost guided to fall from INR1.55/kcal-equivalent in Q1 to about INR1.45 in Q2 and lower in Q3-Q4 (CFO/MD cited Q4 FY26 at INR1.33).
Assam incentive for FY27 revised to about INR115 crore from earlier INR145 crore due to new equated payout rules.

Cost savings of INR60-70 crore expected in Q2 vs Q1 from lower one-off donation and incentive items; further savings from Silchar railway siding (Oct-Nov), Siliguri wagon tippler (about INR150/t saving on Siliguri sales), and EVs over 5-6 months.
Expects double-digit volume growth in Q3-Q4 FY27 once flood waters recede, with pent-up demand.
Subsidy drag expected to end after September 2026, as GST cut base effect rolls off.
capex_capacity: Rajasthan (Nimbol) integrated plant: 3.0 million tonnes grinding and 3.3 million tonnes clinker; public hearing in August, EC expected by early October, groundwork from mid-October to November; commissioning in about 18-20 months (Q4 FY28 to Q1 FY29).
Jhajjar (Haryana) plant of 2 million tonnes; total expansion capex about INR2,700 crore (about INR2,900 crore including GST), vs earlier INR2,250 crore Nimbol plus about INR650 crore Haryana.
Q1 FY27 capex spend about INR93 crore; FY27 capex guidance of INR500 crore unchanged; FY28 capex about INR1,500 crore.

West Bengal grinding decision pending the state industrial policy (expected around 15 August): may redirect the 2 million tonne Bihar (Begusarai) grinding capex to a Siliguri brownfield unit, though a single 1 million tonne unit may not be economic.
Rajasthan plant has standard state package (capital subsidy plus SGST); quantum to be disclosed on a slide.
Northeast clinker capacity about 15.5-16 million tonnes and grinding about 23-24 million tonnes; about 1 million tonnes each of clinker and grinding expected from two players over the next 3 years.
demand_pricing: Northeast demand muted in Q1 and Q2 due to elections, then flooding in Assam; July volumes fell about 12% YoY and August shows marginal growth.
Prices broadly flat since Q1; up about INR3/bag in Northeast and West Bengal and about INR10 in Bihar, with no cuts despite demand weakness.
Packing (PP bag) costs up due to international war-driven crude price increase; management said these are hard to predict.
Premium (PPC/OPC) share about 15.9%; trade share about 80%; lead distance about 210 km; clinker factor about 66.5%; green share about 3% including WHRS.
Fuel mix Q1: FSA about 45%, spot coal about 30%, balance biomass and others; coal diverted to power plants limited FSA rake availability.
Sand mining crackdown in West Bengal has weighed on regional cement demand.
Management said Sept 2025 base was weak due to GST cut, so September 2026 should show easier comparison.

qa_highlights.question: Will volume growth improve in Q2 and what is FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 volume growth is limited by Assam floods; management now expects FY27 cement growth of 8-9% vs earlier 11-12%, with double-digit growth in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR1,500/t EBITDA sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes over the full year (INR1,500-1,600/t), but Q2 is guided to about INR1,400/t due to shutdown costs and rain-hit fixed-cost absorption.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rajasthan timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: EC expected by October, construction from November, commissioning in 18-20 months; combined Rajasthan and Haryana capex about INR2,700 crore (INR2,900 crore with GST).

qa_highlights.question: Is a QIP planned and what leverage is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: No active QIP plan; management targets about 1.5-1.6x net debt/EBITDA to fund expansion, with QIP considered only for opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: How much is outstanding from the Assam government on incentives?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR130 crore outstanding; total scheme value INR794 crore, now paid over 12 years, reducing FY27 expected receipts to about INR115 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a Northeast market share or competition concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no market share loss and that the Q1 dip reflects elections and monsoon, not Dalmia's capacity ramp.
