segments.commentary: Revenue growth stated as 24.7% YoY after management first said ~38.4%, corrected on call; attributed to higher share of wallet with global aviation majors and early defence/propulsion deliveries.

segments.name: Energy and Oil & Gas (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth stated as 26.7% YoY after first being said as 21.6%, corrected on call; driven by gas turbine components and launch of new customer-dedicated lines.

guidance_outlook: Long-term annual revenue growth guidance of over 25% reiterated; Chairman said the guidance will change once the company moves to the next level.

Management says it has met Q1 guidance; manufacturing infrastructure 'running at full throttle', with substantive revenue contributions from new capacity expected from H2 FY27 and acceleration from Q3-Q4.
EBITDA margin guidance framed as 32%-35% for calculation purposes, though company has delivered above 35% consistently.
Other income expected to moderate as treasury cash is deployed into factory infrastructure.
Remaining FY26 expansion initiatives: ~80% stabilised in Q1; major remaining activities due mid-Q2 and full closure by Q3 FY27.
Working-capital targets: debtor days ~200 in H1 and 160-180 in H2 FY27; natural hedge for export receivables expected by Q4 FY27 via bill discounting.
capex_capacity: Tuniki Bollaram Industrial Park: 8 customer-dedicated plants planned; each plant said to generate INR150-180 crore revenue at full utilisation, implying ~INR1,200 crore from newer plants.

Fourth dedicated facility (7,600 sq m, for Baker Hughes) inaugurated April 2026 and commenced operations in Q1; dedicated lines already running for Mitsubishi, GE Power Systems/GE Steam Power and Siemens Energy.
Civil construction at Azad Center of Excellence remaining units to finish within FY27; machine installations in modular phases aligned to customer roadmaps.
Management estimates ~1 year of capex-driven capacity for the next couple of years; capex plans beyond FY29 are being sketched, with quantum and timing to be disclosed in the next quarter.
Hot-section facility (modelled on the Mitsubishi plant) expected to be set up in roughly 7-8 months, also usable for aviation engines.
FY26 capex was roughly INR900 crore over two years per analyst; no new capex number was given by management.
demand_pricing: Turbojet engine: first indigenous expendable turbojet engine delivered to GTRE, DRDO and MoD; next step is weapon testing expected in 4-6 weeks per management (not formally communicated), followed by certification and production scale-up. Management says volumes are unknown (2-, 3- or 4-digit) and existing capacity is fungible for 2-digit volumes.
First 20 engines produced so far; management will share costing after 5-6 engines in a row (about 8-12 weeks away).
Rolls-Royce civil aircraft engine: first batch of qualification parts expected to be delivered within the current quarter.

Cost indigenisation: local suppliers Sunflag and Star Wire qualified for critical raw-material grades; import freight of ~4-5% avoided. Raw material cost fell to ~5% of sales from ~12% a year earlier, per analyst.
Employee cost rose to ~INR42 crore from ~INR29 crore per analyst; management attributed it to inventory build for H2 sales and hiring of ~150-200 people per month into 90-day training.
Management said rupee depreciation can add roughly 5-6% to revenue but is not a planning lever; FX on exports is below EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline from first turbojet engine delivery to orders and capacity planning beyond FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said next steps are weapon testing in 4-6 weeks and then certification and production; capacity is fungible for 2-digit volumes, and capex quantum/timing for next 5-6 years will be clarified in about a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Growth thesis for aerospace hot-section and peers' margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hot-section demand is a multi-billion market, OEMs are already asking when the facility is ready, and margin potential is referenced to high-cost-country peers; no growth number given.

qa_highlights.question: When will working capital days plateau?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO targeted ~200 debtor days in H1 and 160-180 in H2 FY27, mainly via bill discounting that will move ~170-180 day debtors toward ~90 days; finance cost will continue to rise on discounting charges.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide 32-35% EBITDA margin when delivering 37-38%?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said 32-35% is used for guidance and calculation purposes, while margins have been running above 35% due to shop-floor skills and continuous improvement, from ~18-19% at inception.

qa_highlights.question: Is revenue growth above 25% achievable given 3-year potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said 25%+ is guided given current situation and the guidance will change on moving to the next level; no 3-year target given.

qa_highlights.question: Does rupee depreciation benefit revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is natural hedging, with imports offsetting exports; CFO said FX benefit is below EBITDA and not built into the margin.

524404|2026-06.headline: Marksans Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.6% YoY to INR841 crore, with record EBITDA of INR213 crore (25.3% margin) and PAT of INR159 crore.
524404|2026-06.overview: Revenue of INR840.8 crore grew 35.6% YoY, led by UK and Europe at INR356 crore (+74.7%), which includes INR44 crore from the QliniQ acquisition. Gross margin expanded to 59.1% on product mix, low-cost inventory and favourable FX, and EBITDA margin reached 25.3%. Management said the gross margin is sustainable at around 55-56% as freight and raw material costs from the war normalise, and it reiterated FY27 guidance of 15-20% revenue growth and 20-21% EBITDA margin. Cash rose to INR1,058 crore, with net cash of INR1,031 crore after the QliniQ payment.

financial_highlights.change: +35.6% YoY from INR620 crore; Q1 FY26 base
+38.9% YoY; margin +138 bps YoY, +478 bps QoQ
+112.8% YoY from INR100.1 crore; margin +919 bps YoY, +251 bps QoQ
+173.9% YoY from INR58.2 crore; QoQ up from INR149 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Free cash flow (after net capex of INR33 crore)

financial_highlights.change: vs ~159 days in Q1 FY26 and 138 days for FY26
vs INR12.1 crore (2%) in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR1,058 crore; net cash INR1,031 crore
financial_highlights.change: vs INR711 crore at end of Q1 FY26

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue INR377 crore, +15.1% YoY, about 45% of consolidated revenue. Summer demand softer in line with seasonality; Rx price erosion remained in single digits; Canada filings underway.

segments.name: UK and Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue INR356 crore, +74.7% YoY, about 42% of revenue and a record quarter. Ex-QliniQ growth was over 50% YoY, all organic in the UK. QliniQ (Netherlands) contributed INR44 crore; growth ex-QliniQ was 53.1%.

segments.name: Australia and New Zealand
segments.commentary: Revenue INR88 crore, +53.7% YoY; sequential moderation was seasonal after a strong Q4 Southern Hemisphere winter.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Revenue INR20 crore. Management said Middle East and other non-western markets are being hit by shipping disruption from the war.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: revenue growth 15-20% and EBITDA margin 20-21%; management said it will stick with this given geopolitical volatility.
Gross margin sustainable at roughly 55-56%, versus 59% in Q1, as inventory benefit fades and freight and raw material costs stay elevated.
Europe revenue expected at about INR180 crore for FY27. QliniQ guided to INR150-175 crore for the year, with its EUR10 million base growing to EUR14-15 million.
Q2 revenue expected to be above Q1 and Q3 the strongest; EBITDA margin to reach the guided level. Year-end EBITDA margin of 21-22% described as achievable.
Target of INR4,000 crore revenue within two years reiterated; US target moves from $200 million to $300 million, then $400 million over about five years.
Germany expected to generate revenue from early Q3 FY27; Ireland revenue not expected until FY28. Europe target of about INR1,000 crore within five years.
capex_capacity: Goa Unit 2 (Teva facility) revenue at INR50-plus crore against an INR80 crore target, about 60-65% of plan.
Management is evaluating one or two targets for a new Indian manufacturing unit over one to two years; nothing concrete yet. Location open, including other states.
Backward integration (DMFs, CRAMS) is not being actively pursued given the current environment.
Around 65-70% of sales are manufactured in India.
Net capex was INR33 crore in Q1.
demand_pricing: US order book described as strong. US growth expected from all subsidiaries this year, not only the US.
US Rx mix is rising; the US business is still OTC-led, possibly moving from 95:5 OTC:Rx toward 85:15 over time.
UK is about 55% Rx and 45% OTC; Europe is expected to be about 80-85% Rx.
Management sees no major change in US OTC competitive intensity; some large players are struggling.
Rx price erosion in the US stayed in single digits.
Inventory-led margin benefit is being depleted over time; freight and solvent costs are rising due to the war.

qa_highlights.question: How is QliniQ revenue recognised, and what is the FY27 outlook for Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Effective date was 1 April 2026, so Q1 is consolidated. QliniQ is guided at INR150-175 crore for FY27, and total Europe about INR180 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross margin sustainable at current levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 55-56% as the inventory benefit unwinds, and says more upside is unrealistic given freight and crude costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan with over INR1,000 crore of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is earmarked for inorganic growth, mainly in Europe, with nothing concrete yet. Management ruled out riskier instruments such as index investing.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise guidance upward?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Guidance of 15-20% revenue growth and 20-21% EBITDA margin stands, given geopolitical uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US strategy in light of tariff comments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not weight the tariff remarks heavily. US remains an important market, and local manufacturing is an option to keep open.

qa_highlights.question: Could ABCnow and QliniQ scale in the UK and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QliniQ is Rx-tilted, ABCnow has Rx and OTC, and Europe is about 80-85% Rx. Europe is targeted at about INR1,000 crore in five years, mostly through acquisitions.

risks_watch: Gross margin normalising from 59.1% to 55-56% as inventory benefit fades and war-driven freight and solvent costs persist.
Shipping and freight disruption in Rest of World and Middle East markets.
US tariff and policy uncertainty; management expects the policy to change and has not committed to US manufacturing.
Integration and returns on the QliniQ and ABCnow acquisitions; Ireland revenue timing pushed to FY28.
Capacity: management says a new India unit may be needed for the three to five year plan, but nothing is confirmed. Goa Unit 2 is running at 60-65% of plan.
No definite timeline for the next USFDA inspection across the three US-approved plants.
524404|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability but cautious on forward margins and capital deployment. Management repeatedly tied margin and guidance to geopolitical and freight risk, and was non-committal on large M&A and on US manufacturing.

542337|2026-06.headline: Spencer's Retail Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% YoY to Rs 469 crore; EBITDA doubled to Rs 9.4 crore (2% of sales).
542337|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to Rs 469 crore, with Spencer's format up 18% and Nature's Basket down 13% on a YoY basis (quarterly sales Rs 59 crore). Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 9.4 crore versus Rs 4.7 crore a year ago, but last year's base included about Rs 10 crore of lower non-operating income that management stripped out. Management said the EBITDA improvement is shifting from cost-led to sales-growth-led. Nature's Basket saw a management change about 45 days before the call and a reset plan focused on inventory, assortment and execution.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 86 crore YoY; percentage margin flat
vs Rs 4.7 crore (1%) YoY; prior year included ~Rs 10 crore lower other income
vs 19.1% YoY; ~19% like-for-like per management (difference from membership accounting)
vs Rs 15 crore YoY (which included ~Rs 7 crore non-operating income)
-13% YoY (vs Rs 69 crore); +8% QoQ (vs Rs 55 crore)
vs negative Rs 4.5 crore in Q4 FY26; slightly positive in Q1 FY26
vs loss of ~Rs 18 per order in Q1 FY26; ~Rs 12 in Q4
SRL Rs 1,019 crore; NBL Rs 237 crore

segments.name: Spencer's (format)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 18% YoY and 8% QoQ, with offline +14% and online +49%. Sales per sq ft Rs 1,850 in Q1 (internal target Rs 2,000 in festive quarter); store EBITDA reportedly 2x year-ago, from ~2.5% toward a 7.5-8% short-term aspiration.

segments.name: Nature's Basket
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 59 crore, down 13% YoY but up 8% QoQ. Management says the setback was internal (stock availability, long-tail SKUs, online build-out); a reset plan is in place under a new management team about 45 days old.

segments.name: Jiffy (online platform)
segments.commentary: Management cited FY25 scale of about Rs 200 crore; no Q1 figure given. Online growth at Spencer's (+49%) is attributed to the platform.

guidance_outlook: Full-year online business growth to steady at around 25%, with no heavy customer-acquisition spend and unchanged unit economics.
Spencer's offline growth guided at mid to high single digits for the year.
Nature's Basket expected to reach early double-digit growth from Q3 and Q4 FY27 after the reset.
No new Spencer's store additions in FY27 beyond relocations and a few cluster tests; calibrated expansion considered for FY28.
No new Nature's Basket stores; limited capex directed to refurbishing existing stores. Management frames EBITDA breakeven as the ambition, with Q2 as the next update.
capex_capacity: No new stores added in Q1 FY27; productivity gains come from the existing footprint of 89 Spencer's and 31 Nature's Basket stores.
Spencer's sales per sq ft Rs 1,850 in Q1; internal target Rs 2,000 in the festive quarter.
Nature's Basket capex limited to refurbishing ageing stores; a small Spencer's store launched in suburban Kolkata two days before the call.
Nature's Basket online tech stack ready, riding on the Jiffy platform; customer acquisition deferred until inventory is fixed. Update promised in Q2.
Debt refinancing process started, with some expected to close in the current month (August).
demand_pricing: Spencer's YoY growth split about 70% from higher number of bills (NOBs) and 30% from higher average bill value (ABV), which management called underlying volume growth.
Category mix broadly unchanged: staples +100 bps, liquor +100 bps, non-food (apparel, E&E, GM) -100 bps, fresh flat.
Membership: launched July 2025, 125,000+ members (~25% of active monthly customers) contributing ~1/3 of monthly sales; member retention ~2x and monthly spend ~3x non-members, with frequency near 5.
Online ABV above Rs 780; repeat rate ~67%; NPS 85+; in-full rate above 90%; on-time delivery just under 30 minutes.
Management declined to enter quick-commerce marketplaces (Instamart, Blinkit) for Nature's Basket, citing margin sharing and sustainability concerns.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about the growth trajectory across Spencer's, Jiffy and Nature's Basket over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give segment targets. Online is guided to ~25% full-year growth, Spencer's offline to mid-to-high single digits, and Nature's Basket to early double digits from Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What KPIs track the Nature's Basket turnaround?
qa_highlights.answer: Three KPIs: sales per sq ft, rupee gross margin (not percentage), and cost control. Cost cuts are limited in NB's premium format; support overheads were optimised once.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any store expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: No new Nature's Basket stores. Spencer's has no additions this fiscal beyond relocations and cluster tests; a calibrated expansion may come in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Could membership reach 50% of business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management focuses on absolute numbers: target 200,000 members shopping at least 5 times a month, contributing 39-42% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Spencer's growth, volume or pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% from more bills and 30% from higher ABV; category mix stable, with member special pricing cited as a driver of basket-wide buying.

qa_highlights.question: Update on quick commerce for Nature's Basket and debt status?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick commerce was not pursued; the tech platform is ready but customer acquisition waits on inventory fixes. Consolidated debt Rs 1,266 crore, with refinancing under way and some expected this month.

risks_watch: Nature's Basket remains loss-making at EBITDA level (negative Rs 2.5 crore) with revenue still down YoY; reset success depends on the new management team.
Q1 EBITDA improvement partly reflects a Rs 10 crore non-operating income gap versus last year; underlying gains need confirmation in Q2.
Debt of Rs 1,266 crore with a large portion due for refinancing this year; closure timing is not yet confirmed.
Spencer's gross margin fell to 18.2% from 19.1% YoY on reported basis; management attributes this to membership accounting.
Online growth relies on order volume with unit economics positive at about Rs 18 per order, and the target is limited customer acquisition spend.

526807|2026-06.headline: Seamec Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 41% YoY to INR 297 crore, with EBITDA of INR 124 crore (about 42% margin).
526807|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR 297 crore against INR 211 crore a year ago, up 41%, and standalone revenue was INR 283 crore against INR 201 crore. Consolidated PAT rose to INR 81 crore from INR 76 crore, while standalone PAT was flat at about INR 81 crore versus INR 80 crore. Management attributed the quarter to higher vessel deployment, healthy utilisation and cost discipline, with Paladin's dry-dock and the Middle East conflict weighing on the onshore segment. The call focused on the Seamec ANANT acquisition (USD 70 million, expected by end-August), the 40-42% margin band and the 15-20% growth CAGR target.

segments.name: Offshore (IMR/EPC vessels)
segments.commentary: Margins materially better than onshore, attributed to higher vessel deployment. Management said the 40-42% margin band is sustainable on an annualised basis.

segments.name: Onshore / other (Paladin)
segments.commentary: Margins pulled down because Paladin was non-operational in Q1 (dry-dock in Dubai, stuck by Middle East conflict); it incurred cost with no revenue. Paladin has returned to India and resumed contract, with revenue expected from Q2.

guidance_outlook: Management targets 15-20% revenue CAGR over the next 3-5 years and says it is committed to that number.
Margins: management guides 40-42% EBITDA margin, sustainable on an annualised basis; quarterly figures not guided.

Seamec ANANT: acquisition (USD 70 million, funded about 50:50 internal equity and loans) expected to complete by end-August 2026; deployment on ONGC contract about one month after acquisition for statutory formalities, with start expected within Q2 FY27 per Naveen Mohta and in Q3 per Sunil Gupta; expected 95-98% utilisation once working.
Gallant vessel sale: expected to complete in September 2026 after shareholder approval.
Seamec Princess/III: monsoon idle period (May-October); Princess being dry-docked in this period; contract talks for October at an advanced stage, not yet announced.
Seamec II charter ends end-August 2026; intended for EPC work rather than IMR; no rate uplift confirmed.

Management expects FY27 and FY28 growth from newer vessels and higher deployment; Samudra Samrat-type ONGC O&M contracts (Samudra Sevak, Samudra Prabha) continue, with no vessel-wise revenue disclosed.
capex_capacity: Seamec ANANT: USD 70 million purchase from HAL Offshore (binding agreement, related-party parent contract with ONGC); to be owned by Seamec post-completion.
Fleet: Seamec Princess dry-docking during monsoon idle period; Seamec Glorious (barge) off-hire in monsoon period; Seamec III and Princess off-hired.
Growth capex needed for incremental Middle East business since all current vessels are deployed (Sunil Gupta).
Non-core bulk carrier JV: one vessel liquidation agreement signed; OSV purchase in Dubai subsidiary abandoned.
MoU with DG Shipping for ~INR 1,000 crore of acquisitions over the next 2 years; management says it intends to grow the fleet but has no confirmed deal beyond ANANT.
demand_pricing: Management says demand for DSVs remains strong, with supply tight; expects strong demand for 3-5 years and says the Iran sanctions lifting could add more demand.
Management would not give a specific charter-rate outlook; rates depend on demand and supply.
Contract mix: about 35-40% of contracts are short term (EPC is short term, seasonal Oct-May); IMR contracts are mid to long term, some 3-5 years.
Middle East (Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Abu Dhabi) cited as key growth area; Aramco qualification is helping inquiry flow, per management.
India: Andaman and Mahanadi discoveries cited as future opportunities in subsea, diving, inspection and maintenance.
Government's Samudra Manthan policy seen as supportive, but management said the benefit would take 3-5 years to show.

qa_highlights.question: Why are offshore margins better than onshore, and is Paladin contributing now?
qa_highlights.answer: Offshore margins improved on higher vessel deployment; onshore margin was dragged by Paladin's non-operational costs. Paladin has resumed operations and will contribute from Q1 onward per Naveen Mohta, with Sunil Gupta later saying the results will show in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Seamec ANANT: timeline, consideration and financing?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition expected by end-August 2026 under a binding HAL Offshore agreement for USD 70 million, financed roughly 50:50 between internal equity and loans. Vessel returns to the ONGC contract about a month after acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: How long will DSV charter rates stay high?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific rate outlook given; management says rates depend on demand and supply and sees strong DSV demand for the next 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins move back to mid-40s?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management maintains 40-42% as the sustainable annualised band because of off-hire and dry-dock periods, and does not guide quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth targets and FY27/FY28 trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 15-20% CAGR over 3-5 years, with FY27 and FY28 growth from newer vessels and higher deployment; no quantified FY27 figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the royalty review (GT report) and the 4% revenue royalty?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an independent review by Grant Thornton was completed with a satisfactory report under consideration by independent directors; it will not be shared, and the 4% royalty to the parent continues.

risks_watch: Seamec ANANT: completion timing (end-August) and ONGC redeployment (Q2 vs Q3 guidance differs between management speakers); the USD 70 million acquisition is partly debt-funded.
Seamec II and Princess October contracts not yet announced; monsoon idle period leaves three vessels off-hire.
Middle East geopolitical exposure: Strait of Hormuz and Iran sanctions affected Paladin in Q1.
Related-party exposure: 4% royalty to parent continues; GT review report not being shared.
Contract mix: 35-40% of fleet on short-term contracts, so utilisation can swing with EPC seasonality.
Pearl bulk carrier in Dubai subsidiary under arbitration; bulk carrier JV liquidation in progress.
Unclear whether Samudra Manthan benefits will show within 2 years; management says 3-5 years.
526807|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and the 15-20% growth target, but noticeably vague on specifics: charter rates, contract names and timing are deferred to future exchange filings. Management was defensive on the royalty review and on the Seamec II rate question.

532967|2026-06.headline: Kiri Industries Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 63% YoY to INR 295 crore, with PAT of INR 270 crore driven mainly by INR 284 crore other income.
532967|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 63% YoY to INR 295 crore on realisation-led growth in dyes, dyes intermediates and basic chemicals, with standalone material margin at 31.9% versus 23.5% a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA was only INR 17 crore (5.86% margin), so PAT of INR 270 crore was largely a function of INR 284 crore other income, mainly treasury gains and inter-corporate loan interest. Consolidated revenue rose 55% to INR 312 crore with EBITDA of INR 37 crore (7.84%), and the group is substantially debt-free after repaying Claronex Holdings' borrowings. The copper and fertiliser project moved into structured construction, with financial closure still incomplete (over 50% of debt commitments received).

financial_highlights.change: vs 23.5% in Q1 FY26 and 20.4% in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated EBITDA (incl. share of associates and JVs)

financial_highlights.change: interest on inter-corporate loans plus realised and unrealised treasury gains

financial_highlights.metric: Share of profit from associates (Lonsen Kiri, 40% stake)

segments.name: Dyes, dyes intermediates and basic chemicals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Realisations rose across Reactive Dyes, Vinyl Sulphone, H-Acid and certain basic chemicals; management said H-Acid prices are INR 800-900/unit versus INR 350-400 earlier. Average capacity utilisation was about 60% last quarter, targeted at 70-75% for FY27 if markets support.

segments.name: Lonsen Kiri (associate, 40% stake)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 21 crore to consolidated profit in Q1 FY27. Management cited a JV result of about INR 71 crore EBITDA and INR 51 crore PAT on INR 368 crore revenue, as referenced by an analyst; Kiri supplies raw materials to the JV, with 60-70% of JV raw materials sourced from Kiri.

segments.name: Copper and fertiliser integrated project (under construction)
segments.commentary: Total project capital estimated at close to INR 12,000 crore, with INR 1,400 crore deployed to date, all equity so far. Downstream copper tube, rod and refinery phases are planned for Q1 FY28, FY28 and Q3 FY29 respectively.

guidance_outlook: Copper tube plant (35 KT) expected operational June 2027; 2.25 lakh tonne CCR rod plant (8 mm) expected August-September 2027, both stable by January 2028, using imported Japanese LME-grade cathodes.
Part refinery of 1.75 lakh tonnes (anode to cathode) targeted around January 2028, with scrap melting furnace by December 2027-January 2028.
Copper foil trial production targeted around March 2028 (10 KT Phase 1, 40 KT ambition under ECMS scheme); smelter, sulphuric acid plant and fertiliser balance of plant expected Q1 2029.
First copper revenue expected around end Q1 FY28 (May-June 2027); majority of copper operating revenue expected in FY30.
Management said the earlier FY28 revenue guidance of INR 20,000-25,000 crore no longer holds; the numbers are dynamic and depend on vendor timelines.
Debt repayment expected to start in 2029 given moratorium; cash flow expected to ramp stepwise over FY28-FY30.
No dividend declared; no Board decision yet, per management.
capex_capacity: Total copper project capital estimated at close to INR 12,000 crore, excluding additional infrastructure spend; outflow expected over the next two years.
Financial closure incomplete; more than 50% of debt commitments received, balance in process, with complete closure hoped within a few months.
Copper concentrate: MoUs of about 1 million tonnes secured against about 1.5 million tonnes needed at full utilisation; firm contracts typically converted around October each year.
Captive jetty (for bulk imports of copper concentrate, phosphate and ammonia), desalination facility, raw material conveying system and power infrastructure in progress; site near Pipavav Port.
MCB Copper-Gold mine: development not started; 70% off-take structured for Kiri, but Celsius is contesting the off-take in court.
demand_pricing: Reactive Dyes, Vinyl Sulphone, H-Acid and certain basic chemical prices strengthened in Q1 on tighter global supply and Chinese environmental compliance measures.
Demand is mixed across product categories; input costs rose with crude oil-linked raw materials, with pass-through supporting margins.

Management said existing H-Acid and Vinyl Sulphone capacity could drive about INR 2,000 crore of dyes revenue at 75-80% utilisation if current prices hold, versus about INR 1,200 crore cited as the current base.
Copper: management sees sales as not a constraint because India consumes about 1.8 million tonnes a year with about two-thirds imported; customer quality approvals still required.
Management said sustaining margins depends on passing through input cost movements.

qa_highlights.question: Will the earlier FY28 revenue guidance of INR 20,000-25,000 crore still hold given staggered tube and rod commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 20,000-25,000 crore FY28 figure does not hold; projections are moving with vendor delivery timelines. It added that sales are not a constraint since the output would substitute imports.

qa_highlights.question: When will copper revenue start and when will it be fully ramped?
qa_highlights.answer: First copper revenue expected around May-June 2027 (Q1 FY28), with commercial operations from Q2 FY28; majority of operating revenue expected in FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Kiri's standalone profitability low when Lonsen Kiri earns strong margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kiri supplies raw materials to the JV, which captures finished-product margins; the JV also makes products Kiri does not, so the combined value chain should be assessed. Lonsen Kiri is operated by Kiri management with no plan to replicate its products in Kiri.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to raise equity to reduce debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said equity dilution is a plan B option with investor interest tested, but the Board prefers deferred dilution after execution to capture more value. Debt repayment begins in 2029 due to moratorium.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the MCB Copper-Gold mine and the off-take?
qa_highlights.answer: Development has not started; design complete. Shareholder disputes and Celsius litigation are ongoing and sub judice, so management declined to speculate and said Kiri remains a lender.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a stake sale or MMCI interest?
qa_highlights.answer: No current talks on a 40% stake sale in Lonsen Kiri. Management said it would be 100% interested in an MMCI mine stake, subject to the litigation outcome.

538962|2026-06.headline: Minda Corporation Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR 1,846 crore (+33.2% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 212 crore at an 11.5% margin.

Management outlined five growth engines: network expansion (collection-centre-to-lab ratio from 1:24 to 1:35), TruHealth, specialty and genomics, technology/digital, and inorganic growth. 506222|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 133.9% to INR201.4 crore (26.1% margin) even as sales volume fell 26% to 38.9 KT.
506222|2026-06.overview:
Standalone total income grew 6.6% to INR770.5 crore and PAT rose 150.3% to INR137.3 crore, driven by a sharp margin jump, while volumes dropped 26% as non-OEM buyers held back amid Middle East-driven raw material price volatility. Consolidated (India plus Thailand) volume was 50.8 KT, EBITDA INR223.6 crore at 22% margin. Management described the margin gain as a snapshot of a volatile quarter, not a sustainable run rate, and gave no volume guidance. The ABS capacity expansion is said to be on track for completion in FY27 without a firm commissioning month, and Thailand volumes remain subdued.</overview>

segments.name: ABS (India)
segments.commentary: Demand fell in the quarter, with a smaller drop than polystyrene; OEM is about 70% or more of ABS sales. Management did not give a segment volume split.

guidance_outlook: No volume guidance given; management said it is 'virtually impossible' to forecast given the current environment.
Management said Q1 margins are not indicative of sustainable performance; for modelling, assume margins similar to the existing business, with the expansion adding volume.
ABS expansion (about 50,000 tonnes in the chemical plant) to be completed in FY27; exact commissioning month not given.

capex_capacity: ABS expansion is a brownfield project at a running site, so commissioning is complex; management expects completion within FY27.

Recovery of non-OEM volumes and whether destocking or channel stock effects reverse in the next nine months.
ABS expansion timing (within FY27) and execution risk on a brownfield site.
Thailand utilisation and validation progress; cost base still above India's.

qa_highlights.question: Is ordering picking up versus FY26, and what is the outlook for the Indian transmission market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ordering has picked up, bids are being finalised, and inflows should translate from Q2. It expects INR90,000-1,00,000 crore of Indian transmission bids in FY27 and said about 40% of the INR9 lakh crore pipeline has been bid so far.

qa_highlights.question: Is the finance cost decline due to the fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Fundraise funds arrived late July or early August, so Q1 had no benefit; the decline came from working capital management and operating leverage. FY27 finance cost guided at 3.2%-3.5% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is export revenue lost or delayed, and which segment drives 15% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export ordering has not stopped and export order inflow should rise more than 50% YoY. The 15% growth is expected from all three segments, with Infra growing fastest; Q1 and Q2 are seasonally slow due to monsoon, West Bengal elections, and freight disruption.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR9,200 crore order book executes by FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately INR5,000 crore is expected to execute in FY27, with short-term orders adding to this. Orders typically execute over 2 to 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Polymer revenue muted and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to commodity price volatility and trade destocking. It expects about 20% Polymer top-line growth in FY27 with margin improvement, and says growth will come from both volume and value.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited legacy low-margin contracts rolling off, better new-contract quality, operating leverage, and commodity mitigation through firm/variable price mix, inventory and hedging. It called the expansion structural and aimed toward 12% long-term margin.

qa_highlights.question: Does the delay in capacity expansion affect the 15% growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said commissioning is deferred only by a few months to end of Q2, with no impact on the 15% target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Engineering soften while Infra jumped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Engineering is affected by weak FY26 export and domestic order intake plus shipment deferrals due to high freight costs; it called this temporary. Infra growth is from TBCB transmission EPC services, with no change in scope of work.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 order inflow target, and what is the export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets INR7,000 crore-plus of FY27 order inflow, with about INR1,100 crore from exports (about 15% of inflow).

532937|2026-06.headline: Kuantum Q1 FY27 operational income rose 36% YoY to INR304 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR40 crore (13.2% margin) as input costs outran price gains.
532937|2026-06.overview: Paper sales volume grew 35% YoY to 42,922 metric tons, and blended NSR improved about INR3,400/ton QoQ. Cost per ton rose about INR4,200 QoQ on raw material, chemical and fuel inflation linked to the West Asia conflict, so EBITDA stayed broadly flat YoY and PAT was INR6 crore. Management cut its FY27 top-line expectation to INR1,300 crore-plus from the earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore and pushed the 16-18% EBITDA margin target to the year-end. PM3 rebuild completion, pulp capacity additions and anti-dumping applications were the main operational updates.

segments.name: Paper (writing & printing, copier, maplitho)
segments.commentary: Realisation around INR68,000-69,000/ton per management, targeted to reach INR72,000-75,000 in 4-6 months. Specialty grades are just under 20% of mix (18-19% stated), target 30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line revised to INR1,300 crore-plus, versus earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore guidance; management said realisations are running below earlier expected levels.
EBITDA margin at least 16-18% by year-end; management says Q3 onwards is when these margins should be visible, not Q2.
FY28 top line expected INR1,400-1,500 crore; FY29-30 conservatively INR1,500 crore at current pricing, INR1,600-1,650 crore if pricing rises to about INR75,000/ton.
Peak debt about INR760-770 crore; scheduled repayments about INR170-175 crore per year for the next 2-3 years; debt to fall below INR300-350 crore within 3 years.
AI-led opex reduction target of 4-5% by March 2028.
Pulp capacity to rise to about 410-415 TPD from 365 TPD.
capex_capacity: DDS (Double Displacement Digester) for wood pulping commissioned in Q1.
Native starch system commissioned on PM2 and PM3.
Folio ream wrapping machine installed in the finishing house.
PM3 shut for major rebuild; management expects commissioning within about a week of the call (mid-August 2026), completing the upgradation programme.
Pulping capacity of about 200 TPD each for agro and wood, said to be sufficient for all four machines.
EC clearance for PM3 upgrade filed and awaited.
Clonal propagation: record 17.28 lakh saplings in the quarter; plantation area about 19,650 acres after adding about 1,300 acres.
demand_pricing: Demand supported by education, publishing and office consumption; management expects demand to stay supportive.
Chinese imports diminishing, attributed mainly to shipping and container cost issues; imported copier/maplitho price seen at $610-620/ton near port.
Anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duty applications filed for writing and printing paper, covering 40-140 GSM; management hopes for a favourable decision, assumed 5-year duration.
Maplitho hit by inverted duty structure after GST change; management says Kuantum is reducing notebook paper exposure and passing GST losses to customers.
Management says pricing held flat QoQ into Q2 with no discounting; dealer channel inventory described as lean.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance maintained, and what EBITDA margin is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is positive with PM3 commissioning, targeting at least 16-18% EBITDA margin by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak debt and the repayment path?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt about INR760-770 crore; repayments of about INR170-175 crore a year for 2-3 years, with debt below INR300 crore within 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the revenue guidance fall from INR1,400-1,500 crore to INR1,300 crore-plus?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisations are running below earlier expected levels and EBITDA margins are strained by West Asia-driven costs; management says figures are conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall while a competitor's rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to Punjab-specific raw material cost increases, mainly wheat straw, which it says is easing; it expects a gradual reduction in procurement cost.

qa_highlights.question: What share of cost increase is due to the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of the INR4,200/ton cost increase is attributed to West Asia; INR3,400/ton has been passed through in pricing QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Will wheat straw prices come down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said procurement prices fell in Q2 versus Q1 after negotiations with suppliers, with further easing expected as rice straw and corn cobs arrive in September-October.

risks_watch: Cost pass-through: about INR800/ton of the INR4,200/ton cost rise was not recovered in Q1 price gains; watch whether Q2 NSR and margins recover.
Execution on PM3 commissioning (mid-August) and full-capacity ramp; Q2 is expected to be weak with machine and boiler shutdowns.
Revenue guidance cut and inconsistency with earlier FY28-30 projections.
Q2 seasonally weak demand; management says October onwards is when the industry picks up.
Pending EC clearance for PM3 and pending anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duty decision.
Debt of about INR760-770 crore at peak and interest burden on PAT.
532937|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term capacity and specialty mix, but defensive on the FY27 numbers: management conceded the revenue guidance was revised and that margins are being squeezed by costs outside its control. Answers on the guidance gap and FY30 targets were partly contradictory and hard to reconcile.
key_quotes: We should be reaching closer to about at least between 16% to 18% by the year-end.
Peak debt, we are currently looking at about INR760 crores or INR770 crores maximum.
Nobody could have imagined like a war starting in a part of the world and impacting sort of pricing here in India.
Right now, our contribution from specialty paper is just under 20%.

543923|2026-06.headline: IKIO Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to Rs 169 crore and EBITDA rose 94% to Rs 22 crore, but gross margin fell to about 41% on war-driven component and metal costs.
543923|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 41% YoY to Rs 169 crore, led by the other businesses (Rs 124 crore, up 53% YoY but marginally lower QoQ) while home lighting ODM reached Rs 45 crore (up 16% YoY, 18% QoQ). EBITDA rose 94% YoY to Rs 22 crore (13% margin vs 9.4%) and PAT rose to Rs 11 crore from Rs 2 crore. Management said sequential profitability was hit by higher raw material and semiconductor costs linked to the Middle East war and by higher wages after a minimum wage revision. Management kept FY27 revenue growth guidance at 18-20% and group EBITDA margin at 13-14%.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 2 crore in Q1 FY26
down from 44-45% as cited by analyst

financial_highlights.metric: Other business EBITDA margin (implied by analyst math)

segments.name: Other businesses (Lighting, Hearables & Wearables, Energy, Electronic components, Automotive lighting, non-lighting)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 124 crore, up 53% YoY; growth was broad-based across verticals except UAE/Gulf, which declined due to the war. Management said the war cost roughly Rs 10-15 crore of business in the quarter. Hearables and wearables contribute about 15-17% of total revenue.

segments.name: Home lighting ODM
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 45 crore, up 16% YoY and 18% QoQ. Customer concentration fell from about 95% from one customer to 3-4 customers. Management expects FY27 at roughly Rs 170 crore, plus or minus Rs 10-15 crore.

segments.name: Automotive lighting (aftermarket LED)
segments.commentary: Actual production began in May/June 2026 after prototyping and trials. Management says it is aligned with five industry-leading aftermarket LED brands. FY27 contribution is expected to be small.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance kept at 18-20%, as given in Q4; management will revisit by end-Q2 or Q3 if needed.
Group EBITDA margin guided at about 13-14% for FY27; management said it would be 14% or slightly better without the war.
ODM home lighting EBITDA margin expected to stay near 8.4%, give or take 0.5%, if raw material prices stay stable or fall.
Long-term feasible EBITDA margin cited at 17-18%, not the earlier 20-23%. Management targets asset turns of 4.5-5x in about 3-3.5 years.
Management expects raw material and wage pressure to normalise in coming quarters as revenue scale and operating leverage build.
Automotive OEM onboarding targeted by FY28, after aftermarket traction.
Honeywell SKUs expected to rise 3-4x by year-end.
capex_capacity: Block 1 (about 2 lakh sq ft) is operational; Block 2 (Tower-2) partially commercialised in Q2 FY27, with hearables and wearables using two floors.
Block 3 construction is on schedule; about Rs 20 crore of remaining capex is earmarked for Tower-3.
FY27 capex guided at about Rs 20-25 crore, with little left after Tower-2.
Depreciation from Tower-2 expected to start from Q2 FY27; management pointed to cash PAT for comparability.
demand_pricing: Semiconductor prices have roughly doubled in some cases, and lead times have risen from about 4-6 weeks to over a year for some electronic components, forcing spot buying and design changes.
Metals (MS, aluminium, copper) prices have been volatile over the past 4-5 months.
Management is in talks with customers on pricing to offset cost pressure.
Middle East/UAE business declined YoY due to the war, though management says IKIO is outperforming peers there and is entering the developer segment.
About 50% of hearables/wearables products are now IKIO-designed ODM products, up from job work.
Honeywell: amplifiers, PA systems and fire alarm panels are in production, with more products in the pipeline.
Solar inverter/BESS: one sizeable order completed; new products in development.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory given geopolitical and manpower headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are in line with annual guidance. Gross margin was hit by component lead times and metal and semiconductor costs, and the company is negotiating with customers. Long-term feasible EBITDA margin is 17-18%, not 20-23%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall from 44-45% to 41%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed metal price volatility and semiconductor shortages and price spikes. It redesigned products to keep specs while avoiding shortages, and said 41% is sustainable at current raw material prices unless the war escalates.

qa_highlights.question: Was the other business QoQ dip due to seasonality or the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is seasonally the leanest quarter. YoY, Q1 FY27 Rs 124 crore matched the full Q1 FY26 base of about Rs 120 crore, and the war cost an estimated Rs 10-15 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 40% growth in the home lighting ODM business and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: New customers were added and the customer base diversified from one customer to 3-4. Management expects FY27 at around Rs 170 crore, plus or minus Rs 10-15 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hearables and wearables production visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: H&W is about 15-16% of revenue now and is guided at 16-18% for FY27. Customers plan 3-6 months ahead, with 10-12 month pipeline discussions with larger customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of automotive lighting and the OEM path?
qa_highlights.answer: Aftermarket production began in May/June 2026 with five leading brands. OEM onboarding is planned for Phase 2, targeted by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will guidance be raised given stronger growth in the other business?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management kept the 18-20% FY27 growth guidance, citing volatility, and will revisit at end-Q2 or Q3.

526829|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 117% YoY to INR2,408 crore and PAT more than tripled to about INR62.6 crore, driven mainly by LPG volumes.
526829|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue (about INR2,408 crore), EBITDA (about INR147 crore) and PAT (about INR62.6 crore) for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, with basic EPS of INR1.86. Management attributed the top-line jump largely to higher LPG prices during supply disruption from West Asia, while saying volumes also rose sharply (about doubled YoY) and that a portion of the growth came from new bulk and institutional customers on short- to medium-term contracts. Auto LPG volumes slowed temporarily on higher prices and have since recovered per management. Most company-specific numbers (segment revenue split, FY26 capex, LPG import volumes, Type 4 cylinder margins) were deferred to follow-up emails.

financial_highlights.change: +117% YoY (from INR1,112 crore); +98% QoQ (from INR1,216 crore)

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR62.6 crore (management also cited exceeding INR66 crore in one remark)
financial_highlights.change: More than tripled YoY (from INR20.5 crore); +82% QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: PAT margin (analyst-cited, not confirmed by management)
financial_highlights.change: Management said margins are 'intact' and that the drop is due to higher LPG prices

segments.name: Packed LPG (GoGas)
segments.commentary: Packed LPG sales of about 18,000-20,000 MT per month; management said it is more commercial than domestic and price-competitive on commercial. Packed LPG and Auto LPG were named as the highest-EBITDA-margin segments, but no margin figures were given.

segments.name: Bulk LPG / industrial
segments.commentary: About 300 industrial customers served; new accounts added in FMCG, food processing, glass and ceramics. Management said a meaningful part of Q1 was volume-led from new bulk and institutional customers.

segments.name: Auto LPG (ALDS)
segments.commentary: 315+ dispensing stations, all operational. Demand slowed temporarily in the quarter on higher LPG prices, and management said volumes have since recovered. Payback on a new station is said to be under 18 months.

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: 50+ CNG stations completed, with a further 50 targeted in Bengaluru. Average station volume was said to be about 6,000-6,200 kg per day, and total volume about 3 lakh kg per day.

guidance_outlook: Management guided to 10-15% QoQ growth in revenue, PAT and EBITDA in coming quarters; it did not give a multi-year revenue number.
Auto LPG network target: 500 stations, with about 75 added in FY27 and about 100 in FY28, then a further evaluation toward 500.
CNG target to increase from 50 to 100 stations; talks with other CGD players for Mumbai, Hyderabad and Indore, not finalised.
Management expects margins to rise as volumes grow and once prices normalise; no bps or percentage target was given.
Backward integration is under evaluation, including small coastal storage terminals (not finalised) and a 100% Dubai subsidiary for LPG import ease.
Type 4 high-pressure cylinder unit at Butibori (Nagpur): capex complete and machinery installed; production expected in 1-2 months, subject to order book. Margin not disclosed.
capex_capacity: Type 4 high-pressure cylinder plant (Butibori): capex complete and machinery installed; start awaits order book, with production expected in 1-2 months. Target customers are CGD players, car fleet owners and OEMs.
CNG: 50+ stations operational; 50 more planned in Bengaluru.
Auto LPG: 315+ stations; target 500 (75 in FY27, 100 in FY28).

Fleet and infrastructure as stated: ships on time charter, 68+ bottling/blending plants, 478+ LPG road tankers, 225+ HCVs/LCVs, 82 CNG road vehicles, 15 cylinder plants and 3 high-pressure cylinder plants.
Total capacity was cited by an analyst as 608 TMT or 685 TMT; management did not confirm or answer on utilisation.
demand_pricing: India LPG market about 35.04 MMT, projected at about 40-42 MMT by FY2030; OMCs hold about 94% of sales and private marketers about 6%, with CPIL holding about 33% of the private segment (management claim).
During the West Asia disruption, the company diversified sourcing to North America, Africa and the Middle East, and said several marquee customers moved to longer-term contracts.
Management said Q1 revenue growth was mainly price-driven, but also volume-driven (volumes about doubled YoY per management).
Management said it is price-competitive against PSUs in industrial, HoReCa and commercial segments.
Gin Kar Lo, Gin Kar Do scheme (pay-for-actual-consumption cylinder weighing) introduced; direct financial impact not a stated objective.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Type 4 cylinder plant operational, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is complete and machinery is installed at Butibori. Production is expected within 1-2 months, but the start depends on receiving the order book. Management declined to give margin numbers until the first deliveries.

qa_highlights.question: Which cities are in CNG network talks?
qa_highlights.answer: Mumbai, Hyderabad and Indore were named, but none is finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue growth continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue, EBITDA and PAT will grow QoQ, though revenue will move with LPG prices. It later quantified 10-15% QoQ growth.

qa_highlights.question: How is the PAT margin trending and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are intact and rising, and that the lower percentage reflects higher LPG prices. It gave no quantified margin target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 growth came from the West Asia disruption, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company had inventory when PSUs faced constraints, and that new customers signed longer-term agreements. Management said volumes are sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation priority (organic, M&A, debt, dividends)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of new stations, JVs and acquiring infrastructure, plus bottling expansion and backward integration. No allocation split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging of LPG import currency exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payments are made on time and spot contracts are used, so no hedge is currently required; it would hedge in future if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BW exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BW, a strategic investor from 2023-24, exited in the secondary market to focus on its shipping business, with no impact on the company.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Income Tax search?
qa_highlights.answer: The search began 7 October 2025 and closed within 7 days. Assessment is open, no final demand has been received, and management does not expect a large payable.

qa_highlights.question: Break-up of revenue by segment, FY26 capex, and LPG import data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred these to follow-up emails and gave no figures on the call.

544067|2026-06.headline: Innova Captab Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY to INR470.9 crores, with EBITDA up 33% to INR75.1 crores at a 16% margin.
544067|2026-06.overview:
Revenue grew 34% YoY to INR470.9 crores, with CDMO at INR328.7 crores (+32%) and branded generics at INR142.2 crores (+39%). EBITDA was INR75.1 crores (16% margin, +33%) and PAT was INR44.1 crores (+42%). Management said volume growth was 20-22% and the rest of growth came from mix and pricing. Jammu turned EBITDA-positive at roughly INR1-1.5 crores on about INR107 crores of quarterly revenue, up from about INR90 crores in the prior quarter.</overview>

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin profile sustainable ex-Jammu?

qa_highlights.question: What are the maintenance and growth capex numbers for FY27 and FY28?

540025|2026-06.headline: Advanced Enzyme Q1 FY27 revenue rose 2% YoY to INR 1,898 million, but EBITDA fell 10% to INR 510 million as margin dropped to 27%.
540025|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue of INR 1,898 million grew 2% YoY but fell 7% QoQ, held back by an extra INR 100 million sales reversal for export shipments still in transit. EBITDA declined 10% YoY and 19% QoQ to INR 510 million, with margin at 27% versus 30% a year ago, attributed to lower realisation, higher power and fuel costs, and a sales-mix shift. 539300|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 120.64% YoY to INR276.33 crores, but EBITDA margin compressed to 8.18% on raw-material and crude-linked cost pressure.
539300|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR276.33 crores, up 120.64% YoY and 39.85% QoQ, with PAT of INR15.04 crores (up 130.67% YoY). EBITDA rose 94.41% YoY to INR22.59 crores, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 8.18% from 9.28% a year earlier and 10.19% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the margin squeeze to dyes, chemicals, boiler fuel, LABSA and PP packaging costs linked to geopolitical crude volatility, which hit the textile business hardest. Installed FMCG and FMCG-intermediate capacity rose to 20,840 tons per month after a 1,700 MT soap line was commissioned at Roorkee. Management guides FY27 revenue of INR900-1,000 crores and a ~6% profitability level, with a further 0.75-1% improvement in FY28.

financial_highlights.change: +120.64% YoY vs INR125.24 crores; +39.85% QoQ vs INR197.59 crores

financial_highlights.metric: FMCG + FMCG intermediate share of consolidated revenue

segments.name: Roorkee facility
segments.commentary: Soap INR27.50 crores (vs INR17.63 crores in Q4 FY26) and noodles INR87.62 crores (vs INR44.47 crores in Q4 FY26).

segments.name: Bhilwara facility
segments.commentary: Home care and detergent INR40.98 crores (vs INR32.50 crores in Q4 FY26); edible INR30.34 crores (vs INR29.26 crores).

segments.name: Guwahati facility
segments.commentary: Cosmetics INR26.15 crores (vs INR20.91 crores in Q4 FY26); noodles INR37.75 crores (vs INR26.01 crores).

segments.name: Textile
segments.commentary: Management said textile revenue was roughly flat and margins were hit hardest by dye, chemical and fuel costs; no price increase could be passed through in the quarter. Long-run textile share guided at 8-10% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected in INR900-1,000 crores; FY28 growth of 15-20% over FY27 cited, with the INR1,000 crores target for FY28 reiterated.
FY27 profitability expected around 6%, improving by 0.75-1% in FY28; a separate remark targets 7% by FY28 with EBITDA margin up another 2-2.5%.
Management expects raw-material cost pressure to normalise by Q3 or Q4 FY27; textile expected to turn good by Q3 FY27.
Near-term priority: neutralise the Q1 cost increase over the next two to three quarters and raise utilisation of recently added capacity over three to four quarters.
Long-run revenue mix: textile 8-10%, FMCG 90-92%.
capex_capacity: Roorkee soap line commissioned in Q1 FY27 adds ~1,700 MT per month; aggregate FMCG and FMCG-intermediate capacity is 20,840 TPM (from 19,640 TPM at Q4 FY26).
Utilisation is currently ~50-55%; management expects another 25-30% utilisation gain by FY28.
Little further capacity addition expected over the next one to one-and-a-half years; only balancing capex is planned.
Bhilwara spices and savories plant runs one shift; second shift is free for expansion.
Management says existing capacity is enough to reach the INR1,000 crores FY28 revenue target without new capex.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth attributed to newly acquired units and new soap and FMCG capacity added in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27, with customer base added during the quarter.
Business is B2B only; no B2C revenue. Over 200 customers, with quarterly planning forecasts and firm monthly orders.
Textile could not pass on dye, chemical and fuel cost increases in Q1; PP packaging prices spiked with geopolitical tension.
Spice margins described as lower and savory margins as higher.
Management expects revenue growth to come mainly from food and soap segments over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: How did raw-material and crude-linked costs behave in the quarter and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Dyes, chemicals, consumables, boiler fuel and LABSA rose; PP packaging spiked. Textile prices could not be raised in Q1; management expects normalisation by Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 revenue and profit outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue INR900-1,000 crores, FY28 growth 15-20%; FY27 profitability about 6%, rising 0.75-1% in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation at 50-55%; another 25-30% expected by FY28; little new capex needed for one to one-and-a-half years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the raised funds went to Roorkee, and is further fundraising planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Roorkee capacity was funded from the subsidiary's retained earnings. INR98.65 crores raised was used for Bhilwara food and Guwahati soap/noodle/cosmetics facilities, not for Sunrakshakk Agro acquisition, which predated the raise. No further fundraising is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Will textile continue or be demerged?
qa_highlights.answer: No demerger plans; textile is expected to improve by Q3 FY27 after a weak Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What are the next two to three quarter milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Offset the Q1 cost increase and raise utilisation of recently added capacity over three to four quarters.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 8.18% from 10.19% QoQ; recovery depends on input costs normalising by Q3 or Q4 FY27, which management itself flagged as uncertain given renewed pressure in Q2.
Utilisation of 50-55% versus the FY28 target rests on volume ramp; the INR1,000 crore target relies on existing capacity alone.
Textile profitability is weak; management expects a turnaround by Q3 FY27 but has not quantified it.
Working capital is described as balanced but management gave no specific target or days figure.
Some inconsistencies in the call: the FY28 margin guidance was given as +0.75-1% and, separately, as a 7% target with +2-2.5% EBITDA margin; the FMCG share was quoted as 90.60% and 90-91%.
539300|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and capacity, with a clear focus on profitability recovery. Answers were often vague or repetitive on cost and margin specifics, and the management struggled with several individual investor questions on audibility and wording.

540902|2026-06.headline: Amber Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA 28% to INR337 crore, with Electronics EBITDA more than doubling.
540902|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA grew 28% to INR337 crore, with adjusted PAT of INR126 crore (up 19%) before a INR123 crore exceptional loss. Electronics was the standout, with revenue up 29% and EBITDA more than doubling to a 10.8% margin. Railway & Defense EBITDA fell 26% on mix, copper, currency and Haryana minimum wage hikes. Management flagged that PCB margins were compressed by a roughly two-quarter pass-through lag and that cost pressure persists through H1, while Q1 benefited from pre-stocking of compressors and copper. The IL JIN facility incident was a new overhang, with insurance cover and the impact still being assessed.</overview>

Order book stood at INR 1,801 crore as of 30 June 2026, and FY27 guidance of 20-25% revenue growth and 12-14% EBITDA margin was reiterated. capex_capacity: Q1 FY27: one hub and three spoke centres commissioned; July-August added two hubs and three spokes; network at 72 centres at quarter end.
Hub capex about Rs 10-10.5 crore; spoke capex about Rs 1.5-2 crore; spoke centre-level breakeven 3-4 months, HO-level breakeven 8-9 months.
Genexus rapid genome sequencer acquired, in final validation; turnaround for oncology genomic study cut from 14-17 days to 48 hours.
No major additional genomics capex expected in next 2-3 years per CSO.

Kolkata proper: 5 hubs and 6 spokes, with room for 3 more hubs and at least 6 spokes; Greater Kolkata has 9 hubs with scope to double. Jharkhand hub commissioned, another planned with 5 spokes; Assam hub operating with spoke commissioned and another under construction; Agartala (Tripura) hub to follow.
demand_pricing: Like-for-like mature centre revenue growth about 12% YoY; test volume growth about 10-11%; growth attributed to test mix change, with no price increases taken per management.
Patient footfall for consultation up about 11% YoY in June 2026; patient volume up 12.4% QoQ per management.
Repeat patient share down to about 40% (from 52% in FY22-23), which management attributed to new patient additions from expansion, not absolute decline.
B2B carries a margin challenge but volume offsets it; B2C seen as margin-stable with no deep discounting.
Franchisee-run collection centres number 214; these are used as feeder points before spokes are opened.
Organised share of diagnostics in East India is lower than the national 15-20%; Suraksha claimed to be the largest organised player in the region.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ~400 bps margin expansion and can margins reach 33-34% by FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage as revenue scales against largely fixed costs; management said it expects margins to be higher than 33-34% by FY29 and that mature-centre margins are sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA margin outlook given the seasonal pattern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said overall EBITDA will not go below 34% for the year, with Q2 and Q4 strong and Q3 muted.

qa_highlights.question: Why has test volume growth slowed to about 10-11% from around 20% in prior quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was nothing specific and that the company would evaluate it; it did not give a reason.

qa_highlights.question: What is the genomics market size and B2B/B2C split?
qa_highlights.answer: Split is 80% B2C and 20% B2B, with B2B expected to grow as a share. Indian genomics market cited at about Rs 450 million by 2030 (figure as stated; unit unclear). Average realisation not given, since genomic test prices range from Rs 4,000-5,000 to over Rs 50,000.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ROCE/ROE below national peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the young centre base (27 of 45 mature centres under 2 years old); lower only against three or four players.

qa_highlights.question: Are franchisee collection centres affected by new spokes?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; when a collection centre area proves strong, a spoke is opened and the franchisee is relocated to a further location.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 revenue guidance only 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: CSO said the company has been conservative as it is a relatively new organisation; no dearth of effort.

530305|2026-06.headline: Piccadily Q1 FY27 revenue rose 8.1% to Rs 270 crore (distillery +26.3%), while branded alco-bev grew 47.3% to Rs 82.3 crore.
530305|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose to about Rs 270.5 crore and EBITDA to Rs 47.2 crore, with margin up 30 bps to 18.5%. PAT grew 15.4% to about Rs 22 crore and EPS to Rs 2.21. Premium, super premium and luxury brands reached 43.5% of distillery revenue versus 37.8% a year earlier. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 60% company revenue growth, 60-70% branded alco-bev growth and a 23-24% EBITDA margin, with most revenue expected in H2. Chhattisgarh distillery contributed only about Rs 5 crore from roughly 15 days of production.

financial_highlights.change: +8.1% YoY as stated in prepared remarks (CFO said 18.1%)

financial_highlights.metric: Branded alco-bev (premium, super premium, luxury) revenue
Share of branded in distillery revenue

financial_highlights.change: vs about Rs 87 lakh last quarter; mainly FX gain and scrap sale

segments.name: Distillery (total)
segments.commentary: Rs 205.7 crore revenue, 76% of total revenue (71% a year earlier). Segment margin fell YoY, which management attributed to cost pressure on grain and fuel and to mix shift toward lower-margin Whistler.

segments.name: Branded alco-bev (IMFL)
segments.commentary: Rs 82.3 crore, +47.3% YoY. Indri grew high double digits; Whistler grew more than 60% in the quarter; Camikara entered CSD and began contributing.

segments.name: Chhattisgarh distillery
segments.commentary: Commissioned, with about 15 days of production in Q1 and roughly Rs 5 crore revenue. Capacity is 210 KLPD; utilisation targeted at about 50% by year-end.

segments.name: Sugar division
segments.commentary: Demerger scheme filed with exchanges on 28 April 2026; process ongoing. Management expects the hive-off by year-end; company-level margin guidance includes sugar.

guidance_outlook: Branded alco-bev revenue to grow about 60-70% in FY27; H2 expected to contribute about 60-65% of annual branded revenue.
Company-level revenue growth target of about 60% YoY for FY27.
Company-level EBITDA margin of 23-24% for FY27 (includes sugar); management said full-year margin should be similar to or slightly better than FY26's 23%.
Chhattisgarh revenue guidance of Rs 300-400 crore for FY27 reiterated; Indri incremental sales guidance of Rs 250-300 crore reiterated.
Barrel inventory expected at 1.15-1.20 lakh barrels by March 2027, above the 1 lakh target.
No large capex planned for FY27 beyond ordinary-course upgrades; company does not plan to increase debt this year.
capex_capacity: Chhattisgarh distillery commissioned; about 15 days of production in Q1 and first revenue in June 2026. Capacity 210 KLPD; utilisation targeted at about 50% by March 2027.
Indri distillery expansion running at about 60% utilisation.
Malt capacity added last year (30 KL) running at about 80%.
Barrel inventory of 87,000 filled barrels (200-500 litre sizes); about 60-70 lakh litres added each year.
Management stated the company is not planning large capex this year; most heavy capex is complete.
demand_pricing: Indri growing 18-20% YoY, which management described as the only single malt growing at that pace; global single malts are growing 2-3%.
Whistler grew almost 100% last year and more than 60% this quarter; Camikara and Cashmir expected to grow in triple digits this year from a small base.
Management says it will not disclose individual brand margins and speaks only at portfolio level.
Ethanol margin about 10%; country liquor margin about 15-18%; management said branded margins are not under pressure, while distillery ex-branded faces price pressure from grain and fuel costs.
Receivables: branded receivables about Rs 170 crore (incl. excise), receivable days about 100 versus higher in March after a Rs 100 crore March sales spike.
Exports about 25% of sales; management targets a long-term 70% export / 30% domestic mix; North America is the largest export market; exports to 31 countries.
A court order in Chennai halted ethanol plants; management expects orders to resume in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 47.3% branded growth and what is the Chhattisgarh contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Indri grew high double digits, Whistler more than 60%, and Camikara began contributing via CSD. Chhattisgarh contributed about Rs 5 crore from roughly 15 days of production.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin rise only 30 bps and how are costs trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to mix, with Indri the highest-margin product. Cost pressure from grain and fuel hit the distillery segment. Employee, distribution and brand investment costs rose ahead of H2 revenue, and management expects margins to recover as revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: Is there enough aged malt to support Indri growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. The company holds 87,000 filled barrels, which management called the largest in India, and sees no supply constraint for 18-20% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Indri scale ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to reach top-five single malt volumes of about 0.5 million cases in 4-5 years, implying about Rs 1,200 crore Indri revenue at current prices. Current capacity supports about 8-8.5 lakh cases if all malt went to Indri.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Chhattisgarh ethanol exposure a guidance risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 300-400 crore guidance is intact and that ethanol is a stopgap; the company plans branded products from Chhattisgarh. It declined to split ethanol and alco-bev revenue until Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will debt fall and what is the working capital position?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 10 crore of debt was repaid in Q1. Management plans no net debt increase this year, with larger reductions from FY28 after investment in liquid and barrels. Receivable days fell to about 100.

524342|2026-06.headline: Indo Borax Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31.3% to Rs 70.36 crore and PAT rose 59.3% to Rs 16.25 crore, but management guided Q2 to be softer.
524342|2026-06.overview:
Operating revenue was Rs 70.36 crore (+31.34% YoY) with EBITDA of Rs 19.8 crore (+62.16%) at a 28.1% margin and PAT of Rs 16.25 crore (+59.31%) at a 22.3% margin, with EPS of Rs 5.07. Management attributed the quarter to improved capacity utilisation, higher realisations and new leadership after the Zenrock promoter change. The call was dominated by the proposed acquisition of a 64.26% stake in Kronox Lab Sciences from its promoters for about Rs 250 crore, funded partly by internal accruals, asset sales and a term loan. Management said Q2 margins will fall versus Q1 because of raw material inflation from the war and the monsoon-weak quarter, and reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs 250-260 crore revenue at about 20% EBITDA margin.</overview>
