segments.name: Boric acid (technical and IP grade)
segments.commentary: Management says about 80% of revenue comes from boric acid; IP grade is 7-8% of boric acid volume (about 100 tonnes vs 1,500 tonnes technical, per the speaker). Capacity utilisation expected at 96-98% of practical capacity, with output rising to about 18,000 tonnes this year from 15,917 tonnes last year.

segments.name: DOT (Disodium Octaborate Tetrahydrate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume about 900 tonnes; FY27 target 1,500 tonnes against 6,000 tonnes nameplate. Contributes about 9% of revenue this year vs 7% last year. Margin expected broadly in line with boric acid.

segments.name: Kronox Lab Sciences (proposed acquisition)
segments.commentary: Vadodara-based listed specialty chemicals company with 185 products across excipients, reagents, API and nutraceuticals. Dahej expansion of Rs 110 crore planned in phases over 18-24 months, with benefits from FY29 and full impact in FY30-31; management expects 3-3.5x current revenue post-capex.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance Rs 250-260 crore vs Rs 215 crore in FY26, with EBITDA margin about 20% and absolute EBITDA growth of about 11-12%.
Q2 expected to be softer on monsoon-weak volumes and raw material inflation from the ongoing war; margins not expected to match Q1's 28.1%.
Q3 expected to pick up again.
Boron oxide and boric acid capacity additions planned; management expects these to lift margins in FY28.
Capex of about Rs 50 crore over the next two to three years (Boron oxide about Rs 20 crore, boric acid Rs 20-25 crore, plus contingency); the Rs 50 crore figure is a business-plan rounding.
capex_capacity: Nameplate capacity about 26,000 tonnes per year at Pithampur: about 20,000 tpa boric acid and 6,000 tpa DOT.
Practical output expected at about 18,000 tonnes this year vs 15,917 tonnes last year, after planned maintenance days.
Boron oxide capex about Rs 20 crore; boric acid capex Rs 20-25 crore, with plant size flexible between 5,000 and 20,000 tpa.
Kronox Dahej expansion of Rs 110 crore in phases: first phase about Rs 55-60 crore; benefits from FY29, full impact FY30-31; execution 18-24 months.
Management says there is capacity upside of 15-20% at existing Indo Borax plants through process changes.
demand_pricing: Indian boric acid market estimated at about 40,000 tpa, projected to grow about 8% CAGR to about 53,000 tpa by 2030; steel and refractory is 55-60% of demand.

Boric acid prices moved from about Rs 127/kg early in FY27 to about Rs 155-160/kg, per management, as costs rose during the war; some pass-through still pending and spot prices were soft in Q2 seasonally.
Management says Indo Borax prices at a premium to market (market plus), citing specifications.
DOT: management cites about 8,500 tonnes of imports and about 10,000 tonnes total market; Indo Borax targets 1,500 tonnes.
Kronox's Indian market growing about 11% CAGR per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Kronox's previous promoter exit, and what is the status of the Dahej capex delayed by environmental clearances?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on the promoter's reasons. It said the Dahej land and design are ready, audits and studies are complete, and customers have been approached; the capex is to be executed as a first priority once the deal closes.

qa_highlights.question: Is Kronox to be merged into Indo Borax, and what is the group acquisition strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: No decision yet on merger; both entities will continue as separate listed companies for now. Future acquisitions by Zenrock will be evaluated case by case; Indo Borax will focus on integration.

qa_highlights.question: How will the acquisition be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 250 crore to promoters. Rs 134-135 crore from internal accruals plus Rs 48-50 crore from sale of two Mumbai office properties. A term loan is expected in a couple of weeks to fund the open offer (Rs 151 crore) and the remaining gap. Promoter group committed Rs 25 crore contingency; total funding Rs 432 crore vs about Rs 400 crore required.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 50 crore capex plan consistent with the individual product items?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed: Boron oxide about Rs 20 crore and boric acid Rs 20-25 crore total about Rs 45 crore, rounded to Rs 50 crore including inflation and contingency.

qa_highlights.question: Will the open offer be tendered, and when does control transfer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not wait for the open offer to complete; it is using the expedited SEBI route to take control, with the open offer running in parallel. The SEBI holding period currently applies.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for unpledging Indo Borax shares pledged for the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific timeline; the pledge is standard for acquisition financing and is a work in progress.

534139|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 order intake hit a record INR 915 crore (+0.5% YoY, double-digit QoQ) but EBIT fell to INR 32 crore on gross margin pressure and negative operating leverage.
534139|2026-06.overview: Management reported a record quarterly order booking of INR 915 crore, with sales growing about 5% YoY in a seasonally soft Q1 and an order backlog of about INR 2,100 crore entering Q2, up around 33%. EBIT was INR 32 crore, lower than last year, as commodity inflation (copper, aluminium, steel, transformer wire) and legacy fixed-price contracts compressed gross margin, while employee and other costs rose faster than sales. Management attributed the margin dip largely to Q1 operating leverage and FX-driven import costs, and said pricing actions are underway but will take time to flow through. No numerical guidance was given; management said the balance three quarters should be good.

financial_highlights.change: +0.5% YoY; double-digit QoQ growth; highest-ever quarterly order booking
Dipped YoY due to commodity inflation and legacy fixed-price orders
Flat QoQ; YoY increase due to non-cash fair-value accounting gain in last year's Q1
Management cited ~1.9% figure tied to GM pressure and negative operating leverage

segments.name: Power & Grid
segments.commentary: Management said legacy margin pressure is concentrated in Power & Grid, where orders booked before December 2025 carry firm prices; secondary distribution equipment and transformers are mainly Power & Grid products.

segments.name: Emerging segments (data centres, semiconductors)
segments.commentary: Management said more than one-fifth of the order bank now comes from emerging segments; a semiconductor transformer order was described as the largest front-end fab order received, and a data-centre MV panel order was also won.

segments.name: Metals & Mining
segments.commentary: Management said traction is being seen with a healthy pipeline in the MMM segment, without quantification.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue is 10-12% of revenue; the new Kolkata plant is expected to cater to exports, which are only starting to ramp.

guidance_outlook: No numerical revenue or margin guidance given; management declined to give forward-looking figures for Q2 or FY27.
Management said Q2 is expected to do better than Q1 historically, and that the forward-looking three quarters are good for the company.
Pricing actions have been initiated across standard price-list products but will take time to fructify.
Capacity expansions across the Baroda medium-voltage plant, Baroda transformer plant and Kolkata plant are on track, with some completing in calendar 2027 and some in 2028, followed by ramp-up.
Management expects the commodity tailwinds to moderate and margin headwinds to iron out over time.
capex_capacity: Roughly INR 500 crore of capex deployed over the last three years across the company's three plants, aimed at capacity additions and cutting imports from other Schneider factories.
Kolkata plant began capitalisation and operations early in FY27; depreciation is rising and is expected to be accelerated by plant growth.
Multiple capex programmes (Baroda MV factory, Baroda transformer factory, Kolkata plant) have staggered completion timelines and ramp-up plans, all tracking to plan per management.
Company said it is aligned with government capex, including RDSS of about INR 3,00,000 crore, to address secondary distribution and transformer demand.
demand_pricing: Order intake of INR 915 crore was a record quarterly figure; management said Q1 order timing included spillover of 15-20% at times, varying quarter to quarter.
Commodity inflation (copper, aluminium, steel, labour) and INR depreciation of about 8% YTD are the key headwinds cited.
Legacy contracts booked before December 2025 are largely fixed-price; the company cannot always revise prices, hitting gross margin, mostly in Power & Grid.

Price variation clauses cover about 20-25% of the backlog, mainly large execution cycle projects over 6 months to 1 year; mandatory PVC is now being put into new contracts, but not in government tenders.
Imports are 10-15% of COGS, roughly matched by export revenue, providing a natural FX hedge.
Management said pipeline for Power & Grid is healthy, including private utility inquiries, and expects both volume growth and price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin miss driven by lack of operating leverage, and what is the outlook for other expenses growth of ~20% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q1 squeeze is a normal Q1 effect of annual salary increments and cost inflation from 1 April, combined with moderate sales growth of ~5%. Other expenses rose on FX and an 8-10% regular cost inflation; management expects it to even out over the year.

qa_highlights.question: Will you quantify FY27 revenue expectations given the backlog growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers; said Q2 historically does better than Q1 and that the remaining three quarters look good, and that pricing actions are underway.

qa_highlights.question: Are legacy orders (pre-December) hurting margins, and how much of the backlog has price variation protection?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-December orders are largely firm-price; about 20-25% of backlog has price variation clauses; new contracts now carry mandatory PVC except in government tenders where bids are price-fixed with validity.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 order growth is fresh versus spillover from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said spillover from March into April is normal, sometimes 15-20%, sometimes less; it could not quantify it precisely.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export share and medium-term target?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are 10-12% of revenue; management declined to give a percentage target but said absolute export value will rise with the Kolkata plant.

qa_highlights.question: What is the addressable distribution (DISCOM) capex TAM and how selective are you?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is selective, bidding only on strategic accounts with visible sites and lower execution ambiguity; it avoids underground cabling and substation civil work and focuses on equipment and grid modernisation within RDSS.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on pricing actions taking hold and commodity costs stabilising; no quantified price increase was disclosed.
Legacy fixed-price contracts (pre-December 2025) and government tenders without price variation clauses keep margin exposed to commodity and FX moves.
Execution delays on customer projects could again hit gross margin, per management.
Rising INR depreciation (about 8% YTD) affects imported components and FX-linked other expenses.
Next quarter to monitor: EBIT recovery vs Rs 32 crore base, transactional vs systems revenue mix (management to provide from next quarter), and new capacity commissioning in Baroda and Kolkata.
534139|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and the pipeline but cautious and somewhat evasive on margins and FY27 numbers; management repeatedly declined to quantify price increases, Q2 outlook or TAM and attributed the Q1 margin miss mainly to timing and external factors.

544124|2026-06.headline: Vibhor Steel guides ~20% Q1 revenue growth, driven by Jharsuguda; Q1 pipe dispatch only 1,500 t against 1,800 t pipe order book.
544124|2026-06.overview:
Management said Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 20% YoY, with growth coming almost entirely from the Jharsuguda (Odisha) plant, while Mumbai and Hyderabad were broadly flat versus last year. Order books for pipe, crash barrier, transmission line towers (TLT) and poles were described as well above normal, but the second galvanizing tank at Jharsuguda (expected around 1 September) is the binding constraint. Management said new-product contribution would start in Q2 and smooth out in Q3 and Q4. Figures on EBITDA, PAT and margins were not quantified in the call; the company also said it is planning a North India plant via a newly incorporated subsidiary, starting with crash barrier.</overview>

segments.name: Pipe (ERW black/galvanized)
segments.commentary: 83% of revenue. Jharsuguda pipe order book 1,800 t vs ~1,500 t dispatched in Q1; Mumbai order book 6,500 t (1,000 t on hold, ~5,000 t sold); Hyderabad pipe/galv orders ~2,000 t vs 1,000-1,200 t historical average.

segments.name: Crash barrier / highway guardrail
segments.commentary: 12% of revenue. Jharsuguda order book ~600 t and Hyderabad ~850-1,000 t; Jharsuguda crash barrier line is at maximum installed capacity, with another crash barrier line being installed.

segments.name: Transmission line towers (TLT)
segments.commentary: Order book ~2,000 t (MP ~1,500 t, Chhattisgarh 200-250 t, Maharashtra 50-60 t, plus Sikkim, Chennai). Installed capacity ~600-700 t/month; dispatch of 300-400 t expected in the current month. Power Grid approval (~2 months) pending.

segments.commentary: Order book ~250 t, equal to ~75-80% of pole installed capacity of 300 t/month. Last 3 months' max sales 80 t; targets 100 t this month, 200 t next month, 300 t by October.

segments.commentary: RSJ pole first order ~500 t, processed as job work with ~Rs 1 crore revenue; Monopole certification pending, expected Q3. Monopole has highest margin per management.

Second galvanizing tank at Jharsuguda expected to be operational around 1 September; management said it would add at least 1,000-1,500 t of galvanizing capacity and roughly Rs 100-150 crore of revenue (rough estimate, as stated).
Growth from new products expected to start in Q2 and smooth out in Q3 and Q4.
North India plant: land purchase in talks; new subsidiary created for the plant, first phase crash barrier; management did not give capex amount or commissioning date.

North India plant under planning via new subsidiary; land purchase under discussion, not finalised.

Pipe orders arriving at ~100 t/day in Mumbai per management; dealer-MOU based allocation prioritised over end users.

544860|2026-06.headline: Ardee Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.2% YoY to Rs 338.8 crore, but EBITDA was flat at Rs 33.8 crore and margin fell to 10%.
544860|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 35.2% YoY to Rs 338.8 crore on 17,645 MT sales volume, with PAT up 6% YoY to Rs 19.9 crore. EBITDA was flat at Rs 33.8 crore, with margin at 10% versus about 13% in FY26, attributed to higher domestic raw material and petroleum input costs and freight/supply-chain disruption linked to geopolitical issues. Installed capacity rose 50.9% to 156,950 MTPA effective 29 May 2026 via a brownfield debottlenecking of the existing refining unit (about Rs 15 crore capex). Management guided FY27 top-line growth of 10-20%, volume-driven, and EBITDA margin around 10%.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 38,000 in Q4 FY26 and Rs 36,000 in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,167.7 crore / Rs 147.1 crore / Rs 84.7 crore
Long-term debt about Rs 20 crore (created 14 Aug); working capital limits almost unutilised; about Rs 150 crore FDR

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: 61.3% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management says domestic scrap procurement is costlier than imports and faces availability, pricing and GST issues from unorganised sources.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 38.7% of Q1 FY27 revenue; exports rose from about Rs 81.6 crore in FY24 to Rs 465 crore in FY26 across eight countries. Management says export margins are better after incentives and drawbacks, with working capital the same.

segments.name: Lead alloys
segments.commentary: Growing about 30-35% per management; ramp-up is slow due to OEM approvals.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at 10-20%, entirely volume-driven with no metal price contribution; volume target about 85,000 tons vs about 70,000 tons in FY26.
EBITDA margin guided at around 10% for the full year given the geopolitical situation; management said higher margins are possible only if conditions improve.
Plant utilisation expected to be below the 70-75% optimum range in FY27, with the full 70-75% level now expected to spill into FY28.
Working capital guided at 90-100 days; gross working capital requirement for FY27 above Rs 400 crore, of which about Rs 220 crore funded from IPO proceeds.
Management expects return ratios to fall after the equity raise but to stay above 20% in coming years.
EBITDA per ton of about Rs 19,000 seen as fair if raw material costs stay at current levels; management expects a recovery to Rs 20,000-21,000 if the market normalises.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity raised 50.9% to 156,950 MTPA from 104,025 MTPA, effective 29 May 2026, via brownfield debottlenecking of refining capacity in the existing Naidupeta plant at about Rs 15 crore.

Acquired and handed over a 5.56-acre land parcel at Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh, for medium- to long-term expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross profit and EBITDA per ton fall versus Q4 and Q1 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher costs for domestically procured raw material and petroleum-based inputs, plus freight and supply-chain disruption; management expects a recovery if the market improves.

Acquired business margins expected to converge toward the group's original margin profile over 4 to 8 quarters through integration and synergies.
Open-market buyback of INR 106 crore, maximum price INR 478.50, expected to open the week after the call; promoters not participating.
capex_capacity: Acquired 51% stake in an entity (A P Securitas referenced) roughly 20% of SIS's size; remaining 49% to be acquired over the next couple of years, with anniversary in 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Are India margins sustainable and what is the target?

Integration of the acquired 51% stake, which runs at lower margin than the core security business.
Smaller-operator cost arbitrage narrowing under the new principal-employer rules is management's view; its actual effect on share and pricing is not yet evident.

544839|2026-06.headline: Lohia Corp Q1 FY27 revenue rose 60% YoY to INR503 crore, EBITDA margin 19.9% and order book about INR1,778 crore.
544839|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR503 crore versus INR315 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR100 crore (19.9% margin vs 11.5%) and PAT of INR66 crore (13% margin). Management attributed margin expansion to higher volumes, operating leverage and efficiencies, and said it targets about 20% EBITDA margin internally without formal guidance. The order book reached about INR1,778-1,780 crore, up 30% since March 2026 and 195% since June 2025, with about 20% backed by customer advances. Domestic demand now drives the order book, while management expects exports to recover to around 50% of revenue. This was the company's first earnings call after listing.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR17 crore in Q1 FY26; PAT margin 13%

segments.name: Machinery (woven plastic / technical textiles)
segments.commentary: Core business, estimated at 80-85% of revenue. Order book is about INR1,780 crore with about 20% customer advances, and execution quoted at 6-9 months.

segments.name: Spare parts
segments.commentary: Approx. 10-12% of revenue. Management said spare-parts gross margins run 2-3 percentage points above machinery.

segments.name: New initiatives (recycling, monofilament)
segments.commentary: Approx. 5-6% of revenue. Polyolefin recycling only; no polyester recycling yet. Shredding and granulating adjacencies under evaluation.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Domestic approx. 59% and exports approx. 41% of Q1 revenue. Export prices are said to be 10-15% above domestic, net of CIF freight and agency costs.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth of 20-25% (no EBITDA guidance given).
Internal EBITDA margin target is about 20%, described as the new normal; management said it will not formally guide on EBITDA.
Capacity is adequate for about INR2,400-2,500 crore turnover. Beyond that, roughly INR80-100 crore capex per INR500 crore of incremental turnover is needed.
Exports are expected to stabilise at around 50% of revenue and order book over time.
R&D spend is expected to average about 3% of revenue going forward.
capex_capacity: Current utilisation stated at about 70-75%; management said peak achievable is about 80-85% across tape extrusion, circular looms and winders.
Maintenance capex and machine balancing continue each year; major capex not yet planned.
Asset turnover of 3-4x; new capacity could go live in 5-6 months, since land is available adjacent to the Kanpur plant.
New products launched: CoEx 1600 multi-layer coating line, Nova 6 Plus six-shuttle circular loom (up to 1,150 picks/min), FIBC cutting and back-cutting machines.
Virtual remote assistance centre set up at Kanpur; TTRC launched a 3-month certification programme for block bottom bag machines.
demand_pricing: Order book is driven mainly by domestic investment; management expects exports to recover to about 50% of revenue and order book.
Conversion of inquiries to executable orders is about 10-15%, over 2-3 years, per management. The current pipeline figure was not disclosed.
Management said Lohia commands 15-20% price premium over Chinese competitors; export competition in Southeast Asia is mainly from Chinese players, and in developed markets mainly from Starlinger.
Margin defence rests on three levers: repricing new orders to current input costs, short- and medium-term supplier contracts, and discount structure tweaks.
Replacement demand is about 3-5% of the order book today and is expected to rise, given 20-25 year machine life.
Management said the tariff does not affect the company directly, as machinery goes mainly to developing countries; customers export fabric to the US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book rise so steeply from FY24 to about INR1,800 crore, and is this a peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to post-COVID capex recovery, growing non-packaging applications, and single-use plastic bans driving new uses. It said the peak has not yet been reached.

qa_highlights.question: Will exports recover to 40-50% of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export share ranged 45-55% of revenue historically and expects it to stabilise around 50%, though domestic currently leads the order book.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 20% EBITDA margin be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pre-COVID margins were 15-20%, Q1 and Q4 FY26 reached about 20%, and 20% is the new normal internally. It gave no formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue is implied for FY27 from the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: An analyst suggested INR2,150-2,200 crore; Raj Kumar Lohia said 'should be like that', without confirming the figure.

qa_highlights.question: How much did service and spares contribute, and at what margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Spares are about 10-12% of revenue, with gross margins 2-3 points above machinery. Consumable parts run about 2-3% of installed plant value each year, perpetually.

qa_highlights.question: What is the execution cycle for new orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 6-9 months, depending on product complexity. Legacy products can be delivered faster and newer, more complex products take longer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D plan and are there hero products?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is about 3% of revenue and expected to stay around 3%. Confidential automation and IoT technologies are in development, but no launch dates were given.

qa_highlights.question: Are any regulations benefiting Lohia against Chinese competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only customs duty on Chinese and European equipment helps. No BIS or other regulatory benefit was identified.

risks_watch: Raw material and component cost volatility; management said it does not hedge purchases through long-term fixed-price contracts with large steel suppliers.
Margin dilution as domestic mix rises during FY27, since export pricing is 10-15% higher; management says margins will be protected.
Chinese competition, particularly in Southeast Asia, where rupee depreciation has been used to offer higher discounts.
Inquiry-to-order conversion of 10-15% and the lack of a disclosed current pipeline figure.
Management did not confirm the FY27 revenue estimate of INR2,150-2,200 crore; watch the Q2 run-rate and order book conversion.
Capacity utilisation figures given in the call were inconsistent (50%, 70-72%, 75%), so the true utilisation level needs confirming.
544839|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and margins, with a clear focus on the 20% EBITDA target. Evasive or unprepared on the order pipeline figures, capacity utilisation and export share, which the chairman deferred to later email. The call had audio issues and several figures were corrected mid-call.

541556|2026-06.headline: RITES Q1 FY27 revenue grew 9-10% YoY, PAT about 8%; order book at INR 9,450 crore, with export revenue slipping into Q2 on Bangladesh first rake.
541556|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as growth of 9-10% YoY in revenue and about 8% at the bottom line, driven by the record order book from last year, but said execution must step up sequentially. Export revenue from the Bangladesh coach order was not recognised in Q1 because the first rake (about 20 coaches, four coach types) was still being finalised; dispatch is expected within about 10 days, with recognition in Q2. Consolidated EBITDA margin was 22% and PAT margin about 17%, both held sequentially, and management reiterated red lines of 20% EBITDA and 15% PAT margin. Order book reached INR 9,450 crore after 128 fresh orders worth INR 670 crore, with about 70% of fresh orders won competitively.

segments.commentary: Combined export and foreign consultancy order book INR 2,100 crore as of 30 June 2026. Management expects current book to largely execute by next FY.

segments.name: Turnkey projects
segments.commentary: About 50% of order book (about INR 4,700 crore of INR 9,450 crore) and about 30-33% of Q1 revenue; margins about 1.5-2%.

segments.commentary: Balance of order book (about INR 4,700 crore) split roughly 50-50 with export rolling stock consultancy; majority of fresh consultancy wins on competitive basis, with tougher margins.

segments.commentary: Profit about INR 22 crore in Q1 with about 50%+ PAT margin; early progress in international and domestic renewable consultancy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided as substantial vs FY26; management aims for double-digit revenue growth and sequential increase in quarterly revenue.
Export revenue target of at least INR 300 crore in FY27; visibility on Mozambique deliveries and Bangladesh rake cadence expected by end-Q2.
Bangladesh 200-coach order: management expects completion in early Q2 or Q3 of FY28, not this year.
Mozambique locomotive deliveries targeted to begin by end of FY27, with clearer visibility by end-Q2.

Travel costs under pressure in consultancy; guardrails in place.
Turnkey share expected to average below 50% over time, though clients prefer single-point turnkey contracts.

qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised per full rake; first rake of about 20 coaches (four types) had final approval delayed by a few days, and dispatch is expected within about 10 days, so recognition falls in Q2. Later rakes should be faster.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of pending export orders and timelines for Bangladesh and Mozambique?
qa_highlights.answer: Export order book about INR 1,775 crore, with about INR 900 crore Bangladesh; Bangladesh will not finish this year, likely early Q2 or Q3 FY28. Mozambique deliveries may start by end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much export revenue this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: At least INR 300 crore export revenue in FY27; export targeted at about 15% of total revenue this year, with the current order book largely executed next FY.

543358|2026-06.headline: Sansera Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR10,213 million, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and ADS order book lifted to about INR57.5 billion.

A INR169 million exceptional litigation settlement cut reported PAT to INR874 million (8.6% margin, up 39% YoY); PAT excluding the exceptional post-tax impact was about INR1,000 million. Supply chain stress on raw material and child parts; customers helping secure material.

Material cost inflation mainly in aluminium and consumables; steel inflation limited. Pass-through of steel inflation and higher tool and labour costs (mainly northern plants) still under negotiation, with nothing booked in Q1.
Forex movement gave a short-term cushion to realisations.

544886|2026-06.headline: Tempsens Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% to INR118 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 22% from 25.3% on higher employee cost.

segments.commentary: Home loans are 71% of the book and non-HL home equity loans 29% as of June 2026. Non-salaried borrowers are 53.5% of exposure and salaried 46.5%.

segments.commentary: Tamil Nadu accounts for about 57% of the book. Management is now prioritising southern non-TN states (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka), with Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Gujarat and MP in the pipeline.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: Rs.5,000 Cr disbursements, 13-14% AUM growth, and Rs.40 Cr NPA reduction.
Q2 FY27 disbursement target of Rs.1,200-1,250 Cr; management says June, July and early August trends are on track.
Gross NPA to be brought back to about Rs.405 Cr in Q2 and to around Rs.400 Cr by September end; target of less than 2% GNPA by March 2027.
Spread may fall by 10-12bps, at most 10bps, in the next quarter, then broadly stable, as the company sacrifices yield to drive disbursements and curb BT-outs.
Cost of funds expected to stay stable at around 8.3%, supported by the Rs.600 Cr NHB refinance line (Rs.106 Cr drawn in early August, with Rs.100 Cr later referenced as undertaken).
Plans to open 12-13 more branches in FY27, mainly in AP, Telangana, Karnataka and western states.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 242 branches, including about 32 satellite centres; no new branches opened in Q1 FY27.
Plan to add 12-13 branches in FY27, focused on Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and western India.
IT transformation completed in two phases, including mobile apps and API integrations with Perfios, CERSAI and CIBIL to shorten sanction turnaround.
Operating model verticalised: separate vertical for recoveries and SARFAESI, a separate sales vertical, DSAs, DSTs and connectors added.
demand_pricing: Customer rates start at 8.75% with an average of about 10.5% on housing loans; management says pricing is risk-based on 16-17 parameters and PSU-bank rates are not viable at its cost of borrowing.
Q1 disbursement shortfall attributed to April-May transfers and promotions; management says June was good and July and August are running ahead.
BT-outs rose in Q1 versus Q4. Management is retaining good-track-record borrowers with rate concessions and a new incentive scheme for staff.
Competition is intensifying from other HFCs and NBFCs; management says it has grown through competition for 25 years.
Sourcing focus moved partly from DSAs to other channels, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why is customer lending rate high versus banks, and why is the company not diversifying?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rate depends on cost of borrowing (about 8.3-8.35%) and risk profile, and PSU-rate lending is not viable. It has no current plan to diversify beyond housing finance, and an HFC licence limits it to housing and mortgage loans.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q1 disbursement affected by cheque issues, and is there a Q1 backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said month-end disbursements of about Rs.35-40 Cr roll over each month as a normal cycle; June's figure carries the operational impact and any backlog will be made up in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Are June and July run-rates back to normal, and is the Rs.1,200 Cr Q2 target credible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June was good, July was better and August is expected to exceed that, and the MD said he was confident of Rs.1,200 Cr, while declining to give exact figures citing price-sensitive policy.

qa_highlights.question: Have pricing or customer policies changed, and what is driving the higher runoff?
qa_highlights.answer: No major policy change; sourcing focus shifted and some rate concessions were given to retain customers. Higher BT-outs reflect competitors targeting the company's visibility from more aggressive marketing.

qa_highlights.question: Is asset quality deterioration business as usual, and can recoveries outpace provisions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the NPA uptick to transfers and promotions. Soft NPAs (April 2025-June 2026 slippages, about 1,000-1,100 cases, 40-45 per RVM) are targeted for at least 50% reduction, worth Rs.70-75 Cr, and chronic NPAs are being pursued via SARFAESI.

qa_highlights.question: How much spread compression and what does it do to ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread is 3.44% with cost of funds at 8.31%, and ROA around 2.9%. Spread may fall 10-12bps (maximum 10bps) next quarter, then stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company recognising interest and disbursement only on cheque encashment?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said AUM and disbursement are booked only after encashment, and management said this has been the practice for three to four quarters.

532528|2026-06.headline: Datamatics Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore, with EBITDA margin up 343 bps to 19.7%.
532528|2026-06.overview:
Revenue grew 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore and EBITDA rose to INR 101.1 crore at a 19.7% margin, with the margin gain attributed to cost discipline and operational excellence. Digital Operations drove growth (revenue up 16.1%, EBIT margin 19.3%), while Digital Technologies grew 6.1% at an 8.9% EBIT margin and Digital Experiences declined 5.3%. Management reiterated high single-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance, citing softness from geopolitical uncertainty, and said about 60% of FY27 deals won were AI-led or AI-driven. The TNQTech integration into Lumina Datamatics was completed in the quarter, and a INR 200 crore TNQTech payout was made in Q1.</overview>

segments.name: Digital Operations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 296.8 crore, up 16.1% YoY; EBIT margin 19.3%. TNQTech is integrated here, per management.

segments.name: Digital Technologies
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 153.1 crore, up 6.1% YoY; EBIT margin 8.9%. Carries the company's AI R&D spend of about INR 40-50 crore a year, which management says depresses the margin.

segments.name: Digital Experiences
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 64 crore, down 5.3% YoY; EBIT margin 11.7%. Management said several good-sized deals were signed this year and the practice is seeing an upswing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of high single digits, maintained despite market softness.
Full-year EBITDA margin expected to rise about 0.5 percentage point, to close to 20%; management later said 19-20% at year end.
AI R&D spend to stay at about the same level (INR 40-50 crore) in FY27; FY28 budget not yet decided.

Management cited a roughly 3-year target of about INR 3,000 crore revenue, versus about INR 2,000 crore now, to be a mix of organic and inorganic growth; it was described as starting in the current year.
Annual salary increments effective April 2026 are already reflected in Q1 numbers.
M&A dialogue is ongoing but no deal has matured to disclosure stage.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were discussed.

AI platforms cited as growth drivers: KAiBRE and KAiSDLC for legacy modernisation, KAi underwriting for insurance, agentic claims processing, and SuperCX for contact-centre and front-office automation.
Legacy modernisation projects reportedly compress timelines from about three years to about six months; first underwriting-product revenue has been booked with one customer.
demand_pricing: Customers are choosing Datamatics for AI capability; recent wins include SBI Life Insurance (TruAI underwriting), a US pet and veterinary provider (AI voice agent) and a US consumer products company (KAiBRE/KAiSDLC).
About 60% of deals won this fiscal were AI-led or largely AI-driven, per management.
Deal sizes are rising but are increasingly shorter (3-9 month) AI projects rather than multi-year annuity contracts; management said margins are not shrinking.
Competition is increasingly from well-funded local AI start-ups, GCCs and captive tech teams, not from larger listed IT peers.
Top 5, 10 and 20 clients contribute 30%, 41% and 54% of revenue. Education and Publishing is 29%, technology and consulting 20%, BFSI 19%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for AI R&D spend, and is there any plan for buybacks or M&A with the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: AI R&D stays at about INR 40-50 crore this year. Cash of INR 710 crore predates the INR 200 crore TNQTech payout, and management is in M&A dialogue but nothing has matured; no buyback was mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 revenue growth consistent with the full-year guidance, given the strong Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained high single-digit FY27 growth guidance and cited market softness from the war and uncertainty. The CFO clarified that 43% growth refers to PAT, while revenue grew 9.9%.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Digital Technologies grown slowly with margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to traction in KAi underwriting, KAiSDLC and KAiBRE, with legacy modernisation projects starting. It said the segment carries the AI investment, so removing it would give a much healthier margin.

qa_highlights.question: How has the competitive landscape changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not compete much with large listed IT players. Competition comes from funded local AI start-ups, GCCs and in-house tech teams.

qa_highlights.question: What are the risks to the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Key risks are customers automating in-house instead of outsourcing, captive/GCC setups, and geopolitical softness.

qa_highlights.question: What is the five-year blueprint and what are the revenue drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about INR 3,000 crore over roughly three years from about INR 2,000 crore now, with organic growth from AI platforms and bolt-on acquisitions.

risks_watch: Customer insourcing to automation and GCC/captive setups could reduce outsourcing budgets, per management.
Geopolitical uncertainty (the war) is cited as softening demand; management said it needs to settle.
Shift toward shorter AI projects (3-9 months) rather than multi-year annuity deals could affect revenue visibility.
Digital Experiences declined 5.3% YoY and Digital Technologies margin is 8.9%; watch for recovery.
Whether AI R&D spend (INR 40-50 crore) remains flat next year is undecided.
532528|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on AI-led deal wins, margins and the INR 3,000 crore ambition, but cautious on near-term demand, which management said remains soft due to the war. Management was vague on TNQTech's standalone contribution and on the FY28 AI spend.
key_quotes: So, we have projected a high single-digit growth in our guidance. We are maintaining that.
We are seeing strong market validation of our AI-first strategy.
So, a project that will take three years can be probably done in six months now.

540048|2026-06.headline: S.P. Apparels Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 15.9% to INR 61.4 crore on revenue flat at INR 401 crore; FY27 guidance of INR 2,000 crore reiterated.
540048|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was broadly flat year-on-year at INR 401 crore (vs INR 403 crore), while EBITDA rose 15.9% to INR 61.4 crore and margin expanded to 15.3% from 13.1%. PAT grew 20.4% to INR 24.9 crore. Management attributed the soft top line to U.S. tariff-related order holding in March-May and customer-requested shipment deferrals, and said growth will be back-end weighted into H2 FY27. The company reiterated its INR 2,000 crore FY27 revenue guidance, and announced a INR 3 per share dividend and a proposed stock split from INR 10 to INR 2 face value.

segments.commentary: Adjusted revenue INR 337.3 crore with adjusted EBITDA INR 59.2 crore, a 17.6% margin; management attributed the margin to efficiency and product mix, not one-offs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR 2,000 crore reiterated; management expects H2 to be stronger and to recover the Q1 shortfall, though Q1 delivered only INR 400 crore.

Garment division (incl. YBA and Sri Lanka) EBITDA margin guided above 15% for the full year.
Young Brand revenue guided to INR 340-350 crore for FY27 (FY26: about INR 300 crore).
Infant export value guided to INR 1,300-1,400 crore for FY27 (FY26: about INR 1,100 crore; call also cited INR 955 crore for the prior year).
Consolidated interest cost guided to INR 30-35 crore for the full year, excluding exchange loss; Q1 interest of about INR 15 crore included a INR 1.75 crore forex hit.
SPUK guidance of GBP 13 million+ in about 3 years and GBP 50 million in about 5 years; a later answer cited GBP 50-60 million in 3-5 years.

Sivakasi factory started; plan to add about 400 machines over two years.

SPUK added three UK customers (two UK, one EU) and is adding three more; Marks & Spencer named as one of them.

544587|2026-06.headline: Midwest Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35% YoY and PAT 27%, with granite carrying results and quartz Phase 1 still ramping (~5,000 t sold, ~INR5 crore revenue).
544587|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue up 35% YoY, EBITDA up 25% and PAT up 27%, with most of the earnings from granite despite diesel cost pressure. Quartz Phase 1 has begun commercial operations with roughly INR5 crore revenue and about 5,000 tonnes sold in the quarter, and management is targeting a 10,000 t/month run rate by end-Q2 and 15,000 t/month by Q4. FY27 guidance is about INR840 crore revenue (granite INR720 crore, quartz INR100-120 crore), with quartz EBITDA expected to be low this year. Management also flagged an Indonesia MoU with PERMINAS for rare earth oxides and an imminent Sri Lanka licence step, while Kerala remains stalled on government transition.

financial_highlights.value: ~10% in both Absolute Black and Black Galaxy

financial_highlights.metric: Blended EBITDA margin impact from diesel (Q1 FY27)
financial_highlights.change: Diesel ~13% of cost; diesel rose from ~INR85 to INR125-130/litre

segments.name: Granite (natural stone)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth above 30% excluding quartz; volumes up ~10% in both Absolute Black and Black Galaxy, with better realisations and a price hike of about 3-5%. Electrified fleet and solar backing cut diesel sensitivity.

segments.name: Quartz (engineered stone, Phase 1, Kerala-linked plant)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR5 crore on ~5,000 t sold; realisation about INR10,000/t. Mix about 65% engineered stone and 35% solar. Break-even targeted around 10,000 t/month, with plant capacity up to 18,000 t/month.

segments.name: Rare earth / Midwest Advanced Materials
segments.commentary: Sister concern Midwest Advanced Materials focuses on rare earth oxide to permanent magnet. Parent scope is ore-to-oxide via a JV with PERMINAS; no revenue yet, with cash flows expected FY29.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue estimated at ~INR840 crore vs INR645 crore in FY26; management called this conservative and said Q1 run-rate suggests beating it.
Quartz: ~120,000 t production target for FY27 (revised down from 150,000 t); quartz EBITDA this year to be below expectations; break-even around 10,000 t/month, with some profit expected by year-end.
Granite EBITDA margin in line with prior years, with 50-100 bps diesel-related variance; blended EBITDA margin expected in the 26-27% range for FY27.

FY28: quartz Phase 1 revenue INR180-200 crore plus Phase 2 contribution of about INR40-50 crore (around 4 months of production); granite growth 10-12%; blended EBITDA ~29-30%, with quartz EBITDA slightly above 30%.
Sri Lanka: policy finalised; land/licence documentation expected this quarter, groundbreaking around October, 12-15 months build-out; cash flows now expected FY29.
Indonesia (PERMINAS): MoU to be converted to an agreement this quarter and a JV formed next quarter; project report due in 45-60 days; capex to be given next call.
capex_capacity: Quartz Phase 2: total capex ~INR125 crore, with ~INR60-70 crore in Q2-Q3 and the balance in Q4 or early FY28; commissioning now 10-12 months out after machinery was resourced away from China; funded by fresh equity raised.
Quartz Phase 1 capacity can reach 18,000 t/month; 15,000 t/month is the planned stable run rate; ramp to 10,000-12,000 t/month in Q2 and above 15,000 t/month by Q4.
Sri Lanka plant capex ~INR120 crore (internal accruals); Kerala (KMML) pilot plant described as low cost, with no activity pending new government and MD appointment.
Indonesia capex to be higher than Kerala given overseas mining; figure to be given next call.
Electrification of the granite fleet mostly completed this year; regular granite replacement capex funded from operating cash flow.
demand_pricing: Quartz volumes are mostly exported to China; management said Q4 typically carries 30-40% of annual revenue due to Chinese New Year restocking.
Granite pricing improved; a further price increase of about 3-5% was taken to offset fuel costs. Management said no further price action is planned this year unless fuel moves again.
Fuel prices eased slightly from Q1 peaks but remain well above prior-year levels; management expects margin recovery in Q2.
Q3 monsoon risk noted: production is typically lower in Q3 due to rains.
Freight is generally on FOB terms, so freight costs are borne by customers and are not in Midwest's cost base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 quartz volume and the ramp-up timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5,000 t sold in Q1; management guided ~20,000 t this quarter (likely a typo for run rate), 10,000-12,000 t next quarter and above 15,000 t in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will quartz reach EBITDA break-even and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Break-even expected around Q3 FY27 at about 10,000 t/month, with some profit by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 150,000 t FY27 quartz production target still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management revised the target to about 120,000 t after a technical production issue that has since been resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 revenue look lower than Q4 and how does the quartz capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 is seasonally the peak (30-40% of annual revenue) due to Chinese New Year restocking; Phase 2 capex is INR125 crore spread over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 see higher margins with quartz?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Blended EBITDA expected at 29-30% in FY28, with quartz EBITDA slightly above 30%, given Phase 1 revenue of INR180-200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Which granite mine has the AP government revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Black Galaxy; the arrangement is a revenue-share payment to a state-owned lessor that also holds equity.

533156|2026-06.headline: Vascon Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR152 crores (from INR221 crores) and PAT to INR2 crores (from INR22 crores), on EPC execution delays.
533156|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations fell about 31% YoY to INR152 crores, driven by lower EPC execution from cash-flow-stalled government projects. Consolidated EBITDA was INR10 crores versus INR34 crores in Q1 FY26, which included an INR18 crores one-time investment gain; adjusted for that, EBITDA was about INR15 crores at roughly 6% margin. Management said the EPC segment stayed profitable at about 9% EBITDA margin, while real estate booked INR4 crores revenue and a INR4 crores EBITDA loss. Management guided to a recovery from Q3 and reiterated the FY27 revenue target of INR1,200 crores, while net debt rose to about INR152 crores.

EPC phasing revised: Q1+Q2 expected at ~30% of FY revenue and Q3+Q4 at ~70% (vs typical 40:60).
FY27 EPC new order intake target INR1,500-2,000 crores.

Real estate OC targets this year for Coimbatore, Tower of Ascend (Kharadi) in Q3/Q4 and Orchid Santacruz in Q4 (stretch), which would drive revenue recognition.

INR80 crores preferential warrant issue over up to 18 months; first tranche (minimum 25%) received; proceeds ~60-70% for real estate, rest for EPC working capital and corporate purposes.

Thane land parcel (150 acres, Vascon holds 45%) still under acquisition process; no timeline for continuous parcel, at least a year plus.
demand_pricing: Q1 new EPC award: CPWD order of INR295 crores for RBI Colony in Guwahati; LOI of INR126 crores (ex-GST) from Maharashtra PWD for a 300-bed General Hospital at Wardha received August 12, 2026.
Management stated gross profit on EPC remains 13-15%, and real estate gross margin is 25-30%.
Real estate sales: 30,690 sq ft new bookings and ~INR20 crores collections in Q1.
Competition in Mumbai redevelopment described as intense; management targets projects with GDV of INR250-300 crores and focuses on 1-2 acre sites in Western and Central suburbs.
Adani Infra engagement on 3-4 projects at an early design stage; management does not expect construction start in the next 6 months, and revenue may slip to Q4 or next year.

Royal Rides (Goa, ~INR225 crores ropeway-related order): only ~INR15 crores recognised; management assumes no revenue for the next 3 quarters. Reliance order was cancelled by mutual agreement after design and construction method changes.

qa_highlights.question: How much real estate construction spend is pending, and what free cash flow can come from sold and unsold projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said real estate gross margins remain 25-30%, with ~INR300 crores of pending construction cost against ~INR400 crores unsold inventory value plus ~INR116 crores pending collections, implying ~INR220 crores free cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Why has debt risen sharply since March 2025 and where did the cash go?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the rise mainly to EPC: CC limit utilisation increased on milestone-based projects, and net working capital cycle stretched from ~45 to ~65-70 days over the last six months. Real estate also needed equity infusion.

qa_highlights.question: Which government projects face cash-flow issues and when will they ramp up?
qa_highlights.answer: Bihar Supaul and Sindhudurg (Maharashtra) projects; client cash flows now available and ramp-up expected within 1-2 months.

qa_highlights.question: Which real estate projects will recognise revenue and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Coimbatore and Tower of Ascend (Kharadi) OC targeted in Q3/Q4; Orchid Santacruz targeted for Q4 only if achieved.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Vedanta project, Royal Rides and Vashi Hospital?
qa_highlights.answer: Vedanta has restarted with scale-up and is expected to finish this FY; Vashi Hospital expected to start in the coming quarter; Royal Rides stalled with no client go-ahead, assumed zero revenue for next 3 quarters, but still a live order.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 INR1,200 crore revenue target still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated INR1,200 crores, with EPC at ~INR1,000 crores and real estate INR200 crores-plus, with Q3/Q4 carrying ~70% of EPC revenue.

543600|2026-06.headline: Harsha Engineers Q1 FY27 consolidated Engineering supply up 25% YoY to Rs 421 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed on a 6-7% raw material spike pending pass-through.

Management kept FY27 guidance of high-teens India growth and low-teens consolidated growth, with India Engineering EBITDA margin of 22-24%.

Stamping: about 30% growth in FY27 vs Rs 60 crore in FY26.

543653|2026-06.headline: Bikaji Q1 FY27 revenue grew ~12.5% (volume +7.7%) despite a 3–4 day Bikaner plant/dispatch shutdown and labour exits; EBITDA margin ~13.5% vs 12.2% QoQ.
543653|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 as a story of two halves: April to mid-May was hit by a 3–4 day shutdown after the Chairman's passing and a loss of Bengali labour around the Bengal elections, while the last ~45 days saw strong recovery, with management citing ~20% growth in that period. Value growth of 12.5% was led by Western Snacks (+21.3%) and Ethnic Snacks (+11.4%), with exports the only weak channel (-2.2%). EBITDA margin was ~13.5% against ~12.2% last quarter, and management guided FY27 EBITDA margin to 13–13.5% including PLI, with festive-season ad spend rising. Price hikes are on hold until Diwali.

financial_highlights.value: INR 12.5 Crores of INR 14 Crores other operating income

Stores up from 15 to 28 in one year

FY27 revenue growth target of 15%+ (management later said mid-teens to ~16% per quarter, high-teens as aspiration).
Festive sweets expected to grow 12–13% and gifting 17–18% across Q2+Q3.
Advertising spend for the full year targeted at about 2% of sales, with heavier ad spend in the next two quarters.
PLI benefit of about 150 bps of EBITDA this year, falling to about INR 50 Crores next year; mitigation of 50–75 bps targeted via pricing and gross margin, with 1.5–2 years to restore original margin.
Core-state growth budgeted at 13–15%; focus states (UP) 30%+ in budget.
No further price increase planned for the next 30 days or until Diwali, as prices are signed off with large accounts.

Bikaji Bakes (bakery): not yet in full production; trials ongoing, production could start in about two quarters, with no large numbers in FY27 plan.
US business expected to grow about 3x in next 2 years; exports about 3–4% of business now, targeted at 5–6% in 3–4 years.
demand_pricing: Two price increases taken over the last 90 days to offset edible oil and pulse inflation (moth dal, chana dal); one MRP increase taken in April.
Management said modern trade, quick commerce and general trade demand plans for the next 3 months are positive.

Private labels from quick commerce platforms (e.g., Swiggy's Noice) seen as early-stage; management says consumers stay with brands.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the April production loss a factor for the top line, given inventory and recovery time?

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for slower standalone growth (about 11% last year) versus the earlier expected 15–17%?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% margin target achievable this year, given the ad-spend guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Rishabh Jain said 15% is a 3-year target, not for this year; FY27 is targeted at 13–13.5%, with at least 50 bps improvement YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA outlook for THF stores?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the export decline and when will it recover?

qa_highlights.question: What is the core-state growth outlook?

risks_watch: Edible oil and pulse inflation; price hikes paused until Diwali, so gross margin recovery depends on mix and efficiencies.
Labour concentration in Bikaner for core bhujia; single-site risk is being addressed by decentralisation.
PLI roll-off (~INR 50 Crores) from FY28, a 150 bps EBITDA headwind.
Exports: freight costs and US tariff uncertainty could delay shipments for a couple of quarters.
Heavy ad spend in Q2–Q3 could keep EBITDA margin under pressure despite gross margin gains.
Papad sensitivity to monsoon weather.
Quick commerce competition and private-label entrants.
543653|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on demand recovery and festive pipeline, but more cautious and sometimes evasive on margins, export timing and the reconciliation of the 15% margin aspiration. The Q1 shortfall was attributed to one-off disruptions.

500670|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 profit described as second highest in company history after Q1 FY22, driven by better realisations despite lower sales volumes.
500670|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 was shaped by Middle East war escalation and de-escalation, which caused viability-driven shutdowns at acetic acid, ethyl acetate and TDI but lifted realisations. Sales volumes fell well below production, and inventory built up to 30 June was about 15% liquidated by end-July. Fertilizer segment profit rose to about INR85 crores from about INR24 crores, with urea contributing about INR48 crores and ANP about INR12 crores. Management gave no formal quarterly guidance, and several questions on forward realisations and savings went unanswered.

financial_highlights.value: Second highest in company history after Q1 FY22

financial_highlights.change: Up about INR60 crores from about INR24 crores
Held across G-Sec, GSFS and bank

segments.name: Fertilizers (urea, ANP)
segments.commentary: Fertilizer segment result rose to about INR85 crores from about INR24 crores, with urea about INR48 crores and ANP about INR12 crores. Energy norm for urea revised to 6.37 Gcal/MT from 6.20 Gcal/MT, valid for 3 years from FY26.

segments.name: Chemicals (TDI, WNA, CNA, AN Melt, TGU, acetic acid, ethyl acetate)
segments.commentary: Q1 output: TDI 12,800 MT, WNA 113,000 MT (sales 20,800 MT), CNA production 37,500 MT (sales 16,400 MT), AN Melt 55,600 MT, TGU 74,800 MT, formic acid 8,200 MT. Acetic acid and ethyl acetate were shut for part of the quarter; both restarted by 1 August.

guidance_outlook: Management expects TGU output for the rest of FY27 to be broadly at last year's level, against a Q1 run rate it described as about 300,000 MT annualised.

Steam portion of the coal-based Dahej steam and power project is running; power expected in about 45 days. Estimated saving of INR30,000-40,000 per MT of TDI at current gas and coal prices, subject to change.

A.T. Kearney cost-saving quantification is not yet signed off; management expects a clearer P&L picture by end of Q2. Earlier Kearney estimate cited by an analyst was INR250-300 crores, which management confirmed.
Projected incremental revenue of INR1,200-1,500 crores and contribution uplift of INR500-600 crores from the INR2,800 crore project portfolio, given later and subject to price volatility.

Capex for FY27 targeted at INR1,200-1,500 crores more on top of Q1 INR300 crores; most will sit in CWIP, with only partial capitalisation in FY27. Remaining projects commercially operational around mid-2027. Further about INR1,500 crores over the next two years.
capex_capacity: Dahej CCPP (INR613 crores) and other projects are targeted for commercial operation around mid-2027.
Dahej steam portion is online and replacing gas with coal for TDI-II; power portion expected in roughly 45 days.
Weak nitric acid plant running about 3 months behind schedule, to be recouped; AMUGL and AN Melt reported online.
Ammonia output about 173,000 MT, split 54% oil-based and 49% gas-based (as stated, shares sum above 100%). TDI output split 66% Dahej and 34% Bharuch.

Urea and nitric acid ran above rated capacity; CNA ran below design capacity due to weak internal TDI consumption; aniline and nitrobenzene ran above design. Minimum neem coated urea obligation is 637,000 MT.
demand_pricing: TDI: management said global TDI supply exceeds demand, so Covestro and Wanhua maintenance shutdowns will not move global pricing, though Indian TDI shortage will affect local pricing.
Inventory built to 30 June was about 15% liquidated by end-July; realisations were initially lower, then rose, with no single figure given.
Offtake was weak in Q1 even though spreads looked better, causing inventory build-up.

Fuel oil and gas prices rose versus Q4 FY26 on the Middle East crisis; oil prices (per analyst) moved from about INR43-44 to about INR73; easing seen in July-August but not resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Current oil and gas prices and availability versus Q1 averages?
qa_highlights.answer: N.B. Desai said prices eased in July-August but the Middle East crisis is unresolved; gas prices are volatile, though supply has not affected operations.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 realisation direction for chemicals vs Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance, citing that Q1 was the reference point and the market is volatile.

qa_highlights.question: Dahej steam and power savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently about INR30,000-40,000 per MT of TDI; the figure moves with the gas-coal price delta, and coal-based operation benefits if coal prices fall.

qa_highlights.question: Cash, capex and project pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash about INR4,000 crores; Q1 capex INR300 crores; FY27 capex targeted at INR1,200-1,500 crores more; INR2,800 crore projects on hand plus about INR1,500 crores over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Plant restart status for acetic acid, ethyl acetate and TDI?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethyl acetate and acetic acid back on 1 August after July and May shutdowns; Bharuch TDI was down in July, with TDI-I and TDI-II restarting. Methanol sourcing for captive acetic acid has started.

risks_watch: Re-escalation of the Middle East conflict could reopen viability issues and shut plants again, as seen in Q1.
Unsigned Kearney savings estimate; the INR250-300 crore planned saving has not been confirmed by management.
Inventory liquidation and realisation mix in Q2 are unclear; offtake was weak in Q1.
Project timelines: Dahej CCPP and other projects slated for mid-2027; nitric acid plant about 3 months behind.
Gas and coal price volatility drives the Dahej steam and power savings and TDI economics.
Management declined to quantify several forward items (Q2 realisations, project revenue impact), limiting visibility.

507514|2026-06.headline: Som Distilleries Q1 FY27 hit by Madhya Pradesh suspension: consolidated EBITDA INR15.2 crore on INR268.8 crore total income; FY27 revenue guidance cut to INR1,000-1,100 crore.
507514|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was described by management as an extremely difficult quarter, driven by the operational and regulatory disruption in Madhya Pradesh, where the Bhopal brewery remains suspended. Consolidated volume was 45.79 lakh cases, total income INR268.8 crore and EBITDA INR15.2 crore. Karnataka (cases up about 30%) and Odisha (up about 40%) recovered, and the UP brewery (about 10 million cases capacity) began commercial production around June 9, 2026. Gross debt rose only INR10 crore QoQ, with gross D/E moving from 0.3x to 0.31x, and operating cash generation was about INR28 crore. FY27 revenue guidance was lowered to INR1,000-1,100 crore from the earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue was lost from the MP closure in Q1?

qa_highlights.question: Will Bhopal (MP) be restored, and what was the FY27 outlook if it is not?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is in courts and with authorities and is sub judice; it is hopeful of resolution this month. It declined to discuss a plan B or give numbers for a no-approval scenario, and reiterated FY27 revenue of INR1,000-1,100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Could Karnataka or other plants supply Bhopal to lift utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said importing from Odisha or UP to MP would be uneconomic because of MP's very high import fees, potentially leading to a loss.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company use contract manufacturing in states with overcapacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it compares local contract brewing against importing and chooses whichever is better on margin and quality, and that capacity is planned over five to 10 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Hassan plant not converted into a 100% subsidiary like UP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will evaluate and revert soon, with no commitment.

544491|2026-06.headline: Gem Aromatics Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose to INR83 crore (from INR76 crore) but consolidated EBITDA fell to INR3.3 crore (3.3% margin) and consolidated PAT was a INR7.9 crore loss.
544491|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew about 9% YoY to INR83 crore, with consolidated revenue at INR99 crore versus INR88 crore, helped by a seasonally soft Q1. Margins compressed on product mix, clove raw-material costs after Madagascar floods, and a higher fixed cost base at the new Dahej plant. Consolidated PAT was a loss of INR7.9 crore, pressured by INR9.1 crore of higher depreciation after capitalisation of most of the INR270 crore Dahej capex. Management says the new verticals (cooling agents, Safranal/Citral, phenol derivatives) start contributing from Q2 to Q4 FY27, with FY27 framed as a ramp-up year and no guidance given.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR76 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +9% YoY)
vs INR88 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +12% YoY)
Higher depreciation of INR9.1 crore after Dahej capitalisation

segments.name: Gem (core: clove and mint)
segments.commentary: Clove volumes and sales were hit by Madagascar cyclone/floods, with Toamasina port shut for close to 30 days; incoming raw material resumed from May. Mint harvest runs May to July, with export orders now flowing, though some May-June shipments were not yet recognised as they had not reached destinations.

segments.name: Krystal Ingredients (Dahej, wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Safranal commercial production has started, with revenue expected by end-Q2 FY27 and meaningful from Q3. Cooling agents Gemcool 3, 5 and 23 are in production with initial orders; meaningful contribution expected from Q3 FY27. Phenol derivatives: trial production by end-Q2, commercial production targeted Q3, meaningful revenue from Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 revenue or margin guidance; management will give guidance toward calendar year-end for the next year.
Krystal products expected to exceed 50% of overall revenue in FY28.
Management expects Eugenol and derivatives to be fairly close to planned numbers by year-end FY27, per Yash Parekh.
Cooling agents: management expects a large part of the targeted volumes (on 500-ton capacity, about 25% utilisation with two customers) to show up in Q3 and Q4.
Operating leverage expected to support margins and profitability over the medium term as utilisation rises.
capex_capacity: Total Dahej plant capex about INR270 crore; nearly INR265 crore incurred and substantially capitalised.
Standby capacity at Dahej is already absorbing depreciation, interest and manpower costs ahead of revenue.
Cooling agents: 500-ton capacity referenced by analyst; management said utilisation would be close to the analyst's 25% figure.
Phenol derivatives: commercial production targeted Q3 FY27, subject to approvals and quality processes.
Brazil subsidiary approved to expand Latin America distribution for essential oils, aroma chemicals and specialty chemicals.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is back to normal levels, with Western Hemisphere (US and Latin America) demand ramping up.
Cooling agents are used in oral care, confectionery and specialty flavours; cooling agent approvals from two of the world's largest consumers, per management.
Clove raw-material pricing rose after Madagascar supply disruption, weighing on margins.
Shipping challenges out of India and to the Western Hemisphere are a key concern for timing.
Currency: management said the rupee depreciation is neither a tactical advantage nor disadvantage, since imports are hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Where is demand coming from in the core business, and which geographies are growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is back to normal; Western Hemisphere (US and Latin America) is ramping, with export deal flow and new product seasonality expected to show in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the phenol derivatives ramp delayed, and what is the timeline to commercial production?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production by end-Q2 FY27, commercial production in Q3, meaningful revenue from Q4 FY27; pilot batches are approved and customers want plant-level trials. Traders and distributors are being targeted for faster approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Madagascar disruption materially delay the Eugenol ramp, and is clove tree supply structurally at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Port reopened and material is flowing; management expects Eugenol numbers close to plan by year-end. Trees are still productive and sourcing is diversified across Madagascar and East Africa, so no major structural issue foreseen.

qa_highlights.question: How will the business reach sustainable consolidated profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a timing mismatch: depreciation, interest and manpower costs are already in the P&L while higher-margin Krystal revenue has not yet arrived. Profitability should improve as the new products ramp.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital evolve for Krystal?
qa_highlights.answer: Krystal is synthetic and needs less inventory, so its working cycle should be lower than Gem's; factoring is also being used to reduce debtor days.

qa_highlights.question: Can you quantify the Gemcool orders, and are new products higher margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Order values and customer names are not being disclosed. Management said each new product is intended to be more margin-accretive than existing products; several are in approval stages with revenue expected from Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Did the tariff-relief restocking show up in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Mint harvest timing, clove delays and shipping issues pushed revenue into later periods; May-June exports were made but not yet recognised as they had not reached final destinations, with roll-over expected in July-August.

Clove supply from Madagascar and shipping disruptions to the Western Hemisphere.
Clove and raw-material cost pass-through, given higher clove costs in Q1.

Consolidated revenue rose 12.1% to about INR 2,727 crore with EBITDA at 5.1%. Management guided that July-September will be the weakest quarter and gave no full-year numbers.

539336|2026-06.headline: Gujarat Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% to INR9,670 crores and PAT 78% to INR998 crores, led by gas trading EBT of INR726 crores.
539336|2026-06.overview:

demand_pricing: MR spot earnings near $50,000/day last quarter (all-time high); LPG freight rates above $100,000/day; asset prices up ~5-10% in the quarter.
Trade pattern shifts after Hormuz disruption (US and Brazil supplying Asia) raised ton-mile demand; Venezuelan crude now long-haul East; Russian product exports diverted.
Management views the shift as temporary, depending on Hormuz, Russia-Ukraine and sanctions outcomes; pipelines bypassing Hormuz have security and Red Sea risks.
Panama Canal water levels falling, restricting transits; mainly affects LPG.
Asset price cycle risk: management cited a ~20% drawdown in 2025 impairments on ships bought in 2023-24.

qa_highlights.question: Will product-to-crude switching by LR2s be permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Sheth said LR2s switched to Aframax because of the earnings gap and lack of Gulf cargoes; the switch can reverse if LR2 earnings recover.

qa_highlights.question: Buyback framework and whether a buyback is feasible at current valuations?
qa_highlights.answer: G. Shivakumar said there is no price or multiple target; buyback will be assessed by the Board like other capital allocation. The tax disadvantage on buybacks has gone, lowering the premium needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why not deploy incremental cash into ships given strong freight?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prefers to hold most cash and invest only at the margin (1-2 ships), citing the risk that ships bought at peak prices write down; it said it cannot make a market call with this uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: What fuel and earnings savings come from newer ships?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Sheth said 2020s-built ships can save up to 20-25% fuel versus pre-2013 ships, worth about $1,000-2,500/day in earnings depending on size. Switching will continue over the next few quarters, timing depending on deals.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Hormuz-exposed ships and the idle rig?
qa_highlights.answer: All ships that had to exit the Strait have exited; one ship remains there on time charter to ADNOC, trading within the Strait. The idle rig came off in April and is in talks for short-term work after the monsoon; nothing has been finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue spillover from Q4 and the 46% crude operating-days figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4-to-Q1 spillover was about INR 50 crore last quarter and is not significant this quarter. The 46% refers to fixed days for the quarter, not utilisation, since crude tankers are fully spot.

544222|2026-06.headline: Akums Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% YoY to INR1,167 crore and EBITDA 35.4% to INR175 crore, led by CDMO volumes and API prices.

534680|2026-06.headline: SRG Housing management denies Rs 400 crore siphoning report and NHB red flag; no hard financials or audit timeline given on the 16 Sep 2026 call.
534680|2026-06.overview:
This was a clarification call, not an earnings call, held after an Economic Times article (10 Sep 2026) alleged Rs 400 crore of promoter-linked diversion and NPA manipulation. The MD denied all allegations and said the NHB red flag is part of a routine supervisory audit that began in July 2026, with no reasons yet shared. He cited a 39.21% capital adequacy ratio, 25% QoQ PAT growth, and no delays on lender obligations, but gave no amount for collections or liquidity. New disbursements have been slowed, the board has resolved to convert from a housing finance company to an NBFC, and promoters raised their stake by 1%.</overview>
