Working capital days targeted at or below 81 days.
Interim dividend of INR3 per share declared for FY27.
QIP of up to INR600 crore approved by board, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals; the enabling resolution is still under evaluation with no firm plan yet.
INR200 crore tools and plant capex: about 70% to be used in FY27, balance in FY28, staggered quarter on quarter.
capex_capacity: Eco-friendly tower manufacturing facility at Butibori, Nagpur commenced commercial production (started 24 April per management).
Conductor brownfield phase 1 is ready and equipment calibrated; start delayed from Q1 to Q2 FY27 pending approvals from authorities.
Tower capacity expanded; management said supply chain for projects should improve in Q1-Q2.
Acquired Gactel turnkey projects, adding IDCT tower solutions to NDCT cooling tower EPC offering.
INR200 crore capex for tools and plants, staggered use through FY27 and FY28.
demand_pricing: Order intake of about INR1,000 crore in Q1 versus the INR10,000 crore annual target; management attributed this to a 3-5 month lag between bid and award.
Quoted tenders worth over INR20,000 crore across domestic and international markets.
Won a 500 kV HVDC order from an Indian developer during the quarter.
Entered Australia with first monopole supply and seed marketing for monopoles and towers; management cited about 10,000 circuit km requirement there.
Strengthened position in MENA region; global footprint now 6 continents.
Exploring data center EPC, BESS, and drone-based mapping and survey, which management described as early stage; MoA amended to add these areas.
Management cited global electricity demand expected to nearly double by 2050 and India's plan to add 1,91,000 circuit km of transmission lines by 2032.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 order intake only about INR1,000 crore against a INR10,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 3-5 month bid-to-award lag and INR20,000 crore of bids in Q1, with a 10-15% win rate expected to convert in Q2 and Q3. Guidance of INR10,000 crore plus is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-line growth lag guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply chain disruptions in the factory (diesel, LDO, procurement delays) hurt output. It called the 5% growth the best first quarter in company history and expects Q2 to catch up.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company raising capital through a QIP when cash flows are strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the QIP is an enabling resolution for long-term working capital and to take advantage of opportunities, with no firm plan yet. It ruled out greenfield or acquisition plans for now.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to the conductor brownfield capex that was due in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said phase 1 is ready and equipment calibrated, but approvals are pending; start is now expected in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract assets rise and what do they consist of?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said contract assets include retention, TOC retention and unbilled revenue, all recoverable with provisions for doubtful amounts. Retention will rise with revenue. Management acknowledged some delays in collections.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net debt to EBITDA almost double this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to delayed collections and higher working capital deployment, expected to normalise in Q2 and return to about 0.33 by March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR80 crore related-party loan to Burberry and when will it be repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the INR80 crore loan has been outstanding for about 3 years, INR30 crore was received last year, and principal plus interest is due by 30 September 2026. Management said all loans are recoverable.

risks_watch: Order intake of about INR1,000 crore in Q1 is well below the INR10,000 crore FY27 target; Q2 tender conversion must be tracked.
Revenue growth needs to accelerate from 5% in Q1 to about 20% for the year, implying a steep ramp in Q2-Q4.
Net debt rose sharply and collections are delayed; watch the Q2 normalisation and net debt to EBITDA trend.
Related-party INR80 crore Burberry loan due by 30 September 2026.
Conductor brownfield capex start slipped to Q2 pending approvals.
Expansion into data center EPC, BESS and drones is at seed-marketing stage with no tie-ups disclosed; capital use is undefined.
The conductor kilometre figures in the investor presentation were questioned by an analyst and management said it would check the data.
544317|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margins and full-year guidance, but cautious and somewhat evasive on the Q1 revenue shortfall, order intake lag, and working capital. Several answers were hedged, such as the conductor kilometre data and the margin upside, which management deferred to later.

544802|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31% YoY to Rs 1,329 million, with EBITDA of Rs 777 million (58.45% margin) and Cordelia Sky delivered early.
544802|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 1,329 million, up 31% YoY, with PAT of Rs 585 million. H1 FY27 revenue was stated as Rs 3,230 billion (likely Rs 3,230 million, a transcript inconsistency), up 16% YoY, with H1 PAT of Rs 813 million. Cordelia Sky arrived in Mumbai on schedule, about a month early, with sailing set to start 23 October 2026, adding roughly 126% to capacity. Fuel cost per APCD roughly rose 72% in Q2 YoY (Rs 2,471 vs Rs 1,434), which management said cost about Rs 28 crore in H1 that was partly offset by fuel surcharges and cost savings.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 3,230 billion as stated (appears to be Rs 3,230 million)

segments.name: Cruise operations (Empress, Sky, SUN)
segments.commentary: Empress is the operating vessel with 796 rooms and 2,005 beds. Sky (2,400 guests, 1,002 staterooms) arrived early and starts sailing 23 October 2026. SUN, a sister ship slightly larger, is due in about 11 months.

guidance_outlook: Sky revenue to begin contributing from H2 FY27, with larger benefits as utilisation ramps up.

Management hopes fuel costs ease in Q3 and Q4, and expects fuel cost impact to be neutralised by Q4 if prices return toward original forecast. Management said it could not fully absorb the fuel increase.
Management said Q3 and Q4 are the strong quarters (wedding season, Diwali, Christmas, New Year), but declined to give forward booking numbers.
Management said it expects cruise operating margins of about 35% or higher, versus a global range of 35% to 40%.
Fuel cost impact of about Rs 12 crore is expected to remain in the current period after surcharges, per the CFO's answer on Q1 and Q2 impact.
SUN delivery remains on schedule for about 11 months from the call.
capex_capacity: Cordelia Sky (2,400 guests, 1,002 staterooms) delivered early and arrived in Mumbai on the call date; sailing starts 23 October 2026. Capacity rises about 126%.
SUN, a sister ship of Sky, is due in about 11 months, on schedule.
Advance of Rs 4,290 million toward acquisition of new vessels, interest-bearing, held through a subsidiary and an intermediary; not yet used as of the call.

Management is exploring fleet expansion beyond SUN and is at an initial discussion stage. Financing options: lease structure (fixed lease over 10 years, dollar buyout at year 10), internal accruals, or outright purchase with debt.
Sky lease cost is about USD 16 million per year, treated as an operating cost in management's numbers under Ind AS.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per passenger rose to Rs 13,645 in Q2 FY27 from Rs 10,349, driven by higher ticket price and onboard revenue.
Company started charging a fuel surcharge of USD 15-20 per person per day to offset part of the fuel cost increase.
Sky's per-guest pricing is said to be about 100% higher than Empress, and SUN's about 150% higher, driven by cabin mix (suites: 60/69 on Empress, 260 on Sky, 600 on SUN).

Management said the Indian overnight ocean and coastal cruise market was about Rs 8,301 million in FY25 and is expected to grow 20-25% CAGR over FY26-FY31. India had about 4.8 lakh cruise passenger movements in CY2025, about 89% domestic.
Management cited about 95 wedding dates in FY28 versus a typical 65-70, and plans to grow weddings and celebrations as a revenue stream.
Loyalty programme 'Chairman's Club' is being rolled out.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin expansion from operating leverage, and how will fuel, crew and port costs be controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cruise margins globally are 35-40% and the company expects to match or beat that. Shared corporate costs across more ships are expected to lower per-ship operating cost. Fuel is expected to ease, and the company plans to offset it with surcharges, itinerary changes and cost savings.

qa_highlights.question: How will the next fleet addition be financed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the lease structure used for Empress, Sky and SUN (fixed lease over 10 years, then a nominal buyout). It also cited internal accruals (about Rs 220 crore used for Sky and SUN pre-IPO) and possible debt funding for an outright purchase.

qa_highlights.question: Why did short-term borrowings rise by about Rs 344 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the funds were advanced to a subsidiary, which passed them to an intermediary to hold ready for an identified vessel deal. The money is interest-bearing and not yet used.

qa_highlights.question: How much fuel cost is unrecovered and what price increase would neutralise it?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said about Rs 12 crore of fuel cost impact remains after surcharges and savings. Management said full absorption is unlikely and it hopes to return to original forecast by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How does lease cost for Sky and SUN affect earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: Sky lease is about USD 16 million per year. Management said it is included in operating costs and pricing, and below EBITDA under Ind AS it is absorbed at PBT and PAT levels.

qa_highlights.question: What are the bookings for H2, including Empress and Sky?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward numbers, citing restrictions on forward-looking statements. It said demand was strong and that near-term bookings were hard to get.

538979|2026-06.headline: Greenlam Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 18% YoY to INR797 crore, with EBITDA before forex up 48% to INR81 crore and net profit of INR21 crore versus a loss a year earlier.
538979|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 18% YoY to about INR797 crore, while gross margin held near 53% (52.9%) despite sharp input and freight cost increases. EBITDA before forex rose 48% to INR81 crore, with margin up 210 bps to 10.2%, and net profit turned positive at INR21 crore against a INR15.5 crore loss last year. Laminates grew 7% but volumes fell 6% because about INR27 crore of export shipments slipped into Q2 due to container and vessel constraints from the West Asia conflict. The chipboard business turned EBITDA positive for the first time, and plywood losses narrowed. Management reiterated FY27 laminate revenue growth of 10-12% and total revenue growth target of 18%, but gave no visibility on freight or raw material normalisation.

financial_highlights.change: vs 53.1% in Q1 FY26; +140 bps QoQ
+48% YoY vs INR55 crore; margin +210 bps vs 8.1%
vs INR11 crore in Q1 FY26
-25% YoY vs INR26 crore; INR3.5 crore of forex was booked as finance cost last year
vs net loss of INR15.5 crore in Q1 FY26
-3 days vs 59 days in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Laminates
segments.commentary: Revenue INR596 crore, +7% YoY; sales volume 4.62 million sheets (-6% YoY) on export postponement; production 4.9 million sheets at 80% utilisation. EBITDA margin before forex 13.9% (+70 bps). Realisation INR1,240 per sheet, +14% YoY.

segments.name: Plywood and Allied
segments.commentary: Revenue INR106 crore, +20% YoY; EBITDA loss before forex narrowed to INR5 crore from INR9 crore. Plywood sales 1.66 million sq m (+19% YoY), realisation INR276 per sq m (+4%), utilisation 39% vs 28%. Engineered floors and doors together INR29 crore revenue with EBITDA loss of INR1.2 crore.

segments.name: Panel and Allied (chipboard)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR95 crore, nearly 4x YoY; EBITDA before forex INR3.4 crore vs loss of INR10 crore a year earlier. Sales volume 41,418 cubic metres (+167% YoY); realisation INR22,764 per CBM (+15%); utilisation 61% vs 30%.

guidance_outlook: Total revenue growth target of 18% for FY27 reiterated; management expects to achieve it but gave no volume/value split.
Laminate revenue growth guided at 10-12% for FY27, despite Q1 at about 7%; management said it is difficult to guide quarterly volume or margin given raw material uncertainty.
Plywood utilisation expected near 50% for FY27 (about 40% in Q1); EBITDA breakeven targeted within FY27, with timing uncertain; PAT breakeven may slip to FY28.
Chipboard utilisation expected to average about 70% in FY27; 18-20% EBITDA margin possible at full utilisation and better mix, expected around FY29.
FY27 capex budget INR130-135 crore including about INR70 crore for laminate expansion; no large new capacity planned beyond the announced laminate lines.
Debt expected to fall by about INR100 crore in FY27; FY28 repayments slightly above INR150 crore as per schedule, with stronger debt reduction thereafter as capex eases.
capex_capacity: Two new laminate press lines on track for commercial production by Q4 FY27; equipment already ordered, mostly domestic.
Laminate capacity addition aimed at specific categories already near optimum utilisation (laminate at 80% in Q1).
No plan for large capacity addition beyond the laminate lines; FY27 is a year of sweating existing assets.
Chipboard: sufficient capacity for now; management said pre-laminate share will rise as utilisation approaches 80-90%, with any new capacity decision after that, roughly 4-5 quarters away.
Peak utilisation views: laminate and chipboard up to 100%; plywood 85-100% over time; decorative veneer, floors and doors 60-65%.
demand_pricing: Domestic laminate volume fell about 7.5% YoY as real estate and project customers delayed dispatches amid building material cost increases; retail and distribution held up.
Export shipments of about INR27 crore moved from Q1 to Q2 due to container and vessel shortages and longer transit times; Middle East is about 6-7% of business.

Price hikes in April and May on chemicals (about one-third of raw material cost; up to 35% of laminate and chipboard content); partial price cuts in June and July. Net pass-through was 7-8% of the increase.
Plywood price increased modestly in April in phases, with the pass-through limited because chemical content is low; plywood realisation about INR270-275 per sq m.
Chipboard realisation INR22,764 per CBM; management sees headroom through pre-laminate and HMR premium products.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price cuts cause destocking in the trade?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stock is held on demand rather than pushed into channels, so no negative impact is expected; lower prices should help secondary demand.

qa_highlights.question: Will plywood reach EBITDA breakeven, and in which quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven is targeted within FY27, but management said it would be a single quarter, not the full year; PAT breakeven may follow in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the laminate volume decline not reflected in guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 10-12% guidance is on revenue; adding back about INR30 crore of deferred exports brings volume close to the target, and it still stands by the range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR135 crore net (INR70 crore laminate, INR40 crore maintenance, INR10-20 crore past payments), with debt expected to fall about INR100 crore; FY28 repayments are above INR150 crore per schedule.

qa_highlights.question: Is chipboard capacity enough, and when is more needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity is sufficient; management will move toward pre-laminate mix and will decide on new capacity once utilisation nears 80-90%.

qa_highlights.question: Plywood target of about INR20 per sq m EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR20 per sq m equals about 8-8.5% EBITDA, achievable only at 80-90% utilisation over time; current realisation is about INR270-275 per sq m.

500135|2026-06.headline: EPL Q1 FY27 revenue grew 25.3% (20% underlying ex pass-through) with EBITDA margin at 18.8%; revenue guidance raised to high teens.
500135|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue growth of 25.3%, or 20% underlying excluding pass-through of higher raw material prices, with EBITDA up 15.2% and margin at 18.8% (19.6% underlying). Reported PAT fell 1.4% while PBT rose 10%, which management attributed to a low base-year effective tax rate and phasing. Working capital rose roughly INR 180 crore in the quarter, mainly inventory, which management linked to raw material price inflation and safety stock. Revenue growth guidance was raised from early double digits to high teens for the next few quarters, with the 20% underlying EBITDA margin target held. Europe margins contracted on operational issues and transitional costs, and the Indovida merger received CCI approval but is still pending final approval.

financial_highlights.change: Management says in line with plan; FY PAT expected to grow double digits
Full-year ETR guided at 20-22% vs 18% in FY26

financial_highlights.value: About INR 180 crore (analyst back-calculation from net debt)
financial_highlights.change: FY26 full-year increase cited as about INR 170 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Personal Care & Beyond share of portfolio

segments.name: Beauty & Cosmetics (B&C)
segments.commentary: Growth exceeded 20% in the quarter. Management cites current global market share of 8%, with a target of up to 16% over the next few years.

segments.name: Oral Care
segments.commentary: Growth crossed 20% (management cites 24%), which it calls exceptional and not repeatable every quarter; it normally expects high single-digit growth in this mature category.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 20.2% but margins contracted on operational challenges and transitional costs. Management targets a recovery to a mid-teens margin in coming quarters; manufacturing remains in Poland and Germany.

segments.name: Americas
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 29.4%, but sequential EBITDA and EBIT fell sharply due to investments in capabilities for Brazil and the US; management says underlying margin is stronger than reported.

segments.name: EAP / Thailand
segments.commentary: EAP grew 34.3%. Thailand operations are ramping up with recent multinational customer wins.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance raised from early double digits to high teens for the next few quarters.
Underlying EBITDA margin held at 20%, to be sustained going forward.
Full-year PAT expected to grow double digits; full-year ETR expected at 20-22%.
Steady-state ETR range 18-22%, depending on country profitability mix.
On a steady-state basis, EBITDA expected to grow faster than revenue.
Management expects to operate in a high inflationary environment for some time; expects to fully recover cost increases (raw materials, freight, currency) via pricing.
capex_capacity: Significant step-up in capex and opex ahead of the growth curve, including a B&C centre of excellence in India and embellishment and decoration investments (some still outsourced).
Europe investments in extruded capacity, printing, and B&C die and tooling capability; customer service and printing centralised in Poland.
Thailand plant set up and ramping up.
Americas investments in Brazil and US capabilities.
Indovida merger: CCI approval received; completion said to be on planned timeline, pending remaining approvals.
demand_pricing: Customer contracts are on a blended cost basis, so currency depreciation, raw material and freight increases are recovered via pricing; management says entire Q1 cost impact was recovered, with some lag from certain customers.
Some old-cost inventory flowed through consumption in the quarter.
Revenue growth includes Middle East pricing impact; volume growth not disclosed as mix effects distort it.
Oral Care gains attributed to service and quality retention during the crisis, with wallet and market share gains across regions.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly INR 180 crore rise in working capital, and did receivables jump?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Deepak Goyal said the rise is mainly inventory, from higher raw material prices and building safety stock, plus capex ahead of the curve. Receivables rose in line with pricing, but ageing and quality are under control.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Europe transitional costs and is manufacturing footprint changing again?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe had operational challenges now getting focus and expects resolution in coming quarters. Manufacturing stays in Poland and Germany; it did not quantify the transitional cost adjustment.

qa_highlights.question: Does the upgrade to high-teens growth also lift PBT growth, given FX and depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed high-teens revenue and EBITDA growth for the year, with PBT translating to a similar trajectory; PAT was held back by ETR and phasing, with a double-digit FY PAT still expected.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an inventory gain from sharp price moves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said old inventory did affect consumption costs, but the company recovered the entire cost impact in Q1 and expects to continue doing so.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Americas EBITDA and EBIT fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue includes pass-through pricing, which distorts sequential comparisons, and that investments in Brazil and the US capabilities weigh on margins; underlying margin is higher than reported.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ETR outlook and post-merger tax impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year ETR guided at 20-22% (Q1 22%). Management declined to comment on consolidated post-merger ETR but said Indovida's PAT is in line with EPL's and the deal is EPS accretive.

risks_watch: Europe margin recovery: management says operational issues are being addressed, but timing is not quantified; target is mid-teens margin.
Working capital and net debt rising on inventory build and capex; watch receivables ageing and inventory levels next quarter.
Oral Care growth of 24% described as exceptional and unlikely to repeat; normal mid-to-high single digits expected.
Indovida merger still awaiting final approvals; management cannot share underlying information until then.
Americas margin pressure from ahead-of-curve investments in Brazil and US.
Effective tax rate variability (18-22% range) can keep PAT growth lagging PBT growth.
500135|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on top-line momentum and cost recovery, but defensive on margins and PAT, attributing weak Q1 PAT and Americas EBITDA to tax phasing, pricing lag and investment timing. Evasive on Indovida financials and post-merger tax until approvals are complete.

543064|2026-06.headline: Cohance Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 23% YoY to INR4,223 million and adjusted EBITDA margin dropped to 2.2%, with management guiding to a Q2 sequential rebound.
543064|2026-06.overview:
Q1 FY27 was management's stated lowest quarter ever, driven by shipment phasing in Pharma CDMO (down 38.7% YoY), a weak agrochemicals quarter, low formulation revenue and NJ Bio underperformance. Sapala grew 2.5x YoY and the standalone business delivered a 9.2% adjusted EBITDA margin, but NJ Bio's INR328 million adjusted EBITDA loss weighed on the consolidated numbers. Management guided to sequential improvement in Q2 FY27, YoY growth from H2 FY27, and margin recovery weighted to H2. Adjusted EBITDA of INR92 million and gross margin of 71.5% (vs 73%) reflected negative operating leverage. Management also laid out an integrated nucleic acid business under Dr. P.Y. Reddy with a path to full Sapala ownership by FY30, and disclosed a USFDA Form 483 with five observations at Pashamylaram.</overview>

segments.name: Pharma CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue declined 38.7% YoY on shipment phasing; commercial OTIF near 100% YTD and commercial vs development mix 57:43. Restocking order received for one molecule that destocked last year, with visibility for Q4 FY27 and FY28.

segments.name: API+ (API and formulations)
segments.commentary: API performed slightly ahead of internal expectations on favourable pricing and mix. Formulations were below expectations on an API production delay, lower demand for a mature product and a pack configuration change; Nacharam supplies have resumed but remediation continues.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue declined 34.7% YoY, led by H2-skewed AgChem phasing; Performance materials grew and were in line with plan. Two Japanese innovator qualification campaigns are scheduled in FY27.

segments.name: ADC / NJ Bio
segments.commentary: Revenue INR350 million with adjusted EBITDA loss of INR328 million. Some payload deliveries moved from Q1 into later quarters; FTE renewals are at risk from biotech funding conditions.

segments.name: Sapala (oligonucleotides)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR274 million, 2.5x YoY, after supply began on a specialised nucleic acid building blocks programme; EBITDA margin described as strong.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 to show sequential improvement in revenue and EBITDA, with movement toward YoY comparability by end of H1 and YoY growth from H2 FY27.
Margin recovery weighted to H2 FY27; CFO expects Q2 FY27 margin in line with prior-year margin percentage for the current year, accelerating from FY28.
Pharma CDMO: two molecules moved into commercial supply, with six intermediates scheduled for delivery across Q2 and Q3 FY27; customized ADC payload order on schedule for Q2 FY27.
API+: targeting seven new API filings in FY27 and around 10 formulation launches this fiscal year, with two in Q2 FY27.
Management views the USD 1 billion FY30 revenue target as an aspiration; will provide an update by December.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR598 million in Q1 FY27 to support future growth.
Commercial flow reactor at Jaggayyapet expected to be ready next quarter.
New effluent treatment facility commissioned at Ankleshwar; several API debottlenecking projects completed.
Commercialising the new amidites facility and operationalising Sapala's GMP oligonucleotide facility, with validation of priority amidites in progress.
Additional GMP manufacturing laboratory operationalised at Princeton for NJ Bio; another GMP ADC batch released.
Evaluating targeted capacity additions across small molecules, ADCs, API+ and specialty chemicals; Specialty Chemicals R&D, manufacturing and asset strategy being finalised.
demand_pricing: Pharma CDMO RFQ pipeline strengthened, with Phase 3 KSM commercial inquiries from a large pharma company; clients typically have one or two existing sources, which slows conversion.
Ten molecules in Phase 3 pipeline per management; more than 50% are expected to get approval.
Two commercial molecules face patent expiry, but the intermediates supplied are for post-expiry products and revenue impact was already seen in the past two fiscal years.
API+ price increases passed through a major part of raw material escalations, largely in Q4 FY26; API order book described as robust.
Customers in ADC payloads show positive response to MMAE and Exatecan, which are gaining traction as alternatives to Chinese suppliers.
Two CEP approvals obtained and two Korean DMFs filed during the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Growth ranges by segment over 2-3 years and beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Umang Vohra said nucleic acid CDMO could roughly double within 3-4 years, API+ could be a CAGR business and perhaps only 30-40% of its potential, and most growth becomes visible from H2 FY27. He stressed these were directional, not strategic plan targets.

qa_highlights.name: Macro and Indian CDMO RFQ trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Yann D'Herve said geopolitical diversification and US de-risking are increasing late-stage RFQs, but conversion is slow because clients already have one or two sources.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook beyond FY27 after NJ Bio and Sapala changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Agarwal said margins should rise steadily YoY with operating leverage; whether they reach 35% is hard to say. Later, he guided Q2 FY27 margin close to the prior-year level and acceleration from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Restocking contribution from the INR260 crore destocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Agarwal said it is too early to quantify the restocking, since the order for one molecule is spread over two years; clarity is expected by the next call.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses trend and merger costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Agarwal said there were no merger-related or one-off costs in Q1; the expenses are administrative and recurring and should be assumed to continue through the year.

500840|2026-06.headline: EIH Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% to Rs 698 crore and PAT to Rs 120 crore, but EBITDA grew only to Rs 207 crore as margin fell on Rajgarh ramp-up and one-offs.
500840|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 15% YoY to Rs 698 crore (Rs 609 crore) and EBITDA rose to Rs 207 crore from Rs 195 crore, so margin compressed. Management attributed the gap to Oberoi Rajgarh ramp-up, about Rs 4 crore of extra marketing, IT/automation spend, power and fuel inflation from the West Asia conflict, and Rs 6-7.5 crore of renovation write-offs at Mumbai hotels. Growth was domestically led as foreign arrivals fell about 10% in Q1. Standalone numbers were stated to mirror consolidated. PAT of Rs 120 crore is not comparable with last year, which carried a Rs 110 crore Mashobra one-time impact.

segments.name: Trident brand (upper upscale)
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 13.8% vs industry 9.2%; Mumbai TNP and BKC drove it, Trident RGI at 162 vs 155 last year.

segments.name: Oberoi Rajgarh (new, Khajuraho)
segments.commentary: Opened November 2025; in ramp-up, weighing on margins. Management expects about 3 years to stabilise and stronger winter months from October.

Hebbal (Bengaluru) to host an Oberoi and a Trident plus about 763,000 sq ft retail/F&B, total development area over 1.3 million sq ft.

qa_highlights.question: Did flight catering mix and renovation, Rajgarh ramp-up drive the margin gap, and will these persist?

qa_highlights.question: May and June RevPAR growth looked much higher than the quarter. Will that persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to forecast the full year; said Q2 business on books versus last year was very positive.

qa_highlights.question: Will large events like BRICS and the Aviation show boost RevPAR?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, large events have a ripple effect across cities, with Delhi and Mumbai benefiting from overseas visitors to Bengaluru's air show.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Kolkata Oberoi delayed and how firm is the new timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Heritage building restoration uncovered fire and structural safety work, plus a Kolkata construction halt after a fatal incident about two months ago; halt still in place pending building-by-building approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cost overrun on the Oberoi Grand from delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays add cost, the size depending on reasons, and the bigger impact is deferred revenue and profit from delayed market entry.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Mumbai outperformance continue, and what is foreign tourist trend in recent months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bombay market was strong and EIH beat it, but would not forecast 20% outperformance; Q2 foreign trend expected to stay weak.

qa_highlights.question: Rajgarh stabilisation timeline and winter outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3 years to stabilise for a leisure hotel, with winter months from October expected to do considerably better.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the base business margin fall after adjusting for Rajgarh and one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ex-Rajgarh margin was about 30.6% vs last year, with roughly Rs 9 crore YoY impact from power and fuel, Rs 4 crore marketing, IT and renovation costs. Management declined to disclose management fee income.

544055|2026-06.headline: Muthoot Microfin Q1 FY27: record Q1 disbursement of INR2,644 crore, cost of funds down to 10.13%, credit cost 2.6%, and AUM growth guidance raised to 20%.
544055|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the start of an execution-led turnaround, with disbursements of INR2,644 crore (about 49% above Q1 FY26) and collection efficiency near 98%. Cost of funds fell 14 bps QoQ to 10.13% before the benefit of the AA- CRISIL upgrade, and credit cost eased to 2.6% from 2.8%. PPOP rose about 43% YoY and 3% QoQ, and AUM grew 18% YoY. Management raised FY27 AUM growth guidance to 20%, ROA to the upper end of 3.3%, and ROE to around 18%, and said NIM expansion would show from Q2.

financial_highlights.change: about 49% above Q1 FY26; highest Q1 ever

financial_highlights.value: Up about 43% YoY and about 3% QoQ

financial_highlights.change: Full-year FY27 NIM guided 12.3%-12.5%; management said 12.5% upper end is achievable

segments.name: Joint Liability Group (JLG)
segments.commentary: Yield on group loans about 24.85% after a rate hike from 23.5% at end of Q1. Remains one of three priority products.

segments.name: Individual loans
segments.commentary: About INR3,200 crore book with 0.02% 30+ delinquency and no 60+ or 90+. Yield about 23.5%. Built on a creamy layer of about 8.5-9 lakh customers with 700+ scores. Repayments are 100% digital.

segments.name: Gold loans (referral and co-lending)
segments.commentary: Disbursing about INR100 crore per month since April; about INR350-360 crore disbursed to date. Q1 was almost entirely referral business. Co-lending split is 60% on Muthoot Microfin's book and 40% on the parent's book. Referral earns 1.5%.

segments.name: Loan against property and consumer durables
segments.commentary: LAP yield 18%-22%. Consumer durable loans are a pilot of about INR500 crore at 22%-23% yield, funded through CP at about 8.1%-8.2%.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance raised to 20% for FY27.
Disbursement plan exceeds INR12,000 crore for FY27, averaging about INR1,000 crore per month.
Cost of funds targeted to reach single digits by end of FY27, with AA- rating benefit still to flow through.
FY27 ROA guided at 3.3% (upper end expected), ROE around 18% (upper end). Management expects 4%-4.5% ROA within about 18 months and about 5% by FY30.
Credit cost guidance of 2.7%-3.5% for FY27, now expected to be better; long-term normalised range 2%-2.25%.
NIM guidance 12.3%-12.5%; NIM expansion expected from Q2 as liquidity drag eases.
Digital collection to reach about 75% by 2030, possibly earlier. Currently about 40%, improving about 6% per quarter.
Branch count to reach 1,740-1,750 by end FY27 from about 1,670 now.
capex_capacity: Branches about 1,670 now, targeted at 1,740-1,750 by end FY27. Expansion focus on Andhra Pradesh and Assam, plus north, east and west geographies.
AUM per branch rose to INR8.65 crore from about INR7 crore a year ago. Management targets INR12-13 crore per branch.
Gold loans use parent Muthoot Finance branches for storage and assessment, so no separate gold branch capex is needed.
Consumer durables pilot of INR500 crore to be expanded depending on results.
demand_pricing: Industry AUM contracted, but quality is improving. Management says larger, well-capitalised players are gaining share. Industry active customers have fallen from about 8 crore at peak to about 6 crore.

Group yield raised to 24.85% from 23.5% at end of Q1, with no further hike planned for now. Management said the benefit should go to NIM rather than customers.

Liquidity is ample. About INR5,000 crore of sanctions are in hand, plus INR1,000 crore under CGFMU of which only INR200 crore has been drawn. About 20% of AUM is targeted for CGFMU cover; the application is pending.
Management said El Nino rainfall deficit fell from 43% to about 12%. Less than 2% of customers are directly exposed to agri activity in sensitive regions.

qa_highlights.question: Can disbursement return to INR1,000 crore per month, and can AUM growth exceed 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR1,000 crore per month is achievable, with FY27 disbursement above INR12,000 crore. Q1 at INR2,644 crore was the slowest quarter, and Q2 onward should rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended yield, given that the incremental cost of borrowing fell while NIM stayed flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended portfolio yield is about 23%. Reported yield is diluted by non-performing assets in the denominator. Management said Q1 NIM is up about 50 bps YoY, and yield expansion will follow as collections from NPAs improve.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Assam flood or the broader monsoon risk affect the book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has no exposure to upper Assam, where floods are seasonal, and its lower-Assam portfolio is unaffected so far. Natural calamity insurance covers all customers, including drought.

qa_highlights.question: How do the direct assignment (DA) income and gold referral and co-lending work?
qa_highlights.answer: DA income is booked under net gain on fair value changes, not interest income. Q1 DA was about INR355 crore, and FY26 DA was about INR1,600 crore. Gold co-lending began only at quarter-end, so about 98% of Q1 gold business was referral.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 2.7%-3.5% has been beaten, with Q1 at 2.6%. Management expects FY27 to come in below 2.7%, with a long-term normal of 2%-2.25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and ROA/ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM guidance is 12.3%-12.5%, with the upper end expected. FY27 ROA is guided at 3.3% (upper end) and ROE at about 18%. Management targets 4%-4.5% ROA in about 18 months and about 5% by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: What are the MFI vs non-MFI mix targets?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM mix is at 76:24 (JLG to non-JLG) now and is expected to end FY27 at about 70:30. Management's long-term target is 55:45 on AUM and 60:40 on balance sheet after DA.

544803|2026-06.headline: Advit Jewels Q1 FY27 total income rose 37.35% YoY to INR35.40 crore, with PAT up 37.86% to INR8.19 crore and a 23.12% PAT margin.
544803|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR35.40 crore (up 37.35% YoY from about INR25.78 crore), EBITDA of INR11.72 crore (33.12% margin, up 33.02%) and PAT of INR8.19 crore (up 37.86%). Revenue mix in the quarter was about 78% B2B and 22% B2C, both linked to bridal demand. Management said the company is now debt-free and is holding unutilised IPO proceeds for working capital and expansion. The call focused on the planned Jaipur flagship, company-owned metro stores, a franchise model for Tier 2 and smaller cities, and new categories (pret and men's jewellery). qa_highlights.answer: About 78% B2B and 22% B2C, both linked to bridal demand.

qa_highlights.answer: Metro cities will have company-owned stores and Tier 2 and smaller cities franchises. Franchise partners fund inventory, about INR6-8 crore per store. Franchise protocols are due in about one month.

PAT was INR20 crores against INR20.92 crores a year earlier, as higher gas, logistics and ocean freight costs and working-capital-driven finance costs weighed on earnings. qa_highlights.question: How is the demand outlook across infrastructure, construction, water, solar and industrial for the rest of FY27?

qa_highlights.question: What is the end-use mix, and which new industries are emerging?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% construction and infrastructure, 20% water and oil and gas transport, rest engineering, solar and specialised; data centres are an emerging segment.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for EBITDA per ton to reach INR3,750-4,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to exceed INR4,000/t once the three new plants reach critical mass and extra dealer rebates are withdrawn; the target is for FY28 per later comments.

qa_highlights.question: Why was finance cost about INR15 crores against a much lower year-end debt base?

qa_highlights.question: Has the INR300 crore capex guidance changed to INR650 crores?

EBITDA came in at INR101 crores, a margin of about 16%, attributed to lower revenue, product mix tweaks and raw material inflation. qa_highlights.question: Why raise so much debt and how do tariffs affect the US business?
qa_highlights.answer: The recent NCD raise balances debt tenors and maturities and is not incremental capital. US tariff policy flip-flops created inflation and altered demand; tariff outlook has stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: How will fabric capacity of 90 million meters be used versus the 61 million meters home capacity?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Sheeting ramp-down about profitability or US challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: US market share loss, tariff-driven pricing pressure and client concentration led to repositioning the business as Himatsingka 2.0.

risks_watch: Revenue visibility during transition: management warned of volatility over the next couple of quarters.
Sheeting rightsizing and pricing pressure in home textiles, especially US, with utilisation at 52%.
Ramp-up execution of Yarn and Fabric Solutions, with no quarterly revenue split disclosed.
Raw material inflation and margin pressure (EBITDA margin ~16%).
Timing of UK and EU FTAs and Apparel Solutions launch; equity initiatives to be shared later without details.
514043|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the long-term strategic direction but cautious near term, repeatedly flagging volatility and transition for a couple of quarters. Evasive on quarterly vertical revenue split and on the timing and size of equity initiatives.
key_quotes: So our efforts are essentially geared to transforming the Himatsingka model and steering away from U.S. concentration, steering away from client concentration, as we've seen in the Home Textile space, that seems to be a cornerstone of the home textile, let's say, world.
We're keeping our capex limited to just maintenance and organic capex requirements, which is why I keep saying that all of these things are using our existing campus and infrastructure.
So therefore, all in all, we will see a reduction in net debt by the end of fiscal.

532929|2026-06.headline: Brigade Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 36% (from 28%) on real estate margin recovery, though net sales fell 5% to INR1,061 crore.
532929|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue was INR1,179 crore with EBITDA of INR425 crore, and PAT of INR217 crore (up 37% YoY). Real estate EBITDA margin recovered to 21% from 12%, driven by recognition of higher-margin projects, while realisation rose 21% YoY to INR14,256 per sq ft. Q1 had no launches; the Morgan Heights relaunch was stalled after SEIAA revoked its environmental clearance, and management cut that project from the launch schedule. FY27 presales guidance of INR9,000 crore was reiterated, with launches back-ended and the launch pipeline trimmed to about 9.36 million sq ft for the rest of FY27.</overview>

segments.name: Real Estate
segments.commentary: Net sales INR707 crore and EBITDA INR150 crore (21% margin vs 12%); realisation INR14,256 per sq ft (+21% YoY) on price increases and mix shift to higher-value homes. Q1 had no new launches; Q1 presales were about INR1,050 crore per analyst question.

segments.name: Leasing (commercial office)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR328 crore (+9% YoY), EBITDA INR230 crore at 70% margin; operational GLA 8 million sq ft, occupancy 88%, gross leasing 0.22 million sq ft in Q1, rental collections 99%. Office revenue cited as INR200 crore.

segments.name: Hospitality (BHVL)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR144 crore, EBITDA INR45 crore; ADR +7%, occupancy 76% (from 74.5%), RevPAR and EBITDA up about 9%. West Asia conflict cut event/MICE business by about 10%.

segments.name: Retail (Orion Mall)
segments.commentary: Footfalls +11% YoY, retail sales +35% YoY, anchor retailer sales +64%, F&B +46%, electronics +33%, cinema admissions +20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales guidance of INR9,000 crore reiterated; management says sales run-rate per quarter should rise as launches start from Q2.
Launch pipeline for the rolling four quarters is 12.36 million sq ft (residential 12.4 million sq ft at about INR13,400 crore GDV; commercial about 4.03 million sq ft), excluding Morgan Heights.
Within this, about 9.36 million sq ft is planned for the rest of FY27 (Q2 about 2.36 million sq ft, H2 about 7 million sq ft) and about 3 million sq ft slips into Q1 FY28.
Hyderabad Neopolis 2 (about 2 million sq ft) is now expected in Q2; Whitefield-Hoskote is now a Q3 launch; Hyderabad launch pulled forward to Q3 or earlier.
Commercial leasing revenue expected to grow at about 20% CAGR over the next 5 to 6 years; about 6 million sq ft of commercial space to come into the market mainly in FY30.
Operating contribution margin improvement of 5% to 6% expected to be largely retained through FY27; management expects margins to move into the 20s, from late teens at year end last year.
Debt-equity to stay well under 1x, with capex and BD funded first from internal accruals.
BHVL to add 1,700 keys in pipeline, targeting 3,300 keys by FY31; Courtyard by Marriott Chennai WTC (45 keys) to launch in FY27.
capex_capacity: Launch pipeline: Q1 had none; Morgan Heights (about 0.7 million sq ft unsold, attributable value about INR650 crore) removed from launch schedule pending High Court and SEIAA resolution.

Commercial pipeline launched in Q1 about 4 million sq ft across Bengaluru and Hyderabad (Brigade HRC Atrium, an industrial block, Brigade United, Cauvery, Orion Mall Hyderabad), all to be held, none for sale.
WTC Bengaluru: about 1.13 million sq ft building, Brigade holds 0.71 million sq ft, about 50% leased, about 375,000 sq ft vacant.
Upcoming commercial: 2.6 million sq ft Bengaluru (about 65%), 1.3 million sq ft Chennai (about 31%), 0.2 million sq ft Kochi.
Capex for commercial projects to be spent over the next 4 to 5 years; per sq ft capex quoted at INR4,000 to INR10,000 (construction cost, excluding land).

Land bank about 56 to 57 million sq ft, which includes the launch pipeline. Kengeri land parcel in litigation; KIADB 75-acre Devanahalli parcel residential component reduced to about 3 to 4 lakh sq ft.
demand_pricing: Pan-India residential sales down 6% YoY in April-June (Anarock); Bengaluru and Hyderabad among the only major cities with sales growth.
Q1 business development: INR2,400 crore GDV across 2.7 million sq ft, mainly Hyderabad.
Office leasing demand led by industrial and manufacturing, flexible workspace and life sciences; GCCs 58% of gross leasing; IT/ITES 26% of portfolio.
WTC Bengaluru: large-occupier RFPs (1-2 lakh sq ft) postponed due to West Asia crisis; leasing shifting to 20,000 to 40,000 sq ft deals; mark-to-market rent increase of 10% to 15%.

Hospitality: domestic corporate, weddings and social demand offset weaker international travel; Kochi (Four Points rebranded to Courtyard by Marriott) occupancy back in the 70s in Q2, ADR uplift expected at 15% to 20%.

544405|2026-06.headline: Belrise Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR25,465 million, EBITDA margin 11.5%, PAT up 9% to INR1,217 million.
544405|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY, led by manufacturing revenue up 20% to INR21,979 million, while trading revenue fell about 19% on Middle East disruption. EBITDA rose 5% to INR2,933 million, with margin down to 11.5%, and manufacturing EBITDA margin at 12.7%. Management reported a INR17,000 million QIP and the Hyva India tipper acquisition (completion expected Q3 FY27), and a run of new order wins across two-wheeler, renewable energy, and commercial vehicles. Management said cost pressures from steel, polymer, staff and energy have peaked and FY27 EBITDA margins should stay broadly stable versus FY26.

segments.name: Two- and three-wheeler
segments.commentary: Contributed about 81.4% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27; management said segment revenue grew about 18% YoY, below industry growth of roughly 20-25%, attributed to customer mix.

segments.name: Passenger vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 4.6% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27; H-One high-tensile steel capability up to 1470 MPa cited as a differentiator.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.5% of manufacturing revenue; four-wheeler and CV revenue grew about 18% YoY per management opening remarks; Hyva India tipper acquisition announced 4 August 2026.

segments.name: Others (incl. aerospace, defence, renewables, trading)
segments.commentary: About 5.5% of manufacturing revenue. Trading business fell about 19% YoY due to Middle East crisis and logistics; management expects mid-teens group revenue growth. Aerospace and defence target is at least 10% of consolidated revenue in the medium term.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 EBITDA margins broadly stable versus FY26, with no material margin impact from input costs given back-to-back pricing.
Group revenue growth guided at mid-teens with stable EBITDA margins.
Majority of INR17,000 million QIP proceeds to be deployed within FY27, mainly for inorganic opportunities in aerospace and four-wheeler/CV, plus some organic growth.
Hyva India tipper business acquisition expected to complete in Q3 FY27; deal to be EPS and ROCE accretive from day one per management's stated threshold.
Aerospace and defence to reach at least 10% of consolidated revenue in the medium term.

New programs (chassis for fast-growing 2W OEM, US solar tracker assemblies, Sambhajinagar 2W chassis, brake assemblies) to start production in Q4 FY27; margin pressure expected to ease in coming quarters as pass-through takes effect.
capex_capacity: Four new facilities coming up, including brownfield facilities; fixed costs ramping ahead of revenue, per management.
Bangalore brownfield facility to host new 2W chassis program (annual revenue above INR650 million), SOP expected Q4 FY27.
US solar tracker sheet-metal assembly setup to support about 2.5 GW annual supplies; peak annual revenue above INR1,500 million; production from Q4 FY27.
Expansion at existing Maharashtra facilities to support a 59-assembly EV localisation program for a large Indian CV OEM.
Hyva acquisition includes three manufacturing facilities in Pune, Jamshedpur and Bangalore.
Management declined to disclose utilisation or ramp-up details for specific facilities such as Bangalore and Haridwar.
demand_pricing: Order wins: 2W/3W chassis for fast-growing OEM (above INR650 million annual revenue, on top of about INR900 million fuel tank and exhaust win last quarter); cumulative about INR1,550 million with that OEM, about INR2,000 million including suspension and braking wins.
Suspension systems now supplied to five 2W/3W OEMs, including a new Vietnamese 2W entrant in India, with suspension and braking.
Two-wheeler chassis order for an existing model at a large 2W OEM's Sambhajinagar plant, potential annual revenue of about INR500 million.
Management attributed slower 2W/3W growth to a customer mix gap with faster-growing OEMs, with new OEM ramps expected in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Trading business decline was due to Middle East crisis hitting African, Asian and Middle Eastern demand and logistics; management says the worst is behind it.
Input cost pressure (steel, polymer, energy, logistics, minimum wage hike) persisted in Q1; management expects pass-through in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new chassis order additional to earlier two-wheeler wins from South India?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it is over and above the exhaust and fuel tank win from last quarter (about INR900 million), making about INR1,550 million cumulative annual run-rate with that one OEM.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin pressure remains from commodities, staff costs and energy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity, staff and energy/transport cost pressures have largely peaked, with staff cost rise tied to the annual increment cycle and pre-hiring for four new facilities; pass-through expected in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Can management quantify the benefit from raw-material pass-through and the trading decline's margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify either on the call and offered to respond offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did 2W/3W growth (about 18%) lag industry growth (about 20-25%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a customer mix issue, as some faster-growing OEMs it does not work with closely gained share; newly penetrated OEMs should add volumes in Q3 and Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aerospace and defence revenue outlook and the Plasan Sasa defence opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least 10% of manufacturing revenue from aerospace and defence in the short-to-medium term; Belrise already exports parts to Plasan Sasa in Israel, with progress described as gradual given geopolitics.

qa_highlights.question: Can H-One and Mag Filters revenue be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said it manages the business as one group and will not disclose segment-level numbers for H-One or Mag Filters.

543664|2026-06.headline: Kaynes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 40% to INR946 crore and EBITDA rose 31% to INR147.6 crore, but operating cash flow was negative INR259 crore as inventory and metering receivables rose.
543664|2026-06.overview:
Revenue grew 40% YoY to INR946 crore, driven by EMS (standalone EMS up 53%, overseas up 327% on the August Electronics acquisition), while smart metering fell 12% YoY to about INR204 crore as management deliberately curbed supplies over collections. EBITDA was INR147.6 crore at a 15.6% margin, with management flagging margin pressure from component and PCB cost inflation and lead times of 6 to 8 months. Negative operating cash flow was about INR259 crore (management also cited INR235 crore in another bridge), with inventory up about INR177 crore and receivables up about INR68 crore. OSAT and PCB commissioning remains guided for Q3 FY27, with a FY27 revenue target of INR450 to 500 crore across both.</overview>

segments.name: EMS (overall, incl. overseas)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR854 crore including GST, with 40% overall EMS growth and about 48% growth cited by management; collections of INR847 crore. Receivables in EMS were about INR613 crore at quarter end versus INR606 crore at the start.

segments.name: Smart metering (GridCrest)
segments.commentary: Sales about INR240 crore including GST against collections of INR88 crore, so production and supply were halted. Metering receivables rose from INR1,158 crore to INR1,311 crore; about INR200 crore was received in early July.

segments.name: OSAT (Kaynes Semicon)
segments.commentary: Capex to date about INR700 crore; government subsidy of INR170 crore received till July 2026. Commercial billing expected from Q3 FY27; Unit 2 on track for operation by Q3 FY27. Mitsui partnership for Japan access announced.

segments.name: PCB (Kaynes Circuit)
segments.commentary: Capex to date about INR500 crore, with about INR250 crore in transit. Commercial production to start next quarter; one global customer has requested the entire capacity and trials are ongoing with a vendor code approved.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth committed at 2x the market growth; no absolute top-line number given. Market grew about 17% in Q1.
OSAT and PCB combined FY27 revenue target INR450 to 500 crore, with revenue starting from Q3 FY27.
FY27 capex plan: about INR300 crore OSAT, about INR300 crore PCB and about INR250 crore EMS; Q1 spend about INR230 crore in total across these.
Management expects profitability to take a couple of quarters to normalise; FY27 described as a difficult, tough year.
Management expects receivables turnaround in the metering business and cash-positive position by end of FY27.
Working capital to be reported on a rolling 12-month basis going forward.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR180 crore (per management in the call), against a broader plan of about INR300 crore each for OSAT and PCB and about INR250 crore for EMS.
Capex in FY26 was INR473 crore for OSAT and INR324 crore for PCB.
Kaynes Semicon Unit 2 and Kaynes Circuit Chennai remain on track to be operational by Q3 FY27, despite minor slippage from West Asia-related equipment and logistics disruption.
Government subsidy of INR170 crore received in OSAT till July 2026, with more subsidies expected to fund further capex.

First 3U satellite in prototype; launch targeted mid-next year pending regulatory testing and an ISRO launch date (PSLV or GSLV). Titanium gas bottle manufacturing via Crio Precision and Aerotech for ISRO and DRDO.
demand_pricing: Order book of more than INR8,900 crore; management said Q1 order additions exceeded deliveries.

New logos include a second-largest Indian two-wheeler EV maker (serial supply begun after about 8 months of development), German and French global brands, and a leading Indian wireless operator; management cited about 72 customer visits in the quarter.
Component prices up about 30% to 35% per management; PCB prices up about 3x; lead times more than 6 to 8 months in some categories; PCB suppliers demanding advance payment.
FX impact on imports about 3.3% of import level, per management.
Pass-through to customers is on a quarter-on-quarter basis and may lag; management said agreements with strategic customers allow some price pass-through.
Aerospace recovered in the quarter; management said growth was seen across railways, automotive, aerospace and defence.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EMS growth excluding metering, and what is the EBITDA bridge and metering strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said overall EMS grew 40% and metering 28% (per one answer), with standalone EMS up 53% and metering down 12%. Lower other income after QIP proceeds (about 2.5 points on PBT/PAT) and higher depreciation were cited for margin pressure. Management said it is exploring models to divest the service portion of metering to keep receivables off the balance sheet, with details promised by February.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cash flow from operations and metering revenue for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operating cash flow was negative about INR259 crore (inventory up INR177 crore and receivables up INR68 crore), versus negative INR379 crore in Q1 FY26. Another bridge given later cited INR235 crore; the company's cash profit was about INR158 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the receivables, inventory and payables figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Total receivables (current and non-current) rose from about INR1,765 crore to INR1,925 crore. Inventory days were about 105 at Q1 end versus 96 earlier. Management said the 12-month rolling receivable days were about 163 and the quarterly figure about 190.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 revenue growth and the OSAT/PCB FY27 and FY28 scale-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to 2x market growth without an absolute number, citing market volatility. OSAT and PCB together are targeted at INR450 to 500 crore of FY27 revenue from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much of component cost inflation is captured and will gross margins compress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX impact was about 3.3% of imports and back-to-back customer pass-through covers most of the rest, but pass-through may lag by a quarter. Ramesh Kunhikannan said FY27 would be a tough year with margins under pressure, though planned requirements would be met.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and PCB margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex plan is about INR300 crore each for OSAT and PCB and INR250 crore for EMS, with about INR230 crore spent in Q1. Management declined to give PCB margin or ROCE targets, saying it was too early and disputing that PCB margins had fallen.

511144|2026-06.headline: Axis Solutions Q1 FY27 revenue rose 78% YoY to ₹48.98 crore, with EBITDA up 122% to ₹6.21 crore and PAT up 77% to ₹3.09 crore.
511144|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was ₹48.98 crore against ₹27.48 crore a year earlier, and EBITDA margin expanded 252 bps to 12.70%. PAT rose 77% to ₹3.09 crore, but PAT margin was flat at about 6.3% as tax was provided for the first time this year. Management gave no numeric FY27 guidance, only qualitative comments that growth and profit would be "very, very good". Emerging segments (hydrogen storage, Kavach, EV charging) are still pre-revenue, and the company said hydrogen margins are not yet in the financials.

financial_highlights.value: ₹6.21 crore (stated as ₹6.22 crore in one place)

financial_highlights.change: Nil in Q1 FY26; some carried-forward tax provision
Majority expected to execute in FY27, some over 1-2 years

segments.name: Industrial engineering and systems
segments.commentary: 59% of Q1 FY27 revenue vs 28.6% in Q1 FY26, the largest vertical now. Management attributed the mix shift to lumpy timing in the first quarter.

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: 26% of Q1 FY27 revenue vs 55.8% in Q1 FY26. Water share fell as the mix moved toward industrial engineering.

segments.name: Automation and digitalisation
segments.commentary: About 15% of Q1 FY27 revenue vs 15.6% in Q1 FY26, broadly flat share.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 guidance. Management said growth would be 'very, very good' compared with last year and profit 'really very good', and referred to the quarterly results for projections.
Most of the ₹365 crore open order book is expected to be executed in FY27, with some orders running 1-2 years.

Green hydrogen, Kavach and EV charging are described as emerging. No revenue timing was committed; management said commercialisation activities are ongoing and no hydrogen margins are in the financials yet.
MRO/AMC/warranty recurring revenue is about 5-6% of total revenue and is expected to increase over one to two years.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing is in Ahmedabad only, across five purpose-built facilities totalling about 1,40,000 sq ft, with end-to-end manufacturing under one roof.
Management said doubling current turnover would not need new facilities, but new facilities will be needed in the near future. No capex amount or timeline was given.
Saudi Arabia subsidiary (AxisSol Arabia) was incorporated Feb-Jun 2026, with manufacturing there planned but not dated.
Company commits about 10% of annual profit to R&D. It has a registered in-house R&D centre and more than 130 manufactured products.
demand_pricing: Management said it does not compromise on price against competition and credited product life cycles, registrations and in-house R&D for growth.
ATEX and IECEx certifications allow supply to the Middle East, Southeast Asia and Europe. Import substitutes for European and Chinese products were cited.
Named clients include IOC, HPCL, NTPC, Tata Chemicals, BHEL, L&T, Reliance, Adani, Petronas, ADNOC and KAFCO. Customer names were given without order values.
Receivables: management said high ageing is concentrated in Feb-Mar year-end billing; normal terms are 30-60 days or letters of credit.

qa_highlights.question: How do you see growth in the coming years and where will FY27 end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers, saying projections are in the quarterly results. It said growth and profit will be 'very, very good' versus last year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ₹365 crore order book be executed this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of it is expected in FY27, with some orders closing in the following year. New large orders would be announced.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for NSE listing, promoter stake reduction and fundraising?
qa_highlights.answer: NSE listing depends on first meeting minimum public shareholding (MPS) norms, and there is time to do so. No instrument, amount or dilution has been decided and nothing is pending with the board.

qa_highlights.question: What is the green hydrogen product, its patents and when will it generate revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a solid-state hydrogen storage technology, described as a first in India. Management holds both design and technology patents. No revenue timing was confirmed, and commercialisation is ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kavach work and are there orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Axis is in proof-of-concept with several companies and got approval for Kavach. No Kavach orders were disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins low despite about 13 granted patents?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hydrogen revenue and margins are not yet in the financials. It said one industrial engineering and systems patent is in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: MRO, AMC and warranty revenue is about 5-6% of total revenue and is expected to rise over one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and peak revenue capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give utilisation or peak revenue. It said products are customised rather than batch-produced, and the facilities would not constrain the top line.

risks_watch: Revenue mix swung sharply by vertical (industrial engineering 59%, water 26%), so quarterly comparisons are noisy. Management said it is working to neutralise this.
Pre-revenue bets (hydrogen storage, Kavach, EV charging) carry execution and timing risk, and management would not commit to dates.
Receivables ageing was flagged by an analyst; management attributed it to year-end billing. Q2 debtor data should be checked.
MPS compliance (minimum public shareholding) could lead to promoter dilution or a fundraise. Holds 85.64% promoter stake, 12.62% public and 1.74% DIIs.
Tax was nil in Q1 FY26 and ₹37 lakh in Q1 FY27, so PAT growth (77%) lagged PBT growth (about 98%). Watch the effective tax rate.
Disclosure is limited: management declined to give revenue, capacity, subsidiary-level or order-level detail. The call was also marred by audio problems and unanswered questions.
511144|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins, but evasive on guidance, order detail, hydrogen and Kavach commercial timing, and capacity. Management repeatedly deferred to the quarterly results or one-on-one meetings.

544279|2026-06.headline: Godavari Biorefineries Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR2.6 crores (0.5% margin) as sugar-ethanol losses offset a 53% jump in bio-based chemicals EBITDA.
544279|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 4.6% YoY to INR557.9 crores and total income rose 4.9% to INR559.9 crores, but EBITDA dropped to INR2.6 crores from INR6.5 crores. Bio-based chemicals grew revenue 19.4% to INR168.7 crores with EBITDA up 53% to INR19.2 crores, while the integrated sugar, cogeneration and ethanol segment's EBITDA loss widened to INR14.6 crores. The company commissioned a 200 KLPD grain-based distillery at Sameerwadi, taking total distillery capacity to 800 KLPD, and announced a further INR25 crores debottlenecking investment in bio-based specialty chemicals. Consolidated net loss widened to INR19.3 crores from INR16 crores.

vs INR16 crores loss in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Integrated sugar, cogeneration and ethanol revenue
financial_highlights.change: vs INR382.8 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Integrated sugar, cogeneration and ethanol EBITDA
financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR4.5 crores in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Bio-based chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR168.7 crores (+19.4% YoY) and EBITDA INR19.2 crores (+53%), margin 11.4% vs 8.9%, attributed to product mix and debottlenecking benefits. Management guides to about INR190 crores revenue next quarter.

segments.name: Integrated sugar, cogeneration and ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue INR377.9 crores, flat YoY, with EBITDA loss of INR14.6 crores vs INR4.5 crores loss a year ago. Management cited feedstock conditions, higher manufacturing cost and ethanol tender allotments; better sugar realisations provided partial support.

guidance_outlook: Bio-based chemicals revenue expected at about INR190 crores in Q2 FY27, sustained thereafter.
INR25 crores debottlenecking in bio-based specialty chemicals, expected to complete by early FY28, targeting about INR240 crores quarterly revenue at full penetration.
Evaluating 160 KLPD fungible capacity addition within the existing 800 KLPD, mainly a maize grain-preparation front end; no firm timeline or return numbers given.
Debt levels expected broadly similar, with no major change in debt-equity structure.
DME pilot trial results expected by March 2027.

Triple-negative breast cancer molecule: CDSCO permission for preliminary efficacy trials hoped for by end of Q3 FY27; about INR20 crores spend over the next 2 to 3 years to reach preliminary efficacy.

Additional INR25 crores investment in debottlenecking bio-based specialty chemicals, completion expected early FY28.
Evaluating a 160 KLPD maize grain-preparation front end to use idle fermentation and distillation capacity if sugar diversion rises.
Bio-butanol: MoU with Synthomer for use as chemical intermediate; engaging on a government call for butanol pathways.
DME in pilot trials, progressing as planned.

Timing of CDSCO approval for TNBC trials and DME pilot outcomes by March 2027.
Whether the chemicals run-rate reaches about INR190 crores next quarter and INR240 crores after expansion.
Sugar-ethanol capacity diversion decisions and the 160 KLPD maize front-end investment size and returns, not yet disclosed.

532699|2026-06.headline: Royal Orchid Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36% YoY to about INR 107 crore, but PAT fell to INR 6.4 crore from INR 10.9 crore.

Reported PAT declined to about INR 6.4 crore from INR 10.9 crore, which management attributed to higher finance costs, depreciation and Ind AS effects, and ramp-up of leased properties. On a non-Ind AS basis, management said Q1 FY27 PAT was about INR 9.8 crore versus about INR 12 crore a year earlier. Five managed/franchised hotels with 237 keys were added, contributing negligibly to the quarter; management also flagged about INR 2.5 crore of GST input credit loss from a change in GST treatment and an April-June demand hit from the Middle East flight disruption.

financial_highlights.change: vs about INR 12 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: about INR 2.5 crore in the quarter
financial_highlights.change: company-wide, due to 5% output GST regime

segments.name: JLO hotels (owned, leased, JV)
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 70% and ADR INR 6,233 vs INR 5,488 a year earlier. These hotels account for the bulk of revenue; ICONIQA is the newest asset, opened November 2025.

segments.name: Managed and franchised portfolio
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 60.8% and ADR INR 4,300 vs INR 4,031 a year earlier. Management fee income is the revenue line here; fees grew about 14% last year on 7,700 keys.

segments.name: ICONIQA (single hotel)
segments.commentary: Management said Q1 occupancy was hit by April-June travel disruption (April about 79%, May about 60%, June about 70%) versus about 80% in Feb-March. Breakeven estimated at about INR 85 crore annualised revenue; target INR 100 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management is targeting ROCE of 20%+ within about a year, once ICONIQA stabilises.
Target of INR 100 crore annualised ICONIQA revenue, dependent on Q3 and Q4 performance.
Keys expected to rise from about 7,700 to 11,000+ in the next 24 months; 50+ signed hotels to open over 18-24 months.
Management declined to give a revenue growth rate for the next 2-3 years and said it is not assuring any date for INR 150 crore management fees; Vision 2030 target not specified as revenue or fees.
Keshav Baljee expects employee cost to stabilise within range over about another year as new properties open.
capex_capacity: Added five hotels with 237 keys in Q1 FY27, all managed or franchised, with no capex by the company.
Portfolio about 7,700 keys currently with 11,000+ signed; 50+ hotels signed for opening in next 18-24 months.
Shift toward revenue-share and lease models adds capex and upfront Ind AS cost; management says management contracts carry limited maintenance capex.
Premiumisation plan: about 1,000 five-star keys across owned, leased and JV hotels being upgraded for higher ADR.
Lakshminarayan Palace in Vadodara opened, branded under an ICONIQA collection brand, positioned upper upscale.
demand_pricing: April-June demand hit by flight cancellations linked to the war; management said about 50% of India inbound travel runs through three Middle Eastern carriers, which went to zero.
Business hotels seasonally weakest in Q1 (April-June); management said Q3-Q4 are the strongest quarters.
Leisure destinations performed well while business and airport hotels were hit.
Rain in Mumbai in July and August has weighed on ICONIQA occupancy.
Nearby supply: Fairmont (50 keys), Hilton Garden Inn (170 keys) and Roswin (110 keys) opened around the same time as ICONIQA, adding about 1,000 keys within walking distance.
ICONIQA missed the corporate RFP season, so management is relying on online travel portals and repeat guests.

qa_highlights.question: How much Q1 growth came from the 237 new keys, and what is the growth of the existing base?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said the five new hotels are managed/franchised and contributed very negligibly, as only management or franchise fees are earned; growth came from JLO hotels.

qa_highlights.question: What are occupancy and ARR for Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: JLO occupancy about 70% and ADR INR 6,233 (vs INR 5,488). Managed portfolio occupancy 60.8% and ADR INR 4,300 (vs INR 4,031).

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue grow 25% or 30% over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number; managed-segment fees will grow, and JLO growth depends on ICONIQA stabilising over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: When will profit growth come through, and what is the ex-ICONIQA, ex-Ind AS trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROCE is about 17-18% and targeting 20%+ in about a year. Amit Jaiswal said he was not very happy with ex-ICONIQA performance and cited high tax cost; Arjun Baljee said the hotel is about a year from turning the corner.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ICONIQA's top line decline, and what was occupancy in April-June and August?

qa_highlights.question: What is ICONIQA's breakeven and incremental margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven at about INR 85 crore annualised revenue; management said about 60-65% of revenue above that flows to the bottom line, with a target of INR 100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why has employee cost risen from 19-20% to about 23% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee cited the new wage code, annual increments, new leases and management team additions; Amit Jaiswal said the average through the year is about 20-23%.

qa_highlights.question: When can the company build a INR 100-150 crore annual management fee business?
