543529|2026-06.headline: Delhivery Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to nearly Rs.3,000 Cr, with PAT of Rs.17 Cr after a Rs.15 Cr-plus cost drag from two new contracts and unused assets.
543529|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 as a record quarter for revenue but a weak one for profitability, hit by chronic labour shortages, election and weather disruptions, and start-up costs for two large new contracts. Express acquisition consolidation drove much of the 55% YoY growth in the reported figures. PTL yield rose to nearly Rs.12 per kg (per management's wording), and management attributed most of the improvement to organic gains rather than pass-through. Diesel price hikes in May are being passed through to customers with a lag, and management said FY27 outlook is unchanged at 20-30% growth.

financial_highlights.value: Rs.17 Cr (stat P&L ~Rs.30 Cr before ROU/intangible-related items)
financial_highlights.change: Management said PAT before unused-asset costs was ~Rs.62 Cr in press release; reconciliation given on call
Target 16-18% long term; internal exit target 15-15.5%
Stable across FY25, FY26 and Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: ~Rs.35 Cr per management, Rs.30-35 Cr normalised
financial_highlights.change: Relates to Rs.17 Cr in Q1 and delay in Q2
Q1 average linehaul cost ~12.2% of revenue, up ~0.6 pp (diesel)

segments.name: Express / e-commerce & B2B
segments.commentary: Express EBITDA margin exited at 13.4%, with an internal target of 15-15.5% exit and 16-18% long-term. Q1 growth of 55% was flattered by Express base effects, since the acquisition was reported in full only from Q2.

segments.name: PTL (Part Truck Load)
segments.commentary: Tonnage of 542,000 tonnes (+18% YoY) and yield of nearly Rs.12/kg (+20% YoY). Management said most of the yield gain was organic, about 37 paise per kg improvement, of which 6 paise was fuel-linked pass-through.

segments.name: Supply Chain Services (SCS)
segments.commentary: Two new large contracts (industrials and durables) depressed margins in Q1 during fulfilment-centre build-up; billing starts on outbound, so inbound buildup costs are front-loaded. Management expects stabilisation over Q2 and early Q3.

segments.name: New initiatives (Local, Direct, Maps)
segments.commentary: Local ARR is at Rs.150 Cr in July, versus an earlier target of Rs.250 Cr exit ARR for FY27; management revised its expectation to Rs.160-175 Cr. Ahmedabad Local is expected to break even around month three. NBFC approval received in July.

guidance_outlook: Management maintained the FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-30%; the range is wider because the outcome depends on Q2 and early Q3 trends.
FY27 profitability and medium/long-term targets were said to be unchanged, with no major structural headwinds seen by management.
Diesel: management says the pass-through is almost 100% covered (97-98% per Varun Bakshi). July is expected to reflect the May diesel hike with the lag gone.
Corporate manpower costs estimated at Rs.371 Cr for FY27 (as stated on call).
Unused-asset (lock-in/ROU) costs of around Rs.17 Cr are expected to continue until disposal, per management, and are treated as ongoing rather than one-time.
capex_capacity: Two new large SCS contracts required build-up of multiple fulfilment sites with a 45-60 day lead to inbound stock before outbound billing ramps.
Automation: in-facility movement and automated storage/retrieval being introduced at key transportation and fulfilment facilities.
Maps (proprietary GIS) launched on 8 August for internal deployment, with external availability planned later.
Expansion of cross-sell development teams for truck and LCV businesses; coverage now 100% of India versus earlier top-3 cities.
demand_pricing: Demand continued into Q2, with festive-season sales starting to lift volumes; August to date is said to be robust.
D2C volumes are running at 40-45% of PTL volumes and skew to heavier packages, which supports yields.
Pricing contracts are indexed to the prevailing month's diesel rate. Diesel-driven revisions were under negotiation from late April to mid-May, and pass-throughs are expected to show in Q2.
Management said pricing pressure has eased, with no price cuts for customers and reduced irrational competition. Competitor price cuts were disputed by management as not matching its own contracts.
New customer adds were mainly D2C and SME; management said self-serve sign-up through DelhiveryOne is growing.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 20-30% revenue growth guidance range, and what is the trend in new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was soft seasonally but robust after adjusting for Express, and the range is wider because Q2 and early Q3 trends are still forming. New customers are mostly D2C and SME, with festive demand building.

qa_highlights.question: Is the PTL yield increase seasonal or sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yield gains are planned and organic, with about 37 paise per kg of improvement, of which 6 paise was fuel pass-through; the sustained QoQ improvement is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 300 bps margin pressure is from diesel versus other costs, and how quickly can it be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fuel is about 0.6 pp of revenue for PTL; the bigger hit is labour-related minimum wage and rider payout linkage, which lacks a pass-through clause. Diesel revisions have been mostly passed through, and the effect should be evident in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the NBFC (asset-light lending) plan matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not lend heavily from its own balance sheet, but will partner with lending firms and underwrite a part of exposure to help fleet owners get insurance and financing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT difference between the press release and reported figures (Rs.62 Cr vs Rs.32 Cr vs Rs.17 Cr)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs.17 Cr relates to unused lock-in assets and facilities; the stat P&L shows about Rs.30 Cr after ROU and depreciation items. Shah queried recurrence, and management said the unused-asset costs are recurring until disposal.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SCS margins decline and what is the new-contract economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two new large contracts started together and are in an inbound-heavy build-up phase with negative cash flows, but they are expected to stabilise in Q2 and early Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is Delhivery exposed to competition from in-house or 3PL consolidation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has gained share, with volumes retained through the uncertain environment, and that in-house consolidation is an encouraging but unproven trend.

financial_highlights.value: Interest INR2.26 crore, gain on investments INR2.16 crore, rental and export incentives INR3.05 crore, write-backs remainder

financial_highlights.change: management said slightly above internal target; long-term guide ~4%
from INR450 crore; down about 15% YoY

segments.name: PEB India
segments.commentary: Order book at record INR1,008 crore; execution hit by engineering clearance and delivery issues, and PEB margins fell over 200 bps for a month or two until steel price increases were passed through. Management expects margins to recover from Q2.

segments.name: PEB US (Ascent)
segments.commentary: Order backlog crossed USD100 million (about USD70 million cited in one answer as the prior-quarter level), revenue running ahead of plan; US revenue stream described as the highest-margin unit with operating margins above 15%.

segments.name: Engineering Services (structural engineering, BIM)
segments.commentary: Structured engineering grew 26.3%; annual revenue about INR70 crore, mainly US and Europe. Management says productivity gains of 30-35% are being used against AI-driven automation risk.

segments.name: Boilers
segments.commentary: Order backlog at record INR150.75 crore; first industrial power boiler achieved as pre-qualification reference, and first pharmaceutical-sector orders won.

segments.name: Hydraulics
segments.commentary: Order backlog about INR30 crore; US activity slowed on tariff uncertainty while Europe performed well. Management is in wait-and-watch mode; the business is about INR100 crore a year.

segments.name: Tech Pennar
segments.commentary: Named as the weak spot: thin order book and execution issues at some customers; a new sales team is in place with improvement expected from Q2.

segments.name: BIW (body-in-white)
segments.commentary: Hyundai plant commissioned in August 2026 with three programmes; management expects revenue to double over the next three months on a scheduled order basis.

segments.name: Legacy businesses (steel, railways/Cadnum, tubing)
segments.commentary: About INR1,300 crore annual revenue, now about 25% of group revenue and declining; capital is no longer being deployed and management is seeking a value-realisation structure similar to the solar JV with Zetwerk.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27: double-digit sequential revenue and profit growth expected; PEB margins expected to return to prior levels from Q2.
FY27: management says 20% PAT growth is the stated goal for the year; ROCE target about 25-30% for the year (Q2 above 20%).
Debt-to-equity target about 0.7 by year-end FY27; management says anything above 0.7 is unacceptable, with INR20 crore of the promoter's INR50 crore commitment already in.
Over three years PBT margin target of about 7%, from 5.38% now.
Management said it expects the combined entity to grow at double-digit rates from Q2 as higher-growth units scale, while legacy units decline.
capex_capacity: PEB India capacity is available, but execution was hit by engineering clearance delays and labour constraints, which management says are resolved.
PEB US and India advance payments fell to about 25% from 5-10% earlier, as the company moved to reduce working capital.
BIW Hyundai plant commissioned in August 2026; three programmes in place.
Management is deliberately building raw-material inventory ahead of expected PEB revenue, which weighed on working capital.
Management is not deploying capital into legacy businesses (steel, railways, Cadnum aerospace); no material capex.
demand_pricing: Record order books across PEB India, PEB US and boilers; the company says the larger backlog is now ready to execute.
Hydraulics bookings below expectations on US tariff uncertainty; Europe performed well.
Steel price pass-through was delayed for about 1-2 months, which compressed PEB margins.
Management says it has about 6-7% share of an addressable market of INR2.25-2.3 lakh crore, and an obtainable market of about INR80,000 crore.
Solar JV with Zetwerk: Pennar holds 45% of a 2 GW capacity entity with potential revenue of about INR4,000 crore; no current revenue numbers were disclosed.

532926|2026-06.headline: Jyothy Labs Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 8.4% (down ~820 bps YoY) as gross margin dropped to 38.5% on crude-linked input inflation.
532926|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was margin-led weakness: gross margin fell 950 bps YoY to 38.5% and EBITDA margin to 8.4%, as input and packaging inflation outran price increases of roughly 3% realised in the quarter. Ex-Pril and FA, revenue grew 8.1% in value and 5.3% in volume. Fabric Care grew over 14% in value and 10% in volume, while Home Care ex-Pril grew 2.4% and Personal Care was subdued. Management said margins should recover gradually, with H2 better than H1, and that it expects double-digit revenue growth ex-Pril and FA for FY27. Segment reporting was changed to Fabric Care, Home Care and Personal Care from Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Fabric Care
segments.commentary: Value growth over 14% and volume growth 10% in Q1; detergent powders and bars grew double digits, and liquid detergents (Henko, Ujala, Mr. White, Morelight) continued high growth. Management said Fabric Care was priced up close to 5% on a portfolio basis.

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: Grew 2.4% YoY excluding Pril, which exited effective 31 May 2026. Exo Liquid (bioenzyme, launched 3-4 months ago) is at early scale-up; the broader Exo franchise grew mid-to-high single digits in value and double digits in volume. Household insecticides were hit by extended summer and delayed rains.

segments.name: Personal Care
segments.commentary: Performance subdued in Q1 on price increases of about 9-10% and transient supply-chain disruptions; management expects recovery from Q2. Soap noodle prices have risen since June.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ex-Pril and FA: double-digit revenue growth expected; management said high-single-digit volume growth with 3-4% price.
EBITDA margins to stay under pressure through FY27 on elevated crude-linked costs; H2 expected substantially better than H1, subject to demand and commodity stability.
Margin recovery expected gradual and more meaningful from October if commodity prices stay stable; Q2 margin not expected to be materially lower than Q1.
Aim to return to historical margin levels, but management said a large part depends on crude prices.
Step up advertising and brand-building investment after A&P was moderated over recent quarters.
Total price increases since the start of the conflict about 4-4.5%, of which about 3% flowed through in Q1 and the rest in Q2.
capex_capacity: No capacity, capex or commissioning figures were given in the call.
Maxo incense sticks launched in July 2026 as a government-approved product; management said it is priced at par with competition.
demand_pricing: Rural demand resilient; urban demand subdued, and general trade growth muted, though ex-Pril and FA general trade was positive per the CFO.
Modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce among fastest-growing channels; e-commerce and quick commerce growing 25-30%.
Price cuts at SKU level by competition in some SKUs; company said it is at par with competition, which limited price increases to about 3% realised in Q1.
Pril exit: Henkel did not renew the agreement and the matter is before court; no sales beyond 31 May 2026.
Management said liquid detergents are now priced below powders, and premium SKUs across home care are being discounted.
Distributor stock maintained at 15-20 days; significant part of general trade sold on advance payment.

qa_highlights.question: Why is price increase only about 3% when HUL and GCPL took about 5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited competitive SKU-level price reductions; the CFO said the blended increase was about 4-4.5% in total, with Personal Care at 9-10% and other segments at 4-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the margin gap close without crude deflation?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the goal is to return to historical margins, but much depends on crude; raw material inflation was about 15-16% and the total impact was about 9-9.5% after 3% pricing and 3-4% efficiencies and mix.

qa_highlights.question: Has general trade declined, and what is happening in quick commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: General trade was muted on urban demand, but positive ex-Pril and FA; e-commerce and quick commerce were growing 25-30% with no material assortment or pricing gaps.

qa_highlights.question: Will double-digit revenue growth return from this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the aim is double-digit growth from the current quarter, with 3-4% price and high-single-digit volume; the FY27 target excludes Pril and FA.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company looking at M&A after the TTK brand sale to Wipro?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company evaluated the TTK business but did not pursue it because two divisions did not fit strategy and two overlapped; it continues to screen assets with stringent filters.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin pressure structural, and what is the path back to 18-20% EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is not a commodity business and 90% of revenue is crude-linked; it is working on diversifying away from crude-linked raw materials and expects margins to recover once crude cools.

risks_watch: Crude and packaging costs: higher-cost inventory flows through Q2, and soap noodle prices are rising from June.
Pril legal matter pending before court; Pril exit removes a revenue base that management excluded from its FY27 growth guidance.
Competitive pricing pressure in some SKUs, and a larger competitor entering dishwash.
Personal Care recovery after 9-10% price increases and supply chain disruption.
Urban demand weakness and general trade growth; Maxo incense sticks' market entry as the second organised player.
Whether A&P steps up after being cut to 6.5% of revenue from 10.8%.
532926|2026-06.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic on demand and confident that margins are transitory, but evasive on the pace of recovery and on the pricing gap versus peers. Management tied the margin path to crude prices and gave no quantified Q2 margin outlook.

544647|2026-06.headline: Nephrocare Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23.7% YoY to INR282 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 30.7% to INR65 crore and margin at 23.1%.
544647|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 23.7% YoY to INR282 crore on 13% higher guest count (38,262) and 13.3% more treatments (10.3 lakh). Adjusted EBITDA rose 31% to INR65.1 crore, with margin up about 120-125 bps, mainly from a 175 bps lower COGS-to-revenue ratio that management attributed to procurement scale. Adjusted PAT rose 41.7% to INR37 crore. Management reiterated 15-20% medium-term growth guidance, while the Saudi tender remains an investment-phase drag of roughly INR3 crore per quarter on the JV line.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (after ESOP and Saudi JV add-backs)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR43 crore in Q1 FY26
down 133 bps QoQ, up YoY; includes ECL provision of 2-2.5% of revenue

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: 19 clinics added in Q1 (mix of PPP in Bihar, four private, and one or two greenfield); India RPT about $22-23. Management said it will not pursue PPP contracts below return thresholds and exited two Uttarakhand PPP clinics as value dilutive. Tamil Nadu PPP contract signed.

segments.name: Philippines
segments.commentary: 7 clinics added in Q1 (7 acquisitions, towards quarter end), taking the count to 50 clinics across 39 cities; management says it is the second-largest network with about 6-7% share of about 900 standalone clinics. Average centre size is 10-12 beds.

segments.name: International (overall)
segments.commentary: Contributes about 45% of revenue, up from about 30% a year and a half earlier. Uzbekistan is the only private operator, servicing about 1,800 of roughly 9,000 patients.

segments.name: Saudi Arabia
segments.commentary: First clinic at Riyadh Hospital operational in July; home dialysis started; medical operator licence obtained; tender RFI response submitted. Still in investment phase with JV losses of about INR3 crore cited by analysts; no tender documents issued yet.

segments.name: Kazakhstan
segments.commentary: Subsidiary incorporated in Q1 to evaluate Kazakhstan and Central Asia; no revenue or timeline yet. Price points around $75 noted in the market.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term growth guidance of 15-20% over the next three to five years maintained.
Expansion plan: 40-50 clinics a year in India, 10-15 clinics a year in the Philippines, and a new international market every 12-18 months; management does not give capex guidance.
Saudi tender formal process expected to begin in a couple of months; management sees three to four quarters before benefits or clear visibility; no guidance on JV losses.
Tax rate of about 20% offered as a proxy for the year (India and Philippines at 25%, Uzbekistan at 0% if healthcare revenue exceeds 90%).
NIDA renal nurse academy first batch to begin training in Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex of INR44 crore towards centre acquisitions and growth, vs INR43 crore a year earlier.

Depreciation life for machines is 7-10 years depending on country and regulation; RFID asset tracking reduced India depreciation, and about 50 machines a month of replacement activity was paused in the last three months.
Philippines acquisitions generate goodwill split into intangibles amortised over 5-7 years, adding to D&A.

Dialysis is a fixed-capacity business: about three cycles per machine per day; management says network growth comes from adding capacity, and clinics at about 85% utilisation need spare capacity for unplanned guests.
Management says the Philippines greenfield cost about 4 million per bed (referenced by an analyst) and declined to give acquisition cost per bed.
demand_pricing: India is still early in its dialysis market life cycle; management puts the organised (pure-play) share at about 20-22%, with 78-80% still hospital-run.
More than 300 private hospitals partner with NephroPlus on a built-own-operate model, where hospitals provide space and utilities and NephroPlus funds equipment.
Price increases are lumpy: CGHS raised rates about 35% in October 2025 after roughly 10-11 years; PhilHealth raised rates by 55-60% in October 2024.
RPT growth of about 11% CAGR was driven mainly by the international mix; management cautioned that the CAGR will not persist.
Management declined to split revenue or same-centre growth by country, saying it reports at platform level only.
75%+ of clinics are in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities; India operates in 300+ cities across 25 states.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain is from international mix versus cost efficiency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said COGS fell 175 bps as a share of revenue, driven by taking India procurement scale to other markets and by utilisation and supplier terms, not only reuse counts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise YoY, and how did they move QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses fell 133 bps QoQ. Drivers were ECL provisions of 2-2.5% of revenue (KPMG-assisted model), public-company costs such as audit and legal fees, and upfront business development spend for new international markets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did D&A decline QoQ despite Philippines acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited RFID-based asset tracking that cut machine replacements (about 50 a month previously) and a one-time benefit, partly offset by goodwill amortisation from seven Philippines acquisitions late in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi breakeven path and cost exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi is a binary tender market with four clusters; management does not give clinic-count breakeven and said further investment will depend on tender terms. Tender timelines are uncertain, and the company may not win.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose country-level or same-centre growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined, saying it manages capital at platform level and that dialysis growth comes from adding capacity rather than same-store price and volume.

544799|2026-06.headline: Turtlemint Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 40% to INR 294 crores, with adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to minus 9% of revenue from minus 21%.
544799|2026-06.overview: Platform premium grew 49% YoY to about INR 1,205 crores and revenue grew about 40% to INR 294 crores in Q1 FY27. Service EBITDA rose nearly 90% to INR 39 crores (about 13% of revenue), and corporate overheads fell to 22% of revenue from 30%. Adjusted EBITDA loss was INR 26 crores (minus 9% of revenue) and PAT loss was INR 38 crores (minus 13%), versus a INR 47 crore loss a year earlier. Management reiterated a target of adjusted EBITDA breakeven for the full year, with profitability weighted to H2 given seasonality.

financial_highlights.change: about 37% absolute improvement; from -21% of revenue
improved from INR -47 crores (about -22% of revenue)
about 30-33% YoY; vs 72,244 a year ago

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Management implied motor growth of about 50%+ YoY, with PoSP growth and a new Turtlefin platform partner contributing. Motor market Q1 is 16-18% below Q4 and H2 is about 55% of the year.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Q1 health grew about 45%+ YoY. Motor-only DPs starting to sell health grew 40%+ YoY. Nearly half of renewal premium is from health and life.

segments.name: Term life
segments.commentary: Term life grew about 60%+ YoY in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Business expected to grow about 40% YoY for the year, per July post-listing guidance.
Adjusted EBITDA breakeven targeted for full FY27, with profitability weighted to H2; management said PAT should 'not be too far away' but declined to give a PAT timeline.
Service EBITDA margin expected near-term to step up about 2 pp to about 16%, then 18%, reaching about 23-24% over 4-5 years as renewal book grows.
Corporate overheads expected to fall to 7-8% of revenue over 4-5 years (from 22% now).
Fixed costs below service EBITDA expected to rise in line with inflation.
demand_pricing: Digital partner base about 690,000+ after 32,000+ recruits in Q1; Turtlemint Academy ~55,000 monthly active users.
Take rate stable YoY; management said mix shift to renewals is the only change and there was no GST-related impact.
Renewal service EBITDA said to be 2.5-3x new service EBITDA; renewal servicing cost about 0.2% of revenue. Commission cost rises in line with top line.
Insurer relationships: for 17 insurers, Turtlemint's growth contribution was at least 2x industry growth in Q1.
DP attrition: 28-30% in first 24 months, falling to 2-3%; about 65% retained by year 5-6, management said trends unchanged.
Management said PoSP market growing at 30%+ CAGR; claims that Turtlemint has the highest PoSP share among players; competition seen as a 2-3 player market.
Motor TP pricing and commission regulation remain uncertain; management said insurers other than ICICI Lombard are awaiting the GIC appeal before provisioning.

qa_highlights.question: What drives seasonality, given the business is motor-heavy?
qa_highlights.answer: Motor market is about 45% H1 and 55% H2; Q1 is typically 16-18% below Q4. Q1 growth YoY remains strong and Q2, Q3 and Q4 should each be bigger than the prior quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is take rate change driven by renewals or GST, and why did other expenses rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Take rate is unchanged; the only shift is renewal vs fresh mix. Service EBITDA improved about 3 pp: roughly 2 pp from non-commission costs and 1 pp from commission costs. Commission rises with volume.

qa_highlights.question: How would commission cuts affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said health saw three full quarters after the GST-related commission reset, with revenue and margin still growing as volume offset the reset. Strategy will be decided once there is more clarity.

qa_highlights.question: How will service EBITDA margin reach 24-25% and how fast will renewal share rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewal payout and servicing costs are much lower than new business. Management declined to confirm the 70-80% renewal share, saying renewal premium is growing faster and nearly half of renewal premium is from health and life.

qa_highlights.question: What is the productivity trend across DP cohorts?
qa_highlights.answer: Older cohorts are also improving. Revenue grew about 40% while P3M Active grew about 30-32%, with the difference attributed to productivity gains.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI lift long-term EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI is cutting costs and driving growth through personalised onboarding and renewal calling, but it is too early to quantify. AI renewal calls showed a renewal rate 500 bps higher and AI handles 55% of support tickets.

qa_highlights.question: When will PAT break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the adjusted EBITDA breakeven target for FY27 and said PAT is not far off, with ESOP cost about INR 7 crores per quarter. No PAT timeline was given.

risks_watch: Commission regulation and motor TP pricing changes (Supreme Court case; insurers awaiting GIC appeal) could affect payouts and renewal economics.
Seasonality: Q1 is lowest; H2 must carry profitability to meet the FY27 adjusted EBITDA breakeven target.
Mix shift to renewals is the core margin driver; watch renewal share (22% now) and renewal growth versus new.
Competition: management views the market as 2-3 players; new entrants face high tech and distribution barriers.
Track DP activation (P3M Active), cohort productivity and attrition, plus whether AI renewal gains hold.
Corporate overhead ratio trajectory from 22% toward 7-8% over 4-5 years.
544799|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and renewals. Management was more guarded on regulation ('speculative', 'we do not know') and declined to give a PAT timeline or new-vs-renewal margin and renewal-share figures.
key_quotes: Our service EBITDA grew by 89% to INR 39 crores as margins continue to expand.
We also indicated that we'll try really hard for the entire year to be adjusted EBITDA breakeven in the current year.

Renewal from a service EBITDA point of view, if I were to compare renewal service EBITDA to new service EBITDA, renewal service EBITDA is about 2.5 times to 3 times higher than the new service EBITDA.

544515|2026-06.headline: Urban Company Q1 FY27 consolidated NTV rose 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore; Services NTV grew 29% and InstaHelp loss narrowed to ₹(132) crore.
544515|2026-06.overview: Consolidated NTV grew 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore and revenue rose 44% to ₹528 crore, with orders up 79% YoY to 13.2 million. Core Services NTV accelerated for a fourth straight quarter to 29% growth (₹1,056 crore), and Services adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 6.9% of NTV. Consolidated loss was ₹(65) crore, almost entirely from InstaHelp, while the rest of the business delivered an adjusted EBITDA of ₹67 crore. Management retained its guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31, and framed InstaHelp as the main investment area.

financial_highlights.change: +5.2 pp YoY (stated as 170 bps improvement in the margin line in the Q&A)
improved from (11.4)% a year ago (410 bps)
Loss per order ₹(346) vs ₹(447) in Q4
1.2 million new customers added in the quarter

segments.name: Core Services
segments.commentary: NTV ₹1,056 crore, growing 29% YoY, the fourth consecutive quarter of acceleration (10%→19%→21%→26%→29%). Adjusted EBITDA margin 6.9% of NTV, up 5.2 pp YoY per the call; management says the 29% base was muted by unseasonal rains and monsoon in the prior year.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: NTV ₹237 crore, up 76% YoY (58% ex-currency). UAE and Singapore both grew strongly; the Saudi Arabia JV is approaching profitability. UAE and Saudi JV are described as nearing or at profitability, and the company is not planning new international markets.

segments.name: InstaHelp
segments.commentary: NTV ₹119 crore (+51% YoY), net revenue ₹95 crore (+60% YoY); adjusted EBITDA loss ₹(132) crore, or (7.3)% of NTV versus (11.4)% a year ago. Largest investment; management expects it to need 2 or more years of investment and aims for adjusted breakeven within about 18 months.

guidance_outlook: Retains guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28.
Retains guidance of ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31.
Long-term Services adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 9-10% of NTV; currently at 6.9%. Management said it is not in a rush and sees the target as achievable without trading off growth.
Management said Services will be a cash-generating business going forward and that it intends to keep it profitable; InstaHelp is expected to need 2 years or more of investment.
Management explicitly declined to give growth guidance beyond the 29% trend, saying the company does not want to set the wrong expectations.
Top-15-city TAM for InstaHelp is ₹7,000-12,000 crore NTV annually; management's base case is ₹7,000-8,000 crore and the bull case is ₹10,000-12,000 crore.
capex_capacity: InstaHelp: management said the company is investing aggressively in micro-market density, with the investment level still under evaluation.
Core Services trainer and infrastructure capacity is being scaled up with AI support; management says the company is 'all hands on deck' as supply grows.
Beauty segment: partners are being retrained and retooled, and the company moved to a majority of professionals having access to two-wheelers, with the target of approaching 100%.

Services is expected to consume less capital as InstaHelp is scaled; management said capital allocation will be reviewed once InstaHelp approaches adjusted breakeven (hopefully within about 18 months).
demand_pricing: Management said Q1 was among the best quarters in the company's history, with growth broad-based.

InstaHelp pricing: sustainable professional payout is about ₹130-160 per hour, with ₹150 as the rule of thumb. Management said an AOV of about ₹300 is needed for InstaHelp to break even, with ₹200 per hour required to clear gross breakeven.

Management said competitors in the InstaHelp category have pricing of ₹80-120 per hour for full-month subscriptions and that competitive intensity is high; it said the company has no reason to comment on rival strategies.
Management said the 3 major players have limited their household coverage to about 3.5-4 million households; the company believes most spending goes to subsidised repeat orders.
Management said the company has 'underestimated' the Tier 2 opportunity, with Tier 2 cities performing as well as Tier 1.

Management said it is seeing acceleration in MAUs, DAUs and MTUs, with conversion rates improving; the marketing spend in Services was about ₹25 crore in the quarter versus ₹24 crore a year ago (flat).

544515|2026-09.headline: Urban Company's consolidated NTV rose 39.1% to ₹1,432.3 crore in Q2 FY27, with adjusted EBITDA (ex-Native/International investment) at ₹30 crore, up 213% YoY.
544515|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated NTV up 39.1% YoY to ₹1,432.3 crore and revenue from operations up 41.4% to ₹537.3 crore, with adjusted loss of ₹144 crore after a ₹174 crore investment in Native. Core Services adjusted EBITDA was ₹30 crore ex-investments, and management reiterated breakeven for the consolidated business by Q3 FY28 and a ₹1,000 crore EBITDA-type goal for FY31. Management announced a fundraise of up to ₹2,500 crore, framed as flexibility rather than a need to fund losses. Q&A focused on the rationale for the raise, Native's AC launch, professional supply, and pricing/contribution economics.

financial_highlights.change: +213% YoY; ₹119 crore for trailing four quarters, +175%
vs NTV growth of 26%, per management
up 110 bps (from prior level per call)

segments.name: Core Services (India)
segments.commentary: Management said Core Services adjusted EBITDA was ₹30 crore ex-investments and contribution margin rose to 3.5%; NTV growth was attributed to new-customer acquisition, repeat cohorts and densification, with instant service now used in top 7–8 cities.

segments.name: International (UAE, Saudi, Singapore)
segments.commentary: International NTV grew 66.2% YoY per management, with UAE described as a key market; adjusted EBITDA margin was 2% of NTV, improved by 190 bps. Management said war-related concerns are behind it and Q2+Q3 combined growth is expected at 50–55%.

segments.name: Native (water purifiers / AC services)
segments.commentary: Native's loss narrowed by ₹220 crore (per call) with loss per order down 19% QoQ to ₹279; management says Native is being built deliberately with a ₹174 crore investment in Q2 and is in a learning phase for its first AC device.

segments.name: Insta Help (professional/household help)
segments.commentary: Management said Insta Help is in a tougher base with Q2 revenue growth at 26.3% and the festive season falling in Q3; penetration in top 8 cities for largest categories is below 10%.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated breakeven target reiterated for Q3 FY28; management said it is confident, more than ever, of the ₹1,000 crore FY31 goal.
Management expects Q2 plus Q3 combined international growth in the range of 50% to 55%.
Fundraise of up to ₹2,500 crore is for flexibility, mainly for organic build-out of existing businesses and selective M&A; management said nothing imminent.
Native AC device launch: management expects one to two quarters of learning, limited largely to the app, and no material change to Native's trajectory.
Contribution margin target of 9–10% noted as the key lever; management said it is working towards it.
capex_capacity: Orders rose 63% QoQ to 6.23 million; 45% of new orders are reportedly from the Core Services' top categories, per management.
Management is onboarding professionals aggressively in the 3–4 months before the festive season to improve the liquidity coefficient.
Native's offline distribution is in a learning phase; M3 water purifier and Lock Ultra launched in modern retail with pull from offline ecosystem.
Gold premium service rollout: management said results are promising and it intends to scale it out across categories.
demand_pricing: Core Services average spend growth slowed to around 3% (vs historical 6–7%); management attributed this to mix change and season timing, and pass-through of densification benefits in pockets.
Instant service delivered in 30–60 minutes is offered in UAE and Singapore; management said no premium is currently charged.
Professional (partner) supply grew 16% YoY versus NTV growth of 26%; management declined to give forward partner-growth projections.
Hourly pricing roughly ₹200 and net order value roughly ₹300 for an average order of 1.5 hours; partner payout of ₹150 per utilised hour.
Management described the household-help TAM as range-bound with no single winner, and the AC TAM as roughly 10x water purifier TAM.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Core Services' accelerating new-user acquisition and is it sustainable, with average spend growth slowing to 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a stronger product with instant service in top 7–8 cities, AI-led training/QC improving word of mouth, densification, faster growth in Tier-2 markets and higher marketing. Average spend slowed due to mix, seasonality and some densification benefit passed to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the use of proceeds from the ₹2,500 crore fundraise and the M&A framework?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly for flexibility and organic build-out; M&A would be for consolidating existing categories or entering new categories, not new countries, with buy-vs-build tilting to buy if accretive. Nothing imminent.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise capital now given cash on balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the raise is for flexibility, to be aggressive, pursue acquisitions and absorb downside in a high-competition scenario; not primarily to fund losses. Targets remain unchanged, and they would have changed short/medium-term targets if funding were insufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Native AC launch and its allocation impact profitability timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Native is on track for profitability, AC will be a disciplined build-up with R&D the bulk of losses, and any new category would take one to two quarters of learning before scale.

qa_highlights.question: Is professional supply or retention a rate limiter, and what is steady-state unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the challenge is retaining high-quality professionals, not sourcing. Experts care about net take-home pay; the company frames pricing and payouts as competitive. Steady-state unit economics remain under evaluation with a cited framework of payout ₹150 per hour, with ₹50 covering costs at best utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the acceleration in professional-services growth and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said professional growth of 16% is a leading indicator; drivers are utilisation, targeting, and onboarding. Management declined to give specific projections.

qa_highlights.question: Will Native offline distribution expand pan-India in modern retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline share is small and in a learning phase; modern retail response is good; management will expand calibrated and slowly.

risks_watch: Competitive intensity in Core Services and International; management says losses are a deliberate choice.
Average spend growth slowing to 3% versus historical 6–7%.
Professional partner retention and churn as supply expands.
Native profitability and AC device adoption, with a one-to-two-quarter learning phase before scale.
Use and deployment of the ₹2,500 crore fundraise and any M&A execution.

544868|2026-06.headline: Milky Mist Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% YoY to INR973.45 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.9% and gross margin up about 270 bps to 34.2%.
544868|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR973.45 crore, up 44% YoY, led by paneer, cheese, curd, ice cream and yogurt. Gross profit was about INR333 crore (34.2% margin, up ~270 bps), EBITDA INR144.89 crore (14.9% margin vs 12.24% a year earlier) and PAT INR64.67 crore (6.6% margin). Management attributed margin gains to product mix, a ~10.5% price increase taken in Q4 FY26, and scale. The call was the company's first earnings call after listing; several figures were corrected on the call during the prepared remarks.

segments.name: Paneer
segments.commentary: Largest contributor at INR248.29 crore, up 34% in both volume and revenue; management linked this to zero GST on paneer from September 2025 and FSSAI/state bans on analogue paneer. Company claims ~20% share of the organised paneer market.

segments.name: Yogurt (incl. protein range)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR84.5 crore, up 153%; management calls it a key margin driver, with Greek yogurt and Skyr in the protein range.

segments.name: Ice cream
segments.commentary: Volume +45%, revenue +60% YoY, aided by extended summer; management expects demand to stay robust around the year in South except a two-month monsoon dip.

segments.name: Cheese
segments.commentary: Revenue +38% YoY; new natural cheddar plant commissioned in Q1 FY27 with 120 MT/day capacity. Company says cheese sales come from retail, modern trade and quick-commerce, not QSRs.

segments.name: Curd
segments.commentary: Revenue +27% YoY.

segments.name: Regional mix
segments.commentary: South ~69% of revenue, growing ~44% YoY; non-South ~31%, growing ~50% YoY. Management expects a drift toward 60:40 over time.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 to add INR150-200 crore of incremental revenue versus H1 (as stated on the call).
Operating margin: management guided to about 0.5% leverage benefit from scale; asked whether 18% EBITDA margin is achievable in 3-4 years, CFO said 'you can expect that' but CEO declined to quantify.
Maharashtra plant: at drawing-board stage, about three years out; the company aims for 40% utilisation from day one at break-even.
Revenue potential from Perundurai at current MRP: 3x to 3.5x FY26 revenue (as stated on the call).
Plans to deploy more than 50,000 visi coolers, ice cream freezers and chocolate coolers over the next three fiscal years.
Whey protein concentrate plant expected to be operational in about 15-18 months from the call.
capex_capacity: Commissioned new natural cheddar cheese plant in Q1 FY27 with 120 MT/day installed capacity.

Capex in the RHP: about INR500 crore plus INR150 crore, about INR650-700 crore in total; another ~INR380 crore WIP carried from last year. CFO said capex is funded through IPO proceeds and bank funding, with no cash-flow pressure this year.
Planned expansion covers whey protein concentrate, lactose, natural cheese, processed cheese and yogurt capacity.
Capacity utilisation: CEO said more than 12 product categories have spare capacity; paneer utilisation is about 50%.

Milk procurement averaged 13.2 lakh litres per day in Q1 FY27, up 28% YoY. Third-party share is about 10-12% of volume, and the company is expanding direct procurement in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra.
demand_pricing: Price increase of about 10.5% taken in Q4 FY26 (stated as ~11% in one answer); management said this offset milk and input inflation and produced a 2.7% margin expansion net.
Trade spend: about 4.5-5% trade discount from MRP to billing and another 4.5-5% on marketing/promotion.
Milk costs are about 50-55% of input cost; landed cost is INR45/litre (farmer price INR41-42). Aavin raised farmgate prices by INR3 twice recently; management is still studying pass-through.
Pricing is set after a 2-3 month lag following input cost increases, per CFO.
Management said the company has no B2B or QSR sales other than whey powder from cheese and paneer making.

qa_highlights.question: Third-party milk procurement strategy and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party share is about 10-12% through a five-year exclusive contract with MilkLane (linked to a PE-owned entity). Management says payments go directly to farmers and that quality premiums are about 50 paise/litre, with no financial dilution.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin resilience amid milk price inflation and further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credits product mix (paneer +34%, cheese +38%, yogurt +150%, ice cream +60%) and pricing. Price hikes follow a 2-3 month lag after input costs. About 10.5% price increase taken last year.

qa_highlights.question: Freight and logistics model with a single plant serving distant cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-owned fleet of about 375 vehicles with return-load logistics saves ~18-20% on logistics cost. Shelf life of 30+ days (vs 24-48 hours for pouch milk) makes one plant viable.

qa_highlights.question: Low base in Q1 FY26 and seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 FY26 weakness was price-driven (GST and milk rationalisation), not volume-driven. Ice cream is strong in summer and robust year-round in South except a two-month monsoon dip.

qa_highlights.question: Whey protein plans and high-protein B2C products?
qa_highlights.answer: The company generates about 1 million litres of cheese whey daily and currently sells whey powder B2B. A whey protein concentrate plant is due in 15-18 months; high-protein RTD products are in development.

qa_highlights.question: Yield per animal and farmer support?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement volume is up 28% YoY. Initiatives include bank credit via Kisan Credit Cards, herd-size expansion, AI/breeding, feed and health camps.

531179|2026-06.headline: Arman Financial Q1 FY27: consolidated PAT rose to INR45 crore from a loss of INR15 crore a year ago, with AUM at a record INR2,925 crore (+36% YoY).
531179|2026-06.overview: Consolidated disbursements of INR686 crore were up 76% YoY, the highest ever Q1, while cost-to-income improved to 44.3% from 51.7% in Q4 FY26. GNPA fell to 2.76% and NNPA to 0.84%, with collection efficiency at 96.6% for the quarter. Management repeatedly said the sector has not fully normalised and that volumes were below expectations, with a stated focus on quality over quantity. Namra Finance (microfinance) drove most of the profit improvement, and the individual loan book rose to 33% of the book.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR59 crore in Q4 FY26
vs loss of INR15 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR41 crore in Q4 FY26

segments.name: Arman Financial (standalone)
segments.commentary: AUM INR758 crore (+26% YoY, +4% QoQ); disbursements INR156 crore led by MSME; GTI INR66 crore (+30% YoY); PPOP INR24 crore; PAT INR15 crore (+17% YoY, +48% QoQ).

segments.name: Namra Finance (microfinance)
segments.commentary: AUM INR2,167 crore (+39% YoY, +8% QoQ); disbursements INR530 crore; GTI INR138 crore (+35% YoY); PPOP INR52 crore (+64% YoY); PAT INR30 crore vs loss of INR28 crore a year ago; NIM 15.37%; GNPA 2.59% from a peak of 3.8%.

guidance_outlook: Opex-to-AUM target of about 7% by end of FY27; management said the ratio was about 8% this quarter (vs about 9% last quarter) and expects further decline.

Management said FY27 AUM growth of about 25% to 30% was the context for questions, but did not itself restate the figure; growth to be 'careful, calibrated' and recalibrated to collections and delinquency trends.
Credit cost: Vivek Modi said credit cost is expected to stay about 3% to 3.5%; Aalok Patel said including CGFMU cost, 3% sounds about right, maybe 2.5%, and 2% if lucky.
Borrowing cost: approaching rating agencies for upgrades, expected to cut interest cost by about 20-30 bps.
No explicit ROA guidance; Aalok Patel said on a fully levered basis historically about 4.5% and around 3.5-4% at about 20% capital adequacy with current opex.
capex_capacity: Management said current infrastructure can support disbursements of INR750 crore per quarter; Q4 FY26 consolidated disbursements were cited at INR700 crore-plus, and microfinance alone at INR738 crore per the presentation.
Branch network cited by analyst at about 400-425 branches, up from about 275-280 in 2023; management did not dispute this.
CGFMU coverage: about 94% of eligible microfinance portfolio covered as of 30 June 2026.

Liquidity: INR286 crore across cash, liquid investments and undrawn CC limits; INR335 crore undrawn sanctions from existing lenders. Average liquidity about INR300 crore, roughly 1.5 months of repayments plus one month of disbursements.
Solar loans: about INR50 lakh per month in selected areas; zero NPAs so far; yield about 18-20%.
demand_pricing: Q1 volumes were below management's expectations; rejection rates remain relatively high by design.
Individual loans are 33% of the book; about 68-70% of individual-loan EMIs clear via eNACH/UPI by month-end, around 85% cashless in total, with about 14% collected in cash door-to-door.
Management said the individual book is performing better than JLG, while acknowledging the product is new and opex is the key issue.
LAP (loan against property) disbursement is well below the analyst's expected INR40-50 crore per quarter; management cited secured-lending competition from MFIs, SFBs, banks and fintechs.
Rates: management said it would consider cutting rates if the company were earning too much, but has not given it much thought; RBI scrutiny cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why remain cautious given favourable collection and delinquency data?
qa_highlights.answer: Aalok Patel said the data is favourable but rural income growth and jobs quality are concerning on the ground; he called it a little PTSD and said he has no reason to be pessimistic.

qa_highlights.question: Recoveries on written-off accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Modi said about INR185 crore of pool written off over 24 months was sold to an ARC in March 2025; recovery on it this year is about 10%, and overall write-off recoveries are about 3-4%, with 12-18 months still to run.

qa_highlights.question: When will liquidity fall and disbursements pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquidity is already sufficiently low, averaging about INR300 crore, and described the current level as a 'Goldilocks' position; the team has been in collection mode for two years and volumes should recover over the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Yield, funding cost and opex outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex is expected to fall toward 7% of AUM; funding cost of about 11.7% is expected to fall 20-30 bps on rating upgrades; on yields, management said it will reduce rates only if earnings become excessive.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MSME 31-90 PAR and LAP GNPA rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Modi attributed about 10-15 bps of upward movement in MSME PAR to higher stress in Telangana, with other states stable; Aalok Patel said there were other reasons too.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost guidance and July collections?
qa_highlights.answer: July repayment rates were marginally lower than June, about 3 bps on zero DPD, attributed to rain in Gujarat, UP and Bihar; credit cost guided at about 3-3.5% by Vivek Modi, with management saying 2-3% is possible including CGFMU costs.

qa_highlights.question: ROA and individual loan economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it gives no formal ROA guidance; historically about 4.5% on a fully levered basis, and about 3.5-4% at 20% CAR on current opex. Individual loans are preferred but the product is still new.

500144|2026-06.headline: Finolex Cables Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% to INR 2,013 crore and PAT 59% to INR 221 crore, helped by a temporary communication-cable margin spike near 30%.
500144|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations grew about 44% YoY to INR 2,013 crore, with PBT of INR 277 crore (up about 62%) and PAT of INR 221 crore (up about 59%). PBT margin expanded to 13.4% from 11.8% and PAT margin to 10.7% from 9.6%. Electrical cables drove growth on volume and price, while communication cables margins were lifted by low-cost opening fiber inventory that management said will normalise. Copper rod revenue collapsed to INR 8 crore as the rod plant shut on LPG shortage.</overview>

segments.name: Electrical cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,767 crore, up about 47%. Automotive, battery, flexible, solar and agricultural cables grew high double digits in volume; building wire grew low single digits in volume as channel destocked. Management said domestic electrical margin of about 10.5% should be sustainable.

segments.name: Communication cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 176 crore, up about 62% from INR 109 crore, with margin close to 30%. Volumes up about 30%; INR 30-40 crore of the revenue was exports to the US and Europe. Management expects margins to normalise to low double digits by year-end as opening inventory is consumed.

segments.name: Copper rod
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 8 crore vs INR 403 crore a year ago; rod plant shut for the quarter due to continued restriction on LPG availability.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Described as a weak link: fans were short of commercial LPG and conduit pipes short of PVC. Target of INR 5 billion FMEG revenue by FY28 reiterated, though the season was largely lost.

guidance_outlook: Communication cable margin expected to normalise; management still sees double-digit margins, likely low double digits, at year-end if demand holds.
Fiber draw capacity to rise from 4 million km to 8 million km by September 2026 (end of Q2), directly rather than in two phases.
Cabling capacity to rise from 8 million to 10 million km, with a longer timeline than the draw expansion.
Preform (100 metric ton) plant expected to stabilise in the next couple of months; management expects it to be fully functional from the September quarter. Phase 2 preform doubling under review.
FY27 capex unchanged at about INR 300 crore.
FMEG target of INR 5 billion by FY28 still intact per management.
capex_capacity: Fiber draw capacity: moving from 4 to 8 million km in one phase, completion by September 2026; original plan was 4 to 6 then 6 to 8.
Preform plant of 100 metric tons, equivalent to about 4 million km of fiber; the balance of 8 million km requires bought-in preform. Phase 2 expansion will be decided later.
Cabling capacity: one plant full, the other about three-quarters utilised; expansion to 10 million km.
FY27 capex about INR 300 crore, unchanged.
Management confirmed R&D and capex steps for data-centre-grade cables, with no details given.
demand_pricing: Fiber prices (G.652.D): about USD 5-6/km in December 2025, peaked at USD 17-18, now settling at USD 11-13/km; premium fiber sold up to USD 50/km.
Communication cable demand is driven by data-centre and AI build-outs; long-term contracts are over half of communication revenue and were repriced in late June 2026.
Electrical cables: about 60% construction, with automotive cables above 14% of the mix in Q1; LV and HV cables about 7-8% of the mix.
Electrical cable price hike of about 3% taken in May 2026 amid copper at about INR 14,000 per kg level; channel inventory was lower at quarter end.
Domestic fiber consumption about 25 million km per year vs China at 400 million km plus; management sees 50-60 million km potential.
Germanium tetrachloride supply is restricted with long lead times; supply covers the calendar year, with no multi-year contracts available.
BharatNet: no update; winners waiting given high prices.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are EBITDA margins, and how much of the expansion is one-off versus mix or copper pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Export gains came from optic fiber opportunities that may not recur, so management is conservative on them. Domestic electrical margin of about 10.5% should be sustainable; communication margins will fall as old raw material is used up, to low double digits by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What fiber prices are prevailing and how do they compare with December 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: G.652.D went from USD 5-6/km in December 2025 to USD 17-18, and is now settling at USD 11-13/km. Management declined to forecast further movement.

qa_highlights.question: How much of communication cable revenue is exports and to which geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 35-40 crore of the communication revenue was exports, mainly to the US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 100 MT preform plant lift margins by about 100 bps once it is fully functional?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see margins improving from here and called 100 bps stretching it, given that elevated prices may not last.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue reach about INR 300 crore per quarter from fiber?
qa_highlights.answer: At USD 11/km on 8 million km a year, fiber-only sales would be about USD 88 million, or about INR 250-260 crore; cabling adds 20-30% value on top, so INR 300 crore is achievable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FMEG outlook and does the INR 5 billion FY28 target still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed LPG shortages for fans and PVC shortages for conduit pipes; the target of INR 5 billion by FY28 remains.

risks_watch: Communication cable margin of about 30% is temporary; normalisation to low double digits as low-cost inventory runs out.
Fiber supply is tight: preform and germanium are restricted, with preform sourcing still partly external and contracts about a year long.
Input cost volatility from LPG, helium, PVC and fuel after Middle East disruption; supply chain risk to the copper rod plant.
Export revenue depends on episodic opportunities; management cannot give a repeatable export mix.
Preform contract repricing could raise raw material costs once older contracts reset.
FMEG remains weak; catching up on the lost fan and pipe season is uncertain.
500144|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on volumes and demand, with an explicit caution that the communication margin is temporary. Management was evasive on data-centre contracts, R&D specifics and export mix, and declined to predict fiber prices.

544418|2026-06.headline: Oswal Pumps Q1 FY27 revenue fell 7.9% YoY to INR474 crore and operating EBITDA margin dropped to 15.7%, while FY27 guidance of 20-25% growth was maintained.
544418|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR474 crore, down 7.9% YoY and 7.1% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR82 crore (17.1% margin) and operating EBITDA of INR74 crore (15.7%). Management attributed the margin fall to a 9% price reduction in Magel Tyala tenders, higher raw material costs from geopolitical factors, and module sales through the channel, partly offset by value engineering. Receivable days rose to 229 from 155, pushing the cash conversion cycle to 244 days from 172. Management kept FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25% and an operating EBITDA margin of 15-17%, while relying on PM KUSUM 2.0 timing and the PM Surya Ghar rooftop business for the second half.

financial_highlights.value: INR266 crore; net debt/equity 0.15x; net debt/operating EBITDA 0.90x

financial_highlights.change: vs 155 days in Q4 FY26; INR305 crore of receivables not yet due
vs ~40,400 in Q4 FY26 and ~56,000 in Q1 FY26

segments.name: PM KUSUM / Magel Tyala solar pumps
segments.commentary: Core business; order book of 22,025 pumps, with near-term pipeline of ~12,500 pumps across direct PM KUSUM, Magel Tyala, indirect PM KUSUM and exports. Magel Tyala price cuts of ~9% were the biggest margin drag.

segments.name: Solar EPC / PM Surya Ghar (rooftop, utility, C&I)
segments.commentary: Order book ~72 MW with 359 MW pipeline. Dedicated PM Surya Ghar vertical formed; internal target of ~2 lakh installations in FY27, implying INR800-1,000 crore revenue per management. Negligible contribution in Q1; expected to start from Q2.

segments.name: Wires and cables / channel sales
segments.commentary: Management expects INR70-100 crore revenue from wires and cables this year, using existing in-house spare capacity with no significant capex; margins expected to be below KUSUM pumps.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 20-25% over FY26 maintained, back-ended; Q2 YoY growth expected at 10-15%.
FY27 operating EBITDA margin guided at 15-17%; PAT margin guided at 11-13%. Guidance assumes current bids and excludes any PM KUSUM 2.0 upside, which management says would lift margins slightly.
Medium-term growth target of 30-40% after FY27.
Receivables expected to be better in Q2 than Q1 and significantly better in Q3; cash conversion cycle not expected to change sharply in Q2.
PM KUSUM 2.0 launch expected in Q2 FY27 per management, but IR advisor said no one can guarantee August timing.
Inverter in-house production expected within ~6 months; field trials for prototype in ~2 months.
capex_capacity: 1 GW of solar module capacity already invested; commercial production expected by first or second week of September 2026 (first phase of expansion).
Remaining module expansion (total 1.5 GW referenced in question) progressing; management says a 1-2 month gap possible due to rain.
Pump and motor capacity expansion and automation to complete by Q3 FY27.
Management confirmed IPO proceeds will be fully deployed as per plan; analyst cited ~INR200 crore capex in the quarter.
demand_pricing: Magel Tyala tender pricing fell sharply as more bidders entered; management cited 8-9% price impact on realisation.
Raw material costs rose due to geopolitical factors, estimated at 3-3.5% margin impact; operating leverage ~1-1.5%.
Competition increased as PM KUSUM installations grew (about 1.5 lakh in FY24, 3.5 lakh in FY25, 5 lakh in FY26, per management).
Magel Tyala T6 tender bid submitted; financial bid opening expected in 7-10 days.
Solar EPC work in Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan has started execution.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin fall of ~24-25% to 15% is from pricing versus raw materials?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 8-9% to Magel Tyala bidding prices, 3-3.5% to raw material costs, and 1-1.5% to operating leverage, with value engineering limiting the impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15-17% EBITDA margin guidance inclusive of PM KUSUM 2.0?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The guidance is based on current bids, the Surya Ghar bids and channel sales; KUSUM 2.0 would lift margins slightly. Management said it assumed a slightly safer side.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR800-1,000 crore Surya Ghar revenue consistent with 20-25% growth on ~INR2,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified the Surya Ghar figure is for FY27 Q2-Q4, not full-year. Q1 revenue of ~INR470 crore was mainly pumping. Conservatively, INR800 crore of business is assumed including the Magel Tyala T6 tender and wires and cables.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Surya Ghar margins versus KUSUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Surya Ghar margins are lower than KUSUM but the cumulative margin across businesses should be 15-17%. An analyst's reading of 12-15% for Surya Ghar was accepted as broadly correct.

qa_highlights.question: When will receivables normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 receivables to be better than Q1, with a larger improvement in Q3, but said the cash conversion cycle will not change much in Q2 because billing is running in parallel.

risks_watch: PM KUSUM 2.0 timing: repeated delays, and management said it cannot guarantee an August launch.
Receivable days at 229 with INR305 crore not yet due; cash conversion cycle at 244 days.
Margin sustainability: 15-17% guidance with Q1 at 15.7% operating margin, and the Surya Ghar margin likely below KUSUM.
Raw material and copper price volatility; management said any rise would affect the whole industry.
Execution of PM Surya Ghar 2 lakh installation target and inverter in-house timeline.
544418|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on guidance and the recovery outlook, but cautious on timing: management repeatedly said PM KUSUM 2.0 timing is outside its control. Its answers on margin bridging and Surya Ghar economics were detailed but contained some internal inconsistencies, which reduces confidence.

544223|2026-06.headline: Ceigall Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 10.2% YoY to INR901 crore, with EBITDA margin at 13.4% and order book at INR18,568 crore.
544223|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 10.2% YoY to INR901 crore and PAT rose to INR75 crore (8.4% margin) from INR56 crore. Consolidated revenue grew 15.7% to INR970 crore. The company completed its first HAM divestment (Malout-Abohar-Sadhuwali) and started three new projects, while management kept FY27 margin guidance of 11-12.5% and raised revenue growth guidance to at least 15%. Q1 order inflow was modest at about INR600 crore against a INR6,000 crore full-year target.

segments.name: Order book mix
segments.commentary: 19 EPC projects, 10 HAM projects, 1 DBFOT project and 9 tariff-based renewable and transmission projects. Diversification extends to metro rail, renewable energy, T&D and industrial infrastructure.

segments.name: Renewable energy (Solar plus BESS)
segments.commentary: Signed a PPA for a Solar BESS at Morena and emerged L1 for a standalone battery storage project. Maharashtra solar projects MH1 and MH2 started in Q1. Rewa solar awaits a transmission line tender before start.
