segments.commentary: Divested Malout-Abohar-Sadhuwali, the first HAM asset monetised. Signed concession for Ambala-Chandigarh-Zirakpur HAM. Received appointed dates for VRK 11, VRK 12 and Indore-Ujjain HAM after quarter end. Northern Ayodhya bypass execution was about INR42 crore in Q1.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 11% to 12.5% for FY27 maintained, per CFO.
Revenue growth guidance raised to minimum 15% for FY27, from earlier 10-15%.
Order inflow target of about INR6,000 crore for FY27; close to INR600 crore secured so far. Order inflow typically concentrated in Q3 and Q4 (about 45% of the order book came in Q4 last year).
Full-year capex guidance of INR30-35 crore.
Balance equity commitment of INR859 crore in FY27 (INR310 crore solar, INR550 crore HAM) and INR744 crore in FY28 (INR296 crore solar, INR444 crore HAM).
Execution targets: VRK 11 and VRK 12 at least 20-25% in FY27; Southern Ludhiana at least 15% due to only 62% land availability.
Working capital intensity expected to improve in FY27 and further in FY28, citing government relaxation.
Commercial paper of about INR100 crore on private placement, carved out of working capital limits at about 6.8-7% versus WCDL at 7.5-7.8%.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex about INR14 crore, mainly a launcher bought at Danapur; more than INR100 crore of machinery already paid from IPO proceeds.
Full-year FY27 capex guidance INR30-35 crore; specialised machinery to be bought only as required.
Three new projects started in Q1 (MH1, MH2 solar and Indore-Ujjain HAM); three more to start from July after appointed dates.
Two HAM projects (Bihar and Punjab) await appointed dates: Bihar FC expected next month, Punjab around November; work to start 2-3 months after FC.

Equity infusion by project for FY27 includes VRK 11 INR97 crore, VRK 12 INR139 crore, Northern Ayodhya INR61 crore, Southern Ayodhya INR53 crore, Ludhiana-Bhatinda INR53 crore, Southern Ludhiana INR38 crore, Indore-Ujjain INR60 crore, Bihar Sahebganj INR50 crore and Zirakpur INR16 crore.
demand_pricing: Management cited a Q1 seasonal slowdown from monsoon; order inflow was modest in Q1 with the bulk expected in Q3 and Q4.
International: bids in Romania and Dubai; management is taking a conservative approach given the war situation, with focus on India.
Management says the company targets 25% project-level IRR and will sell completed projects, citing Malout-Abohar-Sadhuwali returns above guidance.
Renewable margins guided in line with EPC margins, with an aim to do better.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Northern Ayodhya bypass execution fall to about INR42 crore in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said progress is steady and milestones are being met early; payment is only received on milestone achievement, and rain over the last 1.5 months affected timing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rewa solar project timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: PPA and land are in place; the transmission line tender has been floated and the company expects it soon, after which the project can start quickly.

qa_highlights.question: What equity will be invested in HAM and solar in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 balance commitment INR859 crore (INR310 crore solar, INR550 crore HAM); FY28 INR744 crore (INR296 crore solar, INR444 crore HAM). Initial equity at IPO was INR253 crore; total now INR692 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was margin higher than guidance and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Three new projects started in Q1 and more are starting; the CFO said FY27 margin guidance of 11-12.5% is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation and other income fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation fell due to assets sold in the prior year on WDV method; other income fell as royalty is no longer charged and IPO-linked FD interest ended. About INR320 crore in FDs now earn interest, and management expects this run rate to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the purpose of the commercial paper issuance?
qa_highlights.answer: CP of about INR100 crore is carved out of working capital limits, at about 6.8-7% versus WCDL at 7.5-7.8%, to reduce finance cost and access the market.

543273|2026-06.headline: KMEW Q1 FY27 revenue rose 138% YoY to INR115.41 crore and PAT to INR62.75 crore, driven by one-off-heavy dredging execution.
543273|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR115.41 crore (+138% YoY), EBITDA INR73.41 crore (+258% YoY, ~64% margin) and PAT INR62.75 crore (+466% YoY, ~54% margin). Management attributed the quarter to dredging execution at JNPA (capital rock dredging, completed) and Pondicherry Port (maintenance dredging). Management said revenue and profitability are project-driven and vary by quarter. FY27 growth guidance was raised to "northwards of 60%" from an earlier 30-40%. The company also secured a INR62.40 crore IWAI hybrid ferry contract and raised INR150 crore via preferential issue plus a INR100 crore block deal.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 + Q1 FY27 combined average EBITDA margin (as cited by CEO)
Q4 FY26 + Q1 FY27 combined average PAT margin (as cited by CEO)

financial_highlights.value: More than INR1,300 crore: dredging ~INR240 crore, charter & hire ~INR850 crore, shipbuilding ~INR240 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Intercompany order book placed with Knowledge Shipyard

segments.name: Dredging
segments.commentary: Core segment and main revenue driver this quarter from JNPA capital rock dredging (River Pearl 47, completed) and Pondicherry maintenance dredging (River Pearl 18). Dredging order book ~INR240 crore; management expects ~INR200 crore to execute in FY27.

segments.name: Charter & hire
segments.commentary: Recurring revenue from tugs, mooring, pilot, patrol, survey vessels under multiyear port contracts; order book ~INR850 crore across 15 contracts. Management says it is 3-5% of revenue currently.

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Order book ~INR240 crore across 4 contracts, including IWAI contract for 10 hybrid electric 20-seat ferries (INR62.40 crore, ~10 months, built at Saphale yard). Currently ~9% of revenue; 42 third-party vessels and 5 captive vessels under construction.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now guided to northwards of 60% YoY, up from earlier 30-40%.
Dredging revenue for FY27 expected to exceed FY26 levels; management expects INR200 crore of the INR240 crore dredging order book to execute this year.
Target revenue of INR1,000 crore in FY29; management described it as the next milestone.
Shipbuilding expected to scale significantly from Q4 FY27 after Phase 1 of Saphale yard (14 vessels per year at Phase 1, 18 at full build-out); Phase 1 operational by end of FY27.
Operating (EBITDA) margins guided at 35-40% across segments; management said dredging margins will expand with volumes and it does not expect ~48-63% margins to persist.
FY29 revenue mix target: dredging 45-50%, shipbuilding 40-45%, charter ~5%.
capex_capacity: Capex of close to INR1,000 crore over roughly the next 1.5 years: ~INR250 crore for Green Tugs and green vessels, ~INR450 crore for dredging, balance for shipyard and shipbuilding.
Adding larger TSHDs, CSDs, backhoe dredgers and water injection dredgers; new dredgers of 5,000-7,000 cubic metre capacity cited for deep-sea (Samudra Manthan) work.
Saphale shipyard: Phase 1 to Phase 3 build-out to ~18 vessels per annum; Phase 1 alone 14 vessels.
Portfolio under construction: 10 accommodation boats, 10 work boats, 4 CSD vessels, 2 60-ton bollard pull Green Tugs, 10 hybrid electric passenger ferries.
demand_pricing: Management said dredging faces very little to no competition; it is selective, requiring entry barriers to be met, and targets EBITDA margins of 35-40%.

Bid pipeline results expected in 30-45 days; dredging bids to be executed over 3 years. Maintenance dredging additions of INR100-120 crore in FY27, rising to more than INR250 crore from next year; capital dredging additions ~INR70 crore in FY27 and ~INR150 crore next year.
Historical bid hit rate above 50% over the last 11 years; management said it cannot assume this will continue.
Management attributed peer DCI's margin trend to older equipment needing refurbishment, while KMEW's fleet is more efficiently utilised.
Green Tug contracts are with Visakhapatnam and V.O. Chidambaranar ports, 15-year fixed charter regardless of utilisation; EBITDA margin cited at 75% for Green Tug.
Export shipbuilding inquiries from Europe for ~3,000 DWT vessels under evaluation; payment terms still being negotiated.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 growth guidance including the INR60 crore revenue shift from last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier guidance was 30-40% YoY; management now sees potential northwards of 60% for FY27 on order book momentum.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ~INR1,300 crore order book executes in FY27 and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: INR200 crore of the INR240 crore dredging book is expected in FY27. Management said margins will expand, not contract, though not at the 63% operating margin seen in Q1, which it described as not guidance (35-40% stays the guide).

qa_highlights.question: Why are KMEW's dredging margins rising while DCI's are falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCI has older equipment needing refurbishment, while KMEW is better sweating its assets for efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Subcontracting expense trend?
qa_highlights.answer: FY23-24 subcontracting was high because of a JV structure where KMEW was lead partner. Now projects are executed individually; FY26 subcontracting expected at 5-6% of turnover, mainly shipbuilding and ancillary boats.

qa_highlights.question: Dredging vs shipbuilding mix in 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Dredging 45-50%, shipbuilding 40-45%, chartering ~5%. Shipbuilding pre-subsidy margins 15-20%, post-subsidy expected to go beyond 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Is shipbuilding captive or third party, and how is working capital funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 5 captive vessels (3 tugs, 2 boats) and ~42 third-party vessels. Working capital funded from stage payments (every 10-50% milestone), with no further loans needed; shipbuilding subsidy of 15-20% comes on delivery.

qa_highlights.question: Is dredging a moat given privatisation of ports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disagreed, citing perpetual government demand, DCI's 50-year role and tender structure (domestic below INR250 crore, international above).

532809|2026-06.headline: Firstsource Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.9% YoY to INR27.2bn (+2.2% QoQ cc) with EBIT margin 12.4%, but INR717m exceptional charges and a healthcare BPaaS wind-down weigh on outlook.
532809|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 22.9% YoY and 5.5% QoQ to INR27.2bn (US$288m), or 12.3% YoY and 2.2% QoQ in constant currency, the ninth straight quarter of double-digit YoY growth. EBIT margin was 12.4%, up 110bps YoY and 20bps QoQ, the seventh straight quarter of margin expansion. Reported PAT was INR1.7bn after INR563m net exceptional charges, against adjusted PAT of INR2.2bn. Management said a healthcare payer BPaaS program is being wound down by a client after a leadership change, costing roughly 1-1.5% of quarterly revenue, and reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 10-13% cc growth and 12.25-12.75% EBIT margin.

financial_highlights.change: +22.9% YoY, +5.5% QoQ reported; +12.3% YoY, +2.2% QoQ constant currency
three items: INR357m healthcare program termination, INR284m regulatory penalty indemnity, INR76m contingent consideration fair value (Ascensos)

financial_highlights.value: around 23% in Q1; guided 22-24% for FY27

segments.name: BFS
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 14% YoY and 5% QoQ in constant currency; five new logos added. Management cited a strong exit deal pipeline and collections demand from record US consumer debt.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11% YoY but fell 2% QoQ in constant currency; four new logos added. Payer-side Medicare Advantage programs were paced by CMS rate changes, and one BPaaS payer program is being wound down.

segments.name: CMT
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 6% YoY and 9% QoQ in constant currency; two new logos added. Management cited volatility from work-packet timing and program transitions in Silicon Valley consumer tech.

segments.name: Diverse portfolio (incl. utilities, Pastdue Credit, retail)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 27% YoY and was flat QoQ in constant currency; one new logo added. Management said utilities demand is steady with a healthy pipeline.

segments.name: Geography: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 8% YoY and was flat QoQ in constant currency. Management is setting up sales presence in Canada.

segments.name: Geography: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 18% YoY and 6% QoQ in constant currency; two large deals won in Europe. South Africa is the fastest-growing geography, and a Glasgow office was opened.

segments.name: Geography: Australia
segments.commentary: Revenue doubled YoY, driven by both existing clients and new logos.

guidance_outlook: FY27 constant-currency revenue growth reaffirmed at 10% to 13%.
FY27 EBIT margin reaffirmed at 12.25% to 12.75%.
Original guidance had included about 1% to 1.5% of growth from the healthcare BPaaS program now being wound down; management says guidance holds after absorbing this.
Management expects H2 FY27 to be strong as new wins ramp over roughly the next three months.
Long-term aim of a 14% to 15% EBIT margin over the next two to three years, with 50-75bps annual expansion thesis reiterated.
Management expects the exceptional-item amounts (INR357m and INR284m) to be recovered from the client and insurer, though they were expensed on a prudence basis.
demand_pricing: Four large deals (ACV above US$5m) won in Q1, the sixth straight quarter of four or more; ACV intake was the highest in the last four quarters.
12 new logos added, including three strategic logos; 145 clients above US$1m run-rate; US$5m+ clients up 80% and US$1m+ clients up 45% over two years.
Healthcare deal wins were more than a third of Q1 wins, in line with the roughly one-third revenue share from healthcare.

Hedge book at 30 June 2026: GBP61.6m at an average of 118-120 for the next 12 months; US$119m at about INR92.7/US$. Around 25-30% of the portfolio is in options at roughly 125-130 for GBP; blended GBP rate about 123-124 and USD about 94.
Management said the BPaaS client is wound down by client decision after leadership change, and the client has added more work elsewhere in the account.

qa_highlights.question: What was the revenue impact of the healthcare BPaaS termination in Q1, and what does the INR271m charge include?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the Q1 revenue impact of about 1-1.5%. The charge relates to partner-ecosystem deliverables; Firstsource is the single point of contact and is recovering amounts from the client and repaying partners.

qa_highlights.question: How is guidance maintained despite this hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was the best quarter for new deal wins in the last four quarters and that several wins ramp quickly, offsetting the 1-1.5% loss, so the 10-13% range is retained.

qa_highlights.question: Is the healthcare payer churn a sector-wide issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an isolated, one-off event caused by a new client leader pausing programs, not a secular trend. The same client continues to expand its footprint.

qa_highlights.question: How does the wound-down program compare with the USD50m steady-state run-rate expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 1-1.5% contribution was its estimate at the start of the year, reflecting slower ramp and schedule risk; the program will not reach the implied trajectory this fiscal year.

qa_highlights.question: How are segment margins evolving versus FY24 (BFS above 20% now, healthcare low double-digit)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly segment movements are aberrations from ramp costs and that company margin is up from 11% eight quarters ago to 12.4%, with no systemic issue seen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedge liability and forward book outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the GBP book is typically 50-75% of committed year-one value and USD about 25%; GBP 61.6m and USD 119m are hedged for the next 12 months at blended rates of about 123-124 (GBP) and 94 (USD).

534309|2026-06.headline: NBCC standalone Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 62% to INR 160 crore (8.77% margin) on 10% revenue growth to INR 1,823 crore.
534309|2026-06.overview:
Standalone revenue from operations grew 10% YoY to INR 1,823 crore, while EBITDA rose 62% to INR 160 crore and PAT rose 32% to INR 151 crore, helped by marketing fees from the Bharat Business Park sale. Consolidated revenue was INR 2,260 crore, with a consolidated order book of INR 1,27,000 crore and INR 1,600 crore of orders secured in the quarter. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore and expects INR 18,000-20,000 crore of new awards over the next 2-3 quarters, but several large awards (GPRA 5 colonies, J&K, MAHAPREIT, Supertech) have slipped repeatedly. Management also announced the HSCC merger into NBCC and an SPV for a proposed CPSE REIT.</overview>
<parameter name="financial_highlights">[{"metric": "Standalone revenue from operations", "value": "INR 1,823 crore", "change": "+10% YoY"}, {"metric": "Consolidated revenue from operations", "value": "INR 2,260 crore", "change": ""}, {"metric": "Standalone EBITDA", "value": "INR 160 crore", "change": "from INR 99 crore YoY, +62%"}, {"metric": "Standalone EBITDA margin", "value": "8.77%", "change": ""}, {"metric": "Standalone PAT", "value": "INR 151 crore", "change": "+32% YoY"}, {"metric": "Standalone order book", "value": "INR 1,12,000 crore", "change": ""}, {"metric": "Consolidated order book", "value": "INR 1,27,000 crore", "change": ""}, {"metric": "Consolidated order inflow (Q1)", "value": "INR 1,600 crore", "change": ""}, {"metric": "Cash balance as on 30 June", "value": "INR 666 crore", "change": "Analyst cited INR 6,500 crore last quarter; management did not reconcile the comparison"}]

segments.name: PMC / redevelopment (standalone order book)
segments.commentary: Standalone order book split is about 60% redevelopment and 40% PMC. Management says redevelopment and Amrapali contribute more than 60% of total revenue, and PMC fees are 8% plus 1% marketing on Amrapali.

segments.name: Real estate
segments.commentary: Management expects about INR 500 crore of real estate revenue this year from land, completed inventory and WIP sales. Bharat Business Park was fully sold, raising about INR 10,000 crore across three auctions.

segments.name: HSCC (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue dipped because HSCC foreclosed a Maharashtra health project quoted at about 2% margin, which management says cost about INR 300 crore of top line. Management is merging HSCC into NBCC.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore reiterated; management referred to INR 16,000-17,000 crore in parts of the call.
Standalone FY27 revenue guided at INR 13,000-14,000 crore; FY28 revenue around INR 21,000 crore; FY29 INR 24,000-25,000 crore (consolidated basis per management).
PAT guidance of INR 1,100-1,200 crore for FY27, INR 1,300-1,400 crore for FY28 and about INR 2,000 crore for FY29, on a consolidated basis.
Margin guidance: EBITDA at least 6.5-7% and PAT 6-6.5%.

Awards guided at INR 20,000-25,000 crore this year (including Supertech about INR 10,000 crore, J&K about INR 3,500 crore, Rajasthan Mandapam about INR 3,500 crore), against an earlier INR 30,000-32,000 crore target.
GPRA 5 colonies (Lodhi Colony, Andrews Ganj, DIZ, Lakshmi Bai Nagar) order of about INR 30,000 crore expected; management says cabinet approval is pending.
Redevelopment fund generation of INR 30,000-35,000 crore expected this year, sale-linked and construction-linked, with cash collected over about two years.
capex_capacity: Phase 2 Amrapali is awarded and in execution, with one tower at the 20th floor using Mivan shuttering and others at the 13th floor; Phase 1 has 23 of 24 projects completed.
Standalone order book: about INR 10,000 crore of balance work across GPRA 7 packages, to be completed within about 18-24 months.
Gurugram Sector 37-D: contractor mobilised and test piles done; revised plan and EC approval pending, with sales expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27.
Ghitorni: final lease agreement in process; consultant tender expected to be finalised this quarter; revenue after handover in about two years.
Business Park Tower purchase is construction-linked; only 10% first instalment paid so far, with the balance tied to construction milestones over about two years.
Dubai: 66 housing units under construction on a purchased land parcel; developer licence in hand; construction tender expected in October.
Goa redevelopment: four packages ordered, site mobilised and work started; two more packages pending tender.
demand_pricing: Africa Avenue auction for 262 residential units drew about 2,900 participants; auction postponed on a technical issue and expected in August. Vinayak Mandir auction targeted for September and Palanji area for September-October. Management expects INR 5,000-6,000 crore from Africa Avenue sales.
Amrapali: about 8,800 units in total, with roughly 4,000-4,500 sold; management expects to sell about INR 4,000-5,000 crore of inventory.

Pipeline: Supertech tender to be floated this quarter (16 projects in Noida and Greater Noida, about INR 10,000 crore); J&K infrastructure tender of about INR 3,500-4,000 crore to be floated this month after an initial INR 100 crore package drew about 15 bidders; MAHAPREIT (about INR 25,000 crore) expected in Q3; Naveen Nagpur infrastructure tender after DPR approval.

Recent wins: Odisha schools INR 253 crore, J&K campus INR 171 crore, New AP Bhavan INR 106 crore (Q1); Seychelles housing about INR 620 crore, RBI Amravati about INR 780 crore, Rajasthan science labs about INR 431 crore (July-August).
International: Seychelles has awarded a further 1,000 houses after about 2,000 in Maldives; management cites prospects in Australia, Saudi Arabia and Fiji, none included in projections.

521016|2026-06.headline: Indo Count Q1 FY27 total income rose 13% QoQ to INR1,224 crore and EBITDA margin recovered to 13.1%, with volumes up 12% QoQ.
521016|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with total income of INR1,224 crore (+13% QoQ, +27% YoY) and EBITDA of INR160 crore (+38% QoQ) at a 13.1% margin. Sales volume rose 12% QoQ to 23 million meters but fell 3% YoY on container shortages linked to the West Asia conflict. The new business (utility bedding and US brands) reached INR387 crore in the quarter. Bhilad plant was hit by flooding from 23 July 2026 and only partially resumed on 12 August 2026; the company says it is fully insured.

financial_highlights.change: Nearly tripled over past one year (per management)
vs INR80 crore last year (per management)
Q4 FY26 included one-off ~INR13 crore GST-related hit

segments.name: Core business (bed linen, quilts, comforters etc.)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR837 crore, +4% QoQ; ~70% US and ~30% non-US. Management says core blended margin is around 15%, with standalone margin slightly above 15% in Q1. Quarterly realisation fell on product mix.

segments.name: New business (utility bedding + US brands)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR387 crore in Q1, all US-linked. Split is roughly two-thirds utility bedding (manufacturing) and one-third brands; brand revenue was slightly above INR125 crore. FY27 target INR1,500 crore; brands target about INR500 crore for the year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume guidance reiterated at 105-110 million meters; core business revenue about INR4,000 crore.
FY27 new business revenue target INR1,500 crore; USD275 million new business ambition for 2028 and INR8,000 crore revenue aspiration by CY2028 reiterated.
Non-US revenue expected to grow 20%+ in FY27.
Endeavour to maintain about 13% blended EBITDA margin for FY27 on a consolidated basis; long-term stabilisation target 15-16% for the company as a whole.
Price increases concluded with customers; impact on realisations expected from Q2 onwards. Full-year realisations expected broadly intact.
Interest cost expected at about INR120 crore for FY27 (INR30 crore per quarter), at roughly 6-7%.
Utility bedding utilisation targeted at 60-65% for FY27.
Potential US tariff refund: management expects no material financial benefit; ~80% of exports are FOB; quantification premature, clarity expected by year-end.
capex_capacity: New greenfield facility in North Carolina commenced in January 2026; operations ramping, adding employee costs and a lower-margin gestation period.
Existing US facilities in Ohio and Arizona; utilisation overall around 60-65% in Q1 despite new capacity.

Bhilad (Gujarat) plant hit by flooding from 23 July 2026; partially resumed 12 August 2026 with phased normalisation. Management says other plants are absorbing lost output (endeavour, not confirmed).
Utility bedding business investment about 70-75% complete per management, with balancing investments still to come.
demand_pricing: Volumes recovering as US tariff uncertainty eased; Q1 seen as seasonally softer than Q2 and Q3 (US festive period).
Container availability constraints from the West Asia conflict hit Q1 dispatches; management says the container issue continues.
Raw material costs rose after the February-end war; price increases were negotiated case by case and concluded, with impact from Q2.
Non-US: UK FTA restores level playing field (UK business 8-10% of total); management says client interactions in UK rose from about 4 to 8 a year. EU FTA expected to add further duty-free access.
Competition: India at about 10% US tariff vs neighbours at 10-12.5%; management says no orders or customers were lost even at 50% tariff.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin difference between core bed linen and the new utility bedding and branded businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 15% for both bed linen and utility bedding over time, and brands 100-200 bps above that. Utility bedding is currently lower because the new facility is in gestation; bed linen did slightly better than 15% in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is any US tariff refund expected and how is it accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: No tariff refund was booked in Q1. Management expects no material benefit as ~80% of exports are FOB, and says quantification is premature until year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Will standalone margins decline in Q2 and Q3 given Bhilad disruption and cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined precise quarterly guidance; the endeavour is to hold about 13% blended consolidated margin for the full year. Any one-time losses are covered by insurance (property, inventory, loss of profit).

qa_highlights.question: Why is utility bedding utilisation guided at only 60-65% when Q1 already achieved that?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-65% is the satisfactory level to plan on for the full year, with stability expected for the rest of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost run-rate and weighted average cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest cost is about INR30 crore per quarter (INR120 crore annual); the Q4 figure included a one-off ~INR13 crore GST-related charge. Cost is roughly 6-7%, varying by bank; company rated A1+.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins go beyond 15% long term given the shift to branded and e-commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: No ceiling is set. Long-term target is to stabilise at 15-16% for the company as a whole, to be recalibrated as the business progresses.

risks_watch: Bhilad plant recovery pace after flooding; whether lost output is made up in Q2-Q3 without delays in shipments.
Container availability and West Asia-linked freight constraints, which cut Q1 volumes 3% YoY.
Quarterly realisation pressure from product mix; price increases on raw material costs to flow through from Q2.
Utility bedding: non-cotton input cost inflation, and whether it is fully passed on (management says yes, with 2-3 month lag at times).
New business ramp: management says variability is still unknown and about 70-75% of the investment is in place; USD100 million brand target is three years out.
Potential US tariff refund accounting, with clarity expected only by year-end.
521016|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on recovery and the INR8,000 crore aspiration, but noticeably reluctant to give precise quarterly margin or volume guidance. Management was defensive on Bhilad impact and on the margin question, and fell back on insurance cover and full-year averages.

506194|2026-06.headline: Arihant Superstructures Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 132 crore, with EBITDA margin at 21% and PAT at INR 10 crore.
506194|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 sales bookings were 221 units (2.31 lakh sq ft), up 15% YoY in area and value to INR 173 crore, with average realisation flat at INR 7,500 per sq ft. Consolidated operating revenue reached INR 132 crore (up 9% YoY), EBITDA INR 28 crore (21% margin) and PAT INR 10 crore (7.4% margin). Net debt stood at INR 818 crore against net worth of INR 460 crore, and management reiterated plans to reduce debt from next year while funding hotel and club assets. Management guided to 2,500 unit deliveries by FY27-end and said no new land acquisitions are planned this year.

segments.name: Residential (sales)
segments.commentary: 221 units booked for 2.31 lakh sq ft at a flat average of INR 7,500 per sq ft; average ticket size about INR 78 lakh per unit. Project mix is 41% luxury per management's presentation.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Hotel at World Villas (5-star, Radisson) is concluded; second hotel near Imagicaa is in closing. Hospitality capital deployed so far is INR 35-40 crore (about 7% of capital employed of INR 730 crore), with INR 500 crore total planned over three years for hotels and club.

guidance_outlook: Deliver 2,500 units by end of FY27; expects FY27 numbers a little above FY26, but not exponential growth.
Blended EBITDA margin expected to move towards 30-35% once Town Villas and villa projects contribute largely; management said at least a 10 percentage point rise is achievable over about 12 months.

543591|2026-06.headline: Dreamfolks Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR39 crore (from INR52.6 crore in Q4) and adjusted EBITDA was negative INR16.4 crore, hit by Middle East war and an MMG payment.

544609|2026-06.headline: PhysicsWallah Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,054 crore; pre-Ind AS EBITDA improved to negative INR44 crore, with NEET calendar shift a drag.

Pre-Ind AS EBITDA was negative INR44 crore (margin -4%), a 624 bps improvement from negative INR88 crore last year, while reported EBITDA was positive INR52 crore. Management attributed the enrollment softness to the NEET UG cycle shifting 5-7 weeks, which it said would have added 22-25% to offline growth. Management reiterated full-year FY27 guidance of 30% revenue growth and 100% EBITDA growth, and introduced first-time online/offline segment reporting.

qa_highlights.question: How many offline Vidyapeeth centers are profitable now?

capex_capacity: Offline store expansion was paused for two quarters to realign the product portfolio; now resuming with ~100 net new stores targeted in FY27.
RocketBees expanded from 62 to 72 cities and now handles over 50% of online shipments, a target set two quarters ago and met by June 2026. Delivery turnaround time improved ~20%.
FC Qwik (2-hour quick delivery) grew from ~60,000 shipments in five cities in March to 125,000 in 12 cities in June. Management targets 10% of total shipments on FC Qwik and 20% in specific pincodes.
Manufacturing business is passing crude-linked raw material and rupee-depreciation cost increases to customers.
demand_pricing: Diapering faces heightened competition from quick commerce discounting and new entrants. Management says branded diapering has started improving in Q1 and competitive intensity is softer in July and August.
Non-diapering categories (~85% of GMV, fashion >50% of GMV, home brands >50% of business) are performing well; management said gross margin is expected to improve through home brand and fashion mix.
GMV growth (12%) trails India revenue growth (18%) because the revenue line includes manufacturing and the GMV is at MRP, with GST 2.0 reducing MRP from Q2.
Management said non-diapering consumables are about 15% of India GMV, with healthy margins and no challenge from quick commerce.
Offline GMV grew 15% in Q1 after the width-to-depth assortment change, which added lower price points without a material gross margin impact.

532365|2026-06.headline: Dynacons Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR313 crore (from INR328 crore) on OEM-linked delivery delays, while EBITDA rose to INR40 crore and order book reached INR3,104 crore.
532365|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined year-on-year to INR313 crore from INR328 crore, which management attributed to extended OEM and supply-chain lead-times deferring execution and revenue recognition rather than weaker demand. EBITDA rose to INR40 crore, PAT was about INR20 crore and EPS was INR15.54, and management cited a better business mix and higher-value infrastructure and services. Order inflows were strong, including a INR750 crore RBI private cloud mandate, a INR267 crore NPCI data-centre project and a INR125 crore CBI AI-ready infrastructure mandate, taking the order book to about INR3,104 crore. Management declined to give numeric guidance, and analysts pressed on margins, lease costs, ROCE on the as-a-service asset base and competition from Netweb.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR328 crore in Q1 FY26 (decline)
improved over last two quarters per analyst; management did not dispute
PBT described as flat YoY by analyst; not disputed
analyst cited rise from about INR2 crore; not confirmed by management

segments.name: Data Center and Cloud
segments.commentary: Private cloud and data-centre augmentation wins include INR750 crore RBI mandate and INR267 crore NPCI project; management cites AI-ready infrastructure and containerization (INR125 crore CBI mandate).

segments.name: Networking and Security
segments.commentary: Management lists four reported segments: Data Center and Cloud, Networking and Security, Workplace Solutions and Managed Services; no segment revenue split was given.

segments.name: Workplace Solutions
segments.commentary: Included in the four-segment mix named by management; no segment-level figures disclosed.

segments.name: Managed Services / As-a-Service
segments.commentary: Device-as-a-Service and Core Banking-as-a-Service build-out added fixed assets (about INR158 crore per analyst) and lease costs; management says these are backed by contracted revenue and recurring components are embedded in large projects.

guidance_outlook: Management gives no numeric revenue or margin guidance; it expects delivery timing to normalise progressively over coming quarters.
Management says it expects the growth momentum of the last 10 years to continue, and expects the business mix to improve profitability.
Order book execution: management estimates an average of 18 to 24 months, with some projects immediate and others up to five years.
Management said the lease cost increase in the as-a-service business will continue as that business grows, with no new DaaS project announced in Q1 so lease numbers should be similar to last year.
capex_capacity: Fixed assets and right-of-use assets of about INR158 crore added last year to support the as-a-service business (per analyst); mix of outright purchases and leased assets.
Initial-phase asset utilisation is low and expected to pick up over time, according to management.
Management declined to give an expected ROCE range, saying ROCE may moderate from historically high levels as business mix evolves.
demand_pricing: Management says the revenue shortfall is timing-related and demand is intact; large customers are prioritising mission-critical projects and deferring non-critical ones as budgets rise 30-50%.
Large contracted orders are priced with OEM back-to-back support, so price escalation is not passed through once orders are loaded; new DaaS add-on orders are priced afresh at current rates.
Order sizes have grown: largest order was about INR350 crore previously and now INR750 crore; competition is with larger Tier-1 and global SIs.
Listed competitors named: Orient Technologies (most similar), Dev IT, Coforge and Wipro; Rashi Peripherals' acquired VDA is in a similar space. Management sees Inspirisys as rarely competing.
Management says it has private-sector banks as customers, but orders below the declarable threshold are not disclosed, so the disclosed mix skews to PSU banks.
Hyperscaler/co-lo data-centre work is lower-margin and largely OEM-direct; management says it is working with some global data-centre players.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q1 revenue shortfall fold back into next quarter, and how are Q2 and Q3 shaping up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shortfall is timing-related due to OEM component lead-times; it expects normalisation over coming quarters and continued growth momentum, without giving numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Can operating margin (about 13%) keep rising toward a mid double-digit level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give margin guidance; it credited business mix, disciplined execution and managed services, and said quarterly margins may fluctuate with project mix.

qa_highlights.question: How much of EBITDA is lease rental, and why did PBT stay flat while EBITDA grew?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split lease costs, which cover DaaS and core banking fixed assets; it said the gap versus EBITDA reflects depreciation and lease costs from capitalisation, and that Q1 lease costs should be similar to last year.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR3,100 crore order book convert and can 20%+ growth be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Conversion is 18-24 months on average, with some projects immediate and others up to five years; management acknowledged base effects but expects business mix to lift profitability.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw-material and component price increases handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Large contracted projects carry OEM back-to-back support so escalation is covered; customers are phasing non-critical spending as budgets rise 30-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Netweb taking share given its reported growth and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disagreed, saying order book and demand are strong; it declined to comment on other companies' margins and said Netweb is an OEM rather than a pure SI.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE and utilisation on the as-a-service asset base of about INR158 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a ROCE range, said the assets are backed by contracted revenue and are not loss-making, and that utilisation is lower in the first implementation phase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive landscape and why is PSU share higher than private banks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management named Orient Technologies, Dev IT, Coforge and Wipro as competitors and said private banks are customers but sub-threshold orders are not declared, making the disclosed mix look PSU-heavy.

risks_watch: Revenue declined YoY in Q1 FY27; conversion of the INR3,104 crore order book depends on OEM and component lead-times for GPUs, servers and memory.
Rising fixed assets and lease costs for the as-a-service business, with ROCE undisclosed and management declining to give a range.
Customers may defer non-critical spending as component budgets rise 30-50%.
Larger order sizes (INR750 crore single order) increase working-capital and execution risk; competition from Tier-1 and global SIs.
Margin sustainability: management gave no guidance and said margins may fluctuate with project mix.
532365|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and order book, but cautious and evasive on numbers: management repeatedly declined to provide revenue, margin, ROCE or lease-cost figures, and deflected questions on competitors and R&D.

544198|2026-06.headline: DEE Development Engineers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31.6% YoY to Rs 294.5 crore and EBITDA margin hit 16.9%, despite ~Rs 25 crore of dispatches slipping into Q2.
544198|2026-06.overview:
Revenue from operations was Rs 294.5 crore, up 31.6% YoY, with operating EBITDA of Rs 49.7 crore (16.9% margin vs 16% a year earlier). Management said about Rs 25 crore of oil and gas dispatches, deferred by export customers amid Middle East disruption, moved into Q2. Profit after tax was Rs 16.1 crore, and the Rs 300 crore preferential issue (net ~Rs 293 crore, ~Rs 225 crore earmarked for debt repayment) closed in July. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs 1,500 crore+ revenue, EBITDA margin above 19%, and order inflow of at least Rs 2,000 crore.</overview>

segments.name: Piping and heavy fabrication (core)
segments.commentary: Management guides Rs 1,150-1,250 crore from piping for FY27, with the balance from subsidiaries including Thailand. Piping and heavy fabrication are the large majority of revenue and order book.

segments.name: Thailand subsidiary
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about Rs 130 crore; target Rs 170-200 crore. Management says it is practically 100% booked for three years and no expansion is planned.

segments.name: Power PPA / non-core (Malwa, biomass pellets)
segments.commentary: Pellet plant (72,000 MT p.a., Muktsar) commissioned mid-Q1 FY27, so only partial contribution this quarter. Target combined non-core revenue around Rs 80 crore. Management said PPA EBIT went slightly negative (about Rs 1 crore) as fuel was diverted to the pellet plant; full operation expected from October.

segments.name: Seamless pipe plant (Anjar)
segments.commentary: Commissioned in FY26. Existing orders include about Rs 68 crore from L&T and a Rs 200 crore BHEL order, of which Rs 80-90 crore is expected to use in-house pipe. Management targets about 20% EBITDA on seamless pipe.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 1,500 crore+ reiterated; management called it a minimum and said the plan is to exceed it. Q1 is the weakest quarter, with Q4 typically the strongest.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided above 19%; management said it is 'absolutely on track'.
FY27 order inflow expected at least Rs 2,000 crore; Rs 700 crore already received, with Rs 1,300-1,800 crore expected in the rest of the year.
Net debt expected to be no more than Rs 400-425 crore by FY27 end; no plans for new debt this year.
Anjar plant utilisation expected at 60-65% this year and near 100% by end of FY28. Anjar revenue target of about Rs 1,500 crore by FY28-29.
Inventory days targeted at 150-160 by Q2 and 180-200 days for the overall working-capital cycle.
capex_capacity: Anjar pipe fabrication facility fully operational; seamless pipe plant commissioned in FY26. Plan is roughly 50-50 split between captive and outright-sale use of Anjar capacity.
Biomass pellet plant (72,000 MT p.a.) at Malwa Power Plant, Muktsar, commissioned in Q1 FY27.
Nuclear sector entry planned via a partner; management aims to finalise the partnership agreement in Q2 FY27.
No capex or capacity expansion planned at Thailand facility.
Preferential issue proceeds of about Rs 293 crore net: about Rs 224-225 crore for debt or working-capital repayment, balance for general corporate purposes.
demand_pricing: Revenue slippage: about Rs 25 crore of oil and gas dispatches deferred to Q2 as export customers delayed take-offs due to the Middle East situation; material is ready.
GE: GT orders continuing; HRSG order from GE yet to come, though an agreement exists for around 15-16 units. A GE meeting is set for 14 September.
Siemens: MoU for GT piping starting at 10 units next year, then 15, then 25-30 units. Each GT unit is about EUR 1-1.5 million. Siemens team to visit Anjar in the third week of August.
BHEL: slower than expected, but about Rs 200 crore order received last quarter and more tenders expected to be finalised next quarter. L&T has awarded all orders offloaded so far.
Export mix: about 50% export and 50% domestic for FY27. The order book includes about Rs 400 crore of India HRSG work and about Rs 200 crore from Thailand.
Gross margin pressure attributed to higher material content in power-sector jobs (versus job-work) and the mix shift. Management said conversion costs are lower for power jobs.
Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited domestic order of Rs 386.82 crore received in the quarter, described as one of the largest single orders in recent history.
Gulf reconstruction: inquiries are coming via OEMs; not yet direct, and not included in projections for five years.

qa_highlights.question: Status of GE HRSG orders and Siemens GT piping?
qa_highlights.answer: GE GT orders continue, HRSG order yet to come despite agreement for 15-16 units. Siemens MoU for 10 units next year, 15 the year after, then 25-30. Each GT unit about EUR 1-1.5 million.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 2,000 crore order inflow guidance still valid given delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said inflow may exceed Rs 2,000 crore. Rs 700 crore already received, with Rs 1,300-1,800 crore expected in the remainder of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PPA EBIT turn negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Limited fuel meant the company prioritised the pellet plant over the power plant. Full operation of both is expected from October when new fuel arrives.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt trajectory and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt Rs 718 crore at Q1 close versus Rs 733 crore at FY26 close, expected to fall to Rs 400-425 crore by FY27 end. Rs 224 crore used for working-capital limits reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher material content in power-sector jobs and a mix shift away from job-work. Management still expects EBITDA above 19%.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate for modelling?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone rate 25.17%; consolidated effective rate about 20-21% because of the Thailand subsidiary and subsidy income.

541233|2026-06.headline: Lemon Tree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to Rs 346.8 crore, but net EBITDA margin fell 99 bps to 43.8% on GST and SAR provision.
541233|2026-06.overview:
Revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs 346.8 crore and PAT rose 19% to Rs 57.3 crore, while occupancy rose 314 bps to 75.7% as the company shifted to a volume-led retail strategy. Gross ARR rose only 2% to Rs 6,361 because retail business carries lower net ARR after commissions, and management called Q1 an aberration driven by West Asia-related corporate travel softness. Margin compression came from a GST input-credit loss and stock appreciation rights provision, worth 3.1% of revenue combined. Management expects Q2 to be better, with July described as strong and August as solid. The call also covered the planned demerger of Fleur Hotels and Warburg's Rs 960 crore investment in Fleur.</overview>

segments.name: Owned hotels (Lemon Tree)
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs 320 crore of network revenue, 56% of network revenue. Net EBITDA margin hit by GST input-credit loss and renovation spend of about Rs 9.8 crore (2.25-2.3% of revenue).

segments.name: Managed and franchised (asset-light)
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs 256 crore of network revenue. Opened 6 hotels with 334 rooms and signed 13 hotels with 1,020 rooms in Q1. Same-store managed revenue grew 9-10%.

segments.name: Keys portfolio (Fleur)
segments.commentary: RevPAR up 19% YoY to Rs 2,885, with occupancy up 350 bps to 67% and ARR up 13% to Rs 4,311. Renovation is about two-thirds complete across 7 hotels.

segments.name: Fleur Hotels (pro forma)
segments.commentary: FY27 revenue Rs 311.4 crore (+7%), net EBITDA ex-GST Rs 125.1 crore (+10%, margin 40.2%), PAT Rs 34.7 crore (+23%).

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 net EBITDA margin to be better than the ~47% analyst estimate, and sees a path to at least 50% in FY28 as renovation spend drops and ARR improves.
Management targets a long-term Lemon Tree EBITDA margin of 75-80% as fee income doubles and corporate costs fall as a share of revenue.
Management targets Keys EBITDA of Rs 60 crore on revenue of Rs 115-120 crore, implying Rs 6.5 lakh per key EBITDA.
Target of about 2,000 rooms opened in FY27; management says it is broadly confident, with Q1 at 334 rooms.
Renovation spend is expected to fall to about 1% of revenue from FY28. GST impact is about 2% of net revenue and expected to decline gradually.
Demerger of Fleur expected to complete in H1 CY2027, with Fleur listing in late second half of calendar 2027 after SEBI, shareholder, creditor and GST approvals.
Fleur's long-term plan is to keep debt-to-EBITDA around 2x; Fleur targets roughly 15% ROCE after renovations are complete.
capex_capacity: Aurika Shimla (owned, 90 rooms): about Rs 108 crore deployed as of 30 June 2026; opening shortly as finishing and licences are in final stage.
Aurika Shillong (leased, 165 rooms): about Rs 33 crore deployed; opening expected H2 FY28.
Aurika Varanasi (leased heritage, 47 rooms): work begun; opening expected FY29.
Aurika Nehru Place Delhi: approvals pending; opening on or after FY30; DDA letter of award validity extended by one year.
Renovation: 300 rooms renovated in Q1 at about Rs 10 crore; similar number expected in Q2. Management expects 600-700 rooms in H1 and refurbishments of about 800 rooms in H2.

Fleur plans capital deployment of about Rs 2,500-3,000 crore, funded by Warburg's Rs 960 crore and about Rs 200-300 crore of balance-sheet cash. Management targets about 2,500 rooms of operating and under-development acquisitions.
Asset-light pipeline: 23,381 rooms across 279 hotels, of which 11,946 rooms across 135 hotels are operational.
demand_pricing: Q1 ARR growth was driven by a retail-led volume strategy, which lowered net ARR after commissions. Management calls this temporary and says the mix is returning to balance in July and August.

Corporate demand softened in high-density CBD markets such as Mumbai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru during the West Asia conflict, with lower travel, hiring and relocations. Delhi, Bengaluru and Hyderabad still outperformed; Mumbai and Gurgaon did not.
Mumbai airport micro-market absorbed about 2,000 new rooms over the last two years, creating a temporary supply mismatch. Aurika Mumbai pricing is being reset, with the stated aim of higher ARR.
Around 52% of company room sales are below Rs 7,500 (the GST threshold) and 48% above. Management is repricing demand-dense hotels to reduce GST drag.
OTA share of business is in the mid-30s%, and direct channels rose in Q1 with the retail push. Management expects a better negotiated versus non-negotiated mix from Q2.
Management says July was strong and August solid; Q2 demand is significantly better than Q1.

540762|2026-06.headline: TII Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18% to Rs 2,366 Cr, but PBT fell to Rs 213 Cr on steel cost lag; management expects full recovery.
540762|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew to Rs 2,366 Cr from Rs 2,007 Cr, while standalone PBT declined to Rs 213 Cr from Rs 222 Cr, with management attributing margin pressure to steel price increases in Q4 and Q1 that pass through to customers with a 2-3 quarter lag. Engineering revenue rose 21% to Rs 1,566 Cr with flat PBIT at Rs 153 Cr, and Metal Formed Products PBIT fell to Rs 28 Cr from Rs 37 Cr despite 11.5% revenue growth. The e-mobility (Clean Mobility) business posted its highest-ever quarterly turnover of close to Rs 240 Cr and management said losses likely peaked, with volumes up about 64% QoQ. Management said steel price recovery, including Q1 under-recovery, will be fully recovered, while non-steel inflation (fuel, freight) recovery talks with OEMs are ongoing.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,566 Cr vs Rs 1,298 Cr YoY; PBIT flat at Rs 153 Cr. Volume grew about 17%, and margins were hit by steel cost inflation.

segments.name: Metal Formed Products (MFP)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 408 Cr vs Rs 366 Cr YoY (about 11.5%), but PBIT fell to Rs 28 Cr from Rs 37 Cr. Growth was volume-led, with railways a drag and a Hyundai-linked unit weak; a western region greenfield plant is delayed by six months.

segments.name: Mobility (Clean Mobility / e-mobility)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 250 Cr vs Rs 198 Cr YoY; PBIT Rs 9 Cr vs Rs 7 Cr. Management cited highest-ever turnover of close to Rs 240 Cr (the call figure), with negative EBIT narrowing by about Rs 40-50 Cr per analyst, and three-wheeler billing of 1,924 units.

segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 256 Cr vs Rs 236 Cr YoY; PBIT Rs 21 Cr vs Rs 17 Cr. Includes TI Medical, CDMO (3xper) and Orange Koi, the newly acquired metal injection moulding start-up.

guidance_outlook: Management expects steel price increases, including the Q1 under-recovery, to be fully recovered with a lag, with margin neutralisation in coming quarters.
Management declined to quantify the Q1 under-recovery but reiterated guidance for double-digit EBIT margin growth.
Non-steel inflation (fuel, freight) recovery under discussion with OEMs; update expected in about one quarter.
Cycles business: management targets about 2 bps (as stated, likely 2 percentage points) further margin improvement for FY27 to reach about 5% margin.
TI Medical core surgical business expected to grow about 20% YoY with profitability; IV cannula acquisition plant to start revenue from August/September 2026.
Jayem expected to add a battery business stream; one EV business expected to break even in FY27, and two more in FY28.
Rs 750 Cr total capital infusion into new ventures over time; Rs 250 Cr infused in Q4 FY26, another Rs 250 Cr expected in Q3 FY27.
Management expects engineering demand to remain bullish for the next one or two quarters, barring geopolitical disruption.
capex_capacity: TI standalone capex planned at about Rs 350 Cr for FY27; Shanthi Gears about Rs 100 Cr; group ex-CG Power about Rs 600-700 Cr, per CFO.
Capex directed to engineering and MFP divisions, plus TI Medical and 3xper CDMO.
3xper CDMO 200 KL intermediate capacity: commissioning done, validation batches underway, clean room commissioning in 30-40 days, customer PAS filing and inspection expected in FY28.
Greenfield MFP plant in western region delayed by six months.

demand_pricing: Engineering volume grew about 17% in Q1; management said exports grew strongly with double-digit growth; exports are about 14% of TI revenue.
Steel price increases in Q4 and Q1 caused margin compression; pass-through lag of 2-3 quarters.
Cycles business benefited from strong Q1 seasonality (schools and colleges reopening) with higher market share.
Clean Mobility billing volumes in Q1: 86 heavy trucks, 1,924 three-wheelers, 347 small commercial vehicles, 22 tractors. Three-wheeler FY26 billing about 6,700 vs Vahan registrations about 6,500.
Cell prices expected to stay firm through at least Q3 FY27 due to BESS demand; mitigation via pre-booking long lead-time orders.
Nepal: about 100+ three-wheeler units shipped or in process; African markets (Tanzania, Ethiopia) at exploratory stage.
HCV deployments: about 22 trucks at Welspun's Anjar port, plus single-digit deployments at Vizag and Chennai ports, and Wonder Cement at Tuna and Dahej ports.
